item.title: Engineering student held for cultivating cannabis, selling drugs in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Malkajgiri SOT officials arrested engineering student Ch Sai Dinesh in Jawaharnagar for allegedly cultivating cannabis plants at home and selling dry marijuana. Police seized two plants and four grams of marijuana worth Rs 5,000.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 22-year-old engineering student was arrested by Malkajgiri SOT officials for allegedly cultivating cannabis plants at his residence and procuring and selling dry marijuana to known consumers in Jawaharnagar.

The suspect, Ch Sai Dinesh of Balaji Nagar, allegedly developed a habit of consuming marijuana and later entered the illegal trade by cultivating cannabis plants at home and procuring dry marijuana from unidentified suppliers for sale to consumers. He was allegedly involved in both selling and consuming the drug.

During a search of his residence, police seized two live cannabis plants, each about two feet tall, and a packet containing approximately four grams of dry marijuana. The seized property was estimated to be worth Rs 5,000.

Further investigation is under way to identify the suppliers, trace consumers and establish whether others were involved in the drug network.

item.title: From Lotus growth in 1940 to pollution now: Tracing Hussain Sagar’s troubles
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.category: Telangana State Archives and Research Institute
item.description: Archival records show the Nizam government tackled creeping lotus, water hyacinth and malaria mosquito breeding in Hussain Sagar in 1940, using an underwater cutter designed by State Mechanical Engineer S.K. Iyer.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Even before modern lake-restoration drives involving floating harvesters in Hussain Sagar made headlines, the Nizam government was grappling with plant growth, including water hyacinth and creepers, and malaria mosquito breeding in the lake.

Archival records of the Nizam government show that a memo issued in April 1940 warned of rapidly spreading water hyacinth in the lake.

The Public Works Department, which inspected the lake near the power house, found that the infestation was creeping lotus spreading from cooling ponds towards the Bulkapur channel inlet and power house condenser inlet.

According to an archival record available with the Telangana State Archives and Research Institute, the Nizam government faced a peculiar issue in the lake. Manually pulling out creepers was expensive and delayed regrowth for only about a fortnight.

Armstead, a mint master who had dealt with the issue a few years earlier in the Power House cooling ponds, told the Public Works Department that merely cutting and uprooting the plant was not enough. He suggested injecting super-heated steam into the plant’s roots. However, the department found the suggestion expensive and said it might not work, as some roots were embedded at a depth of up to 20 feet of water.

To tackle the issue, State Mechanical Engineer S.K. Iyer was entrusted with designing a machine that could operate underwater. He developed a cutter that was efficient in operation and inexpensive. The machine cleared nearly 60 per cent of the growth along the foreshore in less than two weeks.

Following the machine’s success, the department sought to manufacture eight rafts with cutters, four shears, and eight plain rafts with one punt at an estimated cost of Rs 2,650. In addition, Rs 1,260 was proposed for weeding and cutting maintenance work for two years, with a monthly expenditure of Rs 50. This included Rs 15 a month for three men, Rs 5 towards cutter and punt repairs, and five per cent charges for miscellaneous and unforeseen works. It took nearly two years to cut fresh shoots that appeared from time to time.

The Nizam government, which was facing a malaria menace, also took up anti-larval measures in the lake after it became a breeding ground for malaria mosquitoes. The then Director of Medical and Public Health sought 75 labourers to clear thick overgrowth along the lake edges for three months. The director also sought 20 labourers to be employed permanently to oil the edges and prevent mosquito breeding.

item.title: Crypto investors seek govt action against WazirX, Binance over alleged fraud
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Thousands of cryptocurrency investors have reportedly approached the ED and CBI over alleged losses linked to WazirX and Binance. Complaints cite account access issues, ownership confusion, post-cyberattack restrictions and concerns over Singapore-based restructuring and reported recovery claims
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Thousands of cryptocurrency investors have approached central investigative agencies, including the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), alleging that crypto exchanges WazirX and Binance caused significant financial losses to them, as per multiple reports.

Reports claim that complaints submitted by investor groups and users have reported alleged unauthorised access to accounts and loss of crypto assets.

Regulatory authorities have been unable to take decisive action due to the absence of a comprehensive legal framework governing cryptocurrency-related frauds in India, they added.

The petitioners said WazirX, which had marketed itself as one of India’s largest and most secure cryptocurrency platforms with around 16 million registered users, operated for several years while maintaining business links with global crypto exchange Binance.

Investors claim that Binance, which announced the acquisition of WazirX in 2019, benefited from the rapid growth of India’s cryptocurrency market and generated substantial revenues through trading activity and token-related business.

However, they alleged that questions over the ownership of WazirX emerged after enforcement authorities in India began scrutinising the platform and issued notices under foreign exchange regulations in 2022.

According to the complaints, Binance subsequently stated that it did not own WazirX, while WazirX’s user agreement continued to reference Binance as a wallet service provider for users’ crypto assets, the reports said.

The petitioners contend that these developments created confusion among customers regarding responsibility for safeguarding user funds.

The investors further alleged that after a major cyberattack on WazirX in July 2024, the exchange proposed measures that effectively distributed losses across both affected and unaffected users.

Users whose holdings were not compromised in the breach also faced restrictions on access to their assets, according to them.

The complaints also questioned WazirX’s decision to seek court approval in Singapore for a restructuring scheme through its Singapore-based entity, Zettai Pte Ltd.

Petitioners argued that the move made it more difficult and costly for predominantly Indian users to challenge decisions affecting their investments.

However, trading on the WazirX platform remained suspended for an extended period following the cyberattack, preventing users from accessing or trading their holdings during periods of market volatility, the reports said.

Meanwhile, some investors alleged that they missed significant gains in certain cryptocurrencies while their assets remained frozen.

The petitioners have also challenged claims that users recovered most of their holdings under the restructuring process, asserting that the actual recovery levels for some investors were substantially lower than publicly communicated figures.

item.title: Google commits $5 million to AI research at IIT Kharagpur
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Google will provide $5 million to IIT Kharagpur to support advanced AI research, education and capacity-building. The initiative will focus on applications in Indic languages, agriculture, materials science and educational technology, while helping develop the next generation of AI talent
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Google is excited to help accelerate IIT Kharagpur’s groundbreaking work in Indic languages, agriculture and education with $5 million to develop advanced AI research, CEO of Google and Alphabet Sundar Pichai said on Saturday, noting that such programmes will help implement Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision that the benefits of AI reach everyone in India.

Pichai — an alumnus of IIT Kharagpur — said the institute is undertaking pioneering work in fields such as Indic languages, agriculture and education, and that the partnership would help accelerate its impact.

The initiative would contribute to developing the next generation of AI talent and support wider efforts to ensure that the benefits of artificial intelligence reach people across the country, he added.

The announcement comes amid growing investments by global technology companies and academic institutions in AI research and workforce development as India seeks to strengthen its position as a global innovation hub.

The funding will be directed towards three key areas — advanced AI research, educational opportunities and AI capacity building across the institute.

As part of the initiative, IIT Kharagpur researchers and students will undertake projects aimed at addressing real-world challenges through AI applications in Indic languages, materials science, agriculture and educational technology, according to the company.

The partnership will also support the expansion of AI training and curriculum development for students, faculty members and educators, while enhancing the university’s AI frameworks and tools to strengthen its broader technological ecosystem.

Google said the funding reflects its commitment to fostering collaboration with academic institutions to advance AI-driven innovation and develop solutions with societal impact.

“Building AI that works for everyone requires deep collaboration and strong academic leadership. Through this fund, we are honoured to support IIT Kharagpur in driving applied AI research and technological solutions that will benefit communities across India and beyond,” the company said.

item.title: CERT-In warns of AI-driven cyber-attacks on business payment systems
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: CERT-In has warned that cybercriminals are using AI-powered tools to manipulate business payment workflows and divert funds. Attacks are increasingly targeting records and approval processes, while agentic frameworks enable automated reconnaissance and intrusion across enterprises, government bodies and institutions
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has flagged that cyber-attacks have extended beyond banks and financial institutions to technology service providers supporting government entities’ payment processes and other platforms handling vendor or partner payouts.

Cybercriminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence-powered tools to manipulate business payment workflows and execute unauthorised transactions, targeting crucial programming languages such as Java or PHP, which support 70 per cent of the internet.

“Recent observations by CERT-In show that unauthorised financial transactions involving business payment systems are not limited to BFSI entities but also affect technology service providers supporting government-linked payment processes and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts,” CERT-In said in a recent advisory.

Unlike traditional attacks that target payment applications’ programming interfaces (APIs), targets have increasingly shifted to altering business records or approval processes that determine whether payments should go through, allowing them to divert funds through “legitimate payment processes.”

Earlier in November, CERT-In had warned that hackers are using AI to breach the live systems of Indian non-banking financial corporations, fintech companies and payment aggregators to steal money.

As these transactions often use trusted systems and established procedures, the activity is difficult to detect immediately.

“The concern is not limited to the security of payment APIs. A transaction may pass the usual application and approval checks even when the records used to initiate it have been changed without authorisation,” the advisory said.

CERT-In has also observed the use of an “AI-driven agentic offensive framework” (AOF) to target enterprises, service providers, government organisations, and academic and research institutions.

It flagged the use of multiple agents or automated workers to undertake reconnaissance, privilege discovery and other intrusion tasks in parallel.

“AOFs allow several intrusion tasks to be carried out with less manual effort and can shorten the time between reconnaissance and subsequent attack stages. Organisations should account for such activity when reviewing their exposure, access controls and monitoring arrangements, irrespective of the sector in which they operate,” CERT-In said.

item.title: AIMIM says Mohammed Siraj’s selection should depend on performance
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: AIMIM spokesperson Waris Pathan has questioned Mohammed Siraj’s exclusion from India’s playing XI against New Zealand, saying selection should be based on talent and performance. The remarks follow allegations by Congress MP Imran Masood over the cricketer’s omission
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Amid the controversy over cricketer Mohammed Siraj’s exclusion from India’s playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) on Saturday said that team selection should be determined by a player’s talent and performance rather than their name or identity.

Siraj, India’s leading wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, was left out of the playing XI for the first Test on Thursday, prompting questions over the team management’s selection strategy. India opted for Anshul Kamboj in their pace-heavy combination, with the youngster featuring alongside Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna and Akash Deep, while the experienced Siraj was named among the reserves.

Speaking to IANS, AIMIM National Spokesperson Waris Pathan questioned the selection decisions, referring to the cases of other cricketers, including Sarfaraz Khan and Mohammed Shami.

“My belief is that earlier, Sarfaraz, he is from our Mumbai, he wasn’t picked either. Earlier, he was told his body is heavy, this and that. He reduced his body, reduced his weight, and gave such good performance in domestic cricket. So why wasn’t Sarfaraz picked? You didn’t pick Shami,” Pathan said.

He further pointed out that Siraj had delivered strong performances for the Indian team and had stepped up whenever the side needed him, including when Jasprit Bumrah was unavailable.

“Mohammed Siraj was playing positive cricket, was giving good performances, was a good help to the team in place of Bumrah; whenever the team needed him, he gave good performances. Why wasn’t he picked? The selection should be based on talent and performance and not the name. On one hand, Jay Shah was made the head of BCCI without any talent and performance, and on the other hand, Sarfaraz, Shami and Siraj, all were dropped,” he added.

This comes against the backdrop of the controversy following Congress MP Imran Masood’s remarks on Siraj’s exclusion from the playing XI, alleging that the cricketer had been overlooked because of his religious identity.

“His name is Siraj – isn’t that reason enough? If he is performing and still not getting selected, what else could be the reason? This alone can be the reason; there can be no other reason besides this,” the Congress leader claimed.

Meanwhile, India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the decision, saying the combination selected for the match was considered the strongest possible by the captain and team management.

item.title: Mangaluru medical student traced to Kerala, refuses to return home
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: A medical student allegedly abducted from a Mangaluru college campus has told the Konaje police that she does not wish to return to her family. Traced to Kerala, she is a legal adult, and police are investigating the incident
item.content:encoded:
Mangaluru: The medical student who was allegedly abducted by her family members from a private medical college campus over her relationship with a Hindu youth in Mangaluru has told the Konaje police that she does not wish to return to her family.

The police recorded her statement on Saturday after tracing her to a relative’s residence in Kerala.

The young woman, who is a legal adult, reportedly made it clear to the police that she did not want to accompany her family members. Based on her wishes, the police have decided to send her to a place of her choice or an observation centre. The police have also conducted a medical examination of the victim.

Meanwhile, the Konaje police have summoned two persons allegedly involved in the abduction to the police station and issued notices to them. A case has been registered in connection with the incident, and further investigation is underway.

The incident came to light after a video showing the student being forcibly taken away in a Thar vehicle from the campus of a private medical college went viral on social media on Friday. The alleged abduction reportedly took place on Thursday evening over her relationship with a Hindu youth.

The video shows a group of men arriving at the college campus and forcibly taking the young woman away as she screams, shouts and resists their attempts to kidnap her. The men are seen lifting her and pushing her into the back seat of a vehicle. One of them also appears to throw her sandals towards her. The incident reportedly took place in broad daylight in the presence of other students.

According to allegations, the Muslim student was taken away by her family members against her wishes because of her relationship with a Hindu youth. The video, recorded on a mobile phone and subsequently circulated on social media, triggered widespread reactions and raised concerns among students.

Reacting to the incident, Mangaluru Police Commissioner Sudhir Kumar Reddy had said that the woman was a legal adult and had the right to decide where she wanted to live. He had clarified that forcibly taking an adult against her wishes constituted an offence.

He had also directed the police to register a case, investigate the incident and trace the student. The police subsequently launched a search operation and tracked her down in Kerala.

item.title: ISI-backed networks recruit Indian youths for smuggling and killings
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Officials say ISI-backed networks have allegedly recruited Indian youths for smuggling arms, ammunition and narcotics, using small payments and promises of wealth. Recruits are reportedly blackmailed into larger operations, including contract killings, as the network seeks to expand beyond Punjab
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Over the past several months, channels backed by Pakistan’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) have recruited scores of Indian youths to carry out various subversive activities. Lured by payments as low as Rs 5,000, these youths have been tasked with collecting and distributing narcotics, arms and ammunition.

The ISI operatives have been employing the dead-drop method to deliver consignments of arms, ammunition, and narcotics, particularly in Punjab. The recruited youths are instructed to retrieve these consignments from designated locations and subsequently distribute them across the state.

An official said a dangerous trend was emerging, adding that the youths, most of whom were recruited by the Shahzad Bhatti network, had been lured with promises of a lavish lifestyle and easy money.

“They were shown photographs of Bhatti and his associates posing in front of luxurious houses and expensive vehicles, dressed in flashy clothes. These images created an impression of wealth and glamour, becoming a major attraction and one of the primary reasons why the youths agreed to join such networks,” the official said.

Once a youth was drawn into the network, he was initially assigned relatively minor tasks involving very little risk and offered paltry sums of money for completing them. He was then promised substantially higher payments for subsequent assignments, a lure many youths fell for without realising the consequences of their involvement.

Another official said the recruitment network had devised a trap that ensured the youths remained under its control. After completing the initial minor assignment, the recruits were paid the promised amount. However, when they were assigned bigger tasks, the promised higher remuneration was withheld. Instead, they were blackmailed into carrying out more serious assignments with threats that they would otherwise be reported to the security agencies.

“As a result, the assignments continue to get executed, but the youths are paid only paltry sums, irrespective of the scale or nature of the task,” the official said.

The youths are often blackmailed into undertaking smuggling operations on a much larger scale. They are even instructed to transport large consignments of arms and ammunition, tasks that they had never initially agreed to undertake but are forced to carry out under the threat of being exposed to the security agencies.

An Intelligence Bureau official said the latest trend was to blackmail these youths into undertaking not only smuggling operations but also contract killings.

“A hit job is the toughest one for these youth to execute it as it is murder and is punishable with either life or death. The youth are aware of this, but are forced into the job as they fear being outed by the ISI-backed networks,” the official.

Further, they are also threatened with dire consequences and often told their families would be informed about the same.

Fearing being ostracised, these youth go about the job despite being paid the paltry amount of Rs 5,000, the official also added.

Last year, there were at least six targeted killings of policemen in Punjab. In most cases, it has been found that the locals have allegedly undertaken the job.

The Bhatti network now wants to expand and rope in youth from other states to carry out similar jobs. It would look to move away from using the locals of a particular state and instead use them in other states. These youths entering another state have a clean slate and no files on them. Neither are they under the scrutiny of the local law enforcement agencies, and this helps a great deal in avoiding detection.

The ISI has intentions of going beyond Punjab to carry out such hit jobs on police personnel. It has been building this huge network of youth from the various states in the North for this purpose. The youths, who are part of such networks, would eventually be blackmailed into carrying out bigger jobs such as targeted killings.

Such youths, who feel trapped should immediately report the same to the police rather than continue to commit crimes which only get bigger with more number of assignments, an official said.

item.title: Adani Defence demonstrates Bagheera AT1 anti-tank missile system in Pokhran
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Adani Defence & Aerospace demonstrated its Bagheera AT1 vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile system at Pokhran, Rajasthan. The company says the system offers an 8-km range, enhanced mobility and resistance to electronic jamming, supporting India’s defence modernisation and indigenous capability development
item.content:encoded:
Pokhran (Rajasthan): Adani Defence & Aerospace has successfully demonstrated ‘Bagheera AT1’, a vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) system, at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan, the company said on Saturday.

‘Bagheera AT1’ is the outcome of 18 months of design and development, during which Adani Defence customised the missile system for Indian terrain, climate and operational requirements.

The result is a complete combat system comprising the missile, automated launcher, day and night sights, mounted on an Adani Defence-designed 4×4 high-mobility armoured vehicle. It engages armour at up to 8 km, twice the approximately 4 km range of the land-based anti-tank missile, according to the Adani Group company.

Four ready-to-fire missiles on the automated launcher and 8 reloads onboard provide a total capacity of 12 missiles per vehicle.

The missile rides a laser beam rather than relying on a radio link, making it highly resistant to electronic jamming on a battlefield increasingly shaped by drones and electronic warfare. Two missiles can be fired in quick succession along the same beam at a single target. The first engages the tank’s Active Protection System (APS), while the second is designed to penetrate its defences.

The system can also engage aerial targets at an extended range. The crew engages from cover and relocates quickly to reduce exposure to enemy fire.

Adani Defence said that the ‘No Cost No Commitment’ (NCNC) demonstration at Pokhran on November 20 was witnessed by senior representatives of the Indian Army, Department of Military Affairs and Ministry of Defence (MoD).

Recent conflicts have underscored the importance of range and mobility in armoured engagements.

‘Bagheera AT1’ offers the Army an additional long-range, mobile ground capability alongside man-portable and helicopter-launched missiles.

India’s requirement for modern anti-tank guided missiles remains substantial, with reported gaps in the ATGM inventory underscoring the need for continued modernisation.

“The in-service backbone remains second-generation ‘Milan-2T’ and ‘Konkurs-M,’ with Spike missiles subsequently inducted to address immediate operational requirements. India is also progressing with the acquisition of ‘Javelin’ systems,” said the company.

India’s defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. The private sector’s share rose to 24 per cent, or about Rs 42,000 crore, from 22 per cent a year earlier, while exports hit a record Rs 38,424 crore.

Bagheera AT1 demonstrates the growing role of India’s private sector in developing, integrating and delivering advanced defence systems tailored to the operational requirements of Armed Forces.

item.title: Nalgonda man dies in New York crash after vehicle hits deer
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Saiteja Eeramalla, 25, a Munugode native from Nalgonda district, died after his vehicle struck a deer and was hit by a cargo van on Interstate 90 in New York, police said.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 25-year-old man from Nalgonda district died in New York on Wednesday after the vehicle he was driving struck a deer and was hit by a cargo van, according to the New York State Police.

Troopers responded to a four-car collision on Interstate 90 Thruway eastbound in Canajoharie at about 6.34 p.m. on Wednesday, police said.

“The investigation determined an eastbound vehicle struck a deer, causing it to be disabled in a travel lane. An eastbound cargo van struck the disabled vehicle, causing a reaction collision with two other vehicles. The driver of the vehicle that struck the deer was identified as Saiteja Eeramalla, 25, of Utica, New York. Eeramalla sustained severe injuries during the collisions and was transported to St. Mary’s Hospital where he was declared deceased,” the police said in a statement.

A passenger in Eeramalla’s vehicle sustained serious injuries and was airlifted to Albany Medical Center, where they remain in critical condition. A passenger in the cargo van was also taken to St. Mary’s Hospital with what are believed to be non-life-threatening injuries, police added.

Saiteja Eeramalla, a native of Munugode in Nalgonda district, had moved to the US for higher studies and was residing in Utica, New York. He was the eldest son of Eeramalla Prasad and Srikanya.

item.title: TGCSB busts movie piracy network, arrests two men from Kurnool
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau arrested two 19-year-olds from Kurnool for allegedly recording newly released films in a theatre and distributing them through piracy websites and Telegram channels, while efforts continue to trace other members.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) has busted an organised movie piracy network involved in illegally recording newly released films in theatres and distributing them through piracy websites and Telegram channels and arrested two teens from Andhra Pradesh in connection with the case.

The arrested suspects were identified as Shaik Rizwan (19) and Rampogu Ajay (19), from Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh.

According to investigators, the suspects recorded newly released films at SVC Cinemas in City Square Mall, Kurnool, and uploaded them to Gofile.com. The recordings were subsequently circulated through the piracy website go2.india4movies.click, with the prime accused coordinating the operation through Telegram.

TGCSB said digital piracy causes substantial losses to the film industry and can also facilitate illegal betting, financial fraud and other cybercrimes.

Further investigation is underway to identify the remaining members and initiate legal action under the applicable provisions of the Cinematograph Act and Information Technology Act.

Police seized three mobile phones allegedly used to record movies inside theatres.

The arrests were made based on inputs generated by the Anti-Piracy Unit (APU). Efforts are underway to trace cryptocurrency transactions and identify other members of the network.

The APU, established in January 2026, through an MoU between TGCSB and the Telugu Film Chamber of Commerce, has so far blocked 42,151 piracy-related URLs, served 87 notices to major hosting servers, identified eight suspects and secured five arrests.

Its anti-piracy efforts reportedly helped save around Rs 33.6 crore in revenue across more than 20 films.

item.title: Malkajgiri commissioner orders removal of low-hanging cables
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation Commissioner T. Vinay Krishna Reddy directed officials and service providers to remove low-hanging and tangled overhead cables after an inspection at Alwal Circle on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: To prevent accidents and ensure pedestrian safety, Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation Commissioner T. Vinay Krishna Reddy directed officials and service providers to immediately remove low-hanging and tangled overhead cables across the municipality.

On Saturday, Reddy inspected Alwal Circle and directed officials to improve waste disposal, sanitation and cable infrastructure.

During the inspection, he found loose and irregularly installed wires belonging to cable television, broadband and internet service providers, including some hanging below 5 feet. He asked officials to coordinate with the electricity department and cable operators to remove loose, abandoned and improperly fixed wires.

Reddy said cables should be managed properly to prevent inconvenience to commuters and protect public safety. He directed departments to coordinate and ensure accountability for sanitation, waste management and infrastructure improvements.

item.title: Hyderabad heritage building that housed civil servants faces collapse
item.dc:creator: Sunil Mungara
item.description: Hyderabad’s century-old Civil Service House, a Grade III heritage structure that later housed the College of Nursing, has suffered partial collapse and wall damage from rainwater seepage, prompting calls for restoration and safety measures.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A century-old heritage building that served as the Hyderabad Civil Service House and housed the administrative offices of top civil servants of the erstwhile Hyderabad State is in a dilapidated condition and awaiting renovation.

Heavy rains have already caused a portion of the building to collapse, while rainwater seepage has weakened its walls. The Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) has notified the building as a Grade III heritage structure and listed it under Reference No. 109 in its heritage records.

The heritage building served as the Hyderabad Civil Service House until 1948. Following Hyderabad’s merger with India, it was converted into the College of Nursing in 1950 and used by the medical and health department to train healthcare professionals for over four decades.

“The building was originally constructed in the 1930s under the reign of the last Nizam of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style, specifically its regional Mughal variation,” according to a city-based historian.

Standing on a stone plinth, the heritage structure covers 2,714 sq metres of the 6,836 sq metres occupied by the Nursing College, revenue records show. The structure is in dilapidated condition due to its aging and lack of maintenance.

Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) Hyderabad Chapter convener Anuradha Reddy said the building, historically known as the Hyderabad Civil Service House, was officially listed as structure No. 37 alongside other iconic Nizam-era landmarks to document its architectural value and physical preservation.

“The Telangana government has to allot funds and restore the iconic structure located in the heart of the city,” she said.

The Government College of Nursing principal Hensel said the college had used part of the heritage building for the principal’s room and other staff until 2016, before shifting to a new building at the rear of the premises.

Students at the Nursing College said they feared moving freely on the premises because the dilapidated structure could collapse anytime, particularly during the rainy season. They urged the Telangana government to install barricades and take measures to prevent further damage to the building for their safety.

item.title: HMDA, HCCB to supply 600 KL of treated water daily for ORR greenery
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority and Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages will supply up to 600 KL of treated water daily from the Avinya facility to irrigate plantations and green spaces along a Medchal stretch of the Outer Ring Road
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) and Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB) will supply up to 600 KL of treated water daily from its Avinya facility to irrigate plantations and green spaces along an identified stretch of Hyderabad’s Outer Ring Road in Medchal.

"The initiative aims to promote water reuse, reduce dependence on freshwater and support sustainable urban greening. The water will undergo multi-stage treatment, stringent quality checks and continuous monitoring to ensure its suitability for non-potable uses. It will be transported by tanker to a designated HMDA receiving point", a press release said.

HMDA Director of Urban Forestry and OSD for BPP (in-charge) Rohith Gopidi said the collaboration would facilitate the use of treated water in HMDA-managed green spaces and further the authority’s commitment to expanding urban greenery and sustainable development across Hyderabad.

item.title: INCOIS to double ocean monitoring network after India joins global alliance
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Hyderabad-based INCOIS will double its Indian Ocean monitoring network after India joined the Ocean Eye International Alliance in Turkey, expanding ocean data-sharing, weather forecasting, disaster preparedness and sea-safety capabilities.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Scientists in Hyderabad will soon track twice as much data on ocean conditions, weather shifts and sea hazards in the Indian Ocean after India formally joined the Ocean Eye International Alliance, a global marine-monitoring alliance, in Turkey on Saturday, INCOIS said.

The Hyderabad-based Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) will lead the expansion under the Ocean Eye International Alliance for the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS).

INCOIS Director T.M. Balakrishnan Nair announced India’s entry alongside fellow new members Albania and the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) during a session, ‘Ocean, Seas, Nature, and Land Use Day’, at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya.

As the country’s main hub for ocean data, cyclone tracking and tsunami alerts, INCOIS will execute India’s new pledges to the alliance, which is co-chaired by the European Union and Canada.

Under the new roadmap, India plans to double its current network of ocean sensors and tracking systems across the Indian Ocean to plug critical data gaps. INCOIS and other Indian agencies will share technical know-how, including tracking Essential Ocean Variables (EOVs), following global data standards, managing complex ocean data and researching tropical ocean patterns.

Addressing delegates at the event, Nair said GOOS is essential for accurate weather and climate forecasts, disaster preparedness and safety at sea. “We must work collectively to make the Global Ocean Observing System more resilient and fit-for-purpose for both national and regional operational delivery,” he said.

Mercator Ocean tie-up

In a separate development at the event, Pierre Bahurel, chief executive officer of Mercator Ocean International, announced a formal cooperation agreement between Mercator and INCOIS.

He said the tie-up would link regional digital ocean systems and cross-check marine data, helping scientists build next-generation “Digital Twins of the Ocean” — virtual models used to test and predict how oceans respond to climate shifts.

item.title: Mega job mela in Gachibowli on November 25 to feature 50 companies
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: A mega job mela with more than 50 companies will be held in Gachibowli on November 25, offering jobs across sectors to freshers and experienced candidates, with selected applicants receiving offer letters on the spot.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A mega job mela offering employment opportunities in various sectors, including non-IT fields, will be held at Aura Convention Lawn Gardens, opposite Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU), Telecom Nagar, Gachibowli, from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. on November 25.

More than 50 companies will offer opportunities to freshers and experienced candidates. Candidates with Class 10, Intermediate, degree and postgraduate qualifications are eligible to participate, irrespective of their year of passing.

Job seekers from all districts of Telangana and other states can attend the recruitment drive. Companies will issue offer letters on the spot to selected candidates.

For further details, interested candidates can contact 8374315052.

item.title: Red inscriptions found at ancient habitation site near Manchirevula
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Hyderabad groups identified red-coloured inscriptions on a boulder wall near Manchirevula Forest Trek Park, with Kotha Telangana Charitra Brundam president Sriramoju Haragopal dating remnants to first-century Brahmi and seventh-century Telugu-Kannada scripts.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Members of the Kotha Telangana Charitra Brundam, Save Rocks, Climate Front Telangana and friends have identified red-coloured inscriptions, rather than rock paintings, on a boulder wall beneath a rock shelter at an ancient prehistoric human habitation site.

The site is on a hill adjacent to the Ghar-e-Mubarak Dargah hill, near the Manchirevula Forest Trek Park, where rock art and Paleolithic tools were previously discovered.

Kavali Chandrakanth, a member of the Kotha Telangana Charitra Brundam, identified the site containing the inscriptions. Sriramoju Haragopal, president of the Kotha Telangana Charitra Brundam, Mir Omar Ali Khan, vice-president of Climate Front Telangana, Siddhartha, and Dr Sudhir Bhanu of Save Rocks inspected the site to decipher the writings.

Haragopal identified the surviving remnants of the faded script as first-century Brahmi script and seventh-century Telugu-Kannada script. In the past, the Brundam identified several label inscriptions and stray letters ranging from Brahmi to Telugu-Kannada scripts alongside rock paintings at rock-art sites including Pandavulagutta, Wargal and Seethammaloddi.

“What makes this discovery particularly significant is the presence of actual inscriptions rather than just rock paintings, spanning from the 1st-century Brahmi script to the 7th-century Telugu-Kannada script,” Haragopal said.

item.title: Car gutted after collision with truck on ORR near Kokapet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: A car caught fire and was gutted after colliding with a truck on the Outer Ring Road near Kokapet in Narsingi on Friday. Its two occupants escaped unhurt, while police began an inquiry.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A car was gutted after it caught fire following a collision with a truck on the Outer Ring Road (ORR) near Kokapet, Narsingi, on Friday.

According to reports, the car was travelling from Shamshabad towards Kokapet when it rammed into a truck moving ahead. Soon after the collision, the car caught fire and was engulfed in flames.

The two occupants managed to get out of the vehicle in time and escaped unhurt. No major injuries were reported in the incident.

Traffic movement on the stretch came to a temporary halt due to the incident. Police reached the spot and took up an inquiry into the accident. The cause of the collision and the fire is yet to be established.

item.title: Hyderabad Odissi Utsav 2026 to be held at Shilparamam on November 22
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: The fourth edition of Hyderabad Odissi Utsav 2026 will be held at Shilparamam amphitheatre in Hitec City on November 22. The festival will bring dancers, students, teachers and institutions together to celebrate Odissi through solo, duet and trio performances. Guest artist
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The fourth edition of Hyderabad Odissi Utsav 2026 will be held at the Shilparamam amphitheatre in Hitec City on November 22, from 10 am to 8.30 pm.

Hyderabad Odissi Utsaav is an initiative aimed at bringing together Odissi dancers, students, teachers and institutions from Hyderabad and other parts of the country on a common platform to celebrate the grace, beauty and rich cultural heritage of Odissi.

“The festival provides a unique opportunity for different Odissi schools and dance institutions to come together under one roof, fostering artistic exchange, mutual encouragement and a sense of community,” said Preeti Mohapatra.

Performances will be presented in three categories — Solo, Duet and Trio. Mohapatra said nearly 80 dancers from Hyderabad participate in the celebration every year. She said a distinguished Odissi dancer from outside the State will attend as the guest artist.

item.title: Sridevi Women’s Engineering College celebrates silver jubilee in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.category: Telangana State Council of Higher Education
item.description: Sridevi Women's Engineering College celebrated its silver jubilee in Hyderabad, unveiling a souvenir on its 25-year journey, honouring long-serving staff and hosting cultural performances, including a musical programme by playback singer Geetha Madhuri.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Sridevi Women's Engineering College (SWEC) celebrated its silver jubilee, marking 25 years of empowering women through education.

Chief guests Professor Dr V. Balakista Reddy, Chairman, Telangana State Council of Higher Education, and Richard King Chatragadda, Regional Head-Academic Alliances, TCS, along with SWEC management members — Chairperson K. Jyothi Devi, Vice Chairman Dr K. Radhakishan Rao, Dr K. P. Srinivas Rao, Dr K. Manjeera and K. Deepa — unveiled a souvenir book reflecting SWEC's 25-year journey.

The celebrations included the felicitation of teaching, non-teaching and supporting staff who had completed 25 years of service, followed by cultural performances by students.

The evening concluded with a performance by playback singer Geetha Madhuri, who enthralled the audience and kept them on their toes with her soulful music.

item.title: Mancherial farmers oppose NH 63 alignment, allege forcible land acquisition
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Farmers in Mancherial district have opposed land acquisition for the NH 63 greenfield highway, alleging coercion and violations of land acquisition laws. They want the alignment changed, while NHAI officials maintain that the project follows prescribed norms.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: Farmers alleged that their agriculture lands were forcibly being acquired for laying NH 63 from Nizamabad to Jagdalpur of Chhattisgarh.
A 131.8 kilometer-long six-lane green field highway between Mancherial and Nizamabad district was initially sanctioned at an estimated cost of Rs 3,000 crore under Bharatmala Pariyojana scheme way back in 2016. The revised estimated cost is Rs 5,354 crore. As many as 1,433 acres were identified to be acquired in 17 villages in Luxettipet and Hajipur of the district for forming the road network.

Farmers from the two mandals accused the officials of asking them to sign on white papers expressing their interest to give their lands, openly flouting the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013. They have been staging protests and rasta-rokos, besides waging a legal battle opposing the project.

V Shyamsundar, a land loser from Hajipur regretted that their views were not gathered as mandated by the Act. He charged that the revenue officials were forcing the farmers to give their lands for creation of the road network. He lamented a uniform compensation was being extended to the farmers and land losers were meting out gross injustice.

The farmers recalled that their lands were already acquired for the Sripada Yellampalli irrigation project. They bemoaned that their lives would be thrown out of gear if their lands were acquired for the national highway. They opined that the existing road could be converted into a six-lane stretch without needing to take agriculture lands for the Greenfield highway.

The land losers argued that the NHAI was moving ahead even as the matter was being heard by Telangana High Court. They cited that the court recently cancelled the notification and stayed earlier alignments. They sought the court to intervene in changing the alignment of the bypass, citing loss of livelihood.
NHAI officials clarified that they were not violating norms while forming the national highway. They said that steps were being taken to cross legal hurdles faced by the project. They informed that the union cabinet committee recently gave its nod to a proposed alignment. They expressed confidence that the HC would deliver its verdict supporting the altered alignment.

  • Project: NH 63, six-lane Greenfield express highway
  • Length: 131.8 kms
  • Estimated cost (Rs): 5,354 Cr
  • Land to be acquired: 1,433 acres
  • Districts: Nizamabad, Jagtial, Mancherial

item.title: CERT-In warns of AI-driven cyberattacks targeting business payment systems
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: CERT-In has warned that cybercriminals are using AI-powered tools to manipulate business payment workflows and divert funds. Attacks are increasingly targeting technology service providers, government-linked payment processes and platforms handling vendor payouts, besides banks and financial institutions.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has flagged that cyber-attacks have extended beyond banks and financial institutions to technology service providers supporting government entities’ payment processes and other platforms handling vendor or partner payouts.

Cybercriminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence-powered tools to manipulate business payment workflows and execute unauthorised transactions, targeting crucial programming languages such as Java or PHP, which support 70 per cent of the internet.

“Recent observations by CERT-In show that unauthorised financial transactions involving business payment systems are not limited to BFSI entities but also affect technology service providers supporting government-linked payment processes and platforms handling vendor or partner payouts,” CERT-In said in a recent advisory.

Unlike traditional attacks that target payment applications’ programming interfaces (APIs), targets have increasingly shifted to altering business records or approval processes that determine whether payments should go through, allowing them to divert funds through “legitimate payment processes.”

Earlier in November, CERT-In had warned that hackers are using AI to breach the live systems of Indian non-banking financial corporations, fintech companies and payment aggregators to steal money.

As these transactions often use trusted systems and established procedures, the activity is difficult to detect immediately.

“The concern is not limited to the security of payment APIs. A transaction may pass the usual application and approval checks even when the records used to initiate it have been changed without authorisation,” the advisory said.

CERT-In has also observed the use of an “AI-driven agentic offensive framework” (AOF) to target enterprises, service providers, government organisations, and academic and research institutions.

It flagged the use of multiple agents or automated workers to undertake reconnaissance, privilege discovery and other intrusion tasks in parallel.

“AOFs allow several intrusion tasks to be carried out with less manual effort and can shorten the time between reconnaissance and subsequent attack stages. Organisations should account for such activity when reviewing their exposure, access controls and monitoring arrangements, irrespective of the sector in which they operate,” CERT-In said.

item.title: Bhavika Ahire to lead India U19 women against England in five-match T20 series
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The BCCI has named Bhavika Ahire captain of India's 15-member Under-19 women's squad for a five-match T20 series against England. The November 26-December 6 series in Vadodara and Surat will serve as preparation for the 2027 World Cup.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) on Saturday announced the 15-member India Under-19 women’s squad for the upcoming five-match T20 series against England, naming Bhavika Ahire captain and Anaadi Tagde vice-captain.

The T20 series will be played in Vadodara and Surat from November 26 to December 6 and will serve as preparation for the ICC Under-19 Women’s T20 World Cup 2027, scheduled to be held in January.

The series will begin with the first T20 at Vadodara on November 26, followed by the second match at the same venue on November 28. Both matches will be played at 6 PM and 1 PM, respectively.

The action will then move to Surat, where the remaining three matches will take place on December 1, 3 and 6. The third and fourth T20Is will begin at 6 PM, while the final match is scheduled for a 1 PM start.

The series will be an important opportunity for the young Indian side to assess its combinations and build momentum ahead of the global tournament.

India are the two-time defending champions of the ICC Under-19 Women’s T20 World Cup, having won the inaugural edition in South Africa in 2023 before retaining the title in Malaysia in 2025. The team will aim to continue its dominance and make it three consecutive world titles in 2027.

The England series comes after the Indian U19 team recently featured in a T20 tri-series at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. India were divided into two teams, A and B, with both sides registering three wins and one defeat each, while Nepal failed to win a match.

The second edition of the Women’s Under-19 T20 Asia Cup is also likely to be held in the UAE from December 8 to 20, with Dubai a possible venue. India are the defending champions of the continental competition, having won its inaugural edition in Malaysia in 2024.

The 2027 ICC Under-19 Women’s T20 World Cup will be jointly hosted by Bangladesh and Nepal from January 21 to February 6. The tournament will feature 16 teams competing across 41 matches.

India U19 squad: Bhavika Ahire [C] [WK], Ira Jadhav, Nidhi Mahto, Purva Siwach, Mehek Narwase, Maitri Maniar, Ishwari Awsare, Deeya Yadav, Shreya S Chawan [WK], Samaira Raghav, Kumari Palak, Uma Kashvi, Achsah Parmar, Anaadi Tagde [VC], Palak Singh

item.title: Revanth Reddy’s ‘stray dog’ remark triggers backlash within Congress
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy's stray dog remarks targeting critics have triggered discontent within the Congress. A section of party leaders defended MLAs who raised allegations of corruption and discrimination in fund allocation, questioning the Chief Minister's response to internal criticism.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s ‘stray dog bitten’ remarks targeting a few Congress leaders have triggered a backlash within the party, with a section of leaders, particularly those from the ‘original’ Congress, coming out in defence of the critics.

Since the Chief Minister too made these remarks at a public meeting, questions are being raised whether the TPCC Disciplinary Committee will initiate any action, as taken in the past against a few leaders.

Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy, Jadcherla MLA J Anirudh Reddy and former Minister Konda Surekha’s daughter Konda Sushmitha have leveled serious allegations against the Chief Minister. They accused the Chief Minister and his family of being involved in various irregularities and alleged rampant corruption in the government.

“Sitting in the Chief Minister’s chair, do not offer Telangana’s valuable resources to contractors and thieves,” Rajgopal Reddy said while speaking to media persons here on Friday.

He also alleged that funds were being sanctioned liberally to the Chief Minister’s Kodangal constituency while other constituencies were being discriminated against. He urged the Chief Minister to stop targeting Opposition parties and introspect on whether his government was providing corruption-free governance.

Jadcherla MLA Anirudh Reddy also levelled similar allegations, claiming that contracts were being awarded to contractors from Andhra Pradesh. He further alleged that officials were demanding bribes to clear bills worth Rs.5 lakh for road works.

Former Minister Konda Surekha was dropped from the Cabinet after her daughter Konda Sushmitha accused the Chief Minister and his brothers of involvement in land deals and irregular land allocations.

Irked by these allegations, the Chief Minister, without naming anyone, remarked that a few leaders in the party appeared to have been bitten by stray dogs. He said they would be taken to Erragadda (Institute of Mental Health) for treatment by the Congress workers. He made the remarks at a public meeting in Siddipet.

However, the comments have not gone down well with a section of Congress leaders, particularly those who have remained loyal to the party for years.

“What wrong did Rajgopal Reddy or Anirudh Reddy say? They pointed out corruption and the lack of development funds for their constituencies. Is it a sin to question a Chief Minister?” asked a senior leader from Gandhi Bhavan.

The leader recalled that former Chief Minister late YS Rajashekhara Reddy had also faced criticism from leaders within his own party on various issues.

Despite hailing from Kadapa, former Minister DL Ravindra Reddy was openly critical of YS Rajashekhara Reddy. However, the former Chief Minister never made derogatory remarks against him or treated him badly, another senior leader pointed out.

“An MLA has every right to question the Chief Minister over funds and projects. Otherwise, there is no purpose in getting elected. Making derogatory remarks against legislators for demanding funds and development projects out of frustration is unacceptable,” the senior leader observed.

item.title: Jaishankar thanks Bulgaria for helping repatriate Indian seafarers from Black Sea
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar thanked Bulgaria for helping repatriate Indian seafarers affected by Black Sea attacks and caring for the injured. During talks in New Delhi, both sides reviewed bilateral cooperation and discussed trade, defence, technology and India-EU ties.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: External Affairs Minister (EAM) S. Jaishankar on Saturday thanked the Bulgarian government for its support in facilitating the repatriation of Indian seafarers affected by attacks in the Black Sea and providing care to those injured.

In his opening remarks, during his meeting with Bulgarian Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova-Chamova in New Delhi, EAM Jaishankar first extended condolences over the loss of life in a recent road accident in Bulgaria and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

“And before we speak about our ties, let me first extend our condolences again to the families who lost their loved ones in the tragic road accident a week ago, and wish a speedy recovery to the injured. I also want to take this opportunity to thank you for the support that your government has extended for the repatriation of our seafarers in the ships that were attacked in the Black Sea and for looking after some of them who had sustained injuries,” the EAM stated.

Recalling his visit to Sofia in June this year, EAM Jaishankar said it had helped inject fresh momentum into bilateral relations.

“I recall my own visit to Sofia in June this year, and that visit, I think, was very helpful in giving new energy and impetus to our relationship. So today we have a chance really to assess the progress in our ties and look at areas from trade and investment to defence, education, science and technology, AI, space, tourism, and mobility,” he stated.

The External Affairs Minister said that the two sides had finalised a detailed roadmap for cooperation, setting out a clear direction for future engagements between India and Bulgaria.

He also thanked Bulgaria for its support towards strengthening India-European Union (EU) ties, adding that the upcoming free trade agreement would provide fresh momentum to the relationship, particularly in trade, technology and talent.

“Our teams have drawn up a detailed roadmap of cooperation, so we will be approving that today, and I think that will give a very clear pathway to our activities ahead. At this time, of course, your visit takes place when we are also intensifying our relationship with the European Union, and we again thank you for all the support that you have extended to that process,” the EAM stated.

“The entry into force of the free trade agreement, which we expect soon, I think, will certainly provide a new dynamism to that relationship. And when it comes to trade, technology, talent, we expect to do much more with Europe,” he added.

The External Affairs Minister also highlighted the growing India-EU cooperation, including the signing of a security and defence partnership and a framework on mobility. He further noted that both sides had concluded negotiations for Horizon Europe and held the seventh India-EU Strategic Partnership Review Meeting.

Emphasising the broader partnership between India and Bulgaria, EAM said, “So, whether it’s our bilateral context, our European context, or indeed our multilateral relationship, where we have a long, close history of working together, there is a very firm foundation on which today we can take our ties forward.”

item.title: Crypto investors approach ED, CBI over alleged losses linked to WazirX, Binance
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Thousands of cryptocurrency investors have reportedly approached the ED and CBI over alleged losses linked to WazirX and Binance. Their complaints raise questions about ownership, fund security, the 2024 cyberattack, frozen assets and the Singapore-based restructuring process.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Thousands of cryptocurrency investors have approached central investigative agencies, including the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), alleging that crypto exchanges WazirX and Binance caused significant financial losses to them, as per multiple reports.

Reports claim that complaints submitted by investor groups and users have reported alleged unauthorised access to accounts and loss of crypto assets.

Regulatory authorities have been unable to take decisive action due to the absence of a comprehensive legal framework governing cryptocurrency-related frauds in India, they added.

The petitioners said WazirX, which had marketed itself as one of India’s largest and most secure cryptocurrency platforms with around 16 million registered users, operated for several years while maintaining business links with global crypto exchange Binance.

Investors claim that Binance, which announced the acquisition of WazirX in 2019, benefited from the rapid growth of India’s cryptocurrency market and generated substantial revenues through trading activity and token-related business.

However, they alleged that questions over the ownership of WazirX emerged after enforcement authorities in India began scrutinising the platform and issued notices under foreign exchange regulations in 2022.

According to the complaints, Binance subsequently stated that it did not own WazirX, while WazirX’s user agreement continued to reference Binance as a wallet service provider for users’ crypto assets, the reports said.

The petitioners contend that these developments created confusion among customers regarding responsibility for safeguarding user funds.

The investors further alleged that after a major cyberattack on WazirX in July 2024, the exchange proposed measures that effectively distributed losses across both affected and unaffected users.

Users whose holdings were not compromised in the breach also faced restrictions on access to their assets, according to them.

The complaints also questioned WazirX’s decision to seek court approval in Singapore for a restructuring scheme through its Singapore-based entity, Zettai Pte Ltd.

Petitioners argued that the move made it more difficult and costly for predominantly Indian users to challenge decisions affecting their investments.

However, trading on the WazirX platform remained suspended for an extended period following the cyberattack, preventing users from accessing or trading their holdings during periods of market volatility, the reports said.

Meanwhile, some investors alleged that they missed significant gains in certain cryptocurrencies while their assets remained frozen.

The petitioners have also challenged claims that users recovered most of their holdings under the restructuring process, asserting that the actual recovery levels for some investors were substantially lower than publicly communicated figures.

item.title: Ian McKellen praises Johnny Depp’s performance in ‘Ebenezer’
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Ian McKellen has praised Johnny Depp's portrayal of Ebenezer Scrooge in the film ‘Ebenezer’. McKellen, who plays Jacob Marley, also discusses his longstanding connection with Charles Dickens' works and the adaptation's return to the story's ghostly origins.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Acclaimed actor Ian McKellen, who essays the role of Jacob Marley in the reimagining of Charles Dickens’ timeless classic ‘Ebenezer’, has spoken about the movie and actor Johnny Depp’s portrayal of the titular character.

Reflecting on the actor’s performance, he said in a statement: “When I realized that he would be playing Scrooge, I was very happy indeed. Johnny gives a performance the like of which you’ve never seen before, but that’s what you expect of Johnny Depp, isn’t it?”

For McKellen, taking on the role of Marley was also an opportunity to revisit his lifelong association with the works of Charles Dickens.

“That’s played out in all sorts of ways,” the actor said.

“I live in the East End of London, which Dickens knew well. One of the first parts I ever played in a regional company was David Copperfield and I went on to appear in several other productions. Another visit to Dickens is part of a pattern that I am very happy to repeat.”

The opportunity to be part of an adaptation of A Christmas Carol that revisits the story’s roots as a chilling ghost story was another exciting aspect for McKellen.

Reflecting on his approach to playing Marley, he says: “The trick of playing a ghost is not to play a ghost, but to be as real as possible. That makes it all the more scary. His chains are a metaphor for all the misery that he inflicted on others during his life. He’s actually trying to keep Scrooge from the same fate.”

Believing that audiences’ fascination with A Christmas Carol remains timeless, McKellen is confident that this adaptation will offer a memorable cinematic experience.

“It’s been adapted for the stage and in film on many occasions,” he concludes.

“This time, we’ve got a superb actor in the lead and a ghost story that you will believe in. Laughter, tears, surprise, shock — the audience will feel all of that in this film. A man on a wayward path morally sees what he’s done wrong, repents his ill behavior and discovers the joys of generosity and friendship and love. That is as happy an ending as you could possibly want.”

It also stars Andrea Riseborough, Sam Claflin, Robert Strange and Tramell Tillman, who play pivotal roles in this fresh take on Charles Dickens’ beloved ghost story.

Directed by Ti West, the film features a screenplay by Nathaniel Halpern, based on Charles Dickens’ beloved novella A Christmas Carol. It is executive produced by Ti West, Adam Bohling, David Reid, Stephen Deuters, Jason Forman, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Molly Smith, Thad Luckinbill, Trent Luckinbill and produced by Emma Watts.

Produced by Paramount Pictures, Ebenezer is now playing in cinemas across India.

item.title: Ravana glorified in ‘Ramayana’, revoke censor certificate of film and stop its screening: VHP
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: New Delhi: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad demanded revocation of Ramayana’s censor certificate and an immediate halt to screenings, alleging the film glorified Ravana and distorted events from Maharishi Valmiki’s epic.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday demanded that the censor certificate granted to the film Ramayana be revoked and its screening stopped immediately, alleging that its makers had made a malicious attempt to glorify demon king Ravana.

Days after the film’s release, VHP general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra expressed outrage over the alleged distortion of several facts from the original Ramayana, as narrated by Maharishi Valmiki, the inclusion of “fabricated” incidents and the deliberate omission of several important characters in the film based on the epic.

In a statement, Bagra said the film attempted to promote a political narrative by playing with the religious sentiments of more than one billion Hindu devotees of Lord Ram.

He said episodes such as the redemption of Ahalya, the friendship of Nishadraj Guha and the devotion of Kevat, which are integral to the universal character of Lord Ram, had not been mentioned in the film.

“Instead, the great mission of Lord Ram to eliminate demons who were enemies of society and obstructed sages and saints in their spiritual practices, yajnas and gurukuls has been portrayed as a personal struggle driven by revenge for the abduction of his wife,” Bagra said.

Bagra alleged that the film attempted to create a political narrative by glorifying the arrogant Ravana as a liberator of the oppressed.

“Ravana, despite attaining the pinnacle of knowledge, devotion and power, was immoral as he terrorised and oppressed every living being in creation, driven by arrogance. This has been unequivocally described in every version of the Ramayana,” Bagra said.

The VHP general secretary said the film had deeply hurt the sentiments of millions of Hindus who have deep faith in Lord Ram and the Ramayana, a tradition established over several millennia.

He said such distortions of the Ramayana, which establishes moral values and principles governing individual, family, social and political conduct, amounted to an attack on the ethical foundations of society.

“Society will never accept such attempts to play with the sentiments of the Hindu community,” Bagra said.

Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The first part of the two-part cinematic adaptation was released worldwide on November 5.

item.title: GTA VI sets entertainment record with 3.79 billion usd in first-day sales
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79 billion in estimated worldwide retail sales on its first day, setting an entertainment launch record. Rockstar Games also reported 32.5 million pre-release sales, with the game surpassing its predecessor's opening performance.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Action-adventure video game Grand Theft Auto VI has generated $3.79 billion in global sales within 24 hours of launch, ranking as the biggest entertainment release ever and breaking the previous benchmark held by its predecessor, “Grand Theft Auto V”.

Developer Rockstar Games said the title sold 32.5 million units through pre-release and launch-day purchases after the game ‌was received with massive fanfare and critical acclaim globally.

GTA VI’s launch-day haul is nearly five times the estimated $800 million its predecessor—GTA V—made on its launch day in 2013.

The new launch has also crossed the lifetime worldwide box-office earnings of “Avengers: Endgame”, which grossed about $2.94 billion globally.

GTA VI follows criminal protagonists Lucia and Jason Blitz in the fictional Vice City and Rockstar Games founder and president Sam Houser described the launch as the beginning of a ‘new chapter’ for the studio.

Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar Games’ parent company, is also the publisher behind other hits such as the “Red Dead Redemption” franchise and the “NBA 2K” basketball series.

Gamers worldwide have reportedly taken paid time off from work and even signed “contracts” with their partners to get uninterrupted game time.

Take-Two has spent nearly $1 billion in production costs for GTA VI, making it one of the most expensive entertainment projects and the game began pre-orders in June but has remained secretive about the sales numbers.

The game’s promotional trailer, “GTA VI: An Extended Look”, released in August, drove a sixfold jump in pre-orders, according to multiple reports.

Investors are keen on details on a PC version and the rollout of GTA Online for the new title, with some industry analysts forecasting both in 2027. The online, multiplayer component of the videogame is key to creating recurring revenue from the acclaimed title.

item.title: BRS MLA Kaushik Reddy alleges 1,029 pensions discontinued in Huzurabad, challenges Revanth
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS MLA Padi Kaushik Reddy alleged that 1,029 Cheyutha pensions had been discontinued in Huzurabad and challenged Chief Minister Revanth Reddy to prove new pensions were sanctioned. He also accused the Congress government of misleading people over pension claims.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS MLA Padi Kaushik Reddy on Friday alleged that 1,029 Cheyutha social security pensions had been removed in his Huzurabad constituency, as against the Congress government’s claims of providing new pensions. He challenged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to prove that even one new pension had been sanctioned in the constituency.

“I will apologise and resign to MLA post if the ruling Congress proves that beneficiaries increased in Huzurabad. Revanth Reddy should to resign if his claims about new pensions were proved false,” he said.

Addressing a press conference at Telangana Bhavan, Kaushik accused the Congress government of misleading people by claiming to have issued new pensions. He said the BRS government under K Chandrashekhar Rao enhanced pension amount and provided 45 lakh pensions every month.

He held Revanth Reddy responsible for drought condition in the State, suspecting that the Chief Minister pledged on the deities. “The Gods and the Godesses must be angry over his false promises and showing their anger without rainfall,” he said. He also criticised the Chief Minister’s language and conduct during public meetings.

item.title: Hyderabad: Langer Houz police books Reshma Don for alleged extortion, trespass
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Langer Houz police registered a case against Reshma alias Reshma Don for allegedly trespassing into a house, demanding money, threatening a family and harassing Munawwar. Police took her into custody.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Langer Houz police registered a case against Reshma alias Reshma Don for allegedly trespassing into a house, attempting to extort money and threatening a family.

According to police, the complainant alleged that Reshma had been harassing her family and regularly demanding money. She allegedly took money from the complainant’s brother, Munawwar, on several occasions. When he refused to pay further money, Reshma allegedly trespassed into their house and threatened the family. She also allegedly followed and harassed Munawwar.

Based on the complaint, police registered a case against Reshma under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and took her into custody.

Police have previously registered several cases against Reshma Don at various police stations across the city.

item.title: Telangana govt sanctions Rs.2.30 crore for Anabheri Prabhakar Rao memorial park
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana government has sanctioned Rs.2.30 crore for developing Anabheri Prabhakar Rao Memorial Park and Hall at Mohammedapur in Husnabad. The decision follows criticism over the memorial's poor upkeep and a proposal submitted after inspections by tourism corporation engineers.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: After criticism from different sections over the poor upkeep, the State government sanctioned Rs.2.30 crore towards development of Anabheri Prabhakar Rao Memorial Park and Hall at Mohammedapur, Husnabad.

Anabheri Prabhakar Rao was a freedom fighter and popularly known as Telangana Bhagat Singh. He was born in Polampally, Karimnagar district and was involved in revolutionary activities against the Nizam of Hyderabad. He died on March 14, 1948.

A memorial was developed at Mohammedapur village but there were complaints over its dilapidated condition.

The Telangana Tourism Development Corporation Limited informed to the government that Husnabad Fort houses Maisamma temple, which attracts many devotees during Dasara festival. The bastion is currently in dilapidated condition and requires restoration and development as a temple tourism destination.

Accordingly, the engineering team of TGDTC inspected the sites and prepared estimates for Rs.2.30 crore. After examining the proposal, the government sanctioned the amount to TGDTC towards development of Anabheri Prabhakar Rao Memorial Park and Hall at Mohammedapur.

item.title: Student found dead in Hyderabad; family alleges denial of leave led to suicide
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Hyderabad police registered a case after an Intermediate first-year student was reported dead Friday night. Family members alleged leave denial for a family function left the student distressed, as protesters demanded action.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Police registered a case and began an investigation after an Intermediate first-year student was reported dead on Friday night.

Family members alleged that the student had sought permission from the college principal to attend a family function but the request was denied. They alleged that the student was distressed over the denial of leave and subsequently died by suicide.

Student union members and the student’s relatives staged a protest following the incident, demanding action. Police rushed to the spot and dispersed the protesters.

Police said the body was shifted to Osmania General Hospital for postmortem examination.

Those in distress can call Tele-MANAS at 14416.

item.title: TG SAFE suspends licences of four Hyderabad eateries, shuts two others
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TG SAFE suspended licences of four Hyderabad eateries and closed two others operating without licences after inspections found unhygienic conditions. Officials collected eight suspected adulterated food samples and seized or discarded about 135 kg of food articles.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) has suspended the food safety licences of four eateries and ordered them to stop operations immediately. Two other establishments were closed for operating without licences.

Eight teams comprising Food Safety officers and police personnel inspected nine eating establishments, including restaurants, caterers and a men's hostel, following consumer complaints, officials said.

The establishments inspected were The Spice Kitchen in Kukatpally, Raju Gari Biryani in Chaitanyapuri, Swaad Spicy in Nagole, Madhapur Bawarchi in Ayyappa Society, Mehfil Restaurant in Balkampet, Annapurna Caterers in Chandanagar, Mataam Al Yamani Arabian Restaurant and Al Kareem Bakers in Tolichowki, and Sri Lakshmi Luxury Men's Hostel in Gowlidoddy.

Officials said they found several violations, including unhygienic kitchens, cockroach and housefly infestation, clogged drains, damaged flooring, dirty walls, greasy chimneys and improper segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food items in refrigerators.

Officials collected eight food samples on suspicion of adulteration and seized or discarded approximately 135 kg of food articles.

The licences of Madhapur Bawarchi, The Spice Kitchen, Mataam Al Yamani Arabian Restaurant and Annapurna Caterers were suspended, with instructions to immediately stop business operations.

Officials said The Spice Kitchen had rat droppings in its storeroom, cockroach infestation, improper segregation of food items and damaged kitchen tiles. Madhapur Bawarchi had greasy floors and walls, cockroach infestation and unhygienic refrigeration facilities.

At Mataam Al Yamani Arabian Restaurant, officials found heavy cockroach infestation, pest activity in food articles, damaged flooring and flaky walls. They also detected the use of synthetic food colours in prepared food items.

At Annapurna Caterers, officials found cobwebs, pest activity, smoke-stained walls, an untidy grinding area and unhygienic ice-cream storage boxes. The establishment also lacked mandatory medical, food testing, water testing and pest control records.
