Al Kareem Bakers in Tolichowki and Sri Lakshmi Luxury Men's Hostel in Gowlidoddy were closed for operating without FSSAI licences in unhygienic conditions.

TG SAFE will issue show-cause notices to Raju Gari Biryani and Swaad Spicy for serious violations, besides the two establishments that were closed. An improvement notice will be served on Mehfil Restaurant, which will be reinspected to verify compliance with food safety norms, officials said.

item.title: INS Sahyadri arrives in Vietnam for three-day goodwill visit
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: INS Sahyadri arrived at Vietnam's Da Nang port for a three-day goodwill visit aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation. The engagement follows a Vietnamese military delegation's visit to Pune and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval's recent trip to Vietnam.
item.content:encoded:
Hanoi: In a move to boost maritime cooperation between India and Vietnam, the Indian Naval Ship (INS) Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city of the Southeast Asian nation for an operational turnaround.

In a post on X on Saturday, the Indian Embassy in Vietnam posted: “The ship was accorded a warm welcome by the Vietnam People’s Navy and local authorities. The visit reaffirms our shared commitment to peace, stability and security in the region and in the Indo-Pacific.”

INS Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city on Friday for a three-day goodwill visit aimed at deepening defence ties and strengthening naval cooperation between India and Vietnam, local media reported.

The Indian Navy frigate was accorded a warm welcome by local authorities, the city’s armed forces and the Naval Region 3 Command.

The Indian Naval ship, with 294 officers and sailors aboard, will remain in Da Nang until November 22 as part of its goodwill visit, Vietnamese newspaper SGGP reported.

As part of the engagements, the Indian Navy delegation will meet the leadership of the Da Nang City People’s Committee and the Naval Region 3 Command. The two navies will also participate in sports exchanges involving their officers and personnel.

The crew will additionally explore the city’s historical and cultural attractions. The visit is expected to promote greater mutual understanding and trust between the two naval forces and deepen defence cooperation between the two countries.

Earlier this month, a four-member delegation of the Vietnam People’s Army visited the College of Military Engineering (CME) in Pune, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme.

The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions.

“Strengthening India-Vietnam Defence Cooperation. A four-member delegation of the Vietnam People’s Army visited the College of Military Engineering (#CME), Pune, from 03 to 05 November 2026, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme,” the Indian Army posted on X.

“The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, HADR and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. The engagement further strengthened professional ties, mutual understanding and bilateral military cooperation between India and Vietnam,” it added.

Recently, National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval was on an official visit to Vietnam, where he called on Vietnamese President To Lam and thanked him for his ‘steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership’.

item.title: Yashveer Goud to lead Hyderabad in Cooch Behar Trophy match against Chandigarh
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: V Yashveer Goud will captain Hyderabad in their Cooch Behar Trophy match against Chandigarh from November 26 to 29. Yashveer was part of India's Under-19 Asia Cup-winning squad, although he did not feature in the final playing XI.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: V. Yashveer Goud will lead Hyderabad in the Cooch Behar Trophy match against Chandigarh in Chandigarh from November 26 to29.

Yashveer was a member of the Indian team which won the Asia Cup (under-19) recently and involved in those animated gestures against the Pakistani palyers after India clinched the thrilling final in Oman. He was not part of the playing eleven.

The team: V Yashveer Goud (capt), Aditya Vardhan (wk & vice-capt), Shaik Rehaan Roshan, T. Shiva Rama Krishna, Palli Prince, Ram Charan Markatta, Aditya Javvaji (wk), M. Durga Ujwal, A. Ved Reddy, Hari Om Singh, Dev M Mehta, S. Nipun Reddy, Ayush Malhotra, ParthSharma and Aditya Malhotra.

Stand-byes: NC Arjun, Arhaan Satwalekar, Jashwanth Mote (wk), B. Hishanth Prem Charan, Tanay Jaddu, Naaka Ritesh, Ishan Narayan Reddy and P. Charan Teja.

item.title: Telangana gram panchayats’ finances shrink under Congress rule
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana's gram panchayats recorded a sharp fall in average receipts and expenditure in 2024-25, according to an RBI report. Receipts dropped to Rs 4.42 lakh per panchayat, while grants and own-source revenue also declined, deepening the fiscal strain.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Rural Telangana took a severe beating under the Congress government with the gram panchayats’ finances moving from surplus to deficit. The average receipts and expenditure plunged in 2024-25 under the Congress government, exposing the financial strain on rural local bodies less than a year after the change of regime.

The Reserve Bank of India’s “Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions – Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India” report shows average receipts per panchayat falling from Rs 16.72 lakh in 2022-23, the last full financial year under the BRS, to Rs 14.38 lakh in 2023-24, which included the change of government in December 2023, and just Rs 4.42 lakh in 2024-25. The latest figure was about one-fifth of the all-India average of Rs 21.3 lakh for the three-year period.

Average expenditure followed the same trajectory, with Rs 16.59 lakh in 2022-23, Rs 15.43 lakh in 2023-24 and Rs 6.24 lakh in 2024-25. In neighbouring Andhra Pradesh, average spending rose from Rs 8.52 lakh to Rs 16.42 lakh during the corresponding the period.

The figures do not, by themselves, establish how much of the decline resulted from policy decisions by either government. But the scale of the contraction in 2024-25 raises questions on the Congress government’s management of rural local finances. The supplied estimate attributes the fall to a 62 per cent reduction in fund allocations over the three years, as the RBI report also identified delayed grants and delays in holding local body elections as possible factors.

The deterioration is not confined to spending. Telangana panchayats’ average own-source revenue through local taxes and non-tax collections, also declined from Rs 2.36 lakh per panchayat in 2022-23 to Rs 1.96 lakh in 2023-24 and Rs 1.62 lakh in 2024-25. Meanwhile, grants from the Centre and the State fell from Rs 14.34 lakh to Rs 12.41 lakh and Rs 2.80 lakh, respectively.

Telangana retained a comparatively strong tax component within its own revenue as taxes accounted for 53.6 per cent, against 60.4 per cent in Andhra Pradesh. The RBI report said Telangana, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu have a more balanced mix of own-source revenue instruments. Yet this relative strength has not insulated the State’s panchayats from falling receipts or their dependence on government transfers.

The RBI’s panel covered 11,025 of Telangana’s 12,994 gram panchayats, or 84.8 per cent. Nationally, panchayats recorded average annual receipts of Rs 21.3 lakh and expenditure of Rs 21.5 lakh per panchayat over the three-year period. Grants accounted for nearly 90 per cent of their total income, recommending stronger local revenue mobilisation and tax collection.

The shift from surplus to deficit places Telangana among a group of States whose panchayats saw their financial position worsen between 2022-23 and 2023-24. While panchayats in Andhra Pradesh and several other States moved from deficit to surplus, Telangana went in the opposite direction under the Congress rule.

For rural local bodies, the consequences are immediate with less room to maintain infrastructure and deliver basic services. The RBI has called for stronger financial powers, adequate funds and better administrative capacity. The Congress government’s challenge is to reverse the contraction and restore predictable funding to panchayats, rather than leave them dependent on delayed transfers and shrinking receipts.

RBI’s “Finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions – Local Finances and Capacity Building in Rural India” report

Average per-panchayat figures (Rs lakh)

Financial indicator ==== 2022–23 ==== 2023–24 ==== 2024–25

Total receipts ========== 16.72 ====== 14.38 ====== 4.42

Expenditure ============= 16.59 ====== 15.43 ====== 6.24

Own-source revenue ====== 2.36 ====== 1.96 ====== 1.62

Centre and State grants== 14.34 ====== 12.41 ====== 2.80

item.title: How Do I Open an Online Bank Account in India With Zero-Balance Requirements?
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Before applying, compare account features, eligibility conditions, charges and interest rates to find an option that suits your needs.
item.content:encoded:
Opening a bank account online can make everyday banking more convenient, especially if you want to avoid minimum balance requirements. A zero-balance account allows you access essential banking services without having to maintain a minimum balance. Before applying, compare account features, eligibility conditions, charges and interest rates to find an option that suits your needs.

What Is a Zero-Balance Savings Account?

A zero-balance account is a savings account that does not require you to maintain a mandatory minimum balance. It can be useful for students, first-time account holders, salaried individuals and people with irregular income.

However, zero balance does not automatically mean every service is free. Debit cards, optional services and certain transactions may carry charges. Some digital accounts also have specific eligibility criteria or transaction limits until full KYC verification is completed.

Documents Required to Open an Account Online

The following documents and details may be required to open an account:

  • PAN (Permanent Account Number): For identity and KYC verification.
  • Aadhaar details: Wherever applicable, for identity verification and digital onboarding.
  • Registered mobile number: For OTP verification and account alerts.
  • Email address: For application updates and electronic statements.
  • Recent Photograph and signature: If required by the bank.

Requirements vary by bank and account type. Keep your details consistent across documents and apply only through the bank’s official website or authorized mobile application.

Steps to Open a Zero-Balance Account Online

Follow these steps to complete your application:

  1. Choose a bank account: Compare eligibility, charges, digital facilities and the applicable savings account interest rates.
  2. Visit the official website or app: Select the zero-balance savings account option.
  3. Enter your details: Provide your name, date of birth, contact information and other requested details.
  4. Complete identity verification: Submit the required PAN and Aadhaar details and follow the instructions for OTP verification or video KYC.
  5. Review the account terms: Check transaction limits, card charges, interest conditions and any initial funding requirements.
  6. Activate your account: Follow the bank’s instructions after your application is approved.

For example, Kotak 811 offers a digital zero-balance savings account for eligible resident Indian individuals aged 18 or older. Applicants can use PAN and Aadhaar details and complete video KYC online, subject to the bank’s conditions.

Compare Interest Rates and Account Features

Although avoiding a minimum balance is important, the account should also suit your everyday banking needs. Compare savings account interest rates, debit card facilities, digital transfers, ATM limits and service charges before choosing a product.

Some banks use progressive interest slabs, meaning different portions of your balance earn different rates. The highest advertised rate may therefore apply only to a particular portion of your savings.

IDFC FIRST Bank also offers the Quantum+ Savings Account, which has no minimum Average Monthly Balance (AMB) requirement and monthly credits. The account can be opened only through the IDFC FIRST Bank mobile app. Its interest rates depend on the balance slab, so review the current rate schedule before deciding whether the account suits your savings goals.

Understand the Account’s Limitations

Before completing your application, check whether the account has restrictions that could affect how you use it.

  • KYC requirements: Some accounts require video KYC or additional verification before all features become available.
  • Transaction limits: Digital accounts may impose limits until verification is complete.
  • Service charges: Physical debit cards, replacement cards or optional services may cost extra.
  • Account eligibility: Some products are available only to resident individuals and may exclude existing customers.
  • Minimum balance rules: Confirm that the selected product has no mandatory minimum balance rather than assuming every digital account is zero-balance.

Reviewing these conditions helps ensure that your zero-balance account remains suitable after activation.

Conclusion

Opening a zero-balance account online can simplify banking while helping you avoid minimum balance penalties. Compare account features, documentation requirements, charges and interest terms before applying. Choosing a suitable account can make everyday transactions easier while keeping your savings accessible.

FAQs

1. Can I open a zero-balance account entirely online?

Yes. Many banks offer digital applications, subject to eligibility and successful KYC verification.

2. Is PAN required to open an account?

If you have a PAN, you must provide it when opening an account. If you do not have a PAN, you must submit form 97.

3. Does a zero-balance account earn interest?

Yes, eligible savings accounts may earn interest according to the bank’s applicable rates and conditions.

4. How can I compare interest rates?

Check each bank’s official rate schedule, applicable balance slabs and interest credit frequency.

5. Can a zero-balance account have transaction limits?

Yes. Some accounts impose limits based on product terms or the stage of KYC verification.

item.title: India take 118-run lead over New Zealand as KL Rahul scores 136 and Shubman Gill misses century by two runs
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.category: India vs New Zealand first Test
item.description: KL Rahul's 136, Shubman Gill's 98 and Devdutt Padikkal's 80 powered India to 486/4 against New Zealand on day three of the first Test. Rishabh Pant remained unbeaten on 55 as India secured a 118-run lead.
item.content:encoded:
Wellington: Captain Shubman Gill fell two short of a hundred in the last over of the day while wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant struck a rapid half-century as India reached 486/4 in 125 overs and took a 118-run lead over New Zealand at stumps on day three of the first Test here at the Basin Reserve on Saturday.

Pant, playing his first match after recovering from a side strain, was unbeaten on 55 off 62 balls at stumps, laced with five fours and two sixes, with nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj yet to get off the mark.

Earlier, KL Rahul made 136 off 290 balls, his first century in New Zealand and second-highest Test score in eight years, while Devdutt Padikkal smashed 80 off 175 balls. Gill had looked set to become India’s second centurion of the day until Jacob Duffy found a way through at the stroke of stumps.

Duffy’s delivery nipped back between bat and pad and hit Gill’s off-stump after deflecting off the pad. That dismissal ended a 146-ball knock of 98 for Gill that included nine fours and two sixes, with his flick and pull being standout shots.

Gill had reached his fifty off 68 balls after tea by pulling Duffy for six to put India into the lead. That shot also made India’s top four the first side to all cross 50 in a first innings of a Test in New Zealand. Rahul hit Duffy for six before dragging a wide one from Nathan Smith onto his stumps, and got a standing ovation from the crowd after playing a marathon knock.

Gill had a stroke of luck on 67 when umpire Richard Illingworth adjudged him out lbw off Smith. He reviewed with three seconds left on the timer after checking with Pant, and although the New Zealanders were convinced they saw a gap between bat and pad, Sonic showed a spike.

The decision was overturned and the Basin Reserve crowd booed. New Zealand had already wasted a review on Pant, whose attempted pull had come off his shoulder. Pant took his time to settle in – scoring 15 runs off his first 37 balls. Then he cut loose by carting Duffy for six, six and four in an 18-run over that pushed India’s lead past 100.

The left-hander brought up his 22nd Test fifty off 55 balls by charging at Duffy and pulling him wide of mid-on for four. He and Gill had just completed a century stand when the Indian captain fell. India’s top four all went past 80, only the 12th such instance in Test history and the first in New Zealand.

New Zealand burnt their last review on an lbw shout against Kamboj in the final over. Duffy, who has bowled seven of New Zealand’s 14 front-foot no-balls in the match, finished with 1-181, as India completed a productive batting day to take control of the match.

Brief Scores: New Zealand 368 in 121 overs (Henry Nicholls 175; Jasprit Bumrah 4-92) trail India 486/4 in 125 overs (KL Rahul 136, Shubman Gill 98; Kyle Jamieson 1-57, Nathan Smith 1-65) by 118 runs

item.title: Telangana Government presses ahead with Global Summit despite appeals for postponement
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana government is preparing for Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 at Bharat Future City from December 7 to 9 despite opposition over the claimed water and power crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Congress government is continuing elaborate preparations for the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 (ITGS 2026), despite calls from various sections to postpone it over what they described as a water and power crisis in the State.

The three-day ITGS 2026 will be held at Bharat Future City from December 7 to 9. The government is planning a much bigger event this year than the previous edition.

The summit is planned to have six expo hangars, compared with a single expo hall in 2025. The total exhibition area is set to increase from 27,500 square metres to 72,250 square metres. More than 60,000 square metres of exhibition space is proposed across 12 sectors and pavilions.

An Advisory Council comprising around 200 eminent leaders from more than 25 sectors has been invited to anchor the plenary sessions. The event will feature 52 sector sessions, six expo hangars, nine events and pavilions.

The summit will also feature Raksha Expo, an acrobatic airshow, IndiaJoy 2026, Creators Corner, the Pharma and Life Sciences Expo and several other events.

However, resident welfare associations, Telangana NRIs and members of the Telangana People's Coalition for El Nino Crisis have opposed the conduct of ITGS 2026. They have written open letters to Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, urging him to reconsider the decision.

In a letter to the Global Summit Advisory Council, members of the Telangana People's Coalition for El Nino Crisis said the government had declared a severe drought and water crisis in 365 mandals across 31 districts due to El Nino conditions.

Despite the situation, the State government had decided to host the Invest Telangana Global Summit at Bharat Future City from December 7 to 9, the letter said.

The letter recalled that the Chief Minister had publicly compared the El Nino crisis to the Covid-19 pandemic. It said he had warned of an acute drinking water and power shortage until July 2027 and advised farmers to give up water-intensive crops.

Public policy expert Donthi Narasimha Reddy criticised the government for proceeding with the event.

"This is a personal propagation exercise. An attempt is being made to build political capital at the people's cost," Narasimha Reddy said.

He alleged that the government was not serious about addressing people's hardships or reviewing its policies. He also criticised legislators for failing to take up public issues with the government.

"Considering the global economic situation, how will the government convince investors, and how fruitful will this exercise be? There is an El Nino crisis, and the Global Summit could have been organised next year," Narasimha Reddy said.

The State government had claimed that the 2025 summit attracted investment announcements worth more than 69 billion US dollars. The event drew over 10,000 delegates and more than 500 global and national companies from over 44 countries. It also saw the signing of over 75 strategic MoUs.

However, the government has not yet made public the status of these investment proposals and MoUs.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said the upcoming Global Summit would lay a strong foundation for the country's growth by attracting substantial domestic and international investments.

Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju is reviewing invitations sent to national and international dignitaries, industry leaders, investors and other prominent personalities, along with the confirmations received so far. He has directed officials to closely monitor invitations and confirmations and ensure proper coordination with all invitees.
