item.title: Allu ArjunAllu Arjun pens adorable birthday wish for daughter Allu Arha, calls her the joy of his life
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Allu Arjun wished his daughter Allu Arha on her birthday, calling her the joy of his life. The actor's upcoming film ‘Raaka’, directed by Atlee, also made headlines after setting a Guinness World Record for motion capture.
item.content:encoded:
Chennai: One of India’s top stars Allu Arjun on Saturday penned an adorable birthday wish to his daughter Arha, in which he called her the joy of his life.

Taking to his X timeline to post a cute picture of him with his daughter, the Telugu star wrote, “Happy birthday to the Joy of My Life #AlluArha.”

The makers of Arha’s debut film as an actor, ‘Shakuntalam’, too wished the little star a very happy birthday on Saturday.

Guna Handmade Films took to its X timeline to post a birthday wish for Arha. It wrote, “Wishing our little star Allu Arha a very Happy Birthday! May your days always be filled with endless smiles, happiness, and magical moments. #HappyBirthdayAlluArha #AlluArha #gunaateamworks #GunaHandmadeFilms #shaakuntalam.”

Meanwhile, Allu Arjun has a number of big projects lined up including his magnum opus ‘Raaka’, which is being directed by Tamil director Atlee.

The film had, only a couple of months ago, been in the news for setting a world record for “Most People Motion-Captured in Real-Time”. What made the accomplishment even more commendable was that the film had achieved this feat, even before its release

Sun Pictures, which is producing the film, had taken to its social media timelines to make the announcement.

It wrote, “HISTORY MADE! A global triumph that takes Indian cinema to the world stage! #Raaka sets a Guinness World Record for the “Most People Motion-Captured in Real-Time”, with 37 performers captured simultaneously! ”

It went on to add, “Mr. Allu Arjun and Mr. Atlee received the Guinness World Records certificate, marking this historic achievement. @alluarjun @Atlee_dir @GWR #Raaka #AlluArjun #Atlee #GuinnessWorldRecords.”

The announcement came on a day director Atlee celebrated his birthday.

Allu Arjun, who greeted Atlee on his birthday, had said that he was looking forward to creating more magic with the ‘Raaka’ director.

item.title: US reports 5,838 measles cases in 2026, loses elimination status along with Mexico and Bolivia
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The United States has reported 5,838 measles cases in 2026, its highest annual total since 1991. The country, along with Mexico and Bolivia, has lost measles elimination status after sustained transmission of the virus was re-established in all three countries.
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles: The United States had reported 5,838 confirmed measles cases in 2026, with the number continuing to rise, according to the latest data released by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The cumulative case count is the highest annual total in the United States since 1991.

As of Thursday, of the total, 5,820 cases were reported across 47 US jurisdictions, while 18 cases were reported among international visitors to the United States, the CDC said on Friday (local time).

A total of 646 patients, or about 11 per cent of confirmed cases, have been hospitalised, reports Xinhua news agency.

About 96 per cent of the cases involved people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status was unknown, according to the CDC.

Pennsylvania, one of the hardest-hit states, had recorded 1,631 confirmed cases and eight measles-associated deaths as of Friday.

The CDC recommends two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine as the best protection against measles. However, CDC data show that MMR vaccination coverage among US kindergartners has declined in recent years.

Meanwhile, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced Tuesday that the United States, Mexico and Bolivia have lost their measles elimination status after sustained transmission of the virus was re-established in the three countries.

The announcement followed a meeting of the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission from November 10 to 13, during which the commission reviewed the latest epidemiological situation across the Region of the Americas.

PAHO said in a statement that the commission concluded that the same measles virus genotype and lineage had circulated uninterrupted for 12 months or more in each of the three countries, meeting the criteria for the re-establishment of endemic transmission.

The commission recommended withdrawing the three countries’ measles elimination status, and PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa accepted the recommendation, PAHO said.

The Region of the Americas became the first WHO region to eliminate measles in 2016. It regained its regional measles elimination status in 2024 after endemic transmission was interrupted in Venezuela and Brazil. However, the region lost its verification as free from endemic measles transmission in November 2025, following the re-establishment of sustained transmission in Canada.

“The subsequent loss of elimination status by Bolivia, Mexico and the United States marks a further deterioration in the regional situation and makes the path towards restoring elimination more challenging,” PAHO said.

PAHO urged countries across the Americas to strengthen vaccination, disease surveillance and outbreak response. It said sustaining at least 95 per cent coverage with both doses of the measles vaccine in every community is essential to closing immunity gaps and preventing further transmission.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition airstrikes kill 41 in Yemen as Houthis claim attacks on Saudi facilities
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: At least 41 people, including 11 children, were reportedly killed in Saudi-attributed airstrikes across Yemen, according to Houthi media. The Houthis claimed retaliatory attacks on a Saudi power plant and port, while the coalition reported intercepting two missiles.
item.content:encoded:
Sanaa: At least 41 people, including 11 children and seven women, were killed in airstrikes attributed to Saudi Arabia across Yemen over the past 24 hours, Houthi-run al-Masirah TV reported, as the Houthis claimed strikes on a power plant and port in southwestern Saudi Arabia.

Citing health authorities in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, the broadcaster Friday (local time) said 28 others, including three children, were injured in the attacks, without providing details on the locations.

The figures could not be independently verified, and there was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities.

Also on Friday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said in a statement that the group targeted the Al-Shuqaiq power plant and Jazan port in Saudi Arabia’s Jazan region, claiming “direct and precise hits” and extensive damage.

The claims could not be independently verified.

Sarea said the attacks were in response to reported Saudi strikes on power stations in Yemen’s northern Saada province and the Red Sea city of Mocha, as well as an attack earlier Friday on Hodeidah port, reports Xinhua news agency.

He warned that further strikes on Yemeni ports or power facilities would trigger “immediate retaliation” against similar Saudi facilities.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles targeting Jazan, and that shrapnel fell in the Al-Shuqaiq area, where relevant authorities were responding.

The coalition did not provide details on casualties or material damage.

The developments come amid intensifying fighting between the Houthis and government forces supported by the Saudi-led coalition, with both sides exchanging attacks across multiple fronts.

In recent days, the Houthis have claimed repeated missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and other strategic targets, while Houthi media have reported intensified Saudi airstrikes on residential areas and infrastructure across Yemen.

Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, prompting Saudi-led military intervention in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

item.title: Putin wants talks to end Ukraine war, says Trump
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed a desire in Shenzhen to end the Ukraine war diplomatically, but announced no ceasefire, negotiations date or terms for Kyiv.
item.content:encoded:
Washington: US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin told him in Shenzhen that he wanted a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine.

Trump, who met Putin on Thursday after addressing leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in China, said the Russian leader had “clearly expressed his desire to see the war between Russia and Ukraine end by diplomatic means”. Trump announced no ceasefire, date for negotiations or terms that Moscow was prepared to offer Kyiv.

At a White House news conference after returning from Asia, a reporter asked how Trump could be sure Putin was acting in good faith, saying the Russian leader had left their meeting and launched another deadly assault on Ukraine. Trump stood by his assessment and said the United States was trying to help both sides find a way to end the war.

He identified hostility between Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as a particular obstacle. “The problem is President Zelensky and President Putin have tremendous hatred, and it's never easy,” he said.

Trump said he had initially thought the war would be among the easier conflicts for him to settle. He said he had since spoken to US representatives involved in the diplomatic effort and believed an agreement was still possible. He put the monthly death toll at about 25,000, most of them soldiers, but gave no source for the estimate.

Asked separately whether he considered Putin a friend of the United States, Trump confined his answer to his own dealings with the Russian leader. He said it was in the American interest for a president to be able to speak directly to the head of a country with one of the world’s largest nuclear arsenals.

Trump cited his first administration’s decision to supply Ukraine with Javelin anti-tank missiles in response to criticism that he was too accommodating towards Moscow. On current US weapons supplies, he said European buyers paid for American equipment and passed much of it on to Ukraine.

Ukraine also came up when Chinese President Xi Jinping joined Trump and Putin for a three-way meeting in Shenzhen. Trump said the leaders discussed how to stop the killing. The specific undertaking he reported from that meeting concerned nuclear weapons. China, he said, had agreed to talks with Washington and Moscow on reducing nuclear risk. He described no agreement among the three on Ukraine.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, eight years after seizing and annexing Crimea. Zelenskyy, who took office in 2019, has led Ukraine throughout the full-scale war. The supply of Javelin missiles cited by Trump dates to his first term, when Ukrainian forces were already fighting Russian-backed separatists in the east of the country.

item.title: Hong Kong Open 2026: Satwik-Chirag lose to Malaysia’s Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun in semifinals
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: India's Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty crashed out of the Hong Kong Open 2026 after losing to Malaysia's Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun in the men's doubles semifinals, ending their campaign with a straight-games defeat.
item.content:encoded:
Kowloon: India’s men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty saw their run at the Hong Kong Open 2026 come to an end after suffering a straight-games defeat to Malaysia’s eighth-seeded combination of Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun in the semifinals.

The fifth-seeded Indian duo went down 18-21, 19-21 in 40 minutes in an error-strewn display, despite entering the contest with a 4-1 head-to-head record against their Malaysian opponents.

The first game was a battle between the two pairs and they traded points until Malaysians edged ahead 17-12 thanks to several remarkable exchanges. Satwik and Chirag fought their way back and after a few effective defensive strokes from Satwik, they were even at 17-17.

But Man and Tee held firm in the final moments to claim first game 21-18.

Indians began second game brightly and went up 7-3, aiming to force a tiebreak. But a few errors at net by India enabled the Malaysian pair to creep up and draw even.

With the set all square, Man and Tee seized the moment to dominate the game 21-19 and qualify for the final.

Their victory in the quarter-finals read 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 in favour of the Indian duo. They suffered a loss in the second game but returned strongly to win the third and reach the semi-final.

Satwik and Chirag made a flying start, taking 6-3, then 9-6, and 11-7 to the first interval. The pair kicked off the second game on a high and moved further ahead at 15-10, before winning the game 21-12 in just 13 minutes.

The second game was a far closer contest as everything was level at 4-4 before the Indians got a slight advantage at 9-9. Hu and Lin took the game at 13-11 and increased the lead to 15-11 before closing it out 21-13.

Indians rallied back in the third game and had a 11-7 advantage at the breather. They continued to keep the winning run on and zoomed away to 15-9 and 17-10, and though the Chinese pair made a spirited effort to reduce the lead towards the end, Satwik and Chirag held their nerves to bag the game 21-16 and book a semi-final berth.

Meanwhile, the Malaysians will be up against the winners of the other semi-final between Leo Rolly Carnando and Daniel Marthin of Indonesia and Kang Min-hyuk and Lee Jongmin of Korea in the final.

item.title: Youth Congress Meta office attack: KTR condemns damage to Brand Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao alleged that a Youth Congress protest at Meta’s Gachibowli campus damaged Brand Hyderabad and investor confidence, while questioning Rahul Gandhi over the alleged vandalism.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao on Saturday accused the Congress government of damaging Hyderabad's reputation as a business destination after Youth Congress workers staged a protest at Meta's largest campus in Gachibowli, which he alleged was vandalised.

Led by Telangana Youth Congress president Jakkidi Shivacharan Reddy, the workers staged the protest against the suspension of the social media accounts of National Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma on Meta platforms.

Rama Rao said Brand Hyderabad fed millions of families across the country and had been built painstakingly over decades through several pro-business policies. He said Meta chose Hyderabad because of its assured safe working environment.

"Congress goons thought vandalising Meta's office in Hyderabad was cool. These idiots are even bragging about it. In three years of your governance in Telangana, did you bring even one big brand like Meta to Hyderabad?" he asked.

Rama Rao said the protest had undermined investor confidence. He also questioned Congress Lok Sabha leader Rahul Gandhi on whether protests and vandalism would attract companies to India.

"Rahul Gandhi, is goondaism your way of bringing companies to India? Yesterday's act didn't just break glass. It broke Brand Hyderabad's trust," he remarked.

item.title: Penelope Cruz announces upcoming film ‘Patricia’, her first narrative feature under Moonlyon
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Penelope Cruz has expressed excitement about ‘Patricia’, the first narrative feature from her production company, Moonlyon. Written by Juan Diego Botto, the film explores violence against women and marks Cruz’s first collaboration with Netflix Spain.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Penelope Cruz has expressed excitement about her upcoming film ‘Patricia’, which marks the first narrative feature film from her production company, Moonlyon.

Sharing the announcement on Instagram, Cruz said the project has been over two years in the making and praised her dear friend Juan Diego Botto for writing the screenplay.

Cruz wrote in the caption: “After more than two years developing what will be the first narrative feature from my production company, Moonlyon, and just about to start shooting, I feel enormous excitement. It has been a beautiful and intense journey alongside my dear friend Juan Diego Botto.”

She also described it as a necessary story highlighting the everyday violence faced by countless women and called it a privilege to portray the titular character. The film marks her first collaboration with Netflix Spain.

“Juan has written a wonderful script, and it is an honor to tell this story with him. PATRICIA is a very necessary story, and an immense privilege to play this character. Patricia represents so many other women who, like her, suffer this kind of violence every day.”

Cruz added: “I am also very grateful for the incredible response from Netflix in Spain. This is my first film with them, and we couldn’t be happier with the care and attention they have shown us. #patricia.”

Talking about Cruz, she has been feted with an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, a Grammy Award, three Goya Awards and a David di Donatello.

Cruz made her acting debut on television at age 16, and her feature film debut the following year in Jamon Jamon in 1992.

She was then seen in films such as Belle Epoque, Open Your Eyes, Don Juan, The Girl of Your Dreams, The Hi-Lo Country and Woman on Top. She has performed in seven films directed by Pedro Almodovar: Live Flesh, All About My Mother, Volver, Broken Embraces, I’m So Excited!, Pain and Glory, and Parallel Mothers.

She also produced several films she performed in, including Ma Ma and On the Fringe.

item.title: KT Rama Rao alleges rural neglect under Congress, cites RBI report
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao alleged that the Congress government neglected rural development, citing an RBI report that showed average gram panchayat expenditure fell from Rs 16.59 lakh in 2022-23 to Rs 6.24 lakh in 2024-25.
item.content:encoded:
Panchayat spending fell to Rs 6.24 lakh

Hyderabad: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao criticised the Congress government for allegedly neglecting rural development, citing a sharp fall in gram panchayat expenditure recorded by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

Rama Rao said panchayats spent an average of Rs 16.59 lakh each in 2022-23, during the BRS regime, but the expenditure fell to Rs 6.24 lakh in 2024-25 under Congress rule, according to the RBI report on Panchayati Raj finances.

In a post on X, Rama Rao claimed that public taxes and government borrowings were being diverted by the Congress leadership, leaving little for development and welfare. He claimed that development had stalled from villages to towns under Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.

item.title: Hyderabad: Two youths killed as motorcycle crashes into electricity pole at Uppal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Two youths were killed after their Yamaha FZ motorcycle crashed into the base of an electricity pole on a road divider at Uppal around midnight on Friday. Police identified the victims as Mohammed Munazir and Mohammed Salauddin.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Two youths were killed after their motorcycle rammed into the base of an electricity pole on the road divider at Uppal around midnight on Friday.

The victims were identified as Mohammed Munazir (34), who worked as a supervisor and was residing at Uppal, and Mohammed Salauddin (35), a worker from Bharuch in Gujarat who was currently staying at Uppal.

According to the police, Munazir was riding a Yamaha FZ motorcycle towards Nagole when he lost control of the vehicle and crashed into the base of an electricity pole located opposite Sri Pooja Glass Hardware shop.

Munazir, who was riding the motorcycle, and Salauddin, who was riding pillion, died on the spot due to the impact, said the police.

On receiving information, police rushed to the spot, registered a case and shifted the bodies to the mortuary at Gandhi Hospital for post-mortem examination.

Further details of the accident are awaited.

item.title: Fish waste to wealth: Telangana’s Gorrekunta shows the way
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: On World Fisheries Day, the Gorrekunta initiative demonstrates how discarded fish resources can be transformed into economic assets, creating livelihood opportunities for fisherwomen and promoting a sustainable circular rural economy
item.content:encoded:
By Pittala Ravinder

On World Fisheries Day, November 21, while governments, fisheries experts and fishing communities discuss the future of the fisheries sector, perhaps it is time to ask a different question: How much wealth are we throwing away after harvesting and selling fish?

Fish is a valuable source of nutrition, livelihood and economic activity. Yet, every day, fish markets across the country generate enormous quantities of discarded material in the form of fish heads, entrails, scales, bones, skin and other processing residues. Much of this material is dumped without proper treatment, creating foul odour, unhygienic conditions and environmental concerns.

But what if this so-called waste could become a source of additional income? What if the discarded portions of fish could be converted into organic fertilizers, compost and protein-rich animal-feed ingredients? And what if fishing communities, particularly fisher-women, could become entrepreneurs in this emerging field? An interesting experiment taking shape at Gorrekunta, near Warangal in Telangana, offers a possible answer.

Small beginning, larger vision

Approximately three years ago, an initiative was introduced at Gorrekunta to help local fisherwomen convert fish-market waste into useful agricultural products. With the initiative of this writer and the technical support of Prakriti Environment Society (PES), the Gorrekunta Fisher-women Cooperative Society began producing Fish Amino Acid (FAA) and organic fish compost on a small scale.

The process was relatively simple. Fresh fish waste was mixed with jaggery in equal quantities and allowed to ferment for approximately 45 days. The mixture was stirred regularly, after which the liquid was separated, filtered and bottled. The remaining solid material was retained for further processing into organic compost.

What began as a modest experiment gradually developed into an encouraging community-level activity. The fisherwomen acquired practical experience, farmers showed interest in the products and the initiative demonstrated that discarded fish material could be converted into economically useful agricultural inputs.

Laboratory testing of the existing Fish Amino Acid recorded 0.58 per cent nitrogen, 5.13 per cent calcium and 0.16 per cent potassium, along with zinc and trace minerals. The findings indicated a distinctive calcium-rich composition, although further technical improvements are necessary to enhance and standardise its nutrient profile.

The experience has now attracted the attention of the Warangal district administration. The District Collector and District Fisheries Officer, encouraged by local Parkal MLA Revuri Prakash Reddy, have responded positively to the proposal for expanding the small venture into a medium-scale commercial unit. The district administration has proposed allotting approximately two acres of land at Gorrekunta free of cost.

This is an encouraging development, particularly because it recognises the potential of a grassroots innovation and the entrepreneurial capabilities of local fisherwomen.

Three products, one resource

The proposed Gorrekunta project is not intended to remain confined to manufacturing liquid fertilizer and compost. Its larger vision is to develop an integrated fish-waste processing facility capable of recovering multiple useful products from the available raw material. The proposed unit will have an initial processing capacity of one tonne of fish waste per day and will focus on three principal products.

• Fish Amino Acid – Liquid agricultural input

Fish Amino Acid is obtained through controlled fermentation of fish material. It contains organic matter and nutrients that may support plant growth and soil biological activity. Its actual agricultural performance depends on its composition, quality and application.

With appropriate machinery, standardised fermentation, filtration and quality-control systems, the existing Gorrekunta product can be developed into a more consistent commercial agricultural input.

Research institutions can help improve the process through better fermentation techniques, enzymatic hydrolysis and appropriate formulation methods. The objective should be to develop a scientifically validated product rather than simply increase production.

• Organic fish compost—turning residues into soil wealth

The solid material remaining after the extraction of liquid FAA can be converted into organic fish compost. By mixing the residue with suitable agricultural waste and carbon-rich organic materials, followed by controlled composting and approximately six months of maturation, a valuable organic manure can be produced. This offers an opportunity to recover nutrients from discarded fish material while supporting farmers seeking alternative organic soil inputs.

• Fish protein powder—recovering nutritional wealth

The third product could open an entirely new avenue for fisheries-based entrepreneurship. Fish waste contains valuable proteins, particularly in the flesh, heads, skin and other protein-bearing portions. Through appropriate segregation, drying, grinding and processing, selected material can be converted into fish protein meal or powder.

An initial technical assessment of a dried fish-waste sample reported approximately 41 per cent crude protein. However, it also identified a high calcium-to-phosphorus ratio and potential microbial and heavy-metal concerns.

Therefore, the present powder cannot be recommended as a human dietary supplement. The immediate opportunity lies in developing a properly processed, tested and certified feed-grade product for aquaculture and animal-feed industries.

Institutions such as the ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (CIFT) and ICAR-Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture (CIFA) could provide valuable assistance in developing suitable processing methods, nutritional standards and quality-control protocols.

The three products offer different commercial opportunities and can diversify the income base of the proposed enterprise. However, all three cannot be produced by counting the same material twice. A scientific assessment must determine how much of the incoming fish waste should be allocated to fermentation, composting and protein recovery. Their respective yields and production economics must be established through pilot trials.

From waste disposal to a circular economy

The real significance of this initiative lies in its underlying philosophy. For decades, the fisheries sector has largely concentrated on increasing fish production, improving marketing facilities, providing cold storage, promoting exports and supporting fishermen’s livelihoods. These remain important priorities. But the next stage of development must also address what happens to the material left behind after fish is processed and marketed.

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) recognises circular-economy approaches as an important means of reducing losses and converting fish-processing by-products into useful products such as fishmeal, fertilizers, animal feed and other valuable resources.

The Gorrekunta proposal seeks to translate this principle into a practical community-owned enterprise. Its objective is to achieve maximum utilisation of collected fish-derived material. The liquid fraction will be processed into FAA, selected protein-rich material will be diverted for protein recovery, and suitable remaining solids will be converted into compost. Proper treatment and management of process water will also be essential.

In other words, the intention is to move from a waste-disposal approach towards a resource-recovery system. Such an approach can improve fish-market sanitation, reduce environmental nuisance, generate additional income and create new economic linkages between fisheries and agriculture.

An opportunity for fisherwomen, entrepreneurs

One of the most encouraging aspects of the Gorrekunta initiative is the central role assigned to fisherwomen. Women are actively involved in fish vending, cleaning, processing and marketing, but their participation in organised value addition and manufacturing remains limited in many places.

A properly supported fish-waste processing enterprise can provide them with an opportunity to move beyond traditional activities and become owners and managers of a manufacturing unit. The proposed two-acre facility could accommodate fermentation vessels, processing machinery, composting yards, drying equipment, packaging sections, storage facilities and a basic quality-control laboratory.

At a proposed intake capacity of one tonne per day and approximately 300 working days annually, the unit could handle around 300 tonnes of fish waste. The preliminary project estimate is Rs 1.50 crore, although the introduction of the fish-protein processing section will require a revised technical and financial assessment.

More importantly, the model need not remain confined to Gorrekunta. Similar enterprises could be established through fisherwomen cooperatives, fishermen’s societies, self-help groups and rural entrepreneurs in other fish-producing districts.

The availability of fish waste in local markets can provide the raw material, while agricultural and aquaculture enterprises can become potential customers for the finished products.

Role of scientific institutions

While the concept offers considerable promise, its commercial success will depend on scientific validation and professional management. The fermentation process must be standardised. Product quality must remain consistent. The compost must satisfy applicable organic-manure specifications. The fish protein product must meet the relevant feed-safety and nutritional standards.

Research institutions such as ICAR-CIFT, ICAR-CIFA, ICAR-CIFRI and ICAR-CIFE, along with agricultural and veterinary universities, can play an important role in this transformation. The National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), the Department of Fisheries, Government of Telangana, and the Union Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying should explore appropriate technical and financial support under applicable programmes.

The Agriculture and Horticulture Departments can facilitate field demonstrations and market linkages for FAA and compost, while aquafeed and animal-feed manufacturers can help evaluate the commercial potential of the protein product.

A phased approach, beginning with the proven small-scale experience and gradually introducing scientifically validated products, would minimise investment risks and improve commercial sustainability.

Let Gorrekunta become a national example

India’s fisheries sector has made remarkable progress in fish production, aquaculture, exports and infrastructure development. Yet, the potential of fish-waste utilisation remains an area that deserves much greater attention.

World Fisheries Day should not merely be an occasion to celebrate production achievements or discuss the welfare of fishing communities. It should also encourage fresh thinking, technological innovation and new avenues of income generation.

The Gorrekunta initiative offers an opportunity to bring these objectives together. It demonstrates how a discarded resource can become an economic asset, how fisherwomen can become entrepreneurs and how fisheries can establish productive linkages with agriculture and animal nutrition.

Perhaps the future of fisheries development should not be measured only by how much fish we produce and sell, but also by how intelligently we utilise every part of the resource we harvest. The fish we sell feeds people. The waste we recover can feed farms, support livestock and aquaculture, and generate new livelihoods. That is the larger promise of Gorrekunta.

From pond to farm, from waste to wealth – it is time to turn India’s fish markets into centres of resource recovery and rural entrepreneurship.

 

(The author is a senior journalist, Convener of the Singareni Affected Areas Research Community — SAARC and State Convener of the Telangana Astitva Vedika-TAV)

item.title: Cricket Australia backs Pat Cummins as Test captain
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Cricket Australia reaffirmed unanimous support for Pat Cummins as Test captain amid speculation linked to the 2018 South Africa ball-tampering controversy, and announced an independent forum for players and staff from that tour.
item.content:encoded:
Melbourne: Cricket Australia (CA) on Saturday reaffirmed its confidence in Pat Cummins continuing as Australia’s Test captain amid allegations surrounding the Sandpaper controversy.

It was widely speculated that revelations by former Australian opener Usman Khawaja in his autobiography about the ball-tampering episode during the 2018 tour of South Africa had made Cummins’ position as captain untenable.

“In the light of the ongoing speculation surrounding the Australian men's team tour of South Africa in 2018, the CA Board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian Cricket and the welfare of all concerned,” CA said in a statement.

CA chair David Boon and chief executive officer Todd Greenberg met Cummins and discussed several issues, including his welfare, the support required by the team and the forthcoming series against New Zealand in December.

“As part of this meeting, the Board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position,” the statement added.

After the meeting, Cummins reiterated his decision to continue as Australia’s Test captain.

“It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd on Friday. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly,” Cummins said.

“Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority,” he added.

Boon said Cummins’ “integrity” as captain had not been compromised amid the turmoil of the past few weeks.

“We’ve expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa.

“We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat’s integrity has been compromised,” he said.

Cummins also lauded Boon and Greenberg for guiding Australian cricket through a difficult period.

“David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018,” he said.

CA also announced that it would set up a forum for players and support staff from the 2018 tour of South Africa to help them share their views and recollections.

Cummins supported the initiative.

“I support the Forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what’s needed,” he added.

Boon shared his views on the forum for players and support staff.

“We are absolutely determined to steward Australian Cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn.

“That’s what the independent Forum we announced this week is about and the Board encourages all players and support staff to share and discuss their stories there. We will be publishing the Terms of Reference in due course,” he added.

item.title: India GDP growth projected at 7% for FY27
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: India’s real GDP growth is projected at approximately 7 per cent for FY27, supported by sustained public capital expenditure, resilient domestic demand and strong services activity, according to a new Brickwork Ratings (BWR) report released on Saturday.

However, persistent inflationary pressures are expected to keep monetary policy tight, with BWR anticipating a further 25-basis-point (bps) repo rate hike in December 2026, taking the policy rate to 5.75 per cent, followed by an extended pause.

“India’s growth momentum is increasingly being supported by the strength of its domestic economy and the resilience of its services exports. However, the external environment remains an important variable, particularly given India’s dependence on energy and other key imports,” said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings.

In the current environment, businesses with healthy balance sheets, adequate liquidity and the ability to manage input-cost volatility will be better positioned to navigate uncertainty, the report said.

For the broader economy, sustaining investment momentum while strengthening external resilience will remain important, Sharan said.

Government capital expenditure reached Rs 6.55 lakh crore in the first half of FY27, supporting infrastructure investment, the report said.

Services activity remained robust, with the Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rising to 55.8 in October and the Composite PMI reaching 56.2.

Industrial production grew 6.7 per cent in September, while manufacturing output expanded 7.6 per cent. October Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections also rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore, reflecting festive demand and higher import-related collections.

Capital goods and electrical equipment, automobiles, IT services and export-oriented sectors are relatively better positioned, the report said.

In contrast, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and housing finance companies face higher funding costs, according to the report.

Retail inflation accelerated to 6.09 per cent in October from 5.54 per cent in September, breaching the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) upper tolerance limit of 6 per cent.

Food inflation stood at 8.94 per cent, while wholesale inflation reached 11.39 per cent in September, indicating persistent price pressures.

The report expects Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation to peak at 5.8-6.1 per cent in Q3 FY27 before moderating towards 5.0 per cent in Q4, taking the FY27 average to 5.2 per cent.

item.title: Amit Shah to review projects, MHA matters during Arunachal visit
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to review development projects and MHA matters in Itanagar, attend police and cooperation programmes, and inaugurate an NDRF campus during his three-day Arunachal Pradesh visit.
item.content:encoded:
Itanagar: Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who arrived in Itanagar on Friday night on a three-day visit to Arunachal Pradesh, was scheduled to attend programmes on Saturday and today, including reviews of major development projects and matters concerning the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), officials said on Saturday.

Shah was received at Donyi Polo Airport in Itanagar on Friday night by Chief Minister Pema Khandu, Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein, other ministers, political leaders and senior government officials.

A senior official said Shah was scheduled to present the President's Police Colour, the highest honour bestowed on a police force in India, to the Arunachal Pradesh Police on Saturday morning in recognition of its distinguished service.

The ceremony was scheduled to be held at the Parade Ground of the Police Training Academy at Banderdewa in Itanagar. Shah was also scheduled to address the gathering.

On Saturday afternoon, Shah was scheduled to review major development projects in Arunachal Pradesh and chair another meeting on matters concerning the MHA and the Arunachal Pradesh government.

Both review meetings were scheduled to be held at Lok Bhavan in Itanagar. Chief Minister Khandu had earlier said Shah would also distribute appointment letters to newly recruited personnel of the police and forest departments and address the gathering.

Today, Shah, who also holds the Cooperation portfolio, will attend a Cooperative Conference at the Dorjee Khandu State Convention Centre in Itanagar.

During the conference, he will unveil the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperation Vision Document 2047, present Cooperation Awards and inaugurate the Saras Mela.

Shah is scheduled to inaugurate the 12th Battalion campus of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) at Hollongi in Itanagar this afternoon. He is scheduled to return to New Delhi this afternoon after completing his engagements in the strategically important border State, the official said.

Officials said elaborate security arrangements had been made in the State capital and Papum Pare district for Shah's visit.

The Papum Pare district administration has declared the entire district a no-fly zone from November 20 to 22 as a security measure.

District Magistrate Mamu Hage issued an order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, prohibiting the flying of all aerial devices during the three-day period.

The restrictions cover drones, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), balloons and all forms of aerial photography and videography across the district.

According to the order, the restrictions were imposed to prevent any disturbance, unlawful activity or potential threat to the safety and security of the VVIP during the visit.

Shah's visit comes as Arunachal Pradesh has witnessed a series of protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), planned across Siang, East Siang and Upper Siang districts.

The proposed mega hydropower project has emerged as a major political and public issue in the State over the past several months, with local residents and various organisations expressing concerns over its potential impact on the region.

Officials said Shah is also likely to hold discussions with leading organisations spearheading the protests against the proposed project.

Arunachal Pradesh shares a sensitive international border stretching 1,863 km with three neighbouring countries — China (1,126 km), Myanmar (520 km) and Bhutan (217 km).

Meanwhile, the Congress in Arunachal Pradesh has sought an assurance from Shah that the proposed 11,200-MW hydropower project would not be imposed on indigenous communities protesting against the proposed dam on the Siang river.

The Congress also said Shah should respond to several other issues, including alleged corruption in highway projects.

“The Congress Party will continue its nationwide mass campaign under the powerful slogans of ‘Vote Chor — Gaddhi Chor’ and ‘Samvidhan Bachao – Desh Bachao’.

“This movement is aimed at defending the sanctity of the electoral process, protecting the people's right to vote, safeguarding democratic institutions and upholding the Constitution of India,” the party said in a statement.

The Opposition party said Shah's visit should go beyond ceremonial engagements and official announcements, and provide an opportunity for the Centre to take concrete decisions and offer written assurances and time-bound commitments on issues affecting the State.

item.title: Trump seeks Huang’s Nvidia return; Says co-founder should apologise
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: US President Donald Trump urged Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang to apologise and return to the chipmaker, while saying Blackwell chips should stay out of China despite allowing sales of older technology.
item.content:encoded:
Says co-founder should apologise

Washington: US President Donald Trump said he wanted Jensen Huang to apologise and return to Nvidia, putting the chipmaker’s co-founder ahead of his own earlier choice for the job, Apple chief Tim Cook.

“I'd like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back,” Trump told reporters at the White House after returning from Asia. He said Huang had made some bad decisions but did not say what he wanted him to apologise for.

Trump brought up Huang while discussing which American chips he was prepared to let China buy. He credited Huang with developing Nvidia’s Blackwell chips and said few people at the company could do what Huang had done. He also said he had discussed Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping during his visit to Shenzhen. Xi, by Trump’s account, spoke highly of him.

Trump stood by his assessment of Cook as a good choice. But when it came to who should lead Nvidia, he said he wanted the company to give Huang another chance. He praised Huang’s technical judgement and questioned whether those now setting out the company’s plans could match his contribution.

“I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance,” Trump said.

On chip sales, Trump drew a distinction between Blackwell and older technology. He said he wanted to keep Blackwell out of China and would accept sales of older chips. He added that he would also be content if no American chips went to China.

Trump acknowledged an argument he attributed to Huang. China already makes its own chips, he said, and if American suppliers decline to sell to Chinese customers, domestic manufacturers will have a reason to develop replacements.

For now, Trump put the US lead over China in chipmaking at 10 years. He argued that Blackwell was too complex to copy. Yet he also predicted it would be obsolete in two years, by which time he said he would be less concerned about who could buy it. He announced no change to export rules.

Chips were one part of a wider discussion with Xi about artificial intelligence (AI). Trump said the two had agreed to work together on safeguards for the most advanced systems. He ranked the US first and China second in the field and said he saw little prospect of a third country catching either of them.

At home, Trump said he wanted American companies to build the data centres that run those systems in the US. He threatened a substantial tax on companies that chose sites overseas and singled out a proposed project in Finland. He did not name the company or give a tax rate. He said the US had previously allowed too much of its chip industry to move abroad.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993. The California company built its early business on graphics processing units for video games. The ability of those processors to handle many calculations at once later made them useful for training AI models, turning Nvidia into a major supplier to the companies that build and run them.

Blackwell is the name Nvidia gave a generation of chips designed for that work. Since 2022, Washington has used export controls to restrict China’s access to advanced computing chips. Those controls have made a chip’s capabilities a central factor in determining whether an American supplier can sell it to a Chinese customer.

item.title: Woman dies by suicide in Hyderabad after mother reprimands her over phone use
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 25-year-old married woman allegedly died by suicide at Hayathnagar after her mother reprimanded her for using a mobile phone. The woman reportedly made her two young children sit before a television before hanging herself. Police registered a case.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 25-year-old married woman allegedly died by suicide at Hayathnagar after her mother reprimanded her for using a mobile phone.

According to the police, Lakshmidevi, a native of Narketpally mandal in Nalgonda district, stayed at Hayathnagar. She was reportedly upset after her mother told her not to use the phone. She allegedly made her two children, a seven-year-old daughter and a three-year-old son, sit in front of the television before going into a room and hanging herself.

On receiving information, Hayathnagar police reached the spot and collected details. A case has been registered and an investigation is under way.

item.title: Trump says Democrats seek immigration talks
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Donald Trump said Democrats had contacted him for talks on immigration and health care, but gave no details on a deal or whether he would support allowing long-settled undocumented workers to remain in the US.
item.content:encoded:
Washington: US President Donald Trump said Democrats had contacted him about immigration and that he expected one of the first issues they would raise would be the fate of people who entered the United States illegally years ago and have since worked in the country.

Trump made the remarks when a reporter asked whether he would veto an immigration proposal backed by Republican Congresswoman Maria Salazar. He gave no direct answer on a veto or on whether he would support allowing long-settled workers to stay.

Instead, he drew a distinction between the people his administration was targeting for removal, including murderers and drug dealers, and those whose cases he expected Democrats to bring to him. He described the latter as “very hard working people that came in, in some cases years ago” and asked what should be done about them.

Trump declined to identify the Democrats who had called him. He said they wanted to discuss two subjects. “They want to talk to me about health care, and they want to talk to me about immigration,” he told reporters at the White House after returning from Asia.

Of the two, health care drew a clearer offer from the president. Trump said it might be easier to reach an agreement with Democrats than for Republicans to try to pass a measure on their own through budget reconciliation. On immigration, he outlined no terms for a deal and gave no date for talks.

Trump also disclosed that the governor-elect of Texas had called him on Thursday to discuss the border. He described the conversation as productive and said she wanted a strong border. He said he thought they could work together but gave no details of what either side had proposed.

The president defended his deportation policy throughout the exchange. He said his administration had focused on people who posed a danger to the public. In some cases, he said, he preferred to keep people convicted of serious crimes in prison because he feared they might return to the US after deportation.

Trump ranked the border among the two or three issues most important to his election.

In a separate exchange about working with the incoming Congress, Trump said he expected to use the threat of a veto to negotiate changes to bills that Democrats sent him. Asked about House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, Trump spoke favourably of both Jeffries and Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer. He did not identify either man as one of his callers on immigration.

Immigration debates in Washington often turn on two distinct questions. One concerns who may enter the country and how the government enforces the border. The other concerns people already living in the US, including those who have spent years working or raising families there. The question about Salazar’s proposal concerned that second group.

item.title: 1st Test: KL Rahul’s unbeaten century, Padikkal’s 80 puts India in charge
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: KL Rahul’s unbeaten 124 and Devdutt Padikkal’s 80 took India to 344/2 at tea on day three in Wellington, 24 runs behind New Zealand’s 368, with Shubman Gill unbeaten on 36.
item.content:encoded:
India 24 runs behind at tea

Wellington: KL Rahul struck his first Test hundred in New Zealand, while skipper Shubman Gill remained unbeaten on 36 as India reached 344/2 in 93 overs at tea on day three of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve on Saturday.

India added 105 runs in 27 overs in the second session for the loss of Devdutt Padikkal, who was bowled for 80 off 175 balls by Kyle Jamieson. India trail New Zealand's first-innings total of 368 by 24 runs.

Rahul was unbeaten on 124 off 265 balls, with nine fours and a six, while Gill was not out on 36 off 40 deliveries, with four boundaries.

New Zealand began the second session with a two-pronged plan. Jacob Duffy bowled short from around the wicket with wicketkeeper Tom Blundell pushed back, while Nathan Smith attacked the stumps.

Duffy struck Rahul on the right arm with a sharp short ball, but the opener pulled the next two deliveries for twos and then tapped one into the cover region in the 69th over to reach his hundred off 207 balls. Rahul pumped his fist, removed his helmet, made his customary gesture for his child and looked to the sky as the Indian dressing room rose.

Rahul became the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries. It was his 13th Test hundred, and he became the third Indian, after Sunil Gavaskar and Surinder Amarnath, to score a hundred in his first Test innings in New Zealand.

Two balls later, Padikkal, on 53, could not keep a cut down off Duffy and Henry Nicholls dropped a low chance at gully. Padikkal then danced down the pitch to loft Glenn Phillips over mid-on for four, while Rahul whipped the part-time off-spinner over mid-wicket for another boundary. In between, both batters needed attention from the physio for their right arms.

New Zealand took the second new ball soon after the drinks break. Jamieson, wayward at first, produced a delivery from around the wicket that held its line, beat Padikkal's outside edge and hit the top of off-stump. The delivery was similar to the one with which Akash Deep bowled Phillips on day two.

Padikkal's 165-run stand with Rahul came to an end. Rahul also became only the third Indian, after Rahul Dravid and Gautam Gambhir, to be part of two century stands in the same Test innings in New Zealand.

It was only the fourth time India had century stands for each of the first two wickets in a Test in a SENA country, after two such instances involving Gavaskar and one featuring Virender Sehwag.

Gill wasted no time in his first Test appearance in New Zealand, charging down the pitch to pull Jamieson for four. He took 15 off one Duffy over, cutting a boundary over backward point and pulling a no-ball to the fence.

The flurry contributed to India scoring 56 runs in 13 overs after the second new ball was taken, as the visitors won another session and set the stage to take the lead over New Zealand in the evening session.

Brief scores: New Zealand 368 in 121 overs (Henry Nicholls 175; Jasprit Bumrah 4-92). India 344/2 in 93 overs (KL Rahul 124 not out, Yashasvi Jaiswal 85; Kyle Jamieson 1-44, Matt Henry 1-70). New Zealand lead by 24 runs.

item.title: All aboard Air Niugini plane safe after emergency landing in Philippines
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: An Air Niugini Boeing 767 carrying 137 passengers and nine crew members made a safe emergency landing at Davao International Airport on Saturday after pilots reported a possible right-engine fire or sparks indication.
item.content:encoded:
MANILA: An Air Niugini plane carrying 146 passengers and crew from Hong Kong to Papua New Guinea made an emergency landing safely at Davao International Airport in a southern Philippine city on Saturday after an indication of possible sparks or fire in its right engine, Philippine aviation officials said.

There were no reports of injuries among the 137 passengers and nine crew members, who disembarked through emergency slides from the Boeing 767-383ER after it diverted from its route, the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines said.

The pilots reported detecting possible sparks or fire in the right engine through an indicator. They followed safety procedures and requested an unscheduled landing in Davao shortly after midnight, Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines spokesperson Eric Apolonio said, without elaborating. He added that an investigation would include the pilots' accounts.

The passengers and crew were taken to the airport terminal and provided assistance and hotel accommodation. There were no immediate reports of damage to the plane.

The Davao airport was closed to other flights to allow emergency response, resulting in the cancellation of two incoming domestic flights. It was reopened later after safety checks were completed on the main runway, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines.

item.title: ATP Finals semis are set: Alcaraz vs Shelton and Zverev vs Medvedev
item.dc:creator: AP
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz beat Flavio Cobolli in Turin to complete group play unbeaten and set up an ATP Finals semifinal against Ben Shelton, while Alexander Zverev will face Daniil Medvedev in the other last-four match.
item.content:encoded:
Turin: Carlos Alcaraz did not appear bothered by his various physical issues as he beat home player Flavio Cobolli 6-4, 6-1 at the ATP Finals.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion broke his Italian opponent’s serve in the opening game of both sets and ended points quickly.

Alcaraz had a huge 29-9 advantage in winners.

“I tried to play as aggressive as I can — hitting the ball as hard as I could, trying not to move that much,” Alcaraz said.

He had an elastic black band on his injured left thigh and a strip of tape on his right knee.

Alcaraz hurt his thigh in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev. He also missed four-and-a-half months — sitting out the French Open and Wimbledon — this year due to a right wrist injury.

“The challenge now is not on the court; it's off the court,” Alcaraz said, “to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape, to feel physically ready for tomorrow.

“It's going to be a really important half a day that I have ahead of me with my team, with my physio, with the doctor.”

Alcaraz had already secured a place in the semifinals against Ben Shelton at the elite eight-man event and completed group play with a perfect record of three wins. The semifinal will be a rematch of the US Open quarterfinal between Shelton and Alcaraz that ended at 3:33 a.m.

While Shelton won that five-set clash in New York, Alcaraz recently got revenge in the Paris Masters final.

In the other semifinal, top-ranked Alexander Zverev will face Medvedev, who beat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4.

The top four seeds advanced to the semifinals: Zverev (1), Alcaraz (2), Shelton (3) and Medvedev (4).

Cobolli’s Turin debut ended with three losses, while Tiafoe went 1-2 in his debut.

Alcaraz is attempting to win the trophy at the Finals for the first time. He lost to Jannik Sinner in the championship match a year ago.

Sinner ended his season early due to a right knee injury.

Alcaraz extended his winning streak to 12 matches after trophies in Vienna and Paris.

“The way that I felt on the court today was incredible,” Alcaraz said. “I'm getting more confident after every match.”

Medvedev, who won the Finals in 2020, has a 14-8 advantage in his career meetings with Zverev. But this is their first meeting this year and the first with Zverev ranked No. 1.

“It's a fast court. You need to serve well,” Medvedev said. “We're both relying on our serve a lot so whenever you have the break point you need to try to get it. and if you're serving well maybe there is no break point. So that's the biggest goal.”

Tiafoe was hit with a time violation and lost his first serve on the point where Medvedev broke for a 5-4 lead in the second set. The American got into an argument with the chair umpire earlier when he was first warned about taking too much time.

item.title: Climate talks in overtime as nations wrestle with response to worsening global warming
item.dc:creator: AP
item.description: Antalya’s COP31 climate talks were extended by a day as negotiators sought a final agreement on global warming, amid criticism that a draft text omitted fossil fuels and calls for greater climate funding.
item.content:encoded:
Antalya: Negotiators at the United Nations climate talks in Turkey will work an extra day in an attempt to reach a final agreement addressing global warming, though hopes are slim that additional discussions will result in concrete plans to drastically slash the use of fossil fuels.

Saturday's talks come as the two-week annual summit, which was supposed to end on Friday, drew strong condemnation from activists and some countries for failing to mention fossil fuels in a draft of the final agreement. The document was meant to address how the world will deal with climate change, which is contributing to devastating heat waves, floods and other disasters worldwide.

To avert the most catastrophic effects of warming, experts warn that urgent and deep cuts to emissions, mainly from the use of coal, oil and gas, are needed. The world is already on track to blow past the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

The summit in the Mediterranean coastal city of Antalya, called COP31, included a warning that progress has stalled for the past five years, even as disasters, including this year's heat waves in Europe and flooding in Nepal, grow more devastating and deadly.

Countries most vulnerable to climate change, including island nations whose lands are battered by rising seas, also say wealthy nations that caused the climate crisis must contribute more to a UN fund to help them recover from disasters and adapt to a warmer world.

But many of the world's top-polluting nations, including the United States, did not participate directly in this year's talks.

Borenstein reported from Kensington, Maryland, and Delgado reported from Bangkok. Associated Press journalist Tammy Webber contributed from Fenton, Michigan.

The Associated Press' climate and environmental coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. The AP is solely responsible for all content. Find the AP's standards for working with philanthropies, a list of supporters and funded coverage areas at AP.org.
