item.title: Pankaj Advani enters World Snooker semi-finals
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Pankaj Advani defeated fellow Indian Digvijay Kadian 4-2 to reach the men’s semi-finals of the IBSF World Snooker Championships in Indore. Reigning women’s champion Anupama Ramachandran also advanced, beating Keerthana Pandian 3-1 in the quarter-finals
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Three-time champion and favourite Pankaj Advani overcame giant-killer and fellow Indian Digvijay Kadian 4-2 to enter the men’s semi-finals of the IBSF World Snooker Championships at the Yeshwant Club in Indore on Friday.

Advani, known for his safety play, seemed to have met his match in Kadian, as the two kept the crowd entertained with some impressive tactical exchanges.

Advani eventually came out on top in both the defensive battle and the match to set up a last-four showdown with Iran’s formidable Ali Gharahgozlou, who outplayed India’s Dhvajj Haria in his quarter-final. The other semi-final will be an all-Hong Kong, China affair between Langyi Ryan Li and Tam Yun Fung.

Kadian seemed to pick up where he had left off in the morning against former professional Harvey Chandler of England. He rifled in a fine 40 after Advani’s poor safety shot. However, when he missed a yellow to the bottom-right pocket while leading 54-0, Advani punished him with a splendid 56 clearance to take the lead in the best-of-seven-frame encounter.

Advani took the next frame as well, with runs of 44 and 20. However, Kadian fought back with runs of 57 and 42 to restore parity at 2-2. The fifth frame was a battle of attrition that lasted almost an hour, with both players resorting to safety play. Advani, although not at his fluent best, went 3-2 up. The sixth frame followed a similar script before the 29-time world champion came through.

Earlier, Brijesh Damani, who stunned Ali Alobaidli in the first knockout round and top seed Sourav Kothari 4-2 in the pre-quarter-finals, went down 2-4 to Langyi Ryan Li.

ANUPAMA IN SEMIS

Meanwhile, reigning women’s champion Anupama Ramachandran came up with a fine display to power into the semi-finals with a comfortable 3-1 win over fellow Indian Keerthana Pandian in the quarter-finals.

The Chennai cueist found her rhythm and range right from the beginning, with breaks flowing regularly from her cue in the best-of-five-frame quarter-final clash.

Anupama put the loss of the opening frame behind her — despite a fine break of 46 — and came up with a fluent 61 in the next to draw level. She then played a percentage game to keep Keerthana on a tight leash and go 2-1 up.

The champion then closed out the frame and match with another fine run of 38 to set up a semi-final clash with Tessa Davidson, who outplayed Filipino cueist Carmille Buhat 3-0 in the other quarter-final.

India’s Amee Kamani, who looked a cut above the rest in the league stage, failed to replicate that form and went down 1-3 to Hong Kong, China’s Shiu Wing Man. The latter will take on her compatriot So Man Yan in the other semi-final.

Results (Indians unless mentioned):

Men: Quarter-finals: Langyi Ryan Li (HKC) bt Brijesh Damani 4-2 (108 (66)-6, 80-36, 19-53, 112 (67)-0, 0-72, 67-28); Tam Yun Fung (HKC) bt Amir Sarkhosh (Irn) 4-3 (15-61, 117 (113)-15, 70-45, 58-69, 62-10, 34-65, 76 (75)-1); Pankaj Advani bt Digvijay Kadian 4-2 (56 (56)-54, 79-55, 5-65 (57), 13-76, 74-41, 74-43); Ali Gharahgozlou (Irn) bt Dhavajj Haria 4-1 (1-76 (69), 71-62, 74-56, 63-22, 88 (55)-0).

Pre-quarter-finals: Damani bt Sourav Kothari 4-2 (66-38, 20-52, 74-78, 82-4, 71-58, 61-40); Ryan Li bt Alijalil Ali (Irq) 4-0 (56-32, 62-39, 85-16, 105 (105)-1); Sarkhosh bt Wang Yuchen (HKC) 4-2 (83 (83)-0, 28-60, 140 (140)-0, 44-79, 63-30, 65-10); Yun Fung bt Michael Mengorio (Phi) 4-3 (11-80, 76-0, 51-61, 70-8, 6-63, 70-51, 57-17).

Advani bt Rayaan Razmi 4-1 (65-23, 61-67, 73-50, 58-21, 63-16); Kadian bt Harvey Chandler (Eng) 4-2 (25-72 (72), 78-40, 71-20, 70 (70)-20, 47-63, 65 (65)-8); Haria bt Kamal Chawla 4-0 (79-55, 60-23, 62 (54)-15, 51-40); Gharahgozlou bt Manan Chandra 4-1 (38-76, 68-34, 73-61, 61-31, 77 (61)-1).

Round 1: Damani bt Ali Alobaidli (Qat) 4-0; Ryan Li bt Malkeet Singh 4-2; Sarkhosh bt Aditay Mehta 4-1; Razmi bt S Shrikrishna 4-3; Kadian bt Nansen Wan (HKC) 4-1; Haria bt Uzair Khan 4-1; Chandra bt Kreishh Gurbaxani 4-3; Mengorio bt Hussain Khan 4-3.

Women: Quarter-finals:** Anupama Ramachandran bt Keerthana Pandian 3-1 (66 (46)-80, 85 (61)-40, 62-30, 76 (38)-39); Shiu Wing Man (HKC) bt Amee Kamani 3-1 (53-39, 77 (36)-49, 0-62, 80-41); Tessa Davidson (Eng) bt Carmille Buhat (Phi) 3-0 (54-13, 69-25, 60 (32)-9); So Man Yan (HKC) bt Yee Ting Cheung (HKC) 3-0 (72-38, 60-25, 52-38).

Round 1: Buhat bt Margaret O’Driscoll (Ire) 3-1; Wing Man bt Ishika Shah 3-1 (52-61, 54-44, 45-36, 63-52).

item.title: Loknath Naik’s 104 powers Hyderabad to police T20 title
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Loknath Naik smashed 104 off 46 balls as Hyderabad defeated Cyberabad by eight wickets to win the Telangana Police T20 Cricket Championship. Hyderabad chased down a target of 151 in 15.3 overs after bowling out Cyberabad for 150
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Hyderabad scored an eight-wicket win over Cyberabad in the final of the Telangana Police T20 Cricket Championship at the Pavilion Cricket Ground here on Friday.

Batting first, Cyberabad Police scored 150 runs, losing all 10 wickets in 20 overs. Hyderabad Police chased down the target, scoring 152/2 in just 15.3 overs to register a convincing victory.

Hyderabad’s Loknath Naik was the star of the final, scoring 104 runs off just 46 balls, including nine fours and six sixes.

Loknath Naik, who hit 104 off 46 balls, was named Player of the Final and also Player of the Series.

Cyberabad’s Naresh was named Best All-rounder and Naveen Babu Best Bowler of the championship, which featured 21 teams.

Telangana DGP M R Anand, IPS, and Future City Commissioner of Police Dr Tarun Joshi gave away the prizes.

item.title: Lakshya Rajesh, Shaina Manimuthu set up girls’ singles title clash
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TT Gnana Dattu and Telangana’s Akhil Reddy Bobba will meet in the boys’ singles final of the Junior National Badminton Championships after contrasting semi-final wins. Lakshya Rajesh and defending champion Shaina Manimuthu will contest the girls’ singles final
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Karnataka’s Lakshya Rajesh will face defending champion Shaina Manimuthu in the girls’ singles final, while 2025 World Championships team bronze medallist TT Gnana Dattu will face Telangana’s Akhil Reddy Bobba in the boys’ singles final of the 49th Yonex-Sunrise Junior National (U-19) Badminton Championships in Gangtok on Friday.

Lakshya, seeded eighth, upset second seed Parul Choudhary of Rajasthan 15-10, 15-7 in the semi-finals, while defending champion Shaina had to fight hard to get the better of 2025 Asian U-17 gold medallist Diksha SR 15-12, 15-17, 17-15 in a 45-minute encounter to reach the final.

In the boys’ singles semi-final, Gnana Dattu eased past Rudhar Pratap Singh Rana 15-7, 15-6, while Akhil Reddy upset second seed Bornil Akash Changmai 15-13, 7-15, 15-6 to set up an all-Telangana summit clash.

Chhattisgarh’s Divyanshu Agarwal will have a chance to grab a double crown after making it to the boys’ doubles and mixed doubles finals.

In the boys’ doubles category, Divyanshu teamed up with Amarjit Singh Khwairakpam to beat the fifth-seeded combination of Aanayan Borah and Bjorn Jaison 15-11, 15-8. Earlier, he and Varna Prabhuanand of Tamil Nadu had defeated Telangana’s Showrya Kiran J and Keerthy Manchala 15-13, 15-12 in the mixed doubles semi-finals.

The results:

Semi-finals

Boys’ singles: Akhil Reddy Bobba bt Bornil Akash Changmai 15-13, 7-15, 15-6; TT Gnana Dattu bt Rudhar Pratap Singh Rana 15-7, 15-6.

Girls’ singles: Shaina Manimuthu bt 6-Diksha SR 15-12, 15-17, 17-15; Lakshya Rajesh bt 2-Parul Choudhary 15-10, 15-7.

Boys’ doubles: Divyansh Agrawal/Amarjit Singh Khwairakpam bt Aanayan Borah/Bjorn Jaison 15-11, 15-8; Pavan S/Punith S bt Rishav Ngangom/Mangsuan Vemai Kyoveio 15-10, 9-15, 15-11.

Girls’ doubles: Aanya Bisht/Angel Punera bt Ananya Arun/Deepika Devanaboina 9-15, 15-12, 15-10; Diya Bheemaiah B/Baruni Parshwal bt Ishita Negi/Varna Prabhuanand 15-5, 10-15, 15-7.

Mixed doubles: Amith Raj Natraj/Suhina Roy bt Punith S/Deepak Raj Aditi 15-8, 15-13; 2-Divyansh Agarwal/Varna Prabhuanand bt Showrya Kiran J/Keerthy Manchala 15-13, 15-12.

item.title: Karandeep Kochhar ends Gaganjeet Bhullar’s winning streak
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Karandeep Kochhar defeated Gaganjeet Bhullar and Aryan Roopa Anand in a three-way play-off to win the Pune Auro Realty Invitational 2026. Kochhar birdied the second extra hole to claim his second IGPL title after a dramatic final round
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Karandeep Kochhar of Krishna Punjab Raptors GC, with the calming effect of his girlfriend, Asian Games gold medallist Pranavi Urs, on the bag, at the Pune Auro Realty Invitational 2026 presented by Auro Goal Eagles, ended Vimtra Chennai Lions GC’s Gaganjeet Bhullar’s incredible three-week winning streak on the Am Green IGPL Tour.

Three players — Kochhar, Bhullar and Aryan Roopa Anand of RVR Delhi Blue Bulls GC — were locked at 10-under after 54 holes of action over the last three days. It took another two holes before Kochhar won on the second extra hole, as Bhullar, who had earlier regaled the crowd with monster putts over the past few weeks, missed a three-footer and Aryan too missed. It was the third play-off finish in a row.

It was also the first time the players were competing for an enhanced purse of Rs 2 crore on the Am Green IGPL. The final three events in Pune, Mumbai and Bengaluru will carry a purse of Rs 2 crore, with the winner getting Rs 30 lakh, as against Rs 22.50 lakh earlier.

The final act of the final-day drama began when Kochhar landed a magnificent eagle on the final hole in regulation play to get into a play-off. After having finished bogey-eagle on the first two days, the 27-year-old Kochhar, after a bogey on the 17th, was once again faced with the same situation, except that this time it was to stay in the tournament. Bhullar had already set the target at 10-under with two birdies in the last three holes.

Kochhar rolled in a 25-30-foot do-or-die putt for an eagle that put him into a three-way play-off with Aryan Roopa Anand, the overnight leader, and Bhullar.

Earlier in regulation play, Aryan Roopa Anand, who had at least a share of the lead for most of the final day, was also faced with a must-make putt from about 15 feet on the 18th to get to 10-under, and he holed it.

All three players birdied the first extra hole, and Bhullar, of all people, missed a three-footer in the second play-off hole and failed to extend the play-off.

Kochhar then rolled a great steely putt from the edge of the green to set up a give-in, which would get him his second IGPL trophy. Bhullar and Aryan failed. Kochhar made no mistake with the give-in winning putt, and that saw him dethrone ‘King G’, as Bhullar has been nicknamed by fellow players for his amazing streak of wins.

It gave Kochhar his second IGPL title, after his first at IGPL Dubai last year. He was also second to Pranavi last year in Mumbai and to Bhullar in Hyderabad last month.

Minutes after his win, Kochhar went to fish out his Rolex watch from the bag and wear it before receiving the trophy.

“I got this timepiece sometime in the middle of this year after feeling that I had played well enough this year to buy myself this lovely timepiece. This was the perfect time to wear it,” said a beaming Kochhar.

Aman Raj of Atri Mumbai Garudas GC had the round of the final day with a 7-under 64, and he was tied sixth with Varun Parikh of Flying Man Kolkata Tigers GC (68). The consistent Sachin Baisoya of Phoenix Hyderabad Firebirds GC was once again in the top 10, at eighth place, while Yashas Chandra of Vimtra Chennai Lions GC was ninth. Pukhraj Singh Gill of Unico Gurugram Tuskers GC and Syed Saqib Ahmed of Flying Man Kolkata Tigers GC rounded off the top 10.

The next event is slated to be held at BPGC, Mumbai, from Nov. 24 to 26.

item.title: FCI Headquarters win third successive Inter-Zonal Hockey Championship
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: FCI Headquarters clinched their third consecutive title at the 55th All India FCI Inter-Zonal Hockey Championship, defeating North Zone 3–2 in the final at Railway Hockey Stadium. Bobby Singh Dhami was adjudged Player of the Tournament
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: FCI Headquarters clinched the championship title for the third consecutive time, defeating North Zone 3–2 in a thrilling final of the 55th All India FCI Inter-Zonal Hockey Championship, organised by the FCI Telangana Region, at the Railway Hockey Stadium here on Friday.

This is the third consecutive title triumph for FCI Headquarters.

Harsh Sharma, Munish Rana and Bobby Singh Dhami scored one goal each for FCI Headquarters, while Nand Kishore and Navraj Singh scored for North Zone.

Bobby Singh Dhami was adjudged the ‘Player of the Tournament’.

Jacintha Lazarus, IAS, Executive Director, FCI, Zonal Office (South), Chennai, and President, ZSCPC, South, who was the chief guest at the closing ceremony, appreciated the efforts and arrangements made by the host Telangana Region and the ZSCPC coordination team.

Anuj Tyagi, General Manager (Region), FCI Telangana, thanked all those involved in the successful conduct of the tournament and highlighted it as a valuable opportunity for employees, emphasising the spirit of accepting victory and defeat gracefully.

General Managers from the FCI Zonal Office, Chennai — Sunil Kumar CT, L. Chatru Naik, Zakeeruddin, Harshit Singh and Devendar Singh, DGM, ZO Chennai — along with DGMs from the FCI Regional Office, Hyderabad — Vemula Sridevi, Ghanshyam, Pradeep Jawalkote and Mohan Chandra — and RSCPC Secretary Srinivasa Rao Mylapalli also graced the prize distribution function.

item.title: Mamata Medical College beat G9 Academy in Hyderabad basketball league
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Mamata Medical College defeated G9 Academy 94-45 in the GM Sampath Kumar annual league basketball championship at YMCA Secunderabad. The winners led 39-22 at half-time. Nizam Basketball Academy also secured a narrow 55-52 victory over Keystone in the women’s section
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Mamata Medical College scored a 94-45 win over G9 Academy in the GM Sampath Kumar annual league basketball championship at YMCA Secunderabad here on Friday.

The winners led 39-22 at half-time.

Vikrant (21), Akash and Sai (20 each) were the leading scorers for the winners, while Sravan and Sameer (14 points each) put up a good show for the losers.

In the women’s section, Nizam Basketball Academy recorded a narrow 55-52 win over Keystone Basketball Academy, with Jahnavi (17) being the top scorer for the winners and Saanvi (24) the leading performer for the losers.

The scores:

Men: Mamata Medical College 94 (Vikrant 21, Akash 20, Sai 20, Srikanth 14, Abhiram 15) bt G9 Academy 45 (Sravan 14).

Women: Nizam Basketball Academy 55 (Jahnavi 17, Khushboo 13, Vennela 11) bt Keystone Basketball Academy 52 (Saanvi 24, Yuktha 9).

item.title: BVP Rao urges IOC to monitor Indian Olympic Association elections
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Former Clean Sports India convenor BVP Rao has raised concerns over alleged government interference in Indian Olympic Association elections. In a letter to IOC President Kirsty Coventry, Rao sought an observer to ensure free and fair elections to the IOA
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: “While people like me, I was a former equestrian, studied Olympism at the International Olympic Academy and led the movement ‘Clean Sports India’, are happy about former sportspersons joining the governance of the IOA, what is worrying is the process, which should not lead to ‘appointed politics’ by those in power,” he said.

The Hyderabad-based Rao said that in the world’s largest democracy, aspiring Indian sportspersons should be groomed as future leaders by encouraging contests in an atmosphere of free and fair elections.

“On the contrary, a precedent is being set that only sportspersons in the Government’s good books are being elected unanimously by making several others withdraw their nominations,” Rao said.

“In the light of these circumstances, I request the IOC to send an observer to ensure free and fair elections to the IOA,” he concluded.

item.title: Telugu Black Hawks enter CAVA Volleyball Club Championship semi-finals
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telugu Black Hawks entered the CAVA Volleyball Club Championship semi-finals after defeating Mumbai Meteors 3-1 in their final league encounter in Bhubaneswar. The PVL side recovered from losing the opening set before winning the next three sets convincingly
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Telugu Black Hawks, the Prime Volleyball League (PVL) team, entered the semi-finals of the prestigious CAVA Volleyball Club Championship, which features some of the finest club teams from across Central Asia.

Playing at the KIIT University campus in Bhubaneswar, the Black Hawks recorded a convincing 3-1 victory over Mumbai Meteors in their final league encounter.

Despite losing the opening set 20-25, the Black Hawks staged an impressive comeback and displayed tremendous composure and determination. They went on to win the next three sets 25-19, 25-22 and 25-18 to seal a memorable victory.

Telugu Black Hawks will face either renowned Iranian club Foolad Sirjan or Bengaluru Torpedoes in the semi-finals scheduled for Saturday.

The Telugu Black Hawks are coached by Argentine coach Ariel Garcia and boast an impressive line-up of international players.

The squad features Federico Pereyra from Argentina, Hector Alexis Cruz from the Dominican Republic and Henrique Meireles from Brazil. The presence of these overseas players adds international quality and depth to the squad as the team continues its campaign for the CAVA championship title.

Black Hawks owner Kankanala Abhishek Reddy said that reaching the semi-finals of such a prestigious international tournament was a matter of great pride for the franchise. He appreciated the players for their determination, teamwork and outstanding performances.

item.title: Amaya Agarwal wins gold at FIDE World Junior Rapid Chess Championship
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: FIDE World Junior Rapid Chess Championship
item.description: Hyderabad’s 11-year-old WCM Amaya Agarwal won the Under-12 gold at the FIDE World Junior Rapid Chess Championship in the UAE. Amaya and twin brother Anay also secured silver in the Under-12 category at the Chess Friendship Festival in Slovenia
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Amaya Agarwal and Anay Agarwal from Ekagra Chess Academy in Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, have brought laurels to the city with their outstanding performances in international chess tournaments.

The 11-year-old chess prodigy Amaya Agarwal, a Woman Candidate Master (WCM), clinched the gold at the FIDE World Junior Rapid Chess Championship held in the UAE during the first week of November.

Competing in the Under-12 category against 184 FIDE-rated players from 40 countries, Amaya showcased exceptional talent and determination to emerge as the champion.

Adding to their achievements, the twin chess stars, Amaya Agarwal and Anay Agarwal, secured silver by finishing second in the Under-12 category at the Kasparov Chess Foundation Chess Friendship Festival held in Slovenia.

The twins have also made their mark on the international chess stage by defeating World Grandmasters and demonstrating remarkable competitive skills.

On Friday, coach Chaitanya Suresh and the Managing Director of Ekagra Chess Academy congratulated Amaya and Anay for their remarkable achievements during a felicitation event at the academy.

item.title: Zaayn Mohammad, Kanishka Govind win singles and doubles titles in Khammam
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana’s Zaayn Mohammad and Tamil Nadu’s Kanishka Govind won singles and doubles titles at the Kisan Projects Pvt Ltd-AITA Super Series in Khammam. Zaayn beat Arjun Dua in the boys’ singles final, while Kanishka defeated Kaashvi Konanki in the girls’ final
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Zaayn Mohammad of Telangana and Kanishka Govind bagged a ‘double’ each, winning the singles and doubles titles in the boys’ and girls’ categories, respectively, in the Kisan Projects Pvt Ltd-AITA Super Series tennis tournament at Khammam on Friday.

In the boys’ final, Zaayn defeated Arjun Dua of Haryana 7-6, 6-3, 6-2 and later combined with him to win the doubles title.

In the girls’ final, Kanishka Govind of Tamil Nadu scored a 6-0, 6-2 win over Kaashvi Konanki of Karnataka. She completed a double by winning the doubles title, partnering Telangana’s Vara Anuha Chitluri.

The results:

Boys:
Singles: Zaayn Mohammad (TG) bt Arjun Dua (Har) 7-6, 6-3, 6-2.
Doubles: Zaayn Mohammad (TG) & Arjun Dua (Har) bt Joel Johnson (TN) & PMA Adhish (TN) 6-7 (4), 7-6 (6), 10-6.

Girls:
Singles: Kanishka Govind (TN) bt Kaashvi Konanki (Kar) 6-0, 6-2.
Doubles: Vara Anuha Chitluri (TG) & Kanishka Govind (TN) bt Kaashvi Konanki (KA) & Dhriti Sharma (HR) 1-6, 6-1, 10-4.

item.title: In India for SCO meet, Pak minister says terrorism issues should be discussed at regional forums
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Pakistan Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik, during his visit to New Delhi for an SCO-related event, avoided directly answering questions on Pakistan's action against terrorism. He stressed that terrorism and regional security issues should be addressed through multilateral forums like the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) rather than bilateral blame games, while highlighting Pakistan's own losses to terrorism.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Musadik Masood Malik, sidestepped a question on the action taken by Pakistan regarding terrorism, saying that he had come to New Delhi for a multilateral forum and did not want “such a big discussion” to be held at a bilateral level.

“I have come here on a multilateral forum and I want a good multilateral forum to be held… These issues are very wide. You just saw some issues of Iran in our neighbourhood, many issues in Central Asia, many issues in Afghanistan…,” Malik said.

Referring to terrorism, Malik said, “Many incidents have occurred in your country as well, however, if you look at us, thousands of people, over the past one, one-and-a-half, or two years, thousands of people, have been martyred. And every day, we have to carry their coffins on our shoulders. So, we also want a lasting solution to be found for all these issues.”

He said that instead of taking up a single incident or moving forward with just a bilateral conversation “and then pointing fingers at one another”, the issues of the entire region should be discussed at forums such as the SCO.

Speaking about the SCO forum, Malik said, “Yes, it is very good. We just had a very good conversation, and we are very pleased to be here. There are many of our neighbours whom we don’t get the opportunity to meet together, to have a conversation with, to listen to their point of view, and more importantly than just listening, to understand it.”

On visiting places in India, Malik said that he had come for just a few days and would be busy with SCO-related matters, so he probably would not be able to explore very much this time.

“However, whatever opportunity I do get, I would want to meet people, see different places, and be able to understand them a bit, to understand the place as well as the people. People and places are one and the same,” he said.

Malik’s visit marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India since the SCO Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Goa in 2023, which was attended by Pakistan’s then Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto.

On November 13, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said that New Delhi’s position on Pakistan after the Pahalgam terror attack is amply clear.

“As far as our position on Pakistan after the Pahalgam terror attack is concerned, it should be amply clear to all as to where we stand,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had said.

item.title: Raunil Kukar wins maiden DP World PGTI title at IndianOil SERVO Masters
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Bengaluru’s Raunil Kukar won his maiden DP World PGTI title at the IndianOil SERVO Masters in Digboi, finishing two shots ahead of Anshul Kabthiyal. Kukar carded 16-under 272 after overcoming a difficult back-nine stretch in the final round
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Bengaluru’s Raunil Kukar claimed his maiden DP World PGTI title with a two-shot victory at the 26th IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf, the opening event of the DP World PGTI’s 2026–2027 season, played at Digboi Golf Links in Digboi, Assam.

The tournament carried a prize purse of Rs 1 crore.

The 28-year-old Kukar (70-65-70-67), who began the final round in a three-way tie for the lead alongside Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh and Mhow’s Om Prakash Chouhan, closed with a five-under 67 to win at 16-under 272.

The 28-year-old Anshul Kabthiyal (67-72-71-64) produced the tournament’s lowest round, an eight-under 64 featuring nine birdies and a lone bogey on the par-3 10th. He climbed from tied seventh overnight to finish runner-up at 14-under 274.

Kukar, who joined the tour in 2022, made eight birdies and three bogeys. He surged ahead with four consecutive birdies from the sixth to ninth holes, opening a four-shot lead at the turn.

However, the Bengaluru golfer endured a difficult stretch on the back nine, beginning with a missed short par putt on the 10th. Three bogeys in four holes allowed the chasing pack to close in, but Kukar recovered with birdies on the 14th, 15th and 17th to seal his breakthrough victory.

Kukar collected Rs 15 lakh and moved to the top of the 2026–2027 DP World PGTI Order of Merit.

Kukar, who had finished joint runner-up at the SECL presents Nava Raipur Open in September, was emotional after securing his first title following a difficult year that included wrist surgery.

Kukar identified his second-round 65 as a turning point, when his putting improved while playing alongside Sumit Kotwal.

Chandigarh’s Akshay Sharma (75-67-66-68) finished third at 12-under 276, while Om Prakash Chouhan (67-68-70-72), a 12-time DP World PGTI winner and 2023 rankings champion, was placed fourth at 11-under 277.

Yuvraj Singh (68-70-67-73) finished tied fifth alongside Bangladesh’s Md Razu (69-70-68-71) at 10-under 278.

item.title: Bellamkonda Sai Sreenivas’s pan-Indian film Haindava’s release postponed
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The makers of Haindava, starring Bellamkonda Sai Sreenivas and Samyuktha, have postponed the film's release from its previously scheduled date of November 27. The production house said the decision was taken to ensure higher technical standards and the best viewing experience, with a new release date to be announced soon.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The makers of director Ludheer Byreddy’s upcoming pan Indian film ‘Haindava’, featuring Telugu star Bellamkonda Sai Sreenivas and Samyuktha in the lead, on Friday announced that they had chosen to postpone their film’s release.

The film was to originally hit the screens on November 27 this year.

Moonshine Pictures, the production house producing the film, took to its social media timelines to share the announcement.

It wrote, “#HAINDAVA has been postponed from its scheduled date to give you all the best experience with high technical standards. A new release date will be announced soon. Stay tuned.”

The makers also shared a poster through which they made it clear that they remained committed to delivering the film to the highest standards of quality.

Thanking audiences for their patience and continued support, the makers said that they would announce a new release date soon.

A teaser that the makers had released last month had triggered great excitement among fans and film buffs.

The teaser showed that the story was set in the village of Rangapuram. The story takes a mysterious turn when all the idols from an ancient temple go missing and a villager is found murdered.

The temple priest however believes that all the idols will return within a stipulated timeframe. An atheist police officer is assigned the task of investigating the unusual case, setting the stage for a compelling clash between faith, reason, and the unexplained.

Bellamkonda Sai Sreenivas plays an atheist police officer who places his faith in humanity rather than God. Samyuktha plays the female lead, while Mahesh Manjrekar appears in a pivotal role as the temple priest. Saurabh Sachdeva, JD Chakravarthy, Shivaji Raja, and Getup Srinu feature in other significant roles.

Produced by Mahesh Chandu, the film boasts of a fine technical team. Production design for the film has been handled by Siva Kamesh D while cinematography for the film is by Harish Kannan. Music director Sam CS has scored the music for this occult thriller while Karthika Srinivas has handled its editing.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO caps explosive growth period for AI startup, filled with contradictions
item.dc:creator: AP
item.description: Anthropic, founded by former OpenAI executives after breaking away to pursue their own AI vision, has grown from a Silicon Valley startup into a Wall Street giant valued at USD 1.75 trillion after its trading debut. Despite building its brand around AI safety and warning about potential risks of advanced AI, the company now faces growing shareholder pressure to balance safety commitments with profit expectations.
item.content:encoded:
New York: A mere five years before breaking the record for the biggest public stock offering ever, Anthropic began as a Silicon Valley startup when its founders broke away from OpenAI with their own ideas about how to develop artificial intelligence.

Today, the company that dedicated itself to prioritising safety, building the Claude chatbot along the way, has been one of the loudest voices raising warnings about how the same technology could bring catastrophe.

It’s one of the contradictions that mark the brief, colourful history of Anthropic, which emerged Thursday from its first day of trading on Wall Street with a market value of USD 1.75 trillion.

The company, which still pledges to prioritise humanity’s benefit, now faces pressure from shareholders to wring profits from the technology its most senior leaders have described as posing existential threats.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei described the push and pull between safety and AI advancement as one of the “central tensions at the heart of the company” on Thursday.

In an interview with CNBC, he described the rapid pace of AI advancements — due in large part to advanced models helping to build the next, improved version of themselves — as akin to building something that lets a driver go 200 miles per hour when they had previously been driving at 60. His company, he said, is working to develop it safely.

“What we’ve done with pacing is essentially said, ‘Look, you know, we could drive at 200 miles an hour. Maybe let’s only drive at 90 miles an hour, spend time figuring out how to do that safely,'” he said. “And the rest of that surplus, we spend building the model in the right way.”

Warning of potential calamity, the company forges ahead

The company’s seven founders — Amodei, 43, his sister and Anthropic’s president Daniela Amodei, 39, and five other former OpenAI employees — left the rival company in pursuit of building one that more clearly prioritised safety in artificial intelligence development.

Anthropic publicly has been committed to safety and transparency around their AI models, but insiders have sounded alarm bells in recent months.

An Anthropic researcher resigned from the company in September, criticising the safety practices of both Anthropic and OpenAI. Jacob Coxon, whose message spurred industry-wide conversations about the speed of AI’s growth, wrote that both Anthropic and OpenAI are “gambling with our lives.” He warned that some working on AI development believe it could threaten human life by the end of the decade.

Dario Amodei responded with an essay calling for an industry-wide slowdown on the technology’s development. He enumerated detailed plans for slowing development and ushering in coordination across different companies and countries, and championed the idea of having independent evaluators embedded within Anthropic and other labs.

But the results from at least one of those independent evaluations underscored Coxon’s concerns. A recent report from the nonprofit Model Evaluation and Threat Research found Anthropic is developing its systems around twice as quickly as it was a year ago, largely because of the help of AI itself.

Amodei said Thursday in comments at the Nasdaq opening bell that the company’s “most difficult safety work lies ahead of us.”

“And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” he said.

A company pledging to benefit humanity has enriched its founders

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, meaning it has a legal obligation to balance shareholder interests with the public good. But these types of companies are rarely public, and of the few that are, they are significantly smaller than Anthropic, so the company is entering uncharted territory.

The company has said it is working towards a future where “AI’s benefits are shared by everyone,” but the initial public offering has created a concentration of extreme wealth for its founders, employees and other investors.

Before the IPO, the two Amodei siblings each had a net worth of just over USD 14 billion, according to Forbes. By Thursday afternoon, Dario Amodei’s net worth was USD 22.7 billion and Daniela Amodei’s was USD 22.8 billion.

The Amodeis and the other co-founders have said they are committed to pledging 80 per cent of their equity to philanthropy, although that commitment is voluntary. The company has an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity, which Anthropic matches. Anthropic has also pledged at least 5 per cent of its stock to a “public benefit” fund.

Speaking to CNBC Thursday, Daniela Amodei said the concept of a public benefit corporation “spoke” to the co-founders when they were initially creating the company.

“We’re really trying to do something that we do think can have this incredible economic value and impact, but we want it to be baked into essentially our structure that we also have to balance that against building things that are good for people,” she said.

Anthropic offers itself as a solution for AI doomsday fears

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission last month, Anthropic devoted an unusually lengthy 93 pages to the risk factors they must spell out for investors. Among the concerns were that advanced AI systems could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.”

Some argue Anthropic has outlined the ways its technology and that of its competitors could have devastating consequences in the name of sheer transparency. But critics have questioned the emphasis the company has placed on these dystopian-like potentials while positioning itself as the logical solution given its safety-minded focus.

A “Saturday Night Live” sketch in September made this contradiction a punchline. Cast member Jane Wickline played Dario Amodei, saying: “Sam Altman, myself, all the major AI players, we have talked about this extensively, and we are all on the same page here: We do not condone what we are doing.”

The faux interview on “SNL” concluded with a line that seems to have resonated with sceptics, showing up on a protest sign outside of Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters on Thursday: “I urge you to urge me to stop.”

item.title: First high-speed rail service will commence in 2027: Vaishnaw on bullet train
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said India's first high-speed bullet train service will begin in 2027, with the Surat-Vapi section opening first. He highlighted major progress on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor, including viaduct construction, station development, tunnel excavation, and indigenous bullet train manufacturing.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Friday said the country’s first high-speed rail service will commence in 2027 and the first section to open will be from Surat to Vapi.

The full corridor to Mumbai will follow in phases, he added in a post on Substack.

Talking about the pace of construction, he said that as of September, 456 km of pier work and 371 km of viaduct construction have been completed.

Six lakh noise barriers have been installed along 299 km stretch and 9,300 OHE masts have been installed across a 206 km viaduct, Vaishnaw wrote.

Additionally, he emphasised that four mountain tunnels have been excavated and 5 km of the 21 km Maharashtra tunnel has been excavated using the mountain tunnelling method.

He stated that civil work has been completed at eight stations, and architectural finishing work is underway.

Work is in progress at all three rolling stock depots at Sabarmati, Surat and Thane, Vaishnaw said.

Talking about the construction of the undersea tunnel, he said that in Maharashtra, the corridor runs through a 21 km tunnel, and 7 km of it passes under the sea, beneath Thane Creek.

This is India’s first undersea rail tunnel.

“Two Tunnel Boring Machines were launched in July 2026, from Vikhroli and Sawli. These are among the largest machines ever deployed in India,” Vaishnaw said.

He added, “Each has a cutterhead 13.6 metres in diameter, as tall as a 4-storey building. Each weigh over 3,000 tonnes, roughly 500 Asian elephants. The machine is 96 metres long, nearly five cricket pitches laid end to end!”

He highlighted the ongoing manufacturing of India’s first bullet trains and said, “ICF and BEML are manufacturing the indigenous B28 trainset, designed for 280 kmph. The first body frame is complete and is undergoing structural testing. Track trials are expected by mid-2027. A faster B35, designed for 350 kmph, is the next step.”

“The fixed infrastructure is being indigenised too. All major transformers of the high-speed electrification system, the cross arms on the masts, the ground, protection and feeder wires: all are being manufactured in India,” he stated.

Talking about the delay of almost a decade since it was first announced in 2017, Vaishnaw said that the project could not start in Maharashtra for close to two and a half years because state permissions and land acquisition were pending.

“Then COVID took away two more years. Full construction began in earnest in 2021,” he said.

“So, when critics ask, ‘where is the bullet train’, the honest answer is: serious construction is just five years old. And look at what five years have built,” he added.

item.title: Murderous attack on MP exposes Jungle Raj in Andhra Pradesh: YSRCP
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has alleged that Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy's convoy was attacked by TDP supporters near Aguduru in YSR Kadapa district during local body election nomination activities. The party accused the Andhra Pradesh coalition government and police of failing to prevent the attack.
item.content:encoded:
Tadepalli (Andhra Pradesh): The YSR Congress Party said that the alleged murderous attack on its Kadapa MP Y. S. Avinash Reddy on Friday exposes ‘jungle raj’ prevailing in Andhra Pradesh.

Condemning the attack on the MP’s convoy in YSR Kadapa district, YSRCP State Spokesperson Putha Sivashankar demanded the immediate dismissal of the coalition government and imposition of President’s Rule.

Addressing the media at YSRCP headquarters, Sivashankar said TDP leader B. Tech Ravi (Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy) mobilised hired goons to attack Avinash Reddy’s convoy with stones, sticks, iron rods and petrol bombs near Aguduru in Simhadripuram mandal.

The MP was accompanying YSRCP-supported candidates seeking to file nominations under High Court protection. Pulivendula Rural CI Shantilal, SI Maddileti and other police personnel stood by as the attack unfolded, he said.

He questioned why DIG Koya Praveen and senior police officers, who previously used force against YSRCP candidates, remained inactive when an MP faced a life-threatening attack. He said police were protecting TDP groups instead of enforcing court orders.

Sivashankar said the coalition feared electoral defeat and had unleashed violence across Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Nellore, Prakasam and Sri Sathya Sai districts. Candidates faced attacks, petrol bombs and destruction of their homes from Rayalaseema to Tadepalligudem. He recalled earlier attacks on MPs Mithun Reddy and Gurumurthy.

He said Lokesh’s ‘Red Book’ threats and assurances of bail had emboldened TDP groups. Despite High Court directions, police continued obstructing nominations, while Chandrababu Naidu politicised non-party Panchayat elections through teleconferences and candidate announcements on TDP letterheads.

Meanwhile, YSRCP Kadapa District president and former MLA Ravindranath Reddy slammed the Chandrababu Naidu government for turning Andhra Pradesh into the country’s number one state for violence and lawlessness, destroying democracy in local body elections.

He said the ruling coalition had made a mockery of Mahatma Gandhi’s vision of Gram Swaraj. Ministers and MLAs were directly involved in tearing opposition nomination papers, while police facilitated attacks and intimidation.

He strongly condemned the attack on sitting MP YS Avinash Reddy’s convoy with petrol bombs, stones and knives near Simhadripuram police station, where the MP was seeking police protection for candidates under High Court orders. Vehicles were damaged while police remained spectators.

In Pedda Cheppali, Kamalapuram mandal, police filed false cases to arrest a woman candidate despite court directions protecting her nomination rights. Similar attacks continued across Pulivendula, Kamalapuram, Badvel and Jammalamadugu.

Ravindranath Reddy said the coalition was using physical violence in Rayalaseema and manipulating nomination scrutiny in Coastal Andhra to secure uncontested victories. He ridiculed TDP’s claims of 87% and 92% strike rates, calling them manufactured victories intended to impress NDA leaders.

He said government-controlled media was concealing electoral violence while the coalition abandoned manifesto promises and pursued commissions and corruption.

item.title: Malkajgiri residents oppose Chandragiri Colony Road widening for RUB
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Residents of East and West Chandragiri Colony, Santoshima Nagar Colony and Safilguda in Hyderabad's Malkajgiri Assembly constituency have opposed the proposed widening of Chandragiri Colony Road for a RUB and urged Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to consider an alternative location.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Property owners in East and West Chandragiri Colony, Santoshima Nagar Colony and Safilguda in Malkajgiri Assembly constituency have objected to the widening of Chandragiri Colony Road for the proposed construction of a road under bridge (RUB).

In a representation, they urged Union Minister of Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw to consider an alternative location.

The property owners have formed a joint action committee (JAC) to press their demand. “Medchal-Malkajgiri district Collector had also written to local railway authorities in July, urging them to explore the feasibility of constructing an RUB on Chandragiri Colony Road following residents’ objections,” P. Bharadwaja Sastry, a JAC member and Chandragiri Colony resident, told Telangana Today.

Railway authorities initially proposed the RUB at Vinayaka Nagar before shifting it to Chandragiri Colony, Bharadwaja Sastry said. The existing 10-metre-wide road has been used for decades, he said.

The proposed RUB at Chandragiri Colony would pose a serious threat to more than 350 individual houses and apartments, Sastry stated in the representation.

Sastry urged the Railway Minister to reconsider the construction of a new RUB and the widening of Chandragiri Colony Road, stating that the project was technically unfeasible and could inconvenience the public while affecting hundreds of families.

Residents who signed the representation demanded that Vaishnaw direct local railway authorities to explore the possibility of building the RUB at Vinayaka Nagar itself.

item.title: Opinion: Telangana Intermediate Board merger—structural change isn’t education reform
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana government’s move to bring Classes IX to XII under a common board will serve little purpose if it remains merely an examination authority and fails to transform classroom learning
item.content:encoded:
By Adama Srinivas Reddy

The Telangana government is now moving towards a major restructuring of school and Intermediate education. The proposal includes a common board for Classes IX to XII and amendments to the existing laws governing school and Intermediate education. The government is also considering a phased transition, with a Bill expected in the coming Assembly session. These steps could reshape how the State organises secondary and higher secondary education.

So far, the debate has focused largely on administrative and institutional questions. Should government high schools be upgraded to offer Classes XI and XII? Should existing Junior Colleges be allowed to add Classes IX and X? How will teachers’ service conditions be protected? What changes will be needed in the boards, affiliation procedures and administration? These questions need clear answers. But there is a more fundamental issue that deserves equal attention: What kind of education should students receive during the two years after Class X?

No Simple Change

The merger should not be treated as a simple administrative change. It gives the government an opportunity to rethink the purpose of Intermediate education, its curriculum and the way institutions function. If this opportunity is missed, the existing system may simply continue under a different administrative arrangement, with all its present problems.

Earlier education commissions and committees had recognised the importance of the higher secondary stage. The Kothari Commission (1964–66) laid the foundation for the 10+2+3 structure. The PD Shukla Committee (1973) argued that changing the structure of education should help improve its quality, rather than become an objective in itself.

The Adiseshiah Committee (1978) stressed the need to link higher secondary education with work and vocational learning. The Amrik Singh Task Force (1997), while examining the role of school education boards, argued that boards should function as autonomous academic bodies rather than merely conduct examinations. It called for boards to take greater responsibility for academic planning, curriculum and educational standards, while remaining free from undue political interference.

These recommendations point to a common idea: the Plus Two stage should provide a sound general education while preparing students for higher studies, employment and responsible participation in society.

The proposed merger offers Telangana an opportunity to address the commercialisation of education, ease the pressure of entrance examinations and strengthen public institutions

The proposed common board therefore deserves attention beyond the administrative convenience of bringing two boards together. The recommendations of the Amrik Singh Task Force suggest that a board should play an active academic role. It should guide curriculum development, improve assessment, support educational research and work to maintain standards.

It should also ensure that students can move between different boards without facing problems of recognition or equivalence. A common board will serve little purpose if it remains only an examination authority. It must have academic autonomy, professional expertise and a clear responsibility for improving the quality of education.

Inter Education

Over time, however, the purpose of Intermediate education has become much narrower. In many institutions, especially corporate Junior Colleges, education has come to mean preparing students for engineering and medical entrance examinations. The race for ranks has pushed other areas of learning to the margins. Languages, humanities, social sciences, sports and arts receive little attention. Students spend much of their time learning how to answer examination questions quickly, often without developing a proper understanding of the subjects or the ability to think independently.

Corporate colleges are not the only reason for this situation. The importance given to a few competitive examinations, the shortage of good higher education opportunities, and the social pressure to enter professional courses have all contributed to it. However, corporate institutions have turned this competition into a business and intensified it. Students are treated as potential rank holders, while their results are used to attract more admissions. High fees, exaggerated claims about results, long study hours and poor attention to student welfare are signs of a system in which commercial interests often take precedence over education.

Preventing corporate colleges from starting Classes IX and X will not solve the larger problem. The government needs to regulate private Junior Colleges effectively. This should include clear rules on fees, infrastructure, teaching hours, hostel facilities and student safety. Colleges should not be allowed to make misleading claims about their results. Nor should entrance coaching take the place of the prescribed curriculum. Students need sufficient time for sleep, sports, recreation and other activities that are part of growing up. Regular inspections and a grievance mechanism through which students can raise complaints without fear are also necessary.

Admission Practices

Regulation alone, however, cannot change the culture of education. The government must also address the excessive influence of entrance examinations. This calls for a review of admission practices, the creation of multiple pathways into higher education and better opportunities across different disciplines. Examinations should assess whether students understand a subject and can apply what they have learnt. They should not reward only memorisation and the ability to follow coaching methods.

Government Junior Colleges also need serious attention. Upgrading selected high schools may help students in rural and remote areas, but enrolment alone should not decide which schools are upgraded. The government must consider the availability of qualified teachers, laboratories, libraries, classrooms, transport, sanitation and a reasonable choice of subjects. Public institutions should offer students a genuine alternative to commercial colleges. They also need counselling, career guidance and academic support.

Students in Classes XI and XII are at an important stage of their intellectual, emotional and social development. They need teachers who understand the challenges of adolescence and can guide them beyond examination preparation. This requires appropriate teacher qualifications, regular professional development, reasonable workloads and freedom to make academic decisions. Teachers must be valued as educators, not judged only by the ranks their students secure.

Education during these two years should prepare students for much more than admission to professional courses. It should help them think independently, distinguish information from knowledge, understand society, respect different cultures and make informed decisions about their lives. It should also prepare them to take part responsibly in a democratic society. Humanities, languages, vocational learning, arts and physical education must have a proper place in the curriculum. They should not be treated as less important than science and mathematics.

The success of the merger should not be judged solely by the money saved, the number of students enrolled or examination results. The real test is whether students receive a better education and whether teaching and learning improve. That will require serious discussions with teachers, students, parents and educationists, as well as a clear plan supported by adequate funds and facilities.

Changing the administrative structure of education does not necessarily change its purpose or practice. Even a well-intended policy change becomes an educational reform only when it makes a difference in classrooms and in students’ lives. Telangana’s challenge is not simply to merge Intermediate education with school education. It is to restore the purpose of this stage by addressing commercialisation, reducing the pressure of rank-based competition and giving students the opportunity to learn in a broader and more meaningful way.

 

(The author is a faculty member at Kakatiya Government College [Autonomous], Hanamkonda)

item.title: NHRC seeks action taken report on government hospital infra crisis in Telangana
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The NHRC has sought an action taken report within four weeks on a complaint alleging gross human rights violations and poor infrastructure in Telangana's government hospitals and PHCs. The petition cited the deaths of three newborns in a fire at RIMS Adilabad.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Thursday sought an action taken report on alleged gross human rights violations and crumbling infrastructure in government hospitals and Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in the State

The Commission’s directive follows a petition by advocate Vinod flagging systemic negligence in Telangana’s public healthcare facilities as criminal negligence and a violation of the Right to Life under Article 21 of the Constitution.

In his complaint to the NHRC, Vinod highlighted the fatal fire at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of RIMS Adilabad, which claimed the lives of three newborns. He also highlighted collapsing ceilings at MGM Hospital, Warangal, rodent and stray animal attacks on patients, and acute shortages of beds and staff forcing patients to be treated on bare floors.

Vinod sought independent safety audits, mandatory sanitation and infrastructure reforms, adequate staffing, and compensation for the bereaved families of the deceased infants.

Forwarding the complaint toTelangana Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju, NHRC Assistant Registrar (Law) Atul Kumar sought an appropriate action and an action taken report (ATR) within four weeks.

item.title: Telangana Tourism launches ‘A Day to Pochampally’ tour from Nov 22
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana Tourism is organising a one-day heritage tour to Pochampally from November 22, offering visitors an opportunity to experience the region's famed Ikat weaving tradition and cultural attractions. The package includes transportation, temple darshan, meals, museum entry and a hands-on weaving workshop.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: In a move to offer visitors an opportunity to explore the rich handloom heritage and cultural traditions of Pochampally, renowned for its world-famous Ikat weaving, Telangana Tourism is organising a special one-day tour titled “A Day to Pochampally” from November 22.

The itinerary includes a visit to the Sri Yadagirigutta Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, traditional lunch prepared by Self Help Group (SHG) women, and a visit to the Ikat Museum.

Visitors will also get an opportunity to interact with weavers, experience the traditional tie-and-dye technique through a hands-on workshop, and shop for authentic Pochampally handloom sarees.

The package includes air-conditioned transportation, darshan at the temple and entry fees, food and refreshments, and a hands-on weaving workshop. The tour, organised on weekends, costs Rs 2,100 for adults and Rs 1,680 for children.

For bookings and further details, visit the link https://tgtdc.in/package/pochampally or call CRO Basheerbagh at 98485 4037, IRO Yatri Nivas Secunderabad at 98481 26947 or Paryatak Bhavan at 9848306435.

item.title: Editorial: Superbugs on the rise
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: India’s indiscriminate antibiotic use is turning it into a global epicentre of antimicrobial resistance
item.content:encoded:
More than half of all antibiotics are sold in India without valid prescriptions. The indiscriminate use of antibiotics is turning India into a global epicentre of antimicrobial resistance. AMR occurs when microbes, which are exposed to high-grade antibiotics, become used to them over time and become resistant to them. This makes treating common infections difficult, increasing the risk of severe illness and death. The resistance also makes them ineffective in preventing secondary infections during surgeries and managing chronic infections. As a result, these microbes become superbugs. Resistance to critical antibiotics, including carbapenems, which are used to treat severe hospital infections, continues to rise. Without effective intervention, annual AMR-related deaths in India could approach two million by 2050. In November 2025, the Centre launched the second round of the National Action Plan on AMR for 2025-2029 with a renewed focus on public awareness, stronger laboratories and surveillance systems, infection prevention and control, research and innovation, and improved governance and intersectoral coordination. Though the initiative marked a shift towards implementation and accountability, the core challenges remain formidable. These include inappropriate antibiotic use, weak regulatory mechanisms, uneven laboratory capacity, gaps in hospital infection control, and inadequate coordination across sectors. One of the biggest challenges is that AMR is not only a health-sector issue. Tackling it requires coordination among various ministries, State governments, environmental regulators and pharmaceutical manufacturers. The latest official surveillance reports from the National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network (NARS-Net) and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) AMR Surveillance Network paint a worrying picture.

Official surveillance figures show a rapid decline in the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotics. Infections caused by certain antibiotic-resistant bacteria are now common in hospital intensive care units (ICUs). Some show resistance to more than 70 per cent of the strongest antibiotics. When these superbugs strike, patients need longer treatment, costlier drugs and often face a higher risk of death. Families are pushed into debt, while hospitals are stretched to their limits. Poorly treated waste from drug factories and hospitals adds resistant bacteria to our water and soil. These germs find their way back into our food and environment, creating a vicious cycle. Experts have described AMR as a slow-moving pandemic that could undermine modern medicine unless tackled urgently. A large share of India’s healthcare is delivered by private providers. However, bringing private hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies into surveillance and stewardship systems remains a continuing challenge. Primary health centres and district hospitals often lack rapid microbiological testing, forcing clinicians to rely on broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics rather than targeted therapy. Public health specialists and infectious disease clinicians stress the need to move beyond awareness campaigns towards structural enforcement and better infection prevention measures. They recommended stricter enforcement of prescription laws, curbing substandard drugs, setting up dedicated AMS committees across both public and private hospitals to audit prescriptions, restrict reserve antibiotics, and stop prolonged post-surgical prophylaxis. Doctors, too, must avoid unnecessary prescriptions and follow strict antibiotic rules.

item.title: Woman accuses live-in partner of refusing marriage after engagement in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A woman in Hyderabad has accused her live-in partner of refusing to marry her after their engagement despite an earlier promise of marriage. She alleged that he coerced her into undergoing an abortion and later demanded an additional Rs 20 lakh as dowry.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A woman lodged a complaint with the Madhura Nagar police, alleging that a man who had been in a live-in relationship with her after promising marriage later refused to marry her despite their engagement.

According to the complaint, Aravind, a resident of Mancherial, allegedly lived with the woman and coerced her into undergoing an abortion. Their engagement was held in October in the presence of elders from both families.

She further alleged that he later demanded an additional Rs 20 lakh as dowry and refused to proceed with the marriage.

The Madhura Nagar police are investigating.

item.title: Telangana moves SSC certificate correction process online through MeeSeva
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana School Education Department has shifted the SSC certificate correction process to the MeeSeva portal, ending the offline application system. Students seeking changes in personal details such as name, parents' names or date of birth must now apply digitally.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Students seeking corrections in their original SSC certificates must now apply online as the School Education department has done away with the age-old process of offline application.

In a recently issued proceeding order, School Education Director Dr. E Naveen Nicolas said submission and processing of proposals for correction of details in original SSC certificates would be carried out through the MeeSeva portal.

He instructed officials concerned and headmasters/principals not to entertain or forward physical/manual proposals for correction of original SSC certificates to the department.

Previously, students seeking corrections in their name, parents’ names, or date of birth on their SSC marks certificate had to apply offline by paying the required fee via bank challan.

As per the new process, applicants must submit their SSC memo correction application through a MeeSeva centre. Thereafter, the application will be routed to the school where the applicant studied Class X.

The headmaster or principal of the school concerned will examine the proposal in the student information system on the ISMS portal. The school authorities must upload necessary documents and present their remarks.

The application will then be forwarded to the mandal educational officer, who can either approve or reject it. If approved, it will move to the District Educational Officer (DEO), where it will be scrutinised by the clerk, superintendent and assistant director before being placed before the DEO for approval.

After the DEO’s approval, the application will be sent to the Director of School Education. If cleared here, the application will be sent to the Directorate of Government Examinations.

Once the final approval is granted, the corrected SSC memo will be uploaded online. If an application is rejected at any stage, officials concerned must provide reasons for rejection.

item.title: Sridhar Babu calls for technology to address real-world challenges at UN summit
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana IT Minister D Sridhar Babu said technological advancement should address real-world challenges and not be limited to economic growth while addressing the Global Impact Summit at the United Nations.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: IT Minister D Sridhar Babu emphasised that technological advancement should go beyond economic growth and help address real-world challenges.

He addressed the Global Impact Summit at the United Nations, organised by 1M1B, on Friday.

The Minister said Telangana had established itself as an important destination for information technology, life sciences and pharmaceuticals. It is expanding its focus to artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing and other emerging technologies, he said.

Highlighting the State Government’s focus on artificial intelligence and digital innovation, he said these technologies offer significant opportunities to improve healthcare, education, sustainability and employment.

“There should be stronger collaboration among governments, industry, academic institutions, startups and global organisations to build an innovation ecosystem capable of developing solutions with wider social and economic impact,” Sridhar Babu said.

He highlighted Telangana’s strengths in IT, Global Capability Centres (GCCs), pharmaceuticals and biotechnology, and outlined Hyderabad’s ambition to emerge as a global centre for artificial intelligence, research, talent development and technology-led entrepreneurship.

Sridhar Babu also emphasised the importance of equipping young people with industry-relevant skills and providing aspiring innovators and entrepreneurs with the opportunities and platforms to take their ideas to the global stage.

item.title: Two killed after falling from Kerala Express at Rebbena station in Asifabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A man and a woman, both aged around 25, were killed after reportedly falling from the New Delhi-bound Kerala Express at Rebbena railway station in Telangana's Kumram Bheem Asifabad district. The victims remained unidentified till Friday evening.
item.content:encoded:
Kumram Bheem Asifabad: A man and woman were killed when they reportedly slipped from the New Delhi bound Kerala express at Rebbena railway station on Friday.

Government railway police said the bodies had not been identified as no one had come forward to claim them till Friday evening. The man and woman aged around 25 were killed. The police were coordinating with their counterparts of Maharashtra and other states to ascertain reasons behind the incident and identify the victims.

Police said the bodies were preserved at a government hospital for identification. A case has been registered and an investigation has been launched.

item.title: Large python rescued from cotton field in Khammam’s Chintakani
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A large python was rescued from a cotton field in Nerada village of Khammam district after farm labourers spotted the reptile while harvesting cotton. Forest Department officials, assisted by local residents, panchayat staff and labourers, captured the 70-kg python and later released it into a forest area.
item.content:encoded:
Khammam: A large python was rescued from a cotton field at Nerada village of Chintakani mandal in the district on Friday.

The incident occurred near Sri Gangamma temple at the village where farm labourers picking up cotton spotted the python and were terrified. They informed the sarpanch, Dusari Netaji about the reptile and he alerted forest department personnel.

Forest department officials, with help from farm labourers, panchayat staff and local residents, caught the python, which weighed about 70 kilograms and later released it into a forest area.

item.title: KTR, Harish Rao greet Chukka Ramaiah on 101st birthday
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president K T Rama Rao and BRSLP deputy leader T Harish Rao extended birthday greetings to noted educationist Chukka Ramaiah on his 101st birthday. The leaders praised his contribution to IIT entrance coaching and his role in the Telangana movement, describing him as an inspiration to generations of students.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao and BRSLP deputy leader T Harish Rao on Friday extended birthday greetings to noted educationist Chukka Ramaiah on his 101st birthday. They recalled his contribution to coaching students for the IIT entrance examinations and his role in the Telangana movement.

Taking to X, Rama Rao termed Ramaiah a mathematics teacher who transformed ordinary students into achievers and helped many realise their dream of entering the IITs. He said Ramaiah’s century-long journey, with IITs becoming synonymous with his name, was an inspiration to generations of students.

Recalling his contribution to education, the BRS leader said Ramaiah had left an indelible mark on history and prayed for his good health and well-being.

Harish Rao called Ramaiah, popularly known as ‘IIT Ramaiah’, a guiding force who not only taught IIT subjects in classrooms but also provided intellectual direction during the Telangana movement.

He said Ramaiah’s commitment to education, simplicity and discipline made him an inspiration. Harish Rao wished him good health and a long life.

item.title: KTR assures BRS support for nationwide OBC caste census
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao has extended the party's support to the demand for a nationwide OBC caste census, arguing that accurate population data is essential for reservations and equitable representation.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao on Friday extended the party’s full support to the demand for a nationwide OBC caste census. He emphasised the need for accurate population data to provide reservations and equitable opportunities in education, employment and political representation to Backward Classes (BCs).

A delegation of the All India OBC Students Organisation, met Rama Rao and sought the BRS’s support. The delegation included coordinators Jayanth Yadav, Rajinikanth Goud, Muralikrishna, Chidvilas, Kiran and Lokesh.

Speaking on the occasion, Rama Rao recalled that the previous BRS government passed an Assembly resolution seeking reservations for OBCs in legislatures and forwarded it to the Centre. BRS MP Vaddiraju Ravichandra had also raised the demand for a caste census in Parliament, he said.

He stated that the previous government had provided BC and most backward class communities with representation in local bodies, the Rajya Sabha, the Legislative Council and nominated posts. It had also prioritised their education and economic empowerment through residential schools, scholarships, fee reimbursement and free coaching for competitive examinations.

The former Minister reminded that the K Chandrashekhar Rao government allotted land and sanctioned funds for buildings for BC caste associations in Hyderabad. It had also introduced community-specific support programmes, including free electricity for Nayee Brahmins, fish seed distribution to Mudiraj and Gangaputra communities and subsidised sheep distribution to Yadavs.

“The BRS government supported handloom workers through loan waivers, employment under the Bathukamma saree programme and procurement of handloom products,” he said.

He felt that a nationwide caste census will provide the data needed to assess the population and socio-economic conditions of backward communities and ensure reservations and welfare measures in proportion to their numbers.

item.title: Priyanka Arul Mohan gets birthday surprise as Ravi Teja’s ‘Thulabaram’ team releases her first look
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The makers of Ravi Teja and Vivek Athreya's upcoming Telugu entertainer Thulabaram unveiled actress Priyanka Arul Mohan's character look as Krishnaveni on her birthday. The film, produced by Bridge Productions, is expected to blend crime, drama and entertainment.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The makers of director Vivek Athreya’s eagerly awaited Telugu commercial entertainer ‘Thulabaram’, featuring Telugu star Ravi Teja in the lead, released the look of actress Priyanka Arul Mohan in the film on the occasion of the actress’ birthday on Friday.

Taking to its social media timelines, Bridge Productions, the production house which is producing the film, wrote, “Every #Thulabharam needs its perfect balance… and ours has a little extra sparkle. A very Happy Birthday @priyankaamohanofficial. With love, The #Thulabharam gang.

The Crime Maharaja @raviteja_2628 @tharunbhascker @vishnuviv @anaswara.rajan @jdmaxmode @oddphysce @thenieswar_isc @raviteja_girijala #GMSekhar @srinivas_raju_i #Laxman #SriniRao @BridgeProdoffl.”

For the unaware, actress Priyanka Arul Mohan plays a character called Krishnaveni in the film.

Ravi Teja, who is currently riding high on the success of the blockbuster ‘Irumudi’, is set to explore a new dimension with this intriguing project. Produced by Laxman and Srini Rao under the banner of Bridge Productions, the film is bringing together two creative forces with contrasting yet compelling strengths.

With Ravi Teja’s trademark energy and Vivek Athreya’s distinctive storytelling, expectations from the film are high. Sources in the know claim that the film will seek to deliver a refreshing story which will blend crime, drama and entertainment.

The title of the film, which was initially being referred to as #RT78, was announced in October this year when the film was officially launched.

The makers had unveiled a ‘Title Documentary,’ an innovative announcement video that had revealed the film’s title through Vivek Athreya’s characteristic storytelling style.

The video took audiences through the fun, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining process behind the selection of the intriguing title- Thulabharam, offering a glimpse into the quirky creative world of the filmmaker.

The video also introduced the key characters of the film. Anil Karella was introduced as Jadeja, Ravi Anthony as Robin, Anaswara Rajan as Sound, Tharun Bhascker as Devaraj, JD Chakravarthy as Sivaji Rao, and Priyanka Mohan as Krishnaveni.

The technical team of the film features several accomplished names. Vivek Sagar, a frequent collaborator of Vivek Athreya, is to compose the music for this film while gifted cameraman Theni Eswar will be in charge of cinematography. Raviteja Girijala will handle the editing, and GM Sekhar will oversee the production design as art director.

item.title: Four held for duping people of Rs 1.45 lakh in cryptocurrency scam in Adilabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Four representatives of a cryptocurrency firm were arrested in Adilabad for allegedly cheating two residents of Rs 1.45 lakh by promising high returns on cryptocurrency investments. Two of the accused had earlier been taken into custody in a separate case involving an alleged Rs 10 crore fraud affecting 500 people.
item.content:encoded:
Adilabad: Four persons were arrested for duping two people of Rs 1.45 lakh under the guise of cryptocurrency here on Friday.

Police said Polamarashetti Rathnaraju, Dondapati Laxman Rao, Gajula Pramod and Vemula Sudheer, all representatives of ITC Global Crypto Currency Pvt Limited, were apprehended for their role in cheating the two persons from Adilabad.

During the investigation, the four reportedly confessed to committing the offence. They admitted to cheating Mekala Rakesh and Duvvada Narasimhulu of the town by luring them with huge profits on investments in cryptocurrency in 2023. They disclosed that they extracted Rs 95,000 from Rakesh and Rs 50,000 from Narasimhulu.

Rathnaraju of Visakhapatnam and Laxmanarao of West Godavari district had earlier been taken into custody for allegedly duping 500 people from both Telangana and Andhra Pradesh of Rs 10 crore in October.

item.title: Telangana records season’s first single-digit temperature at 9.6 degrees
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Winter conditions have intensified across Hyderabad and Telangana, with Sangareddy recording the season's first single-digit minimum temperature of 9.6 degrees Celsius. Several districts and Hyderabad's outskirts experienced chilly mornings, while temperatures in multiple locations dropped close to 10 degrees.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Winter appears to have firmly tightened its grip in Hyderabad and districts of Telangana, with temperatures dropping significantly and the season’s first single-digit minimum temperature of 9.6 degrees Celsius recorded at Satar in Sangareddy district in the early hours of Friday.

Cold wave-like conditions intensified particularly in western and northern Telangana, where dry weather continued to prevail. In the last 24 hours, Sangareddy emerged as the coldest district in Telangana, with multiple mandals hovering near the 10-degree mark.

Based on TSDPS data, some of the other regions that recorded a sharp drop in temperatures (in degrees Celsius) in Sangareddy include Kohir (9.7), Nyalkal and Jharasangam (10). In Zahirabad, Algole recorded 10.3, while Malchelma and Mogdampalle recorded 11.

Dongli in Kamareddy recorded 10.5 degrees Celsius, while Reddy Palle in Rangareddy’s Moinabad mandal followed closely at 10.7 degrees Celsius.

Chilly mornings in Greater Hyderabad and outskirts

While core urban areas of Hyderabad experienced relatively milder nights, locations such as Tirumalagiri recorded 15.2 degrees Celsius and West Maredpally recorded 15.8 degrees Celsius. The outskirts and IT corridor, however, witnessed a significant drop in mercury.

Patancheru and the BHEL region recorded the lowest temperature at 12.2 degrees Celsius, followed closely by the BHEL Factory area in Ramachandrapuram at 12.5 degrees Celsius.

Some of the other regions in Hyderabad and surrounding districts that recorded a sharp dip in temperatures include the University of Hyderabad (Serilingampally) (12.6), Kistareddipet and Sultanpur in Ameenpur (13.0 and 13.3 degrees Celsius, respectively). The Gachibowli region registered 14 degrees Celsius, while MMTS Lingampally recorded 15.1 degrees Celsius.

The Moula-Ali region recorded 13.6 degrees Celsius, while the mercury at Rajendranagar dipped to 13.7 degrees Celsius.

item.title: TBGKS to embark on Singareni Parirakshana Yatra for worker’s welfare, company’s wellbeing
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana Boggu Ghani Karmika Sangham will launch the Singareni Parirakshana Yatra in December across 11 operational areas. The campaign will highlight workers' demands, including pending dues, promotions, wage revisions, land allotment, loans and reinstatement of dismissed employees.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: Telangana Boggu Ghani Karmika Sangham (TBGKS) has planned to embark on the ‘Singareni Parirakshana Yatra’, demanding workers’ welfare measures and seeking to safeguard the company’s interests.

The sangham’s leadership stated that the failure of the recognised and representative trade unions had caused Singareni workers to lose many of their hard-won rights. Similarly, coal production was suffering because of several lapses in the management.

The recognised and representative unions, AITUC and INTUC, which ought to be fighting against the management, had instead limited themselves to lobbying for personal favours, thereby doing a great injustice to the workers.
