Even though their term of recognition had expired, the AITUC, accustomed to influence peddling, was clinging to its position of power, fearing the prospect of fresh elections, alleged the sangham State general secretary, Kapu Krishna.

All these issues had warranted action. Hence, the TBGKS decided to take up the yatra at a recent central committee meeting attended by its State president Miriyala Raji Reddy and central committee leaders from all areas.

Prior to launching the yatra, meetings with BRS MLAs and former MLAs in all SCCL areas would be held. The Singareni Parirakshana Yatra would be launched in December, covering all the 11 SCCL operational areas, Krishna told Telangana Today.

During the yatra, issues and demands such as the clearance of outstanding dues of Rs 60,000 crore owed to SCCL by Genco and Transco, allocation of coal mines to SCCL without going through the auction process, pending promotions and internal examinations would be highlighted.

Focus would also be laid on the 12th Wage Board, payment of an interim relief of 40 percent to workers, allotment of 250 square yards of land, an interest-free loan of Rs 20 lakh to workers and reinstatement of all workers dismissed since 2019, including those dismissed in 2026.

The TBGKS also wanted the issue of discrepancies in names (alias/recorded names) to be resolved, appointment letters to be issued to 300 dependents on the waiting list, one medical board meeting to be convened every month to assess and declare workers unfit, and necessary tools and spare parts, which are currently in short supply at Singareni, to be procured, Krishna added.

item.title: Mancherial rice millers raise concerns over CMR conditions
item.dc:creator: Indrajeet Devulapally
item.description: Rice millers in Mancherial have raised concerns over government conditions for undertaking Custom Milling Rice during Kharif 2026-27. They have sought relaxations in paddy storage, quality checks, solvency certificates and penalties, stating that the existing rules favour the government.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: Private rice millers sent a list of concerns to officials regarding the acceptance of paddy allocated by the government and undertaking the Custom Milling Rice (CMR) process in the district for the forthcoming Kharif season.

The rice millers informed the officials that they were ready to accept paddy under CMR for Kharif 2026-27. They, however, expressed concern over certain conditions set by the government for entering into an agreement with the millers to carry out the process. They submitted a representation to the authorities during a meeting with millers and officials, explaining their constraints and seeking relaxations.

For instance, the millers clarified that they could not separately store seven varieties of fine paddy identified by the government for offering a bonus. They expressed their inability to deploy a representative at Paddy Procurement Centres to determine the quality and quantity of the grains. They stated that they could not submit a solvency certificate five times higher than the value of the paddy, as mentioned by the government in the conditions of the agreement.

The millers disclosed that none was coming forward to stand as a guarantor as criminal and civil cases would be booked against defaulting millers. They urged the officials to consider the shortage caused by the resultant broken rice as rice. They said that the broken rice was supplied to poultry farms and liquor manufacturing companies. They register 10 percent broken rice when 100 kg of paddy is milled.

They clarified that they would sign the agreements if the government relaxed the conditions. They opined that the rules were completely in favour of the government and did not protect the rights of millers. They said they were not allowed to approach a court if an official intentionally harassed a miller. “We would not be able to earn a single penny, but would face inconvenience for accepting paddy under the CMR process,” they regretted.

According to information provided by agriculture officials, paddy would be cultivated on 1.10 lakh acres in the district during the coming Kharif season. Officials estimated that the district would register a yield of 2 lakh metric tonnes this time. About 300 centres would be set up to procure paddy from farmers.

item.title: Traffic advisory issued for Guru Nanak Jayanti celebrations in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Hyderabad Traffic Police will enforce traffic diversions in several parts of the city from 4 pm to 10 pm on Saturday, November 21, for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Sri Guru Nanak Dev.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Hyderabad Traffic Police will impose traffic diversions in parts of the city from 4 pm to 10 pm Saturday, November 21, for the 557th birth anniversary celebrations of Sri Guru Nanak Dev.

The procession will begin at Ashok Bazar Gurudwara and pass through Afzalgunj, S.A. Bazar, M.J. Market, Putlibowli, Gowliguda Chaman and Shanker Sher Hotel before returning to the Gurudwara.

Traffic congestion is expected along the procession route, police said.

The police advised commuters to take alternative routes and follow traffic updates. For travel assistance, commuters may contact the traffic helpline on 9010203626.

item.title: HMWSSB announces 24-hour water supply disruption in parts of Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Drinking water supply will be fully or partially disrupted for 24 hours in parts of Suraram and Saibaba Nagar wards in Hyderabad from 9 pm on November 21 to 9 pm on November 22. The disruption is due to the diversion of a 700-mm drinking water pipeline.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Drinking water supply will be fully or partially disrupted for 24 hours in parts of Suraram and Saibaba Nagar wards from 9 pm on November 21 to 9 pm on November 22.

In a press release, the HMWSSB on Friday stated that the affected areas include Vishwakarma Colony, Vaishnavi Nagar, Vema Reddy Nagar, Lakshmi Nagar, Suraram Village, Telugu Thalli Nagar, Jai Bhim Nagar, Maitri Nagar and Suraram Colony.

The disruption is due to diversion work on a 700mm-diameter drinking water pipeline opposite Malla Reddy Hospital on Suraram Main Road. The pipeline is being shifted to complete the remaining work on an 800mm sewer pipeline from Suraram Cheruvu to the 14 MLD sewage treatment plant at Shivalaya Nagar. About 95% of the sewer pipeline work has been completed, according to the press release.

“Consumers have been asked to use water sparingly,” HMWSSB appealed.

item.title: Cases filed against ‘Chanti Bhai Gang’ members in Khammam
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Khammam police have initiated legal action against several youths accused of promoting gangster culture on social media and engaging in intimidating public behaviour. The Task Force arrested individuals linked to the 'Chanti Bhai Gang', while another youth was held for openly brandishing swords during a birthday celebration in the city.
item.content:encoded:
Khammam: The district police cracked down on youths creating panic among the public by promoting themselves as gangsters under various aliases on social media platforms and celebrating birthdays in public while brandishing knives.

In one such incident in Khammam, One-town CI Sabir Pasha stated that cases had been registered against individuals who were creating a stir on social media under the name ‘Chanti Bhai Gang’. Legal proceedings had been initiated against them.

The Task Force police arrested Mohammad Wajeed, a youth from Shukravarapupeta in the city for posting content and videos on social media projecting himself as a gangster under the gang name, he said.

In another case, Tellapotta Murali Krishna of Pinapaka village in Tallada mandal, currently residing near Khammam bus depot, was arrested for posting intimidating content on social media platforms and portraying himself as a ‘rowdy’ (gangster). He was handed over to the Two-town police for further legal action.

Similarly, Task Force police apprehended Voloji Rakesh, a youth of Chinnamandava in Chintakani mandal, who was seen openly brandishing swords while celebrating a birthday in the middle of the road on Thursday night at Gattaiah centre in the city, the Two-town CI Ramakrishna said.

item.title: Watch: Telangana Youth Congress leaders create ruckus at Meta office in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Youth Congress leaders staged a protest at Meta's Hyderabad office against the blocking of Congress workers' social media accounts. The protesters allegedly damaged furniture and equipment, prompting police intervention. Raidurgam police took 21 workers into custody before releasing them.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Tension prevailed at the Meta office in Hyderabad on Friday after Youth Congress leaders barged into the premises and damaged furniture and other equipment. They were protesting against the blocking of social media accounts belonging to Congress workers and leaders.

The Youth Congress warned the Meta management to lift the restrictions, threatening to shut down its offices if the accounts were not restored.

A group of Youth Congress leaders carrying their organisation’s flags entered the premises and raised slogans of “Meta down down”. They also held placards that read, “Hey Meta, grow spine. Don’t be a dalaal for BJP-RSS.”

Security personnel tried to stop the protesters as they entered the office but failed to prevent them from proceeding. The Youth Congress leaders damaged flower pots and furniture on the premises. Videos of the incident were later shared on social media platforms.

Raidurgam police reached the Meta office after receiving information about the incident. They tried to stop the protesters, but the Youth Congress leaders argued with them. Tension prevailed at the office for some time.

The Telangana Youth Congress shared a video of the protest on X and accused Meta of blocking opposition accounts and silencing independent voices.

“IYC Congress workers stormed into BJP ka Beta – META’s Hyderabad Office. Enough of blocking opposition accounts and silencing independent voices. Meta must follow India’s constitution, not the BJP’s orders,” the organisation posted.

It further warned Meta to remove restrictions on all accounts within seven days or face the closure of its offices.

“Stop the censorship. The countdown begins,” the Youth Congress said in its post.

Raidurgam police took 21 Youth Congress workers into custody and later released them, reports said.

#BREAKING: IYC workers stormed into BJP ka BETA – META’s Hyderabad office!

Enough of blocking opposition accounts and silencing independent voices!

Meta must follow India’s Constitution, NOT the BJP’s orders.

Remove restrictions from all accounts within 7 days, or we will shut down your offices everywhere!

Stop the censorship. The countdown begins!

— Telangana Youth Congress (@IYCTelangana) November 20, 2026

item.title: Ex-MLA Ajmeera Rekha Naik terms ED searches politically motivated
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Former Khanapur MLA Ajmeera Rekha Naik alleged that the Enforcement Directorate's searches at her residence and rice mill were politically motivated and claimed she was targeted for being a tribal woman.
item.content:encoded:
Nirmal: Former Khanapur MLA Ajmeera Rekha Naik alleged that the searches by the Enforcement Directorate were politically motivated. She spoke to media persons in Khanapur on Friday.

Responding to the simultaneous searches by the ED at her residence and rice mill, Rekha wondered why the sleuths did not inspect the residence and rice stocks of the defaulting miller. She said that it appeared that she was targeted for being a tribal woman. She clarified that she would clear all dues owed to the government.

The former MLA further claimed she had cooperated with ED officials during the searches. She regretted that she suffered losses in rice milling at her two mills as she was fully occupied serving the public as a legislator. She said that she was surprised by the searches being conducted when she was not an MLA.

Rekha Naik further said that her mills owed Rs 12 crore, but were fined Rs 22 crore for defaulting on paddy procurement obligations. She disclosed that the mills incurred losses of Rs 12 crore after paddy stocks were damaged by rain. She reiterated that she did not commit a crime and would repay the government’s dues.

item.title: TREA seeks inquiry into intake well sump construction at Nagarjunasagar
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Retired Engineers Association inspected an intake well sump under construction in Nagarjunasagar reservoir's backwaters near Vijayapuri South. The association raised concerns over alleged regulatory violations and sought an inquiry into permissions and potential risks to reservoir safety.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: The Telangana Retired Engineers Association (TREA) inspected the construction of an intake well sump in the backwaters of the Nagarjunasagar reservoir near Vijayapuri South. The association alleged that the work was being carried out in violation of the reservoir’s regulations. A team led by TREA Convenor Shyam Prasad Reddy visited the construction site on Friday to examine the ongoing work in the reservoir’s backwaters.

During the inspection, Shyam Prasad Reddy examined the construction activities on the right bank and questioned how permission had been granted for work that appeared to violate established regulations. The TREA team also examined whether the construction of the intake well sump posed any threat to the safety of the Nagarjunasagar reservoir. The inspection covered various aspects of water resource conservation and the safety of the project.

Shyam Prasad Reddy questioned the procedures followed by the authorities in permitting the construction. He also sought details from officials about the regulations and permissions governing construction activities within the reservoir area.

He demanded that the authorities take action to prevent any construction that could compromise the safety of the project. The association stressed that the authorities were responsible for protecting water resources and ensuring the safety of the reservoir. It also called for clarity on the permissions granted and the regulations governing the construction of the intake well sump.

The TREA team requested officials to conduct a comprehensive inquiry into the alleged unauthorised construction and take appropriate action if any violations were established.

item.title: Australian companies explore technology partnerships in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 36-company Australian business delegation visited Hyderabad as part of the Australian DigiTech Mission. Led by Austrade, the mission explored partnerships with local technology and healthcare sectors, focusing on AI, cybersecurity, digital health, emerging technologies and startup collaboration.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Australian Trade and Investment Commission (Austrade), in partnership with the Tech Council of Australia, led a mission involving 36 Australian companies to Bengaluru and Hyderabad from November 16 to 20.

The Australian DigiTech Mission’s visit to T-Hub in Hyderabad focused on exploring collaborations and commercial partnerships. The mission was powered by the Accessing New Markets Initiative (ANMI), an A$55 million programme designed and jointly delivered by Austrade and industry to help Australian businesses diversify and grow their exports.

In Hyderabad, the mission participated in a networking session organised in collaboration with NASSCOM and HYSEA, connecting delegates with representatives of the local IT industry and healthcare sector. Discussions focused on digital innovation, emerging technologies and partnership opportunities, enabling delegates to explore avenues for collaboration, investment and knowledge exchange.

Following the networking engagement, the mission visited T-Hub, which Austrade described as the world’s largest home for startups, to gain insights into Hyderabad’s innovation ecosystem and explore potential avenues for collaboration.

Mary Overington, Trade and Investment Commissioner, Austrade South Asia, said, “Hyderabad’s technology industry, healthcare sector and startup ecosystem offer valuable opportunities for Australian businesses to build partnerships in AI, cybersecurity, digital health and deep tech.”

item.title: Hyderabad-based CCMB identifies two genes that help nerves regrow after spinal injury
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
item.description: Researchers at Hyderabad's CCMB have identified two genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, that trigger nerve-fibre regrowth after spinal cord injury in adult mice. The findings showed partial movement recovery and could help develop future gene therapies for spinal cord repair.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Researchers at the Hyderabad-based Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) have identified two genes, NR2F1 and NR2F6, that trigger nerve-fibre regrowth after spinal cord injury in adult mice and restore partial movement. The finding could pave the way for spinal cord therapies in the future.

A spinal cord injury severs movement-related commands travelling from the brain to the rest of the body, resulting in paralysis. Injured nerve fibres in the adult mammalian brain and spinal cord usually do not grow back. Decades of research have established why adult neurons lose this ability to regrow, and no treatment currently restores the lost connections.

Led by Dr Ishwariya Venkatesh, with Yogesh Sahu as the first author, the CCMB study, published in The EMBO Journal, found that adult neurons retain the genetic instructions for regeneration, but regulatory proteins that switch on growth-driving genes fade as the brain matures.

While studying the developing mouse brain, the team pinpointed NR2F1 and NR2F6, neither of which had previously been linked to nerve growth in the brain or spinal cord.

Restoring either gene in adult mice with a crushed spinal cord enabled nerve fibres to cross the injury site and grow up to 1.5 millimetres beyond it. Untreated mice showed stunted fibres that stopped at the scar.

From five weeks after injury, treated mice showed lasting improvements in grip strength, hind-limb lifting while walking and backward pushing.

“Adult neurons have not lost the programme for regrowth. They have been silenced as the brain matures. Our work shows that there are two different molecular routes that can bring that programme back, and both lead to recovery,” Dr Venkatesh said.

While the study remains preclinical, with genes delivered before injury and only partial recovery achieved, identifying two distinct routes opens new possibilities for developing gene therapies for spinal cord repair, the researchers added.

item.title: BRS leaders flay Revanth for personal attacks, accuse him of ignoring public issues
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS MLA and former minister Vemula Prashanth Reddy criticised Chief Minister Revanth Reddy, alleging that his public meetings in Siddipet and Sircilla focused on attacking opposition leaders rather than addressing farmers' concerns, drought and governance issues.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Former Minister and BRS MLA Vemula Prashanth Reddy on Friday criticised Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy over his remarks at Siddipet, accusing him of using public meetings to target opposition leaders instead of addressing farmers’ problems, drought and governance issues.

He said the Chief Minister failed to offer answers on public issues and focused on attacking BRS president K Chandrashekhar Rao, working president KT Rama Rao and BRSLP deputy leader T Harish Rao.

Addressing a press conference at Telangana Bhavan, Prashanth Reddy questioned the purpose of Revanth Reddy’s meetings in Sircilla and Siddipet, saying they were aimed at personal attacks on BRS leaders.

He said the Chief Minister should explain what his government had delivered rather than repeatedly criticising the previous regime. He also questioned Revanth Reddy’s announcement that winners in Sircilla and Siddipet would be made Ministers, when three Cabinet berths remained vacant.

The former Minister accused the Congress government of discontinuing several welfare schemes introduced by the Chandrashekhar Rao government and failing to protect Telangana’s water interests. He said the government allowed water from the Kannepalli pumps to flow downstream towards Andhra Pradesh, contributing to the irrigation crisis in the State. He termed the prevailing drought as a consequence of the government’s failure rather than natural conditions.

He also demanded a probe by a sitting judge into allegations of corruption made by Congress MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy against the Chief Minister and his family. He referred to the MLA’s reported claim that Rs 5 lakh crore had been amassed through land deals.

item.title: Harish Rao challenges Revanth Reddy to contest against him from Siddipet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS leader T Harish Rao challenged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to contest against him from Siddipet and demanded an Assembly debate on irrigation. He accused the Congress government of compromising Telangana's Krishna water interests and neglecting farmers.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRSLP deputy leader T Harish Rao on Friday challenged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to contest against him from Siddipet in the next Assembly election. He accused the Chief Minister of resorting to personal attacks to divert attention from the Congress government’s failures in protecting Telangana’s irrigation interests and addressing public grievances.

“I dare you to contest against me from Siddipet as a Congress candidate and let the people decide,” Harish Rao said at a press conference at Telangana Bhavan. He also challenged Revanth Reddy to convene the Assembly and allow him to speak without interruptions, promising to present evidence of the government’s alleged betrayal of Telangana’s water interests.

In a strong rebuttal to the Chief Minister’s public meeting in Siddipet on Thursday, Harish accused the Congress government of allowing Andhra Pradesh to draw Krishna water at Telangana’s expense. He said nearly 1,000 TMCft of river water was allowed to flow downstream instead of being diverted into the State’s reservoirs. Calling Revanth Reddy a “covert, subvert and pervert”, he accused him of helping Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu deprive Telangana of its water share.

Harish questioned the Chief Minister’s claim that the previous BRS government had agreed to a 299 TMCft share in the Krishna river. He said it was only a temporary arrangement following bifurcation and challenged Revanth Reddy to prove that the BRS government had accepted the 299:512 TMCft ratio. “If you prove that we signed the 299:512 ratio, I will resign. If you cannot, are you ready to quit as Chief Minister?” he asked.

He said the ratio figured in the 2013 submission made by the then united Andhra Pradesh government to the Justice Srikrishna Committee. He cited the BRS government’s efforts to secure a fresh tribunal under Section 3, including its representations to the Apex Council and the Supreme Court.

Disputing Revanth Reddy’s claim that Telangana lacked pumps and motors to lift water, the former Irrigation Minister asked why the Devadula pumps were not being operated at full capacity and why water was not being lifted from the Srisailam project. He alleged that the State was not utilising even its existing Krishna water allocation. Stating that crops on 25 lakh acres withered during the Vanakalam (Kharif) season due to the government’s apathy, he demanded a white paper on the number of motors operated, their running hours and the quantity of water lifted, including in Palamuru.

Harish Rao said the Pothireddypadu project and the proposed Banakacherla link reflected attempts to divert Telangana’s water. He recalled that, as the then TRS Minister in the Congress government, he had resigned from the united Andhra Pradesh Cabinet in protest against the Pothireddypadu project, with party legislators stalling the Assembly for 40 days over the issue.

Accusing the Congress of being responsible for Telangana’s water disputes with Andhra Pradesh, he said the previous BRS government had overcome several challenges and safeguarded the State’s interests, while the Revanth Reddy government was reversing that progress.

Harish also accused the government of failing to provide adequate drought relief, crop bonuses and support to farmers. He contrasted the situation with the previous government’s Rythu Bandhu and other welfare programmes, alleging that the Congress had neglected the support systems established during K Chandrashekhar Rao’s tenure.

Citing criticism by Congress MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy and other legislators, Harish alleged that discontent over governance and corruption was growing within the ruling party. He said the Chief Minister had devoted much of his Siddipet speech to attacking BRS leaders rather than explaining the Indiramma family life insurance scheme or addressing public concerns.

“KCR, me and BRS working president KT Rama Rao were mentioned 140 times in the Chief Minister’s hour-long speech,” he added. He stated that more people had been brought to the Siddipet meeting from other districts than the number of local attendees, citing police directions on parking arrangements for buses.

Harish said though Revanth Reddy claimed to have sanctioned funds for Siddipet, development works worth Rs 1,070 crore sanctioned for Siddipet constituency during BRS rule were cancelled after the Congress came to power. He said the BRS would continue to question the government on irrigation, farmers’ distress and other public issues and present its evidence in the Assembly.

item.title: KTR dismisses Revanth Reddy as one-time wonder
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao launched a sharp attack on Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, describing him as an 'ATM' for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and predicting his political relevance would end in 2028. Speaking at a summit in Hyderabad, Rama Rao also questioned the Congress government's record on promises, investments, borrowings and employment.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao dismissed Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy as a one-time wonder and an ATM for Congress Lok Sabha leader Rahul Gandhi. He predicted that Revanth Reddy’s political shelf life will end in December 2028, when the BRS will return to power in Telangana.

“Rahul Gandhi has two ATM cards, Revanth Reddy and Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, whose validity will expire in 2028,” he said, participating in the ABP Southern Rising Summit in Hyderabad on Friday.

Taking a dig at Revanth Reddy’s frequent Delhi visits, Rama Rao said the Chief Minister deserved full marks for carrying bags to the national capital but none for fulfilling promises made to Telangana’s people. Referring to the 2015 cash-for-vote case, he said forensic and documentary evidence existed and the matter was pending before the Supreme Court.

He alleged that Revanth had moved from carrying bags in the cash-for-vote episode to taking them to Delhi for the Congress leadership.

On the Congress government’s performance, the BRS working president said the party made 420 promises, 13 declarations and six guarantees during the 2023 elections, assuring their implementation within 100 days. More than 1,000 days had passed, but the government had no answers on their fulfilment.

“The BRS lost the election by just 1.85 percentage points after the Congress showed people a dream world,” he said, accusing the government of spending its time targeting Opposition leaders through cases and commissions rather than delivering its promises.

Rama Rao blamed the Congress government for the drought conditions in Telangana, dubbing it as the “El Congo” effect rather than the impact of El Nino. He also accused the government of damaging poor people’s livelihoods through demolitions through HYDRAA being selectively used for political pressure, blackmail and extortion.

Citing allegations by Congress legislators, he referred to MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy’s claim of corruption worth Rs 5 lakh crore to Rs 10 lakh crore under Revanth Reddy and MLA Anirudh Reddy’s allegation that commissions of 15 to 20 per cent were being demanded for government work. He said the Chief Minister had failed to respond to the charges.

Questioning Revanth Reddy’s claims of attracting investments through visits to Davos, the US and Japan, Rama Rao demanded a white paper on actual investments, industries established and jobs created. He cited State Budget figures showing that technology jobs in Hyderabad had declined from 9.46 lakh in 2023 to 9.39 lakh in 2026-27, a fall of about 7,000 jobs.

He also called the Bharat Summit a Congress Summit, stating that more than Rs 100 crore of public money was spent on promoting Rahul Gandhi and the party. He questioned what tangible benefits the event had brought to Telangana in terms of industries and employment through the event.

Comparing borrowings under the two governments, Rama Rao said the BRS had borrowed Rs 2.8 lakh crore in 10 years and spent the money on programmes such as Rythu Bandhu, Kaleshwaram project, collectorate buildings and 42 flyovers in Hyderabad among others. He alleged that the Congress government borrowed Rs 4.5 lakh crore in three years without delivering a major new welfare scheme or infrastructure project, and challenged Revanth to explain how the money had been spent.

Drawing a parallel between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Revanth Reddy, the BRS working president said both had failed to fulfil major promises, including financial assistance and job creation. He cited Modi’s assurances of Rs 15 lakh for every poor person and two crore jobs, and Revanth’s promises of Rs 15,000 assistance to farmers and two lakh jobs in the first year.

He said Telangana was being pushed into a mess instead of being made a rising State. He asserted that K Chandrashekhar Rao would remain in the hearts of people for his role in the Statehood movement and development during the BRS decade. “Revanth should compare himself with KCR through his work, not words,” he said.

item.title: Congress will not even get Opposition status in next elections: Harish Rao
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS deputy floor leader T Harish Rao predicted that Congress would lose its principal Opposition status in the next elections. Welcoming former Congress leader Sarupu Shyam into the BRS, he criticised the Revanth Reddy government over welfare schemes and farmers' issues.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS deputy floor leader T Harish Rao declared that the Congress would not even secure the status of the principal Opposition party in the next elections. He asserted that the growing number of leaders quitting the ruling party and joining the BRS indicated a changing political trend in Telangana.

He made the remarks while welcoming former Congress leader Sarupu Shyam and his supporters from Medak district into the BRS at Telangana Bhavan here on Friday. Shyam and his followers joined the party after resigning from the Congress.

Addressing the gathering, Harish Rao said Congress leaders across districts were joining the BRS after losing faith in the Revanth Reddy government. He accused the Congress of failing to implement the Six Guarantees and discontinuing several welfare schemes introduced by former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao. He listed KCR Kits, Nutrition Kits, BC Bandhu, fee reimbursement, sheep distribution, Dalit Bandhu and Kanti Velugu among the schemes discontinued by the government.

He also accused the government of failing to ensure 24-hour power supply and adequate urea availability to farmers. He said farmers were receiving only seven to eight hours of electricity and were struggling to procure fertiliser.

Referring to Revanth Reddy’s speech at Siddipet, the BRSLP deputy leader said the Chief Minister was in frustration and hence, focused on personal attacks rather than public issues. “He is so frustrated that he did not speak a word about Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bima scheme that he launched. Instead, he mentioned KCR’s name 63 times, my name 53 times and BRS working president KT Rama Rao’s name 24 times in an hour-long address,” he said.

item.title: Telangana SSC public exams likely to begin on March 17 or 18
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana SSC Public Examinations 2027 are likely to begin on March 17 or 18, with the School Education department having submitted the Class X examination timetable to the government for approval. The department is also accepting examination fee applications, with different deadlines and late-fee slabs notified for students.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The SSC Public Examinations 2027 are likely to commence from March 17 or 18. The School Education department has recently sent a Class X examinations timetable to the government for approval.

This time, the SSC Public Exams timetable is unlikely to extend beyond a month. During the academic year 2025-26, the Class X exams were conducted from March 14 to April 16. The schedule was extended on the lines of the Class X timetable of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) that gives short gaps between subjects. This was done to reduce pressure and anxiety among students.

Meanwhile, the last date to apply and pay the examination fee without a late fee at the respective schools is November 26. With a late fee of Rs 50 and Rs 200, the exam fee will be accepted up to December 8 and 21 respectively. Students can also pay the exam fee with a late fee of Rs 500 between December 23 and January 4, 2027.

The fee for more than three subjects is Rs 125. Similarly, the fee for up to three subjects is Rs 110. In addition to the regular examination fee of Rs 125 for SSC academic courses, vocational students need to pay an additional Rs 60.

item.title: Hyderabad: Ranigunj underpass renovation to trigger traffic congestion for months
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Renovation work on the Ranigunj Railway under Bridge on MG Road is expected to disrupt traffic for six to eight months. Hyderabad Traffic Police have announced diversions for heavy vehicles and identified 18 junctions likely to witness congestion.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Commuters travelling between Secunderabad and other parts of Hyderabad may have to brace for prolonged traffic congestion as major renovation works on the Railway under Bridge (RUB) at Ranigunj Junction on MG Road are set to begin on Friday.

The project, expected to take six to eight months, is likely to disrupt traffic along one of the busiest commercial and transit corridors connecting Secunderabad.

Ranigunj and MG Road serve as crucial connecting routes for commuters travelling to Secunderabad Railway Station, Jubilee Bus Station (JBS), Paradise, Tank Bund and several commercial establishments. With traffic restrictions affecting multiple adjoining roads, passengers heading to railway stations, bus terminals and Metro Rail connectivity points could face longer travel times, particularly during peak hours.

According to the Hyderabad Traffic Police, excavation work extending up to 1.5 metres will cover nearly three carriageway lanes. Only one carriageway will remain available for two-wheelers, auto-rickshaws and cars, while heavy vehicles, including goods vehicles, private travel buses and RTC buses, will be diverted through alternative routes.

Heavy vehicles approaching from Paradise, Bowenpally, Medchal, Tank Bund and other directions will face diversions at several junctions, including SBI X Roads, Patny, Plaza, CTO, Rasoolpura, Karbala and Sailing Club. Traffic from Paradise and Minister Road towards Ranigunj will be diverted via Audaiah X Road, Distillery Road and Karbala Junction.

The restrictions could also affect movement around Patny, Swimming Pool U-turn, Park Lane, Nallagutta, Ghansmandi, Bible House, CGO Towers and Kavadiguda.

Traffic police have identified 18 junctions where congestion is likely and advised motorists to avoid these stretches wherever possible. Height restrictors with a clearance limit of 10 feet will be installed at five junctions to prevent the entry of oversized vehicles.

The Traffic Police urged commuters to plan their journeys in advance, allow additional travel time and follow traffic updates. For emergency travel assistance, commuters can contact the Hyderabad Traffic Police helpline on 9010203626.

item.title: BRS stages protest against proposed diversion of Koilsagar water to Kodangal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The BRS staged a protest at Koilsagar Project, opposing plans to divert water to Kodangal. Former MLA Ala Venkateswar Reddy warned of a farmers' movement and accused the government of neglecting irrigation needs and allowing illegal sand extraction.
item.content:encoded:
Mahabubnagar: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) staged a protest at the Koilsagar Project on Friday, demanding that the Congress government withdraw its plans to divert water from the project to Kodangal.

Former Devarakadra MLA Ala Venkateswar Reddy and other BRS leaders and party members took part in the demonstration.

Addressing the media, Venkateswar Reddy said the BRS had warned 20 days ago about an alleged conspiracy to divert water from the Koilsagar Project.

He said tenders had already been invited to divert water to Kodangal. Nine days had passed since the tenders were called, but the local Congress MLA had remained unaware of the development. According to Venkateswar Reddy, the MLA responded only after the BRS brought the issue to his attention.

“On behalf of the farmers in the Koilsagar command area, we urge Chief Minister Revanth Reddy to reconsider the decision. Farmers dependent on Koilsagar will be left destitute. The BRS will launch a movement on behalf of the farmers,” Venkateswar Reddy said.

He also accused the government of paying more attention to the illegal extraction of sand from local streams than to ensuring water supply to farmers.

He alleged that a check dam at Pedda Rajamuru had been destroyed. Sand was also being illegally extracted from the Uka Chettu and Pedda Vagu streams for personal gain, he charged.

Questioning the lack of action over the destruction of the check dam, Venkateswar Reddy asked why no one had been arrested in the case.

item.title: Farmers’ families await insurance cover after Rythu Bheema expires
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The expiry of Rythu Bheema on August 14 has left families of farmers who died since then without insurance benefits. With the new IKJB scheme yet to come into effect, activist Puli Raju has demanded interim compensation.
item.content:encoded:
Sangareddy: Even though Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy launched the Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bheema (IKJB) scheme on Thursday, it does not mean that it will come into effect immediately.

The earlier Rythu Bheema scheme expired on August 14, and the bereaved families of farmers who died after this date are not receiving any benefits. Until August 14, the families of deceased farmers received Rs 5 lakh under Rythu Bheema.

Of the 42.5 lakh people enrolled under the scheme, around 20,000 farmer deaths were being recorded in the State every year. However, the families of farmers who died after the scheme expired have been denied the benefit for more than three months, pushing many into a financial crisis after losing their breadwinners.

Since the government has only just started receiving applications for IKJB, it has not specified when the new scheme will come into effect or when the families of deceased farmers will start receiving the benefits.

Social activist Puli Raju, who has been working on farmer suicides for over two decades in Telangana, demanded that the State government pay Rs 5 lakh as ex gratia to the families of farmers who died after August 14 and until IKJB comes into effect.

item.title: HYPEX-2026 showcases rare Nizam-era coins and global currencies
item.dc:creator: Sunil Mungara
item.description: Hyderabad’s HYPEX-2026 exhibition at FTCCI House, Red Hills, is displaying rare Nizam-era coins, historic Indian currency and banknotes from more than 100 countries, with over 60 numismatists and traders attending.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Numismatists, history enthusiasts, curious visitors and students thronged the ongoing HYPEX-2026 exhibition, organised by the Hyderabad Philatelic & Hobbies Society at Red Hills (FTCCI House), to view rare coins and currency notes from pre- and post-Independence India and other countries.

The three-day HYPEX began will continue until November 22.

According to Hyderabad Philatelic & Hobbies Society managing committee member Raj Kumar Agarwal, Over 60 numismatists and traders from across India are attending the three-day event that showcase ancient mintages, princely state coinage, including rare issues from the Nizam’s era, British India currency, and commemorative coins released after 1947.

Collectors have also displayed historic banknotes and coins from more than 100 countries, offering insights into global economic and political history, he said.

A showcase of Nizam-era minted currency at the ongoing exhibition highlights the royal monetary heritage of the Asaf Jahi dynasty. City-based exhibitors brought together a rare array of Osmania Sicca, or Hyderabadi rupees, machine-struck silver rupees, gold Ashrafis and intricate copper paisas minted at the historic Royal Mint in Saifabad.

“The ongoing three-day HYPEX exhibition is offering numismatists a rare opportunity to acquire prized coins and vintage currency notes directly from veteran exhibitors, alongside a display of historical artefacts,” said Vijayawada-based numismatist Vamshi Krishna.

The three-day showcase offers students, academics and history researchers an open-air learning opportunity. Examining centuries-old coins and interacting directly with experts gives young learners insights into the evolution of trade, artistry and economic history across India and the world, said another numismatist from Tirupati, Rajesh.|

item.title: Women farmers may lose out under new Indiramma insurance scheme
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The one-member-per-family eligibility rule under the new Indiramma insurance scheme has raised concerns that women farmers, labourers and tenants may miss out. Experts urge the government to provide family-wide coverage and consult stakeholders before finalising the guidelines.
item.content:encoded:
Sangareddy: With the government deciding to restrict enrolment in the Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bheema (IKJB) scheme to only one member from each family, replacing the earlier Rythu Bheema, most women farmers are likely to be excluded from the scheme. Since men are generally considered the heads of families in farming communities, the man in the family is likely to enrol for the scheme, leaving his wife and unmarried children without the State government’s insurance cover.

Unlike Rythu Bheema, launched by the BRS government in 2018, which provided insurance cover to farmers, only one member of a family would be covered under the new scheme, even if all the family members had land registered in their names. While many welcomed the government’s decision to provide Rs 5 lakh insurance cover to people across sections, including tenant farmers, labourers and the urban poor, experts said women from labourer and tenant families might not enrol for the insurance cover as they would prefer their husbands to enrol.

Speaking to Telangana Today, K Lakshmi of Shivvampet said women rarely enrol in their names as men are considered the heads of families. B Kondal Reddy, convenor of Rythu Swarajya Vedika, said that over 28 per cent of the total beneficiaries of Rythu Bheema since its launch in 2018 were women, underlining the importance of providing insurance cover to them.

Suggesting that the government treat a family as a unit while providing insurance coverage instead of restricting it to just the family head, the social activist urged the government to cover all family members of tenant farmers and labourers, even if it meant spending a few more crores from the government exchequer.

Stating that Rythu Bheema had made a significant impact on the families of farmers who lost their lives, Reddy said the government must organise consultative meetings with all stakeholders before issuing the guidelines for Indiramma Bheema. Over 42 lakh farmers, including women, have enrolled under Rythu Bheema for 2025-26 in Telangana. After launching IKJB at a public meeting in Siddipet on Thursday, Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy failed to provide any clarity on the eligibility criteria.

item.title: Punjab-origin man Garry Rehal, girlfriend shot dead in targeted attack in Canada’s Surrey
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.category: Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers
item.description: Annapurna Studios Chief Technology Officer CV Rao has been named an SMPTE Fellow for 2026. His technical contributions to motion-imaging engineering include establishing complex production pipelines for blockbusters such as the Baahubali franchise and RRR, earning international recognition.
item.content:encoded:
Ottawa: A 24-year-old Punjab-origin man identified as Garry Rehal and his 23-year-old girlfriend were shot dead outside a Walmart store in Surrey in Canada’s British Columbia recently with the investigators believing that it was a targeted attack and possibly linked to organised criminal activity.

The shooting incident took place in the parking lot near the intersection of 88 Avenue and 124 Street and the authorities have not yet revealed the identity of the woman killed in the attack, Khalsa Vox reported.

Officers received information regarding gunfire at approximately 10:38 pm (local time) on November 15, according to the Surrey Police Service. Emergency responders rushed to the site of the incident and tried to revive the two victims before taking them to the hospital. Subsequently, both the victims were declared dead.

Investigators found a red car at the spot, with several bullet holes indicating the intensity of the shooting. Police cordoned off the surrounding parking area as forensic teams started analysing evidence and recreating the sequence of events, Khalsa Vox reported.

Approximately 13 minutes after the shooting incident, police received information about a burning vehicle on Princess Drive. The white vehicle found engulfed in flames is suspected of having been used for the attack.

The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT) has taken charge of the probe into the incident. Sergeant Freda Fong said that the circumstances indicated a targeted attack instead of an isolated or random act of violence. Authorities have been analysing possible links to organised crime, though no gang connection involving the victims has been officially established.

According to reports, Rehal was previously known to law enforcement for weapon offences. Videos have reportedly surfaced on social media showing him in police custody on an earlier occasion.

A local rival gang has reportedly claimed responsibility for the attack. However, investigators have not yet confirmed the claim or revealed the identities of those responsible for the attack.

The incident has renewed concerns regarding organised criminal violence in British Columbia, especially in communities which have substantial South Asian populations.

Earlier this month, two men were charged in connection with a shooting at comedian Kapil Sharma’s cafe in Surrey and a separate attack on a home that injured a woman, according to police and Canadian media reports.

The Canadian Press identified the business as Kap’s Cafe, reporting that the date and location released by police matched the October 16, 2025, attack on the establishment.

British Columbia’s Provincial Extortion Task Force announced the charges against Pardeep Singh and Saveer Khan, both 22. They were arrested in Surrey on November 1 and remain in custody.

Each faces two counts of reckless discharge of a firearm — one for each shooting. The charges have not been proven in court.

The cafe was closed when shots were fired, but two employees were inside. Neither was injured.

Four days earlier, on October 12, police had responded to gunfire at a home in the 13000 block of 103A Avenue, where a woman sustained injuries.

The extortion task force took over both investigations after identifying possible links between the attacks. Its officers worked with Surrey Police Service and British Columbia’s Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit to make the arrests.

Chief Superintendent Duncan Pound, a senior RCMP officer in the Lower Mainland, said the charges followed more than a year of investigative work, including search warrants, judicial authorisations and analysis of evidence.

“We recognise and share the concerns these incidents created within the community,” Pound said in the police statement

item.title: MRI or ultrasound: Which is greener and easier on the pocket?
item.dc:creator: M. Sai Gopal
item.description: AIG Hospitals’ EVERGREEN-IBD study found intestinal ultrasound had the lowest carbon emissions and hospital cost among imaging tests for inflammatory bowel disease, supporting its use in suitable follow-up monitoring.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A Hyderabad-based AIG Hospitals study released on Friday found that intestinal ultrasound had the lowest carbon emissions and hospital cost among imaging tests evaluated for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) care, supporting its wider use in suitable follow-up monitoring.

Published in Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics, the EVERGREEN-IBD study compared the operational carbon footprint of laboratory tests, colonoscopy and enteroscopy, CT, MRI and intestinal ultrasound using a common assessment framework.

Estimated carbon emissions per procedure were 0.85 kg of carbon dioxide equivalent for intestinal ultrasound, compared with 3.87 kg for colonoscopy or enteroscopy, 5.82 kg for CT and 21.25 kg for MRI — an estimated footprint roughly 96 per cent lower than MRI per examination.

At AIG Hospitals, the hospital cost of intestinal ultrasound was about half that of colonoscopy and one-sixth that of MR enterography, a specialised bowel MRI.

Researchers noted that colonoscopy with biopsy remains essential for diagnosis and cancer surveillance, while CT and MRI still play important roles in assessing disease extent and complications.

AIG Hospitals Chairman D. Nageshwar Reddy said, “For chronic diseases, when a less resource-intensive diagnostic test can reliably answer the clinical question, its use deserves serious consideration.”

Lead author Hardik Rughwani, Consultant Gastroenterologist at AIG Hospitals, said, “Intestinal ultrasound stood out for its low operational carbon footprint and lower hospital cost. The practical need is to expand access to appropriately perform ultrasound and integrate it into suitable follow-up assessments.”

item.title: Annapurna Studios CTO CV Rao elevated to SMPTE Fellow for 2026
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: C.V. Rao, Chief Technology Officer of Annapurna Studios in Hyderabad, has been elevated as a Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers Fellow for 2026, recognising his contributions to motion-imaging infrastructure and blockbuster production pipelines.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: C.V. Rao, Chief Technology Officer of Annapurna Studios, has been elevated to the grade of Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (SMPTE) Fellow for the Class of 2026. Founded in 1916, SMPTE is the global standards-setting body behind foundational media technologies.

Rao is among 32 individuals and organisations being recognised across 13 SMPTE honours at this year's annual SMPTE Gala. The Fellowship is one of the highest international honours in motion-imaging engineering, reserved for leaders whose technical foresight and infrastructure contributions have fundamentally shaped how stories are captured, processed and presented worldwide.

Rao's technical expertise was instrumental in establishing the complex pipelines for blockbusters, including the Baahubali franchise and RRR.

"When I started as a graphic designer and 3D artist, I never imagined I’d one day be recognised as an SMPTE Fellow," he said.

item.title: HMWSSB plans trial run to divert additional 40 MGD of Godavari water to Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board is preparing to divert an additional 40 MGD of Godavari water to Hyderabad, aiming to offset half the projected Singur-Manjira supply deficit, officials said.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) is preparing for a trial run to divert an additional 40 million gallons per day (MGD) of Godavari water to Hyderabad, with pipeline integration work nearing completion.

The project is intended to support Hyderabad’s drinking water supply as El Niño conditions deplete reserves in the Singur and Manjira reservoirs. Officials expect the additional 40 MGD to offset about 50% of the projected deficit in areas dependent on the Singur-Manjira network.

HMWSSB and Mission Bhagiratha officials have set a two-day deadline to complete the remaining interconnection pipeline work to carry water from Mallannasagar to the Ghanpur Master Balancing Reservoir.

HMWSSB Managing Director Ashok Reddy and Mission Bhagiratha Engineer-in-Chief Krupakar Reddy inspected the pipeline work on Friday and directed officials to coordinate closely, expedite the remaining tasks and prepare for the trial run.

In a press statement, M D Ashok Reddy said, “The water board planned to complete construction and interconnection works by November 15, but excavation through heavy rock strata along a 150-metre stretch in a forest area caused a minor delay.”

The official said the work had since been accelerated after completion of pipeline works.

item.title: GHMC asks traders to renew 2027 trade licences by November 30 to avoid penalties
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation has asked traders and commercial establishments to renew 2027 trade licences by November 30 without penalty, warning of penalties ranging from 25% to 100% for delayed renewals or operating without a valid licence.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) has urged traders, shop owners and commercial establishments within its limits to renew their 2027 trade licences by November 30 to avoid penalties.

GHMC Commissioner R.V. Karnan said on Friday that existing trade licences obtained for 2026 would remain valid until December 31, 2026. Renewal applications must be submitted during the prescribed 30-day period before expiry.

Applications filed by November 30 will attract no penalty. Renewals submitted between December 1, 2026, and January 31, 2027, will attract a 25% penalty for delays of up to 60 days, while those filed from February 1, 2027, will attract a 50% penalty for delays exceeding 60 days.

Operating a business without a valid trade licence will attract a 100% penalty when detected, followed by an additional monthly fine of 10% until the licence is obtained. The penalties were prescribed under Standing Committee Resolution No. 19, dated September 7, 2017.

Under Section 60(1) of the Core Urban Region (Integrated Governance) Bill, 2026, no person may operate a business or commercial establishment within corporation limits without a valid trade licence granted by the GHMC Commissioner.

Applications can be submitted through the GHMC website, https://ghmc.gov.in, My CURE App, Mee-Seva centres or Citizen Service Centres within GHMC limits.

item.title: Bhumi Pednekar wears sustainable outfit made from vintage silk sarees at Earthshot Prize 2026
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Actress Bhumi Pednekar shared details of her sustainable outfit for the 2026 Earthshot Prize gala in Mumbai. Created by Bodements using archival embroidered textiles and vintage silk sarees, the ensemble celebrated traditional craftsmanship and textile reuse through contemporary fashion choices.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Bhumi Pednekar has spoken about her love for outfits that carry a sense of history and reflect someone’s heritage.

She recently shared details of her ensemble worn for the Earthshot Prize. Taking to Instagram, the ‘Dum Laga Ke Haisha’ actress shared pictures of her look and revealed that the outfit was crafted using archival embroidered textiles and vintage silk sarees. She paired the ensemble with jewellery from Amrapali Jewels. Talking about her choice of attire, Bhumi wrote, “I love wearing pieces that make me feel like I’m wearing a part of history, of someone’s heritage.”

She also credited Bodements for the ensemble and highlighted the ideas of upcycling, recycling and reusing through her look. “For the @earthshotprize , wore this beautiful ensemble made from archival embroidered textiles and vintage silk saree’s by @bodements_, paired with jewellery from @amrapalijewels #Upcycle #Recycle #Reuse.”

At the 2026 Earthshot Prize gala in Mumbai, Bhumi Pednekar opted for a sustainable outfit created by Bodements using archival embroidered fabrics and pieces of vintage silk sarees. The ensemble featured a purple draped skirt teamed with a structured corset-style blouse adorned with gold accents and intricate embroidery. The look highlighted traditional craftsmanship and the idea of reusing heritage textiles.

Notably, Bhumi has often spoken about her interest in sustainable fashion.

The 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai saw the participation of environmental leaders and several well-known personalities. Celebrities brought together traditional Indian craftsmanship, contemporary designs and distinctive ensembles for the occasion.

Among those spotted at the event were Simone Ashley, Bhumi Pednekar, Karan Johar, Khushi Kapoor, Mira Kapoor, Sonam Kapoor, Rakul Preet Singh, Shreya Ghoshal and Kate Middleton.

The Princess of Wales attended the ceremony alongside Prince William, who founded the Earthshot Prize in 2020. Kate also presented one of the awards, marking a significant moment during the royal couple’s three-day visit to India. The event also featured musical performances by Shreya Ghoshal, British pop group Take That, composer Shashwat Sachdev and all-female hip-hop group Wild Wild Women.

item.title: Hyderabad: Electric car catches fire on ORR
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: An electric car was gutted after reportedly ramming into a truck on the Outer Ring Road near Kokapet on Friday morning. All four occupants escaped unhurt, while Narsingi police investigate the incident.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: An electric car was completely gutted after colliding with a truck on the Outer Ring Road (ORR) near Kokapet, within Narsingi police station limits, on Friday morning. No casualties were reported.

The car, reportedly travelling from Kokapet towards Patancheru, rammed into a truck moving ahead. Within minutes of the collision, flames erupted from the vehicle and quickly engulfed it.

Alerted by the sudden fire, all four occupants reportedly stepped out of the car in time and escaped unhurt. The vehicle was reduced to ashes within minutes.

On receiving information, local police and firefighters rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control.

The exact cause of the fire and further details of the accident are yet to be ascertained. Narsingi police are investigating.

item.title: Nine held in online investment fraud in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Malkajgiri Cybercrime Police arrested nine persons for allegedly arranging bank accounts to route Rs 74 lakh cheated in an online investment fraud. Police said two alleged masterminds from Maharashtra are absconding.
item.content:encoded:
Malkajgiri: The Malkajgiri Cybercrime Police on Friday arrested nine persons for allegedly facilitating an online investment fraud involving Rs 74 lakh by arranging bank accounts to route the cheated money.

The arrested persons are Mohd. Azhar Jani, Parvez Khan, Mubeen Khan, M. Kiran, K. Praveen Kumar, D. Venkata Seshu Varaprasad, H. Srikanth, Mudassar Nazar and S. Srinivas.

According to police, the alleged masterminds, Rahul and Gourav, both natives of Maharashtra, are absconding.

According to police, the victim was added to a WhatsApp investment group in June this year, where fraudsters posed as stock market experts and promised returns of 5 per cent to 50 per cent. “Lured by trading tips and fake profit claims, the victim invested through an application and ended up losing a total of Rs 74 lakh,” an official said.

Police said the investigation revealed that the accused allegedly arranged bank accounts to receive and transfer the fraud proceeds in return for commissions. Account holders were promised a 20 per cent commission, while intermediaries received 5 per cent.

Police seized nine mobile phones and SIM cards.

Efforts are on to nab Rahul and Gaurav and trace the money trail, police said.

item.title: DGCA issues show-cause notice to SpiceJet over flight cancellations, delays and grounded fleet
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: DGCA issued SpiceJet a show-cause notice over cancellations, delays, grounded aircraft and alleged regulatory violations. The airline was asked to respond within seven days, as its board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to fund its revival.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Aviation regulator DGCA has reportedly served a show-cause notice on SpiceJet, raising concerns over the airline’s deteriorating operational performance, frequent flight cancellations, schedule disruptions and regulatory non-compliance.

In the notice, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) sought detailed responses from the budget carrier on a range of issues, including a decline in on-time performance (OTP), increasing delays and cancellations, and the inconvenience caused to passengers due to persistent operational disruptions, according to reports.

The regulator also flagged the airline’s failure to adhere to its approved flight schedule and alleged inadequacies in passenger facilitation measures during flight disruptions. SpiceJet has been asked to submit its reply within seven days.

According to the notice, a majority of the airline’s fleet remains grounded and the carrier has not presented a credible plan for returning the aircraft to service, as per the reports.

The DGCA also expressed concern over uncertainty regarding the renewal of mandatory insurance coverage and issues flagged by overseas aviation authorities related to operational disruptions arising from delayed payments to service providers.

The watchdog further sought an explanation for the airline’s failure to pay a penalty imposed earlier despite repeated reminders. It also alleged that SpiceJet had failed to meet eligibility requirements for scheduled international operations and had repeatedly violated Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG) despite earlier enforcement action and penalties imposed in May.

The latest regulatory action comes as the airline continues to grapple with financial and operational challenges. SpiceJet’s domestic market share fell sharply to 0.6 per cent in September from 1.2 per cent in August.

The show-cause notice was issued a day before the airline’s board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its financial position and support revival plans.

Meanwhile, shares of the airline came under pressure in the market, falling nearly 5 per cent to Rs 9.74 during afternoon trade on the BSE.

item.title: BITS Pilani Hyderabad students develop pocket radio device for Indian Army
item.dc:creator: Yuvraj Akula
item.description: Hyderabad-based Krathveil Private Limited, founded by BITS Pilani students, has developed Krath Control, an encrypted pocket radio device for Indian Army personnel to communicate without mobile networks, SIM cards or satellites.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Indian Army personnel will soon have an indigenously developed device to communicate in areas without network connectivity or a SIM card, according to Hyderabad-based start-up Krathveil Private Limited.

Krathveil Private Limited, founded by BITS Pilani Hyderabad campus students Samarth Alok Srivastava and Shresth Prakash Singh, has developed Krath Control to meet the Indian Army’s requirement for a secure and independent communication device.

Weighing under 180 grams, Krath Control is a pocket tactical radio device that uses an encrypted mesh network to connect nearby units. The company said it allows units to exchange voice messages and data and share live locations without requiring a mobile network, SIM card or satellite.

The device can potentially cover more than 100 kilometres with a single hop between hilltops, the company said. Field testing of its range will be carried out soon.

Krathveil said the Indian Army imports similar devices from the United States at Rs 2 lakh per unit. The start-up intends to bring the cost down to Rs 40,000 per unit.

Speaking to Telangana Today, Krathveil Private Limited Founder and Chief Executive Officer Samarth Alok Srivastava said he interacted with Indian Army personnel and learnt about their on-field requirements during his stint at a drone start-up.

“After learning about their requirements, we developed a prototype device that uses an encrypted mesh network to transmit voice messages, data and live location information without relying on mobile towers, satellites or SIM cards. Army officers were impressed by the device, which costs a fraction of what the imported device costs,” said Srivastava, a third-year dual-degree student of MSc Physics and BE Mechanical at BITS Pilani Hyderabad campus.

Srivastava said Krathveil initially built a prototype with a power output of 156 milliwatts. However, two Indian Army units that assessed the device wanted its power output increased to 1 watt and the antennas upgraded.

The young innovator said they are upgrading the device based on feedback from the Army. “In the next five to six months, we will come up with an upgraded version,” he said.

The 20-year-old said he had invested his earnings from his previous start-up in building the prototype. “My family has been extending financial support. There is no attendance requirement at the institution, which is helping me focus on the device development,” he added.

item.title: Gambhir’s childhood coach dismisses ‘Hindu-Muslim’ angle in Mohammed Siraj’s omission from India XI
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Gautam Gambhir’s childhood coach Sanjay Bharadwaj rejected allegations of a religious angle in Mohammed Siraj’s omission from India’s first Test playing XI against New Zealand. He said selection was based on cricketing requirements and the team combination, not personal bias.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Gautam Gambhir’s childhood coach Sanjay Bharadwaj on Friday dismissed allegations of a religious angle behind Mohammed Siraj’s omission from India’s playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, asserting that team selection was based entirely on cricketing requirements and combination.

Bharadwaj said Gambhir had always supported the Indian pacer and did not hold personal grudges against any player, adding that the head coach’s priority was to build a strong team.

“This is baseless. There is no Hindu-Muslim angle in the Indian cricket team. Everyone is an Indian and represents the nation. Gautam Gambhir has always supported Mohammed Siraj, and if Siraj is not part of the playing XI, it is purely because of the team’s requirements. Selection depends on the team’s combination, players’ positions and their performances. Gambhir does not hold personal grudges against anyone. His priority is to build a strong team with the right combination. Even the BCCI does not believe in or promote any Hindu-Muslim divide. Such allegations are completely baseless,” Bharadwaj told IANS.

His remarks came after Congress MP Imran Masood questioned Siraj’s omission from the playing XI for the opening Test against New Zealand in Wellington, suggesting that the pacer’s name could be the reason behind his exclusion despite his performances.

“His name is Siraj—isn’t that reason enough? If he is performing and still not getting selected, what else could be the reason behind it? This alone can be the reason; there can be no other reason besides this,” Masood said.

Siraj, India’s leading wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, was left out of the playing XI for the first Test on Thursday, prompting questions over the team management’s selection strategy.

India opted for Anshul Kamboj in their pace-heavy combination, with the youngster featuring alongside Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna and Akash Deep, while the experienced Siraj was named among the reserves.

India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the decision, saying the combination selected for the match was considered the strongest possible by the captain and team management.

item.title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu, Raj Nidimoru welcome first child, name baby boy Dev
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu and filmmaker Raj Nidimoru have welcomed their first child, a baby boy named Dev. The announcement follows a traditional family puja held at their home on November 17, ahead of the baby’s arrival.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu has embraced motherhood and welcomed her first child with filmmaker Raj Nidimoru.

The actress shared the happy news on her social media account, revealing that the couple has been blessed with a baby boy, whom they have named Dev Nidimoru. Samantha shared a tender glimpse of her newborn son, with the picture capturing the baby’s tiny fingers gently wrapped around her finger.

Sharing the pivotal, Samantha wrote, “Our beautiful baby boy DEV NIDIMORU 19.11.2026 The happiest our hearts have ever been. Samantha & Raj” The arrival of their son comes days after Samantha and Raj held an intimate traditional puja at their home ahead of welcoming their first child.

On November 17, Samantha and Raj gathered with members of their families for the ceremony, which featured prayers, chanting and traditional rituals seeking blessings for the mother and baby and a smooth delivery.

Pictures from the ceremony showed Samantha dressed in a red traditional outfit, while Raj was seen in a cream-coloured kurta paired with white pyjamas. The couple was also seen seeking blessings from elders and participating in the rituals.

Samantha’s sister-in-law shared a detailed account of the ceremony, along with behind-the-scenes pictures. She described the gathering as a coming together of family members who had helped raise them.

She wrote, “When can we do this, Babu?” I’d been asking my annayya for so long. And finally, it was time. Our pinnammas and peddamma who helped raise us came from near and far for Matru Shishu Mangala Ashirvadam, to bless Sam and the precious little one already reigning over our hearts and soon, our Samrajyam.”

She added, “In our family, gathering at the home altar to chant and sing was part of everyday life. We grew up doing it with our grandparents, and aunties. Amma and Nanna made sure we continued. Whatever had happened that day, we sat together in prayer. It reset the home, and us. I’m grateful they gave us that.”

She further added, “I saw it all come alive in our aunties. They had travelled without their families and were together again, chanting, singing, laughing like girlfriends, and doting on my brother and me. This time, Sam and the baby to be born were receiving all that affection too. We offered the Sri Suktam and Gayatri Devi homam, chanted Gayatri 21 times, and shared our familiar family prayers.”

She further added, “Then came a song just for them :). Padma Shri Shobha Raju pinnamma composed it with love and a little mischief. I sang, Padma Shri Vidushi Sumitra Guha peddamma added her beautiful ragas, Neeru aunty joined my lines, and Amma and Usha aunty became our chorus. We had our own little family production :)! I’m grateful to everyone who helped bring us together. Seeing so many mothers blessing Sam was everything I had hoped for.”

“Little one, look at all the love you’ve already brought together- even before you arrived. We seek your blessings for Sam’s smooth delivery and well-being, and for the baby’s long, healthy life, filled with kindness, character, and purpose.”

For the uninitiated, Samantha and Raj tied the knot on December 1, 2025, in an intimate ceremony at the Linga Bhairavi Temple inside the Isha Yoga Centre in Coimbatore. The wedding was attended by a select group of family members and close friends.

The couple first worked together on The Family Man 2, where Samantha played the character of Raji. They later collaborated on Citadel: Honey Bunny and Maa Inti Bangaaram. Their relationship eventually became public before they married in December 2025.

Samantha announced in June 2026 that she was expecting her first child. She had also said that she would take a maternity break after Maa Inti Bangaaram before returning to acting.

item.title: Revanth Reddy calls BRS his main rival, dismisses BJP’s influence in Telangana
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy described the BRS as his main political rival and dismissed the BJP’s influence in Telangana. At the Southern Rising Summit, he rated his performance 6.5 out of 10 and defended investments from the Adani Group.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy said the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) was his main political rival in Telangana and dismissed the BJP as a political force of little relevance in the State.

He said he needed an Opposition in Telangana and was allowing the BRS to survive. “I would have wiped out the BRS from the State through defections, which were encouraged by the previous party,” he said at the Southern Rising Summit 2026, an ABP Network conclave, here on Friday.

Asked about the Congress party’s Vote Chori campaign and its electoral success in Telangana, Revanth Reddy said the BJP had no role in the State’s politics.

He alleged that the BJP was involved in vote theft in places where it had a political presence, but said it had no such opportunity in Telangana. “Here it is KCR vs Revanth Reddy. BJP is just a spectator and has to sit outside and applaud,” he said.

He asserted that the BJP could not make inroads into Telangana and cited its loss of deposit in the recent Jubilee Hills by-election.

Challenging the BJP’s claims of expanding its influence in the State, he said Prime Minister Narendra Modi or Union Home Minister Amit Shah should contest from the Hyderabad Lok Sabha constituency.

With the Congress government completing three years in office, Revanth Reddy rated his performance as Chief Minister at 6.5 out of 10.

With two years remaining in the government’s term, he said comprehensive policies had been framed to achieve the Telangana Rising 2047 target.

Defending his decision to invite investments from the Adani Group and meet its chairman Gautam Adani, the Chief Minister said there was nothing wrong in doing so.

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi is handing over public money to Adani. I am getting the public money out of Adani’s pockets for investing in Telangana,” he said.

Responding to criticism over inviting football legend Lionel Messi to Hyderabad and using Singareni funds for the event, Revanth Reddy said the government was planning to invite another football star, Cristiano Ronaldo, to the city. However, the dates had not been finalised, he added.

item.title: TG SAFE finds drug sale and prescription violations at 90 medical shops in Telangana
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TG SAFE detected violations at 90 shops during raids across Hyderabad and other parts of Telangana. Officials found prescription and record-keeping lapses, unbilled medicine sales and irregularities involving regulated drugs. Show-cause notices were issued to all 90 shops by authorities.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Drugs Wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) detected various kinds of discrepancies in 90 medical shops in Hyderabad.

Conducted with TG SAFE Enforcement Wing police and Excise Enforcement personnel, the raids covered vulnerable pockets in the CURE region including Koti, Abids, Basheerbagh, Nampally, Khairatabad, Panjagutta, Ameerpet, SR Nagar, Sanathnagar, Yerragadda, Yousufguda, Madhuranagar, Jubilee Hills, and Banjara Hills, apart from other districts in Telangana.

Officials conducted decoy operations and test purchases to check compliance on Schedule H1 and Schedule X habit-forming drugs such as Tramadol, Alprazolam, Nitrazepam, Codeine-containing cough syrups, Tapentadol, Pregabalin formulations, Zolpidem and antibiotics.

Violations included dispensing prescription drugs without a valid doctor’s prescription or a Registered Pharmacist, missing or improperly maintained prescription and Schedule H1 registers, selling medicines without bills, and failing to produce sales or purchase bills.

Show cause notices have been issued to the 90 erring medical shops, with action including licence suspension or cancellation and prosecution under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, expected to be taken up, a TGSAFE press release said.

Citizens can report illegal sales or diversion of habit-forming drugs on toll-free number 1800-599-6969 between 10.30 am and 5 pm am only on working days.

item.title: Madhuri Dixit recalls being caned by teacher during school days
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Bollywood actress Madhuri Dixit recalled being caned by a teacher during her school days after she and her classmates created a ruckus in the classroom. She also spoke about her fear of mathematics and her strict schoolteacher.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Bollywood superstar Madhuri Dixit recently took a trip down memory lane on the quiz show.

She recalled an incident from her school days when she and her classmates were beaten with a cane by a teacher after creating a ruckus in the classroom. The actress vividly remembered the moment, saying that the first few seconds after being hit were enough to make her heart sink.

The candid conversation unfolded when contestant Amruta Dale from Pune turned the questions towards Madhuri’s own school life. When asked whether she had ever been hit by a teacher, the actress admitted that it had happened once.

“Yes, once we created such chaos at school that the teacher got angry. She came in with a cane. We each got one whack with it.
