I mean, when the cane first hits you, you know, for two seconds you don’t feel anything abd it hoes numb, and then after a few seconds it starts paining,’” Madhuri further mimicked the sound of the cane.

The memory came up during a conversation about Madhuri’s school days, including her rather different relationship with mathematics. When Amruta asked whether she had enjoyed maths at school, Madhuri immediately said no, recalling how intimidating her teacher had been.

“No, I never liked Maths. We had a very strict teacher. I don’t know if it was the way she’d walk in or what, but we used to get so scared. The very mention of Maths class would fill me with dread. Oh God, Maths class is coming up now.”

Talking about Madhuri Dixit, on the personal front, she was born on May 15, 1967, in a Marathi-speaking family in Mumbai and attended schooling in Andheri, Mumbai. She later pursued higher education in microbiology.

Madhuri has been trained in Kathak from a young age and spent years honing her classical dance skills before entering the Hindi film industry.

After making her film debut with Abodh in 1984, she gradually established herself as one of the leading actresses of Hindi cinema.

item.title: CPI MLC Nellikanti Satyam criticises Telangana government over alleged Krishna water diversion
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: CPI MLC Nellikanti Satyam criticised the Telangana government over alleged diversion of Krishna waters at Nagarjunasagar for the Palnadu Water Grid. He accused officials of inaction, demanded implementation of Reorganisation Act provisions and urged BJP MPs to respond.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: The State unit of the Communist Party of India (CPI), a Congress ally in Telangana, has also criticised the State government for failing to prevent Andhra Pradesh from illegally drawing Krishna waters at Nagarjunasagar.

CPI MLC Nellikanti Satyam criticised the Congress government for its alleged negligence over the diversion of Nagarjunasagar waters at Vijayapuri through the Pothireddypadu head regulator into Andhra Pradesh in the name of the ‘Palnadu Water Grid’.

Addressing a press conference, he alleged that construction works were being carried out clandestinely to facilitate water diversion under the pretext of meeting drinking water requirements.

“These activities have been ongoing for the past eight months. The Congress government’s failure to notice them and its subsequent attempt to merely issue notices without further action is entirely unacceptable,” Satyam said.

He alleged that the State government and concerned engineering officials had failed to act on the issue. The government must be held accountable for the alleged diversion of Telangana’s water, he said, accusing the Andhra Pradesh government of acting against Telangana’s interests with the support of the Centre.

Satyam demanded implementation of the provisions of the Reorganisation Act relating to Krishna river waters to ensure a clear allocation of Telangana’s rightful share. He also urged BJP MPs from Telangana to respond to the issue immediately.

Maintaining that illegal diversion of water would not be tolerated, he called upon people to unite and protest against the alleged injustice.

item.title: Hyderabad doctor trains 1,000 students and faculty in CPR, choking first aid
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr Sivaranjani Santosh is conducting CPR and choking first-aid training for 1,000 students and faculty members at SIMS in Ramagundam. The programme forms part of a broader initiative to train 27,000 people by December this year across Telangana.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: As part of a broader push to train 27,000 people by this December, senior paediatrician from Hyderabad, Dr Sivaranjanjani Santosh is conducting a training program in in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and choking first aid for 1000 high school and college students, along with faculty members at Singareni Institute of Medical Sciences (SIMS) in Ramagundam on Saturday.

Scheduled from 10 am to 1.30 pm, the programme aims to bridge the critical time gap before professional medical help arrives during emergencies.

Led by Dr Sivaranjani Santosh, who has conducted first-aid and CPR sessions since 2010, the drive is being organized by the Goodwill Foundation with support from the Women Pediatricians Forum and visiting doctors from across Telangana.

Dr Dayal Singh and Dr Himabindu have facilitated the programme.

Participants will take part in demonstrations and hands-on practice covering CPR, choking response, seizures, and fainting. Organizers said that timely bystander intervention helps maintain blood circulation during sudden cardiac arrest and addresses airway blockages that can turn fatal within minutes.

“First aid given at the right time saves lives. Six out of 10 deaths can be prevented through timely intervention. Despite the increasing number of patients and my workload, I have never stopped conducting first-aid and CPR sessions since 2010,” Dr Sivaranjani said.

item.title: Former national hockey player EV Prakash dies at 75 in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Former national hockey player EV Prakash passed away in Hyderabad on Wednesday at the age of 75. He represented Coronation Club, Hyderabad State and South Central Railway, and played for Board President’s XI against Poland in a 1974 exhibition match.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Former national hockey player EV Prakash passed away here on Wednesday. He was 75 and survived by two sons. Prakash represented Coronation Club, Hyderabad State and also South Central Railway.

One of the high-points of his career was representing the Board President’s XI against Poland in the international exhibition match in Guntur in 1974. Hockey fraternity remembered his dedication and commitment to promote the sport.

item.title: KRMB cites jurisdictional constraints, asks Telangana and AP to follow approval process for new projects
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The KRMB has cited jurisdictional and procedural constraints in responding to Telangana’s complaint against Andhra Pradesh’s Palnadu Water Grid project. It advised both States to follow the prescribed approval process, while pointing to Telangana’s pending Supreme Court challenge.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) has cited jurisdictional and procedural constraints in responding to Telangana’s November 16 complaint against Andhra Pradesh’s Palnadu Water Grid project. The Board advised both States to follow the prescribed approval process for new projects before taking up construction.

However, the Board neither made direct reference to the Palnadu Water Grid project, assured intervention over Telangana’s request nor sought Andhra Pradesh’s explanation in this regard.

In a letter dated November 19 to the Water Resources Secretaries of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, the Board pointed out that Telangana had challenged the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti’s Jurisdiction Notification, 2021, before the Supreme Court in W.P. (C) No. 666/2024. It said Telangana’s demand for the Board’s intervention, while simultaneously challenging the notification that defined its jurisdiction, was inherently contradictory.

The KRMB also explained that its decisions are generally taken by consensus under its meeting procedure. In the absence of consensus, a matter remains inconclusive unless a dissent is formally recorded. This consensus-based mechanism, coupled with the pending challenge to its jurisdiction, constrains the Board’s ability to act on contested matters, it said.

The Board observed that invoking Principle 9 of the Eleventh Schedule to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for consequential action by the Centre would presuppose an existing Board decision that was within its jurisdiction and had not been implemented by a State.

Reiterating the statutory procedure under Principle 7, the KRMB said new projects require prior appraisal and technical clearance from the Board before being placed before the Apex Council. It cautioned that the perceived availability of unallocated or surplus water does not, by itself, confer any assured or legal entitlement to utilise it. The Board also clarified that project-wise water allocations have to be determined by the competent tribunal.

item.title: #OM review: Dhanush leads an explosive action-packed cinematic experience
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: #OM brings together Dhanush, Mammootty, Sai Pallavi and Sreeleela in an intense action-driven narrative. Backed by Rajkumar Periasamy's direction, powerful performances, atmospheric visuals and Sai Abhyankkar's music, the film promises an electrifying theatrical experience
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Set against a brutal and unforgiving world where crime, power, greed and survival collide, #OM emerges as an intense, hard-hitting cinematic experience, powered by exceptional performances, compelling drama and high-voltage action.

Dhanush is the film’s undisputed showstopper! Delivering a commanding mass avatar, he brings ferocious screen presence, explosive intensity and remarkable emotional depth to his character. His powerful body language, effortless swagger and sheer conviction make every appearance impactful. He dominates the screen with an electrifying performance that stands out as one of the film’s biggest highlights.

Mammootty is an absolute delight! Bringing his trademark charisma, unmatched screen aura and effortless authority, the veteran superstar adds tremendous weight to the narrative. His commanding presence and powerful portrayal make every scene memorable. The combination of Dhanush’s raw intensity and Mammootty’s magnetic screen presence is undoubtedly one of the film’s biggest attractions.

Sai Pallavi delivers a terrific performance! In a refreshing and powerful avatar, she brings remarkable conviction, emotional depth and commanding screen presence to her character. Her expressive performances and natural intensity make her one of the film’s strongest pillars. She effortlessly holds her own alongside the film’s powerhouse performers.

Sreeleela adds freshness, charm and grace to the narrative. With her effortless screen presence and natural approach to the character, she brings a beautiful contrast to the film’s otherwise intense and gritty world. Her performance adds another engaging dimension to the ensemble.

Naseeruddin Shah lends tremendous gravitas to the film. With his seasoned acting prowess, understated intensity and commanding screen presence, he brings further depth and credibility to the narrative. His contribution adds another layer of strength to an already impressive ensemble.

Sai Abhyankkar’s music and background score are major highlights! They add another dimension to the narrative, amplifying the film’s action sequences, emotional moments and dramatic confrontations. The powerful soundscape complements the gritty world and significantly elevates its cinematic impact.

Director Rajkumar Periasamy deserves special appreciation for showcasing his versatility after Amaran. Moving from the emotionally driven world of Amaran to a completely different action-oriented cinematic universe, he demonstrates the ambition and conviction to explore a new genre. The collective performances, coupled with atmospheric visuals, engaging action blocks and emotionally charged moments, keep the narrative compelling.

With its blend of raw action, intense drama, powerhouse performances and an electrifying musical score, #OM delivers a compelling big-screen experience. Director Rajkumar Periasamy deserves appreciation for bringing together an ambitious cinematic world and an impressive ensemble while creating a distinct action-driven narrative.

A POWERFUL DHANUSH SHOW! A MAGNETIC MAMMOOTTY! A COMMANDING SAI PALLAVI! A CHARMING SREELEELA! AN EXPLOSIVE THEATRICAL EXPERIENCE!

item.title: Palnadu Water Grid row: Notices to Telangana engineers raise questions over government’s response
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Notices to Nagarjuna Sagar engineers over Andhra Pradesh’s Palnadu Water Grid project have triggered resentment and raised questions about Telangana’s response. Officials point to conflicting statements by two ministers and the delay in formally approaching the KRMB.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Congress government’s move to hold the Nagarjuna Sagar engineers responsible for failing to flag Andhra Pradesh’s Palnadu Water Grid project has raised questions over its own response, particularly as the government claims it was already aware of the project.

The Irrigation Department sought explanations from engineers at the Superintending Engineer, Executive Engineer, Deputy Executive Engineer and Assistant Engineer levels for allegedly failing to alert the government about the construction of three intake wells and related infrastructure. The government has also sought an explanation from the Nalgonda District Collector.

Sources said reports from the Collector and Nagarjuna Sagar Chief Engineer had been submitted to the administration. Though their contents could not be independently verified, action is likely against at least two officials. Irrigation engineers are reportedly opposed to any attempt to make their colleagues scapegoats.

“If the Minister says the government was already aware of the project and had taken it up with the Union Jal Shakti Ministry, the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) and the Andhra Pradesh government, why are field-level officials now being held responsible for not reporting it?” an Irrigation Department engineer questioned.

The notices have caused resentment among officials, who feel they are being singled out despite the government’s claim of prior knowledge. They are considering a strong response if action is taken against their colleagues.

The conflicting statements by Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy and Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy have added to the questions. While Uttam said the government was aware of the project and had taken it up with the authorities concerned, Venkat Reddy said he had reprimanded officials for failing to bring it to the government’s notice.

The project’s timeline also raises questions. Andhra Pradesh floated tenders in January and issued a Government Order on August 4. Survey and mobilisation activities had reportedly begun in March. The Rs 1,200-crore project involves three intake wells on the right bank of Nagarjuna Sagar and 200 tanks to draw 1.86 TMC of water for drinking needs in Palnadu district. It is jointly funded by the Centre and Andhra Pradesh under the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

Construction had reportedly reached 20 per cent before Telangana lodged a formal objection with the KRMB on November 16, seeking its intervention. But if the government had been tracking the project since its inception, the delay in formally approaching the river management board needs an explanation. If it learnt about the works only recently, the Minister’s claim of having already taken up the matter with multiple authorities requires clarification. Either way, the notices to engineers do not address the central issue of the government’s own response.

While the State government wrote a letter to the KRMB on November 16 reportedly opposing the Palnadu Water Grid project, the Congress government is unwilling to make public the contents of the letter.

Apparently, the project also was not included in earlier KRMB meeting agendas as Telangana had not formally raised the issue. The 21st full-fledged meeting, scheduled for October 26, has been postponed three times. If the government was aware of the project and opposed it, it could have raised the issue at earlier meetings or sought its inclusion in the agenda.

item.title: Mahela Jayawardene appointed Delhi Capitals’ Director of Cricket for WPL team
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Delhi Capitals have appointed former Sri Lanka captain Mahela Jayawardene as Director of Cricket for their Women’s Premier League team ahead of the 2027 season. He will oversee team strategy, talent identification and the development of players and coaching staff.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The JSW and GMR co-owned Delhi Capitals on Friday announced the appointment of Mahela Jayawardene as Director of Cricket for its Women’s Premier League (WPL) team ahead of the 2027 season. In his new role, Jayawardene will oversee all cricketing matters for the franchise, including team strategy, talent identification, and player and coaching staff development. One of the most celebrated batters of his generation, Jayawardene represented Sri Lanka in 149 Tests and 448 One-Day Internationals, scoring 11,814 and 12,650 runs respectively. He captained Sri Lanka and was part of the side that won the 2014 ICC World T20.

Since moving into coaching, he has built a reputation as one of the sharpest leaders in franchise cricket. Commenting on the appointment, Kiran Kumar Grandhi, Co-Owner Delhi Capitals and Chairman GMR Sports, said “Delhi Capitals has been at the forefront of the Women’s Premier League journey, and our ambition has always been to build a team that sets high standards both on and off the field. As women’s cricket continues to grow, we see an exciting opportunity to further strengthen our cricketing approach, build on the foundations already established and create a team that consistently challenges for the title.

“Mahela’s appointment brings an added dimension of experience and strategic leadership to the women’s setup. His understanding of the modern game and experience in building competitive teams will be valuable in taking Delhi Capitals Women to the next level. We look forward to seeing his contribution as we continue to pursue our ambition of establishing Delhi Capitals as one of the leading teams in women’s franchise cricket.” Parth Jindal, Chairman and Co-owner of Delhi Capitals and Founder of JSW Sports, said, “Mahela is one of the finest cricketing minds in the game, and his record as a player, captain and coach speaks for itself. We are delighted to welcome him to the DC family and look forward to the experience and perspective he brings to the group.”

Adding to this, Sunil Gupta, CEO, Delhi Capitals, said: “Mahela’s appointment is a significant step forward in our ambition to build a world-class women’s cricket team and establish a sustained culture of excellence at Delhi Capitals. His proven track record of building winning teams, coupled with his deep understanding of the game and ability to develop talent, makes him an invaluable addition to our leadership. We believe his vision, experience and leadership will play a pivotal role in shaping the next chapter of our WPL journey and building a team that consistently competes at the highest level.” Mahela Jayawardene, Director of Cricket, Delhi Capitals (WPL), said, “Delhi Capitals has a strong identity and an exciting vision for the future of women’s cricket. I am delighted to take on the role of Director of Cricket for the WPL team. The competition has enormous potential to shape the future of the women’s game, and I look forward to working with an established group of talented players and an experienced support team. My focus will be on building on the team’s existing strengths, bringing greater consistency to performances and ensuring we continue to evolve and compete for the title. I am excited about what we can achieve together.”

item.title: India seeks balanced trade with Indonesia, highlights export opportunities
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: India and Indonesia have reviewed their $24.78 billion bilateral trade and explored ways to expand exports, improve market access and resolve trade barriers. Discussions also covered digital payments, services, energy cooperation, critical minerals and the ASEAN-India trade agreement review
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: India has underlined the importance of balanced and diversified trade with Indonesia, highlighting export opportunities in pharmaceuticals, vaccines and medical devices, automobiles and components, machinery, dairy, rice, spices, electronics, and solar and energy-related products.

During the second meeting of the India-Indonesia Working Group on Trade and Investment (WGTI) here, both sides reviewed bilateral trade, which stood at $24.78 billion in FY 2025-26, with Indonesia accounting for 19.30 per cent of India’s trade with ASEAN.

According to an official statement, the discussions focused on the resolution of issues faced by exporters, including market access for agricultural and animal products such as peanuts, horticultural products, buffalo meat and frozen shrimp, approval of establishments, halal certification, standards and certification requirements for tyres and automobiles, registration of pharmaceuticals and AYUSH products, and local content requirements in electronics.

India also proposed designating contact points in the counterpart agencies for time-bound resolution of these issues. Issues raised by Indonesia, including market access for agricultural products and India’s Quality Control Orders, were also discussed.

Both sides explored cooperation in the services sector, including mutual recognition of professional qualifications, mobility of professionals, social security, digital services, health, education and tourism.

India also underlined the importance of an early conclusion of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Review, said the statement.

The two sides also deliberated on customs cooperation; critical minerals and mining; local currency settlement, the linkage of India’s UPI with Indonesia’s QRIS, and banking and insurance; energy, including renewable energy, green hydrogen and biofuels; fertilisers; port and air connectivity; and the implementation of the agreements and MoUs signed during the July 2026 visit.

The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Amit Verma, and the Indonesian delegation by Director of Bilateral Negotiation, Ministry of Trade, Indonesia, Basaria Tiara Desika L. Gaol.

item.title: India increases US Treasury holdings to $228.2 billion in September
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: India's holdings of US Treasury securities rose to $228.2 billion in September, marking a fifth consecutive monthly increase. The country ranked 14th among major foreign holders, even as overall foreign holdings of US government debt declined
item.content:encoded:
Washington: US Treasury securities holdings attributed to India rose to $228.2 billion in September, registering a fifth consecutive monthly increase, according to latest figures released by the US Treasury Department.

The September figure was $8.5 billion higher than August’s $219.7 billion, an increase of about 3.9 per cent. Compared with September 2025, holdings rose by $25.5 billion, or about 12.6 per cent.

The monthly series shows a steady recovery from $181 billion in April. Holdings increased to $181.3 billion in May, $186.4 billion in June and $202.6 billion in July before rising further in August and September.

India ranked 14th among the individually listed countries and jurisdictions in Treasury’s table of major foreign holders.

The increase came as total foreign holdings of US Treasury securities declined to about $9.24 trillion in September from $9.32 trillion in August.

Japan remained the largest listed holder, with about $1.06 trillion, followed by the United Kingdom at $985.8 billion and mainland China at $563.9 billion. China’s holdings fell from $590.7 billion in August.

The figures, published on Wednesday under the Treasury International Capital reporting system, require caution when interpreting individual countries’ investment decisions.

Treasury said the country breakdown relies primarily on custodial reporting.

Holdings managed by overseas investment managers on behalf of clients in other countries can create similar difficulties. The India figure therefore does not establish that the Reserve Bank of India purchased the additional securities or explain the reasons for the increase.

A change in the value of holdings also differs from the amount of securities bought during a month.

The broader September release recorded a net international capital inflow into the United States of $261 billion across long-term securities, short-term US securities and banking flows.

Private foreign inflows totalled $267 billion, while foreign official flows recorded a net outflow of $6 billion.

Foreign investors’ net purchases of long-term US securities were $186.7 billion. That category extends beyond Treasury debt and should not be confused with the country holdings table.

item.title: Nirmal: ED searches former MLA A Rekha Naik’s residence, rice mill
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches at former MLA A Rekha Naik’s residence and a rice mill in Nirmal district on Friday. Officials reportedly seized documents as part of a probe into alleged diversion of paddy worth Rs 40.96 crore.
item.content:encoded:
Nirmal: Sleuths of Enforcement Directorate carried out simultaneous searches in the residence and rice mills of former MLA A Rekha Naik and seized documents relating to rice mills in Khanapur early in the morning on Friday.

The officials conducted searches at the residence in Khanapur and ARS Industries, a rice mill at Sattenapalli village, from 5 am. It is learnt their focus was on the angle of money laundering as well. They reportedly seized documents with regard to allocation of paddy and rice milled under Custom Milling Rice process.

Earlier, Rekha Naik was booked for allegedly diverting 9,639 metric tonnes of paddy worth Rs 40.96 crore in August. Officials of the enforcement department conducted verification of physical stocks at the mill and found that the paddy belonging to three seasons was deficit for. They lodged a complaint with police.

item.title: Rajgopal Reddy hits back at Revanth Reddy, urges him to avoid arrogance and focus on governance
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Congress MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy criticised Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s language and urged him to avoid arrogance, honour electoral promises and ensure corruption-free governance. He also alleged that backward constituencies, including Munugode, were being neglected in fund allocations.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A day after Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy took a dig at him, Congress MLA from Munugode Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy hit back, advising the Chief Minister to speak with dignity and avoid arrogance while holding a high office.

“The people of Telangana and history will never forgive rulers who misuse the power they have gained by sheer luck to indulge in rampant corruption, neglect public needs and govern wickedly. They must never forget this,” he said in a post on X.

Reminding the Chief Minister of the oath he had taken to fulfil promises made to the people, Rajgopal Reddy cautioned him against handing over the State’s valuable resources to contractors and those involved in corruption.

Speaking to media persons here on Friday, the Munugode MLA said the previous BRS government had left Telangana burdened with debt. He urged the Chief Minister to focus on the welfare of the poor and the State’s development with honesty and commitment.

“I pray to Lord Ayyappa to bless you with wisdom. People will bless you when you deliver good governance. But do not speak with arrogance. Stop lashing out at Opposition parties. Instead, recall your electoral promises and introspect on whether you are delivering corruption-free governance,” he said.

Rajgopal Reddy maintained that he was only raising the concerns of people from his constituency and seeking to ensure that they were not subjected to injustice.

Stressing the need for equitable development, he said justice should be done to all backward constituencies, including Munugode. While the Chief Minister and Cabinet Ministers were sanctioning thousands of crores of rupees for their respective constituencies, other regions were being neglected, he alleged.

“I do not like the Chief Minister’s language. When questioned about the allocation of funds to Kodangal, he used unparliamentary language. I only found fault with his attitude,” Rajgopal Reddy said.

item.title: A2H Chess Academy to organise rapid and blitz tournaments in Hyderabad on November 24
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A2H Chess Academy will organise open prize-money rapid and blitz chess tournaments at Smart Kennedy School in Kukatpally, Hyderabad, on November 24. The events will follow a six-round Swiss League format. Registrations are being accepted through FIDE Arbiter S Subba Raju.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A2H Chess Academy will be organizing the Open prize money rapid and blitz chess tournaments at Smart Kennedy School (Kukatpally) here on November 24. There will be six rounds to be held in Swiss League format.

For registrations contact S Subba Raju, FIDE Arbiter on mobile 9866702431.

item.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul lead India’s fightback against New Zealand in first Test
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Yashasvi Jaiswal struck 85 and KL Rahul remained unbeaten on 52 as India reached 159/1 at stumps on day two of the first Test against New Zealand. India trailed by 209 runs, with nine wickets remaining.
item.content:encoded:
Wellington: A blazing 85 off 89 balls from Yashasvi Jaiswal and an unbeaten 52 off 116 deliveries from KL Rahul lifted India to 159/1 in 39 overs at stumps on day two of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve here on Friday.

Replying to the hosts first-innings score of 368, with Henry Nicholls unbeaten on 175, India trail by 209 runs with nine wickets in hand. Rahul is unbeaten on 52 off 116 balls, with Devdutt Padikkal not out on 16 off 35 balls. With batting expected to become easier, India will look to overhaul New Zealand’s 368 and get into taking a lead.

India resumed after tea break from 16/0, especially after Jaiswal and Rahul survived a tricky examination in the second session. Jaiswal soon began to dominate by driving Matt Henry twice past mid-off in the 13th over. Rahul raised the team’s fifty in the 14th over with two boundaries off Jacob Duffy, including off a no-ball.

Duffy struggled for rhythm and conceded 30 runs in his first four overs, as Jaiswal ramped him over the slips, and the pair took 81 runs off the first 15 overs of the session. Jaiswal reached his first Test fifty in New Zealand off 66 balls in the 23rd over with a crisp drive off a Duffy half-volley, and slogged the next ball over the slips for four.

A second ramp from Jaiswal off Nathan Smith brought up the century of the opening stand. It was India’s first for the opening wicket in 17 Tests, since the same pair added 201 runs in the win in Perth in November 2024.

Henry finally had a breakthrough for New Zealand in the 28th over after wicketkeeper Tom Blundell came up to the stumps, as Jaiswal feathered behind a delivery that took a faint edge behind. Neither the umpire nor Blundell was convinced, but Henry insisted on a review and it ended Jaiswal’s innings of 85 off 89 balls, laced with 16 fours.

The 130-run opening stand is India’s second-highest partnership for the first wicket in New Zealand, behind the 149-run association Manoj Prabhakar and WV Raman had in Auckland in 1990.

After that, New Zealand regained some control – Padikkal got off the mark with an inside edge that narrowly missed his off-stump, and Rahul survived a mix-up for a single when Glenn Phillips fumbled on collecting the ball.

After Henry and Jamieson bowled successive maidens, Rahul, playing his first Test in New Zealand, reached his 22nd Test fifty with a push through cover-point. It was his first fifty against New Zealand, and he now has fifty-plus scores in all four SENA countries. Duffy, who overstepped repeatedly, was cut for four by Padikkal in the final over, as India had a solid day of Test cricket.

Brief Scores: New Zealand 368 in 121 overs (Henry Nicholls 175, Glenn Phillips 118; Jasprit Bumrah 4-92, Akash Deep 3-53) lead India 159/1 in 39 overs (Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, KL Rahul 52 not out; Matt Henry 1-43) by 209 runs

item.title: Satwik-Chirag enter Hong Kong Open 2026 semifinals with hard-fought win
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty entered the Hong Kong Open 2026 semifinals after defeating China's Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi. Meanwhile, India's Rakshitha Ramraj bowed out of the women's singles quarter-finals against Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong.
item.content:encoded:
Hong Kong: India’s top men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty stormed into the semifinals of the Hong Kong Open 2026 with a hard-fought three-game victory over China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi on Friday.

In their quarterfinal match, the Indian pair registered a 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 win. They lost the second game but bounced back to win the third to book their spot in the semis.

Satwik and Chirag quickly found their ground, as they led 6-3 and then 9-6 and raced to 11-7 at the first interval. After the change of ends, the pair sprinted ahead to 15-10 and took just 13 minutes to win the opening game 21-12.

The second game was a lot more competitive, and there was nothing between the teams at 4-4 before the Indians were a little ahead at 9-9. Hu and Lin took the game at 13-11 and moved out to 15-11 before winning it 21-13.

The Indians made a strong comeback in the third game and led 11-7 at the interval. They kept the winning momentum going to surge ahead 15-9 and 17-10, and though the Chinese duo pulled some way back towards the close, Satwik and Chirag kept their composure to win the game 21-16 and enter the last four.

On the other hand, India’s Rakshitha Ramraj was ousted in the women’s singles quarterfinals following her 19-21, 16-21 defeat by Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong in 53 minutes.

The 19-year-old Indian fought hard in the first game which saw the scores remain level at 13-13. Chochuwong edged ahead at 17-15 but Rakshitha fought her way back to even at 17-17. Thai shuttler, however, kept her cool to clinch it 21-19.

In the second game, Chochuwong again carried a narrow lead and then scored four in a row to go 14-10 up. She continued to hold the Indian at arm’s length and claimed victory in the 21-16 semi-final.

item.title: Lalit Modi wishes Sushmita Sen on 51st birthday, calls her ‘dear friend’
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Former IPL chairman Lalit Modi wished actress Sushmita Sen on her 51st birthday, calling her his dear friend. His Instagram post comes nearly four years after their relationship became public, with Modi later citing geographical distance as a reason for their separation.
item.content:encoded:
Lalit Modi shares sweet birthday wish for former girlfriend Sushmita Sen, calls her ‘dear friend’

Mumbai: Businessman and former IPL chairman Lalit Modi wished actress Sushmita Sen on her 51st birthday.

He referred to her as his “dear friend” in a social media post, years after their much-talked-about relationship. Taking to Instagram, Lalit shared a birthday message for the actress, extending his warm wishes and called her a dear friend. The businessman shared a black-and-white picture featuring himself and Sushmita. In the photograph, the ‘Main Hoon Na’ actress is seen smiling as she poses in a black dress, while Lalit is dressed in a white pantsuit. The text on their photo read, “Happy Birthday My Friend.”

Alongside the image, Modi wrote, “Wishing you a very happy birthday my dearest Friend@sushmitasen47 – keep smiling.”

The birthday greeting comes nearly four years after Lalit and Sushmita made their relationship public in 2022.

For the unversed, the duo made headlines in July 2022 after Lalit shared several photographs with Sushmita from their vacations in the Maldives and Sardinia. While announcing their relationship, the businessman called the actress his “better half” and described the development as the start of a new chapter in his life.

His social media post also fuelled rumours of an impending wedding. However, Lalit later clarified that they were dating and had not got married.

Rumours of a split between the two surfaced in September 2022 after Lalit changed his Instagram display picture, removing photographs of Sushmita, and deleted mentions of her from his bio.

In February 2025, Lalit appeared to have moved on as he shared a video featuring his new partner, Rima Bouri. Alongside the post, he revealed that their friendship of 25 years had eventually blossomed into love. Later, in June 2026, Lalit spoke about his relationship with Sushmita in an interview. Reflecting on why their relationship did not last, he cited geographical distance as one of the key reasons behind their separation.

item.title: JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard report customer data exposure in cyber incidents
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed cyber incidents involving third-party service providers, with some customer information potentially exposed. The companies said their payment networks and services remained unaffected, while investigations and support measures for affected customers continued
item.content:encoded:
Washington: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed cyber incidents involving outside service providers, with some customer information exposed or potentially accessed, while saying their services or payment networks remained unaffected.

The disclosures concern marketing information and a cardholder benefit programme. Visa said payment data, including card numbers, was unaffected, while Mastercard described the exposed information as email addresses unrelated to payments, a media report said.

JPMorgan said its investigation indicated that attackers had accessed marketing data held by vendors, potentially including some customers’ names and email addresses, according to Yahoo Finance. The bank distinguished the cyberattack from service problems earlier in the week, which it attributed to a software bug.

“Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring,” Chase said in a statement reproduced by NBC Chicago.

The bank said the cyberattack had caused no disruption to its services. Its description of the information potentially accessed remained qualified, reflecting the investigation’s findings so far.

Mastercard said the incident involved a small group of cardholders enrolled in a particular benefit programme. In comments to The Register, senior vice-president Seth Eisen said the exposure had been contained and the company was working with the provider to support affected customers.

“There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards,” he said.

Visa linked the claims concerning its customers to an incident involving a service provider in the Asia-Pacific region. The company told The Register that its own systems were neither involved nor affected, and that payment information such as card numbers was unaffected.

That regional description does not establish that Indian cardholders were affected. The company statements reviewed for this report provided no India-specific figures or notification.

The Wall Street Journal reported that a ransomware group had leaked information belonging to thousands of customers. However, the companies’ statements reviewed did not establish a common affected vendor or a consolidated number of customers across the three businesses.

In its general guidance, the US Federal Trade Commission warns that fraudulent emails and messages can impersonate banks and other familiar companies to solicit financial information. It advises customers to verify unexpected requests through a known telephone number or website, rather than contact details supplied in the message. That guidance is general and was not issued specifically in response to these incidents.

item.title: Cyclone Akvan crosses Andhra Pradesh coast near Gopalpur after weakening
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Cyclonic Storm Akvan crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts near Gopalpur on Friday after weakening from a severe cyclonic storm. Authorities reported no damage, while residents of Srikakulam were advised to remain alert as rain remained likely.
item.content:encoded:
Visakhapatnam: Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ crossed north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur on Friday, the IMD said, adding that the severe cyclonic storm has weakened into a cyclonic storm before making landfall.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in a bulletin that ‘Akvan’ over the westcentral Bay of Bengal near north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 26 kmph during the past six hours and crossed the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur with a wind speed of 70-80kmph gusting to 90kmph during 0730-0830 IST.

It lay centred over south coastal Odisha and adjoining north coastal Andhra Pradesh, close to Gopalpur (Odisha), about 120 km northeast of Kalingapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 130 km west-southwest of Puri (Odisha), and 230 km northeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh).

It is likely to move nearly north-northeastwards across Odisha and weaken into a deep depression during the next three hours and into a depression during the subsequent six hours, it said.

According to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA), light to moderate rain is likely in North Andhra.

Even though the system has crossed the coast, residents of Srikakulam district must remain alert, said Prakhar Jain, Managing Director of APSDMA and Chief Executive Officer of Real Time Governance Society (RTGS).

Authorities in Andhra Pradesh heaved a sigh of relief as ‘Akvan’ weakened before making landfall. There are no reports of any damage from anywhere.

This was the third cyclone to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast in less than a month.

Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ had struck the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 27.

Severe cyclonic storm ‘Murasu’ had crossed the coast between Nellore and Narasapur on November 3.

Two cyclones within a week had resulted in the death of 15 people and caused widespread damage to infrastructure and crops in the coastal districts.

Heavy rains and strong winds caused extensive damage to infrastructure, including electricity networks and roads.

item.title: California launches probe into Nvidia over alleged China technology links
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation into possible technology transfers to China and alleged misleading disclosures. The probe adds to growing scrutiny of the chipmaker, including separate congressional inquiries and internal governance changes
item.content:encoded:
Washington: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia, seeking to determine whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether the company misled investors and the public about the risks.

The California Department of Justice said information obtained through the subpoena would help it assess whether Nvidia’s actions violated state law.

Bonta said the inquiry would examine the conduct of both Nvidia and its former chief executive, Jensen Huang, including whether their actions enabled China to obtain sensitive technology or information.

“Companies cannot mislead their investors,” Bonta said, describing investor protection as the central principle underlying the inquiry.

His office linked the investigation to reports of Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. The announcement did not establish that espionage occurred or that Nvidia’s technology or confidential information had been improperly transferred.

The Los Angeles Times reported that Nvidia did not immediately respond to its request for comment.

Nvidia had previously announced its own independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

In a November 8 statement, the board said it had no reason at that time to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised, while committing to examine the available information.

The company said a committee of independent directors, supported by independent outside counsel, would oversee that investigation and that Huang had committed to cooperate. That statement preceded California’s subpoena and was not a response to it.

The company has since changed its leadership. According to its filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the board accepted Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and director on November 11, effective immediately.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was appointed interim chief executive while retaining her finance responsibilities. Harvey C. Jones became board chair.

On November 17, Nvidia also established a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to supervise its security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risks.

Director Suzanne Nora Johnson chairs the committee, alongside directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri. Nvidia said its national-security and trade-compliance teams would report directly to the committee and to Kress on day-to-day operations.

The committee will meet at least quarterly and work with independent specialists in law, national security and trade compliance. Nvidia presented the move as an effort to strengthen governance and engagement with government authorities.

Separate congressional scrutiny is also scheduled next month.

The House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China committees announced on November 17 that Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter had voluntarily agreed to transcribed interviews.

Huang is scheduled to appear on December 1 and Teter on December 2.

item.title: Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran thank fans after Greece wedding
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Music composer Anirudh Ravichander and Kavya Maran have thanked fans and well-wishers for their love and blessings following their wedding in Greece. The couple recently returned to Chennai, where their wedding reception is scheduled for November 21
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Music composer Anirudh Ravichander and his wife Kaviya have expressed gratitude to fans and well-wishers for showering them with love and blessings as they embark on a new journey together.

The couple shared a heartfelt note on Instagram, saying their wishes had made their new beginning even more special.

“Our hearts are full. Your love and blessings mean more to us than words can express. Thank you for making this new beginning even more special. We carry all your love with us – Kaviya and Anirudh,” Anirudh wrote in the caption.

For the unaware, Anirudh and Kavya Maran, who is also the daughter of Sun Group Chairman Kalanidhi Maran and the owner of the IPL franchise SunRisers Hyderabad, returned to Chennai on Saturday after their wedding in Greece, which was held on November 11 this year.

The wedding, which took place in Greece over a two-day period, had been the cynosure of all eyes as distinguished guests for the wedding were flown to the venue.

Anirudh, who had posted pictures of his wedding, on social media soon after the ceremony, had said, “My once in a lifetime, for a lifetime 11.11.”

Tamil film Superstar Rajinikanth, Union Minister Dayanidhi Maran and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M K Stalin were among those present at the wedding.

The news of the music director’s wedding was first officially confirmed by the Telangana Chief Minister’s office which had put out a post on its X timeline saying that Sun Group Chairman Kalanidhi Maran and his wife Kavery Maran had called on the Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy at his residence in Jubilee hills to invite him to the wedding reception of his daughter Kavya Maran, which was to be held in Chennai on November 21.

item.title: Gold and silver prices crash up to 6.6 pc amid strong dollar, rising US bond yields
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Gold and silver prices plunged up to 6.6 per cent in early trade as a stronger US dollar, rising bond yields and expectations of tighter US Federal Reserve policy weighed on investor sentiment, triggering heavy selling across global bullion markets.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Gold and silver prices witnessed sharp declines in early trade on Friday, plunging up to 6.6 pc as a stronger US dollar, elevated bond yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy from the US Federal Reserve continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures (December) plunged as much as 4.49 per cent or Rs 5,733 to Rs 1,21,719 per 10 grams against the previous close of Rs 1,27,452, hitting an intraday low by 10:30 am.

On the other hand, silver futures (December) also came under heavy selling pressure, falling 6.6 per cent or Rs 10,416 to an intraday low of Rs 1,47,066 per kg so far.

International markets showed a similar trend. Spot gold slipped below $3,550 per ounce after briefly trading near $3,630 per ounce, putting the precious metal on course for a double-digit weekly decline.

Silver also retreated sharply, falling towards the $41-an-ounce mark and heading for significant weekly losses.

Commodity experts attributed the selloff to growing expectations that the US Federal Reserve could maintain a restrictive policy stance for longer amid persistent inflation concerns.

“MCX gold is testing the Rs 1,22,000-1,22,800 support zone, with a decisive breach potentially exposing the next downside cushion at Rs 1,18,000-1,19,000. On the upside, the Rs 1,26,300-1,27,000 region, which held as support until Thursday, has now turned into immediate resistance, followed by Rs 1,30,000-1,30,700,” they said.

“The RSI near 18 signals extremely oversold conditions, while the widening MACD gap points to intensifying bearish momentum. Although the oversold reading leaves scope for a sharp technical rebound, the price structure remains weak,” the analysts added.

The near-term bias remains negative, with a sustained recovery above Rs 1,27,000 needed to stabilise the technical outlook. On the downside, a decisive break below Rs 1,22,000 could accelerate losses towards Rs 1,19,000, despite deeply oversold momentum conditions.

For silver, the experts noted that prices are testing the Rs 1,48,000-1,50,000 support zone, with a decisive break exposing the next downside cushion at Rs 1,40,000-1,42,000.

“On the upside, immediate resistance is placed at Rs 1,56,000-1,58,000, followed by Rs 1,64,000-1,66,000. The RSI near 18 signals deeply oversold conditions, while the MACD continues to slope lower, indicating persistent bearish momentum. Although the oversold reading leaves room for a sharp technical rebound, the chart has yet to show signs of stabilisation,” the experts said.

“The near-term bias remains bearish, with a sustained recovery above Rs 1,58,000 needed to stabilise the technical outlook. Alternatively, a decisive break below Rs 1,48,000 could accelerate losses towards Rs 1,42,000, despite deeply oversold momentum conditions,” they added.

Moreover, rising Treasury yields and a relatively strong dollar have reduced the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold and silver, prompting investors to cut their exposure to bullion.

In addition, the US dollar index remained near multi-month highs, while crude oil prices held above the $90-per-barrel level, adding to inflation-related concerns in global markets.

item.title: Anthropic IPO creates 600 employees with stakes worth over $100 million
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Anthropic's stock market debut has reportedly turned about 5,100 employees into millionaires on paper, with nearly 600 holding equity worth over $100 million. The AI company's listing also coincided with a sharp decline in major US stock indices
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic’s stock market debut has generated substantial wealth for its employees with a majority of the company’s workforce now estimated to hold equity stakes worth more than $1 million, as per reports.

Reports said roughly 5,100 employees, about 96 per cent of Anthropic’s workforce, are now estimated to be millionaires on paper following the company’s public listing.

They further suggest that nearly 2,800 employees hold shares valued at more than $10 million, while around 600 employees have equity stakes exceeding $100 million.

The surge in employee wealth follows Anthropic’s record-setting public offering that raised approximately $81 billion after shares were priced at $83 each.

The stock opened significantly above its offer price during its Nasdaq debut and ended its first trading session with double-digit gains.

Anthropic was founded in 2021 and had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024 before rapidly expanding its workforce amid growing demand for artificial intelligence products and services.

Reports also highlighted that Anthropic adopted a more flexible approach to employee share sales following its listing.

Unlike traditional initial public offerings, which often impose lock-up restrictions preventing insiders from selling shares for several months, the company reportedly allowed non-founder employees to sell a limited portion of their holdings from the first day of trading.

Notably, global equities witnessed heavy selling pressure amid a decline in tech shares after the AI giant’s debut.

The maker of Claude had priced its IPO at $83 a share, valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion.

The stock jumped as much as 39 per cent to $115.10 during the session.

Anthropic shares ended their first day up 17 per cent, valuing the company at just under $1.8 trillion.

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell over 1,000 points or 2.19 per cent to 49,097.06. Similarly, the S&P 500 fell 147.80 points or 2.02 per cent to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 550.68 points or 2.25 per cent to 23,879.20.

item.title: Anish Giri beats Firouzja, takes 11–9 lead in chess final
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Anish Giri defeated Alireza Firouzja 11–9 to take the first-day lead in the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot final in Budapest. Fabiano Caruana also secured an 11–9 advantage against Maxime Vachier-Lagrave in the third-place match
item.content:encoded:
Budapest: Anish Giri won the opening day of the final of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest on Thursday, defeating Alireza Firouzja by 11 points to 9.

Giri’s advantage in blitz proved decisive after the players exchanged rapid victories and drew their Fast Classic game.

A win or draw on Friday would secure Giri the Budapest pilot title without a tiebreak. The scores reset overnight, so Firouzja must win the second day to force an Armageddon tiebreak.

Each knockout day has seven games: four Blitz games, two Rapid games and one Fast Classic. A Blitz win is worth one point, a Rapid win four and a Fast Classic win eight, with half for a draw. Winning both days, or winning one and drawing the other, decides the match. One win apiece, or two drawn days, leads to Armageddon.

Fabiano Caruana also took an 11–9 first-day lead against Maxime Vachier-Lagrave in the match for third place. All 24 players were in action as the finals and placement matches began across the six knockout brackets.

Giri drew the opening blitz game before winning the second with White and the third with Black, the latter after a long battle. A draw in the fourth gave him a 3–1 lead.

Firouzja responded by winning the first rapid game with White. However, Giri immediately answered with a White victory in the second rapid game to regain the lead at 7–5.

Four points apiece from the Fast Classic draw preserved Giri’s advantage and completed his third successive daily victory in the knockout stage, following his two wins against Vachier-Lagrave in the semifinals.

Caruana won the first two blitz games against Vachier-Lagrave, once with each colour, before the remaining five games were drawn. His 3–1 advantage from blitz therefore carried through to an 11–9 daily victory.

Caruana needs a win or a tie on Friday to finish third. Vachier-Lagrave must win the second day to take their match to Armageddon.

Magnus Carlsen recorded his first Fast Classic win of the event, beating Vladislav Artemiev with White to turn a 3–9 deficit into an 11–9 daily victory in the match for 17th place. Carlsen had won three of the four blitz games, but forfeited both rapid games, leaving him needing the eight-point Fast Classic win to take the day.

Hans Moke Niemann remained unbeaten across all seven games against Jan-Krzysztof Duda in the match for fifth place. He won the first three blitz games and the first rapid game, drawing the others to take the day 13.5–6.5. Wesley So also moved ahead, beating Levon Aronian 12.5–7.5 in their match for 13th place.

Home favourite Richard Rapport had already secured the day against Jorden van Foreest by taking an 11–1 lead from blitz and rapid. Having already secured the day’s victory, Rapport forfeited the Fast Classic game, resulting in an 11–9 daily victory in their match for 11th place.

item.title: Badminton: Rakshitha Sree Santhosh exits quarter-finals after impressive run
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj’s impressive badminton campaign ended in the quarter-finals after she lost to Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong in straight games. Earlier, she stunned Tokyo Olympics champion Chen Yu Fei and Denmark’s Mia Blichfeldt.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj’s stellar campaign comes to an end in the quarter-finals as she goes down to Thailand’s World No. 8 Pornpawee Chochuwong 19-21, 16-21.

Earlier in the tournament, Rakshitha produced impressive performances, upsetting Tokyo Olympics champion Chen Yu Fei and Denmark’s Mia Blichfeldt.

item.title: Sensex plunges 615 points, Nifty slips as global sell-off rattles markets
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Indian equity benchmarks fell sharply in early trade on Friday, with the Sensex losing 615 points and the Nifty slipping 170. Metal stocks led sectoral losses, while global weakness, AI valuation concerns and profit booking weighed on investor sentiment
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Indian equity benchmarks traded sharply lower in early deals on Friday, tracking weakness across global markets and profit booking after the recent rally.

Sensex dropped as much as 615 points or 0.74 per cent to an intraday low of 82,403 in early trade.

Nifty 50 declined around 170 points or 0.66 per cent to 25,345 by 9:17 am.

The selling pressure was widespread across sectors with Nifty Metal emerging as the biggest laggard and declining 1.8 per cent.

Nifty PSU Bank declined 0.97 per cent, while Nifty Realty and Oil & Gas indices shed 0.79 per cent each.

In contrast, information technology (IT) shares bucked the trend as the Nifty IT index rose 0.76 per cent.

Among Nifty constituents, Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Titan, Shriram Finance, Larsen & Toubro, Hindalco, SBI and Bajaj Finserv were among top losers.

Analysts attributed the weakness to a combination of global risk aversion and domestic profit taking following the sharp surge in Indian equities this month.

However, they said India’s market remains among the strongest-performing globally this month supported by sustained foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows and robust corporate earnings.

Experts expect near-term volatility to persist amid global market uncertainty, though they believe strong foreign inflows and earnings momentum could continue to support domestic equities.

In addition, concerns surrounding the artificial intelligence (AI) investment theme continued to weigh on global markets after another round of declines on Wall Street. The Nasdaq fell 2.25 per cent overnight, while S&P 500 also declined nearly 2 per cent.

Investor sentiment was also affected by developments surrounding AI company Anthropic’s market debut. Although the stock surged after listing, concerns about elevated valuations in the AI space triggered broader selling across technology-linked markets globally.

Additionally, Asian markets showed negative trend as major indices — Japan’s Nikkei, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng and South Korea’s KOSPI — declined up to 5 per cent.

item.title: Woman dies in accident after CM Revanth’s meeting in Siddipet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: SHG member Kommu Saravva, 55, of Nagaram died after being crushed between two buses in a Siddipet parking area following Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s public meeting. Minister Ponnam Prabhakar announced Rs 5 lakh ex gratia.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: A Self Help Group (SHG) member died after she was crushed between two buses in the parking area following Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s public meeting on the town outskirts on Thursday.

According reports, reckless driving by a bus driver led to the death of Kommu Saravva (55) of Nagaram in Husnabad mandal. Saravva had attended the meeting and was proceeding to catch a bus to return home after Revanth Reddy completed his speech at around 8 pm.

As buses moved helter-skelter in the parking area in a bid to reach their destinations early, Saravva was crushed between two buses and died at the spot after sustaining serious injuries.

Her body was taken to the Government Hospital in Siddipet for postmortem and was to be taken to her residence on Friday morning.

BC Welfare Minister and local MLA Ponnam Prabhakar, who expressed shock over the incident, visited her family at the Government Hospital in Siddipet on Friday morning and consoled the family members.

He announced Rs 5 lakh ex gratia to Saravva’s bereaved family members and assured them of all support in the future. Siddipet police registered a case.

item.title: Fire engulfs electric car after truck collision on Hyderabad ORR
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: An electric car was gutted after colliding with a truck on the Outer Ring Road near Kokapet Friday morning. All four occupants escaped unhurt, while firefighters brought the blaze under control. The Narsingi police are investigating the accident's cause
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: An electric car was completely gutted in a fire following a collision with a truck on the Outer Ring Road (ORR) near Kokapet under Narsingi police station limits on Friday morning. However, no casualties were reported in the incident.

The car, reportedly travelling from Kokapet towards Patancheru, rammed into a truck moving ahead. Within minutes of the collision, flames erupted from the vehicle and quickly engulfed it.

Alerted by the sudden fire, all four occupants reportedly stepped out of the car in time and escaped unhurt. The vehicle was reduced to ashes within minutes.

On receiving information, the local police and firefighters rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control, averting a major tragedy.

The exact cause of the fire and further details of the accident are yet to be ascertained.

The Narsingi police are investigating.

item.title: Apple-laden truck overturns on Hyderabad-Vijayawada highway, driver injured
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: An apple-laden truck overturned on the Hyderabad-Vijayawada National Highway near Abdullapurmet on Friday morning after the driver reportedly lost control. The driver suffered serious injuries, while the accident disrupted traffic and left apples scattered across the highway
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: An apple-laden truck overturned on the Hyderabad -Vijayawada National Highway near Abdullapurmet after the driver reportedly lost control of the vehicle on Friday morning.

As per information available, the truck was carrying a consignment of apples when it veered out of control and overturned on the road, leaving apples scattered across the highway.

The driver suffered serious injuries in the mishap. Local residents rushed to his rescue immediately after the accident.

The overturned truck disrupted traffic, leading to a temporary traffic jam on the busy stretch.

On receiving information, the Abdullapurmet Police reached the spot and took up measures to clear the vehicle and restore normal traffic flow.

The exact cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained.

item.title: Hey Kannamma gets U/A certificate ahead of November 27 release
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Director Sasi Kumar Muthuluri's Telugu romantic entertainer Hey Kannamma, featuring Yashwanth, Dhanasree Verma and Karthika Muralidharan, has received a U/A certificate from the CBFC. Produced by Dil Raju Productions, the film is scheduled for a worldwide release on November 27
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) has now cleared director Sasi Kumar Muthuluri’s upcoming Telugu film ‘Hey Kannamma’, featuring actors Yashwanth, Dhanasree Verma and Karthika Muralidharan in the lead, for release with a ‘U/A’ certificate.

Dil Raju Productions LLP, which is producing the film, took to its social media timelines to make the announcement. It wrote, “U/A Certified! Get ready to experience the new age love story #HeyKannamma on the big screens! Worldwide Theatrical Release on NOVEMBER 27!”

Written and directed by Shashi Kumar Muthuluri, the film, a new age love story is being presented by Zee Studios. The film has been produced by Harshit Reddy and Hanshita under the banner of Dil Raju Productions LLP.

Excitement about the film increased among film buffs after the makers recently released a teaser. The teaser starts with a voice-over. A man is heard saying, “My life, my dreams, my hopes, my desires.. I have lived my life as if I were mine. Now when I see the world through your eyes.. I understand what the love you desire is like, Kannamma.”

The way Yashwanth and Dhanashree Varma have showcased their characters has increased fans interest in the film.

The film boasts of a gifted technical team. While music for the film has been scored by Karthik, its background score has been provided by Jai Krishna, who has also scored the music for the film’s teaser.

Cinematography for the film is by the talented cameraman Rampi Nandigam while production design for the film has been handled by Gandhi Nadikudikar.

The film’s story has been co-written by Tarun Sakala, Teja Reddy, Mahesh Yellapu while its editing is being handled by Madhu. Bandi Ratna has taken on the responsibilities of an executive producer in this film, which is slated to hit screens on November 27 worldwide.

item.title: Delhi AQI stands at 267 as pollution persists amid chilly weather
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Delhi recorded an average AQI of 267 on Friday, with several monitoring stations reporting 'very poor' air quality. Pollution levels worsened despite chilly conditions, while the minimum temperature at Safdarjung dropped to 10.6 degrees Celsius on Thursday
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Delhi continued to experience poor air quality on Friday, with the average Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 267, even as chilly weather conditions prevailed across the national capital during the morning hours.

Several monitoring stations across the city reported elevated pollution levels, with some locations recording air quality in the ‘very poor’ category. Sirifort recorded an AQI of 348, followed by Pusa at 335, JNU at 336, Burari Crossing at 333, Ghoga at 321, ITO at 321, NSUT Jaffarpur at 329, DTU at 319, Talkatora Garden at 316, Punjabi Bagh at 310 and Jahangirpuri at 307.

Other monitoring stations also reported poor air quality. These included Karala (259), Tikri Kalan (214), Chhawla (262), NIH Narela (278), Shadipur (280), Pusa (208), Chandni Chowk (330), IIT Delhi (295), Anand Vihar (267), Rohini (276), Vivek Vihar (277), Bawana (293) and Burari (290).

The deterioration follows a significant rise in pollution levels on Thursday, when Delhi’s average AQI increased by 48 points to 280 from 232 recorded a day earlier. Unfavourable meteorological conditions, which hampered the dispersion of pollutants, contributed to the worsening air quality.

According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), 16 monitoring stations had recorded air quality in the ‘very poor’ category when the official daily reading was taken at 4 p.m. on Thursday. Three stations were in the ‘moderate’ category, while most of the remaining monitoring locations reported ‘poor’ air quality.

According to AQI.in data, Delhi’s AQI touched 502 at 8.30 a.m. and stood at 485 at 9.31 a.m. PM10 concentration was also recorded at 484, nearly 10 times the World Health Organisation’s recommended safe limit.

The sudden deterioration came just two days after the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) revoked restrictions under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) following an improvement in air quality. However, preventive measures under GRAP Stages I and II continue to remain in force.

Delhi’s average daily AQI, as reported by AQI.in, stood at 276 on November 17, the day Stage III restrictions were withdrawn. It subsequently increased to 340 on November 18 before approaching the 500 mark on Thursday morning.

Meanwhile, the national capital recorded its lowest minimum temperature of the season so far on Thursday.

The minimum temperature at Safdarjung fell to 10.6 degrees Celsius, which was 1.7 degrees below the seasonal average and 0.4 degrees lower than Wednesday’s 11 degrees Celsius, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

item.title: ED searches 10 premises in Kerala over suspected gold smuggling, hawala links
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches across four Kerala districts as part of an investigation into suspected gold smuggling, hawala transactions and illegal financial networks. Around 10 premises in and around Kozhikode came under scrutiny during the operation on Friday
item.content:encoded:
Kochi: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday launched early morning searches at multiple locations across Kerala as part of an investigation into suspected gold smuggling and hawala transactions, with around 10 premises in and around Kozhikode coming under scrutiny.

Parallel searches have also begun in Palakkad, Kasargode and Kannur, taking the operation to four districts in the state.

The searches are being conducted as part of the agency’s probe into suspected foreign exchange violations and illegal financial transactions.

The operations began in the early hours of Friday, with ED teams reaching the identified premises and conducting searches.

According to agency sources, the investigation follows information received about hawala networks operating in the state, besides reports of gold smuggling incidents in recent months.

The latest searches are part of efforts to establish the financial links behind these activities and identify those allegedly involved in the illegal transactions.

The agency is particularly focusing on networks suspected of transferring money out of Kerala through illegal hawala channels.

The searches are being conducted at the residences of people allegedly having links with illegal gold and hawala dealings.

The investigation is aimed at tracing the movement of funds, identifying the people behind the suspected networks and examining possible connections between gold smuggling and illegal money transfers.

The ED is also looking into the role of individuals suspected of facilitating such transactions and the financial channels allegedly used to move money outside the formal banking system.

Incidentally, the northern districts of Kerala have figured prominently in investigations and reports relating to suspected gold smuggling and hawala activities.

The latest operation across Kozhikode, Kasargode and Kannur is part of the agency’s efforts to probe these alleged networks.

The ED has been intensifying its action against suspected financial networks in Kerala, with investigations in recent months involving alleged money laundering and illegal cross-border transactions.

The ED is expected to give out more details about the operation later in the day.

item.title: Gangster Naseem Durrani killed in Bulandshahr encounter
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Naseem Durrani, wanted in the alleged murder of Sameer in Delhi’s Sonia Vihar and carrying a Rs 50,000 reward, was killed during a joint police operation in Bulandshahr, officials said.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: A man carrying a Rs 50,000 reward was killed in an encounter during a joint operation by the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF), Delhi Police Crime Branch and Bulandshahr Police in Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr district, police officials said.

The deceased was identified as Naseem Durrani, who was allegedly involved in the murder of Sameer in Delhi’s Sonia Vihar area on Monday (November 16). He was wanted in connection with the murder near Zero Pusta in Sonia Vihar. Delhi Police had declared a reward of Rs 50,000 for his arrest.

Police said Sonia Vihar police station registered a case after the murder and formed multiple teams to trace the accused. The teams had monitored his movements and received intelligence inputs about his presence in Bulandshahr.

Acting on the information, a joint team of the Uttar Pradesh STF, Delhi Police Crime Branch and Bulandshahr Police launched an operation to apprehend him. Police said an encounter broke out during the operation, in which Durrani was killed.

According to the Uttar Pradesh STF, Durrani was also known as Naseem and Rizwan. He was the son of Islammuddin, also known as Budhu. The STF described him as a habitual and desperate criminal who operated in North-East Delhi with his associates and gang members.

The STF said he was allegedly involved in several serious offences, including murder, armed robbery, illegal possession of firearms, theft and assault on police personnel.

The STF listed FIR No. 173/2014, registered at Gokulpuri police station, among the cases against him. In the case, police personnel were allegedly assaulted and stones and bricks were pelted at a police party while an accused was being helped to escape from custody.

The STF said he was also allegedly involved in a murder case registered under FIR No. 289/2010 at Gokulpuri police station, besides multiple cases under the Arms Act and other offences registered at Khajuri Khas, Jafrabad, Dayalpur and other police stations.

The STF said his repeated involvement in serious offences indicated a sustained criminal background and alleged links with organised criminal activities in Delhi. It also said his links with D Company had been reported.

item.title: Three injured as speeding auto rams into RTC electric bus in Malkajgiri
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Three people, including two women, were injured after a speeding auto-rickshaw rammed into an RTC electric bus at Safilguda in Malkajgiri on Friday morning. Residents have urged civic authorities to improve road conditions and prevent frequent accidents
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Three people, including two women, were injured after a speeding auto-rickshaw crashed into a RTC electric bus from behind at Safilguda in Malkajgiri on Friday morning.

According to local residents, the auto-rickshaw driver lost control of the vehicle and crashed into the rear of the bus with considerable force. Two women suffered minor injuries, while the auto driver suffered serious injuries.

The accident has once again raised concerns over road safety in the area, where residents say mishaps occur frequently.
Local residents requested civic authorities to improve road conditions and take preventive measures to curb accidents.

item.title: KTR calls Revanth’s abusive language attempt to divert attention from drought, water crisis
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Reacting to the Chief Minister's remarks at Siddipet on Thursday, Rama Rao questioned why Revanth Reddy was making provocative remarks while farmers were struggling with drought and irrigation problems. He accused the government of turning a blind eye to the alleged diversion of Telangana's water to Andhra Pradesh and targeting the Opposition for exposing the issue.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao accused Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy of using abusive language and personal attacks to divert public attention from the drought, farmers’ distress and Telangana’s water disputes.

Reacting to the Chief Minister’s remarks at Siddipet on Thursday, Rama Rao questioned why Revanth Reddy was making provocative remarks while farmers were struggling with drought and irrigation problems. He accused the government of turning a blind eye to the alleged diversion of Telangana’s water to Andhra Pradesh and targeting the Opposition for exposing the issue.

He said the Chief Minister should focus on protecting the State’s interests and addressing public grievances instead of making personal remarks against BRS leaders. He also questioned Revanth Reddy’s credentials to speak about Telangana martyrs, calling him a traitor to the Telangana movement who never raised the “Jai Telangana” slogan.

Referring to Revanth Reddy’s recent speeches at Sircilla and Siddipet, the BRS working president asked what concrete benefits the Chief Minister had delivered to the State. Instead of being a responsible Chief Minister, he said, Revanth Reddy was bringing disrepute to his position. He said the Congress government had abandoned welfare schemes, failed to fulfil promises and allowed unabated corruption.

Rama Rao warned that the Congress government’s days were numbered and said every constituency would respond like Sircilla and Siddipet whenever elections were held. Calling BRS chief K. Chandrashekhar Rao the pinnacle of Telangana movement leadership and unparalleled, he said, “The Delhi slaves like Revanth Reddy can only draw psychotic pleasure by criticising him and can never reach his level.”

item.title: HCU: Over 30 students fall ill after dinner
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: More than 30 Hyderabad Central University students fell ill after Thursday night dinner at Men's Hostel M, Annex and NRS hostels. They are under treatment at the university health centre, student unions said.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: More than 30 students of Hyderabad Central University (HCU) fell ill after having dinner on Thursday night at Men's Hostel M, Annex and NRS hostels.

The students are undergoing treatment at the university health centre.

Student unions said an emergency medical camp had been set up near Men's Hostel M.

The unions said they demanded better treatment for the affected students, concessions in examinations, appointment of a permanent nutrition officer, and inspections of food quality and hygiene at all messes after the DSW visited the health centre at 2.45 am.
