They also demanded that the health centre facilities be improved, staff strength at the messes increased and steps taken to ensure quality food is served.

item.title: Hyderabad: Woman dies by suicide after boyfriend refuses to marry
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 22-year-old MBA graduate died while undergoing treatment after allegedly attempting suicide in Ghatkesar. Her family alleged that she was distressed after her boyfriend reportedly refused to marry her, despite their relationship lasting nearly a year
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 22-year-old MBA graduate died while undergoing treatment after allegedly attempting suicide following her boyfriend’s refusal to marry her, despite being in a relationship with her for nearly a year in Ghatkesar.

The victim, Aishwarya, daughter of Darnaboyina Jangaiah of NFC Nagar in Ghatkesar, had completed her MBA and was searching for a job. She was reportedly in love with Jama Kiran Kumar, a resident of Uppal, and informed her family about their relationship and plans to marry.

According to the police, both families had initially agreed to the marriage. However, trouble reportedly began when Aishwarya approached Kiran Kumar’s parents recently to discuss the wedding. His mother allegedly rejected the proposal. Following this, Kiran Kumar stopped communicating with Aishwarya and blocked her phone number.

On November 17, he reportedly sent her a message stating that he was not interested in marrying her and that she should consider a match chosen by her parents. Deeply distressed, Aishwarya allegedly messaged him that she would end her life, but he did not respond, her father stated in his complaint.

On November 18, Aishwarya went into a bedroom at her residence and locked the door. When she failed to come out despite repeated calls, her mother, Shailaja, grew suspicious. Her brother Eshwar subsequently broke open the door and found her hanging from the ceiling fan.

Family members rushed her to Ghatkesar Government Hospital before shifting her to Srikara Hospital for advanced treatment. However, she succumbed under treatment on Thursday.

Her father lodged a police complaint alleging that Kiran Kumar had deceived his daughter by promising marriage and subsequently abandoning her, causing her severe emotional distress.

Ghatkesar police registered a case and took up an investigation.

item.title: Cartoon Today on November 20, 2026
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today

item.title: Prachi Desai returns to social media after a year
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Mumbai actress Prachi Desai returned to social media in November 2026 after a year and a half, sharing casual pictures captioned “Proof of existence”. Her previous post was in June 2025.
item.content:encoded:
First post since June 2025

Mumbai: Actress Prachi Desai made a rare social media appearance after more than a year, sharing a series of pictures captioned, “Proof of existence”.

Prachi has maintained a low-key presence on social media in recent years. Her previous post had appeared in June 2025, and she returned in November 2026 after a year and a half.

In the latest pictures, Prachi is seen sitting casually, dressed in a simple white T-shirt and blue jeans, flaunting her quintessential dimple. One of the pictures also appears to capture her enjoying a cold beverage.

On the professional front, Prachi first became a household name on television with Ekta Kapoor’s Kasamh Se. She was 17 when she entered the industry and was cast as Bani Dixit Walia opposite Ram Kapoor, who played Jai Walia.

The 2006 Zee TV show became a major success, and Prachi’s portrayal of Bani quickly won her a huge following. Her pairing with Ram Kapoor became one of the most remembered television couples of that era.

Reportedly, Prachi was pursuing her studies when she was selected for Kasamh Se. She later recalled that she had to leave her studies after her HSC board examinations to pursue acting full-time.

Prachi later transitioned from television to Bollywood. She made her Hindi film debut in 2008 with Rock On!!, directed by Abhishek Kapoor and starring Farhan Akhtar, Arjun Rampal, Purab Kohli and Luke Kenny. Prachi played Sakshi, the wife of Farhan Akhtar’s character Aditya. She returned as Sakshi in Rock On 2 in 2016.

She then appeared in films including Life Partner, Once Upon a Time in Mumbaai, Teri Meri Kahaani, Jannat 2, Bol Bachchan, I, Me Aur Main, Policegiri and Azhar. In 2007, she participated in Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa 2 and went on to win the dance reality show.

item.title: All you should know about historic summit among Trump, Xi and Putin
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first three-way meeting in Shenzhen, agreeing on United Nations reforms, oil supplies and nuclear risks, while their joint declaration omitted the Ukraine and Iran wars.
item.content:encoded:
SHENZHEN: The meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday was the first sit-down involving the leaders of the three countries.

They began by discussing their shared responsibility to keep peace as victors of World War II and global powers. However, post-meeting readouts issued by the three nations contained more symbolism than substance.

The “peace declaration” released after the meeting made no mention of Russia’s war in Ukraine or the U.S.-led war in Iran. It said the leaders agreed on the need for reforms to the United Nations, increasing oil supplies and reducing nuclear risks. The statement did not specify the type or extent of the United Nations reforms agreed upon.

The three sides also agreed that state officials should enjoy immunity from prosecution, opposing what they called “jurisdiction abuse” by the International Criminal Court (ICC), the reports said.

Here are key takeaways from the talks, which lasted more than an hour.

China’s Xi presided over the summit of 21st century powers

Xi added to China’s already burgeoning diplomatic stature by hosting the event.

He said the talks with Trump and Putin were positive and fruitful, and that the three nations had aligned views on safeguarding world peace, according to China’s official Xinhua news agency.

They agreed that major powers should take the legitimate security concerns of all countries seriously and believed differences should be resolved through negotiation and cooperation, Xinhua reported.

“As long as dialogue does not stop, doors remain open, there is hope for peace,” Xi was quoted as saying. “The seeds planted at today’s trilateral meeting will surely take root, sprout, blossom and bear fruit.”

China’s insistence that it has the right to recover the democratically governed island of Taiwan, possibly by force, was not addressed in the leaders’ broadly worded agreement. China considers it a domestic issue.

China likes to position itself as a different kind of superpower from the U.S. and Russia — one that does not get involved in wars and advocates for smaller states, said Ruby Osman, a senior policy adviser at London’s Tony Blair Institute for Global Change.

Beijing’s priority was to steer the meeting away from specifics, she said. “Beijing wanted to be seen as the adult in the room.”

Trump claims a place in history

Trump described the leaders’ gathering as “really making history” and suggested to Xi and Putin that they were shaking things up by abandoning the “old school” way adversaries engage.

The White House set low expectations for the talks. But Trump described them on Thursday as only the beginning — a chance to start discussions on solving some of the world’s most difficult issues.

“A lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start,” Trump told Putin during a one-on-one meeting before their three-way meeting with Xi.

The carefully crafted event was a welcome break for Trump after a couple of difficult weeks for his presidency, during which his Republican Party was defeated in the midterm elections, widespread technology outages alarmed Americans, and Iran escalated attacks on U.S. allies.

Trump said Iran and Russia’s war against Ukraine were on the agenda. China and Russia hold enormous sway with Tehran and have also been accused by the U.S. of supporting the Islamic Republic.

He reiterated on Thursday that he and Xi agreed Iran needed to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for world energy supplies that has become a chokepoint since the start of the war. They also agreed that Iran could not obtain a nuclear weapon, Trump said.

But there were no signs that Trump secured agreements from Xi or Putin to help resolve the Iran conflict.

After the talks, Trump dialled into a meeting in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and more than 40 European leaders supporting Ukraine’s war effort.

Trump told the Berlin gathering that he had spoken to Xi and Putin about finding a peaceful end to the Ukraine war, Witkoff said.

Putin shares spotlight with Trump and Xi

For Putin, the three-way talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit — and his separate meetings with both leaders earlier — offered a sought-after chance for the Kremlin leader to signal that he headed a superpower on a par with the United States and China.

Trump and Putin found common ground in their opposition to the ICC. The Russian leader is wanted by the ICC under an arrest warrant for alleged war crimes in Ukraine. The U.S. opposes the ICC’s arrest warrant against former Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Putin last attended an APEC summit in 2017. His presence as an honoured guest and Russia’s status as a top global power — at least at the gathering in Shenzhen — marked a diplomatic breakthrough.

Just before the summit, Russia sent a pair of nuclear-capable Tu-95 bombers on a visit to Vietnam, in a reminder of its nuclear capability. As Putin arrived in China, Russian television focused on an officer in his retinue carrying a briefcase with the codes for Moscow’s nuclear forces.

Putin addressed Xi as “dear friend” during their talks on Wednesday and smiled contentedly on Thursday as he shook hands with Trump, who called him “my friend” and spoke of their “great relationship for many years.”

Speaking at the start of the three-way talks, Putin underscored the global weight of Russia, China and the U.S. The three nations are “united not only by our status as victors in World War II, but, most importantly, by our shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security,” he said.

They are also among the founders of the United Nations, Putin noted, adding that “we bear responsibility for preserving and strengthening the system of international law.”

“Our nations share many common interests regarding the resolution of regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said.

Russia’s war in Ukraine featured in Putin’s bilateral meetings with Trump and Xi. It was not the main topic of the three-way talks, Putin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.

The Kremlin released a video of the Chinese leader escorting the Russian president to his car at the end of the talks and the two men shaking hands.

“I don’t think anyone even expected things to go so well,” Putin told Xi as the two men parted ways.

Madhani reported from Washington and Leung reported from Hong Kong.

In short

  • Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first three-way meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday.
  • Their peace declaration called for United Nations reforms, higher oil supplies and reduced nuclear risks.
  • The declaration did not mention Russia’s war in Ukraine or the U.S.-led war in Iran.

Readers ask

What did Trump, Xi and Putin agree on?

The peace declaration said they agreed on the need for United Nations reforms, increasing oil supplies and reducing nuclear risks.

Did the summit address the wars in Ukraine and Iran?

The post-meeting declaration made no mention of Russia’s war in Ukraine or the U.S.-led war in Iran.

Why was the Shenzhen meeting significant?

It was the first sit-down involving the leaders of the United States, China and Russia.

item.title: India to unveil indigenous H5N1 poultry vaccine
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first indigenous inactivated H5N1 bird flu vaccine for poultry, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal, to the nation on Friday.
item.content:encoded:
ICAR-NIHSAD developed indigenous vaccine

New Delhi: Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan will dedicate India’s first “indigenous inactivated H5N1 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) virus vaccine” for poultry to the nation on Friday.

The Bhopal-based Indian Council of Agricultural Research-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) developed the vaccine against bird flu, also known as avian influenza, officials said.

The vaccine will be unveiled at the institute and marks a major step towards strengthening disease control in the country’s poultry sector, officials said.

Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), widely known as bird flu, poses a risk to chickens and other avian species, with outbreaks often resulting in total flock mortality.

Bird flu also necessitates mass culling and trade bans, disrupts international markets, raises poultry product prices and causes financial losses to farmers.

Since the first reported case in India in 2006, the country has recorded over 500 outbreaks involving the H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes.

Official estimates indicate that a major outbreak could reduce India’s GDP growth by 1.5 per cent and put more than 20 per cent of the nation’s poultry population at risk.

The 2006 outbreak resulted in estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs 2,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore, while a separate outbreak in Manipur caused losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the State’s GDP.

H5N1 also has public health implications. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, resulting in 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003.

Virological studies show that the “H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a strain” has been responsible for most outbreaks in chickens, with recent infections also detected in mammals alongside three reported human cases.

Until now, no specific commercial vaccine was available to protect poultry against the circulating Clade 2.3.2.1a strain.

ICAR-NIHSAD’s indigenous vaccine will help protect poultry from the circulating strain, reduce economic losses for farmers and limit the virus’s transmission from chickens to other animals and humans, officials said.

In short

  • India’s first indigenous inactivated H5N1 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza vaccine for poultry will be dedicated to the nation on Friday.
  • The Indian Council of Agricultural Research-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases developed the vaccine in Bhopal.
  • Officials said the vaccine will protect poultry against the circulating strain and reduce losses to farmers.

item.title: Telangana High Court questions PIL seeking speedy disposal of ED cases against Jagan
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana High Court questioned the public interest in a PIL seeking speedy disposal of ED cases against former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister YS Jagan Mohan Reddy. The Bench heard arguments on court workload, pending petitions and requests for daily hearings.
item.content:encoded:
Legal Correspondent

Hyderabad: A Division Bench of the Telangana High Court comprising Justice K. Lakshman and Justice Anil Kumar Jukanti on Thursday questioned the public interest involved in a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by former MP Chegondi Venkata Harirama Jogayya seeking expeditious disposal of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) cases against YSR Congress Party president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.

The Bench questioned the counsel appearing for former MP Chegondi Venkata Harirama Jogayya, who filed the PIL, as to why the petition was confined only to the cases involving Jaganmohan Reddy, when several other criminal cases against elected public representatives were also pending before the courts.

The Bench observed that the special CBI court was already burdened with a heavy workload and questioned the purpose of filing such a petition when the High Court was already monitoring the proceedings.

The counsel appearing for Harirama Jogayya submitted that Jaganmohan Reddy was the Chief Minister when the petitions were originally filed and argued that any impression that a former Chief Minister was evading trial would send a wrong message to the public. Opposing the petition, N. Naveen Kumar, counsel appearing for Jaganmohan Reddy, contended that the PIL was not a genuine public interest litigation but was intended to target the former Chief Minister.

He pointed out that more than 80 discharge petitions were pending in connection with the ED cases and that approximately 180 petitions were pending across the proceedings. He further submitted that daily hearings were already being conducted on the discharge petitions. He further relied on several judgments to contend that High Courts should not prescribe specific time limits for subordinate courts to conclude proceedings.

Meanwhile, counsel appearing for the ED submitted that 11 CBI-related cases were progressing regularly, whereas there was considerable delay in the ED proceedings. The ED sought directions for conducting daily hearings in the cases registered under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) against Jagan and others to ensure their expeditious disposal.

The Bench questioned what further steps the presiding officer of the special CBI court could take when the court itself had been impleaded as a respondent. It observed that the special court was already dealing with a substantial workload and that arguments on individual discharge petitions were taking as many as five days. After considering the submissions and the status of the CBI and ED proceedings, the Bench adjourned the matter to November 30 for further hearing.

item.title: Telangana High Court asks Teenmar Mallanna to approach SC on special courts’ jurisdiction
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana High Court suggested that MLC Chintapandu Naveen, known as Teenmar Mallanna, approach the Supreme Court for clarification on extending special courts’ jurisdiction to elected MLCs. The petition challenges their exclusion from courts trying cases involving elected representatives.
item.content:encoded:
Legal Correspondent

Hyderabad: A Division Bench of the Telangana High Court comprising Justice K. Lakshman and Justice Anil Kumar Jukanti on Thursday suggested that MLC Chintapandu Naveen, also known as Teenmar Mallanna, approach the Supreme Court seeking clarification on bringing elected Members of the Legislative Council (MLCs) within the purview of special courts constituted to try criminal cases involving elected public representatives.

The Bench was hearing a writ petition filed by Mallanna challenging the exclusion of MLCs from the jurisdiction of designated special courts constituted under various Government Orders for the trial of criminal cases involving elected representatives.

Counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that the Government Orders restricting the jurisdiction of the special courts to Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) were unlawful and discriminatory. He argued that both MLAs and MLCs are integral parts of the State Legislature and there was no reasonable justification for excluding elected MLCs from the purview of the special courts.

He also sought transfer and consolidation of all criminal cases pending against him across the State before the designated special courts for elected representatives. During the hearing, the Bench observed that the contention regarding equal treatment of MLAs and MLCs was valid. However, it pointed out that the special courts had been constituted pursuant to directions issued by the Supreme Court.

The Bench suggested that if the petitioner intended to extend the jurisdiction of these special courts to MLCs, he should approach the Supreme Court and seek appropriate clarification in the matter. With this observation, the hearing was concluded.

item.title: Ponnam seeks merger of Husnabad mandals with Karimnagar
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Transport Minister Ponnam Prabhakar renewed his demand to merge Husnabad, Koheda and Akkannapet mandals with Karimnagar district. He said the areas were merged with Siddipet district against residents’ wishes during Telangana’s 2016 district reorganisation exercise.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Transport and BC Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar reiterated that parts of his Husnabad constituency demerged from Siddipet district and urged the government to merge again into Karimnagar district.

Speaking during Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s public meeting in Siddipet on Thursday, Prabhakar said that the Husnabad, Koheda, and Akkannapet mandals of Husnabad constituency were forcibly merged with Siddipet district against the wishes of his constituency people while reorganising the districts in Telangana in 2016.

Whenever the government plans reorganisation of the districts in the State in the future, he asked the government to merge these parts again into Karimnagar district.

item.title: Revanth left disappointed Siddipet people as he fails to grant any special funds
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy made no development funding or project announcements for Siddipet during his Thursday meeting. He also did not address pending grants for Mallanna Sagar oustees or explain the guidelines of the Indiramma Kutumba Bheema scheme.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy speech in Siddipet left the citizens of Siddipet even the Congress cadres disappointed as he failed to announce any funds for development works in Siddipet constituency or to any project to Siddipet during his over hour-long speech. Addressing the gathering during the public meeting here on Thursday, Revanth just confined to level abuse remarks against the former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao, BRS Working President KT Rama Rao, Former Minister T Harish Rao and other BRS leaders.

However, he did not make any announcements for development works or even to the displaced under Mallanna Sagar and other irrigation projects. While claiming that he had fought for the displaced under Mallanna Sagar during the BRS rule, he did not even utter any word regarding the pending grants of displaced. Even though several flexi banners surfaced across the Siddipet district highlighting the pending projects in the Siddipet constituency on Wednesday, Revanth did not utter a single word regarding these demands except naming the Siddipet Medical College, built by BRS Government, after former Congress MLA A Madan Mohan Rao.

Even the Congress leaders from each of the constituencies had sent reports to the Chief Ministers office seeking funds for their respective constituencies ahead of Revanth’s visit, the ignorance of Revanth left all of them in a shock. Shockingly, Revanth did not elaborate the guidelines of the Indiramma Kutumba Bheema for the launch which the public meeting was actually organised.

item.title: NITW, KITS Warangal sign renewed MoU to strengthen academic, research collaboration
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: NIT Warangal and KITS have renewed their MoU to strengthen academic and research collaboration. Their partnership has yielded Rs 88.71 lakh in research funding and 23 joint research papers, with the renewed agreement expected to expand institutional exchanges and opportunities.
item.content:encoded:
Warangal: National Institute of Technology (NIT), Warangal and Kakatiya Institute of Technology and Science (KITS), Warangal signed a renewed memorandum of understanding (MoU) to further strengthen their academic and research collaboration.

The MoU aims to promote collaborative research in mutually identified areas, academic interactions, support for higher qualifications, exchange of academic and scientific information, and exchange of students and faculty members.

NITW Director Prof. Bidyadhar Subudhi highlighted the importance of institutional collaboration, which helps jointly organising conferences; faculty development programmes (FDPs), research projects, training programmes and student internships.

KITS Warangal Principal Prof. K Ashoka Reddy said through collaborative and interdisciplinary research by faculty and students resulted in research funding of Rs 88.71 lakh from various government agencies and institutions including SERB, CARS, SERB-TARE and IIT Guwahati Technology Innovation and Development Foundation.

The collaboration also resulted in 23 joint research papers published in reputed journals. The renewed MoU was expected to build on these achievements and create further opportunities for academic exchange, research collaboration, and faculty and student development, he added.

item.title: Revanth Reddy’s Siddipet meeting draws poor turnout
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s Siddipet meeting on Thursday saw a poor turnout, with vacant chairs and attendees leaving midway through his speech. The low attendance highlighted mobilisation challenges for local Congress leaders despite reported inducements and transport arrangements by organisers.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s public meeting, during which he launched Indiramma Kutumba Bheema, in Siddipet on Thursday, evoked poor response from the people. A majority of chairs remained vacant even while Revanth was addressing the public. Several women were seen walking out of the meeting while Revanth’s speech was mid-way. When Revanth was intentionally targeting former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao and former minister T Harish Rao, the people of the area did not receive them well. Revanth was visibly disappointed since the rally he participated in town attracted little participation.

The failure in mobilising the cadre stood as testimony for the differences between the Congress leaders. The police and Congress leaders were seen suggesting the gathering to sit at the meeting place until Revanth’s speech was over. However, they refused to pay heed to their requests and started leaving the place. Since the local Congress leaders could not mobilise people from Siddipet, they Congress leaders from neighbouring districts offered money, liquor, biryani and arranging free transportation.

item.title: Revanth Reddy hits back at Congress critics, threatens to send them to Erragadda
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy hit back at Congress critics in Siddipet, accusing some leaders of highlighting negatives while ignoring government achievements. He defended his stand on Krishna water allegations, targeted the BRS and promised a ministerial berth to Siddipet’s Congress MLA.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has acknowledged dissent within the Congress, openly referring to differences among party leaders and accusing some of them of highlighting negative issues while ignoring the State government’s achievements. His remarks came amid complaints by a few Congress legislators, particularly Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy, about irregularities in the Congress government over the past two days.

Without naming the legislators, the Chief Minister hit back at his critics and questioned whether they had been bitten by a stray dog. “They are discussing the bad things openly on the mike and the good things in ears. There will be a few such persons and they will be taken to Erragadda (Insitute of Mental Health) by Congress party workers,” Revanth Reddy said while addressing a public meeting in Siddipet on Thursday.

Interestingly, the meeting was organised to launch the Indiramma Family Life Insurance scheme. However, the Chief Minister made little mention of the scheme. He also did not address concerns among farmers over the delay in implementing the Rythu Bima scheme. Throughout his speech, which lasted over an hour, Revanth Reddy continued his criticism of BRS chief K Chandrashekhar Rao and the previous government.

He also sought to counter the BRS allegations that his government had colluded with Andhra Pradesh in the alleged illegal release of Krishna river water at Nagarjunasagar. “I am a son of the soil. Will I do injustice to my land? I broke my relationship with TDP chief N Chandrababu Naidu and dedicated myself to Telangana,” he said.

Accusing the BRS government of neglecting pending irrigation projects in erstwhile Mahabubnagar district, Revanth Reddy said the region lacked adequate infrastructure to draw water from the Srisailam, Jurala and Nagarjunasagar projects during the El Nino crisis. He pointed to the absence of tunnels, lifts and canals.

On the six guarantees, the Chief Minister said four generations of leaders had governed the State between 1983 and 2023. He referred to former Chief Ministers NT Rama Rao and YS Rajasekhara Reddy, along with BRS chief K Chandrashekhar Rao. “Not a single welfare programme is abolished. In addition, many more welfare programmes like free bus travel for women are being implemented,” Revanth Reddy claimed.

He said the Congress government had another two years in office and invited people to inform him about any programmes that needed to be implemented. He assured them that the government would consider their requests. The Chief Minister also vowed to ensure that the Congress won the 2029 Assembly elections in Siddipet and across Telangana for a second term.

Appealing to people to elect a Congress candidate from Siddipet, he promised a ministerial berth to the constituency’s MLA if the party won. Revanth Reddy said TPCC president Mahesh Kumar Goud would be responsible for ensuring the victory of the Congress candidate.

item.title: Joshua strikes late as RSB Hyderabad beat Bengaluru 2-1
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: All India Civil Services football tournament.
item.description: RSB Hyderabad registered a 2-1 win over RSB Bengaluru in the All India Civil Services Football Tournament in Goa. With the match heading towards a 1-1 draw, Joshua scored in the dying minutes to secure victory.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: RSB Hyderabad scored a 2-1 win against RSB Bengaluru in the All India Civil Services football tournament in Goa on Thursday. When the match was looking to end in a one-all draw, Joshua produced a decisive moment in the dying minutes, scoring the winning goal to seal a memorable victory for Hyderabad.

The result: RSB Hyd 2 (Joshua 1, Madan 1) bt RSB Bengaluru 1.

item.title: How Financial Behavior Affects Your Eligibility for a Personal Loan
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Your credit report records how you have managed credit accounts, including loan EMIs and credit card bills. Regular, on-time payments can support your credit profile, while missed or delayed payments may lower your score and raise concerns for lenders. A consistent repayment history helps show that you manage existing commitments responsibly.
item.content:encoded:
A steady income is important when applying for a personal loan, but it is only one part of the assessment. Lenders may also look at your age, work history, existing EMIs, credit record and how you manage day-to-day finances. These details help them assess whether you can repay the loan on time. Understanding what affects eligibility for personal loan applications can help you identify gaps in your profile and prepare before applying.

1. Pay Your EMIs and Bills on Time

Your credit report records how you have managed credit accounts, including loan EMIs and credit card bills. Regular, on-time payments can support your credit profile, while missed or delayed payments may lower your score and raise concerns for lenders. A consistent repayment history helps show that you manage existing commitments responsibly.

Set reminders or use auto-debit for regular payments and keep enough money in your account before each due date. Check that payments have gone through. If you miss a payment, clear the overdue amount as soon as possible and continue paying on time. The earlier delay may remain on your credit record, so sustained consistency matters.

2. Keep Credit Card Balances Manageable

Credit utilization is the share of your available credit limit that you are using. High card balances may indicate that you depend heavily on borrowed money and can affect your credit score. Keeping utilization low is a useful habit; staying below 30% is often used as a general guideline, not a fixed eligibility rule for every lender.

Where possible, pay the full credit card statement balance by the due date. This can help prevent interest charges and stop unpaid balances from building up. Your reported utilization depends on the balance and limit reported to the credit bureau, so the timing of a payment may affect when an improvement appears on your report.

3. Show Consistent Income and Employment

Lenders need to assess whether your income is sufficient to cover the proposed EMI alongside your existing expenses. They may consider your monthly income, employment history, time with your current employer and the stability of your earnings. Requirements vary by lender and can differ for salaried and self-employed applicants.

Before applying, check whether you meet the lender’s stated income and work-experience requirements. Keep salary slips, bank statements and employment details ready if requested. If your income varies from month to month, review your average take-home pay and regular commitments to decide what repayment amount you can manage comfortably.

4. Review Your Existing Loans and EMIs

Your current repayments affect how much of your income is available for another loan. If a large share of your monthly income already goes towards EMIs or other debt payments, a lender may decide that a new installment would stretch your budget. The number of active loans is only one part of the picture; the total repayment burden and your payment history also matter.

List your existing EMIs, credit card dues and other regular obligations before applying. Avoid taking on new credit without a clear purpose and do not borrow more than your budget can support. Responsible use of credit can help build a repayment record, but multiple simultaneous obligations may reduce your room to manage an additional EMI.

5. Apply for Credit Only After Comparing Options

A formal loan or credit card application may result in a hard enquiry on your credit report. Several enquiries within a short period can affect your score and may prompt lenders to review your borrowing needs more closely. An enquiry does not automatically lead to rejection and its impact can vary.

Compare the lender’s eligibility criteria, fees, repayment tenure and offered personal loan interest rate before submitting an application. If a lender provides a preliminary eligibility check, confirm whether it affects your credit score. Applying selectively can help you avoid unnecessary enquiries and focus on options that fit your profile.

6. Check Your Credit Report Before Applying

Your credit score is one factor in a personal loan assessment, but it is not the only one. Lenders may also consider income, employment stability, existing obligations and their own policies. A higher score can support an application, but it does not guarantee approval or a particular interest rate.

Review your credit report for incorrect account details, unfamiliar enquiries or payments that have not been recorded correctly. If you find an error, raise it with the relevant credit bureau or lender. Continue paying dues on time and reducing outstanding balances whereve  possible. There is no guaranteed timeline for a score to improve because results depend on your existing record and when updated information is reported.

What Lenders May Check

Eligibility factor What you can do
Age and residency Check the lender’s age range and residency requirements before applying.
Monthly income Review your take-home pay and choose an EMI that fits your budget.
Employment or work history Confirm the required work experience and keep supporting details ready.
Credit score and repayment history Pay dues on time and check your credit report for errors.
Existing EMIs and debt Review your current obligations before taking on another installment.
Credit enquiries Compare criteria and loan terms before making a formal application.

Check the Eligibility Criteria Before Applying

Personal loan requirements differ between lenders, but common checks include age, residency, monthly income, employment stability and credit history. For example, leading financial institutions like Tata Capital have set an age range of 21 to 58 years, ask salaried applicants to earn at least ₹20,000 a month and look for at least one year with the current employer and two years of total work experience. A CIBIL score of 725 or above may be preferred by some lenders. Review the criteria that apply to the loan you are considering.

The application process is another point to compare. Some lenders offer a digital application journey, minimal documentation and flexible repayment options for eligible applicants. These features may make it easier to submit details and review repayment choices, but processing time and disbursal depend on document verification, eligibility checks and the lender’s approval. Always check the fees, tenure and personal loan interest rate offered to you before accepting a loan.

Conclusion

Personal loan eligibility depends on several parts of your financial profile, including income, employment history, existing repayments and credit behavior. Paying bills on time, keeping card balances manageable and reviewing your credit report can help you prepare, although these steps cannot guarantee approval. Before applying, compare lender requirements and check that the EMI fits your budget. Knowing the eligibility criteria in advance can help you make a more informed decision about a personal loan and the personal loan interest rate offered to you.

item.title: Hyderabad: Chief Secretary asks Industries Department to monitor Global Summit MoUs
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju reviewed the implementation of MoUs signed at the 2025 Investors Summit and proposals for the upcoming Global Summit. He also assessed land acquisition for the southern Regional Ring Road and proposed radial roads.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju directed the Industries Department to designate dedicated departmental officers for each sector to closely monitor the status of MoUs signed at Global Summit last year and ensure their effective implementation on the ground.

At a meeting with officials here on Thursday, he reviewed the status of Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) signed during the 2025 Investors Summit. This apart, he also checked about the proposals being considered for the upcoming Invest Telangana Global Summit.

Similarly, he reviewed the progress of land acquisition for the Southern part of the Regional Ring Road (RRR) and the proposed radial roads.

During the meeting, officials informed the Chief Secretary that 4,962 acres of land spread across 90 villages in six districts had to be acquired for the 201-km-long southern section of the Regional Ring Road.

“Concerned District Collectors should expedite the issuance of preliminary notifications for the radial roads and ensure that the entire project is completed within the stipulated timelines,” Sanjay Jaju directed officials.

HMDA Metropolitan Commissioner Sarfraz Ahmed, CEO Invest Telangana Ajit Reddy and other senior officials attended the meeting.

item.title: Opinion: India’s chemical blind spot—the missing architecture of chemical safety
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Fragmented chemical safety framework leaves critical gaps in regulation, exposure monitoring and enforcement
item.content:encoded:
By Dr Kattamreddy Ananth Rupesh

The first International Conference of the Global Framework on Chemicals, being held under the auspices of the United Nations Environment Programme from November 16 to 20 in Geneva, presents India with an unavoidable reckoning. Aspiring to become a global manufacturing powerhouse, can the country afford to remain without a comprehensive and integrated system for regulating the very chemicals that sustain its industrial economy?

The conference seeks to accelerate the safe and sustainable management of chemicals and waste. For India, this deliberation must serve as more than routine diplomacy; it should be a moment of profound regulatory introspection.

Chemicals are essential to pharmaceuticals, agriculture, textiles, plastics, electronics, construction and manufacturing. Yet, their properties, uses, and routes of exposure can also pose severe risks to human health and natural ecosystems. Safety, therefore, requires more than accident prevention or pollution response. It demands a systematic, life-cycle understanding of which chemicals enter the market, what hazards they pose, how populations and ecosystems are exposed to them, and whether their risks can be adequately managed.

Fragmented Regulatory Landscape

India is not operating in a regulatory vacuum. The country possesses an extensive array of laws and administrative rules governing specific categories of chemicals. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, provides the overarching legislative foundation, while specialised rules target industrial hazards, chemical accidents, pesticides (along the Insecticides Act, 1968), and fertilizers.

Waste-management rules cover plastic, hazardous, biomedical and construction waste, as well as e-waste, batteries and end-of-life vehicles. These rules include Extended Producer Responsibility to manage collection, treatment and disposal.

The fundamental flaw is that these instruments operate in silos across separate authorities, with differing definitions and isolated enforcement mandates. A chemical manufactured in one factory might end up in a consumer product, released into water, and eventually enter a waste stream, bringing it under the jurisdiction of different regulatory agencies at each stage. This fragmentation obscures the cumulative picture of exposure and risk.

Moreover, regulatory governance remains heavily bureaucratised, relying on procedural compliance rather than scientific risk assessment. Preventing an industrial accident is not the same as evaluating chronic toxicity, and compliance with product quality does not establish long-term chemical safety.

International Models

International systems offer useful models without requiring wholesale replication. In the European Union, the REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation, and Restriction of Chemicals) Regulation mandates that manufacturers and importers register chemical substances produced or imported at one tonne or more per year with the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA). It places the burden of proof on industry to provide comprehensive safety data rather than expecting regulators to discover hazards independently.

Ministers and bureaucrats cannot replace scientific expertise. The country needs an independent authority to ensure evidence-based chemical safety regulation

The EU’s Classification, Labelling and Packaging (CLP) Regulation complements REACH by standardising hazard communication through the Globally Harmonized System, using universally recognised pictograms and safety statements.

The United States presents a distinct regulatory philosophy through the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA), administered by the Environmental Protection Agency. Strengthened by the 2016 Lautenberg Chemical Safety Act, TSCA gives the regulator authority to maintain a national chemical inventory, review new chemicals before commercialisation, evaluate existing chemicals and impose restrictions when unreasonable risks are identified.

REACH emphasises systematic industry-generated data and registration obligations, while TSCA prioritises rigorous agency scrutiny based on the weight of scientific evidence. Both models institutionalise essential functions that are missing in India: maintaining comprehensive inventories, generating toxicological data, prioritising high-risk substances, and translating evidence into enforceable decisions.

India boasts world-class scientific expertise distributed across universities, research institutes, medical colleges, and national laboratories. Toxicologists, analytical chemists, epidemiologists and occupational health specialists are already working across the country. The issue is not a shortage of talent, but the absence of a permanent, statutory national mechanism to consolidate this expertise into evidence-based regulatory decisions.

Ministers and generalist civil servants cannot be expected to act as toxicologists or environmental scientists. Institutional design must ensure that chemical safety decisions are guided by independent, multidisciplinary technical assessment.

India currently lacks a dedicated national body to systematically evaluate industrial chemicals for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, endocrine disruption, ecotoxicity and persistence. Without transparent scientific rationales and formal mechanisms linking local research to policymaking, regulatory action will remain fragmented and reactive.

India’s Unfinished Reform

India has previously acknowledged this gap through the proposed Chemicals (Management and Safety) Rules, often referred to as India’s REACH. The fifth draft, circulated in 2020, envisaged an integrated framework covering substances manufactured, imported, or placed on the market. It incorporated notification obligations, registration requirements for priority chemicals, safety data sheets, and restriction mechanisms.

However, the prolonged delay in formally notifying and bringing these rules reflects the broader challenge of reconciling industrial growth with public health imperatives. India must recognise that the proposed rules are not an optional compliance burden, but a foundational component of modern public health and environmental infrastructure.

A fragmented framework becomes particularly dangerous when assessing chronic and emerging chemical threats. Some bisphenols and phthalates can interfere with hormonal signalling, while per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, known as forever chemicals, pose severe risks due to their extreme persistence and widespread bioaccumulation. Assessing substances individually may also fail to capture the combined effects of chemical mixtures.

India needs a coordinated national chemical-exposure and human-biomonitoring programme. Collecting data from biological samples alongside environmental monitoring would help map actual national exposure patterns and identify vulnerable groups, including women and children. Reliance on foreign data or theoretical estimates may overlook risks specific to Indian workers, local communities, and consumers.

National Chemicals Authority

To overcome these structural defects, India should establish a dedicated National Chemicals Regulatory Authority, either as an independent statutory body or through a comprehensive restructuring of existing institutions. Its mandate should encompass chemical notification and registration, scientific risk assessment, hazard classification, restriction recommendations, and inter-agency coordination. This authority should be supported by a permanent, multidisciplinary scientific secretariat equipped with expertise in toxicology, epidemiology, exposure science and computational risk modelling.

A unified national chemical inventory must be established to record chemical identities, production volumes, intended uses, and hazard classifications. While legitimate trade secrets must be safeguarded, confidentiality should never serve as a blanket shield against public health transparency. Furthermore, implementing harmonised hazard labelling aligned with the Globally Harmonized System will ensure clear hazard communication for workers, emergency responders and consumers alike.

A Policy Imperative

The Geneva conference should become a catalyst for domestic reform. International commitments carry little value if they are not backed by enforceable national legal structures, technical capacity, and measurable progress. India has a legislative foundation, scientific talent, and industrial capability. What remains missing is the integration of these elements into a coherent, transparent, and scientifically accountable architecture.

Chemical safety is not an impediment to industrial growth; it is the fundamental precondition for sustainable industrialisation, public health and responsible international trade. The question facing India is no longer whether it can afford a comprehensive chemicals management regime, but how much longer it can afford to operate without one.

 

(The author is Associate Professor of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, Siddhartha Medical College, Vijayawada)

item.title: Shaina, Parul reach girls’ singles semifinals at National Junior Badminton Championships
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Defending champion Shaina Manimuthu and second seed Parul Choudhary entered the girls’ singles semifinals at the National Junior Badminton Championships. Bornil Changmai defeated world junior bronze medallist Jagsher Singh Khangurra, while Sparsh Sood’s giant-killing run ended in the quarterfinals.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Top seed Shaina Manimuthu and second seed Parul Choudhary registered contrasting victories to reach the girls singles semifinals while Bornil Changmai defeated world junior championships bronze medallist Jagsher Singh Khangurra in boys singles quarterfinals of the 49th Yonex-Sunrise National Junior (U-19) Badminton Championships in Gangtok on Thursday.

Shaina, the defending champion, had to work hard in the opening game to beat Rishika Nandi 16-14, 15-11 while Parul packed off fifth seed Dianka Waldia 15-9, 15-7 in the quarterfinals. Shaina will now take on 6th seed Diksha SR, who defeated Sneha Lamba 15-8, 15-7 in the other quarterfinals.

The other semifinal will see 8th seed Lakshya Rajesh take on Parul after the former came from a game down to beat Anvi Rathore 13-15, 15-9, 16-14. In the boys singles category, second seed Bornil held his nerves to beat Jagsher 15-10, 13-15, 15-13 to reach the semifinals. Meanwhile, Sparsh Sood’s giant killing run came to an end at the quarterfinals stage.

The unseeded shuttler, who had upset top seed Nishchal Anand in the previous round, went down 15-13, 11-15, 15-10 against Rudra Pratap Singh Rana. Seventh seed TT Gnana Dattu also booked his semifinal berth with a 15-12, 12-15, 15-8 win over third seed Abhinav Garg.

item.title: TG SAFE raids quack’s clinic in Kothagudem, seizes 34 varieties of drugs
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing raided a clinic run by an unqualified practitioner in Erraborru village of Bhadradri Kothagudem district. Officials detected 34 varieties of medicines worth Rs 42,000 and warned wholesalers and dealers against supplying drugs to quacks.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Drugs Wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE), conducted raided on the premises of a unqualified practitioner (quack), Shaik Masthan Vali at First Aid Clinic, Erraborru village, Charla mandal, Bhadradri Kothagudem District, who was conducting clinical practice without proper qualifications at his clinic.

During the raid, TG SAFE officials detected 34 varieties of medicines including antibiotics, steroids, analgesics, anti-ulcer drugs, etc., worth Rs 42, 000, which were illegally stocked at the premises.

The TGSAFE (Drugs Wing) officers lifted the samples for analysis and further investigation will be carried out, and action will be taken as per the law against all the offenders, a press release on Thursday said.

In an advisory, TGSAFE directed wholesalers/dealers supplying medicines to quacks, other unqualified persons, and unlicensed shops, who are found stocking and selling drugs without a valid drug license, shall be liable for penal action under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. Stringent action shall be initiated against such Wholesalers/Dealers involved unauthorized and illegal supply chains, TGSAFE said.

The general public can report such instances and complaints through the TG SAFE – Drugs Wing Toll-Free Number 1800-599-6969 between 10.30 am and 5 pm on all working days.

item.title: Sourav Kothari tops group, advances to IBSF World Snooker knockouts
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Sourav Kothari topped Group J with an unbeaten record at the IBSF World Snooker Championships after a 4-0 win over Chau Hon Man. Meanwhile, Uzair Khan stunned former champion Ali Alobaidli, while 14 Indian men advanced to the knockouts.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Playing some of his best snooker in recent times, Sourav Kothari came up with another authoritative display en route to a 4-0 win over Hong Kong China’s Chau Hon Man in the IBSF World Snooker Championships at the Yeshwant Club in Indore on Thursday. Kothari, who finished his league engagements in Group ‘J’ with an all-win record, was given the top billing in the reseeding.

Of the 24 qualifiers for the knockouts, the top eight advanced to the pre-quarterfinals directly. Kothari’s final league match may have been devoid of any big breaks, but the bespectacled pro relied on a solid percentage game to floor his rival. He produced the breaks when he mattered and resorted to safety play whenever he lost position. He took the opening frame with minuscule runs and went 2-0 up on the black. In the third, he punished Chau’s poor safety with a gritty 59 break, and made a 51 clearance on another error from his rival to take vice-like grip over the proceedings. Early runs of 17 and 28, along with clever safety play ensured his straight-frames victory. Dhvajj Haria, who came through the first-stage qualifiers, finished No. 2 in the group following his 4-0 win over Omar Alajlani of Saudi Arabia. Three-time champion Pankaj Advani signed off from the league phase with a comfortable 4-1 win over Iran’s Shahin Sabzi to be seeded No. 3.

Out of the 21 Indian men in the fray, 14 made it to the knockouts. UZAIR STUNS ALOBAIDLI In a late-evening Group ‘A’ match on Wednesday, unheralded Uzair Khan of India stunned former champion and title contender Ali Alobaidli of Qatar 4-1. The 25-year-old from Bhopal rallied in splendid style after losing the opening frame of the best-of-seven-frame encounter, using his consistency and superior safety play to secure the win. The Indian’s facile victory helped him top the group on better frame difference. Uzair, who won the Commonwealth bronze medal in heyball last month, was involved in a three-way tie with Alobaidli and Paras Gupta with two wins apiece.

The Qatari cueist finished second to advance to the knockouts. FOUR INDIAN WOMEN MOVE UP In the women’s section, India’s Amee Kamani, Keerthana Pandian and defending champion Anupama Ramachandran advanced to the knockout quarterfinals with all-win records from their respective groups. They were joined by England’s Tessa Davidson, Hong Kong China’s So Man Yan and Yee Ting Cheung. Meanwhile, India’s Ishika Shah, the Philippines’ Carmille Buhat, Hong Kong China’s Shiu Wing Man and Ireland’s Margaret O’Driscoll will compete in the first-round knockouts.

item.title: New species of predatory aquatic insect discovered in Eastern Ghats
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Researchers discovered a new predatory aquatic insect species, Enithares deccanensis, in freshwater habitats across the Eastern Ghats. DNA barcoding and morphological studies confirmed its distinct identity, while the findings highlight the biodiversity value of small freshwater ecosystems.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A new species of predatory aquatic insect, recognised for swimming upside down beneath the water surface, has been discovered in the Eastern Ghats. The species was documented from freshwater habitats across the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve in Andhra Pradesh and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana.

Named Enithares deccanensis Banerjee et al, 2026, the newly described species belongs to the family Notonectidae, commonly known as backswimmers, a group of predatory aquatic insects. The research was conducted by Somesh Banerjee, Devadoss Kumar, Dr. Deepa Jaiswal and Karuthapandi Madasamy, with affiliations to the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), Hyderabad, and VHNSN College, Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu.

According to researchers, unlike previously described members of its genus, E. deccanensis possesses a distinctive combination of morphological features, including a dark, V-shaped marking on its wings and a characteristic sickle-shaped male reproductive structure.

The researchers said they employed an integrative taxonomic approach combining detailed morphological examination, DNA barcoding and phylogenetic analyses to establish its identity.

Further, molecular evidence revealed approximately 10–14.5 percent genetic divergence from the examined congeners, further supporting its recognition as a distinct species. Interestingly, specimens exhibited both light and dark colour forms, demonstrating colour polymorphism within the species.

ZSI Hyderabad Freshwater Biology Regional Centre officer-in-charge Dr. Deepa Jaiswal said the discovery also draws attention to relatively small freshwater habitats, including shaded rock pools, forest streams and waterfall-associated pools, which can harbour previously undocumented biodiversity.

ZSI Director Dr. Dhriti Banerjee said the discovery reinforces the importance of sustained biodiversity exploration, taxonomic research and freshwater habitat conservation across India’s Eastern Ghats. The findings have recently been published in the international peer-reviewed journal Journal of Natural History (Taylor & Francis).

item.title: Editorial: Big dream, bigger challenges for India’s semiconductor ambitions
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: India’s semiconductor ambitions risk falling short unless policymakers look beyond chip fabrication and build an indigenous ecosystem encompassing chip design, manufacturing, equipment, materials and packaging
item.content:encoded:
India is dreaming big in the semiconductor sector. However, several challenges lie ahead. Though the country has a strong semiconductor design workforce and enough domestic demand for chips, building intellectual property (IP), attracting skilled talent and developing manufacturing capabilities remain major stumbling blocks. To emerge as a credible global supplier, India needs to scale up the semiconductor ecosystem and strengthen capabilities in chip design and assembly. It needs to develop and manufacture its own machinery and high-precision components required for semiconductor production. Experts say the country’s dream of building a sustainable semiconductor ecosystem will remain unfulfilled unless the focus shifts from fabrication and chip assembly to an end-to-end solutions approach that includes equipment makers, material suppliers, packaging companies, and memory manufacturers. Whether India’s semiconductor push ultimately produces the next Nvidia or ASML is a question that will take years to answer. However, the immediate objective should not be to create a handful of successful companies. Instead, the focus should be on creating an ecosystem that enables hundreds of companies to emerge. In July this year, the Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0, a Rs 1.27 lakh crore mission aimed at deepening the semiconductor ecosystem. This marked India’s most ambitious attempt yet to establish itself as a significant player in the global semiconductor value chain. The initiative represented a shift from merely attracting chip manufacturing plants to building an integrated semiconductor ecosystem encompassing design, fabrication, packaging, materials, equipment, research and skilled manpower.

While the policy push is laudable, India faces several formidable hurdles, including extremely high capital requirements, long gestation periods, difficulties in accessing frontier manufacturing technologies because of commercial and geopolitical considerations, supply chain complexity, infrastructure constraints, talent shortages, and intense global competition. One of the major focus areas of Semicon 2.0 is the domestic development of machinery and materials needed for semiconductor production. Semiconductors constitute a trillion-dollar global industry, while India’s contribution to semiconductor manufacturing stands at around $3 billion. This highlights the gap between the country’s ambitions and its current position in the global semiconductor market. The bigger opportunity is to design products for India, develop the chips that go into them and own the intellectual property. That means developing chips for applications that India specifically needs. To realise its dream of becoming a major global player in the semiconductor sector, India needs to reassess its core strengths and craft suitable strategies. The stark reality is that the country imports 90-95% of the semiconductors it uses today, while domestic demand is projected to exceed $240 billion by 2035. India has spent nearly $150 billion importing semiconductor products between 2017 and 2025. In this scenario, it would be imprudent to attempt to reinvent the wheel only to end up as an also-ran in the global race.

item.title: Arpit Chauhan wins Brilliant Trophy Juniors online chess tournament
