item.title: Hyderabad: TG SAFE suspends licences of six food establishments
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TG SAFE suspended the FSSAI licences of six establishments after inspections uncovered serious hygiene violations. Officials seized or discarded 1,672 kg of food articles worth Rs 6.59 lakh and ordered five other establishments to close for operating without licences.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Continuing its crackdown on food safety violations, the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) has suspended the FSSAI licences of six establishments and ordered them to immediately stop operations following inspections that revealed serious hygiene violations.

Enforcement teams comprising Food Safety Officers and police personnel inspected 15 meat retail and processing units and four Karachi Bakery manufacturing units across the city and surrounding areas on Thursday.

During the inspections, officials seized or discarded around 1,672 kg of food articles worth Rs.6.59 lakh. The violations included operating without valid FSSAI licences, damaged flooring with blood and meat residues, clogged drains, dirty walls, housefly and cockroach infestation, live rodents and failure to maintain mandatory records.

The six establishments whose licences were suspended include Watan Traders at Zamistanpur, Punjab Fish Company at Secunderabad, Hi Protein on SD Road, Karachi INC at Srinagar Colony, Karachi Bakery Pearl at Gaganpahad and SM SEA Corporation at Uppal.

Officials found unhygienic fish-processing and storage facilities, expired food products, live rats in chicken-processing areas, improper storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, pest infestation and poor housekeeping at these establishments.

Officials informed that at Karachi Bakery Pearl’s manufacturing unit at Gaganpahad, officials found several violations, including poor maintenance of machinery, rusty baking trays, pest infestation and improper storage of food products. Around 1,012 kg of packed food articles worth Rs.4.34 lakh were seized after officials found discrepancies in manufacturing dates on the labels.

Five other establishments — Anand Mutton and Chicken Point at Nallakunta, Salman KGN Poultry and New Decent Meat Chicken and Fish Shop at Yousufguda, Protein Foods on SP Road and AP Fisheries Fish Stall at Malkajgiri — were ordered to close for operating without FSSAI licences in unhygienic conditions.

TG SAFE will issue improvement notices to Watan Fresh Mart at Musheerabad and Metro Cash and Carry at Uppal, while show-cause notices will be served on 15 establishments for the violations. Officials said further action, including penalties, would be initiated based on the findings and compliance with food safety norms, officials added.

item.title: Kothagudem: Over 200 persons died in road accidents in last ten months
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Kothagudem district recorded 432 road accidents between January and October, resulting in 206 deaths and 425 injuries. District Revenue Officer Padmavathi directed departments to identify accident-prone areas, strengthen safety measures and create awareness about traffic rules and PM-RAHAT.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: As many as 432 road accidents were recorded across Kothagudem in the last ten months resulting in 206 deaths, the district officials informed.
In view of the increasing number of accidents the District Revenue Officer (DRO) Padmavathi directed officials from relevant departments to take effective and coordinated measures to prevent road accidents in the district.

At the District-Level Road Safety Committee held at the collectorate the DRO reviewed the road accidents, fatalities and injuries recorded in the district as well as necessary preventive actions required to stop them.

Officials stated that of the 432 road accidents that occurred from January 1 to October 31,193 were fatal while 239 were non-fatal. These accidents resulted in 206 deaths, with 28 individuals sustaining serious injuries and 397 sustaining minor injuries.

Accident-prone areas should be identified and safety measures in those locations have to be taken up on an urgent basis. All departments must work together in a coordinated and effective manner to prevent such accidents, Padmavathi said.

Expressing concern over the loss of precious lives due to road accidents, the DRO suggested conducting extensive awareness programmes to ensure that motorists strictly follow traffic rules and take safety measures.

Under the Prime Minister – Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment (PM-RAHAT) Scheme victims of road accidents could receive free medical treatment up to a value of Rs. 1.50 lakh at designated hospitals. The public should be made aware of the scheme, she added.

item.title: Harish Rao demands scrapping of Kukatpally truck parking land’s auction
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS leader T Harish Rao demanded cancellation of the proposed Kukatpally truck parking land auction, warning of disruption to transport operations and workers' livelihoods. He announced BRS support for the planned hunger strike and HMDA siege with Left parties.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS deputy floor leader T Harish Rao demanded immediate cancellation of the proposed auction of the Kukatpally truck parking land. He said the Revanth Reddy government was disposing of public assets for commissions, while ignoring the needs of workers and the city’s growing population.

Speaking at an all-party round-table meeting organised by the Left parties at Somajiguda Press Club on Thursday, Harish Rao said the land was acquired specifically for public infrastructure and cannot be diverted for commercial purposes. He argued that under the Land Acquisition Act, land acquired for a specified public purpose should be returned to the original owners if that purpose was abandoned.

The BRSLP deputy leader said the truck parking facility handled around 1,000 container loads a day and warned that its auction will affect thousands of workers and disrupt transport operations. “The site also housed a traffic police station, nursery, Kukatpally MLA camp office and RTA office, besides serving as an important public space for the surrounding areas of Kukatpally, Qutbullapur and Serilingampally,” he pointed out.

Accusing Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy of prioritising land sales over governance, Harish Rao alleged that the government had already sold 26,000 acres and was targeting land worth Rs 50,000 crore this year. He said the government was paying large commissions to financial intermediaries to facilitate these land transactions and borrowings.

He cited proposed sales of land in Miyapur and Mamidipally, besides smaller plots in Kapra, Ameenpur and Bachupally, and questioned why such spaces could not be used for schools, parks and hospitals.

The former Minister said the BRS would join the hunger strike planned for November 22 and 23 and participate in the HMDA siege on November 25 if the auction was not cancelled. He said the party will coordinate with the Left parties in the agitation and extend full support to the workers. He also urged the Congress high command to intervene, pointing out that Rahul Gandhi had opposed the sale of public sector assets and government land earlier.

The meeting was attended by CPI, CPM, New Democracy and BRS leaders, including CPM State secretary John Wesley and BRS MLAs Madhavaram Krishna Rao and Kotha Prabhakar Reddy.

item.title: Telangana People’s Coalition urges Advisory Council to seek postponement of Global Summit
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana People's Coalition for El Nino Crisis has urged the 16-member Telangana Rising Advisory Council to press the State government to postpone the December 7-9 Invest Telangana Global Summit, citing drought, water shortages and competing relief priorities.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Members of the Telangana People’s Coalition for El Nino Crisis have appealed to all 16 members of the Advisory Council of Telangana Rising: Vision 2047 to urge the State government to postpone the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026. The appeal follows an earlier letter sent to Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy.

The coalition members have written an open letter to the Advisory Council. They pointed out that none of its 16 members is from Telangana. The appeal comes amid a severe drought and water crisis declared by the State government in 365 mandals across 31 districts due to El Nino conditions. Despite the crisis, the government has decided to host the Invest Telangana Global Summit at Bharat Future City from December 7 to 9.

“We have appealed to the CM to immediately call off this Summit and announce its postponement until the state returns to normal conditions,” the coalition members said in the letter. It also raised concerns over several policy decisions of the Telangana government. The members said these decisions were deepening the State’s ecological and economic crisis, as well as social inequity.

They said the decisions had serious implications for agrarian communities, the working class and marginalised sections. They also affected common resources and the environment. Several of these decisions, they added, had been removed from or contradicted the government’s pre-election manifesto.

The Chief Minister himself had publicly compared the El Nino crisis to the Covid-19 pandemic. He had warned of an acute shortage of drinking water and power until July 2027. He had also advised farmers to move away from water-intensive crops. Severe water shortages have also been reported in several urban localities. The media has been reporting extensively on the crisis.

Against this backdrop, the coalition members have called for all public resources, administrative capacity and personnel to remain focused on drought relief, water coordination and grievance redressal. They said these efforts were essential to safeguarding the fundamental right to life. The members argued that these resources should not be diverted to extravagant business summits during the crisis.

Addressing the Advisory Council members, the letter said: “As public-spirited members of the Advisory Council, who we think are in a position to morally influence the state government, we call upon you all as well to issue a similar public communication to the Chief Minister to call off or postpone the Investment Summit in this emergency situation.” A copy of the letter was shared with all 16 members of the Advisory Council.

item.title: Kothagudem: Police cracks Aswapuram temple theft case, arrests three
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Aswapuram police arrested three suspects in connection with thefts at Om Shakti and Sai Baba temples on November 12 and 13. Police said they recovered gold ornaments worth Rs 7.54 lakh and 7.9 kg of silver ornaments from the accused.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: Police have solved a case of thefts that took place at Om Shakti and Sai Baba Temples under the limits of Aswapuram police station a few days ago and have arrested three suspects.

Speaking to the media Bhadrachalam DSP (in-charge of Manuguru), Arun Kumar informed that the thefts took place during the night hours on November 12 and 13. The thieves broke the locks of the temples and stole three gold ornaments weighing 105 grams from the deity along with silver items.

Following a complaint filed by temple supervisor Ramakrishnan Suresh, Aswapuram police registered a case. Special teams consisting of the CCS and Aswapuram police were formed to conduct the investigation.

Based on a tip off, the police intercepted three suspects moving suspiciously near Sitarama canal bridge on the outskirts of Gollagudem on Thursday morning; they were taken into custody and questioned, during which they confessed to committing thefts at the above temples.

Police recovered 7.9 kilograms of silver ornaments along with gold ornaments worth about Rs. 7.54 lakh from the trio. Later the accused Shaik Jani alias Jani Sharif of Navabharat area at Paloncha, Sapka Kantha Rao of Eluru district in Andhra Pradesh and Oora Lingaiah of Kothapeta in Nalgonda district were arrested and produced before the court.

Shaik Jani was involved in 11 theft cases, Kantha Rao in 14 and Lingaiah in eight theft cases in the past. DSP Arun Kumar commended Aswapuram police personnel and the CCS team for their swift action in solving the case.

item.title: SLNITSA principal bats for integrating traditional crafts into higher education
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Jawaharlal Nehru Architecture and Fine Arts University
Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Institute of Traditional Sculpture and Architecture
item.description: The Telangana Gazetted Headmasters' Association welcomed the proposed integration of intermediate and school education but sought vocational courses from Classes IX to XII. It also demanded post upgrades, protection of service rights and a clear policy for institutions.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Institute of Traditional Sculpture and Architecture (SLNITSA), Yadagirigutta, Principal Mothilal Sthapathi emphasised the need to integrate India’s traditional craft knowledge into the formal higher education system through specialised academic programmes, research opportunities and industry-oriented training.

He made a presentation at the national seminar on “Mainstreaming of Craft Education in Higher Education”, organised by the Ministry of Textiles and the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) in New Delhi on Thursday. In his presentation, he highlighted the importance of developing dedicated undergraduate, postgraduate and research programmes in traditional sculpture and temple architecture, stone carving, heritage conservation, traditional painting, woodcraft, metal crafts, handloom and textile design.

“Traditional knowledge systems such as Shilpa Shastra, Vastu Shastra and Agama Shastra, along with the Guru–Shishya Parampara, should be integrated with contemporary design, digital technology, sustainability and entrepreneurship,” Mothilal stressed.

He also advocated greater academic recognition for traditional master craftspeople, Sthapathis and experienced artisans through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), academic credit systems, equivalence pathways and appropriate faculty recognition. He observed that traditional artisans were not merely skilled workers but knowledge holders, innovators and custodians of India’s living cultural heritage.

Presenting Telangana as a successful example of institutionalising traditional knowledge, he showcased the initiatives of SLNITSA, Yadagirigutta, which offers a three-year BA programme in Traditional Sculpture and Architecture, specialising in temple architecture and affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Architecture and Fine Arts University (JNAFAU).

item.title: Telangana: Headmasters seek vocational courses from Classes IX to XII
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Gazetted Headmasters' Association welcomed the proposed integration of intermediate and school education but sought vocational courses from Classes IX to XII. It also demanded post upgrades, protection of service rights and a clear policy for institutions.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Welcoming the State government’s proposal to integrate intermediate education with school education, the Telangana Gazetted Headmasters’ Association on Thursday urged the government to introduce vocational education along with general education from Classes IX to XII.

The headmasters sought the introduction of at least one vocational course, such as computer technology, agriculture, electrical and electronics, and healthcare, in high schools. This should be done based on the geographical, social and economic conditions of the respective areas.

In a representation to Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, association president P Raja Bhanu Chandra Prakash and general secretary G Hema Chandrudu sought the upgradation of 1,817 school complex headmaster posts from Grade-II to Grade-I. Such a move would increase the academic, administrative and supervisory responsibilities of the schools.

In view of the merger, the association sought the re-designation of gazetted headmasters as principals, protection of the existing service rights, status and promotional opportunities of headmasters and teachers. It highlighted the need for a special policy to determine seniority, status and promotions in the integrated education system.

Further, expressing concern over the possibility of permitting private junior colleges to offer education from Classes I to XII, the association wanted the government to roll out a clear policy regarding educational institutions.

item.title: Hyderabad: Man sentenced to 20 years for sexually assaulting minor girl
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A special fast-track court in Rajendranagar sentenced 26-year-old Sujith Rajbhar alias Sudheer to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for sexually assaulting a 15-year-old girl in September 2021. The court also imposed a fine and ordered compensation.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 26-year-old man, identified as Sujith Rajbhar alias Sudheer, was sentenced to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment in a minor girl’s sexual assault case by a special fast-track court in Rajendranagar on Thursday.

The court also imposed a fine of Rs 21,000 and ordered compensation of Rs 5 lakh to the victim.

Sudheer had befriended a 15-year-old girl and continued following her despite her parents warning her to stay away from him. In September 2021, he allegedly sexually assaulted her when she went alone near some bushes in the dairy farm area.

Rajendranagar police arrested him and filed a charge sheet in February 2022.

item.title: Harish Rao questions Revanth Reddy govt over delay in acting against Palnadu Water Grid project
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS deputy floor leader T Harish Rao accused Telangana's Congress government of failing to act against Andhra Pradesh's Palnadu Water Grid project. He alleged delayed intervention threatened water supplies from Nagarjuna Sagar and criticised the government's record on irrigation projects.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS deputy floor leader T Harish Rao on Thursday accused the Revanth Reddy government of remaining inactive for nearly a year while Andhra Pradesh advanced its Palnadu Water Grid project to draw water from Nagarjuna Sagar. He said once again the government woke up only after the BRS and the media exposed the issue.

He demanded that the government apologise to people for failing to protect Telangana’s water rights and acknowledge that it had acted only after the BRS raised the issue.

Questioning the delay at a press conference at Somajiguda Press Club, Harish Rao said Andhra Pradesh issued a GO for the project on August 4, 2026, even as survey and mobilisation works had reportedly been under way for nearly a year. He asked why Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy, who represents Nalgonda district, failed to intervene earlier to protect the interests of his own constituency and the State.

The BRSLP deputy leader pointed to Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy’s admission that he had reprimanded the Nagarjuna Sagar project Executive Engineer and other officials for failing to bring the AP project issue to the government’s notice. He said the statement amounted to an acknowledgement of the government’s failure.

“How can the government blame engineers alone when the project progressed for months without intervention from the Irrigation Department,” he asked.

Harish Rao said the project was designed to draw up to 2 TMCft of water a day through a tunnel, which could amount to nearly 120 TMCft over two months. He questioned the requirement of such a large daily quantity for drinking water and warned that sustained withdrawals could affect drinking and irrigation supplies to Nalgonda and Hyderabad, for which Nagarjuna Sagar project was a major source.

The former Irrigation Minister criticised the Congress government for writing to the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) only after the issue was raised publicly, recalling a similar pattern in its response to the Godavari-Banakacherla project. He said the government was taking a soft approach towards Andhra Pradesh to protect its political interests, than prioritising Telangana people’s interest.

Harish Rao challenged the Congress government’s record on Krishna River water utilisation. He asserted that Telangana used only 28 per cent of its temporary share in 2024-25 and 25 per cent in 2025-26. He said the 34 per cent share accepted during the BRS regime was only a temporary arrangement which was only continuation of the arrangement in erstwhile Andhra Pradesh till fresh allocations were made.

He pointed out that the K Chandrashekhar Rao government secured a fresh tribunal to seek a larger allocation of 600-700 TMCft for Telangana and also filed an affidavit in this regard. He accused the Congress government of failing to present a strong case before the tribunal despite being in office for nearly three years.

On irrigation projects, Harish Rao said the BRS government spent Rs 4,000 crore on Kalwakurthy, Nettempadu, Bhima and Koilsagar, providing irrigation to eight lakh acres in erstwhile Mahabubnagar district. He stated that the BRS had excavated 11.5 km of the SLBC tunnel, while the Congress government had not completed even one kilometre since coming to power. He also questioned the progress of the Palamuru-Rangareddy project and other pending schemes.

The BRS leader cited Devadula, Sitarama and Kalwakurthy lift irrigation schemes, accusing the Congress government of restricting water lifting despite availability in the Godavari and Krishna River basins. He said reduced pumping aggravated drought conditions. He said the government also failed to secure clearances for several projects, including Sitarama Sagar, Sammakka Sagar, Palamuru-Rangareddy and Wardha.

item.title: Andhra Pradesh’s attempts to draw 1.8 tmc from Nagarjuna Sagar will be foiled, says Uttam
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy said Andhra Pradesh had not diverted any Krishna water at Nagarjuna Sagar despite attempting to draw 1.8 TMC through a tunnel. He assured that Telangana would protect its water entitlements.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Admitting that Andhra Pradesh was attempting to draw water from the Krishna river at Nagarjuna Sagar through a tunnel, Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy said that not a single drop of water had been diverted.

Addressing a public meeting at Huzurnagar, the Minister assured people that not a drop of Krishna or Godavari water would be surrendered to Andhra Pradesh.

He stated that the Congress government was committed to protecting Telangana’s water entitlements against any attempts to undermine its interests. “Whatever arguments or pressures may be brought forward, our government is determined to protect Telangana’s water rights,” he asserted.

Referring to Andhra Pradesh’s attempts to draw 1.8 TMC of water from Nagarjuna Sagar in the Krishna basin, the Minister said Telangana had strongly contested the proposals and lodged objections with the Central government and the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB).

He said the State would not allow decisions or unilateral actions that adversely affected its legitimate share and would continue to pursue the matter with determination.

The Minister said Telangana had improved its water utilisation after the Congress government assumed office, resulting in increased irrigation coverage, agricultural activity, paddy production and procurement.

With challenging climatic conditions and the prospect of a difficult summer ahead, Uttam Kumar Reddy said the government was also focused on conserving available water to safeguard drinking water requirements across the State.

He emphasised that irrigation and civil supplies were responsibilities requiring round-the-clock attention, as they directly affected farmers, vulnerable households and the wider public.

item.title: Basketball: SCR women extend winning run with 76-31 victory
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: South Central Railway women defeated St Francis 76-31 in the GM Sampath Kumar Annual League Basketball Championship after taking a 39-15 half-time lead. Mahendra Hills BC also registered a 67-50 victory over Victory PG in the men’s section.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Favourites South Central Railway women, fresh after their historic 4th consecutive All India Inter Railway (Women) Championship win earlier this month, made short work of St. Francis Women 76 – 31 after leading 39 – 15 at half time in the GM Sampath Kumar annual league basketball championship at Samhitha and Kundana played well for St. Francis with Samhitha netting both the three-pointers.

Harini and Jyothi did the honours for the SCR with the latter scoring two quick consecutive baskets at the end of the first quarter which helped her team lead 16-11. In the second quarter, SCR got into the groove and tanked four three-pointers and scored a massive 23 points. St. Francis found it very hard to penetrate the tight defense of SCR as then could manage only four points thereby handing SCR a massive 39 – 15 lead at half time. After a change of ends SCR continued in the same fashion adding another 18 and 19 points with Subhashini doing the bulk of the scoring in the third and fourth quarters respectively, whereas St. Francis could only muster 12 and four points respectively.

The scores: Men: Mahendra Hills BC 67 (Tanay 20, Tagore 12, Krishna 11) bt Victory PG 50 (Prithvi 18, Bilal 10). Women: SCR 76 (Harini 23, Subasini 18, Jyothi 17) bt St. Francis 31 (Kundana 9, Samhitha 9).

item.title: Kakatiya University contract faculty demands CM to regularise their services
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Contract assistant professors at Kakatiya University held a rally demanding regularisation before fresh recruitment. They urged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to honour his earlier promise, implement UGC pay scales and absorb contract faculty into regular university service.
item.content:encoded:
Hanamkonda: Contract assistant professors working at Kakatiya University (KU) took out a rally, urging Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to fulfil his promise of regularising their services.

Following a call by the State committee of the Contract Assistant Professors JAC, contract assistant professors at KU organised a ‘March towards regularisation’ rally on the campus on Thursday. They demanded that their services be regularised before any regular recruitment process was taken up.

KU Contract Faculty Action Committee leaders P Karunakar Rao, Sridhar Kumar Lodh, Bairi Niranjan and Sadhu Rajesh, along with other faculty members, submitted a memorandum of demands to the university Vice-Chancellor, Prof K Pratap Reddy.

Speaking on the occasion, they said the lives of contract assistant professors, who had been teaching for years, remained miserable. They urged the Chief Minister to honour the promise made to contract faculty during their 11-day strike in the past.

Due to the State government’s failure to implement UGC pay scales or regularise their services, many contract assistant professors were suffering from a deep sense of insecurity, with some even succumbing to heart attacks, they said.

They demanded that the government immediately absorb all contract faculty members into regular service at the university and grant them UGC pay scales. The leaders warned that the JAC would launch large-scale protests if the issue was not resolved immediately.

Contract assistant professors B Satish, Damera Bikshapathi, Firoz Pasha, Ranga Reddy, Madhukar Rao, Sadashiva, Kishan, Sangeeth, Aashirvadam, Manjula, Dr Srilakshmi, Blessy Priyanka and others were present.

item.title: Hyderabad: TGSRTC removes driver over rude behaviour
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TGSRTC removed a private hire bus driver attached to Hyderabad-1 Depot after an inquiry into allegations of misbehaviour with a passenger on the MGBS-Raichur route on November 12. The corporation also barred depots from assigning him private hire duties.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) removed a private hire bus driver from duty following allegations of misbehaviour with a passenger, taking serious note of media reports highlighting the incident.

The action was taken against B Surya, a driver attached to Hyderabad-1 Depot, after an inquiry into the incident, which reportedly occurred on November 12.

According to TGSRTC officials, Surya was driving a private hire bus from Mahatma Gandhi Bus Station (MGBS) to Raichur when he allegedly behaved rudely with a passenger at around 5.50 am.

Following an inquiry, the RTC withdrew his services and directed all depot managers across Telangana not to assign him duties on private hire buses at any depot.

The corporation also instructed the bus owner not to bring the vehicle back into online operations until a qualified replacement driver is appointed.

item.title: Malkajgiri civic body to widen bell-mouth areas at Boduppal area to ease traffic movement
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation will develop free-left-turn passages, widen roads, clear encroachments and repair potholes to ease congestion. Commissioner T Vinay Krishna Reddy has also directed officials to shift obstructing utility poles and remove unused cables across Boduppal Circle.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Malkajgiri Municipal Corporation (MMC) will develop bell-mouth portions as free-left-turn passages, clear encroachments, shift obstructing utility poles and upgrade junctions to ease traffic congestion across its limits.

During a visit to Boduppal circle on Thursday, MMC commissioner T Vinay Krishna Reddy directed officials to prioritise traffic management, road repairs and removal of redundant cables. “After inspecting bell mouths at road junctions, Reddy asked Town Planning and Engineering officials to widen stretches with insufficient road width, remove traffic bottlenecks and complete the work at the earliest,” said a press release.

Officials were also instructed to repair potholes and damaged patches on BT roads using the jet-patching method to make travel safer and more comfortable.

Commissioner asked officials to coordinate with cable operators to remove unused cables and unnecessary wires hanging from electricity poles. He directed them to replicate the Sainagar Colony model across all colonies in the circle and prepare a comprehensive action plan to clear unwanted wiring.

item.title: Woman allegedly assaulted by motorcyclist in Banjara Hills
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 21-year-old woman alleged that a motorcyclist identified as Aravind assaulted her while she was walking towards her workplace near the MLA Colony Recreation Centre in Banjara Hills around 1 am on Wednesday. Police registered a case.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 21-year-old woman was allegedly assaulted by a man riding a motorcycle while she was walking towards her workplace in Banjara Hills on Wednesday.

According to the complaint, the woman, a resident of Syed Nagar, had finished her duty and was heading to the staff room near the MLA Colony Recreation Centre on Road No. 12 at around 1 am. While she was walking along the road, a man identified as Aravind, who approached her on a motorcycle from behind, allegedly struck her on the back and behaved inappropriately.

The woman suspected that he was under the influence of alcohol.

Following the incident, she approached the Banjara Hills police and lodged a complaint.

Police registered a case and are investigating.

item.title: Ranajai Nomula’s 68 powers Ranga Reddy to win over Sangareddy in Under-16 cricket
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Ranajai Nomula's 68 helped Ranga Reddy defeat Sangareddy by four wickets in the Telangana Cricket Association Under-16 State League Championship. E Hemanth's 107 went in vain. Mahabubnagar and Khammam also registered victories in their respective matches.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Fine century by E. Hemanth (107) went in vain as Ranga Reddy, powered by a fine knock by man of the match Ranajai Nomula (68) scored a four-wicket win in the Telangana Cricket Association State league (under-16) cricket championship at One Champion Ground in Moinabad on Thursday.

The scores: Mahabubnagar 182/3 in 20 overs ( Nithin Nayak 74, Sai Advit 60, Srikanth 2/36) bt Narayanpet 115 in 19.3 Overs (Srikanth 34, Pavan Kumar 4/18, Balu 2/16). Man of the match: Pavan Kumar. Khammam 166/5 in 20 overs ( K.Shiva Sai Reddy 64, Shakit Swaroop 28, Shaik Uzair 28, B.Chinnu 4/22) bt Gajwel 78 in 18.3 Overs ( M.Charan 18, M.Mahesh 3/24, Shaik Uzair 2/9). Man of the match: K. Shiva Sai Reddy.

Sangareddy 176/6 in 20 overs (E. Hemanth 107, Sai Pradyumna 34, Sagar Kumar 2/8) lost to Ranga Reddy 177/6 in 20 overs (Ranajai Nomula 68, T Vishank Reddy 30 no, J.Sohan 30 no E.Hemanth 3/30). Man of the match: Ranajai Nomula.

item.title: Six test positive for marijuana at Gachibowli men’s PG hostel in Telangana Eagle Force raid
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Six residents of a men's PG hostel in Gachibowli tested positive for marijuana during a Telangana Eagle Force raid. Police seized 15 grams of ganja, identified three suspected suppliers and handed the individuals over to Madhapur police.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Six residents of a men’s PG hostel in Gachibowli tested positive for marijuana consumption during a surprise raid conducted by the Telangana Eagle Force on Thursday.

Following a tip-off, the raid was conducted at Hari Hara Gyaneshwara Men’s PG Hostel in Siddiq Nagar in Madhapur. Eight residents were subjected to urine drug screening tests, of whom six tested positive for THC, the psychoactive component found in marijuana. The remaining two tested negative.
Of those tested positive, three were working as e-commerce delivery executives, two were software engineers and one was employed as a pharmacist.

During the operation, the police team seized 15 grams of marijuana and pre-rolled cones from two residents.
Further questioning reportedly revealed that the residents were procuring ganja from three suspected suppliers identified as Babulu Thakur alias Bablu, Thapan and Krishna.

The alleged suppliers were charging around Rs 600 for a five-gram packet, according to the preliminary inquiry.
The six individuals who tested positive, along with the seized material, were handed over to Madhapur police for further action.

Further investigation is underway to establish the supply network and identify other possible links operating in Gachibowli and surrounding areas.

item.title: BCCI Women’s Under-23 T20: Srujana, Drithi guide Hyderabad to 15-run win over Bihar
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today

Srujana (three for 24) and Kesari Drithi (two for 29) helped Hyderabad score a 15-run win against Bihar in the BCCI Women’s under-23 T-20 cricket championship fourth round match at Raipur on Thursday. Takshith Rao scored a match-winning century (122, 97b, 19×4, 2×6) for Sporting XI against Evergreen with his teammate Mohd Umar (five for 45) being the main wicket-taker.
