item.title: Nirmal: Farmer body leader alleges lack of support for suicide-hit families
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Rythu Swarajya Vedika district president Sangepu Borranna alleged that the government was not supporting families of farmers who died by suicide. He sought compensation, pensions, employment and education assistance for dependants, citing 27 such deaths in Nirmal district.
item.content:encoded:
Nirmal: Rythu Swarajya Vedika district president Sangepu Borranna regretted that the government was not extending support to bereaved families of farmers who died by suicide due to losses in farming. He, along with former sarpanch Bhaskar Reddy, consoled the family members of farmer Parasa Bheem Rao, who died by suicide, and gathered details of the incident at Warthamannur village on Thursday.

Borranna said that 27 farmers from the district had died by suicide after suffering huge losses in farming following crop failures triggered by El Niño from January 1 to date. He stated that Bheem Rao too had died by suicide due to farm losses caused by a decline in yield. He said the district had received scanty rainfall due to El Niño, resulting in crop failure.

The district president expressed concern over the deepening agrarian crisis. He wanted the government to provide compensation of Rs 6 lakh to each family of a farmer who died by suicide, besides offering employment opportunities to dependants as per GO No. 194. He sought a monthly pension of Rs 6,000 for the head of the family and asked the government to bear the education expenses of the children.

The farmer organisation leader urged the government to direct revenue and agriculture officials to create awareness among distressed farmers. He requested it to ensure a monthly income of Rs 15,000 for farmers by encouraging them to take up millet cultivation, poultry and cattle rearing. He wanted the government to take steps to provide financial support to farmers.

item.title: Centre launches CCMB-led guidelines to detect disease-causing pathogens in wastewater
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
item.description: The Union Health Ministry has launched wastewater surveillance guidelines developed by a CSIR-CCMB-led consortium. The framework will help public health authorities detect pathogens, monitor infectious diseases, assess disease burdens and identify potential outbreaks, including threats from emerging pathogens.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched ‘National Guidelines on Wastewater Surveillance for Pathogens of Public Health Importance” developed by Hyderabad-based Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CSIR-CCMB) led consortium of research institutions.

For the past five years, the CCMB, which formed the Alliance for Pathogen Surveillance and Innovations (APSI) with multiple other research and clinical institutions from various parts of the country, had developed protocols to detect pathogens such as SARS CoV-2 and influenza viruses as well as bacteria contributing to antimicrobial resistance, in wastewater.

In fact, during the peak Covid-19 pandemic, the CCMB has initiated the wastewater environmental surveillance programme to check for pathogens in the environment using wastewater from sewage treatment plants or open drains as sample sources.

The protocols formed by CCMB offer a foundation for providing early warning signs for known and emerging infectious disease agents via cost-effective measures of health. The protocols provide a comprehensive disease burden assessment and help in early prediction of outbreaks.

Its significance has been reported globally during the COVID-19 pandemic where it proved to be an invaluable tool in detection of the circulating SARS CoV-2 variants worldwide, a CCMB press release said.

The guideline document is a resource for public health authorities to expand the wastewater environmental surveillance programmes to detect several priority pathogens such as influenza, monkeypox, hepatitis A & E, rota, adeno and respiratory syncytial viruses, bacteria including Vibrio cholerae, Salmonella typhi and paratyphi as well as novel pathogens which may serve as potential pandemic threats.

“We hope that expanding the wastewater environmental surveillance programmes to these different pathogens will help in their effective management as has been possible for COVID-19,” said Dr. Vinay K Nandicoori, Director, CSIR-CCMB.

item.title: KTR accuses Congress government of corruption, vows to recover alleged loot
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao accused the Congress government of corruption, citing allegations by its own MLAs. He vowed to recover the money allegedly looted if the BRS returns to power and questioned the government's pension record.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Citing allegations by Congress MLAs themselves about commissions in government works and large-scale irregularities in contracts, BRS working president KT Rama Rao accused the Congress government of running a corrupt regime rather than the promised “Praja Palana” (people’s government). He vowed that, upon returning to power, the BRS would recover every rupee allegedly looted by Congress leaders.

Addressing a gathering at Telangana Bhavan on Thursday, Rama Rao recalled that Jadcherla MLA Anirudh Reddy had complained that works were not being sanctioned without 20 per cent commissions, while Munugode MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy had accused Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy of Rs 5 lakh crore loot and corruption in tenders. He also cited Congress MLA Yennam Srinivas Reddy’s complaint that funds meant for constituencies were being diverted to Kodangal.

The BRS working president said Congress legislators were left with little to do beyond attending weddings and funerals because the government was not releasing funds. He said the allegations by ruling party legislators exposed the government’s functioning.

Stating that the Congress would be voted out in a year, he said the BRS would not spare anyone involved in corruption and would recover the money allegedly pocketed by those in power.

Further, Rama Rao accused the government of misleading pensioners. He pointed out that the BRS government had provided 44.7 lakh pensions, but the Congress regime had removed 4.7 lakh beneficiaries over the last three years while sanctioning only 4.63 lakh new pensions during the same period. He questioned the claim of expanding coverage when the number of beneficiaries remained lower.

Recalling the Congress election promise, the former Minister said the party had assured people that Aasara pensions would be increased to Rs 4,000 within 100 days of coming to power, but continued to provide the Rs 2,000 fixed by the BRS government. He added that the K Chandrashekhar Rao government had increased pensions from Rs 200 to Rs 2,000 to ensure dignity and financial security for elderly people and persons with disabilities.

He questioned the Congress leadership over its six guarantees and the guarantee cards distributed during the election campaign.

Meanwhile, leaders and workers from various parties in Bhupalpally joined the BRS at Telangana Bhavan in the presence of Rama Rao, former Minister Errabelli Dayakar Rao and former MLA Gandra Venkataramana Reddy.

Welcoming them into the party, Rama Rao said the development and welfare initiatives taken up during the K Chandrashekhar Rao government had strengthened the region and expressed confidence that people would bring the BRS back to power. He said the constituency had received significant administrative and infrastructure development, including the establishment of a municipality, district headquarters and a medical college.

The BRS working president said Telangana was formed through a struggle for self-respect, but Congress and BJP leaders were stooping to new lows to please their respective Delhi bosses. He said leaders from both parties had failed to raise issues concerning Telangana’s interests.

item.title: Cyberabad Moves 2026 poster unveiled
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Chief Minister A Revanath Reddy launched the Cyberabad Moves 2026 poster in Hyderabad. The three-day event at T-Hub, Raidurgam, will focus on road safety, sustainable transport and urban mobility solutions.
item.content:encoded:
Event scheduled from November 26 to 28

Hyderabad: Chief Minister A Revanath Reddy on Thursday launched a poster for Cyberabad Moves 2026, a three-day event aimed at improving road safety, promoting sustainable transport and exploring mobility solutions for Cyberabad.

The event will be held at T-Hub in Raidurgam, Cyberabad, from November 26 to 28, between 9 am and 6 pm. According to a press release, the initiative seeks public participation to address the city’s growing mobility needs.

Citizens, students, professionals, industry representatives and other stakeholders have been invited to share ideas and explore urban transport solutions.

Serilingampally MLA Arekapudi Gandhi, Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) Commissioner G. Srijana, Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh, and senior police and traffic officials attended the campaign event.

The CMC Commissioner urged people to register at https://cyberabadmoves.in and participate in the event.

Readers ask

When and where will Cyberabad Moves 2026 be held?

The event will be held at T-Hub in Raidurgam, Cyberabad, from November 26 to 28, between 9 am and 6 pm.

What is the purpose of Cyberabad Moves 2026?

The event aims to improve road safety, promote sustainable transport and explore mobility solutions for Cyberabad.

How can people participate in the event?

CMC Commissioner G. Srijana urged people to register at https://cyberabadmoves.in and participate.

item.title: FCI Headquarters, North Zone enter final of All India Inter-Zonal Hockey Tournament 2026
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: 55th All India FCI Inter-Zonal Hockey Tournament 2026
item.description: FCI Headquarters and North Zone entered the final of the 55th All India FCI Inter-Zonal Hockey Tournament 2026. Headquarters thrashed East Zone 10–2, while North Zone defeated West Zone 4–2. East Zone claimed bronze after a penalty shoot-out.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: FCI Headquarters and North Zone entered the final of the 55th All India FCI Inter-Zonal Hockey Tournament 2026, organised by Food Corporation of India, Telangana Region, after registering victories in their respective semi-final matches held today at Railway Hockey Grounds here on Thursday. In the first semi-final, FCI Headquarters produced an outstanding performance to defeat East Zone by a commanding margin of 10–2, securing their place in the final.

FCI Headquarters’ goals were scored by Monu Choudhary, Ankur, Manasrij Bora and Munish Rana, who scored two goals each, while Nitin and Bobby Singh Dhami contributed one goal each. For East Zone, Ritik Kujur and Anmol Ekka scored one goal each. In the second semi-final, North Zone defeated West Zone 4–2 to book their berth in the title clash, setting up an exciting final against FCI Headquarters. North Zone’s goals were scored by Nandakishore, Vijay Singh and Harmandeep, with one goal each. For West Zone, Akash Parwar scored both goals.

The bronze-medal match was decided through penalty shoot-outs, in which East Zone prevailed 5–4 to claim the third-place. The final between FCI Headquarters and North Zone will be played on Friday at 10:00 AM at Railway Hockey Grounds, Mrs. Jacintha Lazarus, IAS, Executive Director (South), FCI and President, ZSCPC, South Zone, will be the Chief Guest.

item.title: NHAI says insurance SMS alerts are only for awareness, not enforcement
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The NHAI said SMS alerts reminding motorists about vehicle insurance expiry dates are part of a testing exercise and will not lead to challans or penalties at toll plazas. The proposed initiative aims to improve awareness of mandatory insurance requirements.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has clarified that SMS notifications being received by some highway users regarding the renewal of vehicle insurance policies are part of a testing exercise for a proposed public awareness initiative and are not linked to any enforcement action, an official statement said on Thursday.

According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the initiative is purely informational and aimed at reminding vehicle owners about upcoming insurance policy expiry dates. NHAI said there is no provision to issue challans or impose penalties at toll plazas on the basis of these alerts and assured highway users that the system is not connected to any punitive measures. “The notifications are intended solely to encourage timely renewal of motor insurance policies and ensure continuous insurance coverage,” according to the ministry. The clarification comes amid concerns among some motorists regarding the purpose of the messages and whether they could lead to enforcement action during toll transactions. NHAI said the reminder mechanism is being tested as part of efforts to improve awareness of statutory requirements related to vehicle ownership and road safety. By providing advance alerts on policy expiry dates, the authority aims to promote responsible vehicle ownership and encourage compliance with mandatory insurance norms, it added.

Such awareness-driven initiatives form part of its broader commitment to enhancing road safety and fostering safer behaviour among road users across the national highway network, according to the ministry. Earlier in November, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) introduced a new four-layer structure for motor insurance policies covering private cars and two-wheelers, allowing customers to choose specific covers based on their requirements, effective from December 15, 2026. The revised framework was announced to improve customer choice and transparency by clearly separating different components of motor insurance policies, according to the IRDAI.

item.title: Kadem river bridge work drags on for four years
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Construction of a bridge across the Kadem river has been delayed for four years due to a fund crunch, leaving residents of around 10 interior villages struggling with poor connectivity. Villagers continue to risk their lives crossing the river.
item.content:encoded:
Nirmal: Construction of a much-awaited high-level bridge across the Kadem river at Gangapur and Somvarpet villages has been dragging on for four years due to a fund crunch, leaving residents of around 10 interior villages irked.

People, mostly tribal residents of not only remote Gangapur village but also Korrathanda, Raniguda and surrounding villages, are still deprived of basic road connectivity. They need to travel along a narrow, earthen road that passes through hillocks and dense forests for 15 km to reach Kadem and Khanapur for various needs, including medical emergencies, education and employment. They remain isolated during the monsoon, with hilly streams overflowing. They have been demanding a bridge for quite a long time.

In order to reduce the travelling distance between Gangapur and Kadem and end their decades-long hardships, a bridge was sanctioned across the river at an estimated cost of Rs 10 crore. Work on the bridge commenced in 2020. However, it was stalled after fierce floods swept away two slabs of the under-construction bridge in 2022.

The work resumed in 2024 after the design was altered, the height of the facility was increased and its estimated cost was enhanced to Rs 22 crore. Minister Seethakka and local MLA Vedma Bojju laid the foundation stone for the bridge. They claimed that the woes of the villagers would be a thing of the past. They assured them that the facility would become a reality soon, delighting the villagers.

However, the work is progressing at a snail’s pace. Barely eight pillars have been built so far. A slab and the approach roads on either side are yet to be constructed. The executing agency is learnt to have halted the work following an inordinate delay in the payment of bills. Construction equipment has reportedly been shifted to another site.

Hapless villagers regretted that they continued to struggle owing to the slow progress of the work. They urged officials to take steps to expedite it. They lamented that they were forced to cross the river on country rafts made of bamboo, risking their lives. Following widespread criticism from locals, the sarpanches of Gangapur, Raniguda, Korrathanda and other villages met MLA Vedma Bojju recently. They urged him to speed up the work by striving to get the pending bills released.

Roads and Buildings officials said that steps were being taken to expedite the work on the bridge. They added that efforts were being made to release the pending bills at the earliest. They admitted that the fund crunch had affected the work.

item.title: Hyderabad: Two transgender persons held for extorting money at wedding procession
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chaitanyapuri police arrested two transgender persons for allegedly demanding Rs 20,000 from guests at a wedding procession in Kothapet and threatening to create a nuisance. The victims paid Rs 4,000 before alerting police through Dial 112.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Chaitanyapuri police arrested two transgender persons for allegedly threatening guests and extorting money during a wedding procession in Kothapet on Wednesday.

According to police, the suspects, Kalpana and Roja, demanded Rs 20,000 from those attending the wedding and threatened to create a nuisance if their demand was not met. Fearing disruption, the complainant initially paid Rs 4,000. However, the duo allegedly continued to harass the guests.

The victims alerted the police through Dial 112.

Acting on the information, Chaitanyapuri police reached the spot, caught the duo and sent them to judicial remand. Police authorities warned that strict action would be taken against anyone resorting to threats and forcibly collecting money.

item.title: EPFO raises withdrawal limit to 90 per cent, clears monthly payout plan
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The EPFO has raised the provident fund withdrawal limit to 90 per cent and reduced the waiting period after job loss from 12 months to two. It has also approved a proposal for monthly retirement payouts through a systematic withdrawal plan.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on Thursday raised the limit of withdrawals from the corpus funds for members up to 55 years of age to 90 per cent, from the earlier withdrawal limit of up to 75 per cent, as part of a reform that is expected to benefit a large number of subscribers.
The move is expected to make retirement savings more accessible in urgent financial situations while subscribers can still benefit from the scheme. The EPFO has also cut the EPF withdrawal waiting period after job loss from 12 months to 2 months to reduce the hardship faced by those who fall out of employment. The EPFOâ€s Central Board of Trustees (CBT) also approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP), which will enable retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in monthly instalments instead of withdrawing the entire amount in one go. Instead of withdrawing the entire EPF corpus on retirement, EPFO members can now opt for monthly provident fund withdrawals upon retirement while the corpus continues to earn interest.

The introduction of SWP will enable members to convert their retirement savings into a stable and predictable stream of systematic withdrawals post-retirement, while preserving the ownership of the underlying corpus. “The initiative will enhance retirement financial security by providing members with a flexible, regular and reliable income stream, while safeguarding their families’ interests,” says the EPFO. This will enable them to receive the higher rates of interest that EPFO pays without having to invest in riskier assets outside to earn more interest. In case of the member’s death during the payout period, the nominee or dependent will be able to withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving periodic payments.

The initiative will enhance retirement financial security by providing members with a flexible, regular and reliable income stream, while safeguarding their families’ interests.

item.title: Tara Gaming collaborates with Annapurna Studios for Motion Capture on ‘The Age of Bhaarat’
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Tara Gaming has partnered with Annapurna Studios' A&M MoCap Lab for motion capture production on its upcoming AAA game, The Age of Bhaarat. The collaboration highlights India's growing AVGC ecosystem and combines gaming vision with advanced production expertise.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Hyderabad: Tara Gaming has partnered with A&M MoCap Lab, Annapurna Studios, here for motion capture production on The Age of Bhaarat, its upcoming AAA game.

The partnership reflects the growing role of India’s AVGC (Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics) ecosystem in global entertainment. It brings together Tara Gaming’s vision for a globally ambitious gaming experience and the established filmmaking legacy and advanced production infrastructure of Annapurna Studios and Mihira Visual Labs.

Tara Gaming Executive Chairman Nicolas Granatino said ‘The Age of Bhaarat’ reflects their ambition to create a distinctive AAA gaming experience for a global audience.

“India has an exceptional talent pool and an established production ecosystem. Our collaboration with Annapurna Studios brings together our gaming vision and the studio’s legacy and motion capture expertise,” said Granatino

Annapurna Studios CTO CV Rao, CTO of Annapurna Studios, said they are delighted to collaborate with Tara Gaming on The Age of Bhaarat. “Building on our legacy in Indian cinema and our investment in advanced production capabilities, we look forward to bringing our motion capture expertise to the project,” he added.

item.title: Modi asks India Inc. to turn tax cuts, reforms into jobs and higher wages
item.dc:creator: T Ivan Nischal
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged India Inc. to translate tax cuts and economic reforms into more jobs and higher wages. He also called for greater investment in domestic manufacturing, food processing and export opportunities to reduce import dependence.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday questioned Indian Inc. on whether it had created more employment and raised the incomes of employees following corporate tax reductions and other economic reforms undertaken by the government to boost industry and facilitate the ease of doing business.
Addressing the FICCI Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention here, the Prime Minister said the government had reduced corporate tax rates, provided income tax relief, simplified compliance and signed trade agreements to improve opportunities for Indian businesses. However, industry also needed to demonstrate that it has passed on these benefits in the form of more jobs in the economy and higher wages for employees. The Prime Minister pointed out that businesses should not expect the government alone to drive the country’s development and need to be partners in the growth process. PM Modi also urged the captains of industry to develop concrete strategies to take advantage of India’s expanding network of free trade agreements, instead of relying on the government to identify opportunities.

The Prime Minister said Indian consumers deserved the same quality of products that companies offered in overseas markets, and businesses should not take India’s large domestic consumer base for granted. Questioning the practice of marketing products as being of export quality which are considered superior, PM Modi said, “My countrymen deserve quality goods.” The Prime Minister also called for greater investment in domestic manufacturing capabilities, particularly in sectors where India remains dependent on imports. He cited the example of pharmaceuticals, where India is regarded as the pharmacy of the world but continues to import billions of dollars worth of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and intermediates. The Prime Minister urged companies to identify ingredients that could be manufactured competitively in India and invest in the technologies needed to reduce this dependence.

He also highlighted the aluminium and steel sectors in which India possessed substantial raw material resources but continued to depend on imports for certain specialised products. Agriculture and food processing were another area of concern. PM Modi said India’s share of global agricultural exports remained around 2â€“2.5 per cent despite its large agricultural production base. He urged businesses to invest in food processing and value addition, particularly products designed for overseas demand, rather than concentrating only on domestic consumption.

item.title: Three couples realise parenthood dream through IVF at Gandhi Hospital
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Three couples from economically disadvantaged backgrounds have welcomed babies following successful IVF treatment at Gandhi Hospital. After years of infertility and unsuccessful private treatments costing lakhs, they received assisted reproductive care at the government hospital without financial burden.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Three couples from underprivileged backgrounds in Telangana, who were childless for several years and had spent a sizable chunk of their savings at private fertility clinics, welcomed healthy babies following successful In-Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) treatments at the Government-run Gandhi Hospital.

Notably, two of the three deliveries took place within a span of 36 minutes on Wednesday morning, November 18.

In the first case, 35-year-old Dasari Swaroopa and her 38-year-old husband Raju, a car driver from Warangal, became parents to a baby boy (weighing 1.8 kgs) on November 10 after 16 years of struggling with infertility. According to Gandhi Hospital doctors, the couple had previously spent nearly Rs 4 lakh on unsuccessful IVF procedures at private hospitals before turning to Gandhi Hospital.

For nearly a decade, Peesari Madhavi (26) and Vijay Kumar (35), a security guard from Yadadri Bhuvanagiri, struggled to have children. On Wednesday, at around 10.16 am, they welcomed a baby girl (weighing 2.4 kg) at Gandhi Hospital after undergoing IVF treatment.

On the same day, about 36 minutes later, at 10:52 am, Shanamma (25) and her husband Ananthaiah (28), a farming couple from Tandur mandal in Vikarabad district, delivered a baby boy weighing 2.75 kg.

The couple had struggled with infertility for nine years and had spent roughly Rs 3 lakh on failed IVF cycles at private facilities before seeking treatment at Gandhi Hospital.

Hospital authorities and the families credited the dedicated team of IVF specialists, obstetricians, nursing staff, and support personnel at Gandhi Hospital for making advanced assisted reproductive care accessible to underprivileged families without financial burden.

item.title: Global Citizen Scholarship 2027: Global Schools Group opens applications for students
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Global Schools Group has opened applications for its 2027 Global Citizen Scholarship programme. Selected students can pursue Grades 11 and 12 at designated campuses in Singapore and India, with tuition, accommodation, living expenses and a stipend fully covered.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Global Schools Group (GSG) has announced the opening of applications for the 2027 edition of Global Citizen Scholarship (GCS) programme, an initiative that offers fully-funded scholarship to students to complete their senior secondary school years in its campus in Singapore.

The programme is designed to go beyond conventional academic learning by providing students with international exposure, multicultural interactions and opportunities to develop critical thinking, leadership and problem-solving skills.

Under the scholarship programme, selected students will have the opportunity to pursue Grades 11 and 12 at the GIIS SMART Campus, Singapore and other selected GSG India campuses. The scholarship covers 100 percent tuition fees, boarding, lodging and living expenses, along with a stipend.

Students meeting the programme’s academic and other eligibility requirements are encouraged to apply online on or before December 20.

item.title: BRS seeks clearance of Rs 76 crore dues to government textbook printers
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The BRS has urged the Telangana government to clear Rs 76 crore in pending payments to 56 small printing units supplying government textbooks. Harish Rao said the three-year delay had pushed printers into financial distress, affecting workers and their families.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Nearly Rs 76 crore in payments to 56 small printing units engaged in supplying government textbooks has remained pending for the last three years, pushing them into financial distress and threatening the livelihoods of thousands of workers’ families. The BRS demanded that Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, who holds the Education portfolio, intervene and clear the long-pending dues immediately.

Representatives of the Telangana Web Offset Printers Association met BRS Legislature Party deputy leader T Harish Rao at his residence here on Thursday and requested the Opposition party to press the government for the release of their dues.

Speaking on the occasion, Harish Rao criticised the Congress government for failing to clear the dues despite the printers having supplied textbooks on time and maintained quality. He said the printers, who had served the government for nearly 25 years, were struggling to pay workers’ salaries, rents, electricity bills and suppliers due to the non-payment.

Questioning the government’s spending priorities, he said funds were being spent on Musi beautification, beauty pageants, the Chief Minister’s football activities and other publicity events, while payments to those printing textbooks for poor students were being withheld.

Harish Rao pointed out that the government imposed penalties on printers for delays in supplying books but failed to clear their bills for years. Repeated representations to officials, from the Director and Commissioner to the Secretary and other senior officers of the School Education Department, had yielded no response, he said.

He urged Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka to intervene and secure the immediate release of the Rs 76 crore dues to support the 56 printing units and the families dependent on them.

item.title: Medininagar woman found dead, suspect detained
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 45-year-old woman, Sadhana Singh, was found dead at her Medininagar home on Thursday. Police detained a suspect for questioning after family members alleged he had threatened her earlier.
item.content:encoded:
Medininagar: A 45-year-old woman was allegedly murdered with a sharp-edged weapon at her residence in Nawatoli locality of Medininagar in Jharkhand’s Palamu district on Thursday.

The woman, identified as Sadhana Singh, was found lying on a bed inside her room with multiple injuries to her head. Police detained a suspect and are questioning him in connection with the incident.

Sadhana was alone at home when the incident took place. Her husband, Anand Kumar Singh, works in Jamshedpur, while their 21-year-old daughter lives in Delhi. She had been living alone at the family residence.

The incident came to light on Thursday morning when a tenant living in the same house went upstairs to switch on the water pump and fill the overhead tank. After noticing no movement from Sadhana’s room for a considerable period, the tenant became suspicious.

Finding the door closed and receiving no response, the tenant alerted neighbours. When they checked the room, they found Sadhana lying on the bed.

City Police Station in-charge Jyoti Lal Rajwar reached the spot with a police team and began an investigation. Police inspected the scene and deployed a dog squad to gather clues and trace the suspected attacker.

Family members expressed suspicion against a man identified as Raja alias Yunus. Sadhana’s elder sister, Sandhya Kumari, accused Raja Ansari of involvement in the alleged murder.

According to the family, the suspect had allegedly threatened Sadhana on previous occasions. They also claimed that she received a death threat over the phone a few days before the Teej festival.

Family members said Sadhana and the suspect had known each other for around two years. Police are examining the circumstances surrounding their association and the alleged threats.

Sadar Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Rajesh Yadav said the matter was under investigation and the detained suspect was being questioned.

He said the motive behind the alleged murder and the suspect’s alleged role would become clear only as the investigation progressed. Police are gathering evidence to establish the sequence of events leading to the woman’s death.

item.title: India eye AFC U17 Asian Cup qualification
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: India need a draw against hosts Malaysia in their final Group E match to qualify for the 2027 AFC U17 Asian Cup, after winning all three qualifiers and scoring 20 goals.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The India men's team will be one point away from securing qualification for the AFC U17 Asian Cup for the 11th time in their history when they take on hosts Malaysia in their final Group E fixture at the Kuala Lumpur Football Stadium today.

The Blue Colts have won all three of their matches so far, scoring 20 goals and conceding just three. Having beaten Singapore 4-2, Guam 12-0 and Palestine 4-1, India lead Group E with nine points. They are three points ahead of both Malaysia and Palestine, who have six points each.

Only the group winners will qualify for the final tournament in Uzbekistan, scheduled to be held from May 13 to 29, 2027. A draw against Malaysia will guarantee the top spot for India, who will secure back-to-back appearances at the U17 Asian Cup after qualifying for the 2026 edition also in Saudi Arabia. The other Group E fixture today will see Palestine face Singapore earlier in the day, and if it ends in a victory for the former, even a loss by a two-goal margin will be enough for India because of their superior head-to-head goal difference against Palestine and Malaysia.

India head coach Mehrajuddin Wadoo has been pleased with the team's attacking output, particularly the number of players contributing to the goals. Nine different players have found the net in the campaign so far, giving the side multiple attacking options.

“I think our attacking performance has been brilliant. Scoring goals always gives you an advantage on the pitch, but having different goalscorers in the team is also an advantage. You are not dependent on just one player, and we are blessed to have that,” said Wadoo.

“We have improved a lot in terms of how we control different moments in the game. If you look at the last match against Palestine, we scored in the first half but also conceded a goal. In the second half, we controlled those moments, which is very important for a team. That shows we've gotten mature,” Wadoo said.

The final hurdle, however, will be against a Malaysia side that has also won its last two matches. After losing 0-2 to Palestine in their opening fixture, the hosts recovered with a 2-1 victory over Singapore before registering a 10-0 win against Guam.

Wadoo is aware of the challenge posed by the hosts, particularly with the backing of their home supporters, and expects his boys to be disciplined throughout.

“Malaysia is a good side. They lost their first game against Palestine, which we watched at the stadium, but they were good. They have won against Singapore and Guam and scored 12, so we know they can be a tough opponent,” he said.

“I had a meeting with the players, and I told them that we want to win the game. We have won all three matches so far, and we want to leave Malaysia with another win. I told them that winning is the only option for us and that we are going for it,” Wadoo said.

“A draw may be enough for us, but I have personal experience in my career that when you go into a game looking for a draw, you can end up losing it. I think we have to go for the win because we cannot play for a draw.”

item.title: Governor inaugurates IIMUN Hyderabad Conference 2026
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla inaugurated the IIMUN Hyderabad Conference 2026 at Kuntloor Johnson Grammar School, urging students to embrace unity, peace and global brotherhood. Former MP K Suresh Reddy and diplomat Dr Nagendra Prasad TV also addressed the gathering.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The IIMUN (India’s International Movement to Unite Nations) Hyderabad Conference 2026 was inaugurated at Kuntloor Johnson Grammar School, ICSE, by the Governor, Shiv Pratap Shukla.

Addressing the students, the Governor highlighted the importance of the Indian philosophy of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’, calling upon young people to uphold the values of unity, mutual respect, peace and global brotherhood. He also administered a pledge encouraging students to lead an addiction-free life.

Former MP, Dr K Suresh Reddy, shared insights from the peaceful Telangana movement and highlighted the importance of responsible communication, thoughtful decision-making and constructive leadership among youth.

Dr Nagendra Prasad TV, former Deputy Chief of Mission at the Embassy of India in Berne, Switzerland, and former Ambassador of India to Kazakhstan, spoke about contemporary international developments and their economic, political and social implications for India and its younger generation.

Dr B Mallikarjun Rao, Chairman, Kuntloor Johnson Grammar School, along with Dr B Malathi Rao, Director, Dr K Kalyani Chary, Rector, and G Seshulakshmi, Principal, participated. The inaugural session brought together inspiring perspectives on leadership, diplomacy, culture, patriotism and social responsibility.

item.title: Telangana opens Mee Seva route for borewell permissions
item.dc:creator: Sunil Mungara
item.description: The Telangana government has shifted borewell permission applications to the Mee Seva portal. The Groundwater Department will accept only online applications, which will undergo technical scrutiny, including checks on aquifer capacity, local groundwater conditions and mandatory distance from public drinking water sources.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Telangana government has relaxed restrictions on digging new borewells, allowing citizens to seek permissions online through Mee Seva portal.

Accordingly, the Groundwater Department officials who are currently processing online applications through TG-iPASS, a single-window system that eliminates manual office visits, will now accept applications through Mee Seva.

K Laxma, Director of Telangana Groundwater Department, directed all district groundwater officers to accept applications exclusively through Mee Seva. Offline applications or those submitted through any other channel will not be accepted.

Earlier this month, the Telangana government restricted new borewells in the Core Urban Region Economy for construction and non-drinking purposes amid concerns over El Niño and falling groundwater levels. The GO 259 was subsequently issued for Hyderabad’s Core Urban Region, allowing online applications for emergency drinking water and urgent household construction needs.

An official said applications would be accepted through Mee Seva once login facilities and the application format were set up within a day or two, and processing an application would take at least 15 days.

Each application will undergo technical verification of aquifer capacity, the status of the local assessment zone and mandatory spacing requirements, including a 250-metre buffer from public drinking water sources.

item.title: JioStar unveils campaign film featuring Rohit, Kohli ahead of Sri Lanka series
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: JioStar has unveiled a campaign film featuring Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli ahead of India’s three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka from December 13, building anticipation for the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: JioStar unveiled its latest campaign film as the road to the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027 gathers momentum, celebrating the return of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to home soil ahead of Sri Lanka’s three-match ODI series against India, beginning on December 13 on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network.

Placing the two players at the heart of India’s World Cup aspirations, the campaign captures the nation’s expectations and excitement over a third ICC ODI World Cup title through the eyes of Kohli and Sharma.

Captain Shubman Gill lends his voice to the film, narrating how vital Kohli and Sharma’s experience and legacy are to Team India’s campaign at the quadrennial showpiece. Sri Lanka’s tour of India is presented as the next peak to conquer along the way.

Conceptualised by JioStar, the film captures the anticipation and responsibility that come with representing India on the biggest stage. In the opening sequence, as Kohli heads out of the team hotel, he spots himself on television with the headline, “King’s Cup in 2027?”

In the hotel lobby, an employee hands him a card that reads, “2011 World Cup trophy again”, while a child spots Rohit Sharma and mimics his iconic ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2024 trophy-lifting step. The camera then pans to Gill, where viewers learn that he has been answering a journalist’s question on “pressure”, stating that when the stakes are high, legends throw their hat in the ring. This sets up the film’s punchline, contextualising the series against Sri Lanka: “Preparing for World Cup glory, but first up, it’s Sri Lanka.”

With less than a year to go for the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027, Team India will look to build on the momentum of their 2-1 ODI series win against the West Indies as they embark on a crucial run of home assignments, beginning with Sri Lanka. With Rohit and Kohli bringing their experience and firepower to the batting line-up, and Gill at the helm, the upcoming series will offer India another important opportunity to identify their strongest playing XI and build towards the marquee event. Viewers can catch all the live action from the three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka from December 13 to 19, exclusively on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network.

item.title: Inter students get longer gaps in 2027 examination schedule
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education has scheduled the 2027 Intermediate Public Examinations from February 24 to March 20. The timetable provides longer gaps between several subjects, while practical examinations and other assessments will begin in January.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Intermediate Public Examinations 2027 have been stretched by nearly one month, with the Telangana Board of Intermediate Education scheduling the exams from February 24 to March 20.

As per the timetable issued by the Board on Thursday, the first-year exams will begin with second language paper 1 on February 24, and second-year exams will commence on February 25.

Earlier, the exams had been conducted a little over two weeks apart, with a one-day interval between first- and second-year exams. However, this time, students will have more gaps between two subjects.

A three-day gap has been given for the Mathematics 1A and 2A papers, while students will get a two- and four-day gap for Mathematics 1A and 2B, respectively.

Both first- and second-year students have been given three days’ preparation time before the physics exam on March 9 and 12, respectively. Similarly, first-year students will get a four-day gap before the chemistry exam on March 15, and second-year students will have the chemistry exam on March 16.

For first-year students, exams will conclude with Modern Language Paper 1, Geography Paper 1, and Bridge Course Mathematics Paper 1 on March 19. Similarly, second exams will end with Modern Language Paper 2, Geography Paper – 2, bridge course on March 20.

Prior to theory exams, the Board will conduct practical exams for second-year science students from February 1 to 10 from 9 am to 12 noon, and 2 pm to 5 pm. Practical examinations for first science subjects will be conducted from February 11 to 18.

English practical exams for first- and second-year students will be conducted on January 29 and 30, respectively. The Ethics and Human Values exam is scheduled for January 29, while the Environmental Education Examination will be held on January 27. The first-year students will have an internal assessment from January 20 to 25.

item.title: Cool, hazy spell ahead for Hyderabad; rain likely in eastern Telangana
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad is expected to experience cool, dry and hazy weather over the coming week, even as a cyclonic storm puts coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on alert. Eastern Telangana districts are likely to receive thunderstorms and isolated heavy rainfall.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: While the cyclonic storm Akvan has placed neighbouring coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on high alert, Hyderabad and its surrounding districts are set for a week of nippy, dry, partly cloudy, and hazy weather, even as eastern districts of Telangana brace for thunderstorms and isolated heavy rainfall.

The dry cold northerly winds are keeping daytime humidity low and pulling down night temperatures in western and northern Telangana. While maximum daytime temperatures in core regions of Hyderabad remain at around 30 and 31 degrees Celsius, outer western pockets such as Rajendranagar and Patancheru, along with neighbouring Medak, Sangareddy, Vikarabad, and the northern district of Adilabad, have seen early morning temperatures dip into the 12 to 16 degrees Celsius range.

The IMD, Hyderabad, expects night temperatures in Hyderabad to edge up slightly to 19 degrees Celsius from November 22, once the cyclone makes landfall. According to the seven-day local forecast issued by the IMD, the state capital will experience a ‘partly cloudy sky with haze’ till November 25.

The IMD has issued warnings for thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds at isolated places on Thursday and isolated heavy rainfall forecast affecting districts including Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet, Nalgonda, Mahabubabad, Mulugu, and Jayashankar Bhupalpally.

item.title: Cyberabad Moves 2026 to focus on safer, smarter mobility
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Cyberabad Moves 2026, scheduled from November 26 to 28 at T-Hub, will bring together government agencies, experts and citizens to discuss safer and more sustainable mobility. The event will also showcase local transport solutions through a citizens' innovation challenge.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC), Cyberabad Police, the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC) and the SHIFT Transport Initiative, led by WRI India, will host Cyberabad Moves 2026, a three-day urban mobility exhibition and conclave, at T-Hub, from November 26 to 28.

The event aims to convert traffic data into actionable street solutions and prepare a roadmap for Hyderabad’s IT Corridor.

“The event aims to bring government agencies, global transport experts, corporate leaders, academics, and everyday commuters onto a single platform and build a safer, more inclusive, climate-resilient, and efficient transport network,” said Cyberabad Municipal Corporation Commissioner G Srijana.

The authorities were evaluating continuous one-way loop systems, such as along the Hi-Tech City–Biodiversity corridor, and had trained over 60 civic engineers and traffic personnel in safer street design. The initiative emphasises public participation, with officials engaging nearly 3.5 lakh students across more than 400 educational institutions on road safety and sustainable travel.

The Citizens Innovation Challenge also invites residents, students and RWAs to submit local transit solutions, ranging from posters to digital maps, for display at T-Hub. Registration and volunteer details are available via the official Cyberabad Moves 2026 Portal.

item.title: Fire breaks out in Pacifica Hill Crest tower; no casualties
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A fire broke out in a tower at Pacifica Hill Crest apartments in Puppalaguda on Thursday afternoon, affecting floors five to 14. Fire tenders rushed to the complex, while residents evacuated. No casualties or major property damage were reported.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: A fire broke out in one of the towers at the Pacifica Hill Crest apartment complex in Nanakramguda, Puppalaguda, near the Financial District, on Thursday afternoon. No casualties were reported.

According to fire officials, the department received a call in the afternoon, following which fire tenders from different fire stations rushed to the spot.

Panicked residents rushed out of the building, fearing for their safety.

“The fifth to 14th floors were affected by the fire. There was no major loss of property or casualties. The source and cause of the fire are being ascertained,” a fire department official said.

item.title: Hyderabad: Man flags alleged insect infestation in chocolate
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: An Alwal resident has approached the Food Safety Authority after allegedly finding insects and larvae in a Noice brand chocolate ordered through Swiggy. Dissatisfied with the platform's refund assurance, he has sought an investigation and appropriate action.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: A resident of Alwal has lodged a complaint with the Food Safety Authority after allegedly finding insects and larvae in a Noice brand chocolate purchased through Swiggy.

In his complaint, Akhil alleged that he had ordered the chocolate along with a few other products through Swiggy on November 18. To his shock, he found that the chocolate was infested with insects and larvae.

Akhil initially lodged a complaint with Swiggy. After reviewing his grievance, the company’s executives assured him of a refund. However, dissatisfied with the response, and as the issue raised serious concerns over food safety and public health, he approached the Food Safety Authority, seeking a thorough investigation and appropriate action.

item.title: ACB catches Tolichowki inspector accepting Rs 20,000 bribe
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: ACB officials caught Tolichowki Police Station Inspector L. Ramesh Naik allegedly accepting a ₹20,000 bribe from a cafeteria operator. He had reportedly demanded monthly payments to allow the establishment to operate beyond its permitted closing time of 1 am.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) officials on Wednesday night caught Tolichowki Police Station Inspector L Ramesh Naik red-handed while allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs 20,000 from a person.

According to ACB officials, the inspector had initially demanded a monthly bribe of Rs 50,000 for allowing a cafeteria to operate beyond its permitted closing time of 1 am and not taking any coercive action against the hotel management. “The inspector accepted Rs 20,000 initially and agreed to reduce the monthly bribe to Rs 40,000 for the first month, offering a concession of Rs 10,000,” said the officials.

On Wednesday night, the ACB team caught the inspector while accepting the remaining Rs 20,000. The amount was recovered from his possession at his instance.

During the operation, the ACB also found unaccounted cash of Rs 1.80 lakh in his possession, kept in four separate envelopes. “The inspector had abused his official position to obtain undue financial advantage in return for allowing the cafeteria to function for an additional hour to facilitate the completion of online food orders,” the officials said.

The inspector was arrested and produced before the I Additional Special Judge for SPE and ACB Cases at Nampally for judicial remand. The case is under investigation.

item.title: Yuvraj Singh, Chouhan and Kukar share lead at IndianOil SERVO Masters
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Yuvraj Singh joined Om Prakash Chouhan and Raunil Kukar at the top of the IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf leaderboard at 11-under 205 after the third round in Digboi, Assam, on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh, Mhow’s Om Prakash Chouhan and Bengaluru’s Raunil Kukar shared the 54-hole lead at 11-under 205 after the third round of the 26th IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf, a Rs 1 crore event being played at Digboi Golf Links in Digboi, Assam, on Thursday.

Overnight joint leader Chouhan (67-68-70), 40, carded a two-under 70 featuring six birdies, a double bogey on the par-3 10th and two bogeys to retain his share of the lead.

Kukar (70-65-70), 28, the other overnight joint leader, also returned a two-under 70 comprising five birdies and three bogeys to remain at the top.

Yuvraj (68-70-67), 25, who began the day tied fourth and three shots off the lead, fired a five-under 67 featuring seven birdies and two bogeys to join the overnight leaders. He made six of his birdies in two sets of three consecutive holes, first from the fifth to seventh and then from the 14th to 16th.

Bangladesh’s Md Razu (69-70-68) climbed from tied eighth to fourth at nine-under 207 after a four-under 68 featuring five birdies and a lone bogey on the par-4 eighth.

Mumbai’s Aryaman Aditya Mohan (73-70-65), 25, made the biggest move of the day, climbing from tied 25th to tied fifth at eight-under 208 with a seven-under 65 featuring an eagle on the par-5 seventh, eight birdies and three bogeys.

Chandigarh’s Akshay Sharma (75-67-66) joined Aryaman in tied fifth after a six-under 66 comprising an eagle on the seventh, six birdies and two bogeys.

Chouhan, an 11-time DP World PGTI winner, former European Challenge Tour winner, now known as the HotelPlanner Tour, and 2023 DP World PGTI rankings champion, continued to put himself in contention for another title.

Speaking about his third round, Chouhan said, “I played well today. My putting was good today as well, although I struggled a little with my putting tempo on the 10th hole.”

On playing alongside Kukar, he added, “The atmosphere should be good. I enjoyed playing with Raunil today, and he is a very good player.”

Chouhan also acknowledged the challenge posed by the pin positions, saying, “The pin positions were difficult today, and they affected the game.”

Kukar, playing his sixth consecutive DP World PGTI season, came close to claiming his maiden title at the SECL presents Nava Raipur Open in September, where he finished joint runner-up, one shot behind Khalin Joshi.

Yuvraj said, “It feels good to be at the top of the leaderboard. I think what worked for me today was simply sticking to my process and doing what needed to be done.”

The IndianOil SERVO Masters has a special place in the history of Indian professional golf, as it is the longest-running tournament on the Indian domestic circuit and the DP World PGTI.

item.title: Cyberabad may get personal rapid transit network to ease commuting
item.dc:creator: C. Romeo
item.description: The Telangana government is exploring a Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) for Hyderabad, with a proposed 35-km first-phase corridor connecting key IT hubs in Cyberabad. HMRL has been tasked with preparing detailed plans for the project, which aims to improve urban mobility and ease traffic congestion in the IT corridor.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Soon, Cyberabad could have a new mode of public transport that may change the way people commute to work. With the State government exploring a Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) for Hyderabad, the IT corridor and its surrounding areas could be among the first to benefit from the proposed network.

The proposed first phase envisages a 35-km PRTS corridor connecting Kukatpally, Raidurg, Biodiversity Junction and Knowledge City, with 64 stations.

The proposal is particularly significant for the Cyberabad region, where thousands of employees travel daily between residential neighbourhoods, IT campuses and commercial hubs, adding to the traffic pressure on major roads.

The proposal came up for discussion recently at a review meeting chaired by Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju.

Officials of Hyderabad Metro Rail Limited (HMRL) had also presented the initial plans and outlined the possibilities of introducing PRTS and Group Rapid Transit (GRT) systems to address the city’s growing mobility needs.

The government has further asked HMRL to prepare a comprehensive route map and implementation plan, taking into account passenger demand, existing infrastructure and project costs.

Also, officials have been directed to identify densely populated areas and select corridors that can offer maximum connectivity with minimum expenditure.

The proposed system is expected to complement, rather than replace, existing public transport networks such as the Metro Rail and TGSRTC buses. Integration between different modes of transport will be a key factor in ensuring convenient first and last-mile connectivity for commuters.

The need for alternative transport systems is becoming increasingly important as the city’s population and daily commuting requirements continue to rise. HMRL estimates that daily passenger demand could touch 3.94 lakh by 2030, and increase to 7.96 lakh by 2040 and reach 10 lakh by 2050.

Given the concentration of IT companies, office campuses and commercial establishments in the Cyberabad region, the proposed corridor could provide an additional commuting option for employees and residents. However, the alignment, funding model, technology and implementation timeline are yet to be finalised.

HMRL has been asked to consult several agencies, including GHMC, HMDA, TGSPDCL, TGSRTC, the Hyderabad and Cyberabad police, South Central Railway, HMWS&SB and HYDRAA, before submitting detailed proposals.

For now, the proposal is at the planning stage. If implemented, the PRTS could become another important addition to Hyderabad’s urban transport network, particularly in the congested IT corridor.

item.title: Bondada Engineering, RGUKT Basar join hands for student opportunities
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT)
item.description: Bondada Engineering has partnered with RGUKT Basar to provide students with internships, campus recruitment opportunities and pre-placement offers. The initiative also includes industry interaction sessions and guest lectures, with a focus on improving professional opportunities for rural students.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Bondada Engineering Limited has signed an MoU with Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT), Basar, to establish a structured collaboration focused on internship programmes, campus recruitment and long-term career opportunities for students.

With nearly 85% of RGUKT’s student community coming from rural backgrounds, the initiative aims to provide students with greater access to industry exposure, practical learning and professional opportunities.

Under the MoU, the company and the institute will collaborate on summer and winter internship programmes, long-term internships, campus recruitment drives for graduate and postgraduate students, and Pre-Placement Offers (PPOs) based on internship performance.

The partnership will also facilitate industry interaction sessions, guest lectures and knowledge-sharing initiatives to help students gain a better understanding of industry requirements.

Rear Admiral R. Sreenivas, VSM (Retd.), Chief Executive Officer of Bondada Group, said, “Rural India has an immense pool of capable and aspiring young minds who, with the right guidance, industry exposure and encouragement, can make significant contributions across sectors.”

item.title: Rs 5 coins vanishing? Dentists say viral claim is misleading
item.dc:creator: M. Sai Gopal
item.description: A viral claim that dentists are melting ₹5 coins to make dental crowns has been dismissed as misleading. The controversy originated in Maharashtra, where authorities acted against unauthorised technicians allegedly using uncertified scrap metal to manufacture cheap dental prosthetics.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A strange theory around the disappearance of Rs 5 coins from circulation, claiming that dentists are melting them down for tooth fillings and caps, has gained traction on social media.

What started as a local crackdown in Maharashtra has now become the talk of the town everywhere, sparking curiosity over the improbable theory that dental doctors are to be blamed for a short supply of Rs 5 coins.

That is simply not the case. The claim linking dentists and disappearance of Rs 5 coins stems from a November 6 resolution by the Medical Education department in Maharashtra after more than 350 complaints over a decade flagged unlicensed technicians making cheap metallic crowns using uncertified scrap, including melted Rs 5 coins.

While Maharashtra brought dental laboratories under Food and Drug Administration (FDA) scrutiny to curb illegal operators, the viral posts quickly turned into an indictment of dental surgeons across India.

“The theory has been blown out of proportion because metal-free crowns have long replaced conventional metal crowns. Modern technology has made biocompatible tooth-coloured restorations like zirconia, lithium disilicate (E-max), and advanced ceramics very affordable even in small cities. Modern dental fillings, meanwhile, rely on tooth-coloured composite resins rather than cast metal,” says Dr Ala Srikanth, Central Council Member, Indian Dental Association (IDA), Telangana.

A few years ago, a similar wave of unnecessary alarm broke out over silver amalgam fillings, even though the IDA-trained dentists had already switched to resin-based cosmetic fillings.

Clinically, modern Rs 5 coins are minted from nickel brass consisting of 75 per cent copper, 20 per cent zinc, and 5 per cent nickel, an uncertified alloy that is not at all suitable for oral procedures due to corrosion, metal-ion leaching, and gum inflammation.

Moreover, contemporary crowns are carved by computer-guided machines from solid ceramic blocks rather than cast from molten metal, leaving no place for melted coin metal in legitimate clinics, Dr Srikanth points out.

Senior dentists in Hyderabad point out that expensive machines and materials mean digital methods haven’t reached every town in Telangana and the country equally. As a result, a small, low-cost corner of the market, the kind where unauthorised dental technicians may indulge in making cheap metal caps without a doctor’s prescription.

Under the tightened rules, labs cannot fabricate any prosthetic without a registered dentist’s prescription and strict batch traceability. While unlicensed operators face a crackdown, well-known dental clinics are nowhere near melting your spare change.

item.title: GTA VI: Mayhem in Leonida, the Jason and Lucia Story
item.dc:creator: Aditya Deshbandhu
item.description: After 25 hours with GTA VI, the game's expansive world, intricate details, improved driving and deeper character progression stand out. From home renovations and workouts to combat and exploration, Rockstar's latest offers an experience that extends well beyond its missions.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: In the very first mission of Rockstar’s 13-year-awaited, chaotic epic, the game requires Jason (the male protagonist) to help pilot a boat to fish out packages from the sea.

In those early moments, the game establishes both the massive scope of Leonida, Rockstar’s take on Florida, as well as the incredible amount of detail required to play the game. The game guides you to align the boat and use a fishing pole to reel in the packages, something that can only be achieved with precision and control.

In those early moments, you realise this isn’t just a GTA about causing mayhem, but causing strategic destruction, if you may.

In my 25 hours with GTA VI so far, I have found it to be both incredibly beautiful and unmatched in terms of the depth it offers. No game prior to this has created a map this intricate and filled it with this many NPCs. The possibilities are endless, and I wouldn’t be surprised if many of us play the game not for its story or main missions, but to push its boundaries to see how far it will go.

From modifying cars and weapons to playing video games in your house (GTA VI even has a PS5 lookalike, working games, UI menus and all, called the JoySystem), to using the home gym or even running to places or cycling for a cardio boost – these are elements that the game gives us naturally, almost asking us gamers nonchalantly, “Isn’t this how games have always been?”

Speaking of workouts, you can actually set up a training regimen at Jason’s residence and use different gym equipment for various fitness boosts, rest afterwards to make the effects permanent, and even take a shower or freshen up for a focus boost. This is a game where you can decide both the personalities and physiques you would like your protagonists to have.

In the early missions, there is so much you can do as Jason to prepare for Lucia moving in, from redoing the walls in the house to the wooden boards on the staircase, and even fixing the roof. You can buy flowers, redecorate the living room, buy jewellery and even repair your car. The attention to detail is significant, as the game’s mechanics allow for much deeper relationships to be forced between the main characters themselves and even the NPCs.

In terms of gameplay, I have found the driving in the game to be brilliant, a massive improvement on GTA V, and it will be a big bonus for GTA VI Online whenever it arrives. The combat is heavily inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2, and the gunplay, while a bit erratic in the early missions, is quite authentic. The triple system of Health, Stamina, and Focus is great, as the quality of all of Jason and Lucia’s abilities can be improved with time. Back to it then, make sure to check the full review of GTA VI on Tuesday.

Make sure to give GTA VI a try if you aren’t already. This is the biggest gaming moment of the decade, after all.

item.title: Ten devotees injured as tents collapse atop Yadagirigutta temple hill
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Around 10 devotees, including a child, were injured after temporary tents installed for the Karthika Deepotsavam collapsed atop Yadagirigutta hill due to strong winds. The injured were shifted to hospital, while questions were raised over the decision to install the structures despite safety concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: About 10 devotees, including a child, suffered injuries after the white canopy tents, which are being installed atop Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Yadagirigutta collapsed here on Thursday.

The injured were immediately shifted to a private hospital near the bus stand, down the hill. The incident occurred around 1 pm when the devotees were having prasadam after darshan near the North Gopuram atop the hill.

The temple management was installing 30 tents for the Karthika Deepostavam to be held on Friday at the temple. This is the first time such a programme is being conducted atop the hill.

Despite the temple staff and locals expressing concern over the installation of tents, citing heavy winds, the Executive Officer (EO) J Bhavani Shankar directed the installation of the temporary tents. Accordingly, on Thursday afternoon the scaffolding and rods collapsed during peak rush, reports said.

Interestingly, the police or Special Protection Force personnel were not at the work site when the incident occurred. The fellow devotees immediately alerted the temple authorities about the injuries suffered by a few devotees, reports said.
