item.title: Sreenidi Deccan FC coach Sai Krishna clears AFC A Licence course in Punjab
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Sreenidi Deccan FC coach Sai Krishna has cleared the AFC A Licence course in Punjab, becoming the youngest candidate from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to achieve the qualification.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Mr Sai Krishna, working as a coach at Sreenidi Deccan FC, has passed the AFC A Licence course held in Punjab.

Sai Krishna is the youngest candidate from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to have cleared the course under the mentorship of Vivek Nagul (AIFF Coaches Development Head), Yan Law and Yousuf Dar.

For the record, the Hyderabadi coach has qualified as the AIFF D Licence coach in 2019, AFC C License coach in 2022 and the AFC B Licence coach in 2024 under Jeddy Almeida.

item.title: Shanaya Kapoor Laughs Off Viral ‘Everybody’s From The Village’ Trend
item.dc:creator: Ruchi Rai Agarwal
item.description: Shanaya Kapoor has reacted to the viral ‘Everybody’s from the village, Shanaya’ social media trend by sharing a humorous video of herself laughing at the memes and roast videos. The actor also referenced her show Student Of The Year: After Dark while joining the online conversation.
item.content:encoded:
Shanaya Kapoor is having a laugh at the internet’s expense, as the actor recently reacted to the viral ‘Everybody’s from the village, Shanaya’ trend that has been doing the rounds on social media.

The trend originated from a video by content creator Divyanshi Chauhan, taking a sarcastic dig at people who look down on those from villages. It calls out the notion that moving to a city or having an urban lifestyle makes someone superior, reminding people that their roots often lie in villages too. The phrase ‘Everybody’s from the village, Shanaya’ soon turned into a popular punchline, with users adapting it to mock classist attitudes and urban snobbery.

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Divyanshi Chauhan (@divivocal)


Shanaya, whose name became central to the trend, joined the conversation by sharing a video of herself listening to the roast and laughing. Reacting to the comments, she said, “I just spent six episodes trying to solve a murder, what did I do to your ancestors.”

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Shanaya Kapoor (@shanayakapoor02)

She captioned the video, “me listening to the internet roast ‘Shanaya’ while I’m just trying to get people to watch Soty After Dark.”

The actor has also teamed up with Orhan ‘Orry’ Awatramani for a transition reel that has caught the attention of social media users.

Meanwhile, Student Of The Year: After Dark, featuring Shanaya, premiered on JioHotstar on November 13, 2026.

item.title: BJP steps up poll preparations for council and municipal elections in Telangana
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Telangana BJP reviewed its preparedness for the March 2027 Legislative Council elections, focusing on organisational strengthening, coordination, and electoral strategy. Party leaders also discussed preparations for upcoming municipal polls and reiterated their goal of expanding the BJP's presence across Telangana.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Bharatiya Janata Party’s Telangana unit on Thursday reviewed the party’s preparations for the March 2027 elections to two seats of the Legislative Council.

State BJP President N. Ramchander Rao chaired the preparatory meeting at the party’s state office in the presence of Telangana BJP election in-charge Ashish Shelar. The Legislative Council Election Monitoring Committee also attended the crucial meeting.

BJP’s MLCs A.V.N. Reddy and Malka Komaraiah, as well as BJP State General Secretary Gautam Rao, were among those present during the meeting.

The discussions primarily focused on preparations for the upcoming Legislative Council elections, reviewing the party’s organisational readiness, strengthening coordination among party leaders and committee members, and formulating effective electoral strategies.

The leaders held extensive deliberations on further fortifying the party’s organisational structure at the grassroots level, streamlining election-related activities, and enhancing coordination among party leaders and workers at all levels.

Elections to the Mahabubnagar-Rangareddy-Hyderabad and Warangal-Khammam-Nalgonda Graduates’ MLC constituencies are scheduled to be held in March 2027.

Ashish Shelar and Ramchander Rao have been attending a series of meetings since Wednesday as part of the party’s preparations for the upcoming polls.

On Wednesday, they attended a meeting as part of preparations for elections to the Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri municipal corporations.

Presidents of BJP’s nine district units from the Greater Hyderabad area, state BJP Co-In-charge Abhay Patil, and Rajya Sabha member Dr K. Laxman attended the meeting.

The meeting was also attended by 300 division presidents, nine district in-charges, and district office-bearers.

Ramchander Rao said they held a comprehensive discussion on preparing the party for the upcoming municipal elections, further strengthening the party’s organisational structure at the grassroots level, and formulating future action plans and strategies needed to expand the BJP across Telangana.

He asked the party leaders to strengthen the party at the grassroots level and work towards securing the Mayor’s post in all three corporations.

The state BJP chief accused both the BRS and Congress of betraying Telangana and claimed that the people see the BJP as their only ray of hope.

He alleged that while the previous BRS government ran on 20 per cent commissions, the current Congress government has taken it to the level of 30-40 per cent.

item.title: KCR condoles demise of Telangana activist Accha Vidyasagar
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS president K Chandrashekhar Rao and party leader Vaddiraju Ravichandra condoled the death of senior Telangana movement activist Accha Vidyasagar, recalling his longstanding contribution to the Telangana statehood movement and association with the TRS.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS president and former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao condoled the demise of senior Telangana movement activist Accha Vidyasagar who passed away on Thursday. He recalled Vidayasagar’s association with the struggle since the formation of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS).

Chandrashekhar Rao said Vidyasagar played a key role in the Telangana movement centred around Warangal and described his death as a loss of a committed activist to the State. Recalling their long association since the early days of the TRS, he said Vidyasagar remained closely connected with the movement. KCR conveyed his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family.

BRS Parliamentary Party leader Vaddiraju Ravichandra also condoled the demise of Vidayasagar and recalled his contribution to the Telangana statehood movement. He said Telangana lost a strong voice and extended condolences to the bereaved family.

item.title: Govt issues show-cause notices to Nagarjuna Sagar engineers after KTR questions inaction on AP diversion
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana government has issued show-cause notices to Nagarjuna Sagar project engineers for failing to alert it about Andhra Pradesh's ongoing water diversion project. The move has sparked questions over the government's delayed response, particularly after BRS leader KT Rama Rao highlighted the issue and challenged the administration's claims of acting swiftly.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The State government’s show-cause notices to senior engineers of the Nagarjuna Sagar project for failing to report Andhra Pradesh’s ongoing water diversion project have exposed a contradiction in Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy‘s claims that the government was already aware of the project and had acted swiftly to stop it.

The notices were issued on Wednesday to the project’s Superintending Engineer and Executive Engineers, seeking their explanations within a week on why action should not be taken against them for failing to alert the government about AP’s project. The action came after BRS working president KT Rama Rao questioned how the project had escaped the attention of the Chief Minister, the Irrigation Minister and the administration.

Uttam Kumar Reddy claimed on Wednesday that the government had already lodged objections with the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB), the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Andhra Pradesh government. However, the letter to KRMB seeking intervention was sent less than a week ago, even though Andhra Pradesh began work on the project in March.

The State government’s decision to issue show-cause notices has exposed the delay in its response to the issue, which came under sharp political scrutiny after BRS working president KT Rama Rao questioned the government’s inaction. The move also raises questions over the government’s attempt to shift responsibility to field-level officials for an issue that concerns the State’s water security.

Andhra Pradesh began work in March this year on a Rs 1,200-crore project involving three intake wells on the right side of Nagarjuna Sagar and 200 tanks to draw 1.86 TMC of water for drinking needs in Palnadu district. The works have reportedly been under way for eight months.

The government is said to be unhappy that the Nagarjuna Sagar engineers failed to flag the project during this period. However, the latest action against the engineers for not reporting the project has raised more questions about the government’s own lack of monitoring and prompt response. This is in complete contradiction to the Minister’s claims of a swift response and strong action.

item.title: Newly married techie killed as tree falls on bike in Nagole
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 29-year-old Infosys software engineer was killed and his relative injured after a dried-up roadside tree collapsed on their two-wheeler near Kuntloor in Nagole. The victim, who had married recently and was set to move to Germany for a new job, died on the spot.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 29-year-old software engineer, who married a month earlier, was killed and his relative sustained injuries after a dried-up tree fell on the two-wheeler they were travelling on near Kuntloor in Nagole on Wednesday.

V. Sai Kumar, a native of Rajole in Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district of Andhra Pradesh, was residing at Sri Venkateswara Colony, Bandlaguda, Nagole. He was employed with Infosys.

According to the police, Sai Kumar was travelling with his relative, Satya Phanindra, towards a gas godown near the Outer Ring Road to book a gas cylinder when the incident occurred near Rajiv Gruhakalpa Colony at Kuntloor.

“A roadside tree suddenly collapsed and fell on Sai Kumar, leaving him critically injured. He died on the spot, while Phanindra escaped with minor injuries,” said the police.

Local residents removed the fallen tree and shifted the injured persons to a hospital.

The body of Sai Kumar was shifted to Osmania General Hospital for a postmortem examination. Sai Kumar had got married just a month ago and was scheduled to move to Germany next month after securing a job there.

Meanwhile, residents alleged that they had earlier brought the condition of several dried-up trees in the area, which posed a danger to motorists, to the attention of the authorities, but no action was taken.

item.title: Congress high command seeks report on Rajgopal Reddy’s remarks against Chief Minister
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The AICC has reportedly sought a report from the Telangana Congress leadership on Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy’s remarks against Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and the State government. His repeated criticism has triggered internal discussions within the party ahead of upcoming MLC and GHMC elections.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: With Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy’s remarks against Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy triggering political heat and pushing the Congress government on the back foot, the AICC is learnt to have sought a report from the Telangana Congress leadership on his statements.

The Munugode MLA had alleged that funds were being released only to the Chief Minister’s constituency, while other constituencies were being neglected. At a programme in Nalgonda, he had also criticised the Chief Minister’s language, particularly his remarks against opposition leaders.

The AICC is believed to have directed the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) to submit a report on Rajgopal Reddy’s remarks. Accordingly, the TPCC has shared videos of his statements and supporting reports with the high command.

The Congress MLA has repeatedly criticised the Congress government in the State. On several occasions, he has openly alleged rampant corruption, failure to fulfil electoral promises and a lack of welfare and development.

Telangana Congress leaders have raised objections to the Munugode MLA’s conduct and repeated criticism of the government. However, the TPCC has not initiated any action against him so far.

With the AICC seeking a report on the MLA’s conduct, political activity has picked up at Gandhi Bhavan.

Party leaders are recalling the suspension of Forest Minister Konda Surekha from the Cabinet following anti-party and anti-Chief Minister remarks made by her daughter, Konda Sushmitha.

Congress leaders are also concerned that Rajgopal Reddy’s repeated criticism of the State government could affect the party’s prospects in the upcoming MLC and GHMC elections.

item.title: Raja Singh backs Rajgopal Reddy’s remarks against Revanth Reddy
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BJP MLA Raja Singh backed Congress MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy's criticism of the Telangana government, alleging discrimination in the release of funds to constituencies. He claimed officials were ignoring MLAs and asserted that fund allocation during the previous BRS regime was more equitable.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Goshamahal MLA T Raja Singh has defended Congress MLA from Munugode, Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy’s remarks against Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, stating that the situation was different during the previous BRS government.

Rajgopal Reddy had criticised the State government, charging that funds were being released only to the Chief Minister’s constituency and those represented by Ministers.

Addressing a programme in Nalgonda on Wednesday, he had even warned that he would launch a war if his constituency, Munugode, was discriminated against in the release of funds.

Extending support to the Congress MLA, Raja Singh said there was nothing wrong with the allegations raised by Rajgopal Reddy.

In a video circulating on social media, the Goshamahal MLA said legislators were literally begging officials, including the HMWSSB Managing Director, for funds.

“During the previous BRS government, there were no problems with funds or communication gaps with officials. Today, officials are not listening to MLAs. There is rampant encroachment and drainage systems are overflowing,” Raja Singh said.

Adding to the legislators’ difficulties, the Municipal Commissioner was not responding to their phone calls, he alleged. Despite bringing road and pavement encroachments to the Commissioner’s notice, there had been no response, he charged.

“Rajgopal Reddy was right. A goonda administration is prevailing and corruption is rampant. Funds are being released to MLAs who are close to Revanth Reddy, while other constituencies are being deprived of funds,” Raja Singh said.

He added that although he had ideological differences with the BRS government and it did not support him, funds were released without discrimination.

“There were ideological differences with the BRS government, and it did not support us. But when it came to funds, the then Chief Minister and Municipal Administration Minister ensured that funds were released outright,” he said.

item.title: KTR slams Revanth over spending on football turf
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao accused the Revanth Reddy government of misusing public funds by allegedly spending around Rs 12 crore on facilities linked to the Chief Minister's football practice, while neglecting the needs of the poor.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao slammed the Revanth Reddy government for running a “percentage regime” rather than a people’s government.

He accused it of playing with the lives of the poor while wasting crores of public money to accommodate the Chief Minister’s football practice.

Rama Rao was reacting to allegations that nearly Rs 10 crore was spent on the football ground at the MCRHRD Institute for the Chief Minister’s practice and another Rs 2 crore on its upgradation and maintenance. He accused Revanth Reddy of spending crores of public money on personal facilities while poor people continued to face hardships.

item.title: Nine family members fall ill after eating hotel biryani in Amberpet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Nine members of a family, including four children, were hospitalised after allegedly suffering food poisoning from biryani ordered from a hotel in Amberpet. Food Safety Department officials have been alerted and are expected to investigate the incident.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Nine members of a family, including four children, reportedly fell ill after consuming biryani ordered from a hotel in Amberpet, leading to suspicions of food poisoning.

According to available information, the family members developed health complications after eating the biryani. They were subsequently rushed to the Government Fever Hospital at Nallakunta for medical treatment.

The incident came to the notice of the police, who alerted the concerned authorities.

Teams from the Food Safety Department were also informed, and they will investigate the incident to ascertain the circumstances that led to the suspected food poisoning.

Further details regarding the health condition of the affected family members and the food served by the hotel are awaited.

item.title: Congress to keep exposing system instead of shunning polls: Rahul Gandhi in US
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Rahul Gandhi said Indian democracy is sacred and the Congress will continue contesting elections despite concerns over the electoral system. Addressing students at the University of Chicago, he said boycotting polls would weaken democracy, and the party would instead keep exposing alleged flaws until people recognise the system's condition.
item.content:encoded:
Washington:  Indian democracy is “sacred” and the Congress is ready to face electoral defeats until people realise that the system has been completely demolished, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said.

Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday, Gandhi said boycotting elections over alleged flaws in the electoral system would bring an end to Indian democracy, and the Congress party does not intend to do that.

“Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof,” he said during the interaction moderated by Prof Robert Pape.

The Congress leader said asking the opposition to boycott elections would end democracy that very minute.

“But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, ‘Okay, don’t participate in the election?’ If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don’t want to end the structure of Indian democracy,” Gandhi said.

“So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished,” he said.

Gandhi was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with the students of Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday.

item.title: Several BRS leaders, workers detained ahead of Revanth Reddy’s public meeting in Siddipet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Several BRS leaders and workers were taken into preventive custody across Siddipet ahead of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy's public meeting. The opposition party alleged that over 200 workers were detained and shifted to undisclosed locations as police enforced tight security in the BRS stronghold.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Several BRS leaders and cadres were taken into preventive custody ahead of Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s public meeting scheduled to be held on Thursday evening in Siddipet town.

The police personnel in Siddipet, Gajwel, Dubbak and other constituencies took active BRS leaders and cadres into preventive custody from very early morning on Thursday to avoid any trouble during Revanth’s meeting.

However, the BRS leaders alleged that the police have shifted them to undisclosed locations. The arrested BRS leaders posted their photographs and videos on social media. A BRS party leader said that over 200 party workers were taken into custody in Siddipet town alone until 10 am.

Since Siddipet is known as a stronghold of BRS for more than two-and-a-half decades, the police literally threw the town under a security blanket by deploying thousands of police personnel to ensure the smooth conduct of Revanth Reddy’s meeting.

Many police personnel were seen moving in civil dress to monitor the movement of the BRS cadres and civilians. Following information from the Intelligence Department suggesting that the BRS cadres might create trouble during Revanth Reddy’s meeting by raising local issues during the meeting, the police took them into custody.

item.title: EPFO may discuss flexible retirement withdrawal options for subscribers
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: EPFO may consider giving subscribers greater flexibility in accessing their retirement savings, with the proposal expected to be discussed at the upcoming Central Board of Trustees meeting. The board may also deliberate on raising the minimum EPS monthly pension from Rs 1,000 to Rs 3,000.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi:  The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) may consider introducing greater flexibility in retirement withdrawals for subscribers, according to reports.

Reports said the issue is expected to come up for discussion at the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) meeting scheduled later this month. They suggest the government is exploring ways to provide subscribers with more options to access and manage their retirement savings corpus based on individual financial requirements.

The matter is expected to be discussed at the meeting of the EPFO’s Central Board of Trustees which is the apex decision-making body responsible for overseeing provident fund and pension-related policies.

However, there was no official statement from the EPFO on the reported proposals at the time of writing.

At present, EPF members can withdraw their entire provident fund corpus in a lump sum upon retirement at or after the age of 55, while eligibility for an unreduced monthly pension under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) begins at the age of 58.

For those exiting employment before attaining the retirement age, existing rules permit withdrawal of up to 75 per cent of the EPF balance after unemployment with the remaining amount available after completion of a specified period subject to prevailing regulations.

Separately, reports indicated that the CBT may also deliberate on a proposal to increase the minimum monthly pension under the Employees’ Pension Scheme from Rs 1,000 to Rs 3,000.

The EPS is funded through a portion of employers’ contributions to the provident fund system and provides post-retirement income support to workers in the organised sector.

Currently, out of the employer’s 12 per cent statutory contribution, 8.33 per cent is allocated to the pension scheme, while the remaining amount is credited to the EPF account.

The government currently provides financial support to ensure a minimum monthly pension of Rs 1,000 under the scheme where the calculated pension entitlement falls below that level.

item.title: Telangana HC hears plea seeking compensation for submerged structures by Singoor project
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: The Telangana High Court admitted a petition by Koniti Thukkaiah and 286 others seeking compensation for 208 structures allegedly submerged by the Singoor Project in Sangareddy district, including release of about Rs 3 crore.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Justice K. Sarath of the Telangana High Court has admitted a writ petition filed by Koniti Thukkaiah and 286 others seeking compensation for 208 structures allegedly submerged due to the Singoor Project in Sangareddy district.

The petitioners approached the High Court alleging that the authorities had failed to acquire the affected structures and extend compensation to their owners despite the structures being submerged in the project waters.

They contended that the failure to initiate acquisition proceedings and pay compensation in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act was illegal and arbitrary.

The petitioners further submitted that the continued inaction of the authorities violated the principles of natural justice and deprived them of their legitimate entitlement to compensation for the loss of their properties.

As an interim relief, the petitioners sought a direction to the Engineer-in-Chief, General Irrigation and CAD Department, Telangana, to examine and consider the proposal forwarded by the Chief Engineer through a letter dated May 3, 2024, seeking the release of approximately Rs. 3 crore towards compensation for the affected structures, pending disposal of the writ petition.

The petitioners urged the court to intervene and ensure that the compensation proposal was acted upon without further delay.

item.title: BJP leader’s son killed after bulldozer hits him during Akhilesh Yadav roadshow in Gorakhpur
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: A 13-year-old boy was killed after being hit by a bulldozer during Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow in Gorakhpur. The victim's father alleged the flower-showering bulldozer was moving at high speed behind the convoy when it struck the boy.
item.content:encoded:
Gorakhpur:  A 13-year-old boy was killed after being hit by a bulldozer during a Samajwadi Party (SP) roadshow led by party chief Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh’s Gorakhpur.

The body, identified as Aryavardhan Singh, was a resident of Rajdhani village in Chauri Chaura. His father is a local BJP leader.

According to the officials, the accident occurred in the Koodaghat area during the SP’s Rath Yatra.

The tragic incident has raised questions over the arrangements and crowd management during the political event.

According to the boy’s father, Omkar Singh, the bulldozer was showering flower petals on the rally when the incident occurred. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav’s convoy had already moved ahead when the bulldozer, which was approaching at high speed, struck his son from behind.

Speaking to IANS, Omkar Singh said, “Around 2 p.m., when Akhilesh Yadav’s convoy passed, my son was going to pick up his sister from Kendriya Vidyalaya. While he was crossing the road, Akhilesh Yadav’s convoy had moved ahead.”

“A flower-showering JCB was following the convoy at a very high speed so that flowers could be showered on Akhilesh Yadav from behind. During that time, my son was crossing the road when the JCB ran over him. He died on the spot,” he added.

The impact of the collision reportedly flung Aryavardhan towards a road divider, leaving him with a severe injury to the back of his head. He subsequently succumbed to his injuries.

The incident drew a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which condemned the alleged negligence and criticised the conduct of Samajwadi Party supporters during the procession.

In a statement, the UP BJP said, “In Gorakhpur, SP supporters, in their frenzy to welcome Akhilesh Yadav, took the life of an innocent 12-year-old child! The child died a painful death after being hit by a JCB during the PDA chariot procession — the result of SP supporters’ rowdiness and irresponsible behaviour.”

“This is what they’re like while out of power; imagine the havoc they’ll wreak once they come to power! Should we call them SP supporters or hooligans? Is a show of power more precious to them than an innocent child’s life?” it added.

An investigation is underway and further details are awaited.

item.title: Six killed, one injured as car falls into canal in Bihar’s Araria
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Six people were killed and one injured after a car returning from a pre-wedding tilak ceremony plunged into a canal in Bihar's Araria district when the driver allegedly lost control of the vehicle.
item.content:encoded:
Araria: Six people died, and one was injured after a car in which they were travelling fell into a canal in Bihar’s Araria district, police said on Thursday.

The accident occurred on Wednesday night on the Bidi bridge under the Tarabari Police Station limits when the driver apparently lost control of the car and the vehicle plunged into the canal, a statement issued by the Araria SP said.

The accident occurred when the vehicle was returning from a ’tilak’ ceremony, a pre-wedding programme.

A police team rushed to the spot and took all seven occupants of the car to the Araria Sadar Hospital, where six of them were declared dead, the statement said.

One person is undergoing treatment at the hospital, and his family members have arrived there, it said.

The police said the law-and-order situation in the area remains normal.

item.title: Pierce Brosnan backs Robert Pattinson as next face of James Bond franchise
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Pierce Brosnan has welcomed Robert Pattinson to the James Bond franchise, praising his career and expressing confidence that he will excel as the iconic Agent 007 in the upcoming film directed by Denis Villeneuve.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actor Pierce Brosnan has warmly welcomed Robert Pattinson as he steps into the world of James Bond.

Recalling their time together while filming ‘Remember Me’, Brosnan praised Pattinson’s journey and remarkable body of work, expressing confidence that he would be “magnificent” in the iconic Bond universe.

Sharing a picture of Pattinson, Brosnan wrote in the caption: “Pierce Brosnan: Dear Robert, Welcome to the world of Bond. You are going to be magnificent. I have fond memories of our time together making “Remember Me.” It has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength. Enjoy the ride.

He signed off his heartfelt message with “Grá mor”, translating to great love.

Pattinson has been confirmed as the next James Bond after months of speculation for the part.

The actor will be portraying the iconic British spy in the forthcoming installment of the 60-year-old franchise. The film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve of ‘Dune’ fame and scripted by Steven Knight.

The film marks the 26th title of the James Bond franchise, and Robert Pattinson, 40, will be the 8th actor to take on the role of the legendary Agent 007.

The official handle of the franchise took to their X, formerly Twitter, earlier this week and made the announcement. They shared a picture of the actor holding a gun in the signature pose of the iconic character. They wrote, “Robert Pattinson is James Bond”.

James Bond has left an indelible footprint on global cinema. It was created by British author Ian Fleming. The MI6 secret agent made his cinematic debut with Dr. No in 1962, portrayed by Sean Connery.

The franchise also popularised cinematic conventions such as elaborate opening sequences, elaborate villain lairs, technological gadgets and globe-trotting narratives, influencing generations of action filmmakers. Beyond box-office success, James Bond became a cultural export, shaping perceptions of British identity, masculinity, style and popular culture.

Its influence extends to video games, literature, fashion, advertising and music. Having reinvented itself across changing political and cultural eras, the franchise remains a remarkable example of cinema’s ability to sustain a character across generations.

item.title: Upcoming UP assembly elections will bring a deluge, not change: Azam Khan
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, released on interim bail in a money laundering case, termed the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections a "revolution, not an election". He said voters would focus on issues rather than religion and caste, while also criticising constitutional institutions and central agencies.
item.content:encoded:
Rampur (UP):  Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan has described the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections as a “revolution, not an election”, saying there would be a “deluge, not change”, after his release from jail on interim bail in a money laundering case.

“Is baar chunav nahi hoga, inkalab hoga. Badlav nahi hoga, sailab hoga (This time there will be no election, there will be a revolution. There will be no change, there will be a deluge),” Khan told reporters after reaching Rampur late Wednesday night from Ghaziabad’s Dasna jail, where he was released earlier in the day.

Khan was greeted by a large number of supporters upon his arrival in his hometown.

Speaking about his release on bail by the court, the senior SP leader said it had strengthened his belief that the country was free, but the Constitution was imprisoned.

“With all of us together, we should demand the freedom of the Constitution,” he said.

Asked about the upcoming Assembly elections, Khan said people would no longer fight in the name of religion and caste, but on issues.

“We were ready to die for the Constitution and the law; we are ready and will remain ready,” he said.

Reacting to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s remarks that Khan would get justice if the party formed the government after the elections, he said: “justice is justice, but no one would be subjected to revenge.”

Taking a dig at the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Khan said if a person accused of stealing chickens, goats and buffaloes could face the agency and build a university, he prayed that every street had a “chicken thief” who could build a university.

Khan also questioned the credibility of constitutional institutions, saying they should introspect over the declining public trust and the observations made by the high courts and the Supreme Court.

He sarcastically remarked that had the ED, CBI, Income Tax Department and development authorities existed during the time of Madan Mohan Malaviya and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, the two educationists would also have been jailed.

Earlier, reacting to Khan’s release on Wednesday evening, Yadav said the development had bolstered trust in justice.

“When oppression and high-handedness cross all limits, know that the end of those in power has arrived,” Yadav posted on X.

Khan was released from Dasna jail in Ghaziabad on Wednesday evening, a day after the Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail in a money laundering case linked to his Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.

The ED had taken him into custody on October 31 in the case. He was subsequently remanded to 14 days of judicial custody by a PMLA court in Ghaziabad.

item.title: 1st Test: New Zealand recover to 140/5 at tea despite Bumrah’s three wickets
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips steadied New Zealand with an unbeaten 80-run partnership after India reduced the hosts to 60/4, taking them to 140/5 at Tea on Day 1 of the first Test. Nicholls remained unbeaten on 66, while Phillips was on 42, with Jasprit Bumrah leading India's bowling effort with 3/31.
item.content:encoded:
Wellington: Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips produced a determined fightback to help New Zealand recover from a difficult start and reach 140/5 at Tea on Day 1 of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve here on Thursday.

After India’s pace attack reduced the hosts to 60/4 at Lunch, Nicholls and Phillips added valuable runs through a combination of solid defence and positive strokeplay, taking New Zealand through the second session with the loss of just one wicket.

Nicholls remained unbeaten on 66 off 135 deliveries, while Phillips was not out on 42 off 66 balls as the pair added an unbroken 80-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Their stand helped New Zealand regain some control after Jasprit Bumrah had struck twice in the morning and returned after the break to claim his third wicket.

India made an early breakthrough after the resumption, with Anshul Kamboj removing Tom Blundell for five. The wicket came in the 29th over when Blundell, caught between leaving and playing a short-of-length delivery angled towards the fifth-stump line, edged behind to Shubman Gill at first slip.

Bumrah had earlier dismissed Blundell’s predecessor in the morning session and continued to trouble the New Zealand batters. He had a review against Phillips in the 31st over, but the third umpire upheld the on-field not-out decision after examining the possibility of an inside edge. India subsequently lost the review.

However, Nicholls remained composed at the other end, reaching his half-century with an authoritative pull off Prasidh Krishna in the 36th over. It was his ninth score of 50 or more in 15 innings at the Basin Reserve, underlining his comfort at the venue.

Phillips, meanwhile, brought greater urgency to the partnership, finding boundaries through the off-side with confident drives and using his feet and quick running to keep the scoreboard moving. He also survived a couple of testing moments against the Indian seamers, including an inside edge that narrowly escaped the stumps.

India tried to break the stand by bringing Washington Sundar into the attack and adjusting the field with close catchers around Nicholls. But the left-hander continued to defend resolutely, while Phillips complemented him with timely scoring opportunities.

The pair added 80 runs in the session, with New Zealand scoring 80 runs for the loss of Blundell’s wicket after the Lunch break. Bumrah was India’s leading bowler with figures of 3/31, while Kamboj had 1/39 and Akash Deep 1/22 at Tea.

The surface, which had offered assistance to the seamers in the morning, appeared to ease as the sun came out. The pitch was also beginning to brown, with the post-Lunch assessment suggesting that India could have benefited from bowling a little fuller to extract greater rewards.

New Zealand will look to build on the recovery in the final session, with Nicholls and Phillips having provided the platform for a more competitive first-innings total.

Brief Scores: New Zealand 140/5 in 49 overs (Henry Nicholls 66*, Glenn Phillips 42*; Jasprit Bumrah 3-31, Akash Deep 1-22, Anshul Kamboj 1-39) against India.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim strikes on Riyadh airport, financial centre as cross-border fighting continues
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Yemen's Houthis claimed a large-scale cruise missile attack targeting Riyadh's airport and financial district in retaliation for alleged Saudi strikes in Yemen, while Saudi-led forces said they intercepted Houthi drones amid escalating cross-border hostilities.
item.content:encoded:
Sanaa: Yemen’s Houthis have said they had launched a large-scale missile attack on an airport and a financial centre in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, as the group reported that at least three people, including a child, were killed in Saudi airstrikes in central Yemen.

In a statement on social media platform X on Wednesday (local time), Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the group had fired a “large number of cruise missiles” at King Khalid International Airport and a financial centre in Riyadh, describing the operation as retaliation for what he called Saudi attacks on civilian facilities in Yemen.

Earlier in the day, Sarea said in a separate statement that Saudi aircraft and missiles had carried out 87 strikes across several parts of Yemen over the preceding 24 hours, targeting civilian facilities in the capital Sanaa and eight provinces.

Houthi-run al-Masirah TV reported that at least three people, including a child, were killed and five others injured in Saudi airstrikes in Yemen’s central province of Ibb on Wednesday, according to Xinhua news agency.

The claims could not be independently verified.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it had intercepted and destroyed two drones launched by the Houthis toward the Riyadh and southern regions of Saudi Arabia.

The announcement was made in a statement published by the coalition’s spokesperson on X, without providing further details on casualties or damage.

The reported attacks come amid intensified fighting between the Houthis and Yemen’s government forces supported by the Saudi-led coalition. The Houthis have also claimed repeated missile and drone attacks against Saudi oil infrastructure and military installations.

Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of the country’s north, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

item.title: Trilateral in Shenzhen: Trump to meet Xi and Putin amid hopes for talks on global conflicts
item.dc:creator: AP
item.description: US President Donald Trump is set to hold a trilateral meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, focusing on nuclear arms control and ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. While Trump projects confidence in his dealmaking abilities, experts remain sceptical about any major breakthroughs.
item.content:encoded:
Shenzhen: When President Donald Trump meets on Thursday with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, it could mark a pivot in world history — or become a quickly forgotten photo op.

Trump, who will test his reputation as an expert dealmaker in the trilateral meeting, has promoted his time with Xi and Putin — two of America’s leading rivals — as a chance to hash out rules for controlling nuclear arms and to start resolving the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs.

Trump plans to have a separate one-on-one meeting with Xi — his third substantial meeting with him this year — right before the trilateral. He also added a separate sit-down with Putin to his schedule, marking the first time that the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia’s war in Ukraine.

Trump has frequently boasted of his rapport with Putin, even as relations between the US and Ukraine appear to have cratered recently. Trump rejected new Russia sanctions, while Kyiv was undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones during the war.

Along for the trip — but so far keeping a low profile — is Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX has intermittently throttled the military-grade Starshield satellite system used by Ukraine for launching its drones and intercepting hits from Russia.

One meeting is unlikely to produce a breakthrough in nuclear talks

The trilateral is scheduled to occur after a session with leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit on Thursday morning and is expected to be the capstone to Trump’s Asia trip that started on Tuesday in the Philippines.

Trump has said he wants to talk to the leaders about their nuclear stockpiles. The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States, known as New START, expired in February, and Trump has said he wants “a new, improved and modernised” deal that includes China.

But China has less motivation to accept limits given that its arsenal of more than 600 warheads is many times smaller than the more than 5,000 warheads believed to be in each of the US and Russian stockpiles.

Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Arms Control Association, said Trump’s showmanship could at best start a process that would eventually lead to a sustained set of talks for reducing nuclear arsenals.

“We need more than diplomatic theater and photo opportunities between Xi, Putin, and Trump at APEC,” Kimball said. “And one meeting will not likely produce dramatic breakthroughs.”

Trump boasts about his relationships. But the ties between Xi and Putin are stronger

Putin’s foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Putin, Trump and Xi would likely touch on the war in Ukraine, though the agenda was not fully set. Trump has said he wants to discuss that war — as well as the conflict in Iran.

His ambitions recall an era of great power politics when wealthier countries felt entitled to decide the fate of seemingly lesser nations. Trump is negotiating with China and Russia without the involvement of Ukraine — or countries like Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Japan and South Korea that also have stakes in the outcome of any talks.

The US president has openly pursued a Nobel Peace Prize even as he took military action against Venezuela and Iran. He also threatened earlier this year to take Greenland by force from Denmark, a gambit that led to an agreement for the construction of US military bases.

Trump has long believed that his ability to create personal connections gives him a diplomatic edge. Xi appealed to his ego on Wednesday by greeting Air Force One on the airport tarmac, as the two leaders turned their handshake into a one-armed hug.

But Trump does not appear to always have the same deep relationship based on common interests that Xi and Putin share. For all the compliments the US president has showered on the two autocrats, the warmth has not always been mutually effusive.

On Wednesday at APEC, Xi greeted Putin by calling him “my old friend”. The Russian leader responded by declaring Xi to be his “dear friend”. China has helped to economically support Russia after its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, providing Putin with a financial lifeline after the US and its allies imposed new sanctions.

“China-Russia relations have remained steadfast through storms while taking a long-term view,” Xi said to Putin. “They have brought greater stability and certainty to a world marked by intertwined changes and turbulence.”

The pair discussed the war in Ukraine during their talks and Trump’s envoys who are trying to bring the conflict to an end, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency RIA Novosti.

By contrast, when Xi came to the White House for a state visit in September, he was far more restrained with Trump, saying they had built a “personal rapport and stayed in touch”. Trump and Xi plan to meet a total of four times this year, with their final time together coming in December at the G20 summit being held at the Trump National Doral Golf Club in Florida.

item.title: Man held for trying to forcibly enter Delhi airport’s Terminal 3 without documents
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: CISF personnel foiled an attempt by a man to forcibly enter Delhi airport's Terminal 3 without valid travel documents. The individual was swiftly apprehended with the help of the Quick Response Team, preventing a potential security breach.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) foiled an attempt by an individual to forcibly enter Terminal 3 of Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport without possessing valid travel documents, preventing a possible security breach through its swift and coordinated response.

The incident occurred at the departure gate of Terminal 3, where CISF personnel deployed for security duty noticed an individual trying to gain unauthorised access to the terminal.

Acting promptly, the security personnel intervened and apprehended the person with assistance from the force’s Quick Response Team (QRT).

According to the CISF, the individual was intercepted and brought under control within seconds of the attempted entry. The timely intervention and coordination between the personnel stationed at the departure gate and the QRT helped prevent the person from entering the restricted airport terminal without the necessary travel documents.

Sharing details of the incident in a post on X, the CISF said its personnel displayed exceptional alertness and acted swiftly after noticing the unauthorised entry attempt at the departure gate.

“Displaying exceptional alertness and prompt response, CISF personnel deployed at Departure Gate of Terminal-3, IGI Airport, swiftly apprehended an individual attempting to forcibly enter the terminal without valid travel documents,” the force said.

“With the timely assistance of QRT personnel, the individual was intercepted within seconds, preventing unauthorised entry and averting a potential security breach. The swift and coordinated action reflects the alertness, professionalism and operational preparedness of CISF personnel in safeguarding airport security,” the force said in its statement.

The CISF reiterated that its personnel remain vigilant and operationally prepared to respond to any attempt to compromise security at the airport.

Officials said that legal proceedings are underway.

Further details are awaited.

item.title: Tolichowki SHO trapped over Rs 20,000 bribe
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Anti-Corruption Bureau officials said Tolichowki SHO T. Ramesh Naik was caught accepting Rs 20,000 from a complainant for an official favour in Hyderabad. Around Rs 50,000 in unaccounted cash was also seized.
item.content:encoded:
Rs 50,000 unaccounted cash seized

Hyderabad: Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) sleuths on Wednesday evening caught Tolichowki Police Station Station House Officer (SHO) T. Ramesh Naik red-handed while demanding and accepting a Rs 20,000 bribe from a person.

Following a complaint, the ACB registered a case and trapped Naik when he accepted the amount from the complainant for an official favour, officials said.

The ACB team subsequently seized around Rs 50,000 in unaccounted money from the SHO. He is being arrested and will be produced before the court.

item.title: Democrats seek early action on Immigration Bill covering children of H-1B workers
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries has pledged to push the American Dream and Promise Act, which could provide a pathway to permanent residency for eligible children of Indian H-1B visa holders and other temporary visa workers. He said Democrats would seek passage in the current Congress or reintroduce the measure early in the next Congress if it fails to advance.
item.content:encoded:
Washington: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday pledged to advance immigration legislation that could offer permanent residency to eligible children of Indian H-1B workers, saying Congress should act immediately or Democrats would take it up early in the next Congress.

The American Dream and Promise Act would cover certain immigrants brought to the United States as children, including eligible sons and daughters of people admitted on H-1B and other specified temporary visas.

Jeffries called for passage of the measure during the current Congress, pointing to an effort by Representative Sylvia Garcia of Texas to force a House vote.

“I can guarantee you that if that doesn’t happen, we’re going to move the Dream and Promise Act in the next Congress, early in the next Congress,” he told reporters at a news conference.

The top Democratic leader who is likely to be the next Speaker of the House of Representatives made the commitment while answering a question about Temporary Protected Status for Salvadorans.

He referred specifically to DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals) and TPS (Temporary Protected Status) recipients; the relevance to H-1B families arises from provisions in the existing bill.

Asked separately whether he had spoken to President Donald Trump about an immigration agreement, Jeffries said: “Haven’t heard from the President yet.”

He described the Dream and Promise Act as a starting point for wider changes.

“We should start with the Dream and Promise Act, but that’s the beginning. That’s not the end,” he said.

For Indian families, the significant provision is the bill’s explicit inclusion of eligible children of H-1B, L, E-1 and E-2 visa holders.

H.R. 1589 would generally require applicants to have been continuously physically present in the United States since January 1, 2021, entered at age of 18 or younger.

Applicants would also have to meet education-related requirements and criminal and national security checks.

The proposal provides for conditional permanent residence lasting 10 years, with further requirements for removing those conditions.

These provisions are not law.

The issue affects young people commonly called “Documented Dreamers” — children who grow up legally in the United States as dependents of temporary visa holders but risk losing that status when they turn 21.

Those unable to obtain another lawful status may have to leave despite having spent much of their childhood in the country.

The American Immigration Council, an immigration advocacy organisation, says employment-based green-card backlogs are particularly large for people born in India and China, prolonging uncertainty for their families.

HR 1589, which seeks to bring a resolution allowing consideration of the bill to the House floor, has 217 signatures on the House Clerk’s published tally. It remains one signature short of the threshold required to advance through that procedure.

Jeffries also called for bipartisan immigration reform, saying enforcement should be fair, just and humane and the border safe and secure.

Asked whether Democrats wanted deportations stopped entirely, he said they supported deporting violent felons who harmed Americans, while accusing the administration of targeting law-abiding immigrant families.

If the immigration measure is not enacted before the current Congress ends, it must be reintroduced and begin the legislative process again.

Approval by both chambers and enactment would be necessary before families could obtain relief.

item.title: Debt burden drives electrician to suicide in Siddipet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 24-year-old electrician allegedly died by suicide in Itikyal village of Jagadevpur mandal in Siddipet district due to mounting financial difficulties. After borrowing money to build a house, he reportedly faced pressure from lenders for immediate repayment and, unable to clear the debts, ended his life.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Alleged financial troubles drove a young man, Mettu Praveen (24), to suicide at Itikyal village in Jagadevpur mandal. The deceased man, who was working as an electrician, had no house of his own.

He was married three years ago, but his wife deserted him within a month of their marriage. Since then, Praveen had been determined to build a house for himself and his family.

After borrowing money from friends and relatives, he built a house. However, the lenders reportedly demanded immediate repayment of the loans after the construction was completed.

The family owned no agricultural land. Unable to repay the loans, he died by suicide when he was alone on Tuesday evening. The police have registered a case.

item.title: SCR reschedules two express trains due to Cyclone Akvan
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: South Central Railway has rescheduled two express trains in view of Cyclone Akvan. The Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express and Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express will depart later than their scheduled timings on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: In view of Cyclone Akvan, South Central Railway (SCR) has rescheduled two express trains on Thursday.

Accordingly, the Charlapalli–Shalimar East Coast Express (18046) will depart at 3.40 pm instead of 8.40 am, while the Secunderabad–Howrah Falaknuma Express (12704) will leave at 5.55 pm instead of 3.55 pm.

The SCR authorities requested rail passengers to note the revised timings and plan their journeys accordingly.

item.title: Padmashali Employees Association extends Rs 1 lakh aid to family of civil supplies manager who died by suicide
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Padmashali Employees Association has provided financial assistance of Rs 1 lakh to the family of civil supplies manager Ananthula Lakshminarayana, who died by suicide in Bhadrachalam in October. The association urged employees facing work-related issues to seek institutional support and also demanded a comprehensive inquiry into the incident.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: Telangana Padmashali Employees Association has extended a financial aid of Rs 1 lakh to the family of civil supplies manager Ananthula Lakshminarayana, who died by suicide.

He hanged himself at a lodge in Bhadrachalam on October 17 and left a suicide note in which he held six persons, two HP Gas workers and four journalists, responsible for his death.

To support the bereaved family the association’s state president, Eega Venkateswarlu, handed over a cheque for Rs 1 lakh to Lakshminarayana’s daughter Ananthula Madhulika at a meeting in Hyderabad recently.

Speaking on the occasion, Venkateswarlu stated that the association remains steadfastly committed to the welfare of its members and to supporting their families during times of distress.

He advised employees not to make any impulsive decisions out of frustration, regardless of the difficulties, pressures or harassment they might encounter while performing their professional duties.

Venkateswarlu urged employees of the community to bring any work-related problems to the attention of the association, assuring them that the State committee would provide support with the help of its Legal Aid Committee.

The accused in the case have yet to be arrested even as the association leaders here along with Lakshminarayana’s family submitted petitions to SP B Rohith Raju and district Collector Ankit seeking a comprehensive inquiry into the incident and action against those responsible for his death.

item.title: Sangareddy police crush 200 modified silencers seized during checks
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Sangareddy police on Wednesday crushed 200 modified silencers seized from two-wheelers across the district during routine vehicle checks. Police said such silencers cause noise pollution and inconvenience road users.
item.content:encoded:
Sangareddy: Acting tough on two-wheeler riders found using modified silencers, Sangareddy police crushed 200 modified silencers with a road roller here on Wednesday. The silencers had been seized across the district during regular check-ups.

Speaking on the occasion, Sangareddy DSP Sathaiah Goud said the use of the modified silencers could create panic among fellow road users apart from troubling children, the elderly and women.

He said the police would initiate stern action against those using such silencers and also against the mechanics installing them, since the devices caused noise pollution. Traffic Inspector Ramakrishna Reddy, Town Inspector Ramu Naidu and others were present.

item.title: Man kills 80-year-old wife with spade following quarrel in Mancherial
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: An 80-year-old woman was allegedly beaten to death by her husband in Bheemaram village of Mancherial district following a domestic dispute.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: An elderly woman was murdered by her husband following a family dispute at Bheemaram village on Wednesday

Police said that Munjam Narsamma (80), a resident of the village, was beaten to death with a spade by her husband Lachchayya. Narsamma sustained severe head injuries after her husband attacked her with the spade. She suffered profuse bleeding and died on the spot.

Lachchayya entered into an argument with Narsamma and killed her in a fit of rage. He was quarrelling with her over petty issues and was allegedly addicted to liquor for a long time. Satyanarayana, Narsamma’s son, lodged a complaint with the police.

A case has been registered against Lachchayya.

item.title: Opinion: Inflation is not equal — why India needs a Distributional Inflation Index
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: One inflation rate cannot tell the whole story. India must look beyond headline CPI and introduce a Distributional Inflation Index to measure not just how much prices rise, but who bears the greatest burden
item.content:encoded:
By Dr K S Sujit

India’s inflation debate often begins and ends with a single number: the Consumer Price Index (CPI). When headline inflation rises, concerns centre on monetary tightening; when it falls, policymakers take comfort in the belief that price stability is returning. Yet an important question remains largely outside this debate: whose cost of living is actually rising, and by how much?

Inflation is measured as the average change in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services. However, households do not consume the same basket, nor do they have the same capacity to absorb price increases. A rise in the prices of essential food items has very different consequences for a low-income household that spends nearly half its consumption budget on food than for an affluent household with a substantially smaller food expenditure share.

This distinction deserves greater attention in India’s inflation policy.

The latest available figures illustrate the problem. In October 2026, India’s headline retail inflation stood at 6.09 per cent while food inflation increased more sharply to 8.94 per cent. More significantly, rural inflation stood at 6.63 per cent, compared with 5.41 per cent in urban areas. Rural food inflation was 9.09 per cent, against 8.68 per cent in urban India. These differences suggest that inflation is already experienced differently across geographical and consumption categories.

The distributional dimension becomes clearer when these figures are considered alongside the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2023–24. Food accounted for approximately 47.04 per cent of rural consumption expenditure and 39.68 per cent of urban expenditure. For households with limited disposable resources, even a modest increase in food prices can substantially reduce the resources available for education, healthcare, transport and other essential needs.

The differences in consumption capacity are equally striking. Average monthly per capita consumption expenditure among the bottom 5 per cent of rural households was Rs 1,677 in 2023–24, compared with Rs 10,137 among the top 5 per cent. In urban India, the corresponding figures were Rs 2,376 and Rs 20,310. The same increase in the price of an essential commodity cannot reasonably be assumed to impose an equivalent welfare burden on these households.

The problem, therefore, is not simply how much prices increase, but how that increase is distributed across households.

Beyond the average: A case for a Distributional Inflation Index

India has made important progress in modernising its inflation measurement framework. The revised Consumer Price Index, introduced in February 2026 with 2024 as its base year, uses expenditure weights derived from HCES 2023–24. It has expanded coverage of goods and services and improved the representation of contemporary consumption patterns. However, updating the representative consumption basket does not necessarily capture the differences in inflation experienced by households at different levels of economic well-being.

The proposed index would complement, not replace, headline CPI, giving policymakers a clearer picture of how price movements shape household consumption, savings and inflation expectations

It may be time to consider a complementary measure such as a Distributional Inflation Index (DII).

The proposed index would estimate inflation separately for different household consumption-expenditure groups rather than relying exclusively on a single representative consumption basket. Initially, households could be classified into expenditure deciles, with separate estimates for rural and urban areas. A simpler presentation could report inflation for the bottom 20 per cent, middle 60 per cent and top 20 per cent of households, while retaining more detailed decile estimates for analysis.

Each group would have its own consumption weights, reflecting the proportion of expenditure allocated to food, housing, transport, healthcare, education and other goods and services. These weights would be combined with the corresponding price movements to calculate group-specific inflation.

For example, if food accounts for a substantially larger share of expenditure among lower-consumption households, an increase in food prices would translate into a greater inflation burden for that group than for households with a more diversified consumption basket. Similarly, rising housing, education or healthcare costs could exert greater pressure on particular middle- and higher-consumption groups.

The proposal is not to replace the existing CPI or introduce another competing inflation target. Rather, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) could develop the DII as a supplementary statistical measure. The exercise need not begin from scratch. HCES already provides a statistical foundation through household consumption data and expenditure fractiles. Combining these expenditure patterns with CPI price information could make the proposed index operationally feasible.

An important methodological distinction, however, must be recognised. HCES measures household consumption expenditure rather than comprehensive household income. Therefore, expenditure deciles would initially serve as a practical proxy for economic position. Better integration of household income information into future statistical exercises could subsequently enable more precise income-based estimates.

Moreover, differences in expenditure weights alone may not capture the full variation in inflation experiences. Households may purchase different qualities of the same product, shop in different markets or face different regional prices. The methodology should, therefore, progressively incorporate more granular regional and market-level price information. This would strengthen the reliability of group-specific inflation estimates.

Distribution Matters

Such an index would offer more than an alternative statistical presentation. It could improve the quality of economic policymaking.

For the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the headline CPI must remain the principal reference for the existing inflation-targeting framework. The proposed DII need not replace it or create multiple inflation targets. Instead, it could provide supplementary information to help policymakers better understand the distributional consequences of price movements and assess how inflation affects consumption, savings and household expectations.

This distinction is important because monetary policy operates largely through aggregate demand, credit conditions and inflation expectations. It cannot directly address a temporary shortage of onions, an adverse harvest or disruptions in agricultural supply chains. For context, onion prices alone experienced an inflation rate of 116.22 per cent in October 2026. Higher interest rates cannot compensate a low-income household for such a disproportionate increase in the cost of essential food.

A distribution-sensitive approach would help policymakers distinguish between broad-based demand pressures and price increases concentrated in essential commodities. The latter may require more targeted responses, including better agricultural supply-chain management, improved storage facilities, timely market interventions and appropriately designed social protection measures.

Fiscal policy could also benefit. Government transfers, food subsidies, wage revisions and social protection programmes could be assessed against the inflation experienced by their intended beneficiaries. A distributional inflation measure could also inform discussions on dearness allowance, pension adjustments and the adequacy of welfare transfers.

Beyond price movements, policymakers should examine their consequences for household welfare. When food prices rise, lower-income households may reduce dietary diversity, substitute cheaper food items or cut expenditure on other essentials. A household may, therefore, maintain its consumption budget while experiencing a deterioration in nutritional quality and living standards. This suggests that inflation measurement should be complemented by indicators of essential consumption affordability and real purchasing power.

From Price Stability to Household Welfare

There is a broader economic argument here. Inflation is not merely a monetary phenomenon; it is also a question of purchasing power and economic welfare. Two households facing the same national inflation rate may experience very different reductions in their real standard of living.

International research has already examined differences in inflation across household income groups, including work by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics. India has an opportunity to develop its own framework using its extensive household consumption surveys and expanding price collection system.

The framework should be more sensitive to the distribution of economic costs.

Price stability is a macroeconomic achievement. But equitable protection of purchasing power is a broader economic and social objective. Measuring the first without adequately understanding the second leaves an important gap in India’s policy framework.

 

(The author is Professor, School of Business and Management Bangalore Central Campus, CHRIST [Deemed to be University])

item.title: Hyderabad: Indian Road Congress to focus on climate-resilient infrastructure, new technologies
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The 85th Indian Roads Congress (IRC) conference will begin in Hyderabad on Thursday, focusing on environment-friendly road construction, climate-resilient infrastructure, AI, digital technology, electric vehicles and modern transport systems.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The 85th Indian Roads Congress (IRC), beginning here on Thursday, will focus on environment-friendly road construction, climate-resilient infrastructure and new technologies.

Telangana Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said on Wednesday the four-day prestigious conference will bring together around 3,500 delegates, including road and highway experts, engineers, government officials and representatives from the infrastructure industry across the country.

He stated that this year’s conference would focus on several emerging and important areas, including environment-friendly road construction, climate-resilient infrastructure, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Digital Technology, Electric Vehicles, modern transportation systems and innovative construction methodologies. A special panel discussion on “Right to Walk”, highlighting every individual’s right to safe pedestrian movement, will also be organised.

Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari will inaugurate the conference. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka, Union Ministers from Telangana, Ministers from other States, Members of Parliament and other prominent personalities are expected to participate.

Addressing a press conference, Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said that the government’s primary objective was the overall development of Telangana. The State is working with everyone, irrespective of political differences, to accelerate development, he said.

The Indian Roads Congress, established in 1934, has played a significant role in the development of roads and bridges across the country, particularly in improving construction quality, road safety standards and the adoption of modern technologies. Hyderabad has hosted the IRC six times in the past. The conferences were held in 1938 (4th IRC), 1959 (23rd IRC), 1976 (36th IRC), 1987 (47th IRC), 1999 (59th IRC) and 2016 (77th IRC). The 85th edition will mark the seventh occasion that Hyderabad hosts this prestigious event and the second after the formation of Telangana State.

Following the inauguration, Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy will jointly review Telangana’s road infrastructure and various major projects being undertaken by the State Government.

Highlighting the Government’s commitment to strengthening road infrastructure, Minister Komatireddy said that ₹5,677 crore had been allocated for roads and bridges in the 2026–27 State Budget. He said that improved connectivity is essential to support the growing industrial, commercial and urban development across Telangana.

He stated that the Government is giving priority to several major infrastructure projects, including the Regional Ring Road (RRR), expansion of the Hyderabad–Vijayawada Highway, Hyderabad Elevated Corridor, Future City–Machilipatnam Port Greenfield Highway, development of NH-167, Karimnagar–Warangal Highway and rural road development under the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM).

He said that completion of these projects will significantly improve connectivity between Hyderabad and other parts of the State, facilitate the expansion of industries, attract investments and generate employment opportunities. Better roads will also help farmers transport agricultural produce to markets more efficiently, enable industries to move goods with ease and reduce travel time and transportation costs for the general public.

item.title: Editorial: Tread cautiously on data centres
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Growing global resistance to data centres over their water and energy consumption offers India an important warning, even as several States compete to attract data-centre investments
item.content:encoded:
One of the key messages from the recent midterm elections in the United States was the strong voter backlash against the establishment of data centres in local communities, largely because of environmental concerns. Candidates who campaigned vigorously against these projects emerged victorious. This emphatic public rejection in a country regarded as a global technology powerhouse should serve as a wake-up call for India, where several States are competing to attract data-centre investments. Beyond the US, several European countries have also witnessed growing opposition to such projects. Public resistance is primarily driven by concerns over their impact on local resources, as data centres are massive consumers of water and electricity. In Texas, anxiety among farmers about dwindling water supplies has become a significant political issue. Similar resistance across several American States demonstrates that residents increasingly want a say in decisions that directly affect their lives. Undoubtedly, the rapid expansion of data centres, fuelled by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, presents enormous economic opportunities. However, growing opposition to these projects in developed countries offers an important warning: technological progress should not come at the expense of communities or the environment. India faces a paradox. The need to rapidly expand data-centre capacity to support AI and cloud-computing infrastructure is colliding with the imperatives of environmental protection. States such as Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana stand at a critical crossroads. Ambitious investment drives, including major data-centre proposals, could strengthen digital infrastructure and generate employment. Yet they must balance the goal of promoting the technology industry with the need to safeguard local resources and ecosystems.

Companies must, therefore, prioritise responsible resource-management practices. Every data-centre project must strike a balance between three essential interests: business, community and the environment. Firms should invest in energy-efficient technologies, renewable power, sustainable cooling systems and, wherever feasible, zero-water technologies. Equally important, residents must be provided with clear information about resource consumption, environmental impacts and economic benefits before projects receive approval. Communities should be treated as stakeholders in development rather than passive observers. Data centres can power India’s digital future, but their success should be measured not only by investment figures and computing capacity, but also by the jobs created, resources conserved and communities empowered. Progress must benefit everyone, not just technology giants. As major technology companies race to expand data-centre capacity to support AI, resource consumption is rising, exacerbating the challenges faced by communities already grappling with water scarcity. For instance, the daily water requirement of a 100-megawatt data centre is equivalent to the needs of approximately 6,500 households. India’s growing data-centre ecosystem could consume nearly 37.5 billion litres of water annually, equivalent to the yearly needs of around 7 to 8 lakh people, based on urban consumption norms prescribed by the Central Public Health and Environmental Engineering Organisation.

item.title: Hyderabad Yacht Club wins World Sailing award
item.dc:creator: VV Subrahmanyam
item.category: World Sailing 11th Hour Racing Impact Award
item.description: The Yacht Club of Hyderabad won the 2026 World Sailing 11th Hour Racing Impact Award in Qingdao, China, for its free sailing programme supporting children from economically disadvantaged communities, President Suheim Sheikh said.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: In a historic development in Indian water sports, the Yacht Club of Hyderabad won the 2026 World Sailing 11th Hour Racing Impact Award in Qingdao (China) on Wednesday.

Suheim Sheikh, the untiring President of YCH founded in 2009, said they had been creating life-changing opportunities for children from economically disadvantaged communities in India.

“Through its free programme, the club provides sailing instruction, equipment, transport, education, nutrition and healthcare, and removing financial barriers to participation,” Suheim Sheikh said.

“Since 2014, more than 2,000 children have received training, with sailors achieving 323 national and 29 international medals and representing India at major international competitions,” he said.

“Beyond sporting success, the programme supports education, personal development and pathways into employment, including careers in the armed forces and sailing industry. By combining competitive sailing with long-term social support, the club aims to help young people build brighter futures regardless of their background,” the proud sailing coach with more than three decades of service to the sport said.

The jubilant Suheim Sheikh said: ” From opening up sailing to underprivileged young people to championing inclusivity and helping restore Hussain Sagar Lake, the club is making a real difference on and off the water!”.
