“This is the first time in the history of Indian Sailing that an Indian organisation had been shortlisted for this award. This recognition is not just about the club but about the children, their journey and the opportunities we have been able to create for them,” Suheim said.

Among those who took part in the club’s campaign for public voting for the award were former international cricketer VVS Laxman, well known cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle.

“I dedicate this to each and every sailor who put in such great efforts to win laurels despite many challenges,” Suheim said. “I am also grateful to everyone including the State Government and all those officials who helped me over the years and also the support staff but for whom this Award would not have been possible,” Suheim said.

The Racing Impact Award is the highest recognition of success in marine sustainability. The winners receive an iconic trophy, made from recycled carbon fibre sourced from an America’s Cup boat and infused with bio-resin. Public voting was introduced in 2020 to engage with the wider international sailing community.

In short

  • The Yacht Club of Hyderabad won the 2026 World Sailing 11th Hour Racing Impact Award in Qingdao, China.
  • The club’s free programme provides sailing training, equipment, transport, education, nutrition and healthcare for children from economically disadvantaged communities.
  • Since 2014, more than 2,000 children have trained with the club and won 323 national and 29 international medals, Suheim Sheikh said.

Readers ask

What award did the Yacht Club of Hyderabad win?

The club won the 2026 World Sailing 11th Hour Racing Impact Award in Qingdao, China.

How does the club support children through sailing?

Its free programme provides sailing instruction, equipment, transport, education, nutrition and healthcare, Suheim Sheikh said.

What has the programme achieved since 2014?

More than 2,000 children have received training, with sailors winning 323 national and 29 international medals, Sheikh said.

item.title: Andhra gears up for surge in power demand; Naidu orders enhanced preparedness
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to bolster power sector preparedness as the state's peak electricity demand is projected to reach 14,852 MW in the next six months. The government is simultaneously pushing major renewable energy and transmission projects in the state.
item.content:encoded:
Amaravati: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday directed officials to strengthen preparedness to meet the anticipated rise in electricity consumption, with peak demand projected to touch 14,852 MW over the next six months.

Power consumption in the state increased by 18.23 percent between April and November compared with the corresponding period last year, with officials attributing the unexpected rise to the impact of El Nino.

“Officials should strengthen preparations to meet the anticipated rise in electricity demand, which is projected to reach 14,852 MW over the next six months,” the CM said in an official press release.

Naidu reviewed the Energy Department’s performance at his camp office, discussing the demand-supply position, investments, ongoing projects, renewable energy transmission infrastructure, pumped storage facilities and electric vehicle charging stations.

Further, the review also covered investments secured during the recent CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam and measures to accelerate the implementation of projects announced in the energy sector, it said.

Officials informed the chief minister that plans were being drawn up under Green Energy Corridor-III to establish a major electricity transmission network across Andhra Pradesh at an estimated cost of Rs 21,838 crore.

The proposed corridor is expected to facilitate the transmission of 47 GW of renewable energy, while pumped storage projects with a combined proposed capacity of 36,050 MW are being planned across the state.

As many as 27 potential sites for pumped storage projects have been identified in the Polavaram region as part of the proposed capacity expansion.

Since June 2024, approvals have been granted for 103 energy-sector projects involving investments of Rs 4.2 lakh crore, officials said.

Investment agreements worth Rs 2.5 lakh crore were also signed in the energy sector during the CII Partnership Summit held in Visakhapatnam.

The government is planning to install rooftop solar systems in 2,962 government welfare schools and hostels to reduce their dependence on conventional electricity.

Andhra Pradesh currently ranks fourth nationally in implementing the PM Surya Ghar scheme, with more than 7.42 lakh rooftop solar installations completed. The state has set a target of providing nine lakh connections by the end of November, according to the press release.

Progress is also underway on solar power plants with a combined capacity of 1,162 MW at 224 locations under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) scheme.

Officials informed Naidu that land acquisition for these projects had been completed, while civil works had reached 91 percent progress.

item.title: IFL: Sreenidi Deccan FC draws 2-2 against FC Bengaluru United
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Sreenidi Deccan FC drew 2-2 with FC Bengaluru United in Bengaluru on Wednesday, with Lalromawia and David Castaneda scoring for the Deccan Warriors in the Indian Football League Matchweek 4 clash.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Sreenidi Deccan FC secured another crucial point on the road in Matchweek 4 of the Indian Football League (IFL), playing out a 2-2 draw against debutants FC Bengaluru United in Bengaluru on Wednesday.

Tareck opened the scoring for the hosts, but Lalromawia brought the Deccan Warriors back on level terms in the 27th minute.

David Castaneda then scored in the 42nd minute to give Sreenidi Deccan FC the lead heading into the break. However, Naocha Singh equalised for the hosts in the 48th minute.

Head Coach Antonio Rueda made four changes to his starting XI, with Bhaskar Roy replacing Kamaljit Singh in goal. Deepak DP made his first start of the league campaign, replacing Gurmukh Singh.

Midfielders Ajay Chhetri and Brandon Vanlalremdika started ahead of Lalthankhuma and Jerry Mawia, respectively, while Victor Teister came in for Pape Gassama.

The Deccan Warriors started the game positively, creating early opportunities, although their attempts from set pieces failed to trouble the hosts' defence. However, against the run of play, FC Bengaluru United took the lead in the fifth minute when Tareck's header found the back of the net at the far post.

Having gone a goal down, the Deccan Warriors fought their way back into the contest and were rewarded in the 27th minute. Nishu Kumar's lofted ball found David Castaneda, who laid it into the path of an advancing Lalromawia. The Mizo midfielder made no mistake, slotting the ball into the back of the net to restore parity.

The Deccan Warriors continued to press forward and were rewarded once again in the 42nd minute. This time, David Castaneda rose to meet Nishu Kumar's cross from the left and headed the ball into the back of the net to give Sreenidi Deccan FC the lead heading into half-time.

However, the hosts responded shortly after the restart, with Naocha Singh heading home from close range at the far post in the 48th minute to bring FC Bengaluru United back on level terms.

The Deccan Warriors made attacking changes in search of a winner and continued to create opportunities in the closing stages. Despite their efforts and attacking intent, they were unable to find the decisive goal, as the match ended in a 2-2 draw.

Sreenidi Deccan FC will now return home to face Chanmari FC on November 24 at the Deccan Arena.

In short

  • Sreenidi Deccan FC played out a 2-2 draw against FC Bengaluru United in Bengaluru.
  • Lalromawia and David Castaneda scored as Sreenidi Deccan FC took a first-half lead.
  • Naocha Singh equalised in the 48th minute as the hosts earned a point.

Readers ask

What was the result of Sreenidi Deccan FC's match against FC Bengaluru United?

Sreenidi Deccan FC drew 2-2 with FC Bengaluru United in Bengaluru on Wednesday.

Who scored for Sreenidi Deccan FC?

Lalromawia scored in the 27th minute and David Castaneda scored in the 42nd minute.

Who will Sreenidi Deccan FC play next?

Sreenidi Deccan FC will face Chanmari FC on November 24 at the Deccan Arena.

item.title: Tolichowki SHO caught red-handed taking Rs 20,000 bribe
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Wednesday trapped the Station House Officer (SHO) of Tolichowki police station in Hyderabad while allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs 20,000 from a complainant for official favours.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) sleuths on Wednesday evening caught the Station House Officer (SHO) of Tolichowki police station red-handed when he demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 20,000 from an individual.

Based on a complaint, the ACB registered a case and trapped the police officer, T Ramesh Naik, while he was accepting the amount from the complainant for official favours.

The ACB team also seized around Rs 50,000 in unaccounted money from the official. He is being arrested and will be produced before court.

item.title: Hyderabad’s Praanjala ranked ninth among India’s junior badminton players
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad's 17-year-old badminton player Praanjala Nisarga won silver at the Czech Junior Orlova International and bronze at the Yonex Polish International. Ranked No. 44 in world juniors, she aims to break into the global top 25 by December
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Praanjala Nisarga put up an impressive performance, winning a silver medal at the Czech Junior Orlova International Badminton Championship and a bronze at the Yonex Polish International Championship.

The 17-year-old Hyderabad-based shuttler currently holds the world junior ranking of No. 44 and is the ninth-highest-ranked junior player in the country.

For the record, the talented Praanjala has won medals in the last three BWF tournaments she has participated in, besides winning the State under-15 and under-17 titles during her career.

“My target is to break into the top 25 in the world by the end of December,” Praanjala told Telangana Today.

item.title: Hyderabad doctor secures affordable rare disease drug for seven children with AHDS
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A Hyderabad-based paediatrician, Dr Sivaranjani Santosh, has facilitated access to affordable Tiratricol treatment for seven children suffering from the rare genetic disorder Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS). The initiative, supported by Access to Medicines India and the Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation, has significantly reduced treatment costs for the patients’ families.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: In a relief for families battling rare genetic disorders, city-based paediatrician Dr Sivaranjani Santosh, alongside Access to Medicines India, is set to hand over life-saving medication to seven children suffering from Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS) on November 30.

The medicine, Tiratricol, crucial for managing the rare MCT8 deficiency affecting thyroid hormone transport into brain cells, has been custom-compounded by a Netherlands-based pharmacy through the Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF).

While commercial variants of the medicine cost an astronomical Rs 4.68 crore to Rs 9 crore annually, the compassionate batch for the children, sourced by a senior Hyderabad-based paediatrician, costs roughly Rs 2.5 lakh per child per year.

The breakthrough followed an extensive social media advocacy campaign launched by Dr Sivaranjani after her young patient, Arav, struggled to sustain monthly import costs of Rs 12 lakh to Rs 13 lakh from Germany.

The appeal caught the attention of PAF, paving the way for cost-effective pharmaceutical compounding. Beneficiaries include children under Dr Sivaranjani’s care and five patients identified at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore.

While individual import permits have been secured for a year, healthcare advocates said that relying on foreign imports is unsustainable. Dr Sivaranjani plans to urge the Union government to encourage domestic production, aiming to make treatment permanently affordable for all children nationwide.

item.title: Keystone beat Central GST 65-63 in GM Sampath basketball championship
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Keystone Basketball Academy rallied from a six-point halftime deficit to beat Central GST & Customs 65-63 at YMCA Secunderabad, while St. Francis Boys defeated Sanathnagar Playground 77-73 in the annual league championship.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Keystone Basketball Academy pulled off a thrilling 65 – 63 win over Central GST & Customs after trailing 29 – 35 at half time in the GM Sampath Kumar annual league basketball championship at YMCA Secunderabad.

Central GST & Custom started well with Vijay & Harish playing in tandem. With Kiran Kumar closing the 1st quarter with a 3-pointer scored 15 points.

Karan Deo scored a brace and with Sushi tanking a three-pointer kept Keystone BA within striking distance as Central GST took the firstt quarter 15 – 11.

In the second quarter Harish continued the same rhythm and with Venkat Reddy scoring nine points Central GST added a massive 20 points to their score. Keystone BA too kept the pace with two three-pointers and Subhash scoring six consecutive points added 18 points making it a 6 point game as Central GST led 35 – 29 at half time.

After a change of ends Keystone BA tightened their defense restricting Central GST to just 11 points and playing a fast paced game scored 19 points with Pranav nine points to take a 2 point lead. Vinay of Central GST scored a three-pointer to close the three quarter and reduce the deficit to just two points at 46 – 48.

In the fiercely contested last quarter Vijay scored a three-pointer to take a one point lead, but Pranav responded with a three-pointer to get back the lead. Thereafter there were many lead changes.

With 28 seconds left for the match scores were level 62 – 62. Subhash converted a free throw and Pranav scored through a drive-in to make it 65 – 62.

With just one second left for the match Vinay of Central GST was fouled and awarded three free throws, however he could manage to convert only 1 free throw, thereby Keystone BA winning the match 65 – 63.

In another match St. Francis Boys continued their good form from Level-II to score their second consecutive win in Level-I as they trounced Sanathnagar Playground 77 – 73 after leading 47 – 39 at half time.

The scores: Keystone BA 65 (Pranav 19, Subhash 13, Karan 12, Shreyank 9) bt Central GST 63 (Vijay- 19, Venkat Reddy 19, Harish 12).

St. Francis Boys 77 (Peter 36. Nitish 11, Shoai 10, Balu 10) bt Sanathnagar PG 73 (Sudershan 23, Bharath 23, Tashvik-10).

In short

  • Keystone Basketball Academy beat Central GST & Customs 65-63 after trailing 29-35 at half time.
  • Pranav scored 19 points for Keystone BA, while Subhash added 13 points.
  • St. Francis Boys defeated Sanathnagar Playground 77-73 for their second consecutive Level-I win.

Readers ask

How did Keystone Basketball Academy win?

Keystone BA tightened their defence after half time and scored 19 points in the third quarter to take the lead before winning 65-63.

Who were the top scorers in the Keystone BA match?

Pranav scored 19 points for Keystone BA, while Vijay and Venkat Reddy scored 19 points each for Central GST.

What was the result of the other match?

St. Francis Boys beat Sanathnagar Playground 77-73 after leading 47-39 at half time.

item.title: VKCM contract workers call off strike after talks with contractor in Kothagudem
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: VK Coal Mine Contract Workers JAC
item.description: The nine-day strike by contract workers engaged at the VKCM opencast mine in Kothagudem was temporarily withdrawn following discussions between the workers' Joint Action Committee (JAC), the contractor and SCCL officials. Fresh talks are expected within 15 to 20 days to arrive at a final settlement.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: The strike by contract workers hired by Shodha Constructions Private Limited for overburden removal and coal extraction at the VKCM opencast mine in the Kothagudem area has been called off temporarily, after nine days.

It may be recalled that the contract workers under the banner of VK Coal Mine Contract Workers JAC went on strike on November 10 over payment of 20 percent annual bonus after several rounds talks with the contracting agency failed.

Discussions were held on Wednesday between the JAC and representatives of Shodha Constructions in the presence of SCCL Kothagudem Area General Manager Ch. Venkata Ramana. The contracting agency agreed to address several of the demands put forward by the workers.

The agreement includes an additional bonus over and above the standard 8.33 percent bonus, double-master wages for work on Sundays, an eight-hour workday, the reinstatement of four terminated JAC leaders and an assurance not to dismiss any worker who took part in the strike.

It was also agreed that the workers’ issues would be discussed again in the presence of the SCCL GM to reach a comprehensive and final resolution within 15 to 20 days. Trade union leaders Gattaiah, Kapu Krishna, Razak, Gadipalli Krishna Prasad, CPI leader Sabir Pasha and others were present.

item.title: Mahabubabad sarpanch caught taking first instalment of Rs 13 lakh bribe: ACB
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A sarpanch from Mahabubabad district was caught by the Anti-Corruption Bureau while allegedly accepting Rs 2 lakh as the first instalment of a Rs 13 lakh bribe.
item.content:encoded:
Mahabubabad: The sarpanch of Modhugadda thanda of Seerole mandal in the district was caught in a bribe case following a complaint by Khammam-based granite industry operators.

The accused, Daravath Veeru, was caught by the Warangal ACB team at the complainant’s office in Khammam on Wednesday while accepting Rs 2 lakh as the first installment of Rs 13 lakh bribe he had demanded.

He initially demanded Rs 30 lakh and later reduced the amount to Rs 13 for ensuring that the quarry operations of Sharada Stonex, Premier Granites and Rasi Granites were not disturbed and for facilitating the smooth functioning of their granite business.

The tainted money was recovered; the sarpanch would be arrested and produced before the special court for SPE and ACB cases in Warangal for judicial remand. The case is under investigation, according to an official release.

item.title: Woman critically injured after jumping from under-construction building in Nirmal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A woman sustained critical injuries after allegedly attempting suicide by jumping from the fourth floor of an under-construction building in Nirmal district on Wednesday. Despite efforts by Sakhi counsellors, locals and her mother to dissuade her, she leapt from the building.
item.content:encoded:
Nirmal: A woman sustained serious injuries after she allegedly attempted suicide by jumping off a multi-storied building following family disputes in public view here on Wednesday.

A video of the incident has since gone viral on social media platforms.

Police said that Pravallika alias Sangeetha from Laxmipur received critical injuries when she attempted to kill herself. She was initially shifted to a hospital in Nirmal. She was later rushed to RIMS-Adilabad after her condition deteriorated. Her condition was reported to be serious.

Pravallika was counselled by staffers of Sakhi, a one-stop centre for women in distress before the mishap occurred. She climbed to the fourth floor of an under-construction building. She leapt even as locals and her mother tried to dissuade her from taking the step. In a video clip widely shared on WhatsApp, some people were seen trying to approach her, but in vain.

Laxmi, the mother of the woman, alleged that Pravallika was being subjected to mental and physical harassment by her husband and in-laws for quite a long time. She accused her son-in-law of suspecting Pravallika’s fidelity. Pravallika has two children.

item.title: Uttam Kumar Reddy’s counter to KTR heavy on BRS criticism, light on Andhra project action
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy defended the state government's stand against Andhra Pradesh's proposed Krishna water diversion project, saying objections had been raised with the KRMB, the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti and the AP government.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy’s attempt to counter BRS working president KT Rama Rao over Andhra Pradesh’s proposed diversion of Krishna water largely focused on attacking the previous BRS government and rebutting his remarks.

Except for raising the issue with the Centre and Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) only last week, the ruling Congress appears to have taken no concrete action to stop the works.

Uttam Kumar Reddy claimed that Telangana would not compromise on its water rights and had already raised objections with the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB), the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Andhra Pradesh government over the latter’s proposed 1.8 TMCft drinking water scheme from Nagarjuna Sagar.

He accused the previous regime of spending Rs 1.83 lakh crore on irrigation in ten years without completing a major project in the Krishna basin and neglecting schemes benefiting Mahabubnagar and Nalgonda districts.

The Irrigation Minister cited expenditure of Rs 89,794 crore on Kaleshwaram against Rs 27,513 crore on the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme (PRLIS).

He alleged that changes in the location and design of projects, including shifting the focus from Tummidihatti to Medigadda and from Jurala to Srisailam, escalated costs and delayed PRLIS. He also pointed out that the project’s detailed project report was submitted only in 2022, eight years after it was announced.

He argued that the previous BRS government delayed the PRLIS, highlighting what he described as a disparity in priority between the two projects. Kaleshwaram secured permissions and was completed in a relatively short period, while PRLIS remained delayed. The Minister did not explain why the Congress government had failed to make substantial progress on the scheme after assuming office.

Uttam Kumar Reddy also accused BRS chief and former Chief Minister K Chandrashekhar Rao of accepting a 34 per cent share for Telangana in the earlier Krishna water-sharing arrangement. He claimed that the Congress government was now seeking 71 per cent. He said Telangana had utilised 108 TMCft against AP’s 98.16 TMCft this year.

Reacting to KT Rama Rao’s comments on Sonia Gandhi’s autobiography. He said her role in the formation of Telangana mattered more than whether the State figured in the book, accusing the BRS leadership of ingratitude.

item.title: BRS slams Siddipet civic body for removing its banners, ignoring Congress flexis
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A controversy has erupted in Siddipet after BRS leaders alleged that municipal officials selectively removed the party's flexi banners ahead of Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy's public meeting while ignoring similar banners put up by Congress leaders.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Double standards of Siddipet municipal officials came to the fore a day ahead of Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy’s public meeting.

The civic officials removed the BRS flexi banners installed by a petty shop owner on his pushcart in the town. Interestingly, Congress leaders had installed similar flexi banners close to the same place, but the civic officials turned a blind eye to them.

When BRS leaders questioned the double standards and demanded that the officials also remove the Congress party’s flexi banners, the officials reportedly refused to act. They continued removing BRS flexi banners across the town while ignoring the grand old party banners. An official was reportedly heard saying they were acting on directions from higher authorities.

The BRS cadres, who recorded videos of the entire episode, posted them on social media. Netizens criticised the civic officials for allegedly acting at the behest of the Congress leaders.

item.title: Flexi banners question Siddipet projects ahead of Revanth’s public meeting
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Several flexi banners questioning the Congress government's alleged neglect of Siddipet's development appeared across the town on Wednesday, a day before Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy's public meeting. The banners criticised the shifting of the Government Veterinary College to Kodangal and the suspension of funds for Komati Cheruvu development.
item.content:encoded:
Siddipet: Several flexi banners questioning the neglect of the Siddipet development, purportedly on behalf of Siddipet students, tourism enthusiasts and other responsible citizens, have surfaced in Siddipet on Wednesday a day before the public meeting of the Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy in town.

Questioning the government’s decision to shift the Government Veterinary College sanctioned for Siddipet, some students installed flexi banners with a photograph of the incomplete veterinary college building. The government shifted the veterinary college to Kodangal after coming to power.

Another flexi banner questioned the government’s decision to suspend funds granted for the development of Komati Cheruvu, where former minister and local MLA had planned to build Shilparamam and Necklace Road along the lake.

In the name of tourism lovers, some people installed a flexi banner that also highlighted how the senior BRS leader T Harish Rao developed the lake into one of the most sought after tourist destinations.

The citizens also installed multiple such flexi banners questioning the lack of development activity in Siddipet after Congress came to power. The banners were installed along the way that leads to the Chief Minister’s public meeting venue.

item.title: Raina says Dhoni tried hard to stay fit but knee problems took a toll
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Suresh Raina said recurring knee problems forced Mahendra Singh Dhoni to end his IPL playing career. The former CSK teammate said Dhoni had tried hard to regain fitness but could no longer cope with the physical workload
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s recurring knee problems forced him to call time on his IPL playing career, said his longtime Chennai Super Kings (CSK) teammate Suresh Raina.

Dhoni will now be part of CSK as a mentor. His decision was along expected lines, considering he was not fit enough to play the entire IPL 2026 season.

“Mahi bhai has been playing different sports in the off-season, but he has been struggling with his knees. Both his knees are swollen now. The amount of wicketkeeping he has done and the number of matches he has played have taken a toll,” Raina told JioStar.

“He was trying until now, thinking he would get fit. He was trying very, very hard in the gym. Despite the swelling, he always said in interviews that he never wanted to be an Impact Player.

“That speaks volumes about him as a captain and shows a lot of courage. He wanted to continue playing, but his body is not able to take that load anymore.”

Raina called Dhoni the biggest brand in the IPL.

“He has done so much for CSK and for the IPL. The amount of love he has received from fans, business tycoons, CEOs and children since 2008 has been amazing.

“If CSK have lasted so many years, it is because of Mahi bhai and the support he has received from the Whistle Podu Army. He has also done really well with Stephen Fleming.

“I think he has done remarkably well as a player and as a human being, and he is the biggest brand in the IPL to date. He has played in the IPL for so many years and become such a big player, but I think what we have learnt from him as a human being matters even more,” said the former India batter.

item.title: Sabarimala steps up waste management with 1,000-member Vishuddhi Sena
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: A 1,000-member Vishuddhi Sena has been deployed at Sabarimala and other pilgrimage centres to manage waste during the Mandalam season. The sanitation force will work round the clock until the Makaravilakku festival in January
item.content:encoded:
Pathanamthitta: A 1,000-member sanitation force has been deployed at Sabarimala and other pilgrimage centres to maintain cleanliness during the Mandalam season at the Lord Ayyappa temple.

The sanitation workforce, known as the ‘Vishuddhi Sena’, has been mobilised by the Sanitation Society to keep Nilakkal, Pampa, Sannidhanam (temple complex) and other pilgrimage centres clean and free of waste.

The society, chaired by Pathanamthitta District Collector A Nizamuddin, with the Adoor Revenue Divisional Officer as its member secretary, is coordinating the operations, according to a statement.

Of the 1,000 workers, 300 have been deployed at Sannidhanam, 250 at Pampa, 420 at Nilakkal, 20 at Pandalam and 10 at Kulanada to undertake cleaning and waste management activities.

Most of the workers have arrived from Salem in Tamil Nadu with the assistance of the Ayyappa Seva Sangham, the statement said.

Their primary responsibility is to ensure the timely collection and removal of plastic and biodegradable waste from Sabarimala and the surrounding areas.

The Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB), which manages the hill temple, has installed waste bins in front of shops and at several points along the pilgrims’ routes.

Signboards have also been put up, directing devotees to segregate biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste and dispose of it in designated bins.

At Sannidhanam, cleaning operations have been divided into 15 segments, with workers assigned specific areas, Sannidhanam duty magistrate M Bipin Kumar said.

The duty magistrate monitors the daily progress of the cleaning operations, while the District Collector has appointed a segment officer for each of the 15 divisions.

The officers are appointed on a rotational basis, with each tenure lasting 10 days.

The waste bins are cleared by Vishuddhi Sena workers as and when they are filled. Five tractors have been provided for waste removal under the supervision of the Adoor RDO, the statement said.

Devaswom Board president K Jayakumar told a recent review meeting that the board was prepared to provide additional tractors depending on the volume of waste generated and the increase in pilgrim footfall.

The deployment of the 1,000-member sanitation force will continue until the Makaravilakku festival in January. The workers have been provided with uniforms, boots, slippers, gloves, soap and coconut oil.

Their services will be available round the clock throughout the pilgrimage period, the authorities said.

The Mandalam pilgrimage season at the Lord Ayyappa temple commenced on Tuesday.

item.title: TGPSC imposes Rs 500 fee per question for answer key objections
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Public Service Commission (TGPSC) has introduced a fee of Rs 500 per question for candidates seeking to raise objections to preliminary answer keys of recruitment examinations. While the fee will be refunded if an objection is found valid, the move is likely to increase the financial burden on aspirants.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: At a time when unemployed candidates are losing hope due to the lack of recruitment notifications, the Telangana Public Service Commission (TGPSC) has now levied a financial burden on them.

The Commission has imposed a Rs 500 fee for raising objections on the preliminary answer keys of recruitment examinations. Candidates must pay Rs 500 for each question they wish to challenge. This means that objections to 10 questions will now cost Rs 5,000, and challenging 20 questions will cost Rs 10,000.

Until now, candidates did not have to pay any fee to raise objections. This imposition of a fee will place a financial burden on candidates who want to raise objections to more than one question. However, if an objection is found to be valid, the fee paid will be refunded.

As part of the recruitment examination process, response sheets and question papers are uploaded online after the examination. The preliminary answer key is then released, and candidates are invited to submit their objections. If the objections raised by candidates are valid, they are considered while preparing the final answer key and results are announced.

The TGPSC has also made it clear that objections to the preliminary answer key must be submitted only in English as the designated box for submitting objections supports only the English language. Further, objections must be submitted online and no objections will be accepted offline.

Candidates must upload relevant supporting documents along with their objections. They must also clearly mention details such as the author’s name, book edition and page number of the reference material.

Meanwhile, TGPSC released the preliminary answer key for the written examination conducted to fill Deputy Educational Officer (Deputy EO) posts in the School Education department on Wednesday. It also released the master question papers on its website.

Candidates can submit objections by paying Rs 500 per question until November 21 (5 pm). For more details, visit the website www.tgpsc.gov.in.

item.title: Karthigai Deepam: Devotees can apply online for free darshan tickets
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Arunachaleswarar Temple in Tiruvannamalai will issue 3,000 free tickets for Bharani Deepam and Maha Deepam ceremonies on November 24. Online registration begins Wednesday, with selection through an automated system scheduled for November 20
item.content:encoded:
Tiruvannamalai: In a major initiative to facilitate the participation of devotees in the annual Karthigai Deepam festival at the Arunachaleswarar Temple in Tamil Nadu’s Tiruvannamalai, the temple administration has announced that 3,000 free admission tickets will be issued for the Bharani Deepam and Maha Deepam ceremonies scheduled for November 24.

Temple Joint Commissioner Paranidharan said online registration for the free tickets would begin at 11 am on Wednesday and continue until 3 pm on Friday.

In previous years, around 1,600 tickets, priced at Rs 500 and Rs 600, were made available through online booking for the two ceremonies. However, following directions from Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Minister Ramesh, the temple administration has decided to substantially increase the number of tickets and make them available free of cost this year.

Of the 3,000 tickets, 1,000 have been earmarked for Bharani Deepam and 2,000 for Maha Deepam.

For Bharani Deepam, 500 tickets each will be allocated to devotees from Tiruvannamalai district and those from other districts. Similarly, 1,000 tickets each will be reserved for the two categories for Maha Deepam.

Devotees seeking admission can register using their Aadhaar numbers on the temple’s official website, https://annamalaiyar.hrce.tn.gov.in, within the stipulated period.

The selection of devotees will be conducted through an automated computerised system at 4 pm on November 20.

Successful applicants will receive an SMS with a link to download their electronic admission tickets on their registered mobile numbers. Selected devotees will be allowed to enter the temple on November 24 after their e-tickets are scanned and their identities verified against their Aadhaar cards at the entrance.

The temple administration has clarified that devotees registering for Bharani Deepam will not be eligible to apply for Maha Deepam, and vice versa.

While applicants for Bharani Deepam can register for only one ticket, those seeking Maha Deepam darshan can register for two tickets using separate Aadhaar numbers. All tickets will be allotted exclusively through the automated selection process.

The Karthigai Deepam festival is one of Tamil Nadu’s most prominent religious celebrations, attracting lakhs of devotees from across the country. The lighting of the sacred Maha Deepam atop Annamalai Hill marks the culmination of the festivities and symbolises Lord Shiva’s manifestation as an infinite column of fire.

item.title: CMC asks organisers to notify it of large events at unlicensed venues
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Cyberabad Municipal Corporation has asked organisers of events involving more than 100 people at unlicensed venues to notify it three working days in advance through the CPCB portal. Organisers must also ensure waste segregation, collection, transportation and scientific disposal.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) has instructed organisers of events or gatherings involving more than 100 people at unlicensed venues to notify the local body at least three working days in advance through the CPCB Event Intimation Portal.

In a press statement, CMC Commissioner G Srijana said, “The guidelines, issued under Rule 5(1)(j) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, require organisers to segregate waste at source, hand it over to authorised collectors or agencies specified by the local body, and arrange its collection, transportation and scientific disposal.”

Deputy Commissioners have been instructed to publicise the guidelines among event organisers, function halls, event management agencies and other stakeholders in their jurisdictions. They have also been directed to raise awareness about the portal and mandatory advance intimation, monitor compliance, and coordinate with sanitation officers and field staff for effective implementation.

item.title: Ranigunj RUB revamp: Traffic restrictions, diversions from November 20
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Hyderabad Traffic Police have announced extensive traffic restrictions and diversions from November 20 to facilitate the renovation of the Railway Under Bridge (RUB) at Ranigunj Junction in Secunderabad. The project, expected to last six to eight months, will reduce traffic capacity at the busy stretch.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Hyderabad traffic police have announced traffic restrictions and diversions in view of the major renovation of the Railway Under Bridge (RUB) at Ranigunj Junction on MG Road, Secunderabad, from November 20. The renovation work, being taken up by the railway authorities, is expected to continue for six to eight months.

As the excavation work will be carried out up to a depth of 1.5 metres across nearly three carriageway lanes, only one carriageway will remain available for light motor vehicles including two-wheelers, auto-rickshaws and cars. Heavy traffic congestion is expected at Ranigunj and adjoining stretches of MG Road, Tank Bund and Karbala Maidan.

The traffic police said that heavy vehicles, including goods vehicles, transport vehicles, travel buses and RTC buses, will not be allowed through the RUB stretch and will be diverted at several junctions.

Heavy vehicles coming from SBI X Roads will be diverted towards Rasoolpura and Begumpet, while those coming from Patny X Roads and Clock Tower will be diverted towards Clock Tower and SBI X Roads.

The vehicles approaching from Paradise X Roads will be diverted towards CTO, while those from Park Lane will be diverted towards Patny X Roads.

Heavy vehicles coming from the Medchal-Bowenpally side via NH-44 will be diverted at CTO Junction towards Rasoolpura-Monappa-Nirankari-Lakdikapul or SBI X Roads-YMCA-Sangeeth X Road-Rail Nilayam and onwards towards Musheerabad or Mettuguda.

Similarly, vehicles coming from Ranigunj from Tank Bund will be diverted at Sailing Club towards Kavadiguda. Heavy vehicles from the upper Tank Bund will be diverted at DBR Mills towards Gandhi Nagar, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad. Diversions will also be enforced at Karbala, Bible House and other adjoining junctions.

Light vehicles coming from Paradise and Minister Road towards Ranigunj will be diverted at Ranigunj X Roads through Distillery Road towards Karbala Junction. Traffic at Nallagutta X Road will be diverted towards Necklace Road.

The traffic police will also install height restrictor railings with a clearance limit of 10 feet at Patny, Paradise, Park Lane, Rasoolpura and Karbala junctions to prevent the entry of oversized vehicles.

Citizens have been advised to avoid the 18 junctions where congestion is expected, including SBI X Roads, Patny, Paradise, Park Lane, Ranigunj, Adavaiah X Roads, Nallagutta, Ghasmandi, Sailing Club, Karbala, Bible House, CGO Towers, Kavadiguda and Old Ambedkar Statue.

The traffic police advised motorists to plan their journeys in advance, follow traffic diversion signs and cooperate with traffic personnel to ensure smooth movement during the renovation period.

item.title: Nani-directed ‘Delivery Boy’ starring Leo Sivakumar gets November 27 release date
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The makers of Tamil film 'Delivery Boy' have revealed Brigida Saga's character, Thenmozhi. Starring Leo Sivakumar and Radhika Sarathkumar, the emotional action entertainer, directed by Nani, is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on November 27
item.content:encoded:
Chennai: The makers of director Nani’s upcoming emotional action entertainer ‘Delivery Boy’, featuring Leo Sivakumar, Brigida Saga and Radhika Sarathkumar in the lead roles, on Wednesday revealed the character played by Brigida Saga in the film.

Asasi Creations, the production house behind the film, took to Instagram to reveal Brigida Saga’s character. “Meet BRIGIDA SAGA as THENMOZHI! Between the chaos of action and the rush of thrills, a little love finds its way into the story! Starring: @radikaasarathkumar @iamleosivakumar. Produced by: @lenin_mathesh @amuthaleoni. Written and directed by: @nani_darla,” the production house posted.

The makers had earlier revealed that actor Bose Venkat plays David, a police officer whose entry is expected to bring unexpected twists and turns to the story.

They also announced that actor Kaali Venkat plays Karuppu, while Matheswaran plays Govindarajan, the antagonist. Dushyanth plays Goutham in the film.

The film, which was originally scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on October 23, will now hit screens on November 27.

Shooting for the film was wrapped up in December last year.

Sources close to the unit said the film was shot entirely in Chennai and Coimbatore in just 42 days.

Taking to its X timeline, the production house’s publicists had announced the completion of the shoot, stating, “#DeliveryBoy shoot wrapped up. Coming to theatres soon. Starring @leosivakumar02 @realradikaa @Brigidasagaoffl @DushyanthJayap1 @dhivakargj @DirectorBose @SundaramurthyKS @AmuthaLeoni @nanisignin @teamaimpr.”

Speaking to IANS, director Nani, who worked as an assistant director to well-known filmmaker Suseenthiran before making his directorial debut, had said, “If I have to briefly give you an idea of what the film is all about, it is about the efforts made by a hardworking delivery boy looking to save his mother. The hero of the story comes from a lower-middle-class family, and the story will revolve around his efforts to save his mother. It will be a gripping story that will keep audiences hooked to the screen from beginning to end.”

The director had also said that post-production work was progressing at a brisk pace after the completion of shooting. “We have now started dubbing for the film,” he had said.

Apart from Leo Sivakumar, Brigida Saga and Radhika Sarathkumar, the film will feature character artistes Dushyanth, Kaali Venkat and Bose Venkat, among others.

The film also has a technical team comprising music composer Sundaramoorthy and cinematographer Prasanna Kumar. It is produced by Amutha Leoni under the Asasi Creations banner.

The film has dialogues by Nanda Mani Vasagam and editing by Vasanth. Stunts have been choreographed by Phoenix Prabhu, while Suresh Kalyani is in charge of art direction.

item.title: Shraddha Kapoor opens up about learning Lavani for Laxman Utekar’s ‘Eetha’
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Shraddha Kapoor has revealed how meeting Lavani artist Shakuntala helped her prepare for her role in 'Eetha'. The actress attended workshops, interacted with traditional performers and practised with 4 kg of ghungroos on each leg for the film
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Shraddha Kapoor has opened up about preparing for her role in the upcoming film ‘Eetha’ and revealed how her interaction with Shakuntala helped her understand the nuances of Lavani.

The actress said the traditional dance form is not just about movements but also involves conveying emotions through facial expressions, giving her a deeper insight into the art.

Speaking about her preparation, the ‘Stree 2’ actress recalled how Shakuntala helped her understand that Lavani goes beyond dance and is equally about the emotions expressed through facial expressions. Shakuntala emphasised how the lives of Tamasha artists are reflected in their performances, which convey both sorrow and joy.

Recalling her interaction with Shakuntala, Shraddha said, “She said, ‘The dancing will happen — you will tie ghungroos on your feet and practise. But what you have to express through your face, you will have to understand.'”

Shraddha revealed that she had no prior knowledge of Lavani when she joined ‘Eetha’. She attended workshops, interacted with Lavani and Tamasha artists, and learned from Shakuntala to understand the dance form.

Her preparation also involved practising with 4 kg of ghungroos on each leg. Director Laxman Utekar and producer Dinesh Vijan supported her throughout the process, including when she sustained an injury while shooting a song.

Earlier, Shraddha had spoken about her experience of performing Lavani in the song ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ from her upcoming film ‘Eetha’.

“Performing ‘Ji Ji Re Ji’ as Eetha was such an exhilarating experience. There is something incredibly infectious about Lavani — the rhythm, the expressions, the energy, and the way you connect with the audience. I loved and was equally scared to step into the incredible world of a legendary artist through this song,” Shraddha said.

Directed by Laxman Utekar and produced by Dinesh Vijan, Laxman Utekar and Karishma Sharma, ‘Eetha’ will release in cinemas on December 4, 2026.

item.title: HMWSSB urges citizens to cut water usage by 20 per cent until August 2027
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board
item.description: With rainfall deficit and the El Niño impact raising concerns over water availability, HMWSSB has urged citizens to reduce consumption by 20 per cent. It has also asked schools to promote conservation habits and awareness among students across Telangana.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: In view of the water shortage arising due to deficit rainfall and the El Niño impact, the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB) has asked citizens to ensure at least a 20 per cent reduction in water consumption over the next 10 months or until August 2027. The Board urged individuals, families and institutions to adopt water conservation habits to reduce water usage.

In a letter addressed to the School Education Department, HMWSSB Managing Director K Ashok Reddy said that due to the El Niño effect, there was a rainfall deficit and low water levels in the Singur and Manjeera reservoirs. “Consequently, pressure on water availability may increase during the summer. Using water carefully is everyone’s responsibility,” he said.

The Board said only the required amount of water should be used while brushing teeth, bathing and washing hands, and water must not be allowed to flow unnecessarily. “Students should prevent water wastage at home and school, and create awareness among others about the importance of saving water,” he said.

Urging the department to initiate water conservation measures in schools, Reddy said it was important to inculcate responsible water conservation habits among students from an early age.

“Creating awareness among students to avoid wastage of water not only at home but also in schools and surrounding areas would help spread the message to their families and the wider community,” he said.

He asked authorities to explain to government and private school students across the State the El Niño condition, its impact on rainfall and the need to conserve drinking water during the summer season. He also wanted schools to deliver a special one-minute message on water conservation every day during morning assemblies, administer a water conservation pledge to students, and encourage them to identify and prevent water wastage.

Following the Board’s letter, the department has asked its district education officers to instruct schools to initiate water conservation measures and create awareness among students.

item.title: TG SAFE suspends FSSAI licences of eateries over food safety violations
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: TG SAFE suspended the FSSAI licences of four eateries following inspections that revealed serious food safety violations. Officials also ordered two establishments operating without licences to close, collected eight food samples and seized or discarded around 300 kg of food articles.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) on Wednesday suspended the FSSAI licences of four eateries and ordered them to immediately stop business operations following the detection of serious food safety violations during inspections.

According to officials, five teams comprising Food Safety Officers and police personnel inspected 10 restaurants, hotels and hostels following consumer complaints. The establishments whose licences were suspended are Alpha Hotel and Stores & Lodge in Secunderabad, Pandem Kodi Restaurant in Vengal Rao Nagar, Laham House in Jubilee Hills and Spice Kitchen in Gowlidoddi.

During the inspections, officials detected several violations, including cockroach and housefly infestations, clogged drains, unhygienic kitchens, damaged flooring and improper storage of food articles. In some establishments, vegetarian and non-vegetarian food items were stored together, while mandatory records such as employee health records and water analysis reports were not maintained.

Eight food samples were collected on suspicion of adulteration, while around 300 kg of food articles were seized or discarded.

New Blue Star Restaurant in Rajeev Nagar, Kukatpally, and Srinivasa Boys Hostel in Panjagutta were also ordered to close for operating without an FSSAI licence and in unhygienic conditions.

Show-cause notices will be issued to five establishments, including the two ordered to close, while an improvement notice will be served on Tatva Hotel in Secunderabad to rectify the shortcomings, officials added.

Officials said details of the four establishments whose licences were suspended would be shared with online food delivery platforms Swiggy and Zomato for delisting them until their licences are restored. Re-inspections will be conducted to verify compliance, and further action, including penalties, will follow.

item.title: Hyderabad: Liquor shop owner arrested for adulteration in Nizampet
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Prohibition and Excise Department arrested OG Liquor Mart owner Gandham Praveen Goud in Nizampet for allegedly adulterating premium and medium-priced liquor with water or cheaper liquor. Officials raided the store, seized adulterated bottles and sealed the liquor mart.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Prohibition and Excise Department on Wednesday arrested a liquor shop owner for allegedly adulterating premium and medium-priced liquor and selling it to customers at Nizampet.

According to officials, the suspect, Gandham Praveen Goud, owner of OG Liquor Mart, allegedly removed the bottle caps, drew a small quantity of liquor and replaced it with water or cheaper liquor before resealing the bottles and selling them to customers. The adulteration was being carried out in different brands of premium and medium-priced liquor, officials said.

Acting on information, the excise sleuths raided the store, seized the adulterated liquor bottles and sealed the liquor mart. A case has been registered.

item.title: Telugu producer Bandla Ganesh gets one-year jail term in Rs 95-lakh cheque bounce case
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: A court in Ongole sentenced Telugu film producer Bandla Ganesh to one year of simple imprisonment in a Rs 95-lakh cheque bounce case. It also imposed a Rs 95-lakh fine and gave him a month to appeal before higher court
item.content:encoded:
Amaravati: An Andhra Pradesh court on Wednesday sentenced Telugu film producer Bandla Ganesh to one year of simple imprisonment in a cheque bounce case and imposed a fine of Rs 95 lakh.

The court in Ongole also directed him to bear the legal expenses incurred by the complainant during the proceedings.

The case relates to a Rs 95 lakh loan taken by Ganesh in 2018 from Janaki Ramaiah of Maddiralapadu village in Prakasam district.

After Ramaiah’s death, Ganesh issued a cheque to his father, Jetti Venkateswara Rao, through his production company, Parameswara Arts, towards repayment of the dues.

As the cheque was dishonoured due to insufficient funds in the bank account, Venkateswara Rao approached the Ongole court.

After hearing the case, the court found Ganesh guilty and sentenced him to one year of simple imprisonment, besides imposing a fine of Rs 95 lakh. However, it gave him a month’s time to appeal before a higher court.

A lower court had sentenced Ganesh in the same case in 2024. He subsequently approached a higher court, which upheld the sentence.

Meanwhile, reacting to the Ongole court’s verdict on Wednesday, Ganesh said he had immense respect for the Constitution of India, the judiciary and the police system.

“In our democratic framework, every institution holds a distinct status and carries specific responsibilities. The Constitution provides us with the opportunity to seek justice — from the district courts to the High Courts, and ultimately, the Supreme Court. My firm belief is to move forward with complete faith in the judiciary and with due respect for the law,” he said in a post on X.

Ganesh has faced cheque bounce cases in the past. He was sentenced to imprisonment in similar cases, following which he filed appeals before higher courts.

In 2017, the Erramanzil Special Court in Hyderabad sentenced Ganesh to six months’ rigorous imprisonment and imposed a fine of nearly Rs 16 lakh.

The sentence was in connection with a cheque bounce case filed by scriptwriter Vakkantham Vamsi. Ganesh was granted bail after submitting personal bonds before the court.

Vamsi, who wrote the script for the film ‘Temper’, starring Junior NTR and Kajal Agarwal, approached the court after Ganesh, the film’s producer, allegedly failed to pay his full remuneration of Rs 26 lakh.

Ganesh had issued post-dated cheques to Vamsi, but all of them were dishonoured, prompting the latter to approach the court in 2015. A case was registered under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

During the court proceedings, Ganesh paid Rs 17 lakh but failed to meet the deadline set by the court to clear the remaining Rs 9 lakh.

He was subsequently sentenced to six months’ imprisonment and fined Rs 15,86,550.

In 2019, a court in Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh, issued a non-bailable warrant against Ganesh in another cheque bounce case and remanded him to judicial custody.

Ganesh had allegedly failed to repay Rs 13 crore borrowed from Mahesh, a native of Kadapa, prompting the latter to lodge a complaint.

As Ganesh allegedly did not respond to the notices served on him, the court issued a non-bailable warrant. Acting on the warrant, police arrested him in Hyderabad and brought him to Kadapa.

The court remanded him to judicial custody for 10 days. However, after the two parties negotiated a settlement, he was granted bail.

item.title: Telangana Under-19 chess selection tournament scheduled for November 21 and 22
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana State Under-19 Junior Chess Championship will be held at Sundarayya Bhavan, Nizampet, on November 21 and 22. The top five boys and four girls will qualify to represent the State at the national championship
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Telangana State Under-19 Junior Chess Championship will be held on November 21 and 22 at Sundarayya Bhavan in Nizampet.

The tournament will serve as a selection event for the forthcoming National Under-19 Chess Championship.

Only Telangana-resident Indian citizens born on or after January 1, 2007, are eligible to participate.

The top five boys and four girls will be selected to represent Telangana at the national championship.

Interested players can register by 6 pm on November 20. No spot registrations will be accepted.

Players can register through www.chesstelangana.com. For details, contact 7337578899 or 7337399299.

item.title: Contract assistant professors protest across 12 Telangana universities
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: University Teachers Association – Contract – Telangana State
item.description: Contract assistant professors staged protests across 12 Telangana universities, demanding regularisation or absorption before fresh faculty recruitment. They sought job security, minimum wages and UGC pay scales, citing decades of service, academic qualifications, research contributions and examination-related responsibilities.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Demanding that the State government regularise their jobs or absorb them into the university system before undertaking any fresh faculty recruitment, contract assistant professors staged protests across 12 universities, including Osmania University, on Wednesday. They attended their regular duties wearing black badges and raising slogans to highlight their demands.

Participating in the protest at OU, Dr A Parshuram, president of the University Teachers Association – Contract – Telangana State (UTA-C-TG), and Dr D Dharmateja, working president, said contract assistant professors possessed all the qualifications prescribed by the UGC.

Contract teachers highlighted that they had secured patents besides publishing research articles in reputed academic journals and earning numerous national and international citations.

In addition to regular teaching and research responsibilities, teachers said they also performed various examination-related duties, including invigilation, question paper setting and moderation.

Despite serving universities for the past 20 to 25 years, contract assistant professors said they were not even being paid minimum wages and demanded implementation of the Supreme Court’s principle of “Equal Pay for Equal Work.”

Protesters said that if regularisation took some time, the government should immediately ensure job security and implement UGC pay scales in accordance with the 7th UGC Pay Commission (2016).

item.title: TRSMA opposes Intermediate colleges adding Classes IX, X
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Recognised School Managements Association has opposed allowing intermediate colleges to add Classes IX and X under the proposed education department merger, warning that budget private schools could lose students. It sought permission for recognised schools to upgrade to Classes XI and XII.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: With the State government proposing the merger of Intermediate Education with the School Education department, the Telangana Recognised School Managements Association (TRSMA) on Wednesday urged the government not to permit existing intermediate colleges to add Classes IX and X under the new system.

The TRSMA expressed concern that if such permission were granted, intermediate colleges, with their strong financial resources and infrastructure, would directly affect established economical private schools. This could result in a loss of student strength and eventually lead to the closure of many budget schools.

In a representation submitted to School Education Director Dr E Naveen Nicolas, TRSMA president SN Reddy and general secretary K Anil Kumar urged the government to allow existing recognised schools to upgrade by adding Classes XI and XII, subject to prescribed norms. They also sought permission to establish institutions under the nursery-to-Class-XII pattern, subject to government regulations.

The TRSMA sought continuation of the existing school permission categories, such as pre-primary, nursery to Class V, nursery to Class VIII and nursery to Class X. It said intermediate colleges may be allowed to set up institutions from nursery to Class XII as per prescribed norms.

item.title: Rohit Sharma recalls wife and son dancing to ‘Dholida’ at school function
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.category: Family Full House with Rohit Sharma
item.description: Rohit Sharma shared a family anecdote on Family Full House with Rohit Sharma, revealing that his two-year-old son loves the song ‘Dholida’. The cricketer recalled his wife and son dancing to it at the child’s school annual day
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Ace cricketer Rohit Sharma admitted that his wife is a better dancer than him, saying, “Main apni biwi se achha dance nahi karta” (I don’t dance better than my wife).

Sharing a candid family anecdote about his wife and young son on Sony Entertainment Television’s Family Full House with Rohit Sharma, the cricketer spoke about his dancing skills.

Rohit recalled how the song ‘Dholida’ is particularly special to his family, as it is his two-year-old son’s favourite. He revealed that his wife and son had performed to the song during his son’s annual day function at school.

“Ye gaana mere chhote se 2 saal ke bachche ka favourite gaana hai, kyunki last year annual day hua tha uske school mein, toh is gaane pe mere chhote bachche ko aur meri biwi ko is gaane pe naachna pada tha.” (This song is my little two-year-old child’s favourite because there was an annual day function at his school last year, and my little child and my wife had to dance to this song.)

Rohit said watching the two perform on stage made him want to join them. However, he jokingly admitted that he could not match his wife when it came to dancing.

“Unn dono ko stage pe aise dance karte hue dekh kar mujhe bhi laga ki main bhi karun, lekin main apni biwi se achha dance nahi karta hoon yaar.” (Watching both of them dancing like that on stage made me feel that I should dance too, but I don’t dance better than my wife, yaar.)

item.title: Kreishh Gurbaxani defeats roommate Amir Sarkhosh in seven-frame thriller
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Kreishh Gurbaxani beat friend and former roommate Amir Sarkhosh 4-3 at the IBSF World Snooker Championships in Indore on Wednesday. Sourav Kothari, Pankaj Advani and Aditya Mehta also won, while Amee Kamani and Keerthana Pandian both extended their winning runs
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Kreishh Gurbaxani edged out Iran’s Amir Sarkhosh, his friend and roommate of two years in England, in an entertaining Group ‘G’ match of the IBSF World Snooker Championships at the Yeshwant Club in Indore on Wednesday.

In a high-quality encounter studded with big breaks, Gurbaxani, who came through the first-stage qualifiers, scored a 4-3 victory in a match that could have gone either way. The promising Indian came up with a century and three frame-clinching half-century breaks for his second straight win.

The two cueists, who spent two years on the professional circuit in England, matched each other shot for shot and played an attacking game throughout. The bespectacled Gurbaxani came out all guns blazing with a sublime 119 break in the opening frame.

Sarkhosh responded with a break of 47 after a Gurbaxani error in the next frame to make it 1-1. The Indian cueist then punished his rival’s missed red pot with a flowing break of 98 to go 2-1 up. However, Gurbaxani returned the favour, and Sarkhosh capitalised with runs of 55 and 63 to take a 3-2 lead.

Before much damage could be done, Gurbaxani made a 52 break to level the scores. When his rival missed a red to the top-right pocket, the Indian youngster held his nerve with a gritty 71 break to seal the win.

Elsewhere, Sourav Kothari found his rhythm and range with a crushing 4-0 win over Omar Alajlani of Saudi Arabia. He rifled in breaks of 101 and 127 for his second victory in the group.

Also registering their second wins were favourite Pankaj Advani and Aditya Mehta. While Advani overcame fellow Indian Piyush Kushwaha 4-1, Mehta got the better of Oliwier Nizialek of Poland 4-2.

In a late-night match on Tuesday, India’s S Shrikrishna came up with a sizzling break of 136 — the highest of the tournament so far — for a lopsided 4-0 win over Dhruv Patel in Group ‘B’.

AMEE, KEERTHANA KEEP WINNING

Earlier in the day, challenger Amee Kamani outclassed Iran’s Sayedehsaba Moosavi 2-0 for her third straight win in Group ‘D’, moving closer to a place in the knockouts.

A former runner-up, India’s Amee was in the zone from the outset, compiling breaks of 78 and 44 in her lopsided victory. A century was there for the taking in the first frame, but she was unlucky to miss the penultimate red to the centre pocket. After a scrappy start in the next frame, Amee closed out the frame and the match with a flowing break of 44.

Also inching closer to the knockouts was Keerthana Pandian. The winner of two age-group world snooker titles, Keerthana defeated Yee Ting Cheung of Hong Kong, China, 2-0 for her third consecutive win in Group ‘B’.

item.title: IndiGo extends cancellation of Saudi Arabia flights till Nov 30
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: IndiGo has extended the suspension of all flights to and from four Saudi Arabian cities, Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam, until November 30, 2026, citing the prevailing security situation in the Kingdom.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: IndiGo on Wednesday extended the cancellation of flights connecting Saudi Arabian cities till November 30 amid the prevailing security situation in the Gulf nation.

Earlier, the airline had cancelled the services to and from Jeddah and Madinah till November 21, while the flights to Riyadh and Dammam were cancelled till November 30.

“In view of the prevailing security situation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, all flights to and from Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam have been cancelled until 30 November 2026 (inclusive),” IndiGo said in a post on X on Wednesday.

The airline said it continues to closely monitor developments and assess the situation.

On November 13, Air India and Air India Express extended the cancellation of their flights connecting Riyadh and Dammam till November 30, while services to Jeddah were suspended till November 21.

Akasa, on November 12, announced the cancellation of its flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah till November 30.

Saudi Arabia has faced attacks on its cities and infrastructure from Houthis.

item.title: Sandpapergate controversy: Cricket Australia seeks answers through independent forum
item.dc:creator: AP
item.description: Cricket Australia will establish an independent forum to address conflicting accounts of the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. The move follows fresh claims by Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft, while former captain Pat Cummins has rejected suggestions of a team-wide plan
item.content:encoded:
Hobart: Cricket Australia (CA) said on Wednesday that it would establish an independent forum to address conflicting accounts surrounding the Australian Test team’s ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as Sandpapergate, during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa.

CA interim chair David Boon said the ongoing controversy was becoming a distraction for the sport and expressed hope that players and support staff from the 2018 Test team would participate in the forum.

“This forum is not about relitigating the past,” Boon said in Hobart ahead of the third and deciding one-day international against England. “It’s about creating an opportunity for those who wish to be heard to tell their stories in a respectful, safe environment — and for our sport to listen.”

Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja recently claimed that most members of the 2018 team knew that sandpaper was being used to rough up the ball and give the bowlers an unfair advantage.

Current Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed Khawaja’s claims as nonsense and rejected the suggestion that there had been a master plan within the team to tamper with the ball.

Cricket Australia had banned Steve Smith and David Warner for 12 months and stripped them of their respective roles as captain and vice-captain. It also suspended Cameron Bancroft, who was caught on television cameras with sandpaper in his trousers during the Cape Town Test, for nine months.

Warner defended Khawaja’s comments. Adding to the controversy, Bancroft issued a lengthy statement later on Wednesday, saying that the entire team had been aware of the ball-tampering incident.

CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said players and support staff from that period would not be forced to attend the forum, which would operate entirely independently of Cricket Australia.

“Over the past week, we have had several different and conflicting accounts of what transpired in Cape Town in 2018. And it has been an incredibly difficult and uncomfortable time for the game and for everyone who was involved. The game is really hurting at the moment,” Greenberg said.

Greenberg said CA would decide whether any outcome from the forum would be made public.

“This is not about appeasing any individual. These events were eight years ago. They caused enormous pain and hurt for lots of people, and they’re doing it again. And at some point, we have to move forward, and we can’t move forward without putting some of these steps in place,” he said.

He said there would be no sanctions against anyone participating in the forum and expressed hope that the process would be completed within a month.

“The quicker we can go, the better, but we won’t rush it,” Greenberg said.

item.title: Bhadrachalam tribal youth’s killing reflects deteriorating law and order: BRS leader
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS leader and former Pinapaka MLA Rega Kantha Rao alleged that the killing of a tribal youth in Bhadrachalam over a minor Aadhaar card-related dispute highlighted the deteriorating law and order situation in Telangana. He criticised the state government, police, local MLA and district ministers for failing to prevent rising criminal activities.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: Beating a youth to death publicly in Bhadrachalam town in the district was a testament to the deteriorating law and order situation in the State, said former Pinapaka MLA, BRS leader Rega Kantha Rao.

He expressed deep shock over the incident that took place at Satya Sai Residency in the town late on Monday night. It was inhumane for the perpetrators to drag the tribal youth Tellam Sharath out onto the street and beat him to death instead of resolving a minor dispute regarding an Aadhaar card. Taking lives over trivial disputes was a matter of grave concern for society.

There has been a surge in incidents involving the use of ganja, other narcotics, anti-social activities, violent clashes, and murders recently at the sacred pilgrimage site Bhadrachalam, Kantha Rao alleged.

Despite this, the State government and the police have failed to take adequate measures to stop such incidents. The government, which bears the responsibility of maintaining law and order, has failed to ensure the safety of its citizens’ lives.

It was regrettable that the local MLA Dr. Tellam Venkat Rao had not responded to the incident. It was inappropriate for elected representatives who ought to address public concerns and ensure the safety of the people to remain silent during such incidents, Kantha Rao said.

The three ministers from the district, Bhatti Vikramarka, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy and Tummala Nageswara Rao must accept moral responsibility for the youth’s death. A comprehensive investigation into the incident should be conducted and legal action should be taken against the perpetrators as well as the owner of Satya Sai Residency, he demanded.

The BRS leader questioned why the three ministers had failed to take action against the sand mafia, drug syndicates and the trafficking of ganja. Police should conduct immediate, targeted inspections of lodges in Bhadrachalam to eliminate gambling, the use of ganja and other illicit anti-social activities.

If the police fail to take immediate action in this matter, the BRS party would launch large-scale protests to ensure public safety and restore law and order in Bhadrachalam, Kantha Rao warned.

item.title: India need experienced players like Rohit, Kohli for 2027 World Cup: Madan Lal
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Former India cricketer Madan Lal has backed Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli for the 2027 ODI World Cup, saying their experience and performances will be vital in major tournaments. His comments come amid questions over their future international roles
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Former Indian cricketer and one of the heroes of India’s 1983 World Cup-winning campaign, Madan Lal, believes Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli should be part of India’s squad for the 2027 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup, saying the experience and performances of the two senior batters will be equally important to the team’s campaign.

Madan Lal said experienced players such as Rohit and Kohli bring significant value to the side in major tournaments, where their presence and performances can make a difference. He also expressed confidence that the two former India captains would be keen to win another World Cup before bringing their illustrious careers to an end.

“I believe Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli should feature in next year’s World Cup. Their performances will be equally important for the team. In big tournaments, the team looks up to experienced and accomplished players like them. I am sure both would also want to win another World Cup before calling time on their careers. Therefore, I feel they should be part of the World Cup campaign,” Madan Lal told IANS.

The former all-rounder’s backing comes at a time when questions continue to surround the future roles of Rohit and Kohli in India’s preparations for the 2027 showpiece in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. Both batters endured difficult outings during India’s recent five-match ODI series against New Zealand, which the hosts won 3-1.

Rohit had a particularly disappointing series, managing only 30 runs in four innings at an average of 7.50. His scores of 0, 23, 0 and 7 included two ducks, making it his lowest batting average in a bilateral ODI series as an opener. His final outing ended with him being dismissed for seven at Bay Oval, where he flicked a delivery from Matthew Fisher straight to mid-wicket.

Kohli, meanwhile, finished as India’s leading run-scorer in the series with 86 runs from four innings at an average of 21.50. After beginning the tour with an impressive 74 off 51 deliveries in Auckland, he struggled to maintain the momentum, returning scores of 7, 0 and 5 in his subsequent appearances.

The 2027 edition will provide India with another opportunity to challenge for the ODI World Cup title, with the team looking to build a strong combination under Shubman Gill’s leadership.

item.title: SMAT 2026: Mumbai beat Goa by 18 runs; Baroda thrash UP
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Mumbai defeated Goa by 18 runs to continue their winning run in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Elite 2026. Baroda, Haryana and Puducherry also registered victories, with Baroda completing a comfortable eight-wicket win over Uttar Pradesh
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Mumbai continued their winning momentum in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Elite 2026 with an 18-run victory over Goa, while Baroda, Haryana and Puducherry also registered wins in their respective matches on Wednesday.

Baroda produced the most emphatic result of the day, chasing down Uttar Pradesh’s modest target of 93 in just 9.1 overs. Haryana and Puducherry also registered victories in the tournament.

Baroda bundled out Uttar Pradesh for 92 in 18.1 overs before reaching 96/2 in 9.1 overs to seal an eight-wicket win. Atit Sheth led the bowling attack with three wickets, while Hemant Punde and Rasikh Salam Dar claimed two each to dismantle the UP batting line-up.

Sameer Rizvi top-scored for Uttar Pradesh with 41, but the rest of the batting order struggled to build partnerships. In reply, Shashwat Rawat remained unbeaten on 39, while Amit Pasi contributed 38 as Baroda completed the chase comfortably.

Haryana defeated Tamil Nadu by seven wickets after restricting them to 124 in 19.5 overs. Nishant Sindhu and Yuzvendra Chahal picked up three wickets apiece to lead the bowling effort, with Kanishk Chouhan and Rahul Tewatia claiming one each.

Tamil Nadu’s Amit Sathvik provided an early impetus with 38 off 17 balls, while B. Sachin made 27 and Shahrukh Khan added 22. Haryana’s chase was anchored by captain Ankit Rajesh Kumar, who scored 43, and Sindhu, who remained unbeaten on 33. The pair helped Haryana reach 126/3 in 16.1 overs.

Puducherry also enjoyed a comfortable outing, beating Assam by 61 runs. After posting 192/6 in 20 overs, Puducherry restricted Assam to 131/7.

Aman Khan struck 55 off 32 deliveries, while Parameeswaran Sivaraman made 53 off 43, laying the foundation for Puducherry’s total. Pugazhendi Akash chipped in with 21.

Assam’s chase never gathered momentum, with Pradyun Saikia scoring 44 and Akash Sengupta making 42. Adil Ayub Tunda was the pick of the Puducherry bowlers with figures of 3/19.

Mumbai edged past Goa by 18 runs in a high-scoring contest. Mumbai were bowled out for 207, but Goa managed only 189 in 19 overs despite a strong effort from Lalit Yadav, who scored 81 off 41 balls. Deepraj Gaonkar added 48, but Mumbai’s bowlers kept striking at crucial stages.

Sairaj Patil played a decisive all-round role, scoring 40 off 21 deliveries before returning figures of 3/27 to earn Player of the Match honours. Musheer Khan contributed 44, while Maxwell Swaminathan made 28 and Suryakumar Yadav scored 25. Patil’s contribution with both bat and ball proved crucial in securing Mumbai’s victory.

item.title: Yashoda Hospitals hosts wellbeing roundtable in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Yashoda Hospitals organised a wellbeing roundtable at its Hitec City campus, bringing together public figures and around 500 corporate leaders. Discussions centred on preventive healthcare, healthy longevity, quality of life and improving physical and mental wellbeing among employees.
item.content:encoded:
