Hyderabad: With the objective of promoting awareness about healthy longevity, quality of life, personal wellbeing and employee health, Yashoda Hospitals organised ‘The Wellbeing Roundtable – Adding Life to Years’ at its Hitec City campus.

The event was attended by actor Vijay Deverakonda, Kamlesh D Patel (Daaji), Global Guide of Heartfulness, and Olympic Medallist P V Sindhu. Around 500 invited participants, including CEOs, senior executives, department heads, managers and corporate leaders from Global Capability Centres (GCCs) across Hyderabad, attended the programme.

The discussions focused on the importance of moving beyond disease treatment towards preventive healthcare, scientifically backed approaches to longevity, and promoting the physical and mental wellbeing of employees.

“At Yashoda Hospitals, we see every day how late diagnosis affects patients and their families. Through The Wellbeing Roundtable, we want to shift the focus from treatment to prevention,” said G Ravender Rao, Chairman, Yashoda Hospitals.

Dr Abhinav Gorukanti, Director, Yashoda Hospitals, said, “Life expectancy in India has more than doubled since Independence. However, Indians now spend over ten of those years in poor health, and our hospital data shows that lifestyle diseases are now appearing in people in their thirties and forties.”

item.title: 27 civilians evacuated from seminary before LeT commander’s killing in Kulgam
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: An Army officer and his buddy rescued 25 girls and two teachers from a seminary adjoining a mosque in Kulgam before security forces launched the final assault on Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who was killed in the encounter
item.content:encoded:
Kulgam: Anxious moments gripped Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district on Wednesday when it emerged that 25 girls and two teachers were inside a Darul Uloom (educational institute) adjacent to the mosque where top Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat was holed up, just before troops launched the final assault to neutralise him.

Braving heavy firing from the mosque, an officer from the Army’s 9 Rashtriya Rifles volunteered to enter the adjoining seminary along with his buddy and safely evacuate all 27 civilians, officials said.

Once the civilians were moved to safety, troops of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the Jammu and Kashmir Police launched the final assault and fired tear gas shells into the mosque to smoke out the terrorist, while maintaining a tight cordon to prevent his escape. They exercised maximum restraint to ensure that the religious structure suffered no damage.

Northern Army Commander Lt Gen Pratik Sharma, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief (GoC-in-C), met troops in South Kashmir after the successful conclusion of the operation.

Giving details of the operation, officials said a search party accompanied by local civilians entered the mosque following specific intelligence inputs and found a room on the top floor locked from the inside.

When asked to come out, the occupant opened fire, confirming the presence of Bhat, who carried a cash reward of Rs 15 lakh on his head, inside the premises.

Senior Army officers in South Kashmir had resolved to ensure that Bhat did not slip through the cordon this time, as he had done on previous occasions. He had escaped an earlier encounter in Shopian on July 8, in which another terrorist, Zakir, was killed.

Following a November 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam by Bhat and his associate Umar Nasir Dar, which left three personnel injured, security forces launched massive cordon and search operations across Kulgam and the adjoining districts of Shopian and Anantnag.

Around 2,000 personnel from the Army, SOG and CRPF, supported by a Mobile Bunker Command Post (MBCP), were deployed for the grid-based searches.

“Since November 11, cordon and search operations have been underway. In certain areas, it took us nearly three days to complete the searches due to high population density,” a senior officer said, adding that although the operations may have caused some inconvenience to the general public, there were no complaints of excesses.

Bhat, a school pass-out and former carpenter who was in his early 20s, went missing in November 2025 before joining the LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF).

According to security agencies, he was the prime suspect in several terror incidents in South Kashmir, including the killing of India Reserve Police Head Constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi in Anantnag on July 22 and the targeted killing of two non-local labourers from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam on July 31.

item.title: Madan Lal questions India’s U-19 players’ celebrations after Pakistan victory
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Former India cricketer Madan Lal praised the U-19 team's cricketing performance against Pakistan but criticised its excessive post-match celebrations. He said young players must understand the importance of maintaining dignity and respecting opponents, even after significant victories
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Former India cricketer Madan Lal, a member of the 1983 World Cup-winning team, praised India’s performance in the U-19 Asia Cup final against Pakistan but felt that the players could have shown greater restraint during their post-match celebrations.

India beat Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final in Al Amerat on Saturday to secure a record-extending ninth U-19 Asia Cup title. However, the celebrations after the win, with Indian players expressing their emotions in front of their Pakistani counterparts, sparked a debate among fans and former cricketers.

“The Indian U-19 players displayed some brilliant cricket against Pakistan in the Asia Cup final, and the future of Indian cricket certainly looks very promising. However, I believe they should have exercised a little more restraint during their post-match celebrations. It was a bit excessive. They need to understand that there is a difference between how a big team conducts itself and how a smaller team approaches such occasions. Winning is important, but maintaining dignity and showing respect to the opposition are equally important,” Madan Lal told IANS.

The final ended in dramatic fashion as India chased down a daunting target of 338, finishing at 339/9 off the last ball of the match. After India kept losing wickets at regular intervals and the chase threatened to slip away, Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva put together a crucial late partnership to take their team across the line.

The duo added 57 runs in just 35 balls to revive India’s hopes. Chauhan scored 47 off 32 deliveries, while Ulva remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, hitting five fours and three sixes. Ulva sealed the victory with a boundary off the final delivery, sparking jubilant celebrations among the Indian players.

Earlier, Pakistan had posted 337/9 after opting to bat, with Usman Khan leading the way with 107 off 111 balls. Abdul Qadir contributed 80 off 54 deliveries, while captain Farhan Yousaf scored 63 off 60 balls.

India’s chase was built around a 95-run opening partnership between captain Lakshya Raichandani, who scored 80 off 101 balls, and Aaryavir Sehwag, who made 58 off 61 deliveries. However, Pakistan fought back by taking wickets and reducing India to 252/8 before Chauhan and Ulva turned the contest around.

The victory extended India’s dominance in the tournament, taking its tally to nine U-19 Asia Cup titles.

item.title: Teacher sends girl home for not bathing, row erupts in Sangareddy
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A controversy has erupted in Sangareddy district after a government school teacher allegedly sent a girl student home for not bathing before attending classes. The child's parents said she had skipped bathing on medical advice due to illness.
item.content:encoded:
Sangareddy: A controversy is brewing over the reported decision of a teacher to send a child back home, after coming to know that she had not bathed that day, in Polkampally village of Munipally mandal on Wednesday.

Reports said government school headmaster Sailu ordered a girl student to go home after learning that she had not bathed that day. The schoolgirl was reportedly advised by a doctor not to bathe as she was suffering from an illness. Following this advice, her parents sent her to the Mandal Parishad Primary School without giving her a bath on Wednesday.

When the parents questioned the teacher’s decision, he reportedly refused to answer their queries. The parents were preparing to lodge a complaint with the Mandal Educational Officer (MEO).

item.title: J&K Police intensifies crackdown on terror networks, attaches 122 properties in 2026
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Jammu and Kashmir DGP Nalin Prabhat said local terrorist recruitment had fallen to almost zero over two years, with only two Kashmiri youths joining Lashkar-e-Taiba. He also detailed arrests and property attachments targeting the terror ecosystem across the Union Territory
item.content:encoded:
Udhampur: Jammu and Kashmir Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat on Wednesday said local terrorist recruitment in the Union Territory had been brought down to “almost zero” over the past two years.

Only two Kashmiri youths joined the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) during this period. The last remaining terrorist among them, identified as Lateef Bhat, was killed in an encounter in Kulgam district on Wednesday. The other terrorist, Umar Nisar, was eliminated in the same district two days ago, he said.

The DGP was speaking at the passing-out parade of deputy superintendents of police, sub-inspectors and assistant directors of the Forest Protection Force at the Sher-i-Kashmir Police Academy (SKPA) in the presence of Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha in Udhampur.

“We have brought local terrorist recruitment in Jammu and Kashmir to almost zero over the last two years. During this period, only two Kashmiri youths joined the Lashkar-e-Taiba,” Prabhat said.

“Today, I would like to inform everyone that the last remaining terrorist, Lateef Bhat, was killed in Kulgam today. Two days earlier, Umar Nisar was also killed in Kulgam,” he said.

The DGP said the Jammu and Kashmir Police had been fighting Pakistan-sponsored terrorism for the past 35 years and paid tributes to its martyrs.

“We have been fighting Pakistan-sponsored terrorism for the last 35 years. I pay my tributes and salute our 1,603 martyrs, including our two brave personnel, Babi Chand and Rashpal Kumar, who laid down their lives for the nation in Kishtwar recently,” he said.

“Their supreme sacrifices make us stronger and further strengthen our resolve. The memories of our martyrs always show us the way, remaining our guiding light and source of inspiration,” he said.

The DGP said the police force was not only fighting terrorists but also targeting their support networks and the broader terror ecosystem.

“I am extremely grateful to our Hon’ble Prime Minister, our Hon’ble Home Minister and, particularly, our respected Lieutenant Governor, Manoj Sinha Ji, under whose guidance and leadership the Jammu and Kashmir Police is continuously achieving one success after another and hoisting its flag of victory everywhere.

“We are not only combating terrorism but are also continuously striking at its ecosystem. Our endeavour is to completely dismantle and destroy the entire terror ecosystem,” he said.

Giving details of the action against terror-related networks, the DGP said 240 accused were arrested under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in 2025, while 210 arrests had been made under the stringent law this year.

The arrests included those of people allegedly providing financial and logistical support to terrorist activities, he said, adding that those involved in such activities would not escape the police’s reach.

On action against properties linked to terrorism, Prabhat said 155 properties were attached in 2025 after due legal process, while 122 had been attached so far this year.

He said the action covered properties belonging to terrorists operating from Pakistan, as well as those of other individuals involved in terrorism-related activities under the UAPA.

Top Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Lateef Bhat was killed in an encounter with security forces in Kulgam district on Wednesday, officials said.

Bhat, along with another terrorist, Umar Nisar, was involved in the November 11 attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam, which left three paramilitary personnel injured. Nisar was killed in an encounter in Kulgam on Monday.

item.title: ‘Feels like a dream’: Brevis shares heartfelt message for MS Dhoni
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Chennai Super Kings batter Dewald Brevis penned a heartfelt tribute to MS Dhoni, recalling their association since 2022. He thanked the former India captain for guiding young players and expressed gratitude for having him as a mentor at CSK
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Chennai Super Kings (CSK) batter Dewald Brevis described sharing the dressing room with Mahendra Singh Dhoni as a privilege and said he was grateful to have the former captain as his mentor following Dhoni’s retirement from the Indian Premier League (IPL).

Dhoni has stepped away from his IPL playing career and will take up the role of CSK team mentor from the 2027 season. He concluded his IPL playing career with 278 matches and 5,439 runs. He led CSK to five titles in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023 and finished with 205 wicketkeeping dismissals, including 158 catches and 47 stumpings.

Brevis took to social media to recall his first interaction with Dhoni in 2022, when he was a young Mumbai Indians player, and how their association developed after he joined Chennai in 2025. The South African batter said the former India captain had made a lasting impression on him by taking the time to guide young players.

“Feels like a dream! From meeting you for the first time in 2022 as a young MI player, being so overwhelmed seeing you behind me at the crease, to sharing the CSK dressing room with you in 2025 and 2026,” Brevis wrote on Instagram.

“I’ll never forget how you took the time to speak to us young players after that first game and shared advice that has stayed with me ever since. What a journey and what a privilege! Congratulations on an incredible IPL career. Truly humbled to have you as a mentor at CSK,” Brevis added.

Brevis, who joined CSK in April 2025, has played 17 IPL matches for the franchise, scoring 376 runs at an average of 26.86 and a strike rate of 154.70. He has also been retained by Chennai ahead of the IPL 2027 auction, allowing him to continue playing under Dhoni’s guidance in his new role.

item.title: India inks contract with Israel for Barak missile system upgrade
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The Defence Ministry has signed a Rs 1,976.40-crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries to upgrade and manage obsolescence of the Barak point defence missile system on Indian Navy ships.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The defence ministry on Wednesday signed a contract worth nearly Rs 1,976 crore with Israel Aerospace Industries for upgrade and obsolescence management of Barak point defence missile system for the Indian Navy, officials said on Wednesday.

The upgrade of the system would ensure enhanced features and “potent range anti-air defence capability” of the Indian naval platforms.

As part of the contract, a “comprehensive upgrade” of hardware and software of the system would be undertaken, they said.

The Rs 1,976.40-crore contract between them, under “Other Capital Procurement Procedure”, was inked on November 18 in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi.

The ministry said it has signed the contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgrade and obsolescence management of Barak point defence missile system onboard Indian Navy ships.

item.title: Three seeded players crash out of girls’ singles at National Junior badminton championships
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Karnataka's Disha Santosh stunned third seed Adarshini Shri NB, while Maharashtra's Yashwi Patel defeated seventh seed Nakshatraa Jairaj to reach the girls' singles pre-quarterfinals at the National Junior Badminton Championships in Gangtok. Three other seeded players also exited
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Karnataka’s Disha Santosh upset third seed Adarshini Shri NB of Tamil Nadu, while Maharashtra’s Yashwi Patel defeated seventh seed Nakshatraa Jairaj to reach the girls’ singles pre-quarterfinals of the 49th Yonex-Sunrise National Junior (U-19) Badminton Championships in Gangtok on Wednesday.

Disha came from a game down to beat Adarshini 5-15, 15-10, 16-14, while Yashwi held her nerve in a three-game thriller against Nakshatraa to win 15-12, 12-15, 15-13.

The girls’ singles competition witnessed several upsets in the third round, with ninth seed Nishika Gokhe of Maharashtra, 10th seed Haasana Sree Mallavarapu of Andhra Pradesh and 15th seed Garima Kundu of Haryana also being knocked out.

Gokhe went down 15-10, 20-18 to Punjab’s Gursimrat Kaur Chahal, Haasana lost to Telangana’s Avni Govind 15-10, 17-15, while Garima was beaten 15-8, 11-15, 19-17 by Rajasthan’s Avni Rathore.

Important results:

Boys’ singles: Jagsher Singh Khangurra bt Sachin JT 15-13, 15-9; fourth seed Akhil Reddy Bobba bt Vedant Pahwa 10-15, 15-9, 15-13; Abhinav Garg bt Samuel Tamang 15-11, 15-5; Tanay Mehendale bt Porvash Prasad 15-8, 15-13.

Girls’ singles: Shaina Manimuthu bt Swati Nayak 15-5, 15-5; 11th seed Durga Esha Kandrapu bt Aaratrika Malik 15-6, 13-15, 15-4; Yashwi Patel bt seventh seed Nakshatraa Jairaj 15-12, 12-15, 15-13; Gursimrat Kaur Chahal bt ninth seed Nishika Gokhe 15-10, 20-18; Disha Santosh bt third seed Adarshini Shri NB 5-15, 15-10, 16-14; Avni Rathore bt 15th seed Garima Kundu 15-8, 11-15, 19-17; Avni Vikram Govind bt 10th seed Haasana Sree Mallavarapu 15-10, 17-15.

Mixed doubles: Amith Raj Natraj/Suhina Roy bt top seeds Sainunmawai Sailo/Dianka Waldia 15-13, 15-10; third seeds Punith S/Deepak Raj Aditi bt Vedant Pahwa/Joel Rana 15-9, 13-15, 15-12; Chaitanya Sehrawat/Ananya bt Showrya Kiran J/Keerthy Manchala 16-14, 15-12; Yash Soni/Mokshita Bharadwaj bt seventh seeds H Vaithianathan/J Ramesh 16-14, 15-12.

item.title: England beat Australia by 97 runs to clinch ODI series 2-1
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Ben Duckett's 133 and Sonny Baker's four-wicket haul powered England to a 97-run victory over Australia in the third ODI in Hobart. England clinched the three-match series 2-1 after recovering from an early 1-0 deficit
item.content:encoded:
Hobart (Australia): Ben Duckett and Sonny Baker played starring roles as England beat Australia by 97 runs to clinch the three-match one-day international (ODI) series 2-1 on Wednesday.

Duckett scored a century as the visitors piled up 328 all out in the third and final match at Hobart’s Bellerive Oval.

Australia were then bowled out for 231, with pacer Baker claiming four wickets and Liam Dawson taking three.

England’s victory came despite going 1-0 down earlier in the series. The visitors bounced back with a 135-run win in Adelaide on Sunday.

“It wasn’t an ideal start to the series. We have notoriously been a bit slow getting into series, but the way we bounced back in Adelaide and the performance we put in today, the boys should be really proud,” England captain Harry Brook said.

Duckett scored 133 off 115 balls on Wednesday after Brook won the toss and elected to bat.

The opening batter was eventually dismissed by a top edge, with Matt Renshaw taking the catch. Duckett attempted a slog sweep towards the shorter side of the ground but hit the ball straight up, allowing Josh Inglis to complete the catch.

Will Jacks contributed 59 for England, while Jack Edwards claimed four wickets for Australia and Renshaw took three.

Mahli Beardman, who claimed six wickets on debut in the first ODI, and Alex Carey came into Australia’s side in place of Riley Meredith and Adam Zampa.

Australia slumped to 5-2 in reply after losing Travis Head and Mitchell Marsh. The hosts were then reduced to 34-3 when Inglis was caught by Jordan Cox off Baker’s bowling.

Renshaw top-scored with 55 before being caught and bowled by Dawson, with the score at 108-4.

England sealed victory when Duckett caught Spencer Johnson off Brook’s bowling.

“Well played to England. They outplayed us, and there are lots of areas for us to work on. While we haven’t won and have been outplayed, I still have a lot of excitement about this group. It’s a good group of young lads. They’re on a journey, and the World Cup is still 12 months away, so it’s good to bring them in,” Australia captain Marsh said.

The two teams will begin their T20 series in Melbourne on Saturday.

item.title: Rangareddy crush Khammam as Sagar Kumar slams 96 in State U-16 league
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Nagarkurnool defeated Narayanpet by 80 runs in the Telangana Cricket Association State Under-16 League. Rangareddy, powered by Sagar Kumar's 96, registered a big win over Khammam, while Sangareddy, Mahabubnagar and Vikarabad also recorded victories
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Nagarkurnool registered an 80-run victory over Narayanpet in the Telangana Cricket Association State League (Under-16) Championship, Phase One, at One Champion Ground in Moinabad on Wednesday.

The scores:

Nagarkurnool 157/5 in 18 overs (M. Kyateswar Goud 39, Rithesh 31, Chintu 2/25) bt Narayanpet 77 in 17.2 overs (M. Nikhil 2/6, Jashwanth 2/11). Man of the match: Kyateswar Goud.

Sangareddy 138/3 in 20 overs (Srimaan Bharath 64) bt Gajwel 45 in 17.2 overs (Sai Pradyumna 3/3, Advik Katukuri 3/11). Man of the match: Srimaan Bharath.

Vikarabad 107/6 in 18 overs (Sai Pawar 34, Sai Advit 2/31) lost to Mahabubnagar 109/4 in 15.3 overs (Nithin Nayak 64, Mohammad Mudasir 2/15). Man of the match: Nithin Nayak.

Rangareddy 186/9 in 20 overs (Sagar Kumar 96, N. Karunya 41, Shaik Uzair Maqil 4/25, B. Srujan 2/35) bt Khammam 62 (Md Shoaib Uddin 3/12, Varshith Reddy 2/4, N. Karunya 2/7). Man of the match: Sagar Kumar.

Narayanpet 76 in 15.2 overs (Abhinay 31, K. Yashwanth 3/4, Charan 2/0, Guru Charan 2/10) lost to Vikarabad 77/4 in 8.4 overs (Charan 25, Srikanth 3/19). Man of the match: K. Yashwanth.

item.title: Congress MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy turns critic of Revanth government, questions neglect of Munugode
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Rythu Bandhu assistance be released and restricted to genuine cultivators
item.description: Munugode MLA Komatireddy Raj Gopal Reddy criticised Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy over alleged regional bias in fund allocation, stalled development works and unfulfilled poll promises. He demanded funds for Munugode, pension hikes and Rythu Bandhu assistance for genuine cultivators.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: Not the Opposition or citizens of the State, but Congress MLAs themselves have started questioning the Revanth Reddy government over delays in fulfilling poll promises. Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy found fault with the Chief Minister’s style of functioning, alleged regional bias in fund allocation and delays in fulfilling poll promises.

Reiterating his loyalty to the Congress and Rahul Gandhi, Raj Gopal Reddy said people were unhappy with three years of Congress rule and urged the Chief Minister to treat all regions equally.

Speaking at a programme in Munugode on Wednesday, Raj Gopal Reddy warned of launching another “Kurukshetra” (war) if Munugode continued to be denied development funds, indicating unease within the ruling party over its handling of constituency-level demands. “Is Telangana confined to Kodangal and Madhira? Give Kodangal Rs 20,000 crore if necessary. We have no objection. But why deny Munugode even Rs 500 crore?” he asked, taking strong exception to Revanth Reddy’s recent warning that he would crush those questioning funds to his constituency.

He said development works had stalled as contractors were abandoning projects over non-payment of bills. He cited delays in the Dindi lift irrigation project and the proposed 100-bed hospital at Choutuppal, besides inadequate funding for village tanks and water bodies in his fluoride-affected constituency.

Dismissing suggestions that his criticism was driven by denial of a Ministerial berth, Raj Gopal Reddy said he was not seeking any position but wanted funds for the development of his constituency. He asserted that pointing out government failures did not require an MLA from the Opposition. He alleged that Andhra contractors continued to dominate government works.

He also questioned the delay in implementing the Congress manifesto promise of Rs 4,000 monthly pensions, arguing that benefits should reach all eligible poor people. He demanded that Rythu Bandhu assistance be released and restricted to genuine cultivators, including tenant farmers.

item.title: Hyderabad fall short against Vidarbha in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad lost to Vidarbha by three wickets in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in Kolkata. The latest HCA league fixtures also featured action across Under-19 multi-day, A-Division, B-Division and C-Division competitions, along with the women’s T20 tournament
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Hyderabad suffered a three-wicket defeat against Vidarbha in the third-round match of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 cricket championship in Kolkata on Wednesday.

The scores:

Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 championship – Third round:

At Kolkata: Hyderabad 195/8 in 20 overs (Tanmay Agarwal 49, K Himateja 41) lost to Vidarbha 198/7 in 19.2 overs (Atharva Taide 82).

HCA Under-19 multi-day Super League:

Team D 351/9 in 75.4 overs and 125 in 38.5 overs (N Nitesh Naik 30, N Sudheev Venkat 4/34, Hishanth Prem Charan 5/28) lost to Team A 630/6 declared in 146 overs and 175/3 in 27.1 overs (P Advith Reddy 101 not out, Arjun Chandrasekhar 38).

Team C 322 in 90.2 overs and 173 in 53 overs lost to Team B 249 in 69.3 overs (Arhaan Satwalekar 58, Parth Sharma 42) and 432/5 in 83 overs (Aditya Malhotra 110, Arhaan Satwalekar 170 not out, Rohan Boppana 30, Aditya Vardhan 62 not out).

item.title: Raunil Kukar fires seven-under 65 to join Chouhan at SERVO Masters summit
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana's K. Sai Ratna Hasini Reddy clinched a double crown at the 11th National Deaf Sub-Junior Badminton Championship in Thiruvananthapuram. She won the girls' under-16 singles title and the mixed doubles crown partnering Arman
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Mhow’s Om Prakash Chouhan and Bengaluru-based Raunil Kukar shared the halfway lead at nine-under 135 after the second round of the 26th IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf, a ₹1-crore event being played at Digboi Golf Links in Digboi, Assam.

Forty-year-old Chouhan (67-68) carded a bogey-free four-under 68, featuring four birdies, to move up from tied second place.

Twenty-eight-year-old Kukar (70-65) climbed from tied 14th with a seven-under 65 comprising an eagle on the par-5 seventh, eight birdies and three bogeys to join Chouhan at the top.

Overnight leader Saurav Rathi (65-72) of Gurugram slipped to third at seven-under 137 after carding an even-par 72 featuring five birdies and five bogeys.

Four players shared fourth place at six-under 138: Bangladesh’s Jamal Hossain (69-69), Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh (68-70), Jaipur’s Prakhar Asawa (69-69) and Pune’s Divyansh Dubey (68-70).

Chouhan, an 11-time DP World PGTI winner, former European Challenge Tour (now HotelPlanner Tour) winner and 2023 DP World PGTI rankings champion, made the most of his opportunities on the greens.

He sank a 30-foot birdie putt on the first hole, converted another from 10 feet on the third and holed a 25-footer on the sixth. He added a tap-in birdie on the par-5 11th after reaching the green with a driver and a three-wood.

Playing his first event since the DP World India Championship almost a month ago, Chouhan said, “I am feeling great playing after almost a month’s break following the DP World India Championship. This is my first event since then, and I feel I am playing some of my best golf.

“I am feeling really good about my putting since switching back to my old putter. I have been focusing more on my putting, and it has been working well for me,” he said.

Kukar made an eagle on the par-5 seventh after a strong drive and a five-iron approach that finished on the apron of the green, leaving him with a straightforward chip.

The cut fell at two-over 146, with 51 players from the 120-man field advancing to the final two rounds.

item.title: MEIL raises USD 700 mn from global investment firms through structured financing
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.category: Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited Group
item.description: Hyderabad-based infrastructure major MEIL has raised approximately USD 700 million through a financing structure involving structured equity and proposed monetisation of its road assets. The investment, backed by global firms DK, HH and Varde Partners, values MEIL Group's businesses at around Rs 1 lakh crore.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Hyderabad-based infrastructure firm MEIL on Wednesday said it had raised USD 700 million from global investment firms DK, HH and Varde Partners.

The financing arrangement involves structured equity and the proposed monetisation of its road assets, the company said.

The company said the investment reflected the firms’ confidence in MEIL’s vision, diversified business interests and long-term growth prospects, according to a press release.

“Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited Group has raised approximately USD 700 million through an innovative financing structure involving structured equity and the proposed monetisation of its road assets,” the release said.

The confidence of global investors was also reflected in the valuations assigned to MEIL Group’s businesses, which were valued at approximately Rs 1 lakh crore, it said.

MEIL has business interests spanning irrigation, transportation, energy, oil and gas, manufacturing, clean mobility and advanced infrastructure.

item.title: Why Assam Tribunal declared a man a ‘streamline foreigner’ but recognised his family as Indians?
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: A Foreigners Tribunal in Assam's Cachar district has declared Mohan Lal Das a "streamline foreigner" while recognising his late wife Pramila Das and their children as Indian citizens after examining original documents and witness testimony. The tribunal's fresh order came after the Gauhati High Court allowed the family to submit original records for reconsideration.
item.content:encoded:
Guwahati: A Foreigners Tribunal in Assam’s Cachar district has declared a person a “streamline foreigner”, while holding his wife and children to be Indian citizens.

A ‘streamline foreigner’ in Assam is a legal classification for a person who entered the state from the erstwhile East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) between January 1, 1966 and March 24, 1971 without registering with the government.

The Foreigners Tribunal-4th Member Ranjan Roy passed an order on November 6 that Mohan Lal Das of Sayedpur village in Katigorah is a “streamline foreigner”, but pronounced his late wife Pramila Das and children as Indians.

“OP (opposite party) Mohan Lal Das is a streamline foreigner…. Puspa Bala Das, Suman Bala Das, Sudhan Das (Sredham Das) and Madhu Das are the sons and daughter of Pramila Das and are found Indians, not foreigners,” he added.

The tribunal noted that several cases related to the family were amalgamated for disposal by a common opinion.

Monmohini Das, mother of Mohan Lal, and Pramila Das expired during the pendency of the proceedings. Their names were struck off, and the cases were contested by the surviving members.

They submitted before the proceedings that Pramila Das and Mohan Lal Das had come to India in 1964 from East Pakistan.

Pramila claimed she had come with her father Jamini Kanta Das, whose arrival was recorded as October 6, 1964 at Silchar, and who got a Relief Eligibility Certificate from the Government of India, Ministry of Rehabilitation, on February 4, 1966.

Mohan Lal Das claimed he came on September 30, 1964, at Karimganj, got a similar Relief Eligibility Certificate on February 4, 1966, and later purchased land at Sayedpur vide registered deed no 2460, dated May 22, 1967.

The family produced voter lists from 1970 onwards, Relief Eligibility Certificates, the 1967 sale deed, birth certificates and voter identity cards.

The Tribunal had earlier declared them foreigners after they failed to prove the originals of their documents.

The Gauhati High Court, hearing a writ petition challenging the FT order, in September 2022 allowed them to submit all originals for fresh opinion.

Accordingly, the Tribunal examined the original documents and the statement of Dilip Kumar Das, brother of Pramila Das, who was examined on November 6, 2026.

Dilip Kumar Das exhibited the 1966 voter list in the name of his father Jamini Kanta Das. The FT found his statement “trustworthy and reliable” without any contradiction and not objected to by the state counsel.

The Tribunal said the Relief Eligibility Certificate in the name of Jamini Kanta Das, in which Pramila Das was shown as aged about 11 years, was not accepted as proof by itself, but the statement of Dilip Kumar Das and the voter lists established the linkage.

In conclusion, the FT held that all OPs except Mohan Lal Das were Indians, and Mohan Lal Das was found to be a “streamline foreigner”.

The order has been sent to Cachar’s District Commissioner and the Superintendent of Police (Border) for information and necessary action.

The Gauhati High Court on November 10 noted that 1,16,946 declared foreign nationals in Assam are yet to be apprehended and expelled, describing the situation as a “very grim picture” when it comes to the expulsion of foreigners in the state.

The Assam Assembly was informed on July 8 that 36,358 people were declared foreigners in the five years since 2021, and only 196 of them have been repatriated to Bangladesh till then.

item.title: Elderly woman allegedly killed by husband in Mancherial
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: An 80-year-old woman, Munjam Narsamma, was allegedly beaten to death by her husband, Lachchayya, following family disputes at Bheemaram village in Mancherial on Wednesday, police said. A case was registered on her son’s complaint.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: An elderly woman was allegedly killed by her husband following family disputes at Bheemaram village on Wednesday, police said.

Police said Munjam Narsamma, 80, was allegedly beaten to death with a spade by her husband, Lachchayya. She suffered serious head injuries, bled profusely and died at the spot, police said.

According to police, Lachchayya allegedly argued with Narsamma and attacked her in a fit of rage. He had allegedly been quarrelling with her over petty issues after being addicted to liquor for a long time.

Satyanarayana, Narsamma's son, lodged a complaint with police. A case was registered against Lachchayya.

In short

  • Munjam Narsamma, 80, was allegedly killed by her husband Lachchayya at Bheemaram village.
  • Police said Lachchayya allegedly attacked Narsamma following an argument over family disputes.
  • Police registered a case against Lachchayya after Narsamma’s son Satyanarayana lodged a complaint.

Readers ask

Who was accused in the woman’s death?

Police said Narsamma’s husband, Lachchayya, was accused of allegedly attacking her.

Where did the incident occur?

The incident occurred at Bheemaram village in Mancherial.

What action did police take?

Police registered a case against Lachchayya after Narsamma’s son Satyanarayana lodged a complaint.

item.title: Goa allows shops, malls and shopping complexes to operate 24/7 for three years
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The Goa government has allowed shops, shopping complexes and malls across the State to operate round-the-clock for three years. The Labour Department issued a notification permitting the move, subject to compliance with statutory provisions under the 2025 Act
item.content:encoded:
Panaji: The Goa government has allowed shops, shopping complexes and malls in the State to operate round-the-clock for three years.

The decision, which allows these establishments to cater to customers, including tourists, beyond conventional business hours, came into effect immediately.

The Labour Department on Tuesday issued a notification in this regard under the Goa Shops and Establishments (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 2025.

The permission will remain valid for three years unless revoked by the government.

The notification stated that the relaxation was subject to compliance with the statutory provisions of the Act.

Employers violating any statutory provision or condition will face action, it said.

item.title: Voters left out of draft rolls can seek inclusion before final list, says Telangana CEO
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The Election Commission of India has given another chance to voters excluded from Telangana's draft electoral rolls, particularly those marked under the ASDD category, to apply for inclusion before the final voter list is published. Enumeration forms will be distributed and collected from November 18-30, with the final electoral roll scheduled for publication on December 22.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad:  Telangana CEO C Sudharsan Reddy on Wednesday said the ECI has provided another opportunity to voters excluded from the draft electoral rolls to seek inclusion in the final list.

The opportunity is available to electors categorised as ASDD (Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate) in the draft electoral rolls published on August 17, 2026, following which the Commission has prescribed a fresh schedule for their enumeration.

“The Election Commission has extended another opportunity to eligible voters whose names were left out of the draft electoral rolls to get themselves included in the final list,” Reddy said in an official release.

According to Reddy, distribution and collection of enumeration forms will be carried out from November 18 to 30, while the processing of these forms will be completed by December 10.

The Commission has also revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Telangana.

The notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will continue until December 15, while publication of the final electoral roll is scheduled for December 22.

Electors seeking assistance have been advised to contact their respective Booth Level Officers (BLOs) or call the toll-free helpline number 1950.

item.title: Sai Ratna Hasini Reddy clinches double gold at National Deaf Sub-Junior Badminton Championship
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana's K. Sai Ratna Hasini Reddy clinched a double crown at the 11th National Deaf Sub-Junior Badminton Championship in Thiruvananthapuram. She won the girls' under-16 singles title and the mixed doubles crown partnering Arman
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: K. Sai Ratna Hasini Reddy of Telangana clinched a double crown by winning the girls’ under-16 singles title and the mixed doubles title at the 11th National Deaf Sub-Junior Badminton Championship in Thiruvananthapuram.

Sai Ratna, who trains at the Indian Badminton Academy in Manikonda, defeated Ruchitha Gowda of Karnataka 15-7, 15-4 in the singles final. She then partnered fellow Telangana player Arman to register a 15-7, 15-6 victory over Rahul and Sravya of Gujarat in the mixed doubles final.

item.title: Carpenter-turned-terrorist Lateef Bhat killed in Kashmir encounter
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, exactly a year after he is believed to have joined militancy. Police linked him to attacks and targeted killings in the region
item.content:encoded:
Kulgam (J-K): Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district on Wednesday, exactly one year after he is believed to have picked up the gun and become one of the Valley’s most wanted terrorists.

Bhat, who was in his 20s, was responsible for the attack on a CRPF post in south Kashmir’s Kulgam area on November 11, police said.

A week later, the youth from the Khrewan area of Kulgam was trapped inside a mosque, where he refused repeated appeals to surrender made by senior police and Army officers through video calls. The Army subsequently used tear gas to flush him out of hiding and shot him dead.

The cycle of violence that began on November 18, 2025, ended exactly a year later.

“I do not think there is a bigger success than this in 2026,” Superintendent of Police (SSP), Kulgam, Anayat Ali Chowdhary told reporters.

Terming the operation a major success, he said Bhat was heavily self-radicalised.

“After joining the banned organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba, he was receiving directions from across the border to disrupt peace here, hit tourism and damage the economy. You have all seen his three or four attacks and how ruthlessly he carried them out,” the SSP added.

Bhat had managed to give security forces the slip a few times in the past but was trapped effectively this time, he said.

He is suspected of killing a policeman in Anantnag on July 22, 2026, and is the prime suspect in the targeted killing of two non-local labourers from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam on July 31.

A former carpenter, Bhat completed Class 12 in 2021 and dropped out of college soon afterwards. He went missing in November last year and joined the LeT and its offshoot, The Resistance Front (TRF), officials said.

Security agencies had announced a reward of Rs 15 lakh for information leading to his capture. He leaves behind his parents, a brother and a married sister.

item.title: Telangana gears up to host Khelo India Youth Games 2026
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana Minister Vakiti Srihari unveiled the logo, mascot and brochure of the Khelo India Youth Games 2026 in Khammam. The Games will be held at various centres across the State from December 11 to 22
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Telangana Minister for Animal Husbandry, Dairy Development, Fisheries, Youth Services and Sports Vakiti Srihari unveiled the logo, mascot and brochure of the Khelo India Youth Games 2026 in Khammam.

The Games will be held at various centres across the State from December 11 to 22.

“Our aim is to make Telangana the sports capital of the country under the leadership of Chief Minister Revanth Reddy,” the Minister said.

District Collector Sri Diwakara, Additional Collector (Local Bodies) Dr P Sreeja, District Youth Services and Sports Officer Thumburu Sunil Kumar, In-charge DRDO Sirisha, District Animal Husbandry Officer Dr Purandhar, District Fisheries Officer Mallesham, Madhira Municipal Chairperson Sadhineni Sujatha, Market Committee Chairman Bandaru Narasimha Rao and others participated in the programme.

item.title: Delhi accident: Truck driver dies after vehicle overturns near flyover
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: A truck driver, identified as Pashupati, was killed after his vehicle mounted a divider and overturned near the Mukundpur flyover in north Delhi on Wednesday morning. The accident also disrupted traffic, while police began investigating its circumstances
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: A truck driver was killed after his vehicle mounted a road divider and overturned near the Mukundpur flyover in north Delhi on Wednesday morning, police said.

The deceased, Pashupati, a native of Bihar, is survived by four children, a senior police officer said.

The accident occurred when the truck, travelling from Kamla Market towards Khera, approached the Mukundpur flyover. The driver apparently failed to negotiate a turn and lost control of the vehicle, following which it mounted the divider and overturned, the officer said.

The impact was severe, leaving the truck’s cabin badly damaged and trapping the driver inside. He sustained critical injuries and died.

After receiving information, a police team reached the spot and initiated an investigation. A crane was deployed to remove the overturned truck and clear the road.

Vehicular movement on the Mukundpur flyover was affected for some time following the accident, causing inconvenience to commuters.

The police took custody of the body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Teams are examining the circumstances leading to the accident. Further investigation is underway.

item.title: Vijay inaugurates infrastructure projects, lays foundation stones for new works across Tamil Nadu
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay inaugurated infrastructure projects worth over Rs 430 crore across higher education, healthcare and civic utilities. The initiatives include college buildings, medical facilities, sewage treatment systems, water supply upgrades and solid waste management projects
item.content:encoded:
Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday inaugurated several infrastructure projects and laid foundation stones for new projects across the Higher Education, Health and Family Welfare, and Municipal Administration and Water Supply departments.

The initiatives, involving a total outlay of over Rs 430 crore across the State, aim to strengthen public service delivery, modernise academic institutions and upgrade essential urban and medical infrastructure, an official release said.

Under the Higher Education Department, projects worth over Rs 52.01 crore were launched to upgrade government institutions, including Presidency College in Chennai and various constituent colleges in districts.

These included completed buildings worth Rs 22.10 crore and foundation stones laid for new projects valued at Rs 29.91 crore.

The projects are aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps in institutions, fostering advanced research environments and providing students in urban and rural areas with better learning facilities to prepare them for future professional challenges.

The Health and Family Welfare Department rolled out major medical infrastructure projects worth over Rs 210.14 crore.

These initiatives focus on upgrading critical care facilities, modernising urban and rural health centres, and deploying advanced medical equipment under national healthcare frameworks such as the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM). The projects cover medical college hospitals and primary health centres in districts such as Madurai, Coimbatore, Salem and Tiruchirappalli.

The projects include upgrades to critical care blocks, triage and emergency wards, intensive care units (ICUs), and specialised paediatric and maternal care facilities. They are aimed at improving emergency response and ensuring access to quality healthcare for people in remote and underserved areas across Tamil Nadu.

The Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department also launched urban renewal and utility projects worth over Rs 174.97 crore.

These include completed projects worth Rs 12.11 crore and foundation stones laid for new projects valued at Rs 162.86 crore in urban local bodies, municipalities and corporations, including Chennai, Tambaram, Tiruppur and Vellore.

The works include sewage treatment systems using moving bed biofilm reactors and ultra-filtration technologies, improvements to water supply infrastructure and solid waste management projects.

Urban initiatives also include awards and recognition for outstanding performance in sanitation under State and national Swachh Survekshan frameworks.

item.title: Andhra Pradesh plans 5,000-acre semiconductor hub in Tirupati
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Andhra Pradesh has amended its semiconductor policy to align with the Centre’s Semicon 2.0 programme, offering additional capital support to chipmakers. The State plans a 5,000-acre semiconductor park in Tirupati, alongside investor facilitation, research and training initiatives
item.content:encoded:
Amaravati: The Andhra Pradesh government has amended its Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0 to align it with the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM Semicon 2.0), the Centre’s chip incentive programme.

Under the amendment, the State will match 100 per cent of the Centre’s capital support for silicon fabs, display fabs and chip packaging projects. The amendment was notified through a Government Order.

According to an official release on Wednesday, with the State’s additional support, a silicon fab approved under Semicon 2.0 can receive combined assistance of 80 per cent of its eligible capital cost: 40 per cent from the Government of India and 40 per cent from Andhra Pradesh. Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor, discrete and display fabs, as well as advanced packaging units, can receive 70 per cent. Legacy packaging units can receive 50 per cent.

The State’s comparison with other states shows that the 80 per cent support for silicon fabs is higher than the incentives offered by Odisha (65 per cent), Tamil Nadu (65 per cent), Uttar Pradesh (60 per cent), Madhya Pradesh (60 per cent) and Gujarat (56 per cent).

“Andhra Pradesh wants to be the place where India builds its chips, from design to fab to packaging. By matching the Centre’s support rupee for rupee, giving investors one window and building the talent they need, we are making it simpler and cheaper to build a fab here than anywhere else in the country,” said Nara Lokesh, Minister for HRD, IT and Electronics, Andhra Pradesh.

The amended policy covers all 10 Semicon 2.0 categories under six pillars: design, machines and materials, fabs, packaging, research and development, and talent.

Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) and Outsourced Assembly and Test (OSAT) units will receive State support matching 100 per cent of the Centre’s capital assistance.

For research and development and talent projects, the State will provide 25 per cent of the eligible project cost, with combined Centre and State support capped at 75 per cent.

Total State incentives are capped at 50 per cent of the eligible fixed capital investment, while support from all sources is capped at 90 per cent. The State’s share will be released after each tranche of assistance from the Centre, following the same schedule.

The State is planning a dedicated Andhra Pradesh Semiconductor Park spread across about 5,000 acres in Tirupati as a manufacturing and supplier cluster covering the entire value chain. It will be managed by a public-private park company with an investor-led board and up to three government nominees.

The park will offer developed land, shared industrial cleanrooms, high-voltage power with redundancy, ultrapure water, natural gas and specialty gases, effluent treatment and water recycling facilities, testing laboratories, logistics facilities, and research and training centres.

According to the release, the AP Semiconductor Growth and Innovation Council (APSGIC) will serve as a single point of contact for investors. It will have an Oversight Council chaired by the Chief Minister and a CEO-led Apex Committee of experts to appraise projects, recommend State incentives and facilitate clearances, land, power and water allocations, and coordination with the ISM and the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

The AP Semiconductor Research and Innovation Centre (AP-SRIC) will be a not-for-profit company with independent professional management. It will initially operate from IIT-Tirupati before moving to the park, with photonics as its first focus area.

The AP Semiconductor Training and Capacity Building Centre (AP-STCC) will be set up inside the park, with curricula designed in collaboration with industry and Andhra Pradesh universities. Companies will receive a training subsidy of Rs 10,000 per trainee per month for six months.

item.title: Hyderabad Entrepreneurship Summit on November 20
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Hyderabad Entrepreneurship Summit 2026 will be held on November 20 at HICC Novotel. Hosted by TiE Hyderabad, the event will bring together entrepreneurs, investors and policymakers to discuss business growth, investment, global expansion and opportunities for collaboration.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Hyderabad Entrepreneurship Summit (HES) 2026, hosted by TiE Hyderabad and promoted by the Hyderabad Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Collective (HEEC), will be held on November 20 at HICC Novotel, Hyderabad.

The summit will bring together entrepreneurs, investors, industry leaders, policymakers and ecosystem institutions to explore opportunities for enterprise creation, business growth, investment and global expansion.

Going beyond conventional conference discussions, HES 2026 aims to create meaningful connections between businesses and capital, markets, technology, knowledge and collaborative opportunities, strengthening Hyderabad’s position as a preferred destination for entrepreneurship and enterprise growth.

The HES Expo will showcase the entrepreneurial and technological capabilities of Hyderabad and Telangana, bringing together startups, technology companies, innovators and ecosystem partners.

item.title: COPD risk in India: Experts call for early diagnosis and smoking cessation support
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: On World COPD Day, experts stressed sustained smoking cessation support, early diagnosis and access to respiratory care. They identified smoking as a preventable risk factor and called for evaluation of approaches to reduce exposure among adults unable to quit
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: For millions of adults struggling to quit smoking, the risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a serious concern, with experts stressing the need for sustained smoking cessation support, early diagnosis and a science-led approach to reducing respiratory risks.

Cigarette smoking remains a major contributor to respiratory diseases, with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) attributing up to eight in 10 COPD-related deaths in the country to smoking.

A February 2026 meta-analysis of 23 studies involving 27,319 Indian adults found a pooled COPD prevalence of 37 per cent among smokers included in the studies.

COPD, which includes chronic bronchitis and emphysema, progressively obstructs airflow and can cause persistent breathlessness, cough, sputum production and reduced exercise tolerance.

The disease often remains undiagnosed until lung function has significantly deteriorated, making timely recognition and access to spirometry important.

Dr Pawan Gupta, Director of the Centre for Chest and Respiratory Diseases at BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi, said COPD was often detected late, when patients had already experienced a substantial decline in lung function.

“Persistent cough, sputum production or breathlessness should not be dismissed as routine consequences of ageing or smoking. Early evaluation, spirometry and appropriate treatment can help improve disease management. At the same time, helping people quit smoking must remain a central part of respiratory care,” Gupta said.

Experts said nicotine dependence could make quitting difficult, with many smokers making repeated unsuccessful attempts before achieving sustained abstinence. They emphasised the importance of accessible counselling, behavioural support and evidence-based smoking cessation treatment.

As a country advancing rapidly in science and healthcare, there was a need to approach this challenge more pragmatically, said Dr Chandramani Panjabi, Senior Consultant and Head of the Department of Pulmonology at Mata Chanan Devi Hospital, Delhi.

Countries such as Japan, the US and the UK have adopted different regulatory approaches to evaluating and making science- and technology-based alternatives available to adult smokers, he said.

“These experiences offer important lessons for India as we examine the evolving global scientific evidence. While quitting smoking completely remains the best outcome, we should also consider how appropriately regulated, evidence-based alternatives could help adults who are unable to quit move away from combustible cigarettes, reduce their exposure to harmful substances and protect their long-term health,” Panjabi said.

“Our response must move beyond awareness to sustained quitting support, scientific evaluation and a more comprehensive approach to addressing the smoking challenge,” he added.

Experts also cautioned that COPD was not caused by smoking alone. Exposure to household air pollution, occupational dust and fumes, and other environmental pollutants could contribute to the disease burden. However, smoking combustible cigarettes exposes the lungs to a complex mixture of toxic substances and remains a major preventable risk factor.

Dr Amir Nadeem, Consultant and Respiratory and Critical Care Specialist at Regency Hospital, Gorakhpur, said people who smoke should not wait for severe symptoms before seeking medical advice, particularly if they have persistent respiratory complaints or a history of prolonged smoking.

“COPD prevention must begin with reducing exposure to tobacco smoke, but for those who find quitting difficult, repeated support rather than blame is essential,” he said.

“A practical approach should combine smoking cessation services, early assessment of symptoms and lung function testing with measures to reduce other environmental and occupational exposures. The goal should be to identify disease earlier, prevent further lung damage and ensure that people at risk receive timely, evidence-based care,” he added.

On World COPD Day, experts said addressing the disease required more than awareness campaigns. Strengthening early diagnosis, improving access to respiratory care and supporting smokers through sustained cessation interventions would be essential to reducing the burden of COPD in India.

item.title: St. Joseph’s College emerge champions in OU women’s tennis tournament
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: St. Joseph’s College defeated St. Francis College 2-1 to win the Osmania University inter-college women’s tennis tournament. Bhavan’s College secured third place with a 2-0 victory over Villa Marie College for Women in the classification match
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: St. Joseph’s College defeated St. Francis College 2-1 in the final of the Osmania University inter-college women’s tennis tournament here.

Final: St. Joseph’s College bt St. Francis College 2-1 (Sowmya lost to Sai Ananya 2-6; Chevika bt Hasini 6-2; Sowmya and Chevika bt Sai Ananya and Hasini 6-3).

Third place: Bhavan’s College bt Villa Marie College for Women 2-0 (Kushi bt Khyati 6-1; Hanshika bt P. Aashritha 6-2).

item.title: YSRCP workers protest as police stop nomination rally in Andhra Pradesh
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Tension prevailed in Pulivendula during Gram Panchayat nomination filings after police stopped a YSRCP rally and issued a notice directing Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy not to venture out amid concerns over possible clashes and alleged arrests of Sarpanch candidates
item.content:encoded:
Amaravati: Tension prevailed in a village in Andhra Pradesh’s YSR Kadapa district on Wednesday during the filing of nominations for Gram Panchayat elections.

Police stopped a rally of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which had started from the residence of its state general secretary Satish Reddy to file a nomination in Vempalli village in Pulivendula, the home constituency of YSRCP president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.

Citing prohibitory orders in force, police stopped the rally of YSRCP functionaries. Police officials told them that they could not go in a group to file a nomination.

YSRCP workers sat on the road in protest against the police action. They made it clear that they would not leave without filing the nomination.

Satish Reddy’s brother, Vishnuvardhan, staged a dharna against the police action.

Amid tension in Pulivendula and in view of the violent incidents reported during the nomination process for municipal and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections, the police issued a notice to Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy.

The YSRCP MP was directed not to venture out, citing the possibility of clashes during the filing of nominations for Gram Panchayat elections.

A police officer visited the MP’s residence to serve the notice.

The police said the measure was taken as a precaution to prevent any untoward incidents and maintain law and order.

Avinash Reddy, a cousin of Jagan Mohan Reddy, questioned the police action. He asked a police officer whether they had received orders from above to stall the nomination process.

The MP also questioned the alleged illegal arrests of Sarpanch candidates in Pulivendula mandal.

According to the YSRCP, in Simhadripuram mandal, police took into custody Ramanaiah, a candidate for the post of Sarpanch, along with his proposer, Shiva Pratap, and another person, Babu, from Devatapuram.

The MP confronted the police, demanding to know why candidates were being prevented from filing their nominations.

item.title: 12 years on, Amannagar bomb blast remains unsolved
item.dc:creator: Asif Yar Khan
item.description: A crude bomb explosion in Amannagar, also known as Bhavaninagar, injured two people on May 6, 2014. Despite an extensive police investigation and enquiries into a possible link to a passing train, the case remains unsolved nearly 12 years later.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: It was Tuesday night, May 6, 2014, in the middle of summer. The police across the Old City were on alert in view of the approaching anniversary of the Mecca Masjid blast.

In the densely populated slum of Amannagar, also known as Bhavaninagar, residents were jolted awake by a loud, thunderous explosion. When they rushed out of their homes, they found that two people had been injured in the blast. Within minutes, panic gripped the locality, and police vehicles rushed to the spot to ascertain what had happened in an area then considered highly communally sensitive.

Senior police officials rushed to the scene and began supervising the investigation. The two persons, Shaik Abdullah (80) and Mohd Salman (35), who had sustained injuries from the shrapnel, were questioned. However, neither of the injured persons had seen anyone throwing any object.

The police suspected that the explosion was caused by a ‘throw-down’ bomb containing crude explosive material. It was a crude, handmade device, with explosives and sharp nails wrapped in paper and sealed with duct tape.

Senior officials, including the then Deputy Commissioner of Police, Sarvashresth Tripathi, visited the spot. The Task Force and the Special Investigation Team (SIT) of the Hyderabad police combed the area for possible mischief-makers. Forensic teams, the bomb detection squad and local explosives experts also examined the spot for clues.

The incident, reported just 12 days before the anniversary of the Mecca Masjid blast, prompted the police to step up security. For the next fortnight, the police remained busy searching for suspects who might have thrown the bomb or triggered the explosion. In the absence of closed-circuit cameras in the area at the time, the police questioned several suspects.

As the spot was just a stone’s throw from the railway tracks, the police also made enquiries with railway officials to ascertain how many trains had passed through the stretch around the time of the explosion.

The police later suspected that someone might have thrown the bomb from a moving train and escaped. A case was registered at the Bhavaninagar police station, but the investigation came to a halt in the absence of any concrete clues. Nearly 12 years later, the case remains unsolved.

item.title: Caste Census panel invites YSRCP chief Jagan to Delhi protest
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: The All India Caste Census Coordination Committee invited YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy to join its November 28 Delhi protest seeking a comprehensive caste census and stronger protection for BC and OBC reservation rights.
item.content:encoded:
Tadepalli: The All India Caste Census Coordination Committee has invited former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party President Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy to its protest in New Delhi on November 28.

Members of the committee met Reddy at the party’s central office in Tadepalli and invited him to the ‘Chalo Ramlila Maidan’ protest.

They sought his solidarity and personal participation in demanding a comprehensive caste census to protect BC and OBC reservation rights. Reddy responded positively to the request.

The coalition of various OBC associations across the country and other civil society groups has been demanding that the Centre reconsider its methodology for caste enumeration in the 2027 Census to ensure a comprehensive and accurate caste census.

The delegation included Delhi University Professor Suraj Mandal, grandson of former Mandal Commission Chairman B.P. Mandal; All India OBC Students Association National President Goud Kiran Kumar; Sakal OBC Mahamorcha President Umesh Kurram; Pitti Mallikarjun Yadav; and leaders Rakesh Datta, Pendem Jayanthi Yadav and Rajanikanth Goud. YSRCP State Coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy also attended the meeting.

Addressing the media, Mandal demanded a separate OBC column and a caste-wise dropdown menu in the national census to ensure accurate enumeration and equitable reservation benefits. He said the absence of comprehensive BC data had prevented the Andhra Pradesh High Court from permitting increased reservations in local body elections.

Kiran Kumar said the committee brought together 60 OBC organisations nationwide, including groups from Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, representing communities from Kashmir to Kerala.

He demanded that all OBC communities be enumerated through a comprehensive caste census, with social conditions properly recorded, similar to the enumeration of SCs and STs. He said the committee was approaching political parties outside the NDA for support.

He said reliable caste-wise data was essential to challenge the 50 per cent reservation ceiling and defend BC reservation rights in courts.

In short

  • The All India Caste Census Coordination Committee invited Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy to its November 28 protest at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.
  • The committee sought Reddy’s solidarity and personal participation in demanding a comprehensive caste census to protect BC and OBC reservation rights.
  • Committee members demanded a separate OBC column and caste-wise dropdown menu in the 2027 Census.

Readers ask

Why was Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy invited to the protest?

The committee sought his solidarity and personal participation in demanding a comprehensive caste census to protect BC and OBC reservation rights.

When and where will the protest be held?

The ‘Chalo Ramlila Maidan’ protest will be held in New Delhi on November 28.

What changes does the committee seek in the census?

The committee demanded a separate OBC column and a caste-wise dropdown menu for comprehensive and accurate enumeration.

item.title: Joseph Academy announces two-day football tournament in Alwal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Joseph Academy will organise a two-day football tournament on November 28 and 29 at Kick n Hit Sports Arena in Alwal, Hyderabad. The competition will feature five age categories, from under-9 to under-17, with limited entries available
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Joseph Academy will organise the Joseph Football Tournament on November 28 and 29 at Kick n Hit Sports Arena, Alwal, in the under-9, under-11, under-13, under-15 and under-17 age categories.

Entries are limited. For details, contact Titus Stevenson on 7396554113.

item.title: Telangana’s Syed Akbar Ali Abidi clears AFC A Diploma coaching course
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Former national footballer Syed Akbar Ali Abidi has cleared the AFC A Diploma coaching course conducted in Mohali, Punjab, from March 1 to October 25. The Telangana Football Association congratulated him on the achievement, which saw eight successful candidates
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Former national footballer Syed Akbar Ali Abidi has successfully qualified for the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) A Diploma coaching course.

The Telangana Football Association (TFA) congratulated Abidi on completing the course.

The course was conducted in Mohali, Punjab, from March 1 to October 25.

Of the 24 coaches who participated from across India, only eight successfully cleared the course, making the achievement particularly noteworthy.

“This remarkable accomplishment reflects Syed Akbar Ali Abidi’s (Assistant Manager, SBI) dedication, hard work and commitment to the development of football. His achievement is a matter of pride for the Telangana football fraternity,” the TFA said in a statement on Wednesday.

“We wish him continued success in his coaching career and hope that he will make significant contributions towards the growth and development of football in Telangana and across the country.”

item.title: NEET paper leak trial to begin on November 25, says Delhi court
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: A Delhi court has ordered the framing of charges against 14 accused in the NEET paper leak case. The accused will appear on November 21, while the day-to-day trial is scheduled to begin on November 25
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: A Delhi court on Wednesday ordered the framing of charges against 14 accused in the NEET paper leak case.

Special Judge Ajay Gupta directed that the accused be produced before the court on November 21 for the formal framing of charges.

The court ordered the framing of charges for offences including criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, destruction of evidence and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act.

The court also ordered the framing of charges against all the accused under Section 63 of the Copyright Act for copyright infringement.

The judge said the court would begin the trial on a day-to-day basis from November 25.

A detailed order is awaited.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) had earlier filed a chargesheet against 13 accused in the fast-track court dealing with “criminal cases arising from paper leaks as well as the use of other unfair means in public examinations”.

The agency also filed a supplementary chargesheet against the 14th accused, Sheshrav Bajrang Suryawanshi alias Raj Suryawanshi, a resident of Nanded in Maharashtra, who was arrested on September 2.

The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for medical aspirants.

On May 12, the NTA cancelled the examination scheduled for May 3 amid allegations of a paper leak. A re-examination was conducted on June 21.

item.title: Arshdeep shines in ICC rankings after New Zealand ODI series
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: India pacer Arshdeep Singh climbed 12 places to share 19th position with Axar Patel in the latest ICC ODI bowling rankings. Rohit Sharma slipped to fifth in batting charts, while England's Tom Banton made significant gains
item.content:encoded:
Dubai: India pacer Arshdeep Singh on Wednesday gained 12 places to be tied 19th with teammate Axar Patel in the ODI bowling rankings.

Arshdeep impressed in the five-match series against New Zealand. Spinner Kuldeep Yadav, who played only one game in the series, dropped eight places to 15th. There is no Indian bowler in the top 10 of the rankings.

In the batting rankings, Rohit Sharma dropped one place to fifth following a lean series against New Zealand. Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli retained their first and third positions, respectively.

England opening batter Tom Banton climbed 34 places to 13th after scoring a match-winning century against Australia.

Banton struck 121 off 99 deliveries in the second ODI in Adelaide to help England level the three-match series at 1-1. The innings lifted him to a career-high ranking and gave England four batters inside the top 13.

Ben Duckett slipped one place to seventh, while Joe Root gained two spots to ninth after scoring 62 off 68 balls in the same match. Harry Brook dropped four places to 12th.

New Zealand opening batter Will Young also made progress after scoring 125 off 108 balls in the fourth ODI against India at Mount Maunganui. Despite New Zealand losing their seven-year unbeaten home record in ODI series, Young’s innings helped him rise 15 places to 30th in the batting rankings.

item.title: India enter Blind Cricket Asia Cup final after dominant win over Bangladesh
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.category: Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026
item.description: India beat Bangladesh by eight wickets on Wednesday to reach the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind final. Sunil Ramesh scored an unbeaten 63, guiding the chase of 124 in 13.2 overs and setting up a title clash against Pakistan
item.content:encoded:
Dhaka: India stormed into the final of the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026 after registering a convincing eight-wicket victory over hosts Bangladesh in Dhaka on Wednesday, setting up a title clash against archrivals Pakistan on November 20.

India will have an opportunity to avenge their narrow one-wicket defeat to Pakistan in the league stage when the two sides meet in the final.

After winning the toss and opting to field, India restricted Bangladesh to 123/7 in their allotted 20 overs with a disciplined bowling and fielding effort.

Indian captain T Durga Rao led the attack with figures of 1/10 in three overs, while Lokesha, Debaraj Behera and Sunil Ramesh claimed a wicket each. The Indian fielders also contributed by effecting three run-outs to prevent the hosts from posting a challenging total.

Muhammad Tahafiz was Bangladesh’s highest scorer with an unbeaten 36 off 30 deliveries.

In reply, India made light work of the 124-run target, reaching 124/2 in just 13.2 overs to seal an eight-wicket victory with 40 balls to spare.

Sunil Ramesh was the star performer with the bat, smashing an unbeaten 63 off 41 deliveries, including seven boundaries. He maintained a strike rate of 153.66 to guide India comfortably towards the target.

Sanjay Kumar Shah provided valuable support with 32 off 25 balls, while Sukhram remained unbeaten on 20 off 15 deliveries as India completed a dominant chase.

Speaking ahead of the final, Indian captain Durga Rao said the team was confident of putting up a strong performance against Pakistan after learning from its previous defeat.

“We played well against Bangladesh, and this win gives us confidence going into the final. We lost to Pakistan by just one wicket in the league match, so we know how close the competition is between the two teams. We have learned from that match and will focus on playing our best on November 20,” he said.

Dr Mahantesh G K, chairman of the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), congratulated the players on reaching the final and expressed confidence in their ability to win the championship.

“Congratulations to the Indian Men’s Cricket Team for the Blind on reaching the Asia Cup final. The team has played excellently throughout the tournament, and today’s victory against Bangladesh reflects their preparation and commitment,” he said.

“The close league-stage match against Pakistan showed that both teams are strong competitors, and I am confident our players will give their best in the final. I extend my best wishes to Captain Durga and the entire Indian team for the final. We hope to see India lift the Asia Cup once again,” he added.

item.title: Prehistoric rock art site found near Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A prehistoric rock art site has been identified in a forest area near Ponnal village in Medchal–Malkajgiri district. The red-pigment paintings depict human figures, animals, hunting scenes and geometric motifs, offering insights into the lives of ancient communities.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A rare prehistoric rock painting dating approximately between 5,000 and 2,500 years ago has been identified by Kondaveeti Gopi, Research Scholar, Maulana Azad National Urdu University (MANUU), in the forest region of Ponnal village of Shamirpet mandal in Medchal–Malkajgiri district.

Kondaveeti Gopi, along with Mohammed Naseeruddin, an independent researcher and local guides identified this site.

Numerous ancient paintings in red pigment have been found on the inner ceiling of a naturally formed rock shelter within a massive granite rock formation. These paintings mainly depict human figures, hunting scenes, various wild animals, geometric patterns and abstract designs.

They serve as valuable evidence for understanding the lifestyle, artistic skills and relationship with nature of prehistoric human communities. The hunting scenes provide interesting insights into the hunting methods, community life and subsistence activities of prehistoric humans.

Several geometric and abstract designs — star-like or sun-like motifs, square-shaped patterns with loops on all four sides, hourglass-shaped or damaru-like symbols, and curved zigzag lines — are also visible.

According to Prof Salma Ahmed Farooqui, Director, CDS, Gopi is pursuing research on the Megalithic Culture of the Godavari Basin at MANUU, Hyderabad and has been conducting field-based studies on ancient stone structures, burial monuments, rock paintings and prehistoric cultures. Last year, he also discovered a rock art site of significant prehistoric value near Palwancha in Bhadradri Kothagudem district.

item.title: Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of insulting India abroad
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: BJP president Nitin Nabin accused Rahul Gandhi of insulting India internationally by criticising its economy, despite global institutions acknowledging its growth. He cited India's economic progress and accused the Congress leader of attempting to spread anarchy both domestically and abroad.
item.content:encoded:
Jalandhar: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin on Wednesday accused Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi of “insulting” India at global platforms despite institutions like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank acknowledging the nation’s economic progress.

This comes after Gandhi criticised the state of India’s economy while speaking at Columbia University in the United States, describing the country as sitting on an “economic disaster”. He also alleged that India was facing “massive” unemployment and serious problems in its education system.

Speaking to reporters during his visit to Punjab’s Jalandhar, Nabin said: “Rahul Gandhi Ji is calling India’s economy a ‘disaster.’ He questioned all the constitutional institutions of the country.”
