“Today, I want to ask Rahul Gandhi ji, all the financial institutions of the world, be it the World Bank, the IMF, or other institutions, acknowledge India’s growth at the global level, stating that despite this global instability, India is the fastest-growing country. Today, we are moving forward with a growth rate of 7.1 per cent, and we are progressing in accordance with international standards. Yet, he sees a ‘disaster’ economy,” the BJP president added.

Moreover, Nabin remarked, “I believe that somewhere, there is a disaster going on inside his (Rahul Gandhi’s) own mind. His family is unable to grow, his party is unable to grow, he himself is unable to grow, so he considers that a disaster.”

Reiterating that several renowned institutions have acknowledged India’s economic progress, the BJP chief said: “The country’s per capita income has also increased but he (Rahul Gandhi) cannot see this development. We are now exporting (technology) worth more than 38,000 crore in the defence sector, yet he can’t see this growth and instead questions it on international platform.”

Referring to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s tenure as the Leader of Opposition, Nabin said: “When Atal ji went to attend programmes on global platforms, he spoke about India’s goodwill.”

“However, now it is the country’s misfortune that we have got an LoP (Rahul Gandhi) who insults India at international platforms, even as Prime Minister Narendra Modi works to uphold the nation’s flag and sovereignty at the global level,” he remarked.

Adding to his criticism of the LoP, the BJP chief said: “Rahul Gandhi, your intention of spreading anarchy in India by coming across as a foreign toolkit, will never be fulfilled. You want to bring Europe’s message to India, but ours is the nation which guides the world.”

Nabin added that the LoP “failed to create an atmosphere of anarchy” in India and accused him of now attempting to do the same abroad.

“But the world too will now witness your (Rahul Gandhi’s) failure,” the BJP leader said.

item.title: Rickelton, Rabada and Bavuma power South Africa to 557 against Bangladesh
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Ryan Rickelton scored 102 as South Africa posted 557 against Bangladesh in the first Test at the Wanderers. Kagiso Rabada and Temba Bavuma hit half-centuries, helping the hosts secure a commanding 157-run first-innings lead on Day 4
item.content:encoded:
Johannesburg: Ryan Rickelton’s century helped South Africa take a commanding 157-run first-innings lead on Day 4 of the first Test against Bangladesh at the Wanderers on Wednesday.

Rickelton’s knock of 102, combined with half-centuries from Kagiso Rabada and skipper Temba Bavuma, saw the Proteas bowled out for 557 at lunch in reply to Bangladesh’s total of 400.

Rabada scored 72, with 10 fours and two sixes, and put on 117 runs with Rickelton for the eighth wicket. It was his second Test half-century.

Bavuma, who had to retire hurt on the previous day, returned to score 68 not out. Despite being hampered by restricted movement, he put on 45 runs for the 10th wicket with Dane Paterson (29).

Rickelton reached his fourth Test century off 159 balls. Overall, he faced 165 deliveries and hit 13 fours before being stumped off Mehidy Hasan Miraz.

In between, Miraz had Rabada stumped. Hasan Mahmud bowled Paterson on the stroke of lunch, but it was a no-ball, and the session was extended by 30 minutes because the final wicket was still remaining.

Ebadot Hossain finally removed Paterson to end the innings. The hosts scored 171 runs in the morning session.

item.title: IIIT Junction flyover works gather pace after monsoon in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Sunil Mungara
item.description: Construction of the 3.39-km multi-level interchange at Gachibowli’s IIIT Junction has gained momentum after the monsoon. With 43 of 54 foundational pillars completed, the project aims to ease congestion and improve connectivity across Hyderabad’s IT corridor.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: With the monsoon finally receding, the ground-level construction of the multi-level interchange at Gachibowli’s IIIT Junction has shifted into top gear, marking a decisive post-monsoon push to decongest Hyderabad’s bustling IT corridor.

Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) officials told ‘Telangana Today’ that of the 54 foundational pillars, the work on 43 pillars was complete, with heavy structural concrete beam installation underway for three interconnected steel flyover stretches at Gachibowli.

The CMC is building a 3.39-km signal-free network under the Hyderabad City and Innovative Transformative (H-CITI) project to eliminate one of the IT corridor’s worst traffic bottlenecks. The network comprises three elevated steel flyovers and a six-lane underpass.

The Level-1 Bi-Directional Flyover is a 720-metre, four-lane corridor to handle two-way traffic between ISB Road and DLF Road. Five edge pillars along the flyover are engineered to support Level-1 and Level-2 structures, allowing two curved upper-level flyovers — ISB Road to Gachibowli (1.20 km) and DLF Road to Lingampally (948 metres). The dual-level design reduces land acquisition and overall costs, officials said.

Level-2 Unidirectional Flyover (DLF to Lingampally) spans 948 metres and uses a shared double-decker pier system, with five dual-load edge pillars on the lower deck and dedicated landing pillars along the Serilingampally–Gachibowli Stadium stretch, easing movement toward Lingampally and Gachibowli Stadium.

Meanwhile, another Level-2 Unidirectional Flyover is a 1.2-km, three-lane elevated stretch for commuters from ISB Road towards Gachibowli and Indira Nagar. The longest of the three elevated structures at the junction, it follows a second-tier, or upper-deck, alignment and uses prefabricated structural steel girders. It is engineered to carry right-turning traffic over the lower Level-1 flyover without signal stops.

“The HCITI project, targeted for completion by May 2027, is expected to reduce peak-hour travel times by 10 to 15 minutes for nearly 4 to 5 lakh daily commuters between HITEC City, Financial District, Kokapet and Lingampally and would streamline access to DLF, ISB, Financial District and Outer Ring Road,” said CMC officials.

item.title: Snapchat, crypto used to run Hyderabad drug network; three arrested
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana Eagle Force has busted an alleged drug trafficking network that used Snapchat to receive orders and cryptocurrency for payments. Three persons were arrested, with police seizing marijuana, OG Kush, mobile phones and a car during the operation.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Using Snapchat accounts to receive drug orders and cryptocurrency to handle payments, a gang allegedly operated an organised marijuana and OG Kush trafficking network across the city, supplying narcotics to hundreds of consumers.

The Telangana Eagle Force has busted the network and arrested three persons, seizing 1.24 kg of marijuana, 16.59 grams of OG Kush, three mobile phones and a car.

The arrested persons were identified as Mohammed Idres Kaleem alias Farhan of Tolichowki, Syed Abbas Husaini of Asif Nagar and Mohammed Sheikh, a cab driver from Golconda.

The alleged kingpin, Idres, and Abbas reportedly operated Snapchat accounts under the names ‘OGdude420’ and ‘Dude OG 420’ to communicate with customers, receive orders and coordinate drug supplies.

According to Hyderabad Narcotics Police, the accused claimed to have supplied OG Kush to around 800 to 900 consumers through their online contacts. After their earlier Snapchat account was blocked, they allegedly created another account and continued their operations.

Officials said that Idres and Sheikh procured bulk quantities of marijuana and OG Kush from an alleged supplier, Shaik Farhan, based in Mumbai. The contraband was transported to Hyderabad by bus. Idres allegedly repacked the drugs into sachets of approximately 5 gm and handed them over to Sheikh, who delivered them to customers at different locations. Idres and Abbas reportedly managed orders through Snapchat.

The racket came to light after police received information about the suspects transporting narcotics in a car from Lanco Hills towards a hotel in Manikonda and nabbed them. A significant breakthrough came during the examination of the accused’s digital transactions.

Police found indications that Idres used cryptocurrency to pay suppliers and collect money from customers. Preliminary analysis identified approximately 150 cryptocurrency transactions involving around 60 consumers.

item.title: New Zealand suffer injury blow as Mitchell Santner misses India Tests
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: New Zealand all-rounder Mitchell Santner has been ruled out of the two-Test series against India after fracturing his right hand during the fifth ODI. Dean Foxcroft has been named as his replacement in the New Zealand squad
item.content:encoded:
Christchurch: New Zealand have suffered an injury blow, with Mitchell Santner ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series against India due to a fracture in his right hand.

Santner sustained the injury after being struck on the hand while batting during the fifth ODI in Mount Maunganui. Scans have since revealed that the 34-year-old has fractured his right hand.

The injury has forced him to miss the two Tests against India, which begin in Wellington on Thursday. Moreover, he will be racing against time to be fit for the four-match series against Australia, which starts on December 9.

“Scans have revealed that Santner has fractured his right hand. His return-to-play timeline is being worked through, and his involvement in the Test series against Australia will be updated in due course,” New Zealand Cricket said on Tuesday.

NZC have added spin-bowling all-rounder Dean Foxcroft to the squad as Santner’s replacement. Foxcroft made his Test debut against Ireland in May.

The 28-year-old has played one Test, against Ireland in Belfast in May, ahead of New Zealand’s three-Test tour of England. He scored 98 in New Zealand’s innings victory in Belfast but returned home thereafter, with Santner, who was then recovering from a shoulder injury, taking his place in the Test squad for England.

The first Test starts on Thursday at Wellington’s Cello Basin Reserve, followed by the second at Christchurch’s Hagley Oval on November 27.

New Zealand currently sit at the top of the World Test Championship standings and will be looking to replicate their most recent Test series against India, when they recorded an upset 3-0 series triumph over the Asian side on the subcontinent in 2024.

New Zealand squad: Tom Latham (c), Tom Blundell, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Dean Foxcroft, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner, Will Young.

item.title: Watch: Bike catches fire at Kukatpally fuel station; motorist injured
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 25-year-old motorist suffered severe burn injuries after his motorcycle caught fire at a Kukatpally fuel station. Staff moved the burning vehicle away and stopped fuel transfer from an oil tanker, averting a potentially major disaster.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: A major mishap was averted at a fuel station in Kukatpally on Tuesday afternoon after a motorist’s bike caught fire. The motorist, however, sustained severe burn injuries in the incident.

According to reports, the 25-year-old biker had arrived at the fuel station to refuel his bike and lit a cigarette when it suddenly caught fire. The flames quickly spread to his bike, triggering panic at the station.

The fuel station workers immediately moved the burning bike out of the premises and doused the flames using fire extinguishers. The injured man was shifted to a hospital in an ambulance.

At the time of the incident, an oil tanker was unloading fuel into the underground storage tanks at the station. However, the staff immediately stopped the fuel transfer, preventing the fire from spreading to the tanker and averting a potentially major disaster. Further details are awaited.

item.title: Mancherial teenager dies by suicide after parents reportedly reprimand her
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 16-year-old Intermediate first-year student died by suicide at her residence in Erraguntapalli village in Mancherial district on Wednesday. She was reportedly reluctant to stay in a hostel, following which her parents had reprimanded her, police said
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: An Intermediate first year student died by suicide after her parents reportedly reprimanded for her reluctance to stay in a hostel at Erraguntapalli village on Wednesday.

Police said that Nalla Ravali (16), the daughter of Mahesh from the village, resorted to the drastic step by hanging at her residence. She was studying at Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya in Jaipur. She was reportedly disinterested in staying in a hostel. Her parents reprimanded her for saying no to the hostel.

Mahesh, a shepherd lodged a complaint with the police. A case has been registered.

item.title: Hyderabad to get IMAX screenings again after a decade from December 18
item.dc:creator: Yuvraj Akula
item.description: Hyderabad is set to welcome IMAX screenings again after nearly a decade. AMB Victory Cinemas at RTC Cross Roads will launch its IMAX with Laser screen on December 18 with Dune: Part Three, marking the city's return to large-format cinema.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The wait for Hyderabad’s cinephiles to once again experience IMAX movies is set to end as two screens are returning the format to the city after a long gap of 10 years.

The Asian Cinemas, which entered into an agreement with IMAX Corporation to set up three state-of-the-art IMAX with laser screens in the country via AMB Cinemas this year, is set to launch the format at AMB Victory Cinemas, RTC Cross Roads.

The IMAX screen will open for screening on December 18, with Hollywood’s movie Dune: Part Three. However, the theatre did not list showtimes and seats.

This theatre has already been listed on the official IMAX website. The city is expected to have one more IMAX screen at AMB Cinemas at Hakimpet, while location of another such screen has not yet been disclosed.

The AMB Victory Cinemas, a joint collaboration between Asian Cinemas and actors G Mahesh Babu and his wife Namrata Shirodkar, will comprise one IMAX with laser screen, a 4DX screen and five regular screens.

The AMB Victory Cinemas replaces the Sudarshan Theatre, once a familiar name among moviegoers in the city. Founded and inaugurated by T Narsimhulu on August 15, 1970, this theatre was part of the city’s movie culture much before the advent of the multiplex system. However, after years of operation, the theatre faced several challenges and was ultimately demolished in 2010, reportedly due to financial losses.

Hyderabad’s tryst with IMAX cinema had begun at Prasads Multiplex, which introduced the city to the large-format movie experience. However, the multiplex discontinued screening the films in the original IMAX format after the shift from film reels to digital projection in 2015.

Earlier, movies were released with an IMAX print (reel) that was projected at Prasads multiplex through the IMAX analogue projector. As the digitisation forayed into movie making, the format changed to digital. Now, films are no longer released in reels, considering the cost of processing and logistics of reels and instead are released via digital mediums.

item.title: Rupee closes higher at 93.44 despite strong dollar and market weakness
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The rupee gained 7 paise to close at 93.44 against the US dollar on Wednesday. Lower crude oil prices supported the currency, while a strong dollar, geopolitical tensions and weakness in domestic equities limited its gains
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The rupee pared some of its initial gains and settled 7 paise higher at 93.44 (provisional) against the US dollar on Wednesday, as a decline in domestic equity markets and a strong greenback played spoilsport, despite support from lower crude oil prices.

Forex traders said the rupee reversed its morning gains amid risk aversion in global markets due to fresh geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran, coupled with a strong dollar.

However, a sharp fall in crude oil prices supported the Indian currency.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.47 against the dollar. During intra-day trade, it touched a high of 93.25 and a low of 93.57. The local unit settled at 93.44 (provisional), up 7 paise from its previous close.

On Tuesday, the rupee gained 43 paise to close at a seven-month high of 93.51 against the US dollar.

“The Indian rupee reversed morning gains on a decline in domestic markets from higher levels and a strong dollar. The dollar rose to a fresh 19-month high on hawkish comments by Fed officials and renewed geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran. However, a sharp fall in crude oil prices cushioned the downside,” said Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan.

“We expect the rupee to trade with a slight negative bias amid risk aversion in global markets due to fresh geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran and a strong dollar. Expectations of a US Fed rate hike may also weigh on the rupee. However, weakness in global crude oil prices may support the rupee by easing import bills. Traders may take cues from US housing market data,” Choudhary added.

Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback’s strength against a basket of six currencies, stood at 103.79, up 0.30 per cent.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.46 per cent lower at USD 92.71 per barrel in futures trade.

In the domestic equity market, the Sensex dropped 500.38 points to settle at 82,031.81, while the Nifty declined 159.45 points to 25,227.95.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 4,195.38 crore on Tuesday, according to exchange data.

item.title: HYDRAA warning fails to move unsafe hostels in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Sunil Mungara
item.category: Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA)
item.description: Despite HYDRAA's warning to vacate unsafe buildings within three months, several hostel operators in Hyderabad and Cyberabad remain reluctant to relocate. Residents continue to live in cramped rooms with inadequate ventilation, narrow staircases and limited emergency escape options.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Safety warnings issued by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) appear to have fallen on deaf ears, as several hostel managements in Hyderabad and Cyberabad remain reluctant to vacate unsafe premises or implement mandatory safety protocols.

Following the collapse of an illegally constructed seven-storey building intended as a hostel at Anjaiah Nagar in Gachibowli, killing two workers in the month of August, HYDRAA Commissioner AV Ranganath had instructed hostel operators to relocate from unsafe buildings to structurally sound premises within three months and implement measures to protect inmates.

Ranganath had warned that inspections would begin on January 1 and buildings at risk of collapse would be demolished.

However, several hostel operators in Anjaiah Nagar, Gachibowli, said they were unwilling to vacate their premises as they had taken them on lease for one to three years after paying lakhs of rupees. They said complying with HYDRAA’s caution could lead to the closure of hostels across Hyderabad and Cyberabad because most lacked safety measures.

A few thousand hostels, with narrow staircases, cramped rooms that are shared by two to four inmates, provide accommodation for new IT professionals, trainees, private-sector employees and housekeeping staff. Facilities include breakfast, lunch and dinner, while some women’s hostels also provide separate kitchens.

Thousands of students and young professionals living in private hostels in the city face suffocating and hazardous conditions, with these small living spaces lacking basic ventilation. Despite steep rents, most residents live in tiny, stifling spaces. Undersized lifts and dangerously narrow staircases further increase risks, offering little scope for a quick escape during emergencies, while safety norms remain widely ignored.

A few hostellers said they had no option but to stay in pigeon-box rooms with choked vents and narrow exits because monthly rents were comparatively affordable. Some occupants alleged that management profited from them while operating hostels with no safety measures, leaving thousands trapped in suffocating buildings without safe exits.

Despite repeated alerts over structural risks and encroachment hazards, operators continue to accommodate students and working professionals in the same buildings.

item.title: Air India Express appoints Deepak Rajawat to lead airline’s next growth phase
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Air India Express has appointed its Chief Financial Officer Deepak Rajawat as CEO, effective December 1, 2026. A veteran aviation and finance professional, Rajawat previously held key leadership positions at Vistara, including Chief Commercial Officer
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Air India Express on Wednesday announced the appointment of its Chief Financial Officer, Deepak Rajawat, as the airline’s Chief Executive Officer, effective December 1, 2026.

Rajawat will take over the top role after leading the airline’s finance function and supporting its growth and transformation initiatives during a period of rapid expansion within the Air India group.

“The Board of Directors of Air India Express today announced the appointment of Deepak Rajawat as the airline’s Chief Executive Officer, effective December 1, 2026,” the airline said.

“Deepak, who currently serves as the airline’s Chief Financial Officer, will transition into the role following his successful tenure leading the company’s finance function and supporting the airline’s growth and transformation journey,” it added.

A seasoned aviation and finance professional with more than two decades of experience, Rajawat brings expertise in financial management, commercial operations and strategic planning.

Since joining Air India Express as CFO, he has played a key role in strengthening the airline’s financial position while contributing to its expansion and integration efforts.

Before joining Air India Express, Rajawat was associated with Vistara since its inception and held several leadership positions spanning corporate planning, aircraft acquisition and finance.

He later served as Vistara’s Chief Commercial Officer, overseeing revenue management, network planning, sales and distribution, alliances and partnerships, product development, inflight services, marketing, branding and customer experience.

During his tenure, Vistara grew to become India’s second-largest airline by domestic market share and earned global recognition, ranking among the world’s top airlines in the Skytrax rankings, placing 20th in 2022 and 16th in both 2023 and 2024.

Commenting on the appointment, Nipun Aggarwal, Chairman of Air India Express, said, “Deepak brings a rare combination of financial expertise, commercial acumen and deep aviation experience, built over more than a decade across the Tata group’s airlines.”

Deepak Rajawat, incoming Chief Executive Officer of Air India Express, said, “I am honoured to assume this responsibility at an exciting stage in Air India Express’ journey. Having been part of the Tata group’s aviation ecosystem through Vistara and now Air India Express, I have had the privilege of witnessing first-hand the evolution of Indian aviation over the past decade.”

item.title: KT Rama Rao questions Revanth government over Andhra’s alleged 9 TMCft water diversion
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao accused the Revanth Reddy government of ignoring Andhra Pradesh's alleged 9 TMCft Krishna water diversion project. He threatened a legal battle and public agitation, demanding immediate intervention by the KRMB to protect Telangana's water rights
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao questioned the Revanth Reddy government’s failure to detect and act against Andhra Pradesh’s alleged project to divert 9 TMCft of Krishna River water from Nagarjuna Sagar project. He asked how the project went undetected for a year and sought answers on government’s silence. He warned of public agitation and legal battle to protect Telangana’s water rights.

Raising serious questions over the government’s silence, Rama Rao asked whether Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy was unaware of the project or was deliberately turning a blind eye to it. He also questioned whether the government approached the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB), lodged a complaint or taken any steps to prevent the alleged unauthorised withdrawal. He accused the government of allowing Telangana’s water interests to be compromised while AP proceeded with its project.

“How could such a massive project underway for nearly a year had escaped the attention of the Chief Minister, the Irrigation Minister who hails from the same district, intelligence agencies and irrigation officials? Or they knowingly turned a blind eye?,” he asked, addressing a press conference at Telangana Bhavan on Wednesday.

The BRS working president raised a series of questions on the government’s response, including whether it had approached the KRMB to stop the proposed diversion, sought allocation of the remaining 40 TMCft for Telangana’s drinking water needs or made any special arrangements to protect the State’s rights on Krishna River water.

He also sought details of the water allocated for drinking purposes to Hyderabad, Nalgonda, Mahabubnagar and Khammam districts and the quantities being reserved in Srisailam and Nagarjuna Sagar projects for the same. With borewells failing to yield water in several areas, he questioned how the government could remain indifferent to an alleged attempt to divert 9 TMCft.

Rama Rao opined that the government was either deliberately looking the other way or was constrained by political considerations. He suspected that the project was proceeding with the government’s knowledge and under Revanth Reddy’s watch, but the Chief Minister was choosing to feign ignorance because of pressure from influential quarters and political mentors.

The BRS working president said Andhra Pradesh had taken up the diversion in the name of a drinking water scheme, without obtaining the necessary permissions, and was attempting to draw water even from the dead storage of Nagarjuna Sagar project. He accused the Centre of backing Andhra Pradesh in this regard and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu and Revanth Reddy were collectively doing injustice to Telangana.

He also questioned Telangana’s diminishing voice in the KRMB, alleging that the State had virtually lost effective representation in the river management body. He pointed out that former IAS officer Adityanath Das who created obstacles for Telangana irrigation projects during his stint in Andhra Pradesh was appointed as Irrigation advisor of the State, while the government appointed and extended term of the Engineer-in-Chief who hails from Vijayawada.

Training his guns at eight BJP MPs and two union Ministers from Telangana, the former Minister asked why they were silent when the State’s water interests were being compromised. They should press the Centre to intervene and ensure that the KRMB stopped Andhra Pradesh’s project, he said.

Rama Rao said the BRS will write to the KRMB seeking immediate intervention and take the issue to the Centre. If the government fails to stop the project, he declared that the party will pursue a legal battle and also launch a people’s movement, beginning with meetings in erstwhile Nalgonda and Mahabubnagar districts to mobilise farmers and people.

Further, he accused the Congress government of reversing the gains made in Palamuru region under the previous BRS regime. He said nearly eight lakh acres in the district received irrigation water during the BRS government and that the Palamuru-Rangareddy lift irrigation project had been conceived to meet both irrigation and drinking water requirements. He alleged that Congress leaders filed several court cases to obstruct the project.

The BRS working president said the K Chandrashekhar Rao government also established the Tummilla lift irrigation scheme to compensate for the losses suffered by the Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme (RDS) and protect its ayacut. Accusing the Congress of pushing Palamuru back into distress, he said the district, which had once witnessed large-scale migration, began attracting people from other districts during the BRS regime.

Questioning why Telangana farmers were facing a crop holiday when farmers in Andhra Pradesh were not confronted with a similar situation, Rama Rao accused the Revanth government of failing to protect the State’s irrigation interests. He said the Congress government was inflicting greater injustice on Telangana than the erstwhile united Andhra Pradesh rulers and said the people of Palamuru were once again bearing the consequences of the government’s policies.

Warning that the BRS would not watch silently as Telangana’s water rights were compromised, he said the Congress government might have its political compulsions, but his party had none when it came to defending the State’s water rights. The fight would continue until the alleged diversion was stopped, he added.

item.title: BIMTECH partners with Niva Bupa to launch Joint Certification Programme 3.0
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BIMTECH, Greater Noida, has partnered with Niva Bupa Health Insurance to launch Joint Certification Programme 3.0. The initiative will provide 10 hours of classroom training to PGDM Insurance Business Management students, covering key aspects of the insurance industry
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Birla Institute of Management Technology (BIMTECH), Greater Noida, has signed a MoU with Niva Bupa Health Insurance (NBHI) to launch the Joint Certification Programme (JCP 3.0), a strategic industry–academia initiative aimed at enhancing the professional competencies and industry readiness of students enrolled in BIMTECH’s Post Graduate Diploma in Management – Insurance Business Management (PGDM–IBM) programme.

The launch and MoU signing ceremony was attended by BIMTECH Director, Dr. Prabina Rajib, Deputy Director, Prof. (Dr.) Pankaj Priya, and Registrar, Dr. T. V. Raman along with

Ishwar Dutt Sharma, Executive Vice President and Head – Talent Academy, and Rishika Verma, Head – Campus Relations, Talent Academy.

The JCP 3.0 curriculum designed and to be delivered by subject-matter experts from Niva Bupa Health Insurance will comprise 10 hours of structured, face-to-face classroom training at BIMTECH, covering eight important learning areas of Insurance Industry and Health Insurance, Fundamentals of Insurance, Insurance Products, Health Insurance Underwriting and Claims, Customer Service, Insurance Analytics, Organisational Culture and Future Readiness and Careers in Insurance.

item.title: Rajapet police arrest four for alleged ganja sale, seize 100 grams
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Rajapet police apprehended four persons allegedly involved in ganja sales and seized 100 grams of the contraband packed in small pouches. The suspects reportedly purchased the ganja from Hyderabad's Dhoolpet and transported it to Rajapet for consumption and sale
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Rajapet police on Tuesday apprehended four persons allegedly involved in selling ganja and seized 100 grams of the contraband packed in small pouches from them.

Acting on a tip-off, a police team led by Rajapet Sub-Inspector Mohd Thakiuddin apprehended Gangu Karthik Reddy (21), Dubbasi Dinesh (21), Venkatapuram John (19) and Katkuri Raju (20), all residents of Rajapet mandal in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district.

“During questioning, the four suspects told the police that they had purchased the ganja from Dhoolpet in Hyderabad and transported it to Rajapet for personal consumption and sale,” said Thakiuddin. A case was registered under the NDPS Act.

item.title: India target record fourth title at Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Defending champions India will target a record fourth title at the Women's Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal. Fresh from Asian Games gold and a fifth-place World Cup finish, the hosts open their campaign against Malaysia on Thursday
item.content:encoded:
Bhopal: Riding on a landmark season highlighted by an Asian Games gold medal and a fifth-place finish at the World Cup, defending champions India will look to cap the year on a high when the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy gets underway here on Thursday.

The hosts, who begin their campaign against Malaysia on Thursday, will be chasing a record fourth title in the six-team tournament, having won the previous two editions in Ranchi and Rajgir.

India are currently the joint most successful team in the competition alongside South Korea, with three titles each, and will have an opportunity to move ahead of the Koreans with another triumph on home soil.

Under chief coach Sjoerd Marijne, the Indian team comes into the tournament on the back of an impressive run of results, having qualified for the World Cup through the qualifiers in Hyderabad, won the FIH Women’s Nations Cup in Auckland to earn promotion to the Pro League, and finished fifth at the World Cup in Belgium, their best performance in the competition since 1974.

The team’s biggest achievement, however, came at the Asian Games in Japan last month, where it ended a 44-year wait for gold in women’s hockey at the continental showpiece.

India will be keen to carry that momentum into the tournament, which will be played at the newly built International Sports Complex in Nathu Barkheda, marking Madhya Pradesh’s first international hockey tournament.

The hosts have already sounded a warning to their rivals with a 4-1 victory over Japan in a practice match.

Marijne, meanwhile, is keen to use the competition to build greater depth in the squad by experimenting with players in different positions.

“We want the players to be able to play in different positions. It’s to create more depth in the squad and become helpful if a player gets injured, especially in a tournament like the Olympics,” he said.

India captain Salima Tete said the team would remain focused on its own game rather than worry about the opposition.

“We are not focusing on what our opponents are doing. We are just focusing on ourselves, our structure, and following the coach’s instructions. In short, we want to play our game,” she said.

However, India will face stiff competition from continental heavyweights China, Japan and South Korea in the round-robin league.

World No. 4 China, who lost to India in the Asian Games final, will be determined to make amends and secure their maiden title in the competition. The Chinese will pose the biggest challenge to the hosts with their quality and consistency.

South Korea, with three titles to their credit, will also be eager to reclaim the crown, while two-time champions Japan will bank on their defensive organisation and quick passing game to challenge the leading contenders.

Malaysia and Thailand complete the six-team field and will look to spring a surprise, with the compact round-robin format leaving little room for error.

The top four teams after the league stage will qualify for the semifinals, scheduled for November 27, while the final and third-place playoff will be played on November 28.

India will face South Korea on November 21, Thailand on November 22, China on November 24 and Japan on November 25 after their opening fixture against Malaysia.

The tournament will conclude on November 28.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: Everything to know about the highly anticipated game
item.dc:creator: AP
item.description: After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto VI launches amid enormous anticipation, returning players to Vice City. The game features two protagonists, an expansive Florida-inspired world and a new storyline, while its release has sparked promotional campaigns and awards attention
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles: After a 13-year wait, one of entertainment’s biggest releases is finally here.

‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ launches Thursday, sending players back to Vice City and testing whether Rockstar Games can follow one of the best-selling video games ever made with another cultural and commercial phenomenon.

The latest instalment becomes playable at midnight local time on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, meaning players in Asia and other regions will begin entering the game hours before its US release.

New Zealand will be among the first countries where players can access the game, and internet providers there are preparing for a surge in downloads as midnight arrives.

“The game file size at 212 gigabytes is unprecedented,” said Kurt Rodgers, network strategy manager for Chorus New Zealand. “That’s more than a quarter of the average household’s data usage in an entire month, all in one go.”

The company expects about 35 petabytes of additional traffic across its network, which Rodgers called “enormous”.

The expectations are enormous, too.

The ‘Grand Theft Auto’ franchise has sold more than 470 million units worldwide, while ‘Grand Theft Auto V’, released in 2013, accounts for more than 230 million of those sales and reached $1 billion in retail sales in just three days.

Rockstar is returning to Vice City, its fictionalised version of Miami, with two new protagonists, a sprawling Florida-inspired world and the pressure of following a game that became one of the most successful entertainment products ever released.

Game returns to Vice City after 13 years

At the centre of ‘GTA VI’ are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple whose attempts to improve their lives pull them deeper into the criminal underworld of Leonida, Rockstar’s fictionalised version of Florida.

Lucia has recently been released from prison, while Jason is a former soldier who became involved with drug runners in the Leonida Keys. When a criminal job goes wrong, the pair become entangled in a wider conspiracy.

Their relationship marks one of the biggest departures from ‘Grand Theft Auto V’, which followed three playable protagonists.

Rockstar has promoted Leonida as its largest and most detailed open world yet, stretching beyond Vice City into beaches, highways, wetlands, nightlife districts and smaller communities inspired by South Florida. Developers immersed themselves in the region while building the game, driving through Miami, the Florida Keys and surrounding communities. They flew over the Everglades and researched the area’s history and architecture.

Miami embraces its fictional alter ego

Miami and surrounding communities have leaned into their connection to Vice City ahead of the release, with businesses, sports teams and local governments using the game’s arrival as a marketing opportunity.

Miami-Dade County entered into a $3.9 million promotional deal with Rockstar that includes a giant “Welcome to Vice City” display atop the Miami Heat’s Kaseya Center. The NBA team is also scheduled to wear black-and-pink Vice City uniforms on the eve of the game’s release.

The campaign has not been universally welcomed. Some South Florida officials have questioned whether public resources should be used to promote a franchise known for car theft, gunplay and other criminal activity.

Supporters have argued that the enormous attention surrounding ‘GTA VI’ gives the region an opportunity to capitalise on a global spotlight.

In Seoul, a giant advertisement draped the side of a building, while Warner Music will host a party at a bar on Thursday themed around the game’s soundtrack.

Years of hype arrive on launch day

Few entertainment releases arrive with this much anticipation.

The first ‘GTA VI’ trailer drew more than 93 million YouTube views in its first 24 hours, while Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent company, has said the second trailer generated more than 475 million views across platforms in a day.

The game has also attracted awards attention before most players have had a chance to explore it.

‘GTA VI’ received eight nominations on Tuesday for the Game Awards, including game of the year, game direction, narrative, art direction, score and music, audio design, action/adventure and performance. The awards will be presented on December 10.

The long wait is partly a product of the extraordinary staying power of its predecessor. ‘Grand Theft Auto Online’, the multiplayer component of ‘GTA V’, has kept players engaged for years through updates, activities and in-game purchases.

Music has long been woven into the ‘Grand Theft Auto’ experience, with fictional radio stations and carefully curated soundtracks accompanying players as they drive through the series’ cities.

For ‘GTA VI’, Rockstar commissioned an original adaptive score from Grammy-winning French electronic duo Justice. The music is designed to shift depending on where players are and what they are doing. A 30-track ‘Grand Theft Auto VI: Original Score’ is scheduled for release on December 11 and includes collaborations involving Tame Impala, SZA, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard and Gesaffelstein.

What players will find next

Despite years of trailers and promotional material, Rockstar has kept significant portions of ‘GTA VI’ under wraps.

The full voice cast has not been revealed, including the performers behind Lucia and Jason. Actor Stephen Root has confirmed to The Associated Press that he appears in the game, though Rockstar has not publicly identified his role.

Questions also remain about the full range of characters, locations, activities and gameplay systems waiting inside Leonida.

Those answers will begin emerging first from players in Asia and Europe as midnight arrives in their regions, followed by North America hours later.

Associated Press journalists Charlotte Graham-McLay in Wellington, New Zealand, and Tong-hyung Kim in Seoul contributed to this report.

item.title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu, Raj Nidimoru perform puja ahead of welcoming first child
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu shared pictures from an intimate puja ceremony performed with husband Raj Nidimoru at home. The couple sought blessings from elders ahead of welcoming their first child, while Samantha also shared a playful pregnancy update online
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu recently performed a puja ceremony at home with her husband, filmmaker Raj Nidimoru, ahead of welcoming their first child.

The intimate ceremony appeared to have been attended by close family members and loved ones. Samantha took to Instagram to share glimpses of the special occasion. In one picture, Samantha is seen dressed in a traditional red suit, while Raj opted for a cream-coloured kurta paired with white pyjamas. The couple shared a candid moment, lovingly looking at each other with their backs towards the camera.

Other pictures showed Samantha seeking blessings from her elders and posing with family members. She also shared glimpses of the couple performing the puja rituals at home. The pictures offered a peek into their personal celebrations as they prepare to embrace a new chapter in their lives.

In some pictures, the couple is seen posing with family members. In another frame, the mom-to-be is seen sitting among women who appear to be showering her with blessings. The ‘Oo Antava’ actress simply captioned the post, “Us”.

Samantha is reportedly in the ninth month of her pregnancy and is preparing to welcome her first child with husband Raj Nidimoru. The actress also shared a playful update through her Instagram Stories by posting a meme featuring a pregnant woman enjoying some snacks.

The text on the video asked, “What are your plans this week?” followed by a humorous response listing the plan for every day, from Monday to Sunday, as “Maybe have a baby”.

For the unversed, Samantha Ruth Prabhu and filmmaker Raj Nidimoru tied the knot on December 1, 2025, in a private ceremony held at the Isha Foundation in Coimbatore.

Samantha announced her pregnancy in June 2026 during the success meet of her film ‘Maa Inti Bangaaram’. The actress also spoke about her plans to take a break from acting to focus on motherhood after completing her existing professional commitments. Speaking at the event, Samantha said, “After Maa Inti Bangaaram, I will have to take a small break, given my condition. I’ll have to take maternity leave. After that, I’ll be back with another film for my fans.”

item.title: Supreme Court seeks CJP response on plea to denotify Ramlila Maidan as protest site
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The Supreme Court sought responses from political parties, the Centre, Delhi government and police on traders’ plea to denotify Ramlila Maidan as a protest site, citing business disruptions. The court will hear the matter on November 27
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought responses from the Congress, Cockroach Janata Party, All India Students Association (AISA) and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on an amended plea filed by traders’ bodies seeking to denotify Ramlila Maidan as a designated protest site, claiming that agitations undermined their right to conduct business.

On November 3, the top court had asked the Delhi Kirana Committee and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association to make the organisations holding protests parties to the petition.

During the festival season, the traders’ bodies had sought a halt to protests at Ramlila Maidan in central Delhi, arguing that designated protest sites could not be occupied “for all times to come”.

On Wednesday, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the amended plea and submissions made by senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for the traders’ bodies, and issued notices to the parties.

The bench also issued notices to the Centre, the Delhi government and the Delhi Police Commissioner.

The bench said it would hear the traders’ plea and petitions asserting the right to protest on November 27.

It also said that competing fundamental rights — the right to protest and the right to conduct business — must be balanced.

The CJI said he would notify hearing dates for separate categories of cases related to recent protests in Delhi and elsewhere.

Rohatgi raised concerns over protests disrupting business activities in and around wholesale markets near Ramlila Maidan.

item.title: Bancroft says Australia teammates knew about sandpaper operation in South Africa
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Cameron Bancroft has alleged that the entire Australian team knew about the 2018 sandpaper scandal in South Africa. He admitted withholding details during Cricket Australia’s investigation and said he became the scapegoat for an incident involving more players
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Former Australia opener Cameron Bancroft, who was caught applying sandpaper to the ball during the 2018 tour of South Africa, has alleged that the entire team was aware of the ball-tampering operation, claiming that he ultimately became the “scapegoat” for an incident that went beyond the three players initially punished.

Bancroft broke his eight-year silence on the scandal, revealing that he had withheld crucial details during Cricket Australia’s investigation and questioning the version of events presented by his former teammates.

Revisiting the aftermath of the infamous Cape Town Test, Bancroft claimed that nobody at a meeting involving the entire team stood up to deny knowing about the use of sandpaper. He also pointed to wicketkeeper Peter Handscomb’s involvement after the latter was caught on camera as evidence that the operation was not unknown to the dressing room.

“Peter Handscomb ran out at the drinks break after I’d been caught and shoved the sandpaper down my pants. He said to me: ‘I think it’s time I take that off you now’. And Pete was doing his job after Boof shouted to him on the walkie-talkie, ‘get the f***ing sandpaper off Bangers now’.

“In my opinion, if he didn’t know, he wouldn’t have said that. And if it wasn’t clear enough before, then it was obvious now. Once again. WE ALL KNEW,” Bancroft wrote in a 4,000-word column for The West Australian on Wednesday.

Bancroft ended his account by saying that he had carried the burden of the incident for years and believed the responsibility had been placed disproportionately on him.

“As it turns out, I ended up becoming the scapegoat for the entire team,” he said.

The 33-year-old also admitted that his earlier account to Cricket Australia’s investigators was incomplete, saying he had withheld important information about when the use of sandpaper began, how long it continued and who else was aware of it.

“It was not just the three of us — Steve Smith, David Warner and I — who knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in South Africa. It was the whole team.

“When I was questioned during Cricket Australia’s investigation, I did not give a complete and truthful account. I withheld important details, including when the use of sandpaper began, how long it went on for, and the involvement and awareness of others,” Bancroft said.

Bancroft identified the second Test in Port Elizabeth as the first instance of sandpaper being used, claiming that discussions about generating reverse swing involved bowling coach David Saker and head coach Darren Lehmann.

He alleged that David Warner suggested using sandpaper but could not carry out the plan himself because of the attention he attracted from television cameras. According to Bancroft, Steve Smith made it clear that he wanted no part in the plan.

Bancroft said he knew the act was cheating but, as a young player in the side, saw it as an opportunity to contribute. The practice, he alleged, continued into the third Test in Cape Town, with Saker again approaching him about using sandpaper. Bancroft claimed that the bowlers repeatedly indicated that his efforts to alter the ball were insufficient.

“They all told me what I was doing wasn’t enough,” he said.

The former opener also expressed anger over public statements made by his teammates in the years after the scandal. He singled out a 2021 joint statement by Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, in which the bowlers said they had no knowledge of sandpaper being brought onto the field. Bancroft described the statement as deeply painful.

Bancroft said Cummins’ recent media conference was the final trigger for him to make his account public, particularly after Usman Khawaja’s comments brought the episode back into focus.

“It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone,” he said.

He also expressed regret over the press conference he attended alongside Smith after the day’s play in Cape Town. Bancroft claimed that they were frightened about the potential consequences and had been instructed by Saker and other staff members not to identify the foreign object as sandpaper.

Bancroft received a nine-month suspension for his role in the incident, while Smith and Warner were handed 12-month bans. He said the episode continued to affect his career and that he had not played for Australia since 2019, when Justin Langer was the coach.

“My cricket career has been destroyed and I have never been able to play for my country since Justin Langer was coach in 2019.

“But I have reached a point where continuing to protect an incomplete account of events feels more damaging than the truth,” the Australian stated.

item.title: India face uphill task against New Zealand in Wellington Test series
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: India face a challenging two-Test series against New Zealand in Wellington, with a green Basin Reserve pitch expected to favour fast bowlers. Shubman Gill's captaincy and India's pace combination will be crucial as they seek to revive their WTC final hopes
item.content:encoded:
Wellington: Skipper Shubman Gill’s tactical nous and ability to withstand pressure will be put to the test when India make a desperate bid to stay in contention for the World Test Championship (WTC) final in a two-match series against New Zealand beginning here on Thursday. A green top awaits the pace-heavy line-ups at the Basin Reserve.

This is a series India can ill afford to lose, as they need at least six wins from their remaining seven matches to qualify for the WTC final.

“I feel if we win these two Tests, we will have a very good chance of qualifying for the final,” Gill told reporters 48 hours before the start of the opening Test.

But New Zealand at home are a different proposition, and the conditions make them even more dangerous.

Facing a 6-foot-8-inch Kyle Jamieson, a 6-foot-5-inch Jacob Duffy and the fast and furious Matt Henry, who recently troubled them, the Indian batting unit will need something more than technique.

It will need copious amounts of grit.

Not just the skipper, but Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal and the peerless Rishabh Pant will also need to bring their A game.

When Gill began his stint as Test captain in England in 2025, it was a different challenge for him as both a batter and a leader.

Eighteen months down the line, he has firmly settled into the hot seat, and an away series in New Zealand is the kind of challenge that every captain worth his salt aspires to take on.

His strategic moves will go a long way in setting the tone on a track that is expected to flatten out after the first two days.

Gill has been winning plenty of tosses, and he will be hoping to win another important one on Thursday. He would want his in-form bowling attack to make the most of a track that is expected to have an unprecedented 15-inch grass cover.

Gill had indicated that he would prefer playing four fast bowlers, which could mean that seam-bowling all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy is not a certainty for the match.

Luckily for Gill, he has head coach Gautam Gambhir as his ally. Gambhir has always believed in an “all-or-nothing” philosophy.

The move could prove to be a masterstroke, but if at least three of the seven batters fail to produce substantial performances, it could backfire on Gill and Gambhir.

However, the team management appears ready to take the gamble.

Test matches are won by taking 20 wickets, and India’s biggest challenge will be to select the quartet best suited to exploit the conditions, taking into account the assistance on offer during the first two days and the flatter surface expected over the next three.

While Jasprit Bumrah is a certainty, Mohammed Siraj’s place in the playing XI appears uncertain in the current circumstances.

India want a tall bowler who can hit the deck on the third and fourth days, and Prasidh Krishna, with his experience, might be better placed than young pacer Gurnoor Brar.

The team management’s confidence in Siraj may have taken a hit following his underwhelming returns in Colombo.

Little wonder, then, that the in-form Anshul Kamboj and the skiddy Akash Deep were made to bowl from both ends of the Basin Reserve during an open net session two days before the match. Bowling coach Morne Morkel repeatedly asked them to hit the six-metre length.

Rather than relying on Nitish Reddy’s batting at No. 8, the think-tank could consider both Kamboj and Akash Deep for their ability to strike the ball hard and contribute with the bat.

For New Zealand, Will Young’s return to form during the ODIs is a welcome sign, as is Rachin Ravindra’s comeback from injury.

Skipper Tom Latham has struggled for form, but two quality all-rounders in Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips give the hosts greater balance compared to India.

Squads

India: Shubman Gill (captain), Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul (vice-captain), Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant (wicketkeeper), Dhruv Jurel (wicketkeeper), Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Akash Deep, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Mohammed Siraj, B Sai Sudharsan, Gurnoor Brar, Washington Sundar.

New Zealand: Tom Latham (captain), Rachin Ravindra, Will Young, Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (wicketkeeper), Dean Foxcroft, Jacob Duffy, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner, Henry Nicholls, Devon Conway.

Match starts: 3.30 am IST.

item.title: Create High-End Jewelry Campaign Photography With AI
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: You can now generate images with AI to explore and produce this kind of imagery, and Dreamina is built to handle the sparkle, metal, and glow that make a piece look desirable. Describe the ring, the light, and the mood, and see a polished campaign frame in moments.
item.content:encoded:
Jewelry is photographed unlike almost anything else. The pieces are tiny, reflective, and unforgiving, and every smudge, stray reflection, or flat shadow shows. Campaigns for fine jewelry traditionally rely on specialist photographers, macro lenses, and long retouching sessions, which puts them out of reach for many independent designers. 

You can now generate images with AI to explore and produce this kind of imagery, and Dreamina is built to handle the sparkle, metal, and glow that make a piece look desirable. Describe the ring, the light, and the mood, and see a polished campaign frame in moments.

Here is how to bring the glow of fine jewelry into your own campaign.

What makes jewelry photography different

Most products reveal themselves with good light, but jewelry reveals itself with controlled reflection. Metal can look dull or blown out, and stones can look lifeless or chaotic, depending on what they reflect. The best campaign images feel quiet and precise, with a sense of intimacy that makes the viewer lean in.

Describing metals and stones precisely

Material words do a great deal of work in a jewelry prompt. Being specific helps Dreamina render the right sheen and color.

  • Metals: polished yellow gold, brushed rose gold, cool white platinum, oxidized silver
  • Stones: round brilliant diamond, deep blue sapphire, cabochon emerald, soft pearl
  • Finishes: mirror polish, hammered texture, fine engraving, pave setting

Backgrounds that flatter the piece

The background should frame a piece without stealing attention from it. Dark velvet makes gold and diamonds glow, pale stone suggests purity and calm, and a soft gradient lets the jewelry float. Avoid busy patterns, which compete with the intricate detail you want viewers to notice.

Light as the main ingredient

In jewelry imagery, light is the star. Rim light traces the edges of a band, a soft overhead source gives stones life, and a small, warm highlight adds romance. Describe where the light comes from and how soft it is and mention subtle reflections so the metal feels dimensional rather than flat.

The complete lineup of Dreamina image generation models

Dreamina brings multiple image generation models together in one workspace, so you can match the tool to the moment. Nano Banana is fast, which helps you test settings, backgrounds, and moods for a piece before investing in a final render. 

GPT Image 2.5 follows detailed art direction closely, handy when a brief covers the metal, stone, background, and light in a single, layered description. 

Seedream 5.5 is the newest and most advanced option, and it brings the finest detail and control, which is exactly what small, reflective objects demand. A common workflow is to explore with Nano Banana, refine the direction with GPT Image 2.5, and finish with Seedream 5.5.

Three steps to a collection-ready frame

Step 1: Write a text description 

Go to Dreamina and write a detailed text prompt describing the piece, its metal and stones, the surface, the light, and the mood, much like briefing a jewelry photographer. You can add a reference image of your actual design so its shape and proportions stay accurate. 

Example: A high-end campaign photograph of a delicate platinum necklace with a teardrop diamond pendant draped across black velvet, a soft pinpoint highlight on the stone, cool studio lighting, shallow depth of field, luxury jewelry advertising photography.

Step 2: Adjust parameters and generate

Choose Image 5.5, powered by Seedream 5.5, and set your aspect ratio, size, and resolution. Square suits product grids, vertical suits stories and ads, and 2K helps fine detail hold up when you zoom in. Click Dreamina’s icon to generate.

Step 3: Customize and save

Polish the image with Dreamina’s AI customization tools. Inpaint to refine a setting or highlight, expand to leave room for campaign copy, remove stray reflections or dust, and retouch for a flawless finish. Then click the Download icon to save.

Seedream 5.5: sharper detail where it counts

Seedream 5.5 suits jewelry because small details decide whether an image feels luxurious.

  • Precise image editing: change a stone’s color or metal tone while leaving the composition and light untouched.
  • Layer-based control: adjust the piece, the surface, and the background as separate parts.
  • Reference-grade output: stills are clean enough to serve as the base for short product films.
  • Deep-thinking generation: it manages dense briefs with several materials and reflections.
  • Brand-consistent sets: hold one lighting style and palette across a whole collection.

Showing jewelry on the body

Pieces make more sense when viewers can see how they sit. A ring on a hand, an earring against a jawline, or a necklace at the collarbone adds scale and emotion. Describe the pose and skin tone naturally, keeping the focus on the jewelry rather than the model.

Building a collection mood

A collection feels more valuable when its images share a visual world. Pick one background, one lighting direction, and one palette, and repeat them across every piece. A shared mood lets customers recognize your brand even before they see a logo.

Where jewelry visuals get used

  • Product pages and marketplace listings
  • Seasonal campaigns for gifting moments
  • Lookbooks and press kits
  • Email launches and social announcements

Designing for every placement

Campaign images appear in many shapes, from website banners to narrow story frames. Leave breathing room around the piece so crops do not cut off a chain or a stone, and plan quiet space for text if the image will carry a headline.

Presenting pieces honestly

Generated imagery should reflect what the customer will actually receive. Keep stone size, color, and metal finish faithful to the real piece, and avoid exaggerating sparkle beyond what the product delivers. Honest images lead to fewer returns and stronger trust.

Let every piece shine

Jewelry is bought with the eyes and the heart long before the budget gets a say. With Dreamina and the precision of Seedream 5.5, you can build campaign imagery that feels refined and intimate, and you can start creating your first jewelry frame today.

item.title: Rising AQI levels threaten future generations, says Rakul Preet Singh
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Actress Rakul Preet Singh has urged collective action to tackle rising pollution, stressing that everyone must contribute towards protecting the environment. She also spoke about her experience playing Surpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari's upcoming film Ramayana
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Rakul Preet Singh has stressed the need for collective action to tackle rising pollution levels, saying it is the responsibility of every individual to contribute towards protecting the environment.

Speaking to IANS about the importance of environmental initiatives, the actress highlighted how small steps, including monitoring one’s carbon footprint and vehicle emissions, can make a significant difference in safeguarding the planet for future generations.

“I think the cause is very important, as I just said that it is the need of the day. We read that AQI has reached 600, 1,000. And this is affecting our health and future generations,” Rakul told IANS.

She said that while the present generation may get by, the real question was what kind of planet it was leaving behind for those who would follow.

“I mean, we will live, but how are we leaving the planet for the next couple of generations? And I think it is the responsibility of all of us to do whatever we can from our side, as much as we can. How much carbon footprint do we have? How much pollution has been checked from our car? Small, small things, you know. And I think if we all do it, it will be a collective effort. And I am very happy that Earthshot is doing such an event. And it is a step in the right direction,” she said.

On the acting front, Rakul was recently seen playing Surpanakha in Nitesh Tiwari’s directorial venture, ‘Ramayana’.

She described the experience as a special journey and expressed pride in being part of a story deeply rooted in Indian culture for generations.

Sharing her thoughts, the actress wrote: “Have been waiting to share the experience of playing Surpanakha in Ramayana. It has been such a special journey for me. It’s not every day that you get to be a part of a story that has been a part of our lives and culture for generations. To see Ramayana being brought to life on such a grand scale is truly something else. Being part of a story that means so much to our country, and seeing it come together on such a scale, makes this journey even more special.”

‘Ramayana’, which stars Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi in the lead roles, was released in theatres on November 5.

item.title: Hyderabad: Massive fire breaks out at Nayan Infra Apartments, four fire engines deployed
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A massive fire broke out at Nayan Infra Apartments in Pet Basheerabad on Wednesday, triggering explosions involving gas cylinders and AC compressors in two flats. Four fire engines were deployed to control the blaze. Extensive property damage was reported
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A massive fire broke out at Nayan Infra Apartments in Pet Basheerabad on Wednesday afternoon, triggering panic among residents.

According to preliminary information, the fire reportedly originated from a lamp lit at the place of worship inside one of the flats. The flames quickly spread through the apartment, triggering a series of explosions.

Gas cylinders and air-conditioner compressors in two flats located opposite each other on the fourth floor reportedly exploded, intensifying the blaze. The explosions caused extensive damage to the flats and heightened concerns among residents.

On receiving information, four fire engines were rushed to the spot. Firefighters brought the flames under control and took measures to prevent the fire from spreading to other parts of the apartment building.

Extensive property damage has been reported.

Pet Basheerabad police are investigating the incident.

item.title: Gambhir’s biggest Test: India coach seeks redemption in New Zealand
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Gautam Gambhir returns to New Zealand as India's head coach, hoping to draw inspiration from his memorable 2009 batting performances. Former teammate Vijay Dahiya backs him, highlighting his commitment, strong convictions and tendency to take failures personally
item.content:encoded:
Wellington: When Ajit Agarkar’s term as chairman of the national selection committee officially ended, Gautam Gambhir had hoped that “history will be kinder” to the former Mumbai pacer, who managed to shake up Indian cricket with his bold decisions.

The India head coach could perhaps relate to Agarkar. After all, Gambhir knows a thing or two about being scrutinised over every decision, big or small, in Indian cricket. He, too, is often the first to be blamed when things go awry in the country’s most-followed sport.

“…He is a passionate man. There are no grey shades for him. It is either black or white,” Gambhir’s former teammate and close friend Vijay Dahiya told PTI when asked if the head coach gets a raw deal on ‘Opinion Street’.

That Gambhir wears his heart on his sleeve is hardly a secret. He likes to stand by his decisions firmly.

“Gauti, whether he was captain of Delhi or Kolkata Knight Riders or later their mentor, always believed in getting the assigned job done… Whether people give him enough credit or not, he isn’t someone who is even bothered about public validation for a job well done,” Dahiya said.

Gone are the days when Sachin Tendulkar, Sourav Ganguly, Virender Sehwag, Yuvraj Singh and Suresh Raina bowled anything between six and even 10 overs across formats to ease the burden on frontline bowlers.

With that kind of bowling diversity no longer at his disposal, Gambhir prefers a line-up that bats deep.

Those who work with him would tell you that when Gambhir watches cricket, he is not merely observing; he is devising strategies. Ask Sitanshu Kotak or Morne Morkel, and they would tell you that there is always a plan up for debate or discussion when Gambhir is around.

Standing at the Basin Reserve during India’s net session, Gambhir might have felt a sense of déjà vu.

In 2009, a determined Gambhir used every ounce of his energy to score 72 (Hamilton), 136 (Napier) and 167 (Wellington) in India’s last Test series victory in New Zealand.

That was Test batting at its best, and his 12-hour match-saving knock at Napier remains part of Indian cricket folklore.

If the current Indian batting line-up can replicate that resolve in the series, beginning on Thursday, the visitors will return home with renewed hopes of improving their World Test Championship prospects.

For Gambhir, who often finds himself at the receiving end of criticism, it would be a redemption of sorts after India’s home losses to South Africa and New Zealand in the past couple of years.

“Some people do a job and some people are invested in a job. With Gauti, an assignment is an investment. If things don’t go well, he takes it all upon himself. One thing he possibly needs to do is switch off. He is never switched off,” Dahiya said.

Two series wins in New Zealand, despite the short turnaround between them, should be lauded. But perhaps one of India’s best tacticians would rather move on to the next challenge, hoping to avoid a slip-up instead of revelling in the moment.

This is largely because he is a non-conformist with strong likes and dislikes, traits that often invite harsh scrutiny.

“He could have a strong liking for someone, and it doesn’t mean he dislikes someone else. I can love running. Does that mean I hate walking?” Dahiya asked.

Just as every success belongs first and foremost to the players, every failure cannot be attributed solely to Gambhir.

There are decisions in which captains Shubman Gill (Tests and ODIs) and Shreyas Iyer (T20s) are also stakeholders.

This particular series could well be Gambhir’s biggest Test as India’s red-ball coach, given the conditions and the opposition. But unlike Napier and Wellington in 2009, he cannot do it all by himself.

The head coach needs the team to fire just as much as the team needs its gaffer.

item.title: Tabu joins ‘Tunnel Men’, Netflix series based on 2023 Uttarakhand tunnel rescue
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Tabu has joined the cast of Netflix's upcoming series ‘Tunnel Men’, a fictionalised account of the 2023 Uttarakhand tunnel rescue. Directed by Shiv Rawail, the series draws on the 17-day operation that brought 41 trapped workers to safety.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Bollywood actress Tabu, who was recently seen in ‘Drishyam: The Conclusion’, has joined the cast of the upcoming streaming series ‘Tunnel Men’. The series presents a fictionalised account of the 2023 Uttarakhand tunnel rescue.

In November 2023, the country held its breath as a long and painstaking rescue effort brought trapped workers out of a collapsed tunnel in Uttarakhand. ‘Tunnel Men’ draws on the spirit of that moment, the resilience, teamwork, and the hope that carried it. It was one of India’s most challenging and closely watched disaster-response missions. On November 12, 2023, a portion of the under-construction Silkyara-Barkot tunnel in Uttarkashi district collapsed following a landslide, trapping 41 construction workers inside.

The men remained stranded for 17 days, with rescuers battling unstable terrain, falling debris and repeated machinery failures. Multiple agencies, including the NDRF, SDRF, Army, BRO and international tunnelling experts, collaborated on the operation. Food, water, oxygen, electricity and communication were supplied through narrow pipes to sustain the workers. After several unsuccessful attempts at mechanical drilling, a team of rat-hole miners was brought in to manually excavate the final stretch of debris.

On November 28, all 41 workers were successfully evacuated through a specially inserted steel pipe. The operation became a landmark example of multi-agency coordination, perseverance and human endurance

Tabu is one of India’s finest actresses with a career spanning more than 3 decades, moving with rare ease between mainstream and independent cinema, and across Hindi and regional-language films. Her global credits include Mira Nair’s ‘The Namesake’, in which she played Ashima Ganguli, Ang Lee’s ‘Life of Pi’, and the ‘Dune: Prophecy’ series, where she appeared as Sister Francesca.

Shiv Rawail, who directed ‘The Railway Men’, and more recently the Alia Bhatt and Sharvari-starrer ‘Alpha’ returns as showrunner for ‘Tunnel Men’, bringing the same human storytelling to a new tale of courage.

The series is set to stream on Netflix.

item.title: Minor girl found pregnant, 15-year-old boy booked in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Banjara Hills police registered a case against a 15-year-old boy accused of sexually assaulting his minor female friend. The incident came to light after the girl's parents discovered her pregnancy and approached the police with a complaint
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 15-year-old boy has been accused of sexually assaulting his minor female friend in Banjara Hills and threatening her with serious consequences if she disclosed the incident.

According to information available, the boy allegedly sexually assaulted the girl and warned her against revealing the incident to anyone. Fearing his threats, the girl reportedly kept the matter to herself.

The incident came to light recently after the girl’s parents discovered that she was pregnant. Shocked by the revelation, they approached the police and lodged a complaint.

Based on the complaint, Banjara Hills police registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Further investigation is underway.

item.title: Arshdeep, Banton among biggest gainers in latest ICC rankings
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: India's Arshdeep Singh climbed 12 places to joint 19th in the latest ICC ODI bowling rankings. England's Tom Banton rose 34 places to a career-high 13th after his century against Australia, while several Zimbabwe and Afghanistan players gained ground in Test rankings
item.content:encoded:
Dubai: India pacer Arshdeep Singh made significant gains in the latest update to the ICC Men’s ODI Player Rankings, climbing 12 places to reach a joint 19th position among bowlers following the completion of the three-match series against New Zealand.

Arshdeep was among the biggest movers in the bowling rankings this week, which continue to be led by Afghanistan spinner Rashid Khan. New Zealand pacer Matt Henry also rose significantly, moving up 15 places to share 12th spot, while his teammate Kyle Jamieson climbed 15 places to 45th.

Meanwhile, England batter Tom Banton was another major beneficiary of the latest update following his match-winning century against Australia in the second ODI in Adelaide. Banton smashed 121 off 99 deliveries, his second ODI hundred, to help England register a series-levelling victory and climb 34 places to a career-high 13th in the batting rankings.

His England teammate Joe Root also returned to the top 10, moving up two places to ninth after scoring a half-century in the same match. India’s Shubman Gill continues to lead the ODI batting rankings.

England pacer Jofra Archer returned to the top 10 among ODI bowlers, gaining four places to seventh after taking a wicket in each of the first two ODIs against Australia.

Meanwhile, Zimbabwe and Afghanistan players made notable progress in the latest Test rankings following their closely fought series in Sharjah, which Zimbabwe won 2-0.

Zimbabwe pacer Blessing Muzarabani was the biggest gainer among Test bowlers, climbing five places to share 16th position after taking six wickets in the decisive second Test to earn the Player of the Match award. Spinner Graeme Cremer also moved up six places to 65th.

In the batting rankings, Zimbabwe opener Innocent Kaia climbed 20 places to 50th, while veteran Brendan Taylor rose 40 places to 62nd.

Afghanistan all-rounder Naseer Maroofkhil made his mark on his Test debut with a century and seven wickets in the first innings of the match. He became only the fourth player to achieve the feat in men’s Test cricket and entered the Test batting rankings at 93rd position and the bowling rankings at joint 78th.

item.title: Bike-borne duo snatch 1.5-tola gold chain, phone in Uppal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Two unidentified bike-borne men snatched a 1.5-tola gold chain and a mobile phone from a 45-year-old man near NGRI in Uppal on Wednesday morning. Uppal police registered a case and are examining CCTV footage to identify the suspects
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Two unidentified bike-borne miscreants snatched a gold chain weighing 1.5 tolas and a mobile phone from a man near the National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) in Uppal on Wednesday.

According to the police, the victim, identified as Murali Babu (45), was crossing the road while speaking on his mobile phone at around 7 am when two men riding a motorcycle approached him.

The duo allegedly snatched the gold chain from his neck and took away his mobile phone before fleeing the spot.

The complainant told the police that the suspects escaped towards Tarnaka.

Following a complaint from Murali Babu, Uppal police registered a case and launched an investigation.

Police are examining CCTV footage from the surrounding areas to identify and trace the suspects.

item.title: SMAT 2026: Bihar pull off last-over win as Chhattisgarh defeat Odisha
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Bihar edged Delhi by two wickets in a thrilling chase in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Elite 2026. Chhattisgarh, Andhra and Bengal also registered victories, with Vikalp Tiwari's century and several impressive batting performances highlighting Wednesday's matches
item.content:encoded:
