New Delhi: Bihar pulled off a thrilling two-wicket victory over Delhi, chasing down a target of 225 with one ball to spare, as the first four matches of the day in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) Elite 2026 produced plenty of runs and several standout individual performances on Wednesday.

At the Daly College Ground in Indore, Delhi rode on a sensational 125 off 59 balls from Yash Dhull and a quickfire 51 off 25 deliveries by Tejasvi Dahiya to post 224/5 in 20 overs. Dhull struck 16 fours and seven sixes, while Dahiya contributed four boundaries and four sixes.

However, Bihar responded with an aggressive start. Ayush Loharuka smashed 50 off just 22 balls, while Bipin Saurabh made 49 off 19, putting the chase firmly on course. Raghuvendra Pratap Singh added 25 off 15 balls and later finished as Bihar’s leading bowler with figures of 3/44. Despite a late wobble, Bihar reached 227/8 in 19.5 overs to secure the win, with Raghuvendra named Player of the Match.

At the Jadavpur University Campus Ground in Kolkata, Chhattisgarh defeated Odisha by 51 runs after captain Vikalp Tiwari produced a magnificent century. Tiwari struck 119 off 56 balls, reaching his hundred in just 44 deliveries, while Ajay Jadav Mandal chipped in with 50 off 28 balls as Chhattisgarh posted 228/4.

Odisha managed 177/8 in reply, with Kartik Biswal top-scoring with 57 off 33 balls. Subhranshu Senapati added 31, but Chhattisgarh’s bowlers kept the chase under control, with Jayant Yadav, Dev Aditya Singh and Sourabh Majumdar picking up two or more wickets each.

Andhra registered a 29-run win over Kerala at the Punjab Cricket Association IS Bindra Stadium in Mohali. Seeram Venkata Rahul led the batting effort with 64 off 30 balls, while Shaik Rasheed scored 60 off 39. Contributions from Maramreddy Hemanth Reddy (32 off 16) and Ashwin Hebbar (37 off 15) powered Andhra to 225/7.

Kerala fought back through Abdul Basith’s 70 off 35 balls, supported by Govind Dev Pai (36) and Sanju Samson (26), but finished at 196/5. MD Nidheesh claimed three wickets for Kerala, while Andhra’s KV Sasikanth and K S Narasimha Raju took two wickets apiece.

Bengal completed a seven-wicket victory over Jharkhand at the Sharad Pawar Cricket Academy in Mumbai. After restricting Jharkhand to 148/7, Bengal chased down the target in 18.4 overs, finishing at 149/3. Abhimanyu Easwaran remained unbeaten on 61 off 48 balls, while Abishek Porel contributed 49 off 34.

Jharkhand’s innings was built around Virat Singh’s unbeaten 45 and Shikhar Mohan’s 42, but Bengal’s bowlers ensured the total remained within reach. The defending champions, who started their campaign with a win, have now suffered back-to-back defeats.

item.title: Alia Bhatt showcases black-and-gold lehenga at Earthshot Prize 2026 in Mumbai
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Alia Bhatt shared pictures of her black-and-gold lehenga worn at the Earthshot Prize 2026 in Mumbai. The event brought together celebrities and environmental changemakers, with guests showcasing traditional Indian craftsmanship, contemporary designs and sustainable fashion.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actress Alia Bhatt shared a glimpse of her appearance at the Earthshot Prize. She offered a stylish take on traditional Indian fashion in a striking black-and-gold ensemble.

The ‘Raazi’ actress took to Instagram to share pictures of her look, wearing a black-and-gold lehenga adorned with intricate embroidery and mirror work. She paired the strapless, structured blouse with an embellished skirt and draped a black dupatta around her neck. Statement gold earrings and an ornate arm cuff added to the overall look.

Alongside the pictures, Alia shared a brief message, writing, “Where every story has a purpose @earthshotprize.” Through her post, the ‘Dear Zindagi’ actress highlighted the spirit of the Earthshot Prize, which celebrates people and initiatives working towards solutions for environmental challenges.

In the pictures, Alia is seen striking various poses as she flaunts her elegant black-and-gold lehenga.

The Earthshot Prize 2026 in Mumbai brought together environmental changemakers and celebrated personalities, with the event also turning into a fashion showcase. Several celebrities made stylish appearances on the green carpet, embracing a blend of traditional Indian craftsmanship, modern designs and statement ensembles.

Among those who made a stylish appearance were Simone Ashley, Bhumi Pednekar, Karan Johar, Khushi Kapoor, Mira Kapoor, Sonam Kapoor, Rakul Preet Singh, Shreya Ghoshal and Kate Middleton, each bringing their own fashion statement to the event.

The Princess of Wales attended the event with Prince William, who established the Earthshot Prize in 2020. Kate also presented one of the awards, making it a key moment during the royal couple’s three-day visit to India. The ceremony featured musical performances by singer Shreya Ghoshal, British pop band Take That, composer Shashwat Sachdev and all-female hip-hop group Wild Wild Women.

Shreya Ghoshal highlighted India’s traditional handloom craftsmanship and the importance of sustainable fashion during her appearance and performance at the prestigious Earthshot Prize ceremony.

For the occasion, she opted for a custom-designed gown inspired by underwater corals.

item.title: Peddapalli: Public prosecutor caught red handed while accepting bribe Rs 1.50 lakh
item.dc:creator: T Ivan Nischal
item.description: A public prosecutor in Peddapalli was arrested by ACB officials on Wednesday for allegedly accepting Rs 1.5 lakh from an accused in a murder case. The prosecutor had reportedly demanded Rs 2 lakh before agreeing to accept less.
item.content:encoded:
Peddapalli: A public prosecutor was arrested by officials of Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) while allegedly accepting a bribe of Rs 1.50 lakh from an accused person in a murder case, here on Wednesday.

Karimnagari range ACB DSP Mahender Reddy said that Donkena Ravinder, a public prosecutor at a district court, was caught red-handed when he was receiving the bribe from the accused person to act in his favor in the murder case reported at Rachapalli. Ravinder reportedly demanded Rs 2 lakh, but agreed to accept Rs 1.50 lakh after being requested by the complainant.

Ravinder took up the murder case registered against four persons from the village following land disputes in 2023. He was harrassing one of the accused persons, seeking the bribe. The complainant approached the ACB who in turn laid the trap and arrested the public prosecutor. The accused prosecutor will be produced before a special court for ACB in Karimnagar by evening.

item.title: Manu Bhaker elected to ISSF Athletes Committee for 2026–2030 term
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker has been elected to the ISSF Athletes Committee for 2026–2030. She was among six athletes chosen through online voting during two world championships, with the ISSF Executive Committee set to nominate the remaining members.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker has been elected as a member of the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) Athletes Committee for the 2026–2030 term. The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) received formal confirmation of her election from the global governing body.

In an official communication issued from Munich on 16 November 2026, ISSF President Luciano Rossi and Secretary General Alessandro Nicotra di San Giacomo congratulated Manu on her appointment. Her election followed online voting conducted among active international shooters during two major competitions. Polling took place during the ISSF World Championship 300m Rifle in Cairo, Egypt, and the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar. Manu was one of six athletes elected to the committee across rifle, pistol and shotgun from a field of 22 candidates representing 20 member federations. Two representatives were chosen from each discipline by their fellow competitors.

The ISSF Executive Committee will now nominate the remaining members to complete the panel. Speaking on her election to the committee, Manu Bhaker said: “Honoured to be elected as a Member of the Athletes Committee, and truly grateful to my fellow shooters for their trust. Being on the firing line every day shows what athletes need—from clearer rules and schedules to stronger support systems. With this new responsibility, I’m committed to ensuring the voices of all athletes are heard, grooming talent at the grassroots level, and working together to take our entire shooting fraternity to greater heights.”

The NRAI welcomed the development, noting that Manu’s appointment places a strong Indian voice at the forefront of global athlete advocacy as the sport builds towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

item.title: Sonam Kapoor’s Earthshot look pays tribute to Amrita Sher-Gil’s 1936 portrait
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Sonam Kapoor wore a custom Anamika Khanna ensemble inspired by Amrita Sher-Gil's 1936 portrait at the Earthshot Prize 2026 in Mumbai. Styled by Rhea Kapoor, the look brought together Indian artistic heritage and contemporary couture.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actor Sonam Kapoor brought a slice of Indian art history to the green carpet of The Earthshot Prize 2026 in Mumbai.

The actress chose a custom Anamika Khanna ensemble inspired by a 1936 portrait by legendary painter Amrita Sher-Gil. Styled by her sister Rhea Kapoor, Sonam’s look drew from Sher-Gil’s portrait of her cousin Sumair Apjit Singh, painted in 1936.

Sonam was seen in a deep green sari with long earrings, reflecting Sher-Gil’s fascination with Indian colours and subjects after her years in Europe.

Rhea, describing the significance of the ensemble, wrote, “@sonamkapoor’s Anamika Khanna couture is inspired by Sumair, Amrita Sher-Gil’s 1936 portrait of her cousin Sumair Apjit Singh. Sher-Gil was herself half Indian and half Hungarian, and she stayed trained in Paris before making India her home and her muse. Sumair lived between the same two worlds. She was raised in Patiala with a love for Western style and later modelled in Paris for Elsa Schiaparelli, yet her cousin painted her in a deep green sari, holding a spray of white flowers.”

“Anamika Khanna carries that conversation forward. The pure chiffon sari is hand-painted in shades of green, over it sits a structured silk velvet coat, a Western silhouette edged in zardozi. Nearly ninety years on, the two worlds Sumair moved between come together again on Sonam.”

Sonam appeared at the Earthshot Prize ceremony that was attended by Prince William and Princess Kate Middleton. The awards, held in Mumbai on November 17, marked the first time the global environmental initiative was hosted in India. Sonam was among the presenters and attendees at the event.

This is not the first time Rhea has had a heritage approach for her designs. She had previously used a similar heritage-led approach while styling Kareena Kapoor Khan. For Kareena’s Diwali look earlier this month, Rhea put together a contemporary ensemble that incorporated royal heirlooms from the Bhopal royal family.

Kareena wore a pure silver, or ‘chandi’, kaftan and matching turban by designer Punit Balana. The turban was adorned with a 200-year-old kalgi associated with the Nawab of Bhopal, while she also wore a 30-carat emerald linked to the Begum of Bhopal.

The emerald was carved with Ayat-ul-Kursi and the pieces came through Kareena’s husband Saif Ali Khan’s family.

item.title: Svitolina, Bencic, Kyrgios headline 16-player field for World Tennis League Season 5
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The World Tennis League will stage its fifth season in Bengaluru from December 17 to 20, featuring 16 players, including international stars Elina Svitolina, Nick Kyrgios and Belinda Bencic, alongside eight Indian players across four teams.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The World Tennis League (WTL) is set to bring some of the biggest names in international tennis to Bengaluru for its fifth season, with former world No. 3 Elina Svitolina, Olympic gold medallist Belinda Bencic, former world No. 1 Karolína Plíšková, Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios and two-time Wimbledon doubles champion Harri Heliövaara headlining a 16-player field. The league, licensed and managed by Iconik Sports and Events, will be held from December 17–20, 2026, at the KSLTA, S.M. Krishna Tennis Stadium, Bengaluru.

Season 5 will feature four teams – AKRIXX Eagles, Game Changers Falcons, Aussie Mavericks Kites and VB Realty Hawks – bringing together eight international players and eight of India’s leading tennis talents. The mix of established international champions and emerging Indian players promises four days of competitive tennis, with fans getting the opportunity to watch some of the sport’s biggest names in action on home soil. Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina leads the women’s line-up, a 20-time WTA singles champion and winner of the 2018 WTA Finals who reached the Australian Open semifinals earlier this year. Switzerland’s Belinda Bencic, the Tokyo 2020 Olympic singles gold medallist and a Wimbledon semifinalist in 2025, will also be among the leading attractions. Joining them is Czechia’s Karolína Plíšková, a former world No. 1 and two-time Grand Slam finalist, having reached the US Open final in 2016 and the Wimbledon final in 2021. Spain’s Paula Badosa, a former world No. 2 and 2021 Indian Wells champion, returns to the league following her appearance last season.

The men’s field is equally compelling, with Australia’s Nick Kyrgios bringing his considerable presence to the Bengaluru court. A Wimbledon finalist in 2022 and Australian Open doubles champion in the same year, Kyrgios will be joined by Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik, a nine-time ATP title winner who reached a career-high world No. 10 in January 2026. Belgium’s Zizou Bergs, who claimed his maiden ATP title at Eastbourne this year, and Finland’s Harri Heliövaara, a two-time Wimbledon men’s doubles champion (2024 and 2026), complete the international line-up. India’s representation will feature a strong mix of experienced campaigners and promising young players.

Sumit Nagal, who became the first Indian man to win an ATP Masters 1000 match on clay, returns alongside Yuki Bhambri, India’s leading doubles player who has reached a career-high ranking of No. 18. Dhakshineswar Suresh, who delivered a memorable performance in India’s Davis Cup tie against the Netherlands in Bengaluru earlier this year by winning three matches, will also be back. Completing the men’s contingent is Ramkumar Ramanathan, a former ATP singles finalist and two-time ATP 250 doubles champion.

The women’s Indian line-up will see the return of 17-year-old Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi and Shrivalli Rashmikaa Bhamidipaty, both of whom featured last season. Maaya has emerged as one of India’s exciting young prospects, becoming the first Indian woman since Sania Mirza to reach a WTA Tour singles quarter-final. They will be joined by Rutuja Bhosale, who won mixed doubles gold alongside Rohan Bopanna at the 2023 Asian Games, and Vaishnavi Adkar, India’s No. 1 women’s singles player in 2026.

Both players will make their WTL debuts after reaching the doubles final at the Chennai Open, becoming the first all-Indian pair to achieve the feat at a WTA Tour event. Mahesh Bhupathi, Co-founder, World Tennis League, said: “The quality of players coming together for Season 5 makes this a particularly exciting line-up. We have Grand Slam finalists, an Olympic gold medallist, former world No. 1s and some of the most exciting names on the ATP and WTA tours. Each brings a different style and personality to the court, which will make the team competition all the more interesting.

Equally exciting is the Indian contingent, with experienced players and young talent making their mark on the international circuit. It is this combination of quality, experience and emerging talent that will make Season 5 special.” Hemali Sharma, Co-founder, World Tennis League, said: “Reaching our fifth season is an important milestone for the league, and we are delighted to bring this quality of tennis to Bengaluru. For fans, it is an opportunity to watch some of the biggest names in the sport up close, while for our Indian players, it is a chance to test themselves against international competition and learn from that experience. We have seen the league grow over the years, and our focus remains on making world-class tennis more accessible to Indian audiences while creating more opportunities for the sport to grow in the country.”

item.title: Travis Head will miss IPL 2027, says SRH coach Daniel Vettori
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Sunrisers Hyderabad coach Daniel Vettori expressed disappointment over Travis Head’s decision to skip IPL 2027, citing Australia’s international schedule. He discussed SRH’s retention strategy and auction plans, while Delhi Capitals coach Sourav Ganguly explained the franchise’s releases and trades.
item.content:encoded:
Sad Travis Head will not be with Sunrisers, says Vettori

Hyderabad: Sunrisers Hyderabad head coach Daniel Vettori said it would be sad that Travis Head, who opted out of the IPL to focus on the hectic international calendar for the Australian team, would not be with the team. “But, we are very grateful for his cntributons over the last three years,” Vettori informed JioStar’s ‘Tata IPL 2027 Retention Special’.

“The reason behind retentions, it being the final year of the cycle was obviously a big focus this time. But we also wanted to understand that we had a good season last year and wanted to retain the core of the squad, while also understanding that we were after some improvements and had some issues with player availability,” Vettori said.

“Player availability was a huge part of it. Travis Head, who’s been an integral part of the side for the last three years, has decided that he wants to sit out the season. He’s got a massive year coming up for Australia, and he’s going to prioritise that. So it’s sad that he’s not going to be with us, but we are very grateful for his contributions over the last three years,” he said. On the players SRH will look to target at the auction, Vettori said: “I think every team looks at the gaps in their squad or their team, and it’s just about trying to find improvements. We may find a player from a team that’s been released and feel like he can really suit our squad and playing style.”

“ Particularly from a batting perspective, it’s a great place to bat. So if there is someone released who maybe hasn’t been successful at a certain venue, they can come to Hyderabad and really blossom. So, those are the sorts of players we’ll be looking for to complement our squad. We’re fortunate that we have such a strong team and a strong playing XI, and hopefully we get one or two players who can really contribute to that,” he explained. For his part, Delhi Capitals head coach Sourav Ganguly said: “It’s very difficult to pinpoint the exact thought process behind the releases and retentions. It’s obviously about performance, who the franchise values and who the franchise thinks is good enough to win cricket matches in the IPL. It is also about what’s available at the auction.”

“ It’s a small auction, so the franchise factors in the performance of the last two years and what it feels is required for the next three years. So, there is no thumb rule that this is right or that is wrong. It’s just about faith and belief,” he said. On trading Kuldeep Yadav to LSG for Rishabh Pant, Ganguly said: “It was a tough trade because Kuldeep is a very special cricketer. He’s been with Delhi Capitals for a long period of time, but in the IPL, with 10 teams, it’s always about that one balance factor. And we were looking at a batsman.”

“ We got a domestic batsman in Rishabh Pant, who’s done well for Delhi. Someone whom I rate very, very highly. But it was very hard to let Kuldeep go, and with Axar and Ashutosh, releasing them was a complete no-no. They are very important part of our squad,” the former India captain said. On his first stint as a Head Coach in the TATA IPL, Ganguly said: “It is my first time as head coach in the IPL. I did it for Pretoria Capitals last year, but I am very excited. The IPL is a very different challenge. I have been involved with DC in different ways, more so as the Director of Cricket, obviously organising everything when Ricky was the head coach. Now that I will be the head coach, I will be at the centre of taking this team forward.”

item.title: IPL 2027: 10 franchises retain 184 players, leave Rs 297.95 crore for auction
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The 10 IPL franchises have retained 184 players, including 55 overseas players, for the 2027 season. They have spent ₹1,002.05 crore, leaving ₹297.95 crore and 66 squad slots, including 25 overseas positions, for the auction.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The 10 franchises have finalised their retained player lists for the TATA Indian Premier League (IPL) 2027 season, setting the stage for the next phase of squad-building ahead of the Player Auction. A total of 184 players, including 55 overseas players, have been retained as franchises look to build on their existing combinations and prepare for the upcoming auction.

The franchises have collectively spent ₹1,002.05 crore, leaving a combined purse of ₹297.95 crore for the auction. With 66 squad positions available across the 10 teams, including 25 overseas slots, the franchises will have further opportunities to add to their squads and fine-tune their combinations.

item.title: Cherry blossoms turn Sikkim’s Temi Tea Garden into a pink paradise
item.dc:creator: Ruchi Rai Agarwal
item.description: Sikkim's Temi Tea Garden has turned pink with seasonal cherry blossoms, drawing attention after a viral video. The Sikkim Cherry Festival 2026, being held from November 14 to 28, is showcasing the region's blooms and local culture.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Who says you have to travel to Japan to see cherry blossoms? India has its own little pink paradise, and it is currently winning hearts on social media. The Temi Tea Garden in Sikkim is witnessing its seasonal bloom, with cherry blossom trees adding shades of pink to the lush green tea plantations and surrounding mountains.

A video shared by content creator Ishita Negi has been going viral, giving viewers a glimpse of the beautiful landscape. The visuals show pink blossoms scattered across the green hills, making the tea estate look straight out of a postcard. While cherry blossoms are usually associated with Japan’s spring season, Sikkim offers a chance to witness these blooms during autumn.

https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfpOMiesyPW/

Sharing her experience, Ishita called November the best time to visit and encouraged travellers to explore the destination during the festival.

“Best time to see these blossoms: November. And if you’re planning a trip this year, you can visit between November 14 and 28 to attend the Cherry Blossom Festival. I finally got to see cherry blossoms and I can’t believe it was in India itself. Cancel your plans to visit Japan or Korea to see cherry blossoms because India has it too, and it is undoubtedly a sight to behold,” she wrote.

The video also caught the attention of travel enthusiasts, with many sharing their excitement in the comments. One user pointed out, “You can also find cherry blossom in Shillong. They literally have a festival for this.”

Another viewer, who had visited Japan for the blooms, wrote, “I have visited Japan for cherry blossom but I will definitely go here next.” One more user commented, “India has so much to explore while people only want to go outside India to see the same things.”

Located in Namchi district, Temi is Sikkim’s only tea estate and is known for its views of Mount Kanchenjunga. Visitors can walk through the tea gardens, enjoy the mountain scenery and sample locally grown tea. Khangchendzonga National Park and Karma Rabdenling Goenpa monastery are also worth exploring.

The nearest airport is Bagdogra in West Bengal. From there, visitors can hire a taxi to Namchi and continue to Temi. The Sikkim Cherry Festival 2026 is being held at Temi-Tarku from November 14 to 28, celebrating local culture and community-based tourism.

item.title: U19 Asia Cup: Mohit Ulva’s last-ball four is a moment Yashbardhan Chauhan will never forget
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Yashbardhan Chauhan recalls Mohit Ulva's winning four, India's belief during the tense chase and the emotions behind their celebrations after beating Pakistan by one wicket in the U19 Men’s Asia Cup final on November 14.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: With one ball left to decide the winner of the U19 Men’s Asia Cup, India were on the cusp of an unforgettable victory when Mohit Ulva hit a drive through long-off for four, helping the side win over Pakistan by one wicket on November 14. Vice-captain Yashbardhan Chauhan says that the shot is now fixed in his memory for good.

“That shot from Mohit Ulva on the last ball – even if I try, I will never forget it. That moment will remain in my mind for a lifetime. It was a very huge achievement. I can’t describe it. The match we won is not humanly possible. Bas ab who jeevan bhar yaad rahega (I will never forget it for the rest of my life),” Chauhan told IANS in an exclusive interview.

The finish seemed far-fetched for long stretches of the evening in Al Amerat. India were chasing 338 and stood at 252/8 when Manal Chauhan began taking on the bowling, eventually reaching 47. Back in the dugout, Chauhan recalled that the players and other members of the Indian team dared not move from their seats.

“At that time, Manal started attacking. He was coming in a little momentum. So whoever was sitting in their respective places, we were doing superstitious things. Wherever anyone was sitting, we were just praying to God that we have to win the match today.

“So everyone was sitting in one place, just cheering and praying that we would play because we had deep confidence that if we played 50 overs, then we would win the match. Our batting has a lot of depth, as our number 11 batter also bats. We had a lot of confidence. We just had it in mind that we have to play 50 overs. So we were just cheering and supporting, and everyone else was remembering their respective God,” he added.

Ulva carried the chase from there and finished unbeaten on 49. Chauhan said the team had always backed his hitting. “Yes, I also had that confidence as Mohit has a very good hitting ability. At that time, we just needed hitting. So we had confidence that if Mohit plays, we will win the match. We just had to play 50 overs and not get out. If we play 50 overs, then we will win the match and Mohit played till the end from there,” he said.

Ulva’s winning four capped a fightback that started from the fag end of Pakistan’s innings. Pakistan raced away early but added just 60 in their last 10 overs, thanks to slower balls from Kavya Patel and Chigurupati Venkata. Chauhan said the death overs of both innings decided the title in India’s favour.

“Yes, because as their power play was like that in the starting, we thought it would easily go beyond 400. But then bowling got better. They also bottled it a little bit. So things happened in our favour and it happened that in batting too, the last 10 overs were good in our favour. In bowling too, the last 10 overs were great.

“We won the match from the showing in the last 10 overs in both innings. When we won the match, I thought in my mind that no matter how good the match was, no matter how much we won the match, but do see what the finish is. When we did well in the finishing stage, we won.”

The win gave India the trophy for the first time in five years, and Chauhan admits he still has to remind himself of that every day. “Even now, sometimes it comes out of my mind, then I remember that we have done such a big achievement together. Even now, sometimes I feel that no, no, it’s not like that.

“Then I remember that we are Asian champions now. After 5 years, we became champions and the trophy has come home. So it is a very surreal feeling that you cannot define it – you can feel it. From within, I feel that we have done such a big achievement. It is a very good feeling,” he said.

He said the squad, made up mostly of newcomers, had wanted to prove a point from the start. “Yes, it was like that. We had taken it as a challenge that mostly in all the teams, 5-6 players were old. Our team was such that it was completely new from the start.

“So we said that if we come champions as a new team, then it will be a very big personal achievement for us. So everyone took the challenge and then everyone stepped up to it. Then everyone worked hard and today that trophy has come home.”

According to Chauhan, a close dressing room and clear roles held the side together. “In terms of turning point, I would say that if there is unity and team bonding in any team, then everyone knows what their role is and what is the need of the team in that situation.

“So according to that, you can give your best for the team. So we knew that very well. Our bonding was very good. Our roles were very clear. There was clarity about what situation would come, and who would perform how. So by doing that, we had a lot of clarity and we had a huge benefit of that. A good team bonding had been formed. All the people had understood each other, what the game was, he said.

The last-ball finish also settled an account from the league stage. In that league stage fixture held on Diwali, Arjun Rajput scored a hundred to lift India to 208, but Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten century took Pakistan home by three wickets.

“The conversation was very simple. We lost that league-stage match by a narrow margin. So our mind was clear – that there was a partnership and one of their boys made a century. So we just lost that match and luck did not favour us a little. Otherwise, we had also made a very good start in that game and picked up five wickets.

“But we just lost that match. But after that match, all the boys had the same thinking that the final will be against them and we are going to defeat them in the final. Everyone’s mindset was like this.

“It was going on in everyone’s mind how we would celebrate after winning the final because the boys had confidence that ‘Final toh hum jeet hi rahe hai (We are going to win the final).’ So the team’s atmosphere was very good.”

When Ulva’s four reached the boundary, the Indian players let loose. Their celebrations drew wide attention and split opinion in the cricketing world. Chauhan said the emotion had been building since the earlier defeat.

“The thing is, we lost the league match to them before. So we heard a lot about after losing that game – like gaali-galoch (abusive language). So it was within us that we had to celebrate after winning the match because we never did anything like this before. We usually play like a normal match.

“But when you are poked so much from the front in the first match, then it was within all the boys that if we win that match, it will be celebrated. That’s why that extra excitement came within everyone. It was because everyone had heard all of it and the anger was there. Then after winning, that moment felt different. It felt like we arrived at a very different place after winning that game,” he said.

Chauhan alleged that in the league game, Pakistan players abused every dismissed Indian batter and kept up the on-field taunts after the match. “The thing was, in that game, like whoever was the batter going out after being dismissed, he was being abused – like maa-behen ki gaali (given abuses in name of mother and sister).

“So that happened with every batter. Even after losing that game, they were shouting in our face and outside the dressing room. I mean, they were deliberately showing us that ‘kaunsa bada teer maar liya (What great feat have you accomplished?)’.

“By the way we don’t get into wild celebrations. We say that, ‘Okay, they are like that and used to celebrating all these little things.’ But then these things come to your mind – that it was celebrated against us, so then if you give it, then you have to take it. So that’s the scene. If they have given that treatment, then they will have to take it too. So it was the same for us. If we win, then we have to celebrate too.”

He said the team manager stepped in to keep the celebrations from going further. “Our manager sir was there and he stopped us. Otherwise, it would have gone much further. Our manager sir was stopping us, as he looks after dealing with the match referees. He was thinking that no legal action should be taken or match fees can be deducted. So he was saving us and said, ‘No, no, we have won. Just enjoy.’”

Back home, families were watching that final ball too and felt elated on the win. “Everyone was very happy and saying, you have done a great job today. It is a very proud thing for the country. Everyone forgot their personal performance. But everyone was celebrating India’s victory. The parents said, ‘Tumne bharat ka naam roshan kar diya (You have made India proud).’ You have won the trophy and brought it home,” concluded Chauhan.

item.title: Man allegedly tied up and set ablaze on Bengaluru road in broad daylight
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.category: man tied up and set on fire
item.description: A man identified as Mohammad suffered severe burn injuries after unidentified attackers allegedly tied him up and set him ablaze on a Bengaluru road on Wednesday morning. Police have launched an investigation and are searching for the accused.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru: A shocking incident in broad daylight, in which a man was allegedly tied up and set ablaze in the middle of a road at Veerabhadranagar in Bengaluru on Wednesday, has raised serious concerns among people over public safety and the audacity of criminals.

The victim, identified as Mohammad, suffered severe burn injuries after a group of unidentified persons allegedly attacked him, tied his hands and legs and set him on fire on the road around 6 a.m. on Wednesday. The incident occurred within the limits of Girinagar police station.

According to preliminary investigations, a group of boys allegedly assaulted Mohammad before tying his hands and legs and setting him ablaze.

The accused reportedly fled the spot after carrying out the attack.

During the incident, Mohammad is said to have managed to untie himself and run towards the roadside while engulfed in flames before collapsing.

Locals who noticed Mohammad struggling with severe burn injuries on the roadside rushed to alert the police.

The police immediately reached the spot and shifted the injured man to Victoria Hospital for treatment. His condition is said to be serious, and he is currently not in a position to give a statement to the investigating officers.

The incident, which reportedly took place in full public view, has shocked residents of the locality. The manner in which the attackers allegedly tied up the victim and set him on fire in the middle of the road has triggered concerns over the law and order situation.

Police have secured the scene of the crime and launched a hunt for the accused. However, the identity of the attackers and the motive behind the brutal assault are yet to be established. It is also unclear why Mohammad had come to the locality and what led to the attack.

Given the gravity of the incident, police are collecting evidence and examining available clues to identify the perpetrators.

Further details are awaited.

item.title: Apple restores most services after internal software update triggers outage; rules out cyberattack
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Apple has restored most services after an internal software update caused an outage affecting iCloud and Apple Pay, ruling out a cyberattack. The disruption follows Microsoft's November 12 outage, which affected several Microsoft 365 services worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Apple has said that it has restored most of its services after an internal software update triggered a widespread outage that disrupted customer-facing platforms, including iCloud and Apple Pay and ruled out any cybersecurity incident.

The iPhone maker said the disruption was caused by an internal update, not a cyberattack.

“We are working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible,” an Apple spokesperson said and added that many affected services had already been restored, as per reports.

The outage affected several Apple services with users reporting difficulties accessing iCloud and making payments through Apple Pay.

In addition, Downdetector — an outage-tracking platform — has shown more than 2,000 users reported issues with Apple Pay, while around 1,800 reports related to iCloud were recorded at the peak of the disruption. However, it compiles outage reports from users and other sources and the actual number of affected users may differ from the reported figures.

The incident marks the latest in a string of technology service disruptions affecting major US technology companies in recent weeks.

The Apple outage comes shortly after Microsoft disclosed the findings of an investigation into a major global disruption of Microsoft 365 services earlier this month.

Microsoft said the massive November 12 outage stemmed from a combination of a hidden software flaw, an unusually high volume of traffic and reduced server capacity.

The incident disrupted services including Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office applications worldwide.

According to Microsoft’s preliminary findings, a flaw in networking software, combined with a surge in traffic after Teams workloads were shifted from a backup system and a simultaneous reduction in server availability, triggered cascading failures across its infrastructure.

Microsoft said its engineers eventually identified the faulty code and restored services, with a detailed post-incident review and corrective action plan expected to be released later.

item.title: Microsoft unveils AI models, Copilot platform and Azure upgrades at Ignite
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Microsoft has unveiled a new range of AI products, models and infrastructure upgrades at its Ignite conference. The announcements include Copilot Workspaces, new AI models, an AI transparency initiative and upgrades to Azure infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: US-based technology giant Microsoft on Wednesday unveiled a broad slate of artificial intelligence (AI) products, models and infrastructure upgrades at its Ignite — annual technical conference.

Taking to the social media platform X, Chief Executive Satya Nadella has outlined the company’s vision of using AI to deliver real outcomes for businesses and users, days after the software giant detailed the causes of a major global Microsoft 365 outage.

“Our ambition with everything we are announcing at Ignite today is to parlay technological advances into real outcomes and new points of leverage for people, organisations and society at large,” Nadella wrote on X.

At the centre of the announcements was Copilot Workspaces, a platform designed to enable people and AI agents to collaborate using shared context toward common objectives.

The company also introduced a series of new AI models, including Microsoft-Decision 1.1, Code 2 and Cyber 2 Flash which the company said offers security capabilities that outperform frontier models at a lower cost.

It further expanded its model ecosystem by bringing OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 to its Foundry platform while also adding Meta’s latest models.

Among other product launches, Microsoft announced Agent 365 Business Analytics, which Nadella described as an ERP system for AI that helps companies link AI spending to business outcomes and optimise returns on their investments.

Nadella said Microsoft Perception is now generally available, enabling security teams and AI agents to work together to identify and respond to threats at machine speed.

The company also launched the AI Transparency Initiative, saying it is working with more than 40 organisations to develop open standards for accountable, verifiable and safe AI systems.

Microsoft also announced the general availability of HorizonDB, its distributed PostgreSQL database service on Azure which it said can deliver up to eight times the performance of self-managed PostgreSQL deployments.

Apart from that, Nadella added that Microsoft is rearchitecting core Azure computing, storage and networking infrastructure to support AI agents operating at scale.

Additionally, the company also highlighted collaborations with customers and partners across industries, including Alaska Air, AT&T, BlackRock, BNY, Chevron, Epic, Publicis Groupe, Salesforce and Unilever.

The product announcements come less than a week after a major Microsoft 365 disruption affected services including Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office applications worldwide.

Microsoft had that the outage was caused by a combination of a hidden software flaw, a surge in traffic and a reduction in available server capacity.

item.title: KTR launches ‘Game Changers’ book chronicling journeys of 20 everyday heroes
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao launched Uday Shankar's book ‘Game Changers’, featuring the journeys of 20 individuals who have made a difference to society. Hyderabad-based social activist Azhar Maqsusi, known as the Hyderabad Foodman, is among those featured.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao launched “Game Changers”, a book by Uday Shankar chronicling the inspiring journeys of 20 individuals who have made a difference to society, including Hyderabad-based social activist Azhar Maqsusi, popularly known as the “Hyderabad Foodman”.

The book features the life stories of several achievers, including the ‘Metro Man’ E Sreedharan, the ‘Missile Woman of India’ Tessy Thomas, the ‘Sightless Hero’ Srikanth Bolla, and the ‘Mountain Man’ Dashrath Manjhi among othes.

Praising Maqsusi for his humanitarian work, Rama Rao said he had been distributing free food to the hungry every day for more than 5,000 days, guided by the motto “Hunger has no religion”. He expressed gratitude to Maqsusi for his selfless service and wished him strength to continue helping the needy.

item.title: Chip curbs, mineral supplies test Trump’s China diplomacy ahead of Xi talks
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Donald Trump's meeting with Xi Jinping comes amid US administration divisions over advanced technology restrictions, AI cooperation and trade tensions. The discussions also carry implications for India, which depends heavily on China for rare-earth permanent magnets used across key manufacturing industries.
item.content:encoded:
Washington: US President Donald Trump heads into talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week amid divisions within his administration over restricting China’s access to advanced technology, even as Washington and Beijing pursue cooperation on artificial intelligence risks and seek to preserve their trade truce.

The White House schedule places their bilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, followed by three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. China’s Foreign Ministry has separately confirmed the trilateral meeting for November 19.

The New York Times reported Tuesday that the disagreement over technology restrictions extends beyond Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and much of the National Security Council staff have supported broader limits on China’s access to advanced AI chips, while Lutnick pushed for a softer approach, the newspaper reported, citing current and former officials familiar with the discussions.

The Times also reported concerns among advocates of a tougher China policy that Trump could reverse recently announced restrictions or use them as bargaining material in talks with Xi. Those concerns do not establish that Trump intends to offer such a concession.

Former national security advisor H.R. McMaster told the newspaper that Trump’s confidence in his negotiating ability could undermine a consistent approach to Beijing.

“I think President Trump is often impeded by his belief that he can get the deal nobody else can get,” McMaster said.

The administration announced restrictions Monday aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing advanced American computing technology remotely through overseas data centres.

But technology competition is only one part of the relationship.

The Washington Post highlighted parallel efforts to manage AI risks through model-testing cooperation and an incident-notification channel.

Bessent said Washington and Beijing had begun a dialogue intended to reduce shared risks and prevent misunderstandings.

He outlined plans to exchange practices for evaluating advanced AI models before their release and to establish a direct channel for the two countries to alert each other about any serious incidents involving their models.

Bessent also described the administration’s broader economic approach: “our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple.”

Critical-mineral supplies present another test of whether diplomatic agreements can produce dependable commercial outcomes — an issue with direct relevance to India’s manufacturing ambitions.

A November 10 analysis by the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies found that US imports of the covered rare-earth compounds and metals from China averaged 19.3 metric tonnes a month between November 2025 and September 2026.

That compared with a monthly average of 76.8 metric tonnes before Beijing’s April 2025 restrictions, a decline of about 75 per cent.

India also depends heavily on Chinese supplies of permanent magnets.

An Indian government background paper published in December 2025 said China accounted for between 84.8 per cent and 90.4 per cent of India’s permanent-magnet imports by quantity during the financial years 2022-23 through 2024-25.

India has approved a Rs 7,280 crore scheme intended to establish domestic manufacturing capacity of 6,000 metric tons annually for sintered rare-earth permanent magnets. The materials are important for electric vehicles, renewable energy, electronics, aerospace and defence.

Trump’s engagement with India and other regional partners adds a strategic dimension to the China visit.

At a November 9 CSIS briefing, Edgard Kagan, the organisation’s senior adviser and Freeman chair in China studies, said a Quad meeting before Trump’s China talks would remind Beijing of Washington’s significant regional relationships.

The Quad leaders met in Manila on Tuesday. They discussed Iran, safe navigation and energy security, and affirmed cooperation on critical-mineral supply chains.

The Shenzhen talks will take place against that combination of strategic competition, commercial dependence and efforts to manage technological risks.

item.title: Dhanush thanks Dhoni after CSK exit as player, says game will never be the same
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Actor Dhanush has penned an emotional note for M S Dhoni following his release from Chennai Super Kings as a player. Thanking the former captain for his memories and guidance, Dhanush said he would await Dhoni's presence on the sidelines.
item.content:encoded:
Chennai: Popular Tamil actor and producer Dhanush, who is a big fan of the IPL franchise Chennai Super Kings and its former captain M S Dhoni, has now penned an emotional post in the wake of M S Dhoni’s release from the franchise as a player.

Taking to his X timeline, Dhanush wrote, “Some players entertain us. Some become a part of our lives. MS Dhoni has been both.”

He then went on to thank the cricketing legend, who has now returned to the Chennai Super Kings as its mentor.

Dhanush wrote, “Thank you for all the memories. The game will never be quite the same without you, but I’ll wait to see you on the sidelines. Thousands of youngsters have benefited from your advice and knowledge, hope it continues to inspire and fire up the upcoming generation. Farewell champion (folded hands).”

Dhanush’s family members too are closely associated with the franchise.

In fact, Dhanush’s sister-in-law, director Gitanjali Selvaraghavan had in March last year disclosed that their family was in for a “sweet surprise” when cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni along with other CSK team members arrived for her dad’s book release event.

Gitanjali’s father, P S Raman, a former vice-president of the Tamil Nadu Cricket Association, had his book ‘Leo: The Untold Story of Chennai Super Kings’ released last year.

Gitanjali Selvaraghavan, who took to her Instagram timeline to pen a lengthy post of gratitude in which she thanked Chennai Super Kings CEO Kasi Viswanathan, music director Anirudh and cricketers Ashwin Ravichandran and Krishnamachari Srikkanth for their help in hosting her dad’s book release function, had said, “My father P.S. Raman’s latest book ‘Leo: The Untold Story of Chennai Super Kings’ was released this Sunday in a quiet private function. My sincerest thanks on behalf of our family to the honoured chief guests Mr. CD Gopinath, @anirudhofficial @rashwin99 @cheekaofficial and @suhailchandhok for hosting the event so seamlessly. Thank you @kasiviswanathanvijaya sir for all your help and support. And of course, what a sweet surprise by our own Thala and team for attending the event!”

Gitanjali Selvaraghavan, who is the wife of Dhanush’s elder brother Selvaraghavan, is best known for having directed the film ‘Maalai Naerathu Mayakkam’, which featured Balakrishna Kola and Wamiqa Gabbi in the lead.

The film had cinematography by Sridhar and music by Amrit while editing was by Rukesh. The film, which released on January 1, 2016, was produced by Beeptone Studios.

item.title: Fire destroys furniture shop in Shankarpally; no casualties reported
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A fire at A-One Furniture Shop near Donthanpally Gate in Shankarpally gutted its entire furniture stock on Wednesday. Fire personnel battled the blaze for nearly two hours. No casualties were reported, and an electrical short circuit is suspected.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A major fire broke out at A-One furniture shop near Donthanpally Gate in Shankarpally on city outskirts on Wednesday morning, destroying the furniture and other goods stored inside the premises.

The fire is suspected to have been caused by an electrical short circuit.

Local residents noticed thick smoke and flames emerging from the shop and alerted its owner, Saddam Wajid, and the fire department.

On receiving information, fire department personnel rushed to the spot with two fire engines and fought the raging flames for nearly two hours before bringing the blaze under control.

Fortunately, no casualties were reported as the incident occurred during the night. However, the location of the furniture shop raised concerns as a boys’ hostel is situated nearby, while a paint shop is located on the other side.

Meanwhile, fire department authorities said the furniture shop lacked adequate fire safety arrangements, which contributed to the seriousness of the incident. The entire furniture stock was gutted, resulting in substantial property loss.

Fire personnel prevented the flames from spreading to neighbouring establishments and averted further damage.

The worth of the damaged property was yet to be estimated.

item.title: Sensex falls 370 points, Nifty drops below 25,250 amid profit-taking
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty declined on Wednesday amid profit-taking after a two-day rally. The Sensex fell 370 points during trade, while the Nifty dropped nearly 149 points. Asian markets were mixed, and US indices ended lower on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty declined in early trade on Wednesday amid profit-taking after a two-day rally.

The 30-share BSE Sensex declined 75.10 points to 82,482.30 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty skidded 26.95 points to 25,355.65.

Further in the trade, the BSE benchmark traded 370.43 points lower at 82,144.22, and the Nifty dropped 148.70 points to 25,234.65.

From the Sensex pack, Tata Consultancy Services, Titan, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Finance, and Tata Steel were among the major laggards.

Maruti, UltraTech Cement, Mahindra & Mahindra, and ICICI Bank were among the winners.

The BSE Sensex has jumped nearly 11 per cent so far this month till November 17, and the NSE Nifty climbed over 10 per cent.

Benchmark indices extended the rally for the second straight day on Tuesday. The Sensex rallied 427.40 points, or 0.52 per cent, to settle at 82,532.19 in the previous trade. The Nifty climbed 96.30 points, or 0.38 per cent, to end at 25,387.40.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 0.69 per cent lower at USD 92.53 per barrel.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 4,195.38 crore on Tuesday, according to exchange data.

In Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi and Japan’s Nikkei 225 index traded higher, while Shanghai’s SSE Composite index and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index quoted lower.

The US equity markets ended in negative territory on Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.64 per cent, S&P 500 was down 1.03 per cent and Nasdaq Composite declined 0.74 per cent.

item.title: Israel elects Netanyahu opponent Matan Kahana as parliament speaker amid coalition talks
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Israel's parliament has elected opposition lawmaker Matan Kahana as its new speaker, dealing a setback to Benjamin Netanyahu's camp. The move strengthens opposition control over the legislative agenda as Gadi Eisenkot continues efforts to form a new government.
item.content:encoded:
Jerusalem: Israel’s parliament elected a new speaker opposed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, giving Netanyahu’s opponents control over the legislative agenda as talks to form a new government continued.

Matan Kahana, a lawmaker with Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party, defeated Ofir Katz of Netanyahu’s Likud party by 66 votes to 52, replacing Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana on Tuesday night (local time).

Live broadcast from the chamber showed lawmakers from the anti-Netanyahu bloc breaking into applause, hugging and shaking hands after the vote, reports Xinhua news agency.

Kahana’s election, backed by Arab parties, opens the way for Netanyahu’s opponents to advance plans to repeal legislation passed as part of his government’s judicial overhaul before a new government takes office.

Eisenkot, a former military chief, has until December 6 to form a government, with a possible extension of up to two weeks granted by the president.

Netanyahu’s opponents won 67 of parliament’s 120 seats in the Oct. 27 election, but that majority includes 19 seats held by Arab parties, whose support some of Eisenkot’s prospective coalition partners reject.

Earlier on November 10, Israel’s newly elected parliament was sworn in, as opposition parties moved to use their parliamentary majority to replace key allies of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

President Isaac Herzog opened the inaugural session of the 120-seat parliament, or Knesset, following which the newly elected lawmakers took their oath of office.

The ceremony followed an October 27 election in which Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc lost its majority, securing 53 seats against 67 for parties opposed to him.

Ahead of the ceremony, opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party said more than 61 lawmakers had signed a request to replace parliament Speaker Amir Ohana, a lawmaker from Netanyahu’s Likud party, and nominated Matan Kahana, a Yashar lawmaker, as his successor.

Eisenkot’s allies also agreed on candidates to head key parliamentary committees, including Avigdor Lieberman, a right-wing ally whose opposition to forming a government with Arab parties has complicated coalition talks, as chairman of the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee. Liran Avisar Ben Horin, a lawmaker from former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett’s party, will head the Finance Committee, making her the first woman to hold the post.

item.title: Telangana High Court directs safeguards in placement of rescued women in Protective Homes
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana High Court has directed the State to implement its human trafficking SOP, ensure individual assessment before placing rescued persons in Protective Homes and maintain a district-wise roster. It also ordered awareness programmes and periodic compliance reports from authorities.
item.content:encoded:
Legal Correspondent

 

Hyderabad: A Division Bench comprising Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Narsing Rao Nandikonda issued the directions while disposing of a writ petition filed by Hyderabad-based NGO Prajwala, which challenged an order of the III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, directing the admission of nine women rescued during a raid at Verily Beauty Salon and Spa into its Protective Home. The NGO had objected to the admission of one of the women, M. Renuka, alleging that she was involved in organising brothel activities. It contended that placing alleged organisers alongside trafficking survivors could compromise the safety and rehabilitation of the latter. Senior Counsel L. Ravichander, representing counsel Deepak Misra for the petitioner, submitted that rescued persons must be individually assessed and their antecedents and roles verified before they are placed in Protective Homes. The State informed the Court that Renuka had subsequently been released to her mother and that a consolidated SOP on human trafficking had been formulated on February 26, 2026.

The Bench observed that a person cannot be branded a trafficker merely because an FIR has been registered against them. At the same time, describing someone as a rescued person does not dispense with the need to assess the safety risks they may pose to other residents. It stressed the need for an individualised inquiry and a reasoned judicial decision before placement in a Protective Home. The Court directed the Director General of Police to ensure effective implementation of the SOP through the Women Safety Wing and Anti-Human Trafficking Units. It also directed the authorities to maintain a district-wise roster of recognised Protective Homes and ensure appropriate assessment and placement of rescued persons. The Bench further issued directions for awareness programmes on human trafficking in educational institutions and through Legal Services Authorities. It directed the State to submit an initial compliance report within three months, followed by six-monthly progress reports for one year.

item.title: Hyderabad: Woman allegedly murdered by husband; three-year-old daughter missing
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 30-year-old woman, Asma Begum, was allegedly murdered by her husband at their Hasan Nagar residence in Bahadurpura on Tuesday evening. The suspect reportedly fled with their three-year-old daughter. Police have formed a special team to trace them.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A 30-year-old woman was brutally murdered by her husband, who slit her throat with a knife at their house in Hasan Nagar in Bahadurpura on Tuesday evening.

The victim, Asma Begum, was allegedly killed by her husband, Dharmender, around 7.30 pm. After committing the crime, the suspect reportedly fled from the spot along with their three-year-old daughter, leaving the woman’s body at their residence.

According to preliminary information, the couple had a love marriage around 15 years ago and had migrated from Bihar to Hyderabad. They subsequently moved into a rented house in Hasan Nagar in the Old City about ten days ago.

The motive behind the murder is yet to be established.

On receiving information, Rajendranagar Zone DCP Srinivas and Falaknuma ACP M.A. Javed visited the crime spot and examined the circumstances surrounding the murder. Police collected evidence and initiated an investigation.

The Bahadurpura police have formed special team to trace and arrest the suspect. Police are also trying to establish the circumstances that led to the murder and locate the missing child.

item.title: Telangana High Court issues notices over alleged illegal Task Force searches
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana High Court has issued notices to senior police officials and the Home Department over allegations that Task Force personnel conducted searches and seizures in civilian clothes without registering FIRs or following prescribed procedures. The matter will be heard on December 12.
item.content:encoded:
Legal Correspondent

 

Hyderabad: Justice T. Madhavi Devi of the Telangana High Court on Tuesday issued notices to the Home Department, Director General of Police (DGP), Hyderabad Police Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner of Police (Task Force), seeking their explanation on allegations that Task Force police personnel were conducting inspections, searches and seizures in civilian clothes without following the procedure prescribed under law. The judge was hearing a writ petition filed by B. Balaraj of Borabanda, who alleged that Task Force personnel were acting illegally by conducting searches and investigations without wearing police uniforms and without registering a First Information Report (FIR).

Counsel for the petitioner contended that conducting inspections and investigations unilaterally, even before registration of an FIR, was contrary to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023. It was further argued that the Task Force personnel were conducting searches and seizures without following a transparent procedure or providing the persons concerned an opportunity to explain their position.The petitioner also questioned the authority of Assistant Commissioners of Police to issue search warrants, contending that such warrants could be issued only by Judicial Magistrates in accordance with the procedure established under law. After hearing the submissions, the Judge issued notices to the respondents, calling upon them to file their explanations. The matter was adjourned to December 12.

item.title: Telangana High Court directs government to finalise elevator safety Bill within eight weeks
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Telangana High Court has directed the Chief Secretary to expedite legislation on elevator safety and maintenance in multi-storey buildings. The draft Bill must be placed before the Cabinet within eight weeks amid concerns over accidents and regulatory gaps.
item.content:encoded:
Legal Correspondent

Hyderabad: The Telangana High Court has directed the State Chief Secretary to expedite the process of formulating a legislation to regulate the safety and maintenance of elevators in multi-storey buildings and ensure that the draft Bill is placed before the Cabinet within eight weeks.

A Division Bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Sam Koshy and Justice Chalapathi Rao expressed dissatisfaction over the prolonged delay on the part of the State government in bringing out the proposed Elevator Safety Bill, despite several earlier directions issued by the court to formulate a comprehensive legislation in this regard. The matter came up for hearing on Tuesday in a suo motu public interest litigation registered by the High Court on the basis of letters received from several individuals highlighting the absence of an effective legal framework governing elevator safety in the State. The issue gained significance in the wake of several elevator-related accidents, including the death of a police battalion commandant last year, allegedly due to poor maintenance and inadequate safety standards.

During the hearing, counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that draft rules and proposed guidelines had already been forwarded to the State government in compliance with the earlier directions of the High Court. However, the government had failed to take any concrete steps towards examining the proposals and finalising the legislation. They pointed out that there had been considerable delay in the process despite the seriousness of the issue. The government counsel informed the Bench that the file relating to the proposed Elevator Safety Act had been forwarded to the Industries and Commerce Department for examination. After obtaining the views of the concerned departments, the proposal would be sent to the Law Department for further scrutiny before being placed before the Cabinet.

The government counsel submitted that the entire process was likely to take another two months. Expressing dissatisfaction over the delay, the Bench directed the Chief Secretary to take necessary steps to expedite the formulation of the legislation. It also directed the State government to file a counter affidavit explaining the steps taken towards drafting the proposed Bill. The Bench further observed that the safety guidelines submitted by the petitioners’ counsel should be duly examined and appropriate steps should be taken to incorporate the suggested measures into the proposed legislation, if they had not already been included. The Bench adjourned the matter by eight weeks.

item.title: Mancherial police farmhouse party: Five policemen transferred, Enquiry against nine
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Fourteen police personnel from Bellampalli station face action after videos of them partying at a farmhouse near Thandur went viral. Five have been transferred, while departmental proceedings have been initiated against nine for allegedly skipping duty.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: Five policemen have been transferred and0 attached to Ramagundam Commissionerate, while departmental action has been initiated against nine personnel for partying at a farmhouse by skipping duties at their police station. Ramagundam Commissioner of Police Amber Kishore Jha issued an order to this effect on Tuesday night.

Action has been taken against 14 staffers of the department-Bellampalli station after the party video clips went viral on social media platforms on Tuesday. They danced to songs at a farmhouse near Thandur on Sunday. They reportedly consumed liquor and danced in the rain at the venue as part of birthday celebrations of a colleague.

The policemen and women drew flak for partying and celebrating the birthday at the farmhouse after registering their attendance in the station records and without obtaining permission. WhatsApp users criticised the police for neglecting their responsibility to protect law and order and focusing on parties.

item.title: Trump administration seeks 50.1 billion usd to overhaul US air traffic control systems
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Trump administration has sought $50.1 billion from Congress to modernise US air traffic control systems and airport infrastructure. The request comes as the FAA pauses Juniper router installations following a nationwide flight shutdown linked to a telecommunications failure.
item.content:encoded:
Washington: The Trump administration has formally sought $50.1 billion from Congress to overhaul air traffic control systems and airport infrastructure, as the Federal Aviation Administration paused new installations of routers linked to last week’s nationwide flight shutdown.

The request includes funding for up to five consolidated regional air traffic control centres and construction or improvements at as many as 140 FAA-owned control towers. It goes beyond telecommunications repairs to include major airport and passenger-terminal projects.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and White House budget director Russ Vought sent the request to the leaders of the House and Senate appropriations committees on Tuesday (local time).

Of the total, $10.1 billion would fund air traffic control modernisation, including $7.2 billion for a common automation platform and controller workstations, $2 billion for cloud computing and telecommunications, $600 million for traffic-flow technology and $300 million for consolidation of terminal air traffic control facilities.

Another $10 billion would be split equally between airport improvement and terminal grants. A separate $10 billion pilot program would replace, modernise or reconstruct ageing terminals at selected hub airports.

The remaining $20 billion would be divided between regional control centres and control towers. The package is a funding request requiring congressional approval, not an approved spending program.

The Transportation Department said the proposed consolidated centres would replace facilities in the existing network of 22 regional centres, the newest of which was built in 1969.

The administration is seeking the money in addition to $12.5 billion Congress provided in July 2025.

The request came as investigators continued examining the telecommunications failure that prompted the November 13 ground stop.

Duffy said Tuesday that investigators had reproduced the malfunction at an L3Harris facility in Florida but had not established its underlying cause.

“We’ve been able to recreate what happened in El Dorado, but the root cause of what happened, we don’t have clarity yet,” he said.

Duffy said FAA personnel, technology companies and the FBI were participating in the examination. He said national security agencies had told him the incident was not a hack.

The FAA said it had paused installation of Juniper routers and disabled the relevant functionality on more than 60 other routers as a precaution.

The ground stop began at approximately 3:30 p.m. Eastern on Friday, and air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. About 3,500 aircraft already airborne landed safely, the FAA said.

Democrats on the Senate Commerce Committee demanded an explanation of both the failure and the increased funding request.

In a letter dated November 16 and released Tuesday, 13 senators led by Maria Cantwell of Washington sought a joint technical briefing involving the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper by November 23.

They said identifying a malfunctioning device did not establish why it failed. They also sought stronger operational testing, independent validation and demonstrated backup and recovery procedures before additional routers were deployed.

The senators questioned how the requested money would address the vulnerabilities exposed by the outage, noting that the administration had sought about $30 billion just days earlier.

“Modernisation cannot come at the expense of operational safety,” they wrote.

item.title: Congress MLC Balmoor Venkat escapes with minor injuries in car accident near Kothur
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today Desk
item.description: Congress MLC Balmoor Venkat escaped with minor injuries after his car met with an accident near Kothur bypass in the early hours of Wednesday. The vehicle was badly damaged while he was returning to Hyderabad from Tirupati.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Congress MLC Balmoor Venkat had a narrow escape after the car he was travelling in met with an accident near Kothur bypass, within the Future City limits, while he was returning to Hyderabad from Tirupati on Wednesday early morning.

As per information available, the vehicle was badly damaged in the accident, while Venkat suffered minor injuries. He along with staff left the spot in another vehicle.

The accident reportedly occurred while the MLC was travelling towards Hyderabad. The exact circumstances leading to the mishap are yet to be ascertained.

Despite the damage to the vehicle, Venkat escaped without serious injuries.

The incident has caused concern among his followers, who expressed relief after learning that he was safe.

item.title: Nvidia board rejects Jensen Huang’s return as US lawmakers set questioning dates
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Nvidia's board has rejected co-founder Jensen Huang's proposed return as CEO, while US lawmakers prepare to question him and the company's general counsel over potential national security violations. The company also reported strong quarterly revenue growth despite scrutiny.
item.content:encoded:
Washington: Nvidia’s board has said it does not intend to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as Chief Executive, rejecting his proposed comeback as US lawmakers confirmed dates to question him and the company’s top lawyer over potential national-security and chip-export breaches.

Board Chairman Harvey Jones announced the position during Nvidia’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday (local time), hours after Huang publicly expressed willingness to return to the company he helped build.

“The NVIDIA board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said.

Jones said Nvidia had retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent successor. He declined to take questions about the circumstances of Huang’s resignation or the continuing investigation.

Huang resigned as President, CEO and a Director on November 12. Chief Financial Officer Collette Kress took over as interim CEO while retaining her finance responsibilities. The company said it would consider internal and external candidates for the permanent position.

Earlier Tuesday, Huang said he would be “honoured” to return if the board determined that doing so would serve shareholders, employees, the company and the United States, ABC News reported.

The scrutiny surrounding his departure includes his reported relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed. US officials reportedly suspect she had links to Chinese intelligence. China has rejected the espionage allegations.

On Capitol Hill, the Chairmen of three House Committees announced that Jensen Huang had voluntarily agreed to a transcribed interview on December 1. Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter will appear on December 2.

The interviews will involve the Foreign Affairs Committee, the Intelligence Committee and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.

“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” committee Chairmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford said.

The lawmakers said they wanted answers about access to advanced American chips by Chinese actors and the role of a potential intelligence asset. Their announcement did not establish that a national-security breach had occurred.

Separately, the Justice and Commerce departments disclosed a timeline showing that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024, before the current controversy.

Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed in May 2025. Nvidia placed the company on its internal “no sell” list the following month, the departments said.

Also in June 2025, US investigators and Singaporean law enforcement officials conducted an on-site check at Megaspeed and interviewed Alice Huang, then its CEO.

The joint statement did not announce charges against Jensen Huang or Nvidia.

Megaspeed has said it conducts lawful business and has retained outside lawyers to investigate the allegations internally, NPR reported.

Nvidia also announced Tuesday a standing board committee to oversee national-security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risks. Director Suzanne Nora Johnson will chair the committee, which will retain independent outside experts.

The leadership turmoil accompanied another quarter of strong growth. Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for its third fiscal quarter, up 103% from a year earlier, including $107.6 billion from its data-centre business.

It forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, plus or minus 3 per cent, while assuming no data-centre compute revenue from China.

“Our momentum is real,” Kress said in the earnings release.

item.title: Groundwater depletion raises summer water concerns in Medchal district
item.dc:creator: Sunil Mungara
item.category: Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB)
item.description: A 74% rainfall deficit in October has contributed to a sharp fall in groundwater levels across Medchal-Malkajgiri district. Bachupally, Muduchintalapally, Uppal and Malkajgiri are among the areas facing depletion, raising concerns over water availability next summer.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Northern Hyderabad’s fringes in Medchal-Malkajgiri district face an early water shortage during the coming summer, with the latest Groundwater Department data showing severe depletion of groundwater levels across the district.

The situation has raised concerns among resident welfare associations, Malkajgiri civic body officials and Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWSSB).

According to a Groundwater Department report, Medchal-Malkajgiri district recorded a 74% rainfall deficit in October 2026, receiving just 27.9 mm of rain. The average groundwater level dropped to 12.67 metres below ground level (bgl) this October from 6.51 metres bgl in November 2025, indicating rapid depletion amid deficient rainfall.

The rainfall shortage was officially classified as a ‘Large Deficit’ phenomenon, which affected aquifer recharge, raising water-security concerns in peripheral urban areas ahead of winter and the dry summer cycle, said the report.

The groundwater levels varied sharply across the district. The piezometer at the Municipal Office in Dundigal-Gandimaisamma recorded the deepest level at 37.63 metres bgl in October, while the piezometer at ESI, Nacharam, recorded the shallowest level at 2.30 metres. Meanwhile, Dundigal is in a critical water-stress zone at 21.11 m bgl, indicating shallow aquifers are completely dry.

The groundwater levels in Uppal and Malkajgiri, identified as vulnerable zones, stand at 15.52 m bgl and 17.89 m bgl, respectively, and continue to decline, indicating that already deep levels exponentially increase domestic borewell failure rates.

Water levels also deteriorated rapidly in Muduchintalapally and Bachupally despite their absolute depths not being the worst on the list. Bachupally’s water table fell 36.54%, while Muduchintalapally recorded a 31.66% decline. The trend pointed to localised consumption spikes, possibly from rapid commercial or residential real-estate expansion, coinciding with dry weather.
