item.title: TG- RERA imposes penalties on builders and developers for different violations
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana RERA has penalised Sanali IT Parks and issued orders against several developers over violations, project delays and failure to fulfil commitments. The Authority directed refunds with interest in multiple cases and ordered the handover of a flat in Miyapur
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Cracking its whip, the Telangana Real Estate Regulatory Authority (TGRERA) has imposed penalties on leading builders and developers for different violations.

The promoters were directed to make payments to the consumers with interests in a few cases within the prescribed time. It also cautioned the promoters that failure to comply with its directions would attract penalties under Section 63 of the RERA Act.

A penalty of Rs.25 lakh was levied on Sanali IT Parks for violations of Sections 3 and 4 of the RERA Act, directing payment within 30 days. The Authority directed the respondents to immediately stop advertising, marketing, booking and selling units in the unregistered “Sanali The Edge” project at Manchirevula until RERA registration is obtained.

Telangana RERA directed Sri Aditya Squares to refund Rs.17 lakh, along with applicable interest, due to delays in project construction and the promoter’s failure to refund the amount despite the homebuyer’s cancellation request and the promoter’s assurance to initiate repayment.

Tripura Constructions was directed to refund Rs.41.85 lakh, along with applicable interest, for failing to obtain the necessary statutory approvals, commence construction and deliver possession of the flat within a reasonable period, despite collecting substantial payments from the homebuyer.

Similarly, Vasavi Realtors LLP was instructed to pay 10.85 percent annual interest on Rs.49.50 lakh paid by the homebuyer, from 7 February 2025 until actual possession, due to the delay in completing the project and handing over the flat as agreed.

Telangana RERA directed SVM Aditya Homes to refund Rs.27.16 lakh, along with applicable interest, for failing to obtain the required HMDA approvals, commence and complete the project, and fulfil its contractual obligations despite collecting money from the homebuyer.

Arine Infraa was directed to hand over possession of Flat No. 502 in the ARINE Emerald project at Miyapur, rejecting the promoter’s claim of Rs.6.58 lakh in outstanding charges as unsupported by the sale agreement and registered sale deed.

BVR Infra Developers Private Limited was ordered to refund Rs.7 lakh, along with applicable interest, for failing to complete the plot registration and hand over possession as agreed. The promoter also failed to honour its commitment to refund the amount, despite issuing repayment cheques.

In another case, TG RERA directed Bhuvanteza Infra projects Private Limited to refund Rs.26 lakh, along with applicable interest, after finding that the promoter had abandoned the project and failed to undertake construction or deliver possession despite collecting substantial advance payments from the homebuyers.

item.title: Cheyutha pension programme witnesses clashes across Telangana
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The distribution of Cheyutha pension sanction letters across Telangana witnessed clashes involving Congress, BRS and BJP workers. Disputes over stage access, protocol and local development issues led to heated exchanges in Siddipet, Adilabad and Yadadri-Bhongir on Tuesday
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Ruckus broke out at several venues across Telangana during the distribution of Cheyutha pension sanction letters on Tuesday. The disturbances were triggered by various issues, including alleged protocol violations.

Heated arguments broke out between ruling Congress leaders and opposition BRS members at several places. In a few instances, Congress and BJP workers also clashed.

The Congress government claimed that elaborate arrangements had been made to ensure the smooth conduct of the programme. However, at several venues, Congress leaders reportedly prevented BRS leaders from sharing the stage, leading to heated exchanges.

In Siddipet, Bhongir MP Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy entered into an argument with BRS MLA Palla Rajeshwar Reddy. When the BRS MLA arrived on the stage, Congress workers raised slogans and disrupted the proceedings. Workers from both parties raised slogans against each other.

In Adilabad, Congress and BJP workers reportedly exchanged blows over an attempt to pose for photographs with beneficiaries on the stage. The incident took place in the presence of BJP MLA Payal Shankar. Videos showing workers from both parties attacking each other were circulated on social media.

A similar confrontation was reported in Yadadri-Bhongir, where Congress MLA Beerla Ilaiah expressed anger over BRS sarpanches raising several issues, particularly delays in development works.

When BRS leaders insisted that the MLA take up their concerns with the government, he reportedly asked them to leave the venue.

item.title: Sourav Ganguly backs Rishabh Pant’s return to Delhi Capitals
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Delhi Capitals have retained 16 players ahead of IPL 2027, including captain Axar Patel, KL Rahul and Rishabh Pant. The franchise released nine players, including Mitchell Starc, and will fill vacant slots at the December 16 mini-auction in Goa
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Indian Premier League (IPL) franchise Delhi Capitals (DC) on Tuesday announced the retention of 16 players ahead of the IPL 2027 season, retaining a core group as the franchise begins preparations for the upcoming edition of the tournament.

The retained list features several established Indian names, including team captain Axar Patel, leading Indian batter KL Rahul, wicketkeeper-batter and former team captain Rishabh Pant, who returned to the franchise in June this year, and opener Prithvi Shaw. The squad also retains international experience in the form of David Miller, Kyle Jamieson, Lungi Ngidi and Tristan Stubbs.

The group is further strengthened by a promising crop of young talent, including Sameer Rizvi, Ashutosh Sharma, Madhav Tiwari, Vipraj Nigam, Auqib Nabi, Mukesh Kumar, Tripurana Vijay and Zeeshan Ansari, giving the franchise a blend of experience and emerging talent as it looks ahead to the new season.

Speaking about the thought process behind the retentions and releases, Delhi Capitals coach Sourav Ganguly told JioStar, “It’s a mix of everything – performances over the last few years, what the franchise believes it needs for the next two years, who the franchise values, and who it believes is good enough to win cricket matches in the IPL.”

“It’s great to have Rishabh Pant back at Delhi Capitals. He is a quality player. I’m confident about turning the franchise’s fortunes around,” he said.

Highlighting captain Axar Patel’s importance to the squad, Ganguly told JioStar, “Axar is irreplaceable in Delhi Capitals. Yes, there had been people asking, but we have also gone and asked for players who we knew wouldn’t be released. That’s simply how things work during an IPL trade window. However, when it came to both Axar and Ashutosh, the answer was an outright no. They are integral to our team.”

Speaking about the young players the team has invested in, Ganguly added, “Sameer Rizvi is a young player to watch. His game has been improving, and Ashutosh Sharma is another player we bank on a lot. These are two young players DC has invested in over time, and I hope they have a successful season.”

Delhi Capitals have also released nine players from their previous 25-member squad: Nitish Rana, Karun Nair, Pathum Nissanka, Sahil Parakh, Ajay Mandal, Abhishek Porel, Dushmantha Chameera, Rehan Ahmed and Australian fast bowler Mitchell Starc, who had informed both the franchise and the BCCI of his unavailability for the IPL 2027 season.

The franchise will look to fill the vacant slots at the IPL 2027 mini-auction, scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16, 2026.

item.title: Mahabubabad MP Balram Naik’s controversial remarks draws criticism on social media
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Mahabubabad MP Porika Balram Naik has drawn criticism after suggesting women without husbands need not worry if they have Congress support. His remarks sparked reactions online, following criticism of Agriculture Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao over comments about Deepavali at Khammam
item.content:encoded:
Mahabubabad: Making controversial remarks and slip of the tongue seems to have become a hallmark of Congress leaders in Telangana.

It might be recalled that Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy; his Cabinet colleagues as well as the party legislators faced backlash on many occasions for their controversial remarks against the Opposition leaders and against their own party leaders.

Mahabubabad MP Porika Balram Naik was the latest man to join the team as his remarks made at a programme in the district have drawn severe criticism and condemnation on social media as well as mainstream media.

Speaking after participating in a foundation-laying ceremony for development projects in Gudur mandal he suggested that women do not need to worry even if they do not have husbands, having the Congress party with them was enough.

“There are some women, our sisters, who have placed their trust in the Congress party; even if they do not have their husbands by their side, it does not matter to them, as long as they have the Congress party,” remarked Balaram Naik.

He further stated that welfare schemes such as old-age pensions, supply of PDS rice, Indiramma houses and free electricity would be available to them only when the Congress party was in power and that other parties could not provide these benefits.

Hitting at the MP’s rather absurd comments on social media, several netizens advised the Telangana Congress leaders to keep their tongue under control while speaking at public meetings.

It might be recalled that Agriculture Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao had faced criticism on social media for rather objectionable language he used at a public meeting in Khammam on October 21.

The Minister asked the public when the festival of Deepavali was and when no one could answer, he remarked sarcastically, ‘Okka naa kodukki kuda Deepavali eppodu teliyada?’ which roughly translated into ‘Does not a single idiot know when Deepavali was?’ Many netizens expressed extreme anger at the Minister’s rather insulting comments directed at the public.

item.title: Hyderabad’s SFR Snehit wins men’s singles title at National Ranking Table Tennis Championships
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad's SFR Snehit claimed the men's singles title at the third National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Punjab on Tuesday. Maharashtra's Divyanshi Bhowmick won the women's title, defeating Tamil Nadu's Ananya Muralidharan in a seven-game final to secure the crown
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Hyderabad’s SFR Snehit won the men’s singles title at the third National Ranking Table Tennis Championships, held at the Shanti Devi Mittal Indoor Stadium, Lovely Professional University, Punjab, on Tuesday.

Divyanshi Bhowmick of Maharashtra won the women’s singles title, defeating Ananya Muralidharan of Tamil Nadu 7-11, 11-7, 10-12, 11-7, 12-10, 4-11, 14-12.

The seventh-seeded Snehit, representing IA&AD, ended his title drought by defeating fourth-seeded Ankur Bhattacharjee of Haryana 4-3 (12-10, 6-11, 11-6, 7-11, 11-5, 4-11, 11-8) to clinch the title.

Snehit and Ankur repeatedly traded the initiative through fast-paced, high-quality rallies. After splitting the first four games, Snehit moved ahead by taking the fifth, but Ankur forced a decider with a convincing response in the sixth.

The seventh game seemed to tilt in Ankur’s favour when he opened up a 5-3 lead. However, Snehit found another gear at precisely the right moment, turning the contest around and allowing his opponent just three more points. His 11-8 finish not only secured the title but also marked a long-awaited breakthrough in his national ranking, following several previous appearances in finals.

In the semifinals, Snehit overcame Maharashtra’s Raegan Albuquerque 4-2, while Ankur had to work considerably harder against Assam’s Priyanuj Bhattacharyya, recovering from a two-game deficit to prevail 4-2.

Results:

Men’s Singles: Final: SFR Snehit (IA&AD) bt Ankur Bhattacharjee (Har) 12-10, 6-11, 11-6, 7-11, 11-5, 4-11, 11-8. Semifinals: Ankur bt Priyanuj Bhattacharyya (Asm) 11-6, 11-8, 6-11, 9-11, 11-7, 11-7; Snehit bt Raegan Albuquerque (Mah) 11-9, 11-9, 5-11, 11-9, 6-11, 11-1.

Women’s Singles: Final: Divyanshi Bhowmick (Mah) bt Ananya Muralidharan (TN) 7-11, 11-7, 10-12, 11-7, 12-10, 4-11, 14-12. Semifinals: Ananya bt Ankolika Chakraborty (WB) 11-8, 11-8, 11-4, 11-3; Divyanshi bt Yashaswini Ghorpade (PSPB) 11-8, 11-6, 11-7, 11-7.

item.title: Editorial: Countering China’s dominance
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: India’s participation in the San Francisco Declaration and the US-backed Pax Silica initiative offers an opportunity to strengthen AI capabilities, diversify supply chains, and deepen strategic partnerships
item.content:encoded:
It is an undeniable fact that China continues to wield an outsized influence over the global supply chains for critical minerals and artificial intelligence. Efforts are ongoing to counter this dominance and ensure fair competition in an area that impacts virtually every sphere of human activity. The ‘San Francisco Declaration’ is the latest initiative in this direction. Ten countries — India, the United States, Australia, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE, and the United Kingdom — have signed the multilateral agreement to ensure that no country can secure the AI ecosystem alone and that AI development must span multiple jurisdictions and industries, requiring coordinated action among trusted partners. The San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity is linked to the broader US-sponsored Pax Silica initiative, which seeks to secure the global technology and AI ecosystem. The agreement aims to reduce reliance on concentrated markets, counter economic and supply chain pressure from China, address non-market overcapacity, and prevent hostile actors from acquiring sensitive technologies that could grant military or intelligence advantages. For India, the declaration presents both strategic opportunities and new responsibilities. India’s inclusion signals that it is being viewed as an important participant in the global AI ecosystem rather than merely a technology consumer. This elevates India’s standing among major technology and strategic powers of the Indo-Pacific. China currently dominates global critical mineral supply chains, accounting for around 60 per cent of mining, 90 per cent of processing and separation, and 94 per cent of permanent magnet manufacturing.

China has extended the temporary suspension of export controls on rare earth elements, lithium-ion batteries, and graphite anode materials until January 10, 2027. There is a growing convergence among global economies on the need for joint efforts to “de-risk” critical technologies by linking AI governance with resilient supply chains and long-term economic security partnerships. To achieve this, it is essential to break China’s semiconductor chokehold and build alternatives to strengthen economic security. Becoming a member of Pax Silica will open up avenues for India to significantly accelerate its semiconductor and AI ambitions. The Pax Silica declaration lays out a shared vision of economic and technology cooperation across supply chains — from raw materials to semiconductors and AI infrastructure — and a commitment to mutual prosperity and security. Resilient semiconductor supply chains are critical in a world that has witnessed the weaponisation of supply chains. Of late, China has tightened controls on rare earth exports, requiring government clearance before the minerals can be shipped abroad. Its dominance in production and processing gives Beijing considerable leverage in trade talks. India can benefit from stronger partnerships, diversified supply chains, investment, and access to advanced technologies. Collaboration with trusted partners can also reduce excessive dependence on others and strengthen economic resilience. The signatories to the San Francisco Declaration have agreed to share a list of high-priority technologies and critical infrastructure to guard against theft, illicit transfers, and undue foreign control.

item.title: Opinion: India deserves a seat at the APEC table
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: As Asia-Pacific leaders meet in Shenzhen, India’s evolving trade policy offers an opportunity to revive a conversation that has been on hold since 2010
item.content:encoded:
By Komal Karwa

When leaders of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meet in Shenzhen, China, on November 18 and 19, one of Asia’s largest economies will once again follow the proceedings from outside the room. India, home to more than 1.4 billion people, has never been a member of the 21-economy grouping, despite showing interest for nearly three decades.

The timing of this year’s meeting makes India’s absence worth revisiting. China, the 2026 host, has chosen the theme “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together,” with priorities including supply chain resilience, digital cooperation, and progress towards a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. Each of these goals touches India directly. Moreover, India’s own trade policy has changed considerably since its membership bid was last seriously debated.

Forum Built on Pacific Rim

APEC was founded in 1989 as an informal forum of Pacific Rim economies. Today, its members account for about 62 per cent of world GDP and 48 per cent of global trade, according to the forum’s own figures. APEC currently has 21 member economies. Unlike the World Trade Organization, APEC does not negotiate binding agreements.

India first sought membership in the 1990s. Its hopes stalled in 1997, when APEC imposed a 10-year moratorium on admitting new members. When that freeze approached its end, India was among about a dozen economies with pending membership requests, alongside Mongolia and Colombia. The moratorium expired in 2010, but no new member has been admitted since.

The Door Stays Closed

Geography was never the only obstacle. Members have long debated how far the forum should expand beyond the Pacific Rim, and every new entrant requires consensus.

Trade policy weighed even more heavily. In a 2016 assessment, Amitendu Palit of the Institute of South Asian Studies at the National University of Singapore argued that India’s foreign policy had moved faster than its trade policy, and that the gap made it harder to secure support. Two years earlier, Alyssa Ayres of the Council on Foreign Relations noted that India’s position on the WTO’s Trade Facilitation Agreement had created doubts among some APEC members at a sensitive moment.

China has chosen ‘Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together,’ as the theme for this year’s meeting on Nov 18-19. Its priorities include supply chain resilience, digital cooperation and progress towards a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific—all issues with direct implications for India

Some subsequent decisions reinforced that perception among observers. In November 2019, India chose not to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, citing concerns over market access and its trade deficit with China. In September 2022, it stayed out of the trade pillar of the US-led Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, while joining its other pillars. Each decision had sound domestic reasons. Taken together, however, they led some partners to wonder whether India was ready for open-ended regional trade commitments.

What has Changed Since

The picture in 2026 looks rather different. India has signed or implemented an unusually large number of trade agreements in a relatively short period, several with APEC economies.

The India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement has been in force since December 2022. On October 20, 2026, India’s free trade agreement with New Zealand entered into force, offering duty-free access for all Indian exports to the New Zealand market, according to Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal. India launched negotiations with Canada in March 2026, signed terms of reference for a trade agreement with Mexico on October 28 and is expanding its arrangement with Chile, according to an industry tracker. Talks with the United States on a bilateral trade agreement are also continuing.

Beyond the Pacific, India’s comprehensive agreement with the United Kingdom came into force in July 2026, and negotiations with the European Union were concluded in January. A country that once hesitated over trade pacts is now negotiating with several of APEC’s leading members at the same time.

This does not mean India has embraced every element of the APEC agenda. Agriculture and some manufacturing sectors remain carefully protected, and New Delhi remains cautious about commitments that could limit its policy space. Nevertheless, the claim that India is inherently reluctant to liberalise is harder to sustain today than it was a decade ago.

The Case on Both Sides

Supporters of Indian membership have long argued that APEC would benefit from its inclusion as much as India would. A 2019 report by the Perth USAsia Centre, with contributors from India and six APEC economies, concluded that the region had strategic and economic interests in India’s accession. Former Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd launched an Asia Society Policy Institute initiative on the subject in 2015.

For India, membership would offer a seat at discussions that shape regional standards on digital trade, customs procedures and supply chains, areas in which its exporters already operate. Analysts at the Confederation of Indian Industry have also pointed to APEC’s non-binding, voluntary approach as a better fit for India than rigid trade blocs.

The concerns are real too. A larger membership could make APEC’s consensus-based process slower. Some members may still question whether India would accept the forum’s direction on tariff reduction. Any expansion would raise the question of how to accommodate other applicants waiting in line.

Practical Path Forward

Full membership is unlikely to be decided in Shenzhen, and it need not be. A more modest approach could build trust over time.

India could seek to participate in selected APEC working groups, such as those dealing with small business, digital trade or customs cooperation, where its experience with digital public infrastructure could make a valuable contribution. Its new partners, including Australia and New Zealand, could encourage such participation as a natural follow-up to their bilateral agreements. APEC, for its part, could revisit its long-pending membership review and set out clear criteria for future entrants, so that applicants know what is expected of them.

India’s absence from APEC is less a judgment on its importance than a product of history and timing. Both have shifted. With the Asia-Pacific searching for ways to keep trade open in uncertain times, a conversation that has been on hold since 2010 may finally be ready to resume.

 

(The author is a public policy researcher associated with the Policy, Politics and Governance Foundation and South Asia Monitor. An appointed UGC NEP SAARTHI Ambassador and former Lok Sabha legislative researcher, she is currently a postgraduate scholar in Political Science)

item.title: VIT ranks 293rd globally, fifth in India in QS Sustainability Rankings 2027
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Vellore Institute of Technology has secured the 293rd global position and fifth rank in India in the QS Sustainability Rankings 2027. The university improved 59 places, citing solar power generation, waste recycling, bioenergy initiatives and campus biodiversity efforts
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) secured the 293rd position globally and the 5th rank in India in the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027.

According to a press statement issued by VIT Chancellor Dr. G. Viswanathan, the university scored 81.2 overall, improving by 59 places from its previous global rank of 352nd and entering the global top 300. VIT was ranked 7th in India in the previous edition. The 2027 edition assessed approximately 2,000 universities worldwide.

The QS Sustainability Rankings evaluate universities across three core pillars: Environmental Impact, Social Impact, and Governance.

Chancellor Viswanathan attributed VIT’s improved ranking to several sustainability-focused initiatives implemented across the campus. A 441 kW solar panel installation over vehicle-parking areas generates 650 MWh of electricity annually and helps prevent an estimated 470 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions.

Food waste from student hostels is recycled to generate 200 kW of electricity, while around 15 tonnes of woody waste is converted into bioenergy every year, the university said, adding that it also enforced a strict ban on single-use plastics and maintains a green, tree-filled campus that supports native and seasonal bird species.

item.title: Sreenidi Deccan FC face FC Bengaluru United in crucial IFL clash
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Sreenidi Deccan FC will look to recover from their previous defeat when they face FC Bengaluru United in the Indian Football League. The hosts, unbeaten at home, are targeting another victory to move into the top three
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Sreenidi Deccan FC will look to bounce back from their previous-fixture defeat when they take on a confident FC Bengaluru United, who are unbeaten at home, in Match 16 of the Indian Football League (IFL) 2026-27 at the Bangalore Football Stadium in Bengaluru on Wednesday.

The match will be telecast live on DD Sports and streamed on the Unite8 YouTube channel, Z5 and the WAVES app.

Wednesday’s evening encounter will see promoted side FC Bengaluru United looking to consolidate their home form against a reinforced Sreenidi Deccan FC outfit that has spent the early weeks of the season negotiating a gruelling multi-city road trip.

FC Bengaluru United, coached by Nallappan Mohanraj, will return to the Bangalore Football Stadium aiming to establish their home ground as a fortress in their debut Star Cement IFL campaign.

The Bengaluru outfit has shown an eagerness to play on the front foot in familiar conditions and currently sits fifth in the standings with four points from three matches, following an entertaining 2-2 draw against Real Kashmir FC last Saturday.

In that encounter, FC Bengaluru United fell behind early but responded with a moment of brilliance as Colombian playmaker Maikol Andres Herrera Casseres unleashed a stunning right-footed curling strike from distance to equalise. After falling behind again, the hosts pressed relentlessly until the final whistle and earned a point when Under-22 centre-back Abdul Hannan rose highest to head home a dramatic 90th-minute equaliser.

Currently level on four points with their midweek opponents, a victory on Wednesday would break the deadlock and propel FC Bengaluru United into the top three.

Speaking ahead of the midweek clash, FC Bengaluru United head coach Nallappan Mohanraj emphasised the importance of his side’s resilience and its ongoing adaptation to the top division.

“A win is a win, and we would have been happy if we had got the three points. But the way we came back into the game, being 2-1 down and scoring in the 90th minute to get a point, we have to accept that fact because everyone worked together and fought well,” Mohanraj said.

“As a coach at home, I would have liked to take all three points. But the way we fought for that one point made me very happy, and the boys deserved it.”

Assessing the threat posed by Sreenidi Deccan FC, Mohanraj added: “As a newly promoted side in the Star Cement IFL, it takes time for many of our boys, who are playing at this level for the very first time, to settle into the intensity of the opposition. Sreenidi Deccan is a very good, experienced side and we are prepared to face them.

“We are going to give everything from the first minute to the last. That is what we have prepared for, and that is the attitude and character the team is showing. It is our home game, and we have to push ourselves to the maximum.”

item.title: Amee Kamani begins IBSF World Snooker Championship campaign with twin wins
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Amee Kamani began her IBSF World Snooker Championships campaign with two convincing victories in Group D. She defeated fellow Indian Afeefa Fakhrudeen 2-0 with a break of 54 before overcoming Ireland's Ella O'Connor by an identical margin
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Former champion and favourite Pankaj Advani served a warning to his rivals with two century breaks during a comprehensive win in his opening Group L match against Filipino Michael Mengorio at the IBSF World Snooker Championships in Indore on Tuesday.

The three-time champion rifled in a break of 100 in the opening frame and then fired a break of 109 in the fifth to seal a comfortable 4-1 victory. Barring the fourth frame, when Mengorio came up with a fine clearance, Advani hardly put a foot wrong.

Earlier in the day, India’s S Shrikrishna, a former world champion in the shorter format, was in impressive form as he registered a comprehensive 4-0 win over Abdullah Alyousef of Kuwait in a Group B match.

The 26-year-old from Chennai seemed to be in a hurry as he dominated his rival with some fine breaks. After getting used to the table speed in the opening frame, the Indian cueist came up with breaks of 78, 52 and a fluent 102 in the fourth frame.

Later, India’s Rayaan Razmi, who came through the first-stage qualifiers, edged out France’s Nicolas Mortreux 4-3 in his opening Group C match. The 24-year-old from Mumbai got off to a good start, only to fritter away his advantage with a series of errors that nearly cost him the match.

The French cueist capitalised on his rival’s errors to draw level at 2-2. After the two players split the next two frames, Razmi made an early break of 38 in the decider but let Mortreux back into the match when he missed a red while attempting to pot it into the top-left pocket.

However, the Frenchman came up with a poor safety shot after losing position while on a break of 31. Razmi seized the opportunity and compiled a break of 27 to close out the match.

There were also wins for Kamal Chawla, Aditya Mehta, Manan Chandra and Sourav Kothari. Shoaib Khan rallied from 0-3 down to edge out Mohamed Shehab of the UAE 4-3.

AMEE BEGINS WELL

In the women’s section, title contender Amee Kamani kick-started her campaign with two wins in Group D. After outclassing fellow Indian Afeefa Fakhrudeen 2-0 with a break of 54 in the first frame, Amee returned later in the evening to register a commanding 2-0 win over Ireland’s Ella O’Connor.

Defending champion Anupama Ramachandran also began her campaign with a 2-0 win over France’s Ophelie Laval in Group A, although she was not quite at her fluent best.

Results (Indians unless mentioned):

Men:

Group A: Ali Alobaidli (Qat) bt Michal Kotiuk (Pol) 4-1; Paras Gupta bt Uzair Khan 4-3.

Group B: S Shrikrishna bt Abdullah Alyousef (Kuw) 4-0; Tam Yun Fung (HKC) bt Dhruv Patel 4-3.

Group C: Rayaan Razmi bt Nicolas Mortreux (Fra) 4-3; Wang Yuchen (HKC) bt Ketan Chawla 4-1.

Group D: Aditya Mehta bt Ali Hussein (Irq) 4-2; Nansen Wan (HKC) bt Oliwier Nizialek (Pol) 4-3.

Group E: Shoaib Khan bt Mohamed Shehab (UAE) 4-3; Manan Chandra bt Langyi Ryan Li (HKC) 4-2.

Group F: Kamal Chawla bt Christian Richter (Ger) 4-1; Hussain Khan bt Sunny Wang (Sin) 4-1.

Group G: Kreishh Gurbaxani bt Laxman Rawat 4-1; Amir Sarkhosh (Irn) bt Hesham Shawky (Egy) 4-3.

Group H: Ali Gharahgozlou (Irn) bt Thaha Irshath (SL) 4-0.

Group J: Sourav Kothari bt Dhvajj Haria 4-1.

Group K: Alikalil Ali (Irq) bt Sabin Tamang (Nep) 4-1.

Group L: Pankaj Advani bt Michael Mengorio (Phi) 4-1.

Women:

Group A: Anupama Ramachandran bt Ophelie Laval (Fra) 2-0; Reyna Maria Legaspi (Phi) 2-1 (opponent’s name to be confirmed).

Group B: Keerthana Pandian bt Pooja Galundia 2-0; Megan Randle (Ire) bt Setayesh Amirazimi (Irn) 2-1.

Group C: So Man Yan (HKC) bt Margaret O’Driscoll (Ire) 2-0; R Umadevi bt Sanvi Shah 2-1.

Group D: Amee Kamani bt Afeefa Fakhrudeen 2-0; Amee Kamani bt Ella O’Connor (Ire) 2-0; Carmille Buhat (Phi) bt Ella O’Connor (Ire) 2-0.

The results will be available on the website www.telanganaopenschool.org at 11 am. Both SSC and Intermediate examinations were conducted in October 2026.

item.title: Gnana Sree stars as Sangareddy beat Khammam in Telangana U-16 league
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Gnana Sree's 69 helped Sangareddy defeat Khammam by 31 runs in the Telangana Cricket Association State League Under-16 Championship Phase One. Vikarabad and Ranga Reddy also registered victories, while Nagarkurnool defeated Mahabubnagar in another match
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Gnana Sree (69) top-scored as Sangareddy registered an impressive 31-run win over Khammam in the Telangana Cricket Association State League (Under-16) Championship Phase One at One Champion Ground in Moinabad here on Tuesday.

Results:

Sangareddy 166/1 in 20 overs (Gnana Sree 69, Syed Ziyan 35, Sai Pradyumna 37) bt Khammam 135/7 in 20 overs (KrantiShiva Sai Reddy 57, Sai Pradyumna 3/11). Man of the match: Sai Pradyumna.

Nagarkurnool 136/9 in 20 overs (Mohammed Mudassir 3/15) lost to Vikarabad 137/4 in 18.3 overs (Yuvaraj Pawar 43, R. Dinesh Bantu 32). Man of the match: R. Dinesh Bantu.

Gajwel 91 in 18.3 overs (Rishwath 23, N. Ranajai 3/9, Varshit Reddy 3/15) lost to Ranga Reddy 92/5 in 11.4 overs. Man of the match: N. Ranajai.

Nagarkurnool 149 in 19.5 overs (David Benjamin 50, Balu 3/27) bt Mahabubnagar 142/8 in 20 overs (Sai Advit 38, Sai Teja 4/22). Man of the match: David Benjamin.

item.title: ECI extends Telangana SIR deadline to December 15, final voter list on December 22
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Election Commission of India has extended Telangana's Special Intensive Revision schedule, setting December 15 as the deadline for claims and objections. The final electoral rolls will now be published on December 22, while ASDD enumeration forms must be processed by December 10
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Tuesday extended the schedule of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Seven States, including Telangana.

ECI Under Secretary Sandeep Kumar has fixed December 15 as the deadline for disposal of claims and objections, and notice phase in the State. Earlier, it was November 26. Final electoral rolls, initially scheduled for November 30, would now be published on December 22.

The ECI has sent a letter to Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharsan Reddy, informing the State about the revised schedule.

Meanwhile, the ECI also revised the schedule for Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate (ASDD) electors who had earlier been removed from draft electoral rolls as they failed to submit enumeration forms.

The Telangana CEO has been asked to generate enumeration forms of ASDD voters by November 18. Distribution and collection of enumeration forms is scheduled from November 18 to 30. The collected forms have to be disposed by December 10.

SIR schedules in Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Nagaland, Maharashtra, Haryana and Jharkhand have also been revised. Although the starting dates for the notice phase and the disposal of claims and objections vary across these States and Union Territories, the ECI fixed December 15 and 22, as the common date for disposing claims and objections, and publishing the final electoral rolls respectively.

Prior to commencement of SIR exercise, Telangana had a total of 3,38,26,448 voters. During the enumeration phase, 2,64,87,213 voters submitted forms and remaining 73,39,235 were categorised under the ASDD category.

Among those who submitted forms, the ECI flagged logical discrepancies and the absence of mapping with the SIR 2002 list for 92,88,188 voters. As many as 92,88,045 electors were served notices and hearings of 92,82,119 voters were completed as of Tuesday.

So far, 2,63,53,511 electors, including 91,77,438 voters who were served SIR notices, have been marked for inclusion in the final electoral list. A total of 57,644 electors were found ineligible, while 76,058 voter names were pending for a decision.

item.title: Cong delaying paddy procurement to deny bonus to farmers: Harish
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Former Minister T Harish Rao accused the Congress government of delaying paddy procurement and denying farmers the fine rice bonus. He demanded a government order on bonus payments and criticised the government for allegedly failing to provide drought relief
item.content:encoded:
Sangareddy: Former Minister T Harish Rao accused the Congress government of delaying the paddy procurement to deny bonus to fine rice. Speaking after inspecting the paddy procurement progress at Nizampet procurement centre on Tuesday, Harish Rao said that the government failed to start the process of procurement even though the farmers have brought heaps of paddy a long ago.

While the middlemen were purchasing the fine rice at Rs 2,600 per quintal, Rao said that the traders were not coming forward to buy the coarse paddy, leaving the farmers to wait at the procurement centres for days. Demanding the government to issue a GO regarding the bonus payment of fine rice, the former minister said the farmers had got poor harvest this year due to El Nino induced drought.

Even though the neighbouring Karnataka and Maharastra states had released Rs 5,000 per acre for farmers as an immediate relief, he said that the Congress government failed to make any step towards to support the farmers who were hit the by the drought. Rao recalled that how the BRS government extended Rs 10,000 per acre support to farmers when they suffered losses due to untimely rains.

He interacted with the farmers to know their struggles. Former Narayankhed MLA Mahareddy Bhupal Reddy and others were present. Later, Harish Rao participated in a spirtual programme at Sanjeevraopet.

item.title: YMCA Secunderabad defeat Alpha Basketball Academy in league championship

item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: YMCA Secunderabad breezed past Alpha Basketball Academy 54-17, registering double-digit scores in all four quarters, in the GM Sampath Kumar Annual League Basketball Championship here on Tuesday.

Men: YMCA Secunderabad 74 (Rakesh 21, Vivek 16, Rusuf 15) bt Nizam Basketball Academy 55 (Samaran 16, Aravind 14).

Women: YMCA Secunderabad 54 (Krishna 12) bt Alpha Basketball Academy 17 (Apeksha 7, Parishi 7).

Nizam Basketball Academy 61 (Jahnavi 14, Vennela 12, Tanmay 11) bt Loyola Academy 19 (Deepthi 7, Litisha 6).

item.title: Telangana allocates Rs 203.36 crore for Khelo India Youth Games-2026
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana aims to become India's leading sports hub as it prepares to host Khelo India Youth Games-2026, with Rs 203.36 crore allocated. Sports Minister V. Srihari outlined plans for infrastructure, grassroots talent identification, athlete mentorship and long-term sporting excellence
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Telangana Sports Minister V. Srihari said the State aimed to emerge as India’s leading sports hub. As part of this effort, the Khelo India Youth Games-2026 would be hosted on a large scale, with Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy allocating Rs 203.36 crore for the event.

Addressing an interaction with eminent sportspersons at the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat on Tuesday, the Minister said hosting the Khelo India Youth Games-2026 presented a significant opportunity for Telangana to showcase its organisational capabilities and set new benchmarks in sporting excellence.

The meeting was attended by SATG Chairman K. Shiva Sena Reddy, Special Chief Secretary (Sports) Vani Prasad, SATG Vice-Chairperson and Managing Director A. Sonibala Devi, senior officials and prominent sportspersons, including J.J. Shobha, Neeta L. Dadwe, Ismail Baig, Esha Singh, Ambati Tirupati Rayudu, Agasara Nandini, Gagan Narang, Jwala Gutta, Col. Nachhatar Singh Johal, Boria Majumdar and Nikhat Zareen.

The Minister emphasised that developing international-standard stadiums, grounds, tracks, training facilities and other sports infrastructure would be a priority, with a strong focus on long-term quality and accountability.

He said the State was committed to identifying grassroots talent and creating opportunities for athletes to excel at the national and international levels, with the ultimate objective of producing Olympic champions.

Highlighting the importance of athletes’ participation, the Minister proposed assigning eminent sportspersons responsibilities for overseeing individual sporting venues and mentoring young athletes.

item.title: PD Joshua to lead Hyderabad team in All India Civil Services Football Tournament
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: All India Civil Services football tournament.
item.description: Former national-level footballer P.D. Joshua will lead the Regional Sports Board Hyderabad team at the All India Civil Services Football Tournament in Goa. The squad comprises 22 players, with T.M. Prabhu as coach and N. Anbu Alagan as manager
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: P.D. Joshua, a former national-level footballer who represented Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, will lead the Regional Sports Board (RSB), Hyderabad, team in the All India Civil Services Football Tournament, which begins in Goa on Wednesday.

The team: Reddi Rai Naidu, P.D. Joshua, P. Tatam Naidu, Raja Deb Nath, Shaik Umar, Syed Abbad Anas, Y. Krishna Reddy, Md Nizamuddin, P.D. Emanuel, R.R. Sai Rakesh, Vikas Yadav, Lucky Imran, Annamreddy Naidu, Jabro Faisal Bin Osman, Kumari Hari Babu, Md Moazzam, Mohd Murtuza Hussain, Syed Abid Hussain Razvi, K. Madan, G. Mani Bhushan, T. David Prasanna Kumar and Vivek Adhikari.

Coach: T.M. Prabhu.

Manager: N. Anbu Alagan.

item.title: Sneha Lamba, Tanay Mehendale cause upsets at National Junior Badminton Championships
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Rajasthan's Sneha Lamba and Maharashtra's Tanay Mehendale scored upsets at the 49th Yonex-Sunrise National Junior Badminton Championships in Gangtok, defeating fourth and sixth seeds in their singles events. Top seeds Shaina Manimuthu and Nishchal Anand also advanced after tough matches
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Rajasthan’s Sneha Lamba and Maharashtra’s Tanay Mehendale caused early upsets at the 49th Yonex-Sunrise National Junior (U-19) Badminton Championships in Gangtok on Tuesday, defeating higher-ranked opponents in straight games.

Sneha packed off fourth seed Tanvi Reddy Andluri, who recently represented India at the World Junior Championships in Cairo, Egypt, 15-12, 15-6 in the girls’ singles second round. Mehendale got the better of sixth seed Shaurya Mishra 15-13, 16-14 in the boys’ singles to advance to the third round.

The seeded players had received byes in the opening round, and all eyes were on the top contenders to deliver on the second day of the individual competitions in Sikkim’s capital.

While girls’ singles top seed Shaina Manimuthu was pushed to three games by Maharashtra’s Naishaa Kaur Bhayoye, the Karnataka shuttler held her nerve to win 15-9, 11-15, 15-5. Boys’ singles top seed Nishchal Anand was also made to work hard before defeating Prangan Choudhary 15-11, 14-16, 15-10 in the second round.

However, the 11th and 13th seeds in the boys’ singles event were shown the door. Eleventh seed Sai Nachiketh Bhatraju lost 10-15, 15-9, 12-15, while 13th seed Harshad Shadish bowed out after a 15-12, 13-15, 15-9 defeat against Sparsha Sood.

Important results

Boys’ singles: Tanay Mehendale bt 6-Shaurya Mishra 15-13, 16-14; Sparsha Sood bt 13-Harshad Shadish 15-12, 13-15, 15-9; 1-Nishchal Anand bt Prangan Choudhary 15-11, 14-16, 15-10; Prince bt 11-Sai Nachiketh Bhatraju 15-10, 9-15, 15-12; 7-Gnana Dattu TT bt Shreeram Ratan 15-6, 15-9; 3-Abhinav Garg bt Malsawmhlua 15-12, 15-9.

Girls’ singles: Sneha Lamba bt 4-Tanvi Reddy Andluri 15-12, 15-6; 1-Shaina Manimuthu bt Naishaa Kaur Bhayoye 15-9, 11-15, 15-5; 11-Durga Esha Kandrapur bt Konyak A Ponlih 15-3, 15-6.

item.title: Kothagudem police seize 280 BGL shells in forest dumps
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Kothagudem police seized 280 Barrel Grenade Launcher shells from three Maoist dumps in the Dandakaranya forest near the Telangana-Chhattisgarh border. Superintendent of Police B Rohith Raju said the recovery followed information provided by surrendered Maoists.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: The district police have seized 280 Barrel Grenade Launcher (BGL) shells from the Dandakaranya forest along the Telangana-Chhattisgarh border.

According to Superintendent of Police B Rohith Raju, the explosive projectiles were seized based on reliable information provided by surrendered Maoists. Cherla police, with the help of Special Party personnel and a bomb disposal (BD) team, conducted search operations in the forest area near Pujari Kanker village along the Telangana-Chhattisgarh border on November 16.

During the search operations, three dumps belonging to the PLGA battalion of the CPI (Maoist) party were identified. The shells were stored in a synthetic water drum at each dump and were recovered.

The police found that the BGL shells had been hidden in the dumps during the decentralisation of the CPI (Maoist) PLGA battalion in early 2025. The Maoists, considering the dense forest area safe, had hidden the dumps for future use, intending to use the shells if the Maoist movement revived, Rohith Raju told the media at Cherla on Tuesday.

In the latter part of 2025 and early 2026, several Maoists surrendered before the Telangana police. Along with Muppala Lakshmana Rao alias Ganapathi, two other Maoists were still in hiding and should join the mainstream of public life, he said.

As per the Telangana government’s surrender and rehabilitation policy, the State police have been providing necessary facilities to surrendered Maoists and looking after their welfare with a humanitarian approach.

The government paid cash rewards to the surrendered Maoists. Facilities such as agricultural land, house plots, bank loans for self-employment and health cards were being provided, along with skill training. In return, Maoists were informing the police about the dumps hidden by the Maoist party, the SP added.

item.title: BRS strengthens in Mudhole as 11 sarpanches, four deputy sarpanches join party
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The BRS inducted 11 sarpanches, four deputy sarpanches and several local leaders from Mudhole constituency at Telangana Bhavan. Led by senior leader Ramadevi, the group included elected representatives from the BJP, Congress and Independent candidates.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The BRS received a boost in Mudhole constituency, with 11 sarpanches, four deputy sarpanches and several leaders from different political parties joining it in the presence of party working president KT Rama Rao at Telangana Bhavan on Tuesday. Rama Rao welcomed them by presenting party scarves and assured them of a political future in the BRS.

Congress and BJP leaders from Tandur and Kubheer mandals joined the BRS under the leadership of senior leader Ramadevi. They included eight sarpanches elected on BJP tickets, one from the Congress and two Independents. All four deputy sarpanches belonged to the BJP. Two former MPTCs, former sarpanches and other local leaders also joined the party.

Speaking on the occasion, Ramadevi said that despite having a Congress MLA and MP, Mudhole had seen little development, with public representatives limiting themselves to inaugurations rather than taking up new works. She said the failure to declare Lokeswaram and Tandur mandals drought-affected had caused widespread discontent. She accused leaders of both the Congress and BJP of neglecting public issues.

item.title: Farmers in Karnataka protest, seek water for chilli crops
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Chilli farmers in Karnataka's Yadgir district staged a protest in Shahapur, demanding the release of water from the Basavasagar reservoir until December. The agitation comes amid similar protests by farmers in Telangana seeking water for standing crops.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Farmers in neighbouring Karnataka, like their counterparts in Telangana, are taking to the streets demanding water to save their standing crops. The farming community is facing distress, which farmers have attributed to the alleged negligence of the Congress governments in both States.

After farmers, particularly those from the erstwhile Nalgonda and Mahabubnagar districts, staged protests demanding the release of water from the Nagarjuna Sagar and Jurala projects, respectively, chilli farmers in Karnataka have now taken to the streets with a similar demand.

On Monday, farmers staged a protest in Shahapur town of Yadgir district, demanding that the Congress government release water from the Basavasagar reservoir.

The farmers took out a rally using tractors and two-wheelers from the APMC in the town to the KBJNL office near Bhimarayanagudi. Citing the hardships they were facing, they demanded that water be released from the Basavasagar reservoir until December.

Vyas Laxminarayana, a BJP District Council member, commented on the situation in a post on X. “Water scarcity increased in Karnataka. Farmers are coming out for protests demanding water for chilli crops. Another Congress ruling State is ruined. Except something similar in Telangana in coming days. States under Congress rule are doomed,” he said.

item.title: Even top former police officer not spared by land grabbers in Telangana!
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Authorities suspect that 4.5 acres of land worth over Rs 20 crore belonging to a retired IPS officer was illegally mutated in Sangareddy district. The incident has raised concerns over suspected hacking of Telangana's Bhu Bharati land records portal
item.content:encoded:
Sangareddy: In a development that is bound to shake the administration, authorities have found that unscrupulous land grabbers managed to transfer four and half acres of land owned by a retired IPS officer to the name of another person in Sangupet village of Andole mandal.

A very interesting and disturbing angle to the illegal mutation of land worth over Rs 20 crore was that the retired officer of the rank of Director General of Police (DGP) had noticed that land in his name was transferred to one Mir Murad Ali, when he checked the land records after obtaining an encumbrance certificate. It is also suspected that the land grabbers managed to hack the Bhu Bharati website to transfer the ownership of the land. However, there is no official confirmation about the hacking of the website so far.

Incidentally, the wife of the retired officer is also a retired IAS officer, who served at Special Chief Secretary level.

According to sources, the officer couple bought 4 acres and 27 guntas of land at Sangupet village of Andole mandal in 2007. Subsequently, some unidentified persons had transferred the land on to the name of Mir Murad Ali, a native of Jogipet, but settled down in Hyderabad.

As the land on his name was transferred to another person’s name without his knowledge without any clearance from the local Tahsildar or registration office, the retired police officer reportedly used his good offices at highest level in the administration and get the land restored to his name again.

Even though the officer did not file any complaint officially, the officials were suspecting the role of a team that carried out the illegal mutation of three acres of land, worth Rs 100 crore, in Kollur area earlier this year. While investigating into the illegal mutation following a complaint filed by RC Puram Tahsildar on Kollur illegal mutation, the State government handed over the case to Crime Investigation Department (CID).

The officials have arrested four persons in Kollur case for carrying out the mutation in violation of Bhu Bharathi Act-2025. The illegal mutation carried by the conmen without the involvement local revenue and sub registration officials in both the cases left both the revenue and police department officials in a shock.

The officials suspected the the mutations were done by hacking the Bhu Bharathi website. The officials were inquiring to trace out the gang that was carrying the illegal mutations. The gang reportedly carried such mutations at several places across Telangana which is being investigated.

item.title: Bilkis Bano shocked by SC order granting bail to two convicts
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Bilkis Bano has expressed shock over the Supreme Court's decision to suspend the life sentences of two convicts and grant them bail. She said the order was passed without hearing her and vowed to fight it for justice.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Bilkis Bano has expressed shock and disbelief at the Supreme Court order suspending the life sentences of two men convicted of gangraping her and murdering seven of her family members during the 2002 Gujarat riots, and granting them bail.

In a statement issued to the media, Bano said the top court order was passed without hearing her. She said she learnt through press reports that the court had suspended the two convicts’ life sentences and granted them bail.

“I make this statement even when words come slowly through fresh tears of pain, shock and disbelief. I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me. I learnt of this through press reports…”

“I was a young girl, just 19 years old, when my world, my baby daughter, my family, my home, my trust in humanity was brutally wrenched from me. For 24 long years since that day, I have stood up to fight for justice, for myself and for women everywhere, again and again and again. For 24 years I have searched for and found reservoirs of courage I did not know I had, only because a million voices of support and solidarity came my way,” Bano said.

A Supreme Court bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale granted bail to Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya, noting that they had been incarcerated for more than 17 years.

“Having heard the parties, suffice it to state that the appellants have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years, and also the fact remains that one of the appellants has a severe handicap. Certainly, there are issues to be decided in the appeal, both on fact and law,” the apex court said in its October 28 order, which has now been uploaded.

“In view of the above and considering the issues involved in this appeal, we suspend the sentence and grant bail to the appellants on such terms and conditions as may be imposed by the concerned trial court,” the bench had said.

Bano questioned how the top court could suspend the sentences of the two men without hearing her.

“I have walked to courtroom after courtroom, and been grateful each time I was vindicated; each time my faith in the idea of justice was restored. I have rebuilt from the rubble of my life, with the love of family and friends. I have yearned for peace. I have learned to smile.

“Yet today I find myself losing the very justice I had fought so hard to win. Familiar fears are resurfacing. I am scared once again. For myself, my family, and my children. And I am scared of losing faith in justice, yet again. How could the honourable Supreme Court simply suspend the sentence of the men who did this to me? How could they not even inform me? How could they not even make sure my voice was heard in their courtroom?” she said.

Bano said she would challenge the order as her children did not deserve to live haunted by these fears and scars for the rest of their lives.

“I do this for my three-year-old Saleha who deserved to live, and whose memory demands justice. I do this for women everywhere. Because no woman, no survivor, no citizen should have to endure this eternal test of belonging and equality, and fight for justice for the rest of her life,” she said.

item.title: Tejaswin Shankar dedicates 2025 Arjuna Award to family and athletics fraternity
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Indian decathlete Tejaswin Shankar dedicated his 2025 Arjuna Award to his family and the athletics fraternity. He also outlined his preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and said India's potential 2036 Olympic hosting bid could inspire young athletes
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Indian decathlete Tejaswin Shankar described receiving the 2025 Arjuna Award from President Droupadi Murmu as a dream come true, dedicating the honour to his family and the entire athletics fraternity.

Speaking to the Sports Authority of India (SAI) after receiving the prestigious award, Tejaswin said such opportunities arise only once or twice in a lifetime and that he felt honoured to be among the few to receive the recognition.

“I feel honoured and privileged to receive the Arjuna Award from the Honourable President of India. It is a dream come true for me, as such opportunities arise only once or twice in a lifetime,” he said.

Shankar, who is also a TOPS athlete and receives regular funding for his training and support staff, acknowledged the hard work that had gone into earning the honour before dedicating it to his family and recognising their sacrifices.

“I think I would like to dedicate this award to myself first because, obviously, I have put in the hard work, dedication and all of the above (to be here). But I think the biggest sacrifice was made by my family in terms of time. They spent very little time with me because I am mostly on the road, travelling and competing. So, I would definitely like to dedicate this to my mom and the rest of my family,” he said.

He added that success in athletics was never a one-man show, saying: “I would like to dedicate this award to the athletics fraternity, as it is never a one-man show. There are always a lot of people behind every individual who achieves something significant. I am grateful to every single one of them and would like to dedicate this award to all of them.”

Tejaswin then spoke about the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and his preparations to qualify for the global event.

“My whole objective in staying in the US for long periods, pursuing a master’s degree and higher education, and competing in high-intensity sports is to focus on LA 2028. My goal is to stay there for extended periods so that I can prepare in that environment, alongside the best athletes and amid cut-throat competition. That way, when 2028 comes, I will have no excuses,” he said.

Talking about the upcoming season, he added: “I want to put myself in that position early on, and that is what I have been trying to do for the last few years. We still have a year before LA 2028, and for my event, the qualification window opens in the next few months. So, my window of opportunity begins in just two months, and I am pretty excited about that.”

When asked about India being in the running to host the 2036 Olympics, Tejaswin recalled how he took up athletics and said hosting the Games could inspire a whole new generation of athletes, just as the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi had inspired him.

“It would be a huge moment if India were to secure the bid to host the 2036 Olympics. I feel it would be a dream come true for many. My first inspiration to take up sports came from watching the 2010 Commonwealth Games in Delhi. That was why I actually started playing sports. I had seen some athletes on television and then watched athletes compete live. I saw weightlifting and badminton. Those were some of my heroes back in 2010, when I knew nothing about the Commonwealth Games or the Olympic Games. Then, in 2012, I watched the London Olympics for the first time,” he said.

“For India to host the 2036 Olympic Games, if that happens, would be a phenomenal opportunity for many young Tejaswins who would be 10, 12 or 13 years old. I feel that if such an opportunity arises, it would be phenomenal,” Tejaswin concluded.

item.title: BRS MLC Dasoju Sravan seeks ACB probe into alleged commission culture
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS MLC Dasoju Sravan has sought an ACB probe into alleged commissions in public works, citing claims by Congress MLA J Anirudh Reddy. He questioned Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy over the allegations and demanded action against corruption.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS MLC Dasoju Sravan has demanded an immediate ACB probe into allegations of commissions in contract works, citing remarks made by Jadcherla Congress MLA J Anirudh Reddy about corruption in the State government. Calling the ruling party MLA’s comments a “charge-sheet” against the government, he asked Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to respond to the allegations and take steps to end the alleged commission culture.

In a statement, the BRS MLC referred to Anirudh Reddy’s claim that officials were demanding 10 to 20 per cent commissions at the measurement book (M-Book) recording stage to clear bills for public works. He said that, in the case of a Rs 5 lakh cement road, 20 per cent allegedly went to officials and intermediaries, while contractors retained another 30 per cent as margin. Consequently, only Rs 2.5 lakh would be spent on the actual work, he alleged.

Sravan questioned whether this amounted to the good governance promised in the Congress manifesto and accused the government of replacing public administration with a percentage-based regime. He also asked the Chief Minister to disclose who was receiving the alleged commissions and whether the money was being diverted to fund elections in other States.

He warned that alleged extortion from contractors, real estate developers and industrialists was discouraging fresh investments and affecting employment prospects for Telangana’s youth. Pointing out that the Home portfolio and the Anti-Corruption Bureau were under the Chief Minister’s control, he questioned why no action was being initiated.

item.title: BSFI releases centenary book celebrating 100 years of Indian cue sports
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Billiards and Snooker Federation of India
item.description: The Billiards and Snooker Federation of India has released ‘A Century to Savour’ to mark its centenary, chronicling 100 years of Indian cue sports. Pankaj Advani and Geet Sethi unveiled the commemorative book alongside Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Billiards and Snooker Federation of India (BSFI) marked a historic milestone in its centenary year with the release of A Century to Savour, a commemorative book chronicling a century of Indian cue sports.

The book traces the federation’s remarkable journey from its founding in 1926 in Calcutta (now Kolkata) to India’s rise as a global powerhouse in cue sports, particularly billiards. It also captures the personal stories of the legends of the sport who brought glory to the nation.

At a special ceremony held at the Yeshwant Club in Indore, coinciding with the inauguration of the IBSF World Snooker Championships on the eve of the second stage, the sport’s greatest icons, Geet Sethi and Pankaj Advani, came together to unveil the book along with Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav.

“It’s a proud moment for us to be hosting the IBSF World Snooker Championship in our centenary year, and more so as we had hosted the first-ever World Amateur Snooker Championship in 1963,” said BSFI president S Balasubramaniam.

From Wilson Jones’ epochal 1958 World Billiards title to the modern triumphs of today’s champions, the book traces every major chapter of the sport. Jones’ historic victory put India firmly on the world sporting map, making him the first Indian athlete to win a world title in any sport.

Reflecting on the milestone, Pankaj Advani, who has won an astounding 29 world titles, said: “We have a rich legacy. Right from the time we started producing world champions, from Wilson Jones to Michael Ferreira to Geet Sethi and so many others, it has been a wonderful 100-year journey for cue sports.”

“We have had some great administrators in the past and people who have been involved in the game for so long because of their passion. I would like to thank each and every person, right from its inception until now. We wish them all the best and look forward to playing our little part,” added Advani.

The book, curated by R Satya and R Kaushik, also reflects on India’s legacy as a preferred destination for global cue sports events. From hosting its first World Amateur Billiards Championship in Kolkata in 1958 to the current IBSF World Snooker Championships, India has remained a regular and gracious host of major world and Asian events.

item.title: Rajgopal Reddy reminds Congress government of Rs 4,000 Cheyutha pension promise
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy has urged the Congress government to increase the monthly Cheyutha pension from Rs 2,000 to Rs 4,000, as promised in its 2023 Assembly election manifesto, citing rising prices and beneficiaries' hardships.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: The Congress government is yet to fulfill several promises made in its ‘Abhaya Hastham’ manifesto, released on November 17 ahead of the 2023 Assembly elections. Reminding the government of its commitment, Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy has demanded that the monthly Cheyutha pension be increased from Rs.2,000 to Rs.4,000, as promised in the party manifesto.

The Congress had promised a monthly Cheyutha pension of Rs.4,000 to senior citizens, widows, persons with disabilities, beedi workers, single women, toddy tappers, weavers, AIDS and filaria patients, and kidney patients undergoing dialysis. However, even after three years, the promise remains unfulfilled. The Congress government continues to provide a monthly pension of Rs.2,000. The amount had been increased from Rs.200 by the previous BRS government during its tenure.

“The Congress party had promised this in its manifesto, and I want the government to fulfil that commitment. I will fight on your behalf,” Rajgopal Reddy assured people at a Cheyutha pension distribution programme in Choutuppal on Tuesday.

The Congress MLA said rising prices of essential commodities had added to the hardships of beneficiaries. He said the existing monthly pension of Rs.2,000 was inadequate. “This government is meant for the welfare of poor people. Not Rs.4,000, even Rs.5,000 would be insufficient,” Rajgopal Reddy said. He added that the government should work for the welfare of the poor rather than contractors and businessmen.

He also said beneficiaries, particularly senior citizens in villages, were questioning the delay in increasing their pensions. Rajgopal Reddy urged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to consider their hardships and raise the monthly pension to Rs.4,000. The MLA also criticised rampant corruption. He said there should be no scope for corruption in the name of development.

item.title: Telangana to witness widespread rainfall from November 19 to 22
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana is likely to witness widespread rainfall between November 19 and 22 under the influence of Cyclone Akvan. The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in several districts, while Hyderabad may receive isolated light showers during this period
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The ongoing dry and chilly weather conditions in Telangana are expected to continue for a day or two before rain bearing clouds, under the influence of cyclone Akvan, trigger widespread downpour between November 19 and 22.

While Hyderabad and its surrounding districts including Medchal-Malkajgiri, Rangareddy and Yadadri Bhongir district could witness isolated light showers, the eastern and south-eastern districts will witness much of the action.

The IMD, Hyderabad in its weather forecast on Tuesday said that from November 19 to 20, districts, including Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Warangal, and Hanumakonda, Nalgonda and Suryapet will witness light to moderate rain or thundershowers accompanied by lightning and gusty winds.

The forecast indicated heavy to very heavy rainfall warning in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet, and Mahabubabad between November 20 and 21. In the same time frame, heavy rainfall and squally winds are likely at Mulugu, Nalgonda, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon, and Yadadri Bhuvanagiri districts.

Between November 21 and 22, heavy to very heavy downpours are expected in Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, and Khammam districts while heavy rainfall is expected in Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahabubabad, Warangal, and Hanumakonda districts.

The cyclonic system is expected to weaken gradually by November 22 and 23.

item.title: Gas leak from ONGC well in Andhra’s Konaseema district triggers panic
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: A massive gas leak at an ONGC well near Geddada village in Andhra Pradesh's Konaseema district triggered panic on Tuesday. Authorities evacuated residents within a one-kilometre radius, halted traffic and mobilised specialised teams to contain the leak.
item.content:encoded:
Kakinada: A massive gas leak occurred at an ONGC gas drilling well in Andhra Pradesh’s Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema district on Tuesday, triggering panic among people in surrounding villages.

The gas leak from the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) well occurred near Geddada village in Mamidikuduru mandal.

According to officials, the gas began leaking around 4.30 am on Tuesday, accompanied by a loud noise, and was spewing out in large volumes.

The incident triggered panic among residents and commuters on National Highway 216.

Gas was reportedly spreading to nearby villages, with residents complaining of a strong gas smell. People living in the vicinity and motorists passing through the highway ran to safety after noticing the leak.

Police halted vehicular movement on the Geddada-Mamidikuduru highway as a precautionary measure.

ONGC officials and police were alerted, while specialised teams were being mobilised to contain the leak. A control team from Narsapur left for the spot to contain the blowout.

Officials stated that there had been no fire so far and that the wellhead remained secure. ONGC personnel were taking measures to prevent the gas from spreading near ground level.

Firefighters arranged a water curtain around the rig to prevent a fire.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu spoke with officials regarding the gas leak.

He directed that residents in the affected areas be evacuated to safer locations.

The Chief Minister said public safety must be given the highest priority. He said ONGC must take immediate action by deploying specialised technical teams to bring the gas leak under control.

Noting that such incidents had occurred frequently of late, the Chief Minister instructed officials to immediately engage with ONGC management.

He ordered a review of safety protocols in consultation with the ONGC Chairman and other senior officials of the organisation.

Authorities had already evacuated residents living within a one-kilometre radius of the gas well.

As a precautionary measure, diesel generators and other equipment were shut down and removed from the vicinity. A cementing team was arriving at the site to completely plug the leaking gas well.

ONGC officials stated that the gas leak would be brought fully under control within the next four to five hours.

item.title: Six arrested for illegal LPG cylinder refilling in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Six persons were arrested for allegedly refilling small LPG cylinders illegally at a scrap shop near Bapughat in Hyderabad's Langer Houz. Police seized 46 domestic cylinders, 36 smaller cylinders, refilling equipment and two trolley autos worth Rs. 4 lakh
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Golconda Task Force, along with Langer Houz police on Tuesday arrested six persons for allegedly illegally refilling small LPG cylinders from domestic gas cylinders at a scrap shop near Bapughat in Langer Houz.

The police seized 46 domestic LPG cylinders, 35 empty 3-kg cylinders, one 5-kg cylinder, seven refilling kits, a weighing machine and two trolley autos, all worth Rs.4 lakh from them.

According to the police,the suspects were allegedly refilling cylinders without safety precautions and selling them in the black market. One of the arrested persons, Ravi, was previously involved in a similar case. A case was registered at Langer Houz police station.

item.title: Motorists object to FASTag charges at Telangana forest checkposts
item.dc:creator: Padala Santosh
item.description: Motorists have objected to increased Ecosystem Management Coordination charges collected through FASTags at forest checkposts in Telangana. While officials say local residents are exempt, vehicle owners from outside designated forest-fringe areas must pay Rs 600 to cross protected areas.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: Motorists have expressed displeasure over the Ecosystem Management Coordination (EMC) charges collected through FASTags at certain checkposts of the Forest Department in tiger reserves and protected areas in Telangana.

The Forest Department integrated FASTag systems at entry points to select forest and tiger reserves to collect the EMC fee automatically through its digital applications. The system was introduced at checkposts in Amrabad Tiger Reserve, Eturunagaram in Mulugu district, and the Kawal Tiger Reserve in Mancherial, Nirmal and Adilabad districts in a phased manner.

The FASTag system was first implemented in Eturunagaram in 2025 but was later extended to the Amrabad and Kawal reserves despite protests from locals. While the charge is Rs 300 for local motorists, those from outside Telangana have to pay Rs 600 to pass through the reserves and protected areas. The charge was Rs 150 for locals and Rs 300 for outsiders a few months ago.

However, motorists from villages near the reserves and protected areas claimed that they were forced to pay Rs 600 for using vehicles registered in the erstwhile Andhra Pradesh. They said they were being overcharged for passing through the tiger reserves and that the charge was causing a financial burden on them.

Forest officials clarified that the EMC charge had been doubled recently and that non-local motorists had to pay Rs 600 for travelling on routes passing through tiger reserves and protected areas. They advised motorists to change their vehicle registration by approaching the Road Transport Authority to avoid the additional charge. They added that local residents were exempted from the charge.

The officials explained that vehicles owned by local tribal groups and permanent residents of villages situated in the core and buffer zones of the reserves had been exempted from paying the EMC fee. They are required to register their vehicle numbers at counters at the entry points. Private vehicles registered outside the immediate forest-fringe mandals are charged the standard fee.

Aboriginal tribal communities and residents of villages located in the core areas have been staging protests against the collection of toll charges at the entry points to the reserves. They are backed by local public representatives from the Congress, particularly Khanapur MLA Vedma Bojjju, who has openly expressed anger against Forest Department officials over the collection of the fee.

item.title: BRS chief KCR invited to Ayyappa Swamy Maha Padi Puja
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Ayyappa Swamy Maha Padi Puja Mahotsavam
item.description: BRS president K Chandrashekar Rao was invited to the Ayyappa Swamy Maha Padi Puja Mahotsavam in Shambipur on November 19. Former Bhongir MLA Pailla Shekar Reddy and other leaders also met the BRS chief to extend wedding invitations.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS president and former Chief Minister K Chandrashekar Rao was invited to the Ayyappa Swamy Maha Padi Puja Mahotsavam scheduled to be held at Shambipur in Hyderabad on November 19.

BRS MLC Shambipur Raju, accompanied by a group of Ayyappa devotees, met him at his Erravelli residence on Tuesday and handed over the invitation. BRS Quthbullapur leader Shambipur Krishna was also present.

Former Bhongir MLA Pailla Shekar Reddy and his family also called on Chandrashekar Rao and his wife Shobha and invited them to his daughter’s wedding. Former Gajwel municipal vice-chairperson Dumbala Aruna and Bhupal Reddy, and former Tellapur municipal chairperson Mallepally Lalitha and Somireddy, also extended wedding invitations to the BRS chief.

item.title: Apollo Hospitals launches specialised mother and child care institute in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Apollo Institute of Parents and Children
item.description: Apollo Hospitals inaugurated its Institute of Parents and Children at its Financial District facility in Hyderabad on Tuesday. Inaugurated by Upasana Kamineni Konidela, the institute offers specialised care for women, mothers, newborns and children, including high-risk pregnancies and premature babies
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Apollo Hospitals on Tuesday inaugurated the Apollo Institute of Parents and Children at its Financial District facility, strengthening specialised healthcare services for women, mothers, newborns and children. The institute was inaugurated by Upasana Kamineni Konidela, Director, Apollo Hospitals Projects, according to a press release.

The facility features a dedicated obstetrics wing, a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and an attached perinatal centre to provide comprehensive care for mothers and newborns, including high-risk pregnancies and premature babies.

Sharing her personal experience of postpartum challenges following the birth of her twins, Upasana Kamineni Konidela said “My postpartum journey with the twins was extremely tough. It is still too raw to talk about. Couples should not withdraw into a cocoon but come out and seek help and support”.

The institute offers integrated services covering fertility counselling, fetal assessments, high-risk pregnancy management, maternity care, specialised labour and delivery services and general paediatric care, Senior gynaecologists at the facility Dr Phani Jyothsana and Dr Pujitha Devi, said.

item.title: BRS decade built Telangana’s economic base, growth slows under Congress: CESS study
item.dc:creator: PS Dileep
item.description: Telangana recorded robust economic growth, rising per capita income, agricultural expansion and stronger revenue mobilisation during its first decade under BRS.
