However, growth slowed to 6.5 per cent in 2024-25 under Congress, alongside declining revenues, mounting debt and increasing fiscal pressures
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Telangana’s economy expanded faster than the national average during its first decade, with higher per capita income, a sharp rise in agricultural activity and a growing revenue base. However, the growth momentum weakened in the post-pandemic years, with the State’s real growth rate falling to 6.5 per cent in 2024-25, its first full financial year under the Congress government.

These trends emerge from the Centre for Economic and Social Studies (CESS) latest study, Public Finances of Telangana: Trends, Challenges and Policy Priorities, which examined the State’s economic and fiscal performance from 2014-15 to 2024-25.

Telangana’s nominal Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) increased by 219 per cent, from Rs 5.05 lakh crore in 2014-15 to Rs 16.09 lakh crore in 2024-25. This was higher than the growth of 165 per cent recorded by the national economy and 206 per cent by Andhra Pradesh.

The State also registered a 68 per cent increase in real per capita income between 2015-16 and 2023-24, from Rs 1,12,267 to Rs 1,88,436. The increase exceeded the national average of 48 per cent and Andhra Pradesh’s 63 per cent. Telangana moved from eighth to sixth place among general category States in real per capita income rankings. In nominal per capita income, it ranked second in 2023-24.

Agriculture and irrigation drive expansion

Agriculture and allied activities recorded a 176 per cent increase in value addition between 2014-15 and 2024-25. Crop production grew by 131 per cent, while allied activities expanded by 231 per cent.

According to the study, the expansion coincided with a substantial increase in cultivation and irrigation. Gross sown area rose from 131 lakh acres in 2014-15 to 222 lakh acres in 2022-23. Gross irrigated area increased from 62 lakh acres to 135 lakh acres by 2021-22. The rise in per capita power consumption, from 1,356 units in 2014-15 to 2,140 units in 2022-23, also reflected the expansion of electricity use across the economy.

These gains strengthened agriculture’s contribution to the State’s economic expansion, though the sector’s share in Gross State Value Added (GSVA) remained relatively low compared with its employment share.

Revenue base and fiscal capacity

Telangana also expanded its own revenue mobilisation during the decade. The State Own Tax Revenue (SOTR) increased from Rs 39,975 crore in 2015-16 to Rs 1,09,233 crore in 2024-25, a rise of 173 per cent. Its share in revenue receipts increased from 52.5 per cent to 65 per cent.

Total revenue receipts rose from Rs 76,134 crore to Rs 1,67,804 crore during the same period. The report identified the State’s ability to mobilise internal resources and its relatively lower dependence on Central transfers as important strengths.

The expansion of the tax base helped finance infrastructure, economic services and welfare programmes. Between 2015-16 and 2024-25, expenditure on economic services increased from Rs 33,207 crore to Rs 88,371 crore. Social services expenditure rose from Rs 32,618 crore to Rs 65,124 crore.

Services expand, industry loses share

The services sector remained the largest contributor to Telangana’s economy. Its value added increased by 248 per cent between 2014-15 and 2024-25. Industry grew by 169 per cent, while agriculture and allied activities expanded by 176 per cent.

Services accounted for 67 per cent of GSVA in 2024-25, against 18.9 per cent for industry and 14.1 per cent for agriculture. The growing services economy, supported by Hyderabad’s investment and employment base, strengthened the State’s overall output. However, the declining share of industry points to the need for a stronger manufacturing base.

Post-pandemic growth loses momentum

The report flagged a sustained weakening of Telangana’s real growth after the pandemic. The economy contracted by 6 per cent in 2020-21, recovered with 11.1 per cent growth in 2021-22, but slowed to 6.9 per cent in 2022-23 and witnessed marginal recovery of 7.4 per cent in 2023-24.

However, growth fell to 6.5 per cent in 2024-25 under Congress rule, matching the national rate but trailing Andhra Pradesh’s 9.2 per cent. Telangana’s nominal growth also declined from 16.4 per cent in 2022-23 to 11.9 per cent in 2023-24 and 10.6 per cent in 2024-25.

Revenue collections and fiscal pressure

Revenue receipts declined from Rs 1,69,294 crore in 2023-24 to Rs 1,67,804 crore in 2024-25. SOTR also fell from Rs 1,11,798 crore to Rs 1,09,233 crore. Central grants in 2024-25 were only 37 per cent of the Budget Estimates, adding to the pressure on the State’s finances.

The report also pointed to the rising debt burden. Outstanding public debt stood at Rs 3,89,941 crore, or 24.2 per cent of GSDP, at the end of March 2025. Including public account liabilities and other obligations, total liabilities were estimated at Rs 5,61,787 crore, or 34.9 per cent of GSDP, exceeding the State’s fiscal responsibility limit of 32.8 per cent.

The CESS study recorded a decade of substantial economic expansion and stronger internal revenue mobilisation, while flagging the loss of post-pandemic growth momentum, mounting liabilities and pressure on fiscal space. It called for stronger revenue mobilisation, better targeting of welfare expenditure, greater investment in education and human capital, and more transparent accounting of borrowings and expenditure.

item.title: Supreme Court asks authorities to address railway station amenity gaps
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The Supreme Court has asked railway authorities to examine a representation on passenger amenities and take remedial measures to protect passengers. The plea cited a CAG report highlighting unsafe drinking water, poor sanitation and other deficiencies at railway stations nationwide
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court has asked the authorities concerned to examine a representation regarding passenger amenities at railway stations and take appropriate remedial measures to ensure the health and safety of passengers.

A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order while hearing a plea seeking directions to the authorities to ensure the availability of safe and hygienic drinking water, cleanliness and sanitation, emergency medical facilities, functional toilets and accessibility for passengers at railway stations.

The bench observed that the petitioner had approached the top court on the basis of a report by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), which highlighted deficiencies in sanitation and the maintenance of various passenger amenities at railway stations across the country.

It noted that a similar representation had been submitted to the authorities concerned in September this year.

“While we are of the considered view that the nature of grievances flagged by the petitioner are of substantial public interest, we also take note of the fact that the authorities may require reasonable time to examine the recommendations made in the CAG report and the other issues raised by the petitioner,” the bench said in its November 16 order.

“Accordingly, we direct the petitioner to pursue the aforesaid representation before the authorities concerned, who shall look into the same and take appropriate remedial measures, as may be necessary, to ensure the health and safety of passengers availing railway services,” it said, while disposing of the petition.

In the plea filed before the apex court, the petitioner had sought directions to the authorities to ensure comprehensive and periodic testing of all drinking water sources for passengers at railway stations in accordance with prescribed standards.

The plea also sought directions to undertake time-bound corrective and remedial measures at railway stations to ensure hygienic drinking water, cleanliness and sanitation, functional toilets, proper waste management, accessibility, emergency medical facilities and all prescribed minimum essential amenities to safeguard the health, safety, dignity and lives of railway passengers.

“Issue an appropriate writ, order or direction, directing the respondents to ensure comprehensive and periodic testing of all passenger drinking water sources in accordance with the prescribed standards, including for E coli, total coliforms and other bacteriological and chemical parameters, and to immediately discontinue every unsafe or contaminated source and provide safe alternative drinking water until rectification and certification,” the plea read.

It referred to a CAG report tabled in Parliament in August this year, which flagged the presence of E coli bacteria in drinking water from water coolers and unhygienic conditions in washrooms at several stations.

The plea also sought a direction to the authorities concerned to implement, within specified timelines, the applicable recommendations of the CAG report through station-wise corrective action and an effective and transparent monitoring mechanism.

It said that, in the event of failure, neglect or unjustified delay in rectifying the deficiencies within the prescribed timeframe, responsibility and accountability should be fixed on the officers concerned, with appropriate action taken in accordance with the law.

The petitioner urged the court to direct the authorities to immediately address deficiencies directly affecting passenger health and safety, particularly those relating to unsafe drinking water, sanitation and cleanliness, toilets, waste management and emergency medical preparedness.

item.title: Dulquer Salmaan’s Aakasamlo Oka Tara to release on November 20 with U/A certificate
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Dulquer Salmaan and Satvika Veeravalli-starrer Aakasamlo Oka Tara, directed by Pavan Sadineni, has received a U/A certificate from the CBFC. The emotional drama, which follows a village girl's dream of becoming an astronaut, releases worldwide on November 20
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Central Board of Film Certification has cleared director Pavan Sadineni’s upcoming film ‘Aakasamlo Oka Tara’, featuring actors Dulquer Salmaan and Satvika Veeravalli in the lead, for release with a ‘U/A’ certificate.

Geetha Arts, which is jointly presenting the film along with Swapna Cinemas, took to its X timeline to share the update.

It wrote, “An Inspiring story of people just like us…made for Everyone. #AakasamLoOkaTara Certified U/A. Watch #AOTTrailer Now!”

The film is slated to hit screens worldwide on November 20 this year.

A teaser the makers had released recently showed that Kalpana is a brilliant student who secures the district’s first rank. However, despite her academic excellence, she faces discouragement from everyone, including her parents, who eventually get her married. Krishna, who comes into her life, becomes her biggest source of strength and encouragement.

When others tell Kalpana that she cannot even cross the boundaries of her village, she boldly declares that she will cross the boundaries of the earth and reach for the sky. Fortunately, Krishna shares her vision and encourages her to dream big, work hard, and strive to achieve her goals.

It may be recalled that the makers had marked the birthday of actor Dulquer Salmaan earlier this year by releasing a new poster of the actor from the film and announcing that he played the character of Krishna in the film.

The makers of the film had, some months ago, introduced Satvika Veeravalli as the lead of the film.

The film, which is being produced by Sandeep Gunnam and Ramya Gunnam under the Light Box Media banner, is being presented by well known production houses Geetha Arts and Swapna Cinema.

Geetha Arts had, some months ago, taken to its Instagram page to share the introduction video of the actress. It had then said, “She carries a dream bigger than the sky…. Introducing Satvika Veeravalli – The dreamer who gives wings to #AakasamLoOkaTara #AOTMovie.”

The introduction video begins with a child, pointing to the sky and asking “How do I go to space?” Viewers are then given a glimpse of the heroine.The introduction video shows Satvika Veeravalli as a youngster from the rural parts who is dissuaded from pursuing her dream of going to space.

We hear a man’s voice saying, “Coming from a village that has no roads, you harbour plans of going to space? First, you show us if you can cross the borders of the village. Then, we’ll see.”

It is evident that the film will revolve around the character that Satvika Veeravalli plays and that she is actually the protagonist. The film is about a girl from a remote rural region realising her dream of becoming an astronaut and going to space.

The film boasts of a fantastic technical team. It has two-time National Award winner G V Prakash Kumar scoring music for it. Cinematography for the film is by one of the best in business, Sujith Sarang. The film has editing by National Award winning editor K L Praveen.

item.title: Pakistan, Sri Lanka fined for slow over-rates in Rawalpindi Test
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Pakistan and Sri Lanka have been fined 25pc and 50pc of their match fees, respectively, for slow over-rates in the opening Test of their World Test Championship series in Rawalpindi. Both sides will each lose one point per over short
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Pakistan have been fined 25 per cent and Sri Lanka 50 per cent of their respective match fees for maintaining slow over-rates in the opening match of their two-match ICC World Test Championship series in Rawalpindi. Both teams will also lose one World Test Championship competition point for each over they fell short.

Dean Cosker of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees imposed the sanctions after Pakistan were found to be five overs short of the required rate and Sri Lanka 15 overs short, after time allowances were taken into consideration.

In accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which deals with minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fees for every over their team fails to bowl within the allotted time, subject to a maximum penalty of 50 per cent.

Captains Babar Azam and Kusal Mendis pleaded guilty to the offences and accepted the proposed sanctions, respectively, meaning there was no need for formal hearings.

On-field umpires Adrian Holdstock and Rod Tucker, third umpire Allahuddien Paleker and fourth umpire Faisal Afridi levelled the charges.

item.title: AICWA thanks Salman Khan and Sonu Sood for helping Sharad Kapoor
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: AICWA has thanked Salman Khan and Sonu Sood for supporting actor Sharad Kapoor, who recently spoke about his difficult circumstances and appealed for work. The association said Sood had discussed a project and arranged medical assistance for him.
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has thanked Bollywood stars Salman Khan and Sonu Sood for extending a helping hand to actor Sharad Kapoor after the Josh actor opened up about going through a difficult phase in life.

Sood recently met Kapoor, while there are reports that Salman has also reached out to his Jai Ho co-star.

AICWA, a non-profit organisation working towards the betterment of artists and workers in the Indian film industry, shared a statement on Tuesday on Instagram.

“The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) warmly thanks Salman Khan for coming forward to support actor Sharad Kapoor with financial help in this difficult time. Such a gesture gives hope not only to Sharad Kapoor ji, but to every artist who fears being forgotten in his hard days.

“AICWA also extends its heartfelt gratitude to Sonu Sood for reaching out to Sharad Kapoor ji. Sonu Sood ji has reportedly met him to discuss a project that could bring him back to work, and has also arranged medical support for him. Work, with dignity, is exactly what Sharad Kapoor ji asked for,” the statement read.

AICWA said Kapoor had worked in films alongside stars such as Shah Rukh Khan (Josh) and Hrithik Roshan (Lakshya), and now needed the industry’s support to bounce back.

The film body said there were many others like Sharad Kapoor who were fighting silently.

“Helping them in such a moment is not charity; it is humanity, and it is our duty,” Suresh Shyamlal Gupta, president of AICWA, said.

In videos that have gone viral on social media, Kapoor said he needed work.

“I need help financially, morally, and mentally. I am a big fan of all my actors. I always consider myself their fan. So I appeal to you – please help me,” he said.

In a separate video, Kapoor also appealed to the Cine And TV Artistes’ Association (CINTAA) to help him with job opportunities.

“I’m looking for good work, and I need your support and I know you’ve always supported people around you. So, I’ll be very thankful to you if you can support me. I’m a brilliant actor,” he added.

item.title: Nani’s Delivery Boy: Bose Venkat’s character revealed ahead of November 27 release
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The makers of director Nani's upcoming film Delivery Boy have revealed that Bose Venkat plays a police officer named David. Starring Leo Sivakumar, Brigida and Radhika Sarathkumar, the emotional action entertainer is scheduled for release on November 27
item.content:encoded:
Chennai: The makers of director Nani’s upcoming emotional action entertainer ‘Delivery Boy’, featuring actors Leo Sivakumar, Brigida and Radhika Sarathkumar in the lead, on Tuesday revealed the character actor Bose Venkat plays in the film.

Asasi Creations, the production house producing the film, took to its Instagram page to reveal Bose Venkat’s character. It wrote, “Meet DAVID –

A police officer whose entry brings unexpected twists and turns to the story! Bose Venkat as DAVID – Every move has a new turn! Delivery Boy | In theatres from November 27!”

The makers also revealed that actor Kaali Venkat plays a character called Karuppu in the film.

The film, which had originally been scheduled to hit screens worldwide on October 23, will now hit screens on November 27.

Shooting for the film had been wrapped up in December last year.

Sources close to the unit had said that the film, which had been shot entirely in Chennai and Coimbatore, was shot in a span of just 42 days.

Taking to their X timeline, the publicists of the production house Asasi Creations, had then said, “#DeliveryBoy shoot wrapped up. Coming to theatres soon. Starring @leosivakumar02 @realradikaa @Brigidasagaoffl @DushyanthJayap1 @dhivakargj @DirectorBose @SundaramurthyKS @AmuthaLeoni @nanisignin @teamaimpr.”

Talking to IANS, director Nani, who worked as an assistant director to well known director Suseenthiran before turning director, had said, “If I have to briefly give you an idea of what the film is all about, it is about the efforts made by a hardworking delivery boy looking to save his mother. The hero of the story comes from a lower middle class family and the story will revolve around his efforts to save his mother. It will be a gripping story that will keep audiences hooked to the screen from the beginning to end.”

The director had also disclosed that now that the shooting had been wrapped up, post production work was progressing at a brisk pace. “We have now started dubbing for the film,” he had said then.

Apart from Leo Sivakumar, Brigida and Radikaa Sarathkumar, who play the lead, the film will also feature a host of gifted character artistes including actors Dushyanth, Kaali Venkat and Bose Venkat among others.

The film also boasts of a good technical team. Produced by Amutha Leoni on behalf of the banner Asasi Creation, ‘Delivery Boy’ will have music by Sundaramoorthy and cinematography by Prasanna Kumar.

The film, which has dialogues by Nanda Mani Vasagam, will have editing by Vasanth. Stunts in the film have been choreographed by Phoenix Prabhu while Art direction is by Suresh Kalyani.

item.title: Saurav Rathi takes two-shot lead at IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Saurav Rathi opened the 2026-27 DP World PGTI season with a seven-under 65 to take a two-shot lead at the 26th IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf in Digboi, Assam, despite nursing a left-leg injury sustained earlier this week
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Gurugram’s Saurav Rathi opened the 2026-27 DP World PGTI season with an impressive seven-under 65 to take a two-shot lead in the first round of the 26th IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf, a Rs 1-crore event being played at the picturesque Digboi Golf Links in Digboi, Assam.

The 24-year-old Rathi made eight birdies and dropped his only shot of the day on the par-4 18th, his closing hole, to emerge as the outright leader on a course where only 29 players in the 120-man field managed to break par.

Delhi’s 21-year-old Anshul Kabthiyal and seasoned campaigner Om Prakash Chouhan shared second place at five-under 67.

Rathi, a regular on the DP World PGTI since 2019, recently secured his full playing rights for the new season after finishing 17th at the DP World PGTI Qualifying Tournament Final Stage in Ahmedabad.

Despite nursing a left-leg injury sustained after slipping on wet stairs at the golf course on Monday, Rathi produced a commanding display, hitting 12 of 14 fairways and 15 greens in regulation.

Chouhan, an 11-time winner on the DP World PGTI, a former winner on the European Challenge Tour (now the HotelPlanner Tour) and the 2023 DP World PGTI Rankings champion, also carded a 67, making eight birdies against three bogeys.

Four players shared fourth place at four-under 68: Gurugram’s Kushal Singh, Pune’s Divyansh Dubey, Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh and Lucknow’s Sanjeev Kumar.

Kushal made seven birdies and three bogeys, while Divyansh registered six birdies and two bogeys. Yuvraj recovered from a double bogey on the par-5 15th and another bogey with seven birdies, while Sanjeev produced five birdies against a lone bogey.

Despite measuring just 6,348 yards, the par-72 Digboi Golf Links presented a stern test in the opening round, with fewer than a quarter of the field returning under-par scores.

item.title: Karnataka targets global leadership in AI and deep tech
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit opened with Karnataka outlining its ambitions in artificial intelligence, deep technology, semiconductors and biotechnology. The State highlighted its startup ecosystem, investment inflows, research institutions, skilling programmes and initiatives to attract global innovators.
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru: The 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit, themed ‘AI and Beyond’, was inaugurated by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar here on Tuesday, with Karnataka aiming to position itself as a global hub for Artificial Intelligence, deep technology, semiconductor manufacturing and biotechnology.

Addressing the gathering of international delegates, industry leaders, investors, scientists and young innovators, Shivakumar said Karnataka was preparing to lead the next phase of global innovation through progressive policies, strong research institutions, a thriving startup ecosystem and skilled human resources.

Welcoming participants, he said Bengaluru had evolved into one of the world’s largest technology clusters by embracing talent, diversity and ambition from across the globe.

“Karnataka laid the foundations of modern industry and technology through institutions of learning and research, strong public sector enterprises and the trust of global companies. Some of India’s most ambitious scientific and engineering projects have found a home here,” he said.

Highlighting the State’s contribution to India’s technology economy, Shivakumar said Karnataka accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports, amounting to approximately $173 billion last year.

He said Karnataka had received $9.4 billion in FDI equity inflows in the first half of FY 2025-26, accounting for 26.7 per cent of India’s total inflows during the period. More than 1,000 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) had chosen Bengaluru as their base, while over 30 new GCCs brought investments exceeding $1 billion into the State in 2025 alone.

Referring to Karnataka’s contribution to India’s scientific and technological achievements, he cited Chandrayaan-3, the digital identity platform developed at IIIT-Bengaluru, Biocon’s global pharmaceutical reach and Bengaluru-based Sarvam’s role in developing India’s own AI model.

Shivakumar said Karnataka was home to more than 24,000 recognised startups, with nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originating from the State. Bengaluru ranked eighth among the world’s startup ecosystems and second in Asia for AI-native startups. Bengaluru attracted $4.4 billion in technology funding, nearly matching the combined $4.8 billion raised by the next five Indian cities. Karnataka startups had collectively raised approximately $79 billion, while women founders in Bengaluru had secured $13.4 billion in funding, he said.

Under the ELEVATE initiative, the government had supported nearly 1,500 startups through equity-free grants amounting to $41 million over a decade.

Through ELEVATE NxT, the State was offering grants of Rs 1 crore to deep-tech startups. Since last year, 33 such startups had received equity-free funding of Rs 30 crore.

He also announced that the government’s deep-tech accelerator, Innoverse, would support 35 growth-stage ventures over the next five years, helping them transition from product development to industrial-scale operations.

Under the Government First initiative, the government would become the first customer for startups, with a dedicated allocation of Rs 25 crore to procure innovative solutions developed by them.

Describing Artificial Intelligence as the foundation of Karnataka’s next phase of technological development, Shivakumar said Bengaluru accounted for nearly 50 per cent of India’s AI and Machine Learning talent.

The government was building India’s first government-driven AI University, with an AI Hub at its centre to bring startups, researchers and industry together.

An additional Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur would extend AI applications to the 13 districts of North Karnataka, with solutions for agriculture, healthcare, education and small businesses.

He also highlighted the proposed BRAINZ (Bengaluru Robotics and AI Innovation Zone), which would create an ecosystem for Artificial Intelligence and robotics research, prototyping and manufacturing.

Under the Rs 300 crore Nipuna Karnataka reskilling mission, the government was preparing the State’s workforce for emerging technology requirements. More than 33,000 people, including women returning to the workforce after career breaks, had already become industry-ready through partnerships with leading global technology companies.

On semiconductor development, Shivakumar said Karnataka was home to more than 100 fabless chip companies, while three out of every five engineers working in India’s semiconductor capability centres were based in Bengaluru.

He said the State accounted for one-fifth of India’s electronics exports and was now moving from semiconductor design towards manufacturing.

Global companies were investing more than Rs 23,000 crore in semiconductor research and manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru and Mysuru, he said.

Four electronics manufacturing clusters, stretching from Dharwad to Mysuru, would provide ready infrastructure, land, power and skilled talent, supported by incentives under the Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) Policy.

He also highlighted the role of SFAL, the fabless semiconductor accelerator, the 2D Innovation Hub at IISc and Infifab, proposed as India’s first microfabrication translation centre, in strengthening semiconductor research, innovation and manufacturing capabilities.

Shivakumar said Karnataka accounted for one-fifth of India’s bioeconomy, valued at $39.2 billion last year and contributing more than a tenth of the State’s economy.

The government was expanding biotechnology into marine resources, agriculture and healthcare through initiatives such as the Marine Biotechnology Policy, Karnataka Institute of Marine Biotechnology and Blue Economy, Agri Innovation Park and Krishikalpa Centre of Excellence for Agriculture.

He also referred to plans for a new institute for genome editing and gene therapy, Charaka Centre of Excellence for health and medical technology, and a Centre of Excellence for AI in Biotechnology. Eleven new incubators would help translate research into commercial ventures.

Pointing to the growing international participation at the summit, Shivakumar said more than 75 countries were participating in this year’s edition, compared to 57 last year. The number of exhibitors had nearly doubled, while business visitor participation was expected to increase by nearly a third.

Inviting global investors, innovators and industry leaders to partner with Karnataka, he said, “We will bring the talent, the policies and the partnership. You bring your ambition. What lies beyond AI, we want to build here, with you.”

Declaring the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit open, Shivakumar said Karnataka was committed to creating technologies and industries not just for India but for the world.

He concluded his address with the slogans, “Jai Hind. Jai Karnataka.”

item.title: Kohli’s childhood coach keen to see him play T10 cricket
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Virat Kohli's childhood coach Rajkumar Sharma is enjoying his first stint in the Abu Dhabi T10 with United Tigers. He discusses the format's intensity, backs Abhishek Sharma and maintains that Test cricket remains the ultimate measure of ability.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Virat Kohli has never played ten-over cricket, but he is keeping an eye on the Abu Dhabi T10. His childhood coach Rajkumar Sharma, who is with the United Tigers this season, made sure Kohli knew where he was headed.

“I told him I’m going there and what my role is. He knows about the tournament, and I know he’s watching it,” Sharma said after the Tigers’ seven-wicket defeat to the Arabian Aces at Zayed Cricket Stadium on Monday. Sharma would like to see his old pupil try the format. “He hasn’t played this format, but if he plays, he will do well, and people will love it.”

Sharma has spent close to three decades teaching cricket the long way. He founded the West Delhi Cricket Academy, turned a young Kohli into a batter, and still believes Test cricket is where a player is made. This month, he is learning a format that gives nobody time to settle.

“I’m definitely enjoying this role,” he said. “The team is good, the atmosphere is very good, and I’m really excited.”

Sharma calls himself an old-timer more than once, and he means it. “It’s a different kind of cricket. Honestly, this is my first time in T10, and as an old-timer I’m still understanding it. But it’s very exciting. I’ve done 50 overs and 20 overs, and now ten overs is a new lesson for me. There’s a lot of energy, the intensity is high and it’s hard to make a comeback. It’s very competitive cricket.”

Ask him where a young cricketer should start, though, and the answer has not moved. “As an old-timer, I feel Test cricket is actual cricket,” he said. “If someone is good at Test cricket, he can always play one-day, T20 or T10. But I don’t think a T10 or T20 player can easily become a good Test player. There are exceptions, but technically it’s different, because there is a lot of power-hitting here.”

Away from Kohli, the Indian he would most like to see in a ten-over side is Abhishek Sharma. “If you look at Abhishek Sharma and the rest of our youngsters, they are just too good,” he said.

Rajkumar will not, however, name the next Virat Kohli. “No one can replace Virat. It takes very long to become Virat Kohli,” he said. “Somebody has to play for more than ten years to be in contention with such players. Youngsters are coming, and they are very talented. We have a lot of good players. Shubman Gill is one of the best we have, and Abhishek Sharma is also a good player. But they need time. Play a few years, perform consistently, and then we can think about whether someone can replace Virat.”

item.title: KTR questions absence of Telangana in Sonia Gandhi’s autobiography
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao questioned the Congress' claim that Sonia Gandhi was instrumental in Telangana's formation, citing the absence of any reference to the State in her autobiography. He credited the prolonged people's movement led by K Chandrashekhar Rao for achieving statehood.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao on Tuesday questioned the Congress’ claim that Sonia Gandhi was instrumental in the formation of Telangana, asking why the State found no mention in her autobiography if it had a place in her heart. Reacting to her autobiography, Belonging, he said the absence of any reference to Telangana in the book exposed the hollowness of the Congress’ claim that Sonia Gandhi had gifted statehood to the region.

“Telangana was neither a gift from her nor the outcome of the Congress’ benevolence, but the result of a prolonged people’s movement led by BRS president K Chandrashekhar Rao,” he asserted during an informal interaction with mediapersons.

The BRS working president said the Congress agreed to the formation of Telangana only because the massive movement had created a political compulsion. The party had yielded to the demand out of fear of being swept away by the agitation rather than out of genuine concern for the aspirations of the people, he added.

He accused the Congress of attempting to appropriate the history of the Telangana movement and the sacrifices made by millions of people. He asserted that the State was achieved through the relentless struggle of its people under Chandrashekhar Rao’s leadership, and no party could erase that history or claim exclusive credit for it.

Rama Rao also referred to BRS MLC Vani Devi’s response to Congress leaders who have recently been expressing admiration for former Prime Minister PV Narasimha Rao. She had questioned why his last rites were not conducted in Delhi if the Congress leadership had so much respect and affection for him, he said.

He said the Congress had consistently viewed Telangana’s aspirations and its leadership through the prism of political convenience. “Its present attempts to claim credit for statehood, while overlooking the movement and its sacrifices, are therefore misplaced,” he said.

item.title: Interstate egg donation racket: 43 women rescued in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: C. Romeo
item.description: Malkajgiri police have busted an alleged interstate egg donation racket in which economically vulnerable women were reportedly lured with cash offers and brought to Hyderabad. Forty-three women were rescued and nine persons arrested. Police are investigating links to fertility centres and ART banks.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: From recruiting young women from different states with promises of Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 for donating their eggs, bringing them to the city, accommodating them in rented apartments disguised as women’s hostels and directing them to IVF centres for egg collection, this was the alleged modus operandi of the interstate illegal egg donation racket recently busted by Malkajgiri police.

Investigations until now have revealed that agents allegedly targeted young women from economically weaker backgrounds in West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and other states. After convincing them with financial offers, the recruiters arranged their transportation to Hyderabad and accommodated them in rented premises. The women were subsequently referred to fertility centres for egg donation procedures.

At these centres, the women were allegedly administered hormonal injections and medicines to stimulate their ovaries before their eggs were collected.

Police suspect that the collected eggs were supplied to IVF centres and ART banks through intermediaries, with possible links to institutions in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Delhi.

Also, the network allegedly involved separate individuals handling recruitment, accommodation, medical coordination, documentation and financial transactions.

One of the premises at Prakash Nagar in Begumpet was allegedly operated as a women’s hostel while serving as a base for the racket for nearly two years, with a monthly rent of around Rs 50,000.

According to Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B Sumathi, 43 women were rescued and nine persons arrested following coordinated raids by Begumpet and Saroornagar police, along with the Special Operations Team (SOT), at multiple locations, including Begumpet, Erragadda, Saroornagar and Gopalpuram. During which, vials of Humog HP 150 IU injections, syringes, needles, hormonal tablets and documents were seized.

Police are probing possible coercion, deception, repeat donation cycles, financial exploitation and human trafficking, besides tracing the recruitment network and identifying the beneficiaries of the alleged illegal trade. They are also examining possible violations of medical supervision, informed consent and biomedical waste disposal regulations.

Meanwhile, two complaints were lodged by the Telangana Medical and Health Department alleging illegal oocyte collection and donation at fertility clinics in Jubilee Hills and Film Nagar. Sadguru Health Care Services Private Limited, which operates Oasis Fertility clinics and an ART bank, has come under scrutiny, with its director Dr Durga Rao and clinic in-charges named in the complaints.

As part of the investigation, police have issued notices to 14 fertility hospitals, IVF centres and ART banks seeking donor registration records, identity documents, consent forms, medical histories and payment details. Another suspect, Praveen, was arrested over alleged manipulation of Aadhaar-related documents.

Until now, three cases were booked under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021.

item.title: Over 3.2 lakh pages of Hyderabad State gazettes digitised
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: More than 3.2 lakh pages of gazettes issued by the erstwhile Hyderabad Government between 1869 and 1956 have been digitised. The collection includes records in Persian, Urdu and English, along with historical documents on administration, education and infrastructure projects.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Over 3.20 lakh pages of gazettes issued by the then Hyderabad Government from 1869 to 1956 will now be available in digital format.

Noor Microfilm International Centre (NMIC), New Delhi, which has undertaken digitisation and preservation of archives, has handed over digital data, comprising 3,20,598 pages of Persian, Urdu and English Gazettes to the Telangana State Archives and Research Institute in the third phase of the project.

The Institute Director, Dr Zareena Parveen, said in addition to the gazettes, the collection includes 40 segments of historically significant archival records, such as Daftar Diwani, The Revolt of the Asif Jahi government documents, Makharej Sarkar Daulatmand Mahalat, Tafseel-e-Jageer, Diplomatic Correspondence, and Report on the State and Progress of Education in the Central Provinces.

She said the digital images of several important records relating to major irrigation and infrastructure projects had also been handed over. These include documents concerning the Construction of Osman Sagar Project, Effects of Deforestation and Denudation on Irrigation Projects, Himayat Sagar, Construction of a New Reservoir on the Esa River, Lotus Growth in Hussain Sagar Tank, and Moderation of the Musa River.

NMIC regional director Ali Akber Niromand said the digital images had been prepared to international standards of quality and the specialised conservation techniques help protect archival documents for up to 100 years.

State Archives assistant director MA Raqeeb said approximately 11 lakh digital images had so far been handed over and remaining digital data, comprising approximately 6 lakh images, would be handed over in the first week of December.

item.title: Hyderabad researchers find way to disarm drug-resistant fungus
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB)
item.description: CSIR-CCMB researchers in Hyderabad have identified compounds that prevent Candida albicans from developing into invasive filaments. The approach could help control fungal infections and improve the effectiveness of existing antifungal drugs, with encouraging results in preclinical mouse models.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Researchers from Hyderabad-based Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CSIR-CCMB) have unveiled a promising new strategy to combat drug-resistant fungal infections by disarming pathogens rather than killing them.

Traditional antimicrobial drugs face a growing challenge as microbial populations rapidly develop resistance to drugs. The same happens in fungal infections, where pathogens are rising but antifungal options remain scarce.

To address the challenge, a new study from Dr Sriram Varahan’s lab at CCMB focuses on Candida albicans, a common skin fungus that turns dangerous when it enters internal organs. It causes painful infections by shape-shifting from harmless round cells into long, invasive filaments that the immune system cannot control.

By targeting glycolysis, the sugar metabolism pathway that acts as a cellular switch for the physical transformation (from round cells to long invasive filaments), the team screened a library of small molecules and identified compounds that successfully block filament formation.

Interestingly, the researchers identified certain compounds that allow the fungus to survive without causing disease, highlighting pyruvate kinase as a vital metabolic node for controlling fungal behaviour.

Moreover, in the study, the researchers reported that one of the lead compounds increased pathogen sensitivity to conventional drugs like fluconazole and amphotericin B, and significantly improved survival in preclinical mouse models. Published in ACS Infectious Diseases, the research was conducted in collaboration with BRIC-THSTI scientists.

item.title: Sabarimala opens for Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple opened on Tuesday, marking the beginning of the Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season. Authorities have arranged virtual queue and spot-booking facilities, medical services, sanitation measures and crowd management arrangements for the expected influx of devotees.
item.content:encoded:
Sabarimala: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple opened at 3 am on Tuesday, marking the beginning of the two-month-long annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season, with thousands of devotees arriving at the hill shrine chanting ‘Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa’.

The newly appointed Melsanthi (chief priest), Areekkara Subramanian Sankaran Namboothiri, opened the sanctum for devotees on the first day of the Malayalam month of Vrischikam. The Malikappuram temple also opened at the same time, with its newly appointed Melsanthi, A Damodaran Namboothiri, beginning the rituals there.

The temples had opened on Monday evening as part of the preparatory ceremonies, during which the outgoing chief priests handed over charge to their successors. The new Melsanthis assumed office after the traditional consecration ceremonies performed by Tantri Kandaru Brahmadathan.

State Devaswom and Health Minister K Muraleedharan witnessed the Nirmalya Darshan at the Ayyappa temple at 3 am.

With a large number of devotees expected during the opening days, the authorities have put in place arrangements to regulate the flow of pilgrims, particularly through the 18 holy steps.

Spot-booking facilities have been arranged at Nilakkal, the main base camp, Erumeli and Sathram near Vandiperiyar.

No spot-booking facility has been provided at Pamba, as officials fear that it could lead to overcrowding at the riverside pilgrim centre. Devotees without virtual queue bookings can obtain tokens at the designated centres before proceeding to the shrine.

Reviewing the arrangements at Sabarimala on Tuesday morning, Muraleedharan said all necessary measures had been taken to ensure a smooth and hassle-free pilgrimage.

“At present, 60,000 devotees are allowed to book through the virtual queue system and another 14,000 through spot booking every day. Steps will be taken to increase the booking limits, with the permission of the court, if the number of pilgrims rises in the coming days,” he said.

The minister said Rs 3.36 crore had been allocated to local self-government institutions for managing Sabarimala pilgrim centres (edathavalams), following the special initiative of Chief Minister V D Satheesan.

He said adequate stocks of appam and aravana prasadam had been ensured and arrangements were in place to increase production according to demand. Sanitation workers had been deployed at all locations, with officials assigned sector-wise responsibilities to ensure regular waste removal.

Under the Health Department’s ‘Swasthyam Saranam’ project, five allopathic hospitals and 24 emergency medical centres have been set up along the Pamba-Sannidhanam route.

The services of 35 doctors, including five cardiologists, have been arranged, besides trained nursing staff and adequate stocks of medicines.

Ayurveda and homoeopathy facilities will also function round the clock, with the services of four therapists. Fifteen ambulances have been stationed at Pamba and another 10 at Nilakkal.

Meanwhile, Devaswom Board president K Jayakumar urged devotees not to leave their clothes in the Pamba river after taking a bath, warning that the practice caused pollution. More volunteers would be deployed to remove clothes from the river, and officials had been asked to clear waste at least once every three hours.

CCTV cameras will also be installed at locations where annadanam (free food distribution) is held, he said.

In a message marking the beginning of the pilgrimage season, CM Satheesan extended his greetings to devotees and wished them a spiritually fulfilling journey.

“May the golden rays of the Vrischika dawn fill every heart with the divine light of devotion to Lord Ayyappa,” he said in a social media post.

Referring to the devotional chants echoing in homes and along the pilgrimage routes, Satheesan said he hoped the prayers of every devotee undertaking the journey to Sabarimala would be fulfilled.

“May this Mandala season, reverberating with chants of ‘Saranam Ayyappa’, bring everyone spiritual fulfilment and the blessed experience of Lord Ayyappa’s darshan,” he said.

The Chief Minister also assured devotees that “Keralam stands with you”.

item.title: Gurnoor Brar reprimanded for Code of Conduct breach
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: India pacer Gurnoor Brar has been reprimanded for a Level 1 breach of the ICC Code of Conduct during the fourth ODI against New Zealand. His aggressive celebration after Tim Seifert's dismissal earned him one demerit point, taking his total to two.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: India bowler Gurnoor Brar has been reprimanded for breaching Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct during the fourth ODI against New Zealand in Mount Maunganui on Friday.

Brar was found to have breached Article 2.5 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to “using language, actions or gestures which disparage or which could provoke an aggressive reaction from a batter upon his/her dismissal during an International Match”.

In addition, one demerit point has been added to Brar’s disciplinary record. It was his second offence in a 24-month period, taking his accumulated total to two demerit points.

The incident occurred after the dismissal of Tim Seifert at the end of the 12th over. Brar celebrated in an aggressive manner that could have been interpreted as demeaning to the batter, potentially provoking an equally aggressive reaction.

Brar admitted the offence and accepted the sanction proposed by Ranjan Madugalle of the Emirates ICC International Panel of Match Referees, so there was no need for a formal hearing.

On-field umpires Chris Brown and Kumar Dharmasena, third umpire Paul Reiffel and fourth umpire Wayne Knights levelled the charge.

Level 1 breaches carry a minimum penalty of an official reprimand, a maximum penalty of 50 per cent of a player’s match fee, and one or two demerit points.

item.title: Shami joins Rajasthan Royals ahead of IPL 2027
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Experienced pacer Mohd Shami will join Rajasthan Royals for IPL 2027, moving from Lucknow Super Giants in a trade that also brings left-arm spinner M Siddharth to RR and sends all-rounder Sam Curran to LSG ahead of the upcoming tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Experienced right-arm pacer Mohammed Shami will represent the Rajasthan Royals (RR) in the upcoming TATA Indian Premier League (IPL) 2027 season after being traded from Lucknow Super Giants (LSG). After being acquired for Rs 10 crore by LSG, Shami will now move to RR for a revised fee of Rs 8 crore.

Shami will further strengthen RR’s bowling attack with his skill and striking ability. The right-arm pacer has taken 145 wickets from 132 IPL matches so far.

Left-arm spinner M Siddharth, known for his accuracy and control, will also move to RR from LSG for his existing fee of Rs 75 lakh.

Meanwhile, all-rounder Sam Curran has been traded to LSG from RR for his existing fee of Rs 2.4 crore. He has claimed 59 wickets and scored 997 runs in his IPL career so far. Known for his variations and ability to deliver in pressure situations, Curran adds valuable depth and versatility to the squad.

item.title: Hyderabad police bust alleged fake silver waraq manufacturing racket
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad police raided four units allegedly manufacturing aluminium leaves and passing them off as edible silver waraq. The products were reportedly supplied to sweet manufacturers and bakeries, while officials seized aluminium leaves, flakes and other materials.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: The Hyderabad Commissioner’s Task Force on Tuesday raided four units in the city engaged in allegedly making edible silver waraqs using aluminium instead of genuine silver.

The police seized 49 bundles of aluminium leaves, 10 kg of aluminium flakes in cartons, fake silver-coated sugar balls, paan chutney, tobacco, maize starch and other raw materials.

According to Hyderabad Police Commissioner, MM Bhagwath, the four units — Waraq Shop owned by Mohammed Akber, UTC Silver Leafs owned by Mohammed Wali Uddin, M A Metro Waraq Shop of Mohammed Shareef, and Tara Unit owned by Mohammed Jaleel Khan — were manufacturing aluminium leaves and passing them off as genuine edible silver products.

“The fake waraqs were supplied to sweet manufacturers for use in Kaju Katli, Kaju Rolls and Cham Cham, while aluminium-coated sugar balls were supplied to bakeries for cake decorations. The suspects were also procuring aluminium flakes from Uttar Pradesh and using them in Zarda and flavoured paan preparations,” he said.

As per Food Safety and Standards regulations, edible silver leaf must have a minimum silver purity of 999 parts per thousand (99.9%). The units were allegedly operating without valid FSSAI licences and violating prescribed food safety standards, pointed out Bhagwath.

The police cautioned that prolonged consumption of food containing non-food-grade aluminium may pose health risks, including kidney damage, neurological problems, bone disorders and digestive irritation.

How to identify fake silver waraq

Two preliminary tests can help identify fake silver waraq, though laboratory analysis is essential for confirmation.

In the dilute hydrochloric acid test, aluminium reacts with the acid, producing hydrogen bubbles, while genuine silver normally does not. In the rubbing test, genuine silver breaks into fine particles, whereas aluminium tends to crumple, tear or form small ball-like pieces.

Chemical testing should be undertaken only by trained personnel with proper safety precautions. The use of aluminium foil in place of genuine silver waraq is a serious violation of food safety standards.

item.title: BRS protests against AP project at Nagarjuna Sagar
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The BRS staged a protest at Pylon Colony in Nagarjuna Sagar against an unauthorised tunnel and pipeline network project allegedly being undertaken by Andhra Pradesh. Led by former MLA Nomula Bhagath, protesters demanded immediate action to stop the project.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) staged a protest at Pylon Colony in Nagarjuna Sagar Municipality on Tuesday against an unauthorised tunnel and pipeline network project being undertaken by the Andhra Pradesh government at Nagarjuna Sagar.

Former BRS MLA Nomula Bhagath led the protest. BRS leaders raised slogans against the Telangana and Central governments, accusing them of failing to protect the state’s interests.

The protesters also condemned what they described as the policies of the Central and Andhra Pradesh governments. They alleged that farmers and the people of Telangana would be deprived of their rightful share of water.

BRS leaders from across the constituency took part in the protest. They demanded that the Congress government take immediate measures to ensure that the project was stopped.

item.title: Tension in Vemulawada as BJP opposes temple tower demolition
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Tension prevailed at the Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Devasthanam in Vemulawada after BJP cadres protested the demolition of a temple tower during renovation works. They alleged violations of Agama Shastra norms, demanded an inspection and were later shifted to the police station.
item.content:encoded:
Rajanna Sircilla: Tension prevailed for a while after BJP cadres opposed the demolition of a temple tower at the Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Devasthanam in Vemulawada on Tuesday.

The ancient abode of Lord Shiva is undergoing renovation at an estimated cost of Rs 250 crore. The temple precincts are being expanded to around 7 acres. A new prakaram, or outer wall, is being built around the main temple. The holy tank is also being upgraded. As part of the development works, the tower was razed using an earthmover.

On learning about this, BJP leaders and activists rushed to the temple and picked an argument with the shrine authorities. They argued that the tower was being dismantled in violation of Agama Shastra norms, hurting the sentiments of devotees. They staged a sit-in in front of the temple, demanding that officials halt the development works.

BJP district general secretary Srinivas, town president Rapalli Sridhar, councillors Vangala Srinvas and Kondlepu Muthyam, leaders Regula Santosh and others wanted officials to allow them to inspect the works. They demanded that the Collector and authorities of the Vemulawada Temple Development Authority visit the site immediately and clarify their doubts.

The cadres then attempted to barge into the premises of the temple, which is undergoing renovation. They were stopped by policemen present at the spot. The two sides jostled, resulting in tension for a brief period. However, large contingents of police were deployed and brought the situation under control. The protesters were shifted to the local police station.

The serene surroundings of the temple were disturbed for a while following the protest by BJP cadres and their subsequent arrests.

item.title: Hundreds of devotees take part in Maha Padayatra from Kagaznagar to Tonkini
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Around 10,000 devotees joined a 20-km Maha Padayatra from Kagaznagar to Sri Siddi Hanuman temple at Tonkini village on Tuesday, marking the walkathon's 25th anniversary. Devotees offered prayers, while volunteers distributed food and fruits.
item.content:encoded:
Kumram Bheem Asifabad: Hundreds of devotees took part in a Maha Padayatra from Kagaznagar to the Sri Siddi Hanuman temple at Tonkini village in Sirpur (T) mandal on Tuesday, marking the 25th anniversary of the walkathon. The devotees covered a distance of 20 km.

Around 10,000 devotees from Kagaznagar, as well as Asifabad, Rebbena, Dahegaon, Bejjur and Chintalamanepalli mandals, joined the walkathon. They then visited the shrine and offered special prayers. Some of them took a holy dip in the Wardha river before having darshan of the deity.

Meanwhile, followers of Sirpur (T) MLA Dr Harish Babu provided food to the devotees, while BRS leader Konappa and community organisations distributed fruits to the participants. The village came alive with the presence of a large number of devotees. Around 100 policemen were deployed to prevent untoward incidents.

According to locals, the temple was built at scenic Tonkini on the banks of the Wardha river around 100 years ago. It is believed that the wishes of devotees are fulfilled if they offer a mudupu (tying a specific auspicious item in a cloth bundle) to the deity while praying for a wish. Locals claimed that the village had withstood severe floods ever since the temple was built.

item.title: Married couple kills pet dog before dying by suicide in Warangal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A couple was found dead at their home in Warangal's Rangasaipet late Monday night. A purported suicide note cited financial difficulties and debts, and blamed a tailor from whom they had borrowed money. Police have registered a case and begun an investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Warangal: A married couple allegedly died by suicide at Rangasaipet, under the limits of Mills Colony police station, late on Monday night.

The couple, Nallapogula Shobha (53) and her husband Sanjay Kumar (60), were found hanging from the ceiling of their house. They had also killed their pet dog before taking their own lives. In a suicide note purportedly left by the couple, they stated that financial difficulties had driven them to take the extreme step.

They said they killed the pet dog because it had remained with them through good and bad times and they did not want to leave it alone. They also mentioned that many people had mocked them for keeping a pet dog despite their financial troubles and debts. The couple appealed to Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to ensure that their cremation was performed along with that of the dog.

The couple held a tailor, Divya, from whom they had borrowed money, responsible for their deaths. They requested their family members not to inform their children, who live elsewhere, about their deaths.

Police registered a case in connection with the incident and took up the investigation.

item.title: Guru Nanak Jayanti celebrations to begin in Hyderabad on November 19
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Hyderabad’s Sikh community will celebrate the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji with Nagar Kirtans in Secunderabad and Hyderabad, a Kirtan Darbar and a joint Gurupurab programme at Exhibition Grounds, Nampally, on November 24.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Guru Nanak Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj, will be celebrated in the city in a grand manner, Ashok Bazar Gurudwara Saheb president Sardar Guru Charan Singh Bagga said on Tuesday.

Speaking to media persons along with Secunderabad Gurudwara Managing Committee president Sardar Kuldeep Singh Saluja, he said Nagar Kirtan programmes will be held from November 19 to 23 in Secunderabad and Afzalgunj areas.

Prabhandhak Committee Gurudwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha of Hyderabad & Gurudwara, Secunderabad Gurudwara will jointly conduct the 557th Gurupurab of Guru Nanak Dev ji Maharaj on November 24 at Exhibition Grounds, Nampally, Hyderabad.

The upcoming programmes include Nagar Kirtan from Secunderabad Gurudwara Sahib on November 19 and proceed via Manohar Talkies, Clock Tower, Natraj Theatre, Patny Circle, Kingsway Circle, Sharda Stores, Monda Market, Guru Shopping Centre, Alpha Hotel and return to Gurudwara Saheb.

A Nagar Kirtan on November 21 in Hyderabad will cover Guru Nanak Marg, Ashok Bazar and proceed via Afzalgunj, Siddiamber Bazar, Moazamjahi Market, Jambagh, Puthlibowli, Central Gurudwara Saheb, Gowliduga and return to Gurudwara Saheb by 9-00 pm. Kirtan Darbar will be on November 23 at Gurudwara Saheb, Secunderabad.

item.title: Nagaraju walks 95 km praying for KCR’s return as CM
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Nagaraju, a resident of Hasanparthi, walked more than 95 km from Warangal's Bhadrakali temple to Yadagirigutta, praying for BRS chief K Chandrashekhar Rao's return as Telangana Chief Minister. He plans to continue his padayatra to KCR's Erravalli farmhouse.
item.content:encoded:
Nalgonda: Deep admiration for BRS chief K Chandrashekhar Rao has prompted Nagaraju to undertake a padayatra from the Bhadrakali temple in Warangal to Yadagirigutta in Yadadri-Bhongir district.

Nagaraju walked more than 95 km to offer prayers for the BRS chief’s return as Chief Minister of Telangana.

A resident of Hasanparthi in Hanamkonda district, Nagaraju began his padayatra last Friday from the Bhadrakali temple in Warangal. He reached Yadagirigutta on Tuesday.

Upon reaching the temple town, Nagaraju offered prayers at Vaikuntha Dwaram. He also climbed the steps leading to the hill temple on his knees.

After having darshan of Lord Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy at Yadagirigutta, Nagaraju plans to continue his padayatra to the farmhouse of BRS chief K Chandrashekhar Rao at Erravalli.

item.title: Indian enrolment in US master’s programmes drops 34.4%
item.dc:creator: Yuvraj Akula
item.description: Indian enrolments in master's programmes at US universities fell 34.4% in 2025-26, according to the Open Doors report. Overall student numbers declined 6.5%, with visa issuance and appointment shortages cited as factors behind the downturn.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: For the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, Indians enrolling in master’s (MS) programmes in US universities plummeted by 34.4 per cent in 2025-26. The enrolments came down massively from 1,77,892 in 2024-25 to 1,16,609 in 2025-26.

Indian undergraduate numbers also dropped by 1.1 per cent to 39,711 as compared to 40,135 in 2024-25. Further, non-degree numbers went down from 1,252 in 2024-25 to 914 in 2025-26.

These numbers were revealed in the Open Doors report, which releases comprehensive information on international students in the United States and on US students studying abroad, released in 2026 report on Monday.

One of the main reasons for the drop in enrolment was attributed to a reduction in the number of visa issuances. As per reports, data from the International Trade Commission found that the US issued about 3,13,138 student visas in August 2025, a month when students join universities, which was a 19.1 per cent drop compared to August 2024.

For Indians, the drop was pegged at 44.5 per cent during the same period.

As per the Open Doors, a reduction of 52.6 per cent in F (academic students) visas, 28.3 per cent in J (exchange visitor programmes) and 21.8 per cent in M (vocational or non-academic study) visa issuance was recorded during 2025-26 as compared to 2024-25.

Speaking to ‘Telangana Today’, IMFS Founder KP Singh said the fall in numbers was not because of a lack of interest among students, but it could be attributed to visa issuance by the US Embassy and Consulates in India.

“Meritorious students from some of the famous colleges in the city applied to US universities, but there were no visa slots available. Given the US visa issue, students joining universities in Germany, UK and Australia have increased considerably. This prompted countries to introduce new norms for international students,” he added.

Overall, Indians in US universities fell by 6.5 per cent to 339,435 in 2025-26, a reduction from 363,019 in 2024-25. However, India remained the largest source of international students for the third consecutive year.

During the pandemic, Indians enrolment in the US fell from 1,93,124 in 2019-2020 to 1,67, 578 in 2020-21, which was a 13.2 per cent decline. But admissions gradually increased, with 1,99,182 Indians enrolling in 2021-22, 2,68,923 in 2022-23, 3,31,602 in 2023-24, and 3,63,019 in 2024-25.

Of the total enrolled in the US in 2025-26, 1,82,201, a majority were on the Optional Practical Training (OPT). In the previous academic year, 1,43,740 Indians were on OPT.

Texas, New York, Massachusetts, California and Illinois were top five States where Indians joined, with overall 64.5 per cent enrolling in public and 35.5 per cent in private universities.

item.title: Revanth Reddy seeks NOC for Sammakka Sarakka barrage from Chattisgarh
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has sought a No Objection Certificate from Chhattisgarh for the Sammakka Sagar barrage. Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai reportedly assured him that the NOC process would be completed expeditiously, according to an official release.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Telangana government has sought a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for the Sammakka Sagar barrage from the Chhattisgarh government.

Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, along with Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy, on Tuesday requested Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai to issue a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for the Sammakka Sagar project.

During the meeting, the Telangana Chief Minister briefed his Chhattisgarh counterpart on increasing water requirements in view of the prevailing drought conditions, especially due to El Nino weather conditions in the State.

The Chief Minister requested permission to store water in the Sammakka Sagar barrage. He also sought cooperation in obtaining other pending clearances for the project.

“Responding to Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s plea, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister assured that the process for issuing the NOC will be completed expeditiously,” a press release from the Chief Minister’s Office said.

Initially, the Telangana government envisaged plans to construct the Sammakka Sagar project at Kantanapalli. It was estimated that 11,408 acres of land would be submerged, affecting 17 Adivasi (tribal) villages and security infrastructure. To minimise submergence, the site for the barrage construction was shifted to Tupakulagudem.

According to a study conducted by IIT Kharagpur, approximately 33 acres of land in Chhattisgarh would be submerged when the water reaches its full reservoir level. Even during heavy flooding, the affected area would not exceed 100 acres.

At the request of Chhattisgarh, the Telangana government had already paid Rs 9.883 crore to IIT Kharagpur for the study in April. The IIT centre submitted its report to the Chhattisgarh government on July 30.

The Sammakka Sagar barrage has been constructed at Tupakulagudem in Mulugu district. At its full reservoir level of +83 metres, it has a storage capacity of 6.94 TMC. The objective of the project is to utilise Godavari river water to meet the irrigation and drinking water needs of drought-affected, backward and tribal regions.

“Telangana government is committed to providing the required funds for land acquisition, compensation, and rehabilitation in Chhattisgarh in accordance with the established regulations,” Revanth Reddy said.

The Chief Minister also explained that the construction of the project had already been completed and requested the issuance of a No Objection Certificate (NOC) in the public interest.

item.title: KTR accuses Congress of failing Telangana, calls manifesto ‘biggest fraud’
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS working president KT Rama Rao accused the Congress government of failing to fulfil poll promises, worsening Telangana's debt and neglecting irrigation, drought relief and welfare schemes. He demanded transparency on investments, jobs and public spending, announcing Deeksha Divas programmes.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Three years after riding to power on a manifesto packed with more than 420 promises, BRS working president KT Rama Rao said the Congress government had little to show beyond publicity campaigns, mounting debt and unfulfilled commitments. He declared that Telangana was not rising but falling under the Congress rule.

In a broadside against Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and his government during an informal interaction with mediapersons on Tuesday, Rama Rao called the Abhaya Hastham manifesto the century’s biggest fraud. He challenged the government to publish a white paper on investments actually realised and jobs created, rather than showcase announcements and summit declarations.

The BRS working president said the government had pushed Telangana into a debt burden of over Rs 4.5 lakh crore, apart from selling or mortgaging valuable public land. He cited the government’s own statistics showing a decline of around 7,000 IT jobs, from 9.46 lakh in 2023 to 9.39 lakh. He questioned how this could be reconciled with claims of investments worth lakhs of crores of rupees. He sought details of new companies established, capital actually deployed and jobs generated since the Congress came to power.

Rama Rao accused the government of damaging Hyderabad’s real estate sector through the wrongful inclusion of large parcels of land under Section 22-A, selective demolitions by HYDRAA and alleged intimidation of builders. Accusing the government of collecting “RR tax” of Rs 200 per square foot, he said uncertainty in the sector was affecting construction workers and affiliated businesses.

On the drought situation, Rama Rao accused the ruling Congress of failing to announce relief despite declaring 365 mandals drought-affected. He sought a relief package, loan rescheduling and measures to secure Central assistance, asking why drought assessment teams had visited Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra but not Telangana. He said available Krishna and Godavari river waters were being allowed to flow downstream while farmers faced irrigation shortages.

Though around 250 TMCft of Krishna river water had flowed downstream, he said the Palamuru and Kalwakurthy pumps were not operated. He questioned why water was being allowed to be taken to Kuppam, around 730 km from the Krishna river basin, while farmers in Palamuru, barely 70 km from the river, were left without it.

The former Minister criticised the Congress government for neglecting the Kaleshwaram project for three years. “Operating the pumps at Kannepalli could have supplied water to almost all districts except Mahabubnagar, besides parts of the erstwhile Nalgonda district and Hyderabad,” he said. He ridiculed Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy’s claim that Hyderabad had no drinking water shortage, citing around 8,000 water-tanker bookings a day and 2.5 lakh bookings in a month.

On the Musi project, he questioned the proposal to bring 10 TMCft of water for the river when the same quantity could meet Hyderabad’s drinking water needs for a year. He also alleged that public hearings were conducted without allowing residents and elected representatives to participate and that tenders were invited without a detailed project report.

He also demanded disclosure of the share of works awarded to BC, SC and ST contractors, recalling the Congress manifesto’s promise to reserve 72 per cent of government contracts for these communities.

Rama Rao questioned the proposed Global Investment Summit, calling it a “Goebbels Summit”, and demanded that the government first disclose the outcome of investment commitments announced at earlier events. He also criticised the expenditure on the Bharat Summit, Miss World pageant and football match featuring Messi in Hyderabad, alleging that public money was being spent on publicity while farmers were denied drought assistance. He described the Bharat Summit as a Congress political event that had yielded no tangible benefit to Telangana.

The BRS leader flayed Revanth Reddy for acting like a bodyguard to the Gandhi family and said leaders of both the Congress and BJP were compromising Telangana’s self-respect before their national leadership. He warned that a future BRS government would rename projects and institutions bearing Congress leaders’ names if the ruling party continued renaming schemes and projects initiated by the previous BRS government. He clarified that the objection was to political names and not projects such as Nagarjuna Sagar.

Responding to Congress allegations that he had encroached on 8,000 acres, Rama Rao challenged the Chief Minister to identify the village, survey numbers and farmers concerned, stating that no evidence had been produced even two months after the allegations were made. He also questioned Revanth Reddy’s repeated claim that BRS chief K Chandrashekhar Rao’s Erravelli residence covered 1,000 acres, pointing out that the Chief Minister himself had referred to 67 acres in the Assembly.

He accused the government of abandoning welfare schemes for weavers, including Bathukamma sarees, Chenetha Mitra and Nethanna ku Bima. He also said the government was using cases, including the phone-tapping investigation, to divert attention from its failures and suppress dissent, citing the arrest of BRS leaders for merely reposting a social media message.

The BRS working president said the party would expose the government’s irrigation record with details of projects, clearances and infrastructure completed during its tenure. He contrasted the completion of the Kaleshwaram project in three years under the previous government with Revanth Reddy taking three years to secure an appointment with the Maharashtra Chief Minister to discuss the Tummidihatti project.

He announced that Deeksha Divas programmes would be held across all constituencies and a public meeting in the erstwhile Karimnagar district on November 29, marking the launch of K Chandrashekhar Rao’s hunger strike for Telangana statehood.

item.title: Metro extension demand gains ground in north-west Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Residents of north-west Hyderabad have urged the State government to extend the Metro from Kukatpally Y-Junction to Gandimaisamma. The proposed corridor would cover several growing residential and industrial areas, including Jeedimetla, to ease traffic congestion and improve connectivity.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Residents of north-west Hyderabad have urged the State government to extend the Hyderabad Metro Rail network from Kukatpally Y-Junction to Gandimaisamma, citing rapid urbanisation, population growth and increasing traffic congestion in the region.

In a representation to Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sai Chandra Malladi proposed extending the Metro corridor through Chintal, IDPL, Shapur Nagar, Gajularamaram, Jeedimetla and Suraram.

The proposal received support from residents of several localities in the north-western part who pointed out that the region had witnessed rapid residential, commercial and industrial growth, with Jeedimetla Industrial Estate emerging as a major employment hub.

“The absence of Metro connectivity has left thousands of residents, employees and students dependent on road transport, resulting in longer commuting hours, traffic congestion and increased pollution,” said P Sai Reddy, a resident who supported the demand.

Another resident, Sri Vani, urged the government to consider the proposal on priority and take steps towards its implementation. “We face severe traffic problems every day and are unable to reach home on time,” she said.

Dr Sai Chandra urged the government to include the proposed corridor in the next phase of Metro expansion and commission a feasibility study, passenger-demand assessment and Detailed Project Report (DPR).

The demand comes amid ongoing efforts to expand Metro connectivity, with the Old City Metro extension planned and the second phase of expansion, including the Miyapur corridor, under consideration.

item.title: CognitiveBotics releases Children’s Day film on small wins
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: CognitiveBotics has released 'Progress is Priceless', a Children's Day film celebrating everyday achievements of neurodivergent children. Produced with Atom Studios, it follows a boy's first independent tooth-brushing attempt, highlighting the patience, effort and sacrifices involved.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: CognitiveBotics, an AI-powered early intervention platform for autism and developmental delays, has released ‘Progress is Priceless’, a Children’s Day brand film celebrating the small, everyday victories of neurodivergent children and the parents who help make them possible.

Produced with Atom Studios, the film follows Kabir, a young neurodivergent boy, and his parents on an ordinary evening at home. At the dining table, Kabir’s father adds up the cost of the things that fill his son’s world: toys, crayons, a play mat and the many everyday objects that support his learning and play.

Elsewhere in the house, Kabir’s mother is settling him for bedtime when he puts down his tablet and runs towards the washroom. Concerned, she hurries to his father, takes his hand and leads him away from the bills. In the washroom, they find Kabir brushing his teeth by himself for the first time. On the tablet he left behind is the tooth-brushing guide he had been watching.

The film is built around an insight many parents of neurodivergent children know well: progress rarely arrives as a dramatic milestone. More often, it involves a child completing a routine, communicating a need or trying something new with a little more confidence.

These moments carry the weight of patience, repetition and quiet effort, much of it happening at home, between therapy sessions and school days. For many families, that effort also involves real financial and emotional strain, from the cost of therapy and learning aids that adds up every month to long nights of worry about what comes next.

Udaya Dintyala, Founder and Chairman of CognitiveBotics, said, “On Children’s Day, we wanted to celebrate the wins that may look small to the world but mean everything to a family.”

item.title: Series of tremors in Kothagudem’s Manuguru area causes panic among locals
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Residents in Manuguru and surrounding areas reported tremors and rumbling sounds on Tuesday, with houses vibrating in locations. The cause and magnitude remain unconfirmed. Locals questioned a possible link to mining blasts, saying the timings did not match scheduled operations.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: A series of tremors reported in the Manuguru area of the district on Tuesday has left local residents anxious and alarmed.
