According to locals, the ground shook near the Malapalli open-cast mine around 11:28 am and again at around 11:40 am. Residents of Shivalingapuram, where underground mines were located, reported hearing loud rumbling sounds three times, while the roofs of their houses vibrated.

People in Manuguru town, Rajupet, Vittalrao Nagar, PK-1, Bapanagunta, Kotha Kondapuram and several surrounding areas also reported experiencing the tremors. However, there was no official confirmation of their cause or magnitude.

Locals said they sometimes experience tremors in the vicinity of open-cast mines due to blasting activities associated with mining. However, the timing of the tremors on Tuesday did not coincide with any scheduled blasting, which usually takes place at 3 pm.

Residents of Rajupet, including Yugandhar, Prabhakar and Rani, told the media that the tremors were felt across multiple locations rather than being confined to a single area. They said this had raised questions about the actual cause of the incident.

Local residents recalled that similar tremors had been felt in the Manuguru area in the past. Enquiries with SCCL officials revealed that there was no Richter scale installed in the area. The incident had not been reported on the National Centre for Seismology website until the time of filing this report.

item.title: Drunk man allegedly kills 73-year-old mother in Medak
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A man allegedly killed his 73-year-old mother, Padmamma, at Shivaipally in Medak district on Monday night. The accused reportedly attacked her with a pestle following an argument while drunk. Police registered a case and took him into custody.
item.content:encoded: Medak: A man, who was reportedly drunk, allegedly killed his elderly mother at Shivaipally on Monday night. The accused, Chilkamukku Papaiah, picked up an argument with his mother, Padmamma (73), while he was drunk. In a fit of rage, he attacked her with a pestle. She died on the spot after sustaining bleeding injuries. The police registered a case and took the accused into custody.

item.title: Citizens urge Telangana government to defer Global Summit amid drought
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Around 400 citizens, environmentalists and academics have urged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to defer the December Global Summit, citing drought and water shortages. They want government resources redirected towards relief, livelihoods and water-supply coordination.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Around 400 citizens, environmentalists, scientists, academics and representatives people’s organisations have urged Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy to cancel or postpone the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026, scheduled to be held on December 7–9, in view of the severe drought and water crisis across the State. Instead, they called for urgent measures to support rural and urban communities, farmers and vulnerable sections.

Some prominent people among the signatories include Prof Shantha Sinha, Prof D Narasimha Reddy, Akunuri Murali, K Babu Rao, Lalita Ramdas, Rukmini Rao, Sagari Ramdas, Bandari Laxmaiah, K Bhanu, Donthi Narasimha Reddy, G Kondal Rao, Kanneganti Ravi, Hyma, Khalida Parveen, Kiran Kumar Vissa, Sr. Lissy Joseph, Maria Tabassum, Mary Dias, M Venkataiah, M Thimma Reddy, Puli Kalpana, Sajaya K, S Seethalakshmi, A Suneetha, Sarah Mathews, Saraswati Kavula, K Satyavati, Ashalatha S, SQ Masood, Venkat Reddy, Uma Shankari, Akhil Surya, Meera Sanghamitra and many others from Telangana.

From across India, EAS Sarma, Prafulla Samantara, Prof Roop Rekha Verma, Soumya Dutta, Indranee Dutta, Gabriele D, Kalyani Menon Sen, Prof Shamshul Islam, CR Neelakandan, Jayasree Saubramanian, Neelam Ahluwalia, Prasad Chacko, Rajesh Ramakrishnan, Rajkumar Sinha, Ramesh Patnaik and many others, are also among the signatories.

In an open letter dated on Tuesday, the citizen activists asked the government to defer the summit until normal conditions return and the drought declaration is withdrawn. They also demanded that all available financial, administrative and human resources be directed towards drought relief and protection of people’s livelihoods.

The signatories pointed out that the government declared drought in 365 mandals across 31 districts through GO Ms No. 3 on October 24. They recalled that the Chief Minister warned of a prolonged drinking water crisis, potentially lasting until July 2027, and urged farmers to avoid water-intensive crops.

They questioned the decision to host a global event expected to draw around 4,000 delegates, with world-class facilities, when the State was facing acute water and power shortages. The summit’s programme includes a Climate Conclave on El Nino, climate change and drought on December 8, they pointed out.

The representatives argued that the event would add to demand for water, electricity and public resources, while diverting administrative attention from drought response. They also questioned the reported deployment of one government officer for each delegate.

The signatories demanded that district and mandal officials, municipal and panchayat staff and other departmental personnel remain fully engaged in drought mitigation, water-supply coordination and grievance redressal, rather than guest facilitation. They also cited the Bharat Summit held in Hyderabad from November 12 to 14, stating that the State cannot afford another large event amid the crisis.

item.title: Watch: Probe ordered into Bellampalli police staff’s farmhouse party
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Ramagundam Police Commissioner Amber Kishore Jha has ordered an inquiry after videos showed around 10 Bellampalli police personnel partying and celebrating a birthday at a farmhouse near Katherla village. The staff allegedly attended without prior permission.
item.content:encoded:
Mancherial: Ramagundam Commissioner of Police Amber Kishore Jha ordered an inquiry into a party and birthday celebrations held by staffers of Bellampalli police station at a farmhouse near Katherla village on Tuesday.

Kishore Jha reportedly expressed anger over the police station staff partying without prior permission. He instructed officials to conduct an inquiry and submit a report. He asked them to verify whether the police had obtained permission from higher officials, whether they were on duty and how many personnel had taken part in the party and celebrations.

Earlier, videos of the incident went viral on social media platforms. In the videos, around 10 policemen and women were seen dancing to songs at a farmhouse on the outskirts of Katherla village on Sunday. They were reportedly consuming liquor and dancing in the rain at the venue.

The police drew flak for partying and celebrating a birthday at the farmhouse after registering their attendance in the station records and without obtaining permission. WhatsApp users criticised the police for neglecting their responsibility to protect law and order and focusing on parties.

item.title: Hostel fire puts spotlight on safety gaps at Telangana medical colleges
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The fire at the Narayanpet medical college hostel has renewed concerns over infrastructure and student safety at newly established government medical colleges in Telangana. Students have flagged overcrowding, poor sanitation and transport problems, while medical associations seek safety audits.
item.content:encoded:
HYDERABAD: The fire accident in the senior girls’ hostel at Government Medical College (GMC), Narayanpet, in the early hours of Monday has once again highlighted the poor infrastructure and safety hazards plaguing newly established medical institutions in districts of Telangana.

According to the members of Telangana Junior Doctors Association (TJUDA), students at the GMC Narayanpet endure severe overcrowding with about 10 members per room, pest infestations including rat bites, and a gruelling 12-km daily commute without dedicated transport.

Similarly, students pursuing medicine at GMC Jagtial have staged protests demanding compliance with National Medical Commission (NMC) standards due to a lack of proper lecture halls and permanent hostel facilities. Also, the newly established teaching hospital at Mulugu continues to struggle with acute space shortages that force incoming batches to sleep on administrative floors alongside sanitation issues.

The MBBS students at GMC Maheshwaram face severe logistical strains, unlit approach roads without perimeter walls, and a punishing 40-kilometre daily commute to their teaching hospital.

In response to the growing criticism, the Director of Medical Education (DME), Dr N Vani, stated that all these institutions are functioning with adequate facilities, that furniture has been supplied, and that permanent buildings at Mulugu and Jagtial are nearing completion.

However, student bodies and medical associations continue to urge the health department, KNRUHS, and the NMC to step in immediately, conduct safety audits, and expedite permanent campus completions before student safety is further compromised.

item.title: BRS tears up Congress manifesto, calls it “Bhasmasura Hastham”
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS leaders tore up copies of the Congress's Abhaya Hastham manifesto at Telangana Bhavan, accusing the ruling party of failing to fulfil its poll promises. Jagadish Reddy, V Srinivas Goud and Balka Suman criticised the government.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS leaders tore up copies of the Congress party’s “Abhaya Hastham” election manifesto and threw them into a dustbin at Telangana Bhavan on Tuesday, accusing the ruling party of betraying people by failing to fulfil its poll promises.

Marking three years since the release of the manifesto on November 17, 2023, former Minister G Jagadish Reddy said the Congress had made more than 420 promises, guarantees and declarations but failed to honour them after coming to power. “Abhaya Hastham has turned into Bhasmasura Hastham (suicidal),” he said. He added that the government had failed to ensure even irrigation and drinking water for the people.

He said farmers, youth, BCs, SCs, STs, minorities, students and employees had all been deceived. He pointed out that the Congress had promised loan waivers, enhanced pensions, one tola of gold, scooters for college-going girls and benefits for auto drivers, besides making assurances through affidavits and bond papers. “But people’s aspirations were turned into disappointment and the manifesto is nothing less than a waste paper,” he said.

Former Minister V Srinivas Goud accused the Congress of misleading people with assurances that all promises would be implemented within 100 days. He questioned Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s silence on the commitments made to Telangana. Referring to Rahul Gandhi’s visit to Ashok Nagar during the Assembly elections, he asked why the Congress leader had avoided a similar interaction with unemployed youth during his recent Hyderabad visit.

He said employees and teachers protesting for the abolition of the CPS were being threatened. He also alleged that Telangana’s share of river waters was being diverted to Andhra Pradesh under the Congress government.

Former MLA Balka Suman said the government was compelled to announce relief measures only when the BRS raised the issues. He asserted that the party would continue fighting for people’s issues and compel the government to implement its promises. He said the party would take the manifesto issue to villages and hold the Congress accountable for its promises.

Former MLAs Bhaskar Rao, Bhupal Reddy, Methuku Anand and Mutthireddy Yadagiri Reddy, among others, were also present.

item.title: Excise Task Force busts fake premium liquor racket in Shamshabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Excise Task Force arrested two persons in Shamshabad for allegedly filling cheap liquor into empty premium whisky bottles and selling it at higher prices. Officials seized 10 filled bottles and more than 30 empty bottles during a raid.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Prohibition and Excise Department Task Force on Tuesday caught two persons for allegedly selling cheap liquor after filling it into bottles of premium whisky brands during a raid at Shamshabad. The officials seized 10 bottles containing the adulterated liquor and more than 30 empty premium liquor bottles during the raid.

According to Excise Superintendent Vijaya Bhaskar Goud, the prime suspect, Vangali Ashok (43), had earlier worked at a distillery but quit the job about six months ago and took up work as a cab driver. He allegedly used his house to mix cheap liquor with the intention of passing it off as premium brands and selling it at higher prices.

“Ashok allegedly procured empty premium liquor bottles from a scrap shop owned by Mohammed Yaqoob Pasha (29). After cleaning the bottles and removing their caps, he filled them with Down Ten liquor, which costs around Rs 560 a bottle, and sold them as expensive whisky brands including Johnnie Walker, Dewar’s and 100 Pipers,” said Bhaskar Goud.

On a tip-off, a team raided Ashok’s house located in the Sathamrai area of Shamshabad, and seized the liquor bottles and other material. The officials said they were examining the buyers’ role and would take further action. Ashok and Yaqoob Pasha were arrested. Further investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Hyderabad: Pan shop worker held with 21 kg of marijuana in Balapur
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: The Task Force and Balapur police arrested a 20-year-old man and seized 21 kg of marijuana, worth Rs 10.5 lakh, from his house. Police said two alleged suppliers, one from Odisha and another from Hyderabad, are absconding.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Task Force (Charminar) and local police arrested a drug peddler and seized 21 kgs of marijuana, worth Rs 10.5 lakh, from his house in Balapur on Tuesday.

Police said the suspect, Ahmed Emad Mohammed alias Ahmed (20), who worked at a pan shop in Shaheen Nagar, allegedly procured the contraband from a supplier named Samuel from Berhampur in Odisha.

Further, on the instructions of Ibrahim Bin Saleem Baamar alias Ibrahim Baamar, he brought the consignment to Hyderabad and stored it at his residence for further sale to consumers in his contacts.

Both Ibrahim and Samuel are currently absconding. The Balapur police booked a case under the NDPS Act and are investigating.

item.title: The Balcony Makeover Trend Bringing Cosy Corners to Hyderabad Homes
item.dc:creator: Ruchi Rai Agarwal
item.description: Residents in apartment complexes are increasingly transforming balconies into personalised, functional spaces using artificial grass, furniture, lighting, swings and décor. Interior designers say balconies should be treated as extensions of home interiors, helping create relaxing retreats for reading, yoga, coffee breaks and leisure activities.
item.content:encoded:
In apartment living, balconies are often among the most underutilised spaces in a home. But that is slowly changing, with residents finding creative ways to turn these little extensions into cosy corners where they can unwind, enjoy their morning coffee or simply take a break from their daily routines. From artificial grass flooring and comfortable seating to hanging swings, decorative lights and wall accessories, balconies are getting personalised makeovers that go beyond simply adding a few plants.

The idea is to make the most of the available space and create a spot that feels like a little escape within the home. Some homeowners are opting for artificial grass or wooden deck flooring to give their balconies a garden-like appearance, while others are adding compact chairs, coffee tables, floor cushions or hanging swings to make the space more inviting. Wall planters, decorative mirrors, outdoor artwork and warm fairy lights are also being used to add character without taking up too much floor space.

Interior designers believe that balconies should be treated as an extension of the home’s interiors rather than just functional areas. “A balcony can become a beautiful personal retreat with thoughtful use of textures, lighting and furniture. Even a small space can be transformed with artificial grass, a comfortable chair, a swing or some interesting wall decor. The key is to make it functional without overcrowding it,” said Mansa, an interior designer based in Hyderabad.

For residents who have given their balconies a makeover, these spaces are becoming more than just decorative corners. Some use them for morning yoga sessions, while others turn them into reading books or simply as a quiet place to unwind after a long day. The purpose is to create a space that suits their lifestyle and offers a change of setting without having to step outside.

“I wanted a place where I could sit with my coffee, read or just relax after work. Adding a swing, a few plants and some lights completely changed how I use my balcony. It has become my favourite spot at home,” said Rachna, a Hyderabad resident.

Whether it is a green garden, a cosy reading corner or a small outdoor lounge, balconies are increasingly becoming personal spaces that reflect the homeowner’s style. With a little creativity and thoughtful planning, even the smallest balcony can be transformed into one of the most loved corners of a home.

item.title: Deepfake blackmail case: Narsingi police arrest seventh accused
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Narsingi police have arrested a seventh person in the case involving alleged blackmail of MLC Mirza Rahmat Baig using morphed photographs and deepfake videos. The accused allegedly demanded Rs 5 crore to prevent the circulation of the content.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The Narsingi police have arrested another person in connection with the circulation of morphed photographs and deepfake videos of MLC Mirza Rahmat Baig.

The arrested suspect has been identified as Salman, president of HYC, who was arrested on the city outskirts.

With this arrest, the number of persons held in the case has increased to seven. Six persons were earlier arrested by Narsingi police on November 6, while several others are still absconding.

According to police, the suspects allegedly threatened the MLC using morphed photographs and deepfake videos and demanded Rs 5 crore to avoid circulating the content. They had reportedly collected Rs 5 lakh from him. Police recovered Rs 4.70 lakh in cash during the earlier arrests.

Rahmat Baig lodged a complaint alleging that the accused blackmailed him, extorted money and damaged his reputation by creating and circulating fake videos. Further investigation is underway to identify and nab the remaining suspects.

item.title: Samakalpa presents second edition of classical dance festival Pravritti in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Samakalpa presented the second edition of Pravritti at CCRT, Hyderabad, celebrating four Indian classical dance forms — Odissi, Kuchipudi, Kathak and Bharatanatyam. The programme featured established performers and senior disciples of noted gurus.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: The second edition of ‘Pravritti’, a celebration of India’s rich classical dance traditions, was presented by Samakalpa at the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT), Hyderabad.

Founded by Arpita Pany and Sonali Mohanty, Samakalpa is dedicated to nurturing, preserving and promoting Indian classical dance through education, performance and artistic exploration. Following the encouraging response to its inaugural edition, Pravritti returned with an evening celebrating four major Indian classical dance traditions – Odissi, Kuchipudi, Kathak and Bharatanatyam.

The evening’s presentations included Arpita Pany, Debashree Patnaik, Somya Das and Sonali Mohanty, representing Samakalpa (Odissi); Lasyakalpa Ensemble, featuring Vaishnavi PB and Kiranmayee Madupu, disciples of Guru Shri D S V Sastry (Kuchipudi); Manya, Kundanika and Yeshaswini, senior disciples of Srivalli Rao (Kathak); and Pramod Reddy and Abhinetri Ensemble (Bharatanatyam).

Dr Anupama Kylash, an accomplished Kuchipudi and Vilasini Natyam exponent, scholar and researcher; Preeti Mohapatra, an eminent Odissi dancer, teacher and founder of Nrityashala; Guru Sanjay Kumar Joshi, a Kathak exponent; Guru D S V Sastry, a distinguished Kuchipudi exponent, vocalist, and choreographer, were present.

item.title: Blue Blocks Opens Admissions for 2026–27 and 2027–28, with Montessori Education from 15 Months to 16 years
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Founded in 2009, Blue Blocks operates campuses in Gachibowli and Tellapur, offering Montessori education from 15 months to 16 years, through Grade 10 and Cambridge IGCSE. For parents considering a playgroup in Hyderabad, the school begins with a conversation about the child, not just their age.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad:Even before they speak in full sentences, some toddlers notice when an adult struggles to retrieve an object and offer help. That emerging wish to participate is among the things Blue Blocks Montessori School invites parents to notice as it accepts applications for the 2026–27 and 2027–28 academic years.

Founded in 2009, Blue Blocks operates campuses in Gachibowli and Tellapur, offering Montessori education from 15 months to 16 years, through Grade 10 and Cambridge IGCSE. For parents considering a playgroup in Hyderabad, the school begins with a conversation about the child, not just their age.

“When parents ask whether their child is ready for school, I ask them to tell me about their child at home. What do they enjoy? What are they trying to do on their own? How do they respond to difficulties? These little things tell us so much. We are not looking for a child who is already independent. We want to understand the child and offer an environment that supports their next stage of development,” says Pavan Goyal, founder of Blue Blocks.

Readiness Begins with Understanding the Child

In a 2006 study published in Science, psychologists Felix Warneken and Michael Tomasello presented 24 children aged 18 months with situations in which an adult had difficulty completing a task. In one experiment, the adult dropped an object and struggled to retrieve it. The children were more likely to help when the adult appeared to need assistance than when an object was deliberately discarded. Twenty-two of the 24 children helped in at least one situation.

The study did not investigate school readiness or Montessori education. It does, however, invite adults to notice something significant: a young child’s contribution may begin well before they can explain it in words.

Blue Blocks’ Toddler Community in Gachibowli welcomes children from around 15 months, subject to age eligibility and individual readiness. In Montessori terminology, this early environment is an Infant Community or Toddler Community, often called a Montessori playgroup in Hyderabad by families. Adults observe how children move, communicate, explore and seek reassurance. A child who watches before joining an activity is not necessarily less ready than one who immediately reaches for a material. Neither response is a pass-or-fail test.

Why Parents Begin with an Admission Workshop

The admissions process begins with an enquiry and a Saturday Admission Workshop. Parents explore the prepared environment, handle Montessori materials and discuss how movement, language and independence are supported in daily practice. It gives families an opportunity to understand the school’s expectations before they apply.

“I don’t want parents to choose Blue Blocks simply because they liked the campus or heard good things about us. I want them to understand how their child will spend the day, why we do things differently and what children are truly capable of. That’s why we spend time with parents before admission. I want every parent to leave our workshop understanding their child better than when they walked in,” says Goyal.

The workshop is followed by age-appropriate application steps and conversations with the admissions team and founder. For children aged 2 years 9 months and above, the published process specifies observation in the environment before submission of the admission form. Families enquiring for younger toddlers can confirm the steps that apply to their child. The school explains the process on its playgroup admission in Hyderabad page.

Inside a two-hour Toddler Community session

Blue Blocks offers two Gachibowli sessions: 9.00–11.00 am and 11.15 am–1.15 pm. Low shelves, child-sized tools and familiar places for materials give children opportunities to make suitable choices and participate in looking after their environment.

A morning may include movement, language with real objects and pictures, sensorial exploration, caring for plants, wiping a table, music, outdoor time and preparing a shared snack. Children may repeat a familiar activity rather than immediately move to something new. The guide’s role includes observing what holds a child’s attention and offering assistance when it is needed.

That observation can be systematic. In a three-session Blue Blocks Micro Research Institute classroom dataset involving six young children, researchers recorded the length of engagement with individual materials and whether work was put away independently, left unfinished or completed with an adult prompt. These descriptive records do not establish a causal effect of Montessori education. They show the sort of detail adults can attend to beyond whether a child finished an activity.

The Toddler Community is guided by educators with individual AMI Assistants to Infancy (0–3) diplomas, an age-specific qualification of the Association Montessori Internationale. An educator’s AMI diploma should not be confused with institutional AMI school accreditation.

Settling In Is About Building Trust

For some families, playgroup is the child’s first regular separation from home. Blue Blocks follows a gradual settling-in process, allowing shorter initial attendance and support from a parent or familiar caregiver as appropriate. Guides and families work together as the child becomes familiar with the space and the adults receiving them.

“For many parents, this is the first time they are leaving their little child with someone outside the family. We understand how emotional that can be for both. Some children settle quickly, while others need more time. We never expect every child to adjust in the same way. What matters is that the child feels safe, builds trust with the guide and gradually looks forward to coming to school. We give that relationship the time it needs,” says Munira Hussain Kagalwalla, co-founder of Blue Blocks.

Parent–guide conversations and educational workshops continue after admission, giving families opportunities to share observations and ask questions as their child’s needs change.

A Montessori Journey Across Two Hyderabad Campuses

The Gachibowli campus, opposite DLF, serves the Toddler Community and Blue Blocks’ Self-Interpretive Environment, approximately ages 2½–6. In general Montessori terminology, that next stage corresponds to the Primary Environment or Children’s House, traditionally ages 3–6.

At Tellapur, the school offers early-years provision, Elementary (Grades 1–6) and the Erdkinder adolescent programme (Grades 7–10). The later academic pathway incorporates Cambridge Lower Secondary and IGCSE. Transitions are considered with the child and family; they are not determined by birthdays alone.

For families considering playgroup admission in Gachibowli, the relevant first visit is usually the early-years campus. Parents looking for a playgroup near Gachibowli can check the location and programme before enquiring about places, fees and workshop dates.

A First School Decision Begins with Trust

For a parent, choosing a first school means inviting unfamiliar adults into a very personal part of family life. A thoughtful admissions process should help that trust grow from understanding rather than reputation alone. What matters just as much is how the adults will come to know that child: what interests them, when they need help and what makes them feel secure. For parents, a meaningful first school experience begins with the confidence that this understanding will guide the care their child receives.

Quick Facts for Parents

Admissions at a Glance

  • Educational continuity: Montessori education from 15 months to 16 years.
  • Admissions: Applications for 2026–27 and 2027–28, with enquiries accepted throughout the year.
  • First step: Parent enquiry followed by a Saturday Admission Workshop.
  • Enquiries: School admissions at Blue Blocks.

Gachibowli Campus

  • Toddler Community (Playgroup): From 15 months, with independent walking and developmental readiness considered, to approximately 2½ years.
  • Toddler timings:00–11.00 am or 11.15 am–1.15 pm.
  • Self-Interpretive Environment (Nursery, PP1, PP2): Approximately 2½–6 years.
  • Primary timings:30 am–1.30 pm.
  • Location: Opposite DLF, Gachibowli, Hyderabad.

Tellapur Campus

  • Self-Interpretive Environment (Nursery, PP1, PP2): Approximately 2½–6 years.
  • Primary timings:00 am–2.00 pm.
  • Elementary: Grades 1–6.
  • Erdkinder (Adolescent Programme): Grades 7–10, with Cambridge Lower Secondary and IGCSE.
  • Elementary and Erdkinder timings:30 am–3.30 pm.
  • Location:Tellapur, Hyderabad.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What are the playgroup admission procedures in Hyderabad?

At Blue Blocks, the process starts with an enquiry and a Saturday Admission Workshop, followed by age-appropriate application steps and family conversations. The published procedure specifies a child observation for children aged 2 years 9 months and above. Requirements and availability should be confirmed for the individual child.

2. What makes Blue Blocks playgroup unique compared to other schools?

Blue Blocks offers a Montessori Toddler Community with age-specific AMI-qualified guides, two-hour sessions, a parent workshop and gradual settling-in. Families can examine these features directly when deciding whether the environment suits their child’s needs.

3. Must my child be toilet trained or comfortable separating before joining?

No fixed level of independence is expected of every child. Toilet learning and self-care are supported in the Toddler Community, while settling-in is planned gradually. Parents should discuss their child’s care needs and the support available with the admissions team.

4. Can children continue Montessori education beyond playgroup at Blue Blocks?

Yes. Blue Blocks offers education from approximately 15 months to 16 years. Children may progress through the Self-Interpretive, Elementary and Erdkinder environments, with Cambridge studies in the later grades. Families should confirm current programme availability and transition arrangements directly with the school.

item.title: Prashant Bajaj exits Anil Sharma’s Arjun Naga over creative differences
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Actor Prashant Bajaj has reportedly stepped back from filmmaker Anil Sharma’s upcoming project Arjun Naga, citing creative differences and concerns over on-set arrangements and prior commitments. He says a significant role alone is not enough to secure his participation.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Actor Prashant Bajaj has reportedly decided to step back from filmmaker Anil Sharma’s upcoming project, Arjun Naga, citing creative differences and concerns over the film’s on-set arrangements and commitments.

While the prospect of being part of a significant role may have initially generated excitement, Bajaj’s decision highlights the importance of clarity, professionalism and a shared creative vision when an actor commits to a project.

Speaking about his decision, Bajaj said, “Being told that a role is big is not enough. For me, the creative vision, the working environment and the commitments made before coming on board are equally important. Unfortunately, the setup was not as per the commitments discussed, and there were creative differences. I felt it was better to step back rather than continue in a situation that did not align with my expectations.”

For Bajaj, the decision appears to reflect a professional choice to prioritise the right working environment and creative alignment over the size of a role. His stance also highlights the importance of transparency, mutual understanding and honouring commitments between actors and filmmakers.

As the project moves forward, Bajaj’s decision marks a change in his association with Arjun Naga.

item.title: 5 Things That Have Quietly Become Expensive
item.dc:creator: Ruchi Rai Agarwal
item.description: Rising costs in Hyderabad are making everyday leisure and household activities more expensive. From coffee dates and food deliveries to movie outings, dining out and grocery shopping, residents are increasingly feeling the impact of higher spending on their monthly budgets.
item.content:encoded:
Living in Hyderabad comes with its own little pleasures, whether it is grabbing coffee with friends, ordering in after a long day, catching the latest movie or stepping out for a weekend outing. But somewhere along the way, these simple plans have started costing a lot more than they used to. What once felt like an affordable treat can now leave you thinking twice before spending. Here are five everyday things that seem to be getting increasingly expensive in Hyderabad.

A Casual Coffee Date

Remember when stepping out for coffee meant spending a few hundred rupees? With speciality coffee, elaborate beverages and trendy cafes becoming popular, a simple coffee date can now turn into a rather expensive outing. Add a dessert or a quick bite, and the bill climbs even higher.

Ordering Food on a Lazy Day

Ordering your favourite meal after a long day sounds convenient, until you reach the payment page. Between restaurant prices, delivery fees, packaging charges and other additional costs, even a regular food order can feel surprisingly expensive.

A Weekend at the Movies

A movie plan is no longer just about buying two tickets. Premium screens, weekend pricing, popcorn, beverages and parking can make a cinema outing quite a splurge. What was once an easy weekend plan now requires a little budgeting.

Spending an Evening at a Cafe or Restaurant

Going out with friends has become an experience in itself, with beautifully designed spaces, elaborate menus and speciality dining concepts. However, spending a couple of hours at a popular restaurant or cafe can cost considerably more than expected.

A Quick Grocery Run

One of the most noticeable expenses is the monthly grocery bill. A quick trip to the supermarket for milk, snacks, fruits and household essentials can easily turn into a much bigger purchase. Individually, the price differences may seem small, but they become more noticeable when added to the monthly budget.

item.title: Model School teachers protest over salary payments in Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.category: Model School Teachers’ Joint Action Committee
item.description: Model School teachers from 197 schools staged a protest at the Directorate of School Education in Hyderabad, demanding salary payments under the 010 head of account and seeking resolution of pending service and welfare benefits, including DA arrears, promotions, transfers, and pension-related issues.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Tension prevailed at the Directorate of School Education as a large number of Model School teachers staged a huge protest here on Tuesday, demanding that the State government pay their salaries under the 010 head of account.

As per the Model School Teachers’ Joint Action Committee’s call, staff from 197 Model Schools staged a sit-in protest, while slogans such as ‘we want justice’ filled the air. Some teachers also sang songs highlighting their demands. They wanted compassionate appointments to be taken up and families of deceased teachers be provided gratuity and family pension benefits.

Notional benefits for trained graduate teachers, release of arrears relating to five pending DA installments, promotions and transfers of eligible teachers, and junior lecturer pay scales to postgraduate teachers were other demands raised by the Model Schools staff.

item.title: IPL 2027: Harshal Patel joins Gujarat Titans in trade from Sunrisers Hyderabad
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Harshal Patel has joined Gujarat Titans following a trade from Sunrisers Hyderabad. The two-time Purple Cap winner brings vast IPL experience, having taken 151 wickets in 124 matches and finished as the tournament's leading wicket-taker in 2021 and 2024.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Two-time Purple Cap winner Harshal Patel will represent Gujarat Titans (GT) after a successful trade from Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH). Patel, who was acquired for Rs 8 crore by SRH at the TATA IPL 2025 Auction, will move to GT for Rs 4 crore.

Known for his variations and tactical nous, the wily pacer brings considerable experience, having played 124 matches and claimed 151 wickets across four franchises since making his IPL debut in 2012.

A consistent performer over the years, the seasoned campaigner was the leading wicket-taker in the 2021 and 2024 editions of the tournament, representing Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) and Punjab Kings (PBKS), respectively.

item.title: NEET-PG aspirants squeezed as KNRUHS hikes university fees by over 300 percent
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Telangana medical aspirants face financial hardship after KNRUHS increased annual university fees for postgraduate medical seats by over 300 percent. Following protests and legal intervention, the High Court permitted students to pay a reduced fee pending further orders
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: For thousands of young doctors in Telangana who spent years preparing to crack the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduate courses (NEET-PG), the recent four-fold increase in the university administrative fees by Kaloji Narayana Rao University of Health Sciences (KNRUHS) has come as a shock and a formidable financial barrier.

While baseline annual tuition fees for PG medical courses remained untouched under official government orders, the university’s sudden tinkering with institutional, registration, and processing fees caught aspirants completely off guard.

A few weeks ago, KNRUHS sharply revised its university fee for Category B postgraduate medical seats from Rs 50,000 to Rs 2,00,000 annually, a huge 300 percent hike that sent immediate shockwaves through middle class families. As if this was not enough, the KNRUHS revised the university fee for Category-C seats from Rs. 70, 000 to Rs 3, 00, 000 (NRI Quota).

For aspirants already bracing for the rigorous financial demands of postgraduate specialization, the cash crunch forced many to run from pillar to post just to meet admission deadlines.

Usually, medical admissions operate under rigid timelines and when a university increases administrative and processing dues just a few days before the start of the counselling, it catches the rank holders and their parents off-guard.

For middle-class families who have already stretched their finances to support years of MBBS education, these sudden hikes leave very few options other than liquidating savings or taking on high-interest commercial loans.

“We were totally caught unaware by the rise in university fees. It is a genuine burden for young doctors hailing from middle-class families. We took up this issue with all the senior health officials. We have received judicial help (pro-bono) from advocates, who have represented our concerns in the High Court,” says senior member of Healthcare Reforms Doctors Association (HRDA), Dr Kartik Nagula.

Through dedicated efforts, the postgraduate medical aspirants along with senior advocates reportedly managed to get High Court’s directive, permitting students to pay only a reduced fraction of the contested university fee until further orders are passed, providing vital breathing room for the aspirants.

“It is very common for university fees for MBBS and medical postgraduate seats to be hiked every other year. However, hiking by over 300 percent is shocking. We urged the authorities to give some breathing space,” the aspirants said.

item.title: 27 crew members of damaged vessel rescued off Odisha coast
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: A major maritime disaster was averted off Odisha after Paradip Port Authority and the Indian Coast Guard rescued 27 crew members aboard distressed vessel MV Vishva Uday. The vessel suffered water ingress and propeller shaft failure but was safely towed and anchored
item.content:encoded:
Paradip: A major maritime disaster was averted on Tuesday after the Paradip Port Authority (PPA) and the Indian Coast Guard rescued 27 crew members of a distressed vessel off the Odisha coast, officials said.

The joint operation was initiated following an urgent communication received from the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), which reported that the vessel was experiencing water ingress and a propeller shaft breakdown, they said.

The vessel, MV Vishva Uday, was successfully towed to safety and anchored off the outer port limits on Tuesday morning, the officials said.

“Maritime Rescue: Successful Salvage Operation by Paradip Port Authority! Responding swiftly to an urgent request from SCI Limited, Paradip Port Authority (PPA) launched a coordinated rescue operation for MV Vishva Uday, carrying 27 crew members, after the vessel reported water ingress and a propeller shaft breakdown approximately 50 nautical miles off Paradip Port,” the PPA said in a post on X.

Official sources said the vessel was travelling from West Bengal’s Haldia Port to Mozambique in East Africa when its propeller shaft reportedly became dysfunctional, leaving it stranded in the middle of the sea. Water began entering the vessel, raising fears that it could sink.

In a social media post, the Indian Coast Guard said: “In a swift Search and Rescue operation coordinated by Indian Coast Guard District Headquarters Paradip, ICGS Amulya and ICGS Vijaya were deployed to assist MV Vishva Uday during the intervening night of Nov 15-16, after the vessel reported severe engine room flooding caused by a damaged tail shaft off Paradip.” “Battling adverse sea conditions, a specialist Damage Control Team boarded the distressed vessel, rigged submersible pumps, and successfully arrested the water ingress,” it added.

item.title: 17-year-old tribal girl gang-raped on way to home in Bengal’s Purulia; six held
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.category: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
item.description: A minor tribal girl was allegedly gang-raped by a group of men, including her boyfriend, while returning home after watching a Jatra performance in West Bengal's Purulia district. Six accused have been arrested
item.content:encoded:
Kolkata: A 17-year-old tribal girl was allegedly gang-raped by a group of men, including her boyfriend, while returning home after watching a Jatra performance in West Bengal’s Purulia district, police said on Tuesday.

Six accused have been arrested in connection with the incident. The incident took place on Monday in the Kashipur police station area of Purulia district. The arrested accused will be produced before the Raghunathpur sub-divisional court later in the day, where police are expected to seek their custody for further interrogation.

According to the police, the Jatra performance continued till Monday morning. The girl was reportedly returning home after watching the folk theatre performance when her boyfriend called her to an isolated place. Three people, including the boyfriend, allegedly raped her, while others sexually assaulted her and facilitated the crime. The girl somehow managed to escape and approached the organisers of the Jatra committee to report the incident.

The organisers subsequently informed her family. Her father arrived at the spot and took her home before lodging a complaint of gang-rape at the Kashipur police station. The survivor underwent a medical examination later on Monday. Acting on the complaint lodged by her family, police arrested six people during the night.

“Based on the family’s complaint, a case of gang-rape has been registered. Relevant provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, have also been invoked. Six accused have already been arrested and will be produced before the Raghunathpur sub-divisional court today,” a senior Purulia district police officer said.

The arrested have been identified as Sudeep Mandi, Rajesh Mandi, Sagun Murmu, Meghnath Mandi, Sushant Mandi and Binand Soren. The police are investigating the involvement of other persons in the alleged crime and are questioning the accused to establish the sequence of events.

The incident has once again brought sexual violence against women and minors in West Bengal into focus. In recent months, accused persons in three separate rape cases in the state were killed in police encounters. However, such incidents continue to be reported from different parts of the state.

item.title: Sabarimala witnesses heavy rush as Mandala pilgrimage season begins
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple opened at 3 am on Tuesday, marking the start of the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season. Authorities have arranged special booking facilities, medical services, sanitation and crowd management measures to accommodate thousands of devotees
item.content:encoded:
Sabarimala: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple opened at 3 am on Tuesday, marking the beginning of the two-month-long annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season, with thousands of devotees arriving at the hill shrine chanting ‘Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa’.

The newly appointed Melsanthi (chief priest), Areekkara Subramanian Sankaran Namboothiri, opened the sanctum for devotees on the first day of the Malayalam month of Vrischikam. The Malikappuram temple also opened at the same time, with its newly appointed Melsanthi, A Damodaran Namboothiri, beginning the rituals there.

The temples had opened on Monday evening as part of the preparatory ceremonies, during which the outgoing chief priests handed over charge to their successors. The new Melsanthis assumed office after the traditional consecration ceremonies performed by Tantri Kandaru Brahmadathan.

State Devaswom and Health Minister K Muraleedharan witnessed the Nirmalya Darshan at the Ayyappa temple at 3 am.

With a large number of devotees expected during the opening days, the authorities have put in place arrangements to regulate the flow of pilgrims, particularly through the 18 holy steps.

Spot-booking facilities have been arranged at Nilakkal, the main base camp, Erumeli and Sathram near Vandiperiyar.

No spot-booking facility has been provided at Pamba, as officials fear that it could lead to overcrowding at the riverside pilgrim centre. Devotees without virtual queue bookings can obtain tokens at the designated centres before proceeding to the shrine.

Reviewing the arrangements at Sabarimala on Tuesday morning, Muraleedharan said all necessary measures had been taken to ensure a smooth and hassle-free pilgrimage.

“At present, 60,000 devotees are allowed to book through the virtual queue system and another 14,000 through spot booking every day. Steps will be taken to increase the booking limits, with the permission of the court, if the number of pilgrims rises in the coming days,” he said.

The minister said Rs 3.36 crore had been allocated to local self-government institutions for managing Sabarimala pilgrim centres (edathavalams), following the special initiative of Chief Minister VD Satheesan.

He said adequate stocks of appam and aravana prasadam had been ensured and arrangements were in place to increase production according to demand. Sanitation workers had been deployed at all locations, with officials assigned sector-wise responsibilities to ensure regular waste removal.

Under the Health Department’s ‘Swasthyam Saranam’ project, five allopathic hospitals and 24 emergency medical centres have been set up along the Pamba-Sannidhanam route.

The services of 35 doctors, including five cardiologists, have been arranged, besides trained nursing staff and adequate stocks of medicines.

Ayurveda and homoeopathy facilities will also function round the clock, with the services of four therapists. Fifteen ambulances have been stationed at Pamba and another 10 at Nilakkal.

Meanwhile, Devaswom Board president K Jayakumar urged devotees not to leave their clothes in the Pamba river after taking a bath, warning that the practice caused pollution. More volunteers would be deployed to remove clothes from the river, and officials had been asked to clear waste at least once every three hours.

CCTV cameras will also be installed at locations where annadanam (free food distribution) is held, he said.

In a message marking the beginning of the pilgrimage season, CM Satheesan extended his greetings to devotees and wished them a spiritually fulfilling journey.

“May the golden rays of the Vrischika dawn fill every heart with the divine light of devotion to Lord Ayyappa,” he said in a social media post.

Referring to the devotional chants echoing in homes and along the pilgrimage routes, Satheesan said he hoped the prayers of every devotee undertaking the journey to Sabarimala would be fulfilled.

“May this Mandala season, reverberating with chants of ‘Saranam Ayyappa’, bring everyone spiritual fulfilment and the blessed experience of Lord Ayyappa’s darshan,” he said.

The Chief Minister also assured devotees that “Keralam stands with you”.

item.title: Government services hit as employees stage protest for OPS restoration
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Government services across Telangana were affected as employees took mass leave and staged a protest at Hyderabad's Indira Park, demanding the scrapping of the Contributory Pension Scheme and restoration of the Old Pension System, a key Congress poll promise.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: Services at many government offices were affected on Tuesday after employees availed mass leave pressing for their demand of abolishing the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) and restoring the Old Pension System (OPS).

The employees staged a protest at Indira Park. This was done undeterred by the Congress government’s instructions that stern action would be initiated against employees participating in the protest and availing leave.

The employees are demanding that the Congress government implement its poll promise of abolishing the CPS and restoring OPS.

“It has been nearly three years since the Congress government came to power in the State. Yet, the promise to restore OPS has not been fulfilled,” an employee said at Indira Park.

Holding placards, the employees, including women, have turned up in large numbers to participate in the protest.

This is not the first instance of employees staging protests. On August 23 this year, the employees had assembled at LB Stadium to press for their demand.

Nearly 1.5 lakh employees are reported to have availed casual leave across the State. Many government offices are sporting a deserted look with employees participating in the protest, including in the districts.

“We have been demanding the government to initiate measures for restoring the OPS. But, our appeals have not been considered so far. After this protest, we will chalk out our future course of action plan,” another employee said at the protest.

item.title: Sohum Shah on Jesper Kyd’s return to ‘Tumbbad 2’: ‘We wanted to retain that creative connection’
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Composer Jesper Kyd is returning to score 'Tumbbad 2', reuniting with actor-producer Sohum Shah and director Adesh Prasad. The sequel aims to retain the original film's distinctive musical identity and is scheduled for a worldwide theatrical release on December 3, 2027
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Actor and producer Sohum Shah has opened up about having composer Jesper Kyd return to the world of ‘Tumbbad’ for its sequel, ‘Tumbbad 2.’

Reflecting on the role music played in shaping the identity of the original film, Sohum said Jesper’s distinctive sound elevated its atmosphere and storytelling. He added that bringing the composer back was important to retain their creative connection while taking the world of ‘Tumbbad’ forward.

Speaking about welcoming Jesper back to the franchise, Sohum said, “The music of Tumbbad was as much a part of its identity as its visual world. Jesper brought a very distinctive sound to the film, one that elevated its atmosphere and storytelling. Having him return for Tumbbad 2 was important to us because we wanted to retain that creative connection while taking the world forward. I’m delighted to welcome him back, and excited for audiences to experience what we are creating together this time.”

Expressing his excitement about returning to the franchise, Jesper shared, “I’m very excited to be returning to score Tumbbad 2 and teaming up with director Adesh Prasad and actor-producer Sohum Shah for another ambitious journey into the world of Tumbbad. Adesh was the one who first approached me for Tumbbad, and I remember watching an early version of the film and thinking it was one of the coolest worlds I had ever seen. I’m thrilled to be returning to this world and exploring it further through music.”

Talking about reuniting with Jesper, director Adesh Prasad said, “Jesper’s music was an integral part of creating the world of Tumbbad. Right from the beginning, I knew that the film needed a very distinct sonic identity, something that could capture its mystery, scale, and unsettling atmosphere.” “Jesper understood that vision beautifully and brought a completely unique musical language to the film. Having him return for Tumbbad 2 is incredibly exciting because we share a creative understanding of this world, and I look forward to taking that collaboration further and exploring new dimensions of its soundscape,” he added.

Composer Jesper Kyd is returning to the ‘Tumbbad’ franchise to create the original score for its sequel, ‘Tumbbad 2’. Sohum Shah is backing the film in collaboration with Dr. Jayantilal Gada’s Pen Studios. Kyd, known for his work on video game franchises such as ‘Assassin’s Creed,’ ‘Hitman,’ and ‘Borderlands,’ also composed the score for the 2018 film ‘Tumbbad.’

His music contributed to the film’s atmosphere, complementing its folklore, mystery, and mythology. The composer received the Best Score award at the 2019 Critics’ Choice Film Awards for his work on the film.

“Tumbbad 2” is being spearheaded by Sohum Shah under his banner Sohum Shah Films, in collaboration with Pen Studios, headed by veteran producer Dr Jayantilal Gada. The film is directed by Adesh Prasad, who is helming the highly anticipated next chapter of the Tumbbad universe. “Tumbbad 2” is slated for a worldwide theatrical release on 3rd December 2027.

item.title: Our future must be shaped by ‘cooperation, not competition’: PM Modi to ASEAN leaders
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi told ASEAN leaders that India and the 11-member grouping must shape their shared future through cooperation rather than competition. At the India-ASEAN Summit in Manila, he emphasised peace, stability, economic partnership and a stronger Indo-Pacific region
item.content:encoded:
Manila: India and ASEAN together represent nearly a quarter of the world’s population, and their common future must be shaped by “cooperation, not competition,” Prime Minister Narendra Modi told leaders of the 11-nation grouping on Tuesday.

Modi, speaking at the India-ASEAN summit, said New Delhi’s commitment to the grouping’s unity and centrality in the partnership “is and will remain steadfast.” “In the past few years, the world has faced a series of crises. What the world needs most today is peace, stability and predictability,” said the prime minister. “In this context, our theme this year – ‘Navigating Our Future, Together’ – holds special significance.” The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is a regional intergovernmental bloc that promotes economic growth, political stability, security, and cultural cooperation among its member countries in Southeast Asia.

Founded in 1967, ASEAN has 11 members — Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam. India and several other countries, including the US, China, Japan and Australia, are its dialogue partners.

“India and ASEAN together represent nearly a quarter of the world’s population. Therefore, it is essential to ensure that our future is determined by cooperation, not competition,” the prime minister said.

Modi said India and ASEAN have both the strength and the resolve and together, both sides can make this region a symbol of peace and stability.

“We believe that India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply intertwined. In the coming years, the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and Developed India 2047 can play a crucial role in realising our shared aspirations.,” he said “I am confident that today’s meeting will elevate our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” he added.

item.title: Harish Rao slams Congress govt over Aarogyasri dues
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Harish Rao alleged that the Congress government has pushed Telangana's healthcare system into crisis by failing to clear Aarogyasri dues to government hospitals, leading to fund shortages, supply disruptions and suspension of surgeries.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS Legislature Party Deputy Leader T Harish Rao accused the Congress government of pushing the State’s healthcare system into crisis by failing to clear Aarogyasri dues to government teaching hospitals.

Reacting to news reports that the hospitals were owed around Rs 800 crore, he said the Revanth Reddy government had turned Aarogyasri into “Bakayi Sri” (Dues Scheme), keeping poor patients away from healthcare.

According to media reports, Osmania, Gandhi and Niloufer hospitals alone were owed Rs 266 crore. Due to the delay in clearing pending bills, the hospitals were facing challenges including funding shortages, disruption of medicine and surgical supplies, suspension of surgeries and difficulties in meeting daily expenses.

item.title: Calcutta HC issues show-cause notice to Abhishek Banerjee over derogatory remarks on judiciary
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Calcutta High Court issued a show-cause notice to Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee over alleged derogatory remarks accusing sections of the judiciary of bias. Justice Krishan Rao directed him to respond within 15 days, with the next hearing scheduled for December 8
item.content:encoded:
Kolkata: A single-judge bench of the Calcutta High Court, on Tuesday, slapped a show-cause notice on the Trinamool Congress General Secretary and the party’s Diamond Harbour Lok Sabha member Abhishek Banerjee over the latter’s recent derogatory comments accusing a section of the judiciary of being “biased”.

The single-judge bench of Justice Krishan Rao, on Tuesday, directed the Diamond Harbour MP to reply to the show-cause notice within the next 15 days on why the court should not initiate proceedings against him for such comments.

Justice Rao also observed that Banerjee, who is an elected MP, through his comments, tried to influence the trial system. Hence, Justice Rao observed that the court wanted an explanation as to why disciplinary action would not be initiated against Banerjee in light of his attempts to influence the court proceedings and making “disgraceful allegations” in the trial process.

The next hearing in the matter will be on December 8.

Last week, Justice Rao expressed anguish over the reported derogatory comments by Banerjee, who is the nephew of the former West Bengal Chief Minister, Mamata Banerjee.

On November 12, during the final hearing on a petition by Abhishek Banerjee, seeking restoration of his “Z-Plus” security, the West Bengal government Counsel and the state’s Additional Advocate General, Billawdal Bhattacharya, drew the attention of the court to a recent social media message made by the Diamond Harbour MP, in which the latter made some remarks that directly challenged the country’s judicial system and the dignity of the courts.

Bhattacharya then sought the court’s intervention in the matter and strong legal action against Abhishek Banerjee. Thereafter, Abhishek Banerjee’s Counsel said that his client’s comments were in the context of certain developments, as petitions filed by him were pending before the court for several months. Thereafter, Justice Rao expressed his displeasure after this comment.

In very strict language, Justice Rao asked Abhishek Banerjee’s lawyer to submit a complete list of which judges were with the Bharatiya Janata Party and who were with the Trinamool Congress. “Ask your client (Abhishek Banerjee) which judges are with the BJP and which are not! He thinks he is very intelligent. Ask him to give a list; I will look into it,” Justice Rao said.

item.title: Food delivery worker beaten to death after dispute at Bhadrachalam lodge
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 22-year-old food delivery worker was allegedly beaten to death by lodge staff and associates at a private lodge in Bhadrachalam following an argument over Aadhaar verification and room charges. Police have launched an investigation while the accused are absconding.
item.content:encoded:
Kothagudem: The staff and persons connected with the management of a lodge at Bhadrachalam in the district had allegedly beaten up a youth to death over a petty issue, leaving the local residents in the temple town in a state of shock.

According to eyewitness accounts, the deceased Tellam Sharath (22) along with two others Kursam Prashanth and Keesara Karthik, who worked for Swiggy and Zomato, went to stay at Sathya Sai Residency, a private lodge in the town late on Monday night.

An altercation arose between the trio and the lodge personnel regarding an Aadhaar card and the amount charged for a room. As the altercation heated up, the staff and lodge management’s associates allegedly assaulted the trio.

Sharath collapsed on the spot, after being repeatedly punched in the chest and face by one of the assailants. Fearing the consequences, the assailants themselves took him to a hospital, where doctors examined him and declared him dead.

Following the incident, the assailants fled the scene. On receiving information, the local police rushed to the spot. Based on the complaint lodged by the deceased man’s friends, the police launched a probe into the incident.

It was said that one of the accused was already booked for murdering a person on Holi last year at Venkatreddypet of Alluri district in Andhra Pradesh. Sharath belongs to Thotti Pampu village in Annapureddipalle mandal.

item.title: M Night Shyamalan says ‘Remain’ trailer reflects the film’s ‘human touch’ and handmade artistry
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Filmmaker M Night Shyamalan has unveiled the trailer of his upcoming film 'Remain', calling it the beginning of storytelling rather than just promotion. Co-created with author Nicholas Sparks, the film features a hands-on creative process involving rehearsals and VistaVision cameras
item.content:encoded:
Mumbai: Filmmaker M Night Shyamalan has shared the trailer of his upcoming film ‘Remain’, describing it as more than just a marketing exercise and calling it the beginning of telling the story.

In a video posted on Instagram, the director opened up about the creative process behind the film and spoke about collaborating closely with author Nicholas Sparks on the idea explaining how the team focused on rehearsals, storyboarding and a hands-on approach to filmmaking to bring the project to life.

He shared in the video: “I’m so excited about this trailer for Remain. It represents a lot of things. First of all, it represents this idea that Nicholas Sparks and I came up with actually in this building behind me, and it represents a kind of aesthetic or a feeling about filmmaking.” Shyamalan shared that they shot it on VistaVision cameras, 40-year-old cameras.

The filmmaker said: “We shoot it like a play. I storyboard everything. We rehearse. Jake and Phoebe and Ashley Walters, all of them come and we rehearse, and then we go shoot the movie. We edit it in this building for a year. It’s very homegrown, Pennsylvania, handmade artistry. At least that’s the hope.”

He shared: “So when you watch this trailer, I hope you get that feeling of that human touch in everything, and I think that matters. So here it is, the trailer for Remain.”

Taking to the caption section, the filmmaker said that he just wanted to express that this trailer is not just marketing. “It’s the beginning of telling the story. The marketing team at Warner Bros. has become some of my closest friends. They come and stay at the house, and they saw the first assembly of the movie months and months ago, so that we’re all telling the story together, saying the right things, and telling you guys just enough, but not too much. We want to make sure it represents everything that Remain is about and I hope you enjoy it.”

item.title: Two including child killed after building collapses in Delhi’s Shahdara
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Two people, including a child, were killed after a two-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Shahdara on Tuesday. Several others are feared trapped under the debris as rescue operations continue. The incident follows multiple fatal building collapses across the national capital
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Two, including a child, were killed after a two-storey building collapse in Delhi’s Shahdara on Tuesday, officials said, adding that several are feared trapped under the debris. The incident occurred in the Jwala Nagar area of ​​Vivek Vihar, located in the Shahdara district.

Upon receiving the information, police, along with rescue officials, reached the site and initiated a rescue and relief operation. Efforts are underway to rescue the trapped individuals, officials said. Further details are awaited. This comes just days after a multi-storey building collapse in Delhi’s Chawri Bazar, in which seven people were killed.

The three-storey under-construction building in Gali Sitara, near Chawri Bazar Metro Station, collapsed on November 5.

Subsequently, a massive rescue operation involving the Delhi Police, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Services and the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) was launched. Police arrested the building owner, Saimullah alias Ayub, a resident of Delhi.

In addition to this, three contractors were also arrested after being apprehended from Sirohi village in Faridabad. According to the police, the construction work underway in a now-collapsed building in Delhi’s Chawri Bazaar area was illegal, and the building was unsafe.

Meanwhile, the Municipal Corporation suspended its Junior Engineer (JE) and Assistant Engineer (AE), and an FIR has been registered against the contractor following the tragedy. This also comes just months after the tragic building collapse in Delhi’s Satya Niketan, which claimed seven lives.

The collapse occurred on the afternoon of September 6. Due to the weekend and concurrent rainfall, students were inside the building at the time of the collapse. A series of other tragic building collapses occurred in the national capital in the past few months. A portion of a multi-storied building collapsed in north Delhi’s Seemapuri area on October 7.

Four people were killed in the incident. On October 25, an under-construction structure (ground-plus-two floors) in Milan Garden, Harsh Vihar in Northeast Delhi collapsed after an illegal attempt to add an extra lintel/floor caused the lower slab to cave in. A 60-year-old father, Chanderpal, and his 33-year-old son, Vijay Kumar, lost their lives.

item.title: NIA to probe module of overground workers linked to Pak-based terrorist outfits in J&K
item.dc:creator: PTI
item.description: The NIA has registered a case to investigate an alleged overground worker network linked to Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed in Jammu and Kashmir. The probe follows the arrest of two Rajouri residents accused of providing logistical and shelter support to terrorists
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered a case to probe a module of overground workers linked to the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorist outfits in Jammu and Kashmir, officials said on Tuesday.

They said the NIA case stems from a First Information Report (FIR) registered by Jammu and Kashmir Police relating to the busting of a terror ecosystem in September.

The Jammu and Kashmir Police arrested Zakir Hussain and Mohd Azam, both residents of Kotcharwal Teryath in Rajouri district, during the investigation of a terror module active in the region.

Preliminary investigation revealed that the accused were allegedly involved in providing logistical support, safe transit and other ground-level assistance to terrorists, according to the local police.

On September 11, police station Dharamsal (Rajouri district) received credible information that Hussain, Azam and their associates were closely associated with and facilitating the activities of LeT and JeM terrorists, according to the NIA’s FIR.

Accused persons were allegedly harbouring and concealing terrorists and providing them shelter, logistical assistance, material support and other forms of assistance and, pursuant to a criminal conspiracy, were facilitating and furthering their unlawful and terrorist activities, it said, giving details of the suspected offence.

The NIA registered the case on the direction of the Union Home Ministry.

In its order, the Home Ministry said the case warranted an NIA probe considering “gravity of the offence, its grave implications for the security, integrity and sovereignty of India, and the need to unearth the larger conspiracy”.

item.title: Prabhudeva, AR Rahman’s ‘Moonwalk’ to hit screens on December 24
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Prabhudeva-starrer 'Moonwalk', directed by Manoj NS, is set for a worldwide theatrical release on December 24 as a Christmas entertainer. The film marks Oscar-winning composer AR Rahman's acting debut and features Yogi Babu in 16 different roles
item.content:encoded:
Chennai: The makers of director Manoj NS’s ‘Moonwalk’, featuring actor Prabhudeva in the lead, have now announced that the film will hit screens for Christmas on December 24 this year. The film has triggered huge expectations among fans and filmbuffs as the film will also mark the acting debut of Oscar award winning music composer AR Rahman.

Sources say that the ace music director will make a fun cameo appearance in the film. A R Rahman, who took to his X timeline to share the update on the film’s release, wrote, “MOONWALK – A FAMILY COMEDY ENTERTAINER! Worldwide theatrical release on December 24! #FamilyLaughter #HolidaysLaughter Starring @PDdancing @iYogiBabu @AjuVarghesee #ArjunAshokan @Satzsathish321 Directed by #ManojNirmalaSreedharan Produced by #ManojNirmalaSreedharan #DivyaManoj and @praveenelak @behindwoods DOP @Anoopvshylaja.”

It may be recalled that the film had originally be scheduled for release for Deepavali. Behindwoods Productions, while announcing the film’s release for Deepavali, had said the film would deliver to audiences a spectacular festive celebration filled with laughter and unforgettable family moments.

Apart from acting in it, AR Rahman has also scored the music for the film. Apart from Prabhudeva, the film will also feature actors Yogi Babu, Aju Varghese, Arjun Ashokan, Satz, Nishma, Sushmitha, Redin Kingsley, Mottai Rajendran, Lollu Sabha Swaminathan, Dr Santhosh Jacob, Deepa Shankar, and Ramkumar Natarajan among others.

Another highlight of the movie, sources say, will be Yogi babu appearing in 16 different roles. Sources claim that ‘Moonwalk’ will seek to seamlessly blend comedy, music and dance into a vibrant cinematic celebration.

The film features cinematography by Anoop V Shylaja, choreography by Sekhar VJ and Piyush Shazia, production design by Shanoo, and costume design by Divya George and Swetha Raju.

MOONWALK, produced by Manoj NS, Divya Manoj and Praveen Elak under the banner of Behindwoods Productions, will release simultaneously in Tamil, Telugu and Hindi languages. Romeo Pictures has acquired the worldwide distribution rights, while Lahari has acquired the film’s music rights.

item.title: Girl electrocuted while playing on terrace of Musheerabad girls’ home
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: An 11-year-old girl died after accidentally touching a high-tension power line with a cleaning stick while playing on the terrace of a girls' home in Musheerabad. Another girl was injured while attempting to rescue her, and police have launched an investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: An 11-year-old girl died after suffering an electric shock while playing on the terrace of a girls’ home in Musheerabad on Monday evening. Another girl suffered injuries while trying to rescue her.

According to Musheerabad police and the management of the Nightingale Home for Girls, three inmates identified as Rebecca (11), Nandini (14) and Jayashree (9), went to the terrace of the building on the premises of Musheerabad Government School to play.

While playing, Rebecca, a Class IV student, accidentally touched a high-tension power line with a floor-cleaning stick. She suffered a severe electric shock and collapsed. Nandini, who was standing nearby, suffered injuries when she tried to help Rebecca.

Jayashree, who witnessed the incident, panicked and rushed downstairs to alert the home authorities.

The management immediately shifted the girls to Gandhi Hospital, where doctors attempted CPR on Rebecca, but she did not respond. They declared her dead.

Musheerabad police are investigating the incident.

item.title: ‘Akvan’ set to intensify into severe cyclone by evening; Andhra CM takes stock of situation
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Cyclonic Storm Akvan over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before making landfall between Nellore and Tuni on November 20. Andhra Pradesh authorities have issued alerts and initiated precautionary disaster management measures
item.content:encoded:
Visakhapatnam: Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ over the Southeast and adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening. According to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA), the cyclone moved at a speed of 3 km/h over the last six hours. It is currently centred 610 km from Chennai, 660 km from Machilipatnam, 670 km from Visakahapatnam, and 790 km from Gopalpur (Odisha), said Prakhar Jain, MD of the State Disaster Management Authority and CEO of Real Time Governance Society (RTGS).

It is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening. Moving in a west-northwesterly direction, it is expected to strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by the morning of Thursday (November 19). The cyclone is likely to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni by Friday (November 20) afternoon. At the time of landfall, strong winds are expected at speeds of 120-130 km/h, potentially reaching a maximum of 145 km/h.

He said people in coastal areas should remain alert Meanwhile, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu in the morning held a teleconference with officials on the impending cyclone. He inquired with officials about the cyclone’s trajectory. The officials reported that the cyclone is moving at a speed of 3 km/h and that there will be greater clarity regarding the intensity of the cyclone by this evening.

RTGS officials warned that it could intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by this evening. Heavy rainfall is expected on November 19 and 20 due to Cyclone ‘Akvan’.

Chief Minister Naidu stated that this is the third cyclone to hit the state in recent days. He said there was no need to panic due to these disasters; instead, measures must be taken to ensure the public is not adversely affected. Weather warnings must be continuously communicated to the public and to those in the areas likely to be impacted by the cyclone. Information should be conveyed directly to the people in the affected areas through ‘Swarna Grama’ and ‘Swarna Ward’ staff, he said.

The Chief Minister told officials that precautions must be taken to ensure that fishermen do not venture out to sea. The public must be assured that, regardless of the scale of the disaster, the government and its officials are there to support them. If trees fall or electricity poles collapse, they must be cleared immediately, and restoration work should be undertaken, he said.

He wanted officials to make assessments in real-time, undertake rescue operations and provide rehabilitation. Precautions must be taken to prevent breaches in tanks and canals due to the cyclone, the Chief Minister added.

item.title: Raveena Tandon visits Mahakaleshwar Temple with children
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Bollywood actress Raveena Tandon visited Ujjain's Mahakaleshwar Temple with her daughter Rasha Thadani and son, offering prayers to Lord Mahakal. She expressed happiness at bringing both children together to seek blessings at the revered Jyotirlinga shrine
item.content:encoded:
Ujjain: Bollywood actress Raveena Tandon on Tuesday morning visited the famous Mahakaleshwar Temple in Ujjain along with her daughter Rasha Thadani and son, offering prayers and seeking the blessings of Lord Mahakal.

The 54-year-old actress said the visit was particularly special for her as she could bring both her children to the temple this time. She also mentioned that her daughter had earlier accompanied her on visits to religious places, including the 12 Jyotirlingas across the country. “Today is a very fortunate day for me because I have brought both my son and daughter along. My daughter has visited before, as we have already visited all 12 Jyotirlingas,” Tandon said while sharing her experience.

She said her son had also joined her on the temple visit this time, along with other relatives and friends, making the occasion more memorable for the family.

“But today, my son has also come, along with our other relatives and friends,” she told IANS. The visit comes amid the continued arrival of devotees and prominent personalities at the Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas dedicated to Lord Shiva.

Situated in Ujjain, the temple is among the most revered religious centres in the country and attracts a large number of devotees throughout the year. The temple is particularly known for its Bhasma Aarti, a distinctive early-morning ritual performed before the deity.

Raveena Tandon has been associated with the Hindi film industry for several decades and is known for films such as ‘Mohra’, ‘Dilwale’ and ‘Daman’.
