Her 21-year-old daughter, has also made her debut in the film industry. The actress’s visit to the temple highlighted the family’s religious outing, with Tandon expressing happiness at being able to seek the blessings of Lord Mahakal in the company of both her children.

item.title: Six Pakistani soldiers killed in 4 drone Ops across Balochistan: BLA
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claimed responsibility for four drone operations targeting Pakistani military camps, convoys and security posts across Balochistan, reportedly killing six security personnel and injuring several others. Pakistan's military confirmed two deaths in a drone attack
item.content:encoded:
Quetta: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed that its aerial and drone warfare unit carried out four operations in different parts of Balochistan over the past few days, killing six Pakistani security personnel and injuring several others, local media reported.

In a statement issued on Monday, BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that the group’s aerial and drone warfare unit, “QAHR”, had targeted Pakistani army camps, posts and convoys in a series of operations across the province. He said that the BLA targeted a vehicle belonging to a Pakistani army convoy in a drone strike in the Kurdgap area of Mastung on November 14. The operation was carried out based on what he described as credible intelligence provided by the group’s intelligence wing, “Zirab”.

Two Pakistani personnel, including a senior official, were killed in the attack. The BLA’s official channel, Hakal, has also released a one-minute-and-25-second video of that attack, which showed its drone unit, “QAHR”, targeting a vehicle of the Pakistani Army convoy in the Kurdgap area of Mastung.

Meanwhile, the Pakistan Army’s Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) )– the official media and public relations wing for Pakistan’s Armed Forces confirmed the deaths of two personnel, stating that senior army officers and other personnel had been targeted in a drone attack, The Balochistan Post reported.

According to the BLA statement, the group also launched drone attacks on the Pakistani Army’s main camp in the Khadkocha area of Mastung on November 11, targeting its key positions and installations. The attacks killed two security personnel and caused financial losses. The spokesperson further said that on November 9, the QAHR unit targeted the Pakistani Army’s main camp in Khadkocha in a drone strike.

He said that the group targeted the forces and armoured vehicles inside the military camp, killing one security personnel on the spot. In another operation on November 5, the BLA claimed that its fighters carried out three drone attacks on the Pakistani Army’s main camp in the Mangchar area of Kalat district, targeting security personnel, installations and vehicles.

The attacks reportedly killed one security personnel and injured at least three others, while a vehicle was also severely damaged. These latest attacks come amid a series of drone strikes targeting Pakistani security forces in recent days, highlighting the growing use of unmanned aerial capabilities by armed groups operating in Balochistan.

item.title: SC upholds relief to Azam Khan in fake birth certificate case; grants relief to wife, son
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: The Supreme Court dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government's plea challenging the stay on Azam Khan's conviction in the fake birth certificate case. It also stayed the convictions of his wife Tazeen Fatima and son Abdullah Azam Khan, granting relief to all three
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government’s plea challenging the Allahabad High Court’s decision to stay the conviction and seven-year sentence of senior Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan in a fake birth certificate case.

A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu also granted relief to Khan’s wife, Tazeen Fatima, and son Abdullah Azam Khan, by staying their conviction in the case. The proceedings arose from three separate petitions filed before the Supreme Court, including one by the Uttar Pradesh government challenging the relief granted to Azam Khan and two others filed by Abdullah Azam Khan and Tazeen Fatima against the Allahabad High Court’s refusal to stay their convictions.

In May 2024, the Allahabad High Court stayed Azam Khan’s conviction and seven-year sentence in the case. However, it had declined to grant similar relief to his wife and son, although all three had been granted bail.

Aggrieved by the High Court’s decision, the Uttar Pradesh government approached the Supreme Court, seeking to set aside the relief granted to the senior Samajwadi Party leader.

Meanwhile, Abdullah Azam Khan and Tazeen Fatima challenged the High Court’s refusal to stay their convictions, stating that they too had been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the trial court in the same case. The case dates back to January 3, 2019, when Akash Saxena, now a BJP MLA from Rampur, lodged a complaint alleging that Azam Khan and his wife had procured two birth certificates for their son.

According to the prosecution, one birth certificate issued by the Rampur Municipality mentioned Abdullah Azam’s date of birth as January 1, 1993, while another certificate showed his date of birth as September 30, 1990, in Lucknow. On October 18, 2023, a sessions court convicted all three and sentenced them to seven years’ imprisonment in the alleged forgery case.

The trio was convicted under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), including Sections 420 (cheating), 467 (forgery of valuable security), 468 (forgery for the purpose of cheating), 471 (using a forged document as genuine) and 120-B (criminal conspiracy).

item.title: Woman seeking work allegedly abducted, assaulted and robbed in Uppal
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: A 30-year-old woman seeking daily-wage work was allegedly abducted by an unidentified man in Uppal, sexually assaulted near Nalla Cheruvu, and robbed of her gold earrings. Police have registered a case and launched efforts to trace the suspect.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: A woman who was waiting for daily-wage work was allegedly abducted, sexually assaulted and robbed of her gold earrings by an unidentified man in Uppal.

According to police, the 30-year-old woman from Boduppal was waiting by the roadside for work on Monday, when an unidentified man approached her, claiming that he had worked for her. He allegedly took her in an auto-rickshaw towards Uppal.

The suspect reportedly dropped her near Nalla Cheruvu, forcibly took her into nearby bushes and sexually assaulted her. He later used cutting pliers to remove her earrings before fleeing the scene.

Based on the victim’s complaint, Uppal police registered a case and are investigating.

Efforts are on to identify and nab the suspect.

item.title: Piyush Goyal concludes Egypt visit, discussion on bilateral trade pact to begin
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: India and Egypt agreed to establish a Working Group to explore a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), aiming to boost bilateral trade, investment and cooperation. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal’s visit also reinforced the $12 billion bilateral trade target
item.content:encoded:
New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal concluded his official visit to Egypt, with both sides agreeing to constitute a Working Group to discuss the modalities and framework for the Terms of Reference for entering into a mutually beneficial trade pact or CEPA, after evaluating the gains for both sides, covering trade in goods, services and investment, an official statement said on Tuesday.

The visit marked his first bilateral visit to an African country. During the visit, the minister held a series of high-level bilateral meetings, co-chaired the 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC), participated in business engagements and interacted with representatives of the Indian and Egyptian business communities.

It provided renewed momentum to the longstanding India–Egypt economic partnership, with both sides reaffirming their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, promoting investments, strengthening industrial cooperation and enhancing business-to-business linkages, according to an official statement.

During the visit, Goyal called on Prime Minister of the Arab Republic of Egypt Dr. Mostafa Madbouly, held bilateral meetings with Egyptian Ministers and met leading business representatives in Egypt. The 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee was elevated to the Ministerial level, reflecting the growing importance of economic and commercial engagement between the two countries. Both sides reviewed developments in bilateral trade and agreed to work towards achieving a target of $12 billion in bilateral trade.

They emphasised the importance of diversifying the trade basket, promoting higher value-added exports, strengthening market access and addressing trade-related challenges.

Bilateral merchandise trade during April–September 2026 stood at $5.04 billion, registering growth of 64 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year. India’s exports to Egypt during FY 2025–26 stood at $3.87 billion, while imports from Egypt amounted to $2.60 billion. The discussions covered a broad range of areas, including agricultural and veterinary cooperation, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, food security, transport and logistics.

Both sides underscored the importance of regular exchanges of business delegations, buyer missions, trade exhibitions and business-matching activities. Both sides reviewed investment opportunities in Egypt, particularly in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE). Approximately 70 Indian companies are operating in Egypt, with investments of around $5 billion.

The Egyptian side welcomed greater Indian participation in investment opportunities in sectors such as automotive and auto components, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, textiles, food processing, engineering, renewable energy and logistics. In the areas of digital technology and fintech, both sides acknowledged the potential of linking India’s UPI with Egypt’s Instapay, the positive role of trade in local currencies in enhancing exports, and leveraging India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to accelerate Egypt’s digital transformation.

During his interactions with Egyptian leaders and the business community, Goyal extended invitations to participate in the Vibrant Gujarat Summit 2027, to be held in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and Bharat Mobility 2027, scheduled from February 4-9, 2027 in New Delhi.

item.title: J&K: Minimum temperature drops below freezing point in Srinagar
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: Srinagar recorded its first sub-zero night temperature of the season at minus 0.1°C, while Gulmarg and Pahalgam recorded minus 3.4°C and minus 3.8°C, respectively. Authorities revised school timings amid intensifying cold, with dry weather forecast across Jammu and Kashmir
item.content:encoded:
Srinagar: For the first time in this season, night temperature dropped below the freezing point in Jammu and Kashmir’s Srinagar city on Tuesday, with the tourist resort of Gulmarg and Pahalgam hill station recording minus 3.4 and minus 3.8 degrees Celsius as the minimum temperature, respectively.

Mukhtar Ahmed, Director of the local Meteorological Department, said, “For the first time this session, the minimum temperature dropped to minus 0.1 degrees Celsius in Srinagar today. This is the lowest minimum temperature recorded so far this season in the city.” The minimum temperature dropped to minus 3.4 degrees Celsius in the ski resort of Gulmarg, while it was minus 3.8 degrees in Pahalgam on Tuesday.

In Jammu city, the minimum temperature was 11 degrees Celsius; in Katra, it was 10.6 degrees; in Batote, it was 6.9 degrees; in Banihal was 9.8 degrees; and Bhaderwah recorded 1.1 degrees.

Due to the morning chill, authorities announced that schools for nursery to middle classes will open at 10.30 a.m. and close at 2.30 p.m., and from Class 8 to Class 12, schools will open at 10.30 a.m. and close at 3.30 p.m. from this day onwards.

The Meteorological Department has forecast generally dry weather till the end of the month. Due to the clear night sky, minimum temperatures are likely to drop further across Jammu and Kashmir in the coming days. Tourists have been visiting Gulmarg, Pahalgam and Sonamarg these days to see the season’s fresh snowfall. For some of these tourists, who are in the Valley for the first time, seeing snow on the ground and the snow-clad mountain tops is a lifetime experience.

Sunil Kumar, 22, has come to Kashmir for the first time. “Believe me, I won’t have missed the fun of falling snowflakes for any other experience in my life,” he said while watching fresh snowfall in Gulmarg. For locals, however, it is time to wear the traditional tweed overgarment called the ‘Pheran’, as people living in villages are making charcoal from fallen Chinar leaves to light their earthen firepot called the ‘Kangri’ in the colder days ahead.

item.title: Massive gas leak at ONGC well sparks panic in Andhra’s Konaseema
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: A major gas leak from an ONGC drilling well near Geddada village in Andhra Pradesh's Konaseema district triggered panic in surrounding villages, leading to evacuations, traffic restrictions, and emergency containment efforts. Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu directed officials and ONGC to prioritise public safety and bring the situation under control.
item.content:encoded:
Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh): A massive gas leak occurred from an ONGC gas drilling well in Andhra Pradesh’s Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district on Tuesday, triggering panic among people in surrounding villages.

The gas leak from the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) rig occurred near Geddada village in Mamidikuduru mandal.

According to officials, the gas began leaking around 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday, accompanied by a loud noise, and is currently spewing out in large volumes.

The incident triggered panic among residents and commuters on the National Highway 216.

Gas was reportedly spreading to nearby villages, with residents complaining of a strong gas smell. People living in the vicinity and motorists passing through the highway ran to safety after noticing the gas leak.

Police halted vehicular movement on the Geddada-Mamidikuduru highway as a precautionary measure.

ONGC officials and police were alerted, while specialised teams were being mobilised to contain the leak. A control team from Narsapur left for the spot to contain the blowout.

The officials stated that there have been no fires so far and that the wellhead remains secure. ONGC personnel were taking measures to prevent the gas from spreading near the ground level.

Fire-fighters arranged the water umbrella around the rig to prevent fire.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu has spoken with officials regarding a gas leak incident.

He directed that residents in the affected areas be evacuated to safer locations.

The Chief Minister said public safety must be given the highest priority. He said ONGC must take immediate action, deploying specialised technical teams to bring the gas leak under control.

Noting that such incidents have occurred frequently of late, the Chief Minister instructed officials to immediately engage with ONGC management.

He has ordered a review of safety protocols in consultation with the ONGC Chairman and other senior officials of the organisation.

Authorities have already evacuated residents living within a one-kilometre radius of the gas well.

As a precautionary safety measure, diesel generators and other equipment have been shut down and removed from the vicinity. A cementing team is arriving at the site to completely plug the gas well leak.

ONGC officials have stated that the gas leak incident will be brought fully under control within the next 4-5 hours.

item.title: Terrorist involved in Nov 11 Kulgam attack on CRPF men, killed; hunt on for 2nd
item.dc:creator: IANS
item.description: One terrorist involved in the November 11 CRPF attack in Kulgam was killed during an encounter at Laroo, while security forces continue searching for Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat. The incident follows another terror attack in Kishtwar that killed two SPOs
item.content:encoded:
Srinagar: One of the two terrorists involved in the November 11 attack on CRPF personnel in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district has been killed in an operation, while the hunt for the second involved terrorist is on, sources told IANS on Tuesday.

Highly placed sources told IANS that on November 10, Umar Nisar Dar, along with Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) / TRF Commander Lateef Bhat, conducted reconnaissance at multiple locations, including Mir Bazaar, Akhran, Hablish and Kilam, to identify targets and plan attacks on security forces.

“On November 11, Umar Nisar Dar, accompanied by LeT Commander Lateef Bhat, carried out an attack on a CRPF Naka at Akhran before fleeing the scene. During the analysis of CCTV footage from November 10 and 11, security agencies found both Umar Nisar Dar and LeT Commander Lateef Bhat captured on multiple CCTV cameras installed at the identified locations. The footage documented their movements while conducting reconnaissance and subsequently fleeing after the Akhran attack,” the sources said.

“Following Umar Nisar Dar’s disappearance, his family had lodged a missing report at Police Station Kulgam. During the course of the investigation, investigating agencies established that Umar had been providing shelter and assistance to LeT Commander Lateef Bhat for the past five to six months,” the sources added.

“Investigations further revealed that immediately after the Akhran incident, Umar Nisar Dar joined the TRF outfit,” the sources further said.

After fleeing the scene of the attack, both Umar Nisar Dar and Lateef Bhat were intercepted by security forces at Laroo on Monday. During the ensuing encounter, Umar Nisar Dar was killed. The hunt for LeT Commander Lateef Bhat is underway, sources added.

The Kulgam attack was followed by another terror strike in the Kishtwar district of Jammu division in which terrorists killed two special police officers (SPOs) identified as Babi Chand and Yashpal Kumar. The two SPOs were reportedly going to join the Army during an anti-terrorist operation in the Kyar-Dachan area of Kishtwar when the terrorists killed them. The occurrence of two terrorist attacks, one after the other, has created cynicism about the official claims of having ended terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir.

Both the ruling National Conference and the opposition BJP in the union territory have questioned the official claims of having dealt a death blow to terrorism.

item.title: KTR recalls Telangana statehood movement’s 2011 padayatra
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: KT Rama Rao recalled the six-day padayatra conducted in November 2011 during the Telangana statehood movement, stating that the march, led on K. Chandrashekhar Rao’s call, remains an inspiring chapter that received widespread public support.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS working president KT Rama Rao on Tuesday recalled the six-day padayatra undertaken 15 years ago as part of the Telangana statehood movement, on the call of party president K Chandrashekhar Rao.

The padayatra, held from November 16 to 21, 2011, began at Vikarabad and passed through Nawabpet, Shankarpally, Patancheru, Serilingampally, Kukatpally and Balanagar before reaching Quthbullapur.

Taking to X, Rama Rao described the march, which received support from people across all sections of society, as an inspiring chapter in the struggle for Telangana statehood.

item.title: Jadcherla MLA alleges Rs 15,000 bribe for hereditary property transfer
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: Congress MLA J. Anirudh Reddy alleged rampant corruption among government officials in Jadcherla, claiming bribes were being sought for routine administrative work and commissions demanded from contractors. He urged journalists to expose such irregularities and assured support in taking action against corrupt officials.
item.content:encoded:
Mahabubnagar: Congress MLA from Jadcherla J. Anirudh Reddy has once again admitted to rampant corruption in the Congress government, accusing officials of demanding bribes to carry out routine administrative works.

The MLA said officials were corrupt and urged the media to expose such practices through their reports.

Addressing a programme in Jadcherla on Monday, Anirudh Reddy recalled an incident in which an official was allegedly paid a bribe of Rs.15,000 to complete a hereditary property transfer.

“In Jadcherla, I instructed officials to execute one virasat (hereditary property transfer), but my instructions were not followed. However, when Rs. 15,000 was offered as a bribe at the same office, the work was completed,” Anirudh Reddy said. His remarks were captured in a video that is circulating on social media.

Citing another instance, he charged that officials were demanding commissions ranging from 10 to 20 per cent to clear bills for cement road works worth Rs. 5 lakh.

The Congress MLA urged journalists to highlight these irregularities and assured them of his support. He asked them to report why contractors were reluctant to take up work and why several projects were being suspended.

“For every Roads and Buildings contract or road work, the government collects seigniorage charges in advance. Yet, officials threaten contractors and demand commissions,” the Congress MLA maintained.

Anirudh Reddy said journalists could play a crucial role in exposing corruption. Once such reports appeared in newspapers or other media platforms, he would take up the matter, identify the officials concerned and ensure action against them, he said.

Admitting that several administrative lapses were taking place, the MLA said the problem was rooted at the ground level. “Journalists and politicians are not corrupt, but officials are. However hard you try to do good, the system at the ground level is not functioning properly,” he said.

item.title: Harish Rao flays Congress for betraying people on poll promises
item.dc:creator: Telangana Today
item.description: BRS leader T Harish Rao accused the Congress government of failing to fulfil its manifesto promises three years after releasing them and questioned why legal status had not been granted to the Six Guarantees despite repeated assurances.
item.content:encoded:
Hyderabad: BRS Legislature Party deputy leader T Harish Rao flayed the Congress government for betraying people without implementing its manifesto promises even after three years.

He demanded answers from AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge, Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka and Minister D Sridhar Babu.

Marking three years since the Congress released its manifesto on Tuesday, Harish Rao said the party equated it to the Bhagavad Gita, Quran and Bible for it and assured that it would implement every promise.

“But the Congress’ Abhaya Hastham turned into an empty hand as it failed to implement them even after three years,” he said.

He pointed out that the ruling Congress promised legal sanctity to its Six Guarantees in the first Cabinet meeting, but failed. “Even after 38 Cabinet meetings, why has legal status not been given to the Six Guarantees?” he asked.

The BRSLP deputy leader alleged that the Congress secured votes by making 420 promises under the six guarantees but subsequently either diluted or abandoned them. He said the party converted people’s hopes into votes and left them unfulfilled after coming to power. He felt that the Congress that invokes the Gandhi family for politics, should be ashamed for failing to implement the promises made in Gandhi Bhavan itself.

He said people recognised the Congress’s deceptive politics and were ready to teach it a lesson.
